English rendering of Rik 3.6; Special topics: "tūtujānaḥ," "brahmāṇi," "harivaḥ," "dadhiṣva"; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O Indra, come hither quickly with the tawny horses to our prayers and accept our food in this libation."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

तूतुजानः (tūtujānaḥ) — For this word the Bhāṣyakāra gives "tvaramāṇaḥ" ("hastening") and Skandasvāmī gives "kṣipram" ("quickly, swiftly"). Among Western scholars, in their treatment of the sense of this word in this Ṛk: Ludwig gives "hasty, speedy, exerting"; Williams, "fleet"; Benfey, "exerted"; Rosen, "hastened." Besides this, Ludwig, in the places where this word is used — the references printed are Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-29-5; 10-44-1 — gives "exerting"; (at 7-84-5) "Urging"; (at 4-32-2) "Pushing"; (at 10-44-1; 1-129-1) "Prompt"; and (in the Ṛks 4-32-2; 1-61-12; 7-67-6; 7-84-5) "Active, strong," as meanings of this word. The reference-numbers in this list are hard to read in the print and the assignment of numbers to meanings may be off; the same number appears under more than one meaning as read. Please re-check before relying on them.

ब्रह्माणि (brahmāṇi) — The matter of this word was set out in the preceding Ṛk.

हरिवः (harivaḥ) — For this the Bhāṣyakāra gives "harayo 'sya santi" ("harayo 'sya santīti"; हरयोऽस्य सन्तीति — "he who has Haris [horses]"), that is, "one possessed of horses." The sense given by the other commentators is the same. "One possessed of horses" means "one seated in a chariot to which horses are yoked." "Harī" means Indra's horses. This sense is supported by the mantra:

तिष्ठा हरी रथ आयुज्यमाना याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नो अच्छ । (ऋ. सं. ३-३५-१) tiṣṭhā harī ratha āyujyamānā yāhi vāyur na niyuto no accha | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-35-1) Gloss: "Mount, with the two bay horses being yoked to the chariot; come to us, like Vāyu with his team."

Among Western scholars: Griffith gives "Having a gold colour horse"; Williams, "provided with the horse named Hari"; Ludwig, Rosen, Benfey, "Possessed of bey [sic] or towny [sic] horses" — thus they have explained the meaning of this word.

दधिष्व (dadhiṣva) — This word is the "loṭ" (imperative) form of the root "dhā." Its sense here may be given as "accept."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

"Tūtujānaḥ": when the affix "liṭ" is placed after the root "tuj," then by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-8) — when "liṭ" follows, the first part of the root that is not already a reduplicative syllable and contains a single vowel is doubled. In the case where the root begins with a vowel (ajādi), the second … continues on the next page; this is the Kannada rendering of the grammar characterized on p. 43 Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 5 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." This page is pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, setting out for "tūtujānaḥ," "harivaḥ," "brahmāṇi/upa" and "dadhiṣva" the same steps already given in Sanskrit on p. 43. Per the standing convention for dense Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā with no bearing on the sense already given, it is translated in compressed form rather than line by line; every sūtra the page cites is kept, in all three layers, so that nothing is silently dropped. Sūtra-numbers are as printed in Kannada numerals.

original p. 45

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.6 (Kannada) — characterized

  1. "Tūtujānaḥ." continuing from p. 44 In the case where the root begins with a vowel, the second one-vowel part is the one doubled. Here, after doubling "tuj" (giving "tuj-tuj + liṭ"), the rule हलादिः शेषः (halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, पा. ७-४-६०) leaves only the first consonant of the reduplicative syllable and drops its other consonants — so the first "tuj" is reduced to "tu." By लिटः कानज्वा (liṭaḥ kānaj vā, पा. ३-२-१०६) — in the Veda the substitute "kānac" for "liṭ" is optional, and it is chosen here; in "kānac" the letter "c" is a marker and "āna" remains: "tu-tuj + āna." Then तुजादीनां दीर्घोऽभ्यासस्य (tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya, पा. ६-१-७) — the reduplicative syllable of the roots of the "tuj" group is lengthened — gives "tū-tujāna." Finally अभ्यस्तानामादिः (abhyastānām ādiḥ, पा. ६-१-१८९) — when a "lasārvadhātuka" affix beginning with the accented vowel (including the "iṭ"-position) follows, the first syllable of the reduplicated stem becomes acute; hence the first syllable of "tūtujānaḥ" is acute.

  2. "Harivaḥ." "Harayo 'sya santi" ("he has horses") — the affix "matup" by तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् (tad asyāsty asminn iti matup, पा. ५-२-९४). By छन्दसीरः (chandasīraḥ, पा. ८-२-१५) the "m" of "matup," after a word ending in "i" or "r"-type letter, becomes "v" (so "hari-vat"). For the vocative singular ending, "matup" being "u"-marked (ugit), by उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः (ugid-acāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ, पा. ७-१-७०) the augment "num" comes (even to a non-root stem), giving "harivan-t + (su)"; then संयोगान्तस्य लोपः (saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ, पा. ८-२-२३) — loss of the final of a conjunct — and, by "hal-ṅyābbhyo…" (हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल् — hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt su-ti-sy-apṛktaṃ hal, पा. ६-१-६८ [number as read]) the loss of the ending, leave "harivan." Then मतुवसोरु संबुद्धौ छन्दसि (matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi, पा. ८-३-१) — in the Veda, in the vocative, "ru" replaces the last letter of "matup" and "vasu" stems — and, by the paribhāṣā अलोऽन्त्यस्य (alo 'ntyasya, पा. १-१-५२) the substitute goes to the final letter "n"; the "r" then becomes visarga: "harivaḥ." Here the vocative-accent of the eighth chapter (aṣṭamika anudātta) arises.

  3. "Brahmāṇi" and the "a" of "upa." By सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवत्स्वरे (subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare, पा. २-१-२) a vocative is treated, for accent, as part of the following word. But this operates only where there is mutual connection of sense, by the governing paribhāṣā समर्थः पदविधिः (samarthaḥ pada-vidhiḥ, पा. २-१-१). Here "brahmāṇi" and "harivaḥ" have no mutual syntactic connection, hence no such connection of sense, and no "parāṅgavad-bhāva" arises. Consequently "brahmāṇi" does not receive the aṣṭamika vocative-anudātta; it stays acute on its first syllable. Then the unaccented "a" of the preceding "upa," standing before this acute syllable, becomes "sannatara" (lowered still further) by उदात्तस्वरितपरस्य सन्नतरः (udātta-svarita-parasya sannataraḥ, पा. १-२-४०).

  4. "Dadhiṣva." After the root "ḍudhāñ" (dhāraṇa-poṣaṇayoḥ — "to hold, to nourish"), in the "loṭ," ātmanepada, madhyama-puruṣa, ekavacana, the ending "thās" is taken; then थासः से (thāsaḥ se, पा. ३-४-८०), the "ṭ"-marker (ṭakāra-it)… Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Mandala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." As on p. 45, the grammar is characterized (compressed translation, every cited sūtra kept in three layers).

original p. 46

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.6 concluded; end of the Fifth Varga; Saṃhitā and Pada text of Rik 3.7

  1. "Dadhiṣva" continued from p. 45 In place of the "la"-ending ("loṭ") the ending "thās" is replaced by "se" by थासः से (thāsaḥ se, पा. ३-४-८०). Then by सवाभ्यां वामौ (savābhyāṃ vāmau, पा. ३-४-९१) — the "e" of the loṭ-ending, after "s" and "v," is replaced respectively by "va" and "am" — the "e" becomes "va": "dhā + sva." By छन्दस्युभयथा (chandasy ubhayathā, पा. ३-४-११७) — the affixes prescribed in the root-section carry, in the Veda, both labels, "sārvadhātuka" and "ārdhadhātuka" — both labels apply; taking first the "sārvadhātuka" label, by कर्तरि शप् (kartari śap, पा. ३-१-६८) the "śap" comes when a "sārvadhātuka" affix with agent-sense follows. Then जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः (juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, पा. २-४-७५) — after the roots of the "juhotyādi" group "śap" is elided (luk-like "ślu"). With "ślu," by श्लौ (ślau, पा. ६-१-१०) the root is doubled: "dhā-dhā + sva"; by ह्रस्वः (hrasvaḥ, पा. ७-४-५९) and अभ्यासे चर्च (abhyāse car ca, पा. ८-४-५४) the reduplicative syllable is shortened and its aspirate unaspirated ("da"): "da-dhā + sva." Now taking the "ārdhadhātuka" label, by आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ, पा. ७-२-३५) the augment "iṭ" is given to "sva": "dadhā + iṣva"; by आतो लोप इटि च (āto lopa iṭi ca, पा. ६-४-६४) — the "ā" is elided before an "ajādi" ārdhadhātuka or before "iṭ" — the "ā" drops; and by आदेशप्रत्यययोः (ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ, पा. ८-३-५९) the "s" becomes "ṣ": "dadhiṣva."

  2. "Canaḥ." "cāyater anne hrasvaś ca" — चायतेरन्ने ह्रस्वश्च (उ. सू. ४-६-३९ [as read from the print; see the note below]) — when the sense "anna" (food) is intended, the root "cāy" takes the affix "asun," the affix also takes the augment "nuṭ," and the "cā" is shortened. So with "asun," "nuṭ" and the shortening one gets "cay-an-"; and by लोपो व्योर्वलि (lopo vyor vali, पा. ६-१-६६) the "y" is elided, giving "canaḥ." ॥६॥ Reference note: the Uṇādi-sūtra number for "cāyater anne hrasvaś ca" is printed here as "4-6-39" (adhyāya-pāda-sūtra form), and on p. 43 as "4-199" (a running number): both are clear in the second scan; the print gives the sūtra in two numbering styles.

इल्लिगे ऐदनेय वर्गवु मुगिदुदु — illige aidaneya vargavu mugidudu — "Here the fifth varga is finished."

Sūkta 3, The Seventh Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ओमा॑सश्चर्षणीधृतो॒ विश्वे॑ देवास॒ आ ग॑त । दा॒श्वांसो॑ दा॒शुषः॑ सु॒तं ॥७॥

ómāsaścarṣaṇīdhṛto víśve devāsa ā́ gata | dāśvā́ṃso dāśúṣaḥ sutáṃ ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: in the Pada text, "carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ" is a compound; the print shows a small sign between "carṣaṇī" and "dhṛtaḥ" that is read as the avagraha-division, "carṣaṇī-dhṛtaḥ," but cannot be made out with certainty, so the word is given undivided. The sense-portion at the top is transcribed in full in three layers; the long technical accent-debate that follows is characterized, not transcribed line by line, per the standing convention for dense Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, and this is stated again at that point.

ओमासः । चर्षणीधृतः । विश्वे । देवासः । आ । गत । दाश्वांसः । दाशुषः । सुतम् ॥७॥

Sūkta 3, Seventh Mantra: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे विश्वे देवास एतन्नामका देवविशेषा दाशुषो हविर्दत्तवतो यजमानस्य सुतमभिषुतं सोमं प्रत्या गत । आगच्छत । ते च देवा ओमासो रक्षकाः चर्षणीधृतो मनुष्याणां धारका दाश्वांसः फलस्य दातारः । मनुष्या इत्यादिषु पञ्चविंशतिसंख्याकेषु मनुष्यनामसु चर्षणिशब्दः पठितः । अश्विनावित्यादिष्वेकत्रिंशत्संख्याकेषु देवविशेषनामसु विश्वे देवाः साध्या इति पठितम् । he viśve devāsa etan-nāmakā deva-viśeṣā dāśuṣo havir-dattavato yajamānasya sutam abhiṣutaṃ somaṃ pratyā gata | āgacchata | te ca devā omāso rakṣakāḥ carṣaṇīdhṛto manuṣyāṇāṃ dhārakā dāśvāṃsaḥ phalasya dātāraḥ | manuṣyā ity ādiṣu pañcaviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu manuṣya-nāmasu carṣaṇi-śabdaḥ paṭhitaḥ | aśvināv ity ādiṣv ekatriṃśat-saṃkhyākeṣu deva-viśeṣa-nāmasu viśve devāḥ sādhyā iti paṭhitam |

Translation: "O 'viśve devāsaḥ' — gods of this name, a special class of gods! Come ('pratyā gata' = 'āgacchata') to the Soma that has been pressed ('sutam' = 'abhiṣutam') of the sacrificer ('dāśuṣaḥ') who has given the oblation. And those gods are 'omāsaḥ' — protectors; 'carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ' — upholders of men; 'dāśvāṃsaḥ' — givers of the fruit. Among the twenty-five names of human beings beginning with 'manuṣyāḥ' (in the Nighaṇṭu), the word 'carṣaṇi' is read. Among the thirty-one names of particular classes of gods beginning with 'aśvinau,' 'viśve devāḥ' and 'sādhyāḥ' are read."

एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याख्यातवान् । अवितारो वावनीया वा मनुष्यधृतः सर्वे च देवा इहागच्छत दत्तवन्तो दत्तवतः सुतमिति तदेतदेकमेव वैश्वदेवं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते यत्तु किञ्चिद्बहुदैवतं तद्वैश्वदेवानां स्थाने युज्यते यदेव विश्वलिङ्गमिति शाकपूणिः । नि. १२-४० । इति । अत्र विश्वशब्दः सर्वशब्दपर्याय इति यास्कस्य मतम् । देवविशेषस्यैवासाधारणं लिङ्गमिति शाकपूणेर्मतम् । etām ṛcaṃ yāska evaṃ vyākhyātavān | avitāro vāvanīyā vā manuṣyadhṛtaḥ sarve ca devā ihāgacchata dattavanto dattavataḥ sutam iti tad etad ekam eva vaiśvadevaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate yat tu kiñcid bahudaivataṃ tad vaiśvadevānāṃ sthāne yujyate yad eva viśva-liṅgam iti śākapūṇiḥ | ni. 12-40 | iti | atra viśva-śabdaḥ sarva-śabda-paryāya iti yāskasya matam | deva-viśeṣasyaivāsādhāraṇaṃ liṅgam iti śākapūṇer matam |

Translation: "Yāska has explained this Ṛk thus: 'Protectors, or those to be desired, upholders of men; and all the gods, come here — having given, to the one who has given — the pressed (Soma). This is the one Vaiśvadeva Gāyatra tṛca found in the "daśatayī" (the ten-book arrangement of the Saṃhitā). Whatever hymn has many deities is fitted into the place of the Vaiśvadevas; indeed, "whatever bears the mark of viśva," says Śākapūṇi.' (Nirukta 12.40). Here, that the word 'viśva' is a synonym of 'sarva' (all) is Yāska's view; that it is the particular, uncommon mark of one class of gods is Śākapūṇi's view."

अवन्तीत्योमासो देवाः । मन्नित्यनुवृत्त्या अविसिविसिशुषिभ्यः कित् । उ. १-१४३ । इति मन्प्रत्ययः । ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च । पा. ६-४-२० । इत्यूट् । मनः कित्त्वेऽपि बाहुलकत्वाद्गुणः । आज्जसेरसुक् । पा. ७-१-५० । इति जसेरसुगागमः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । चर्षणयो मनुष्याः । तान्सृष्टि दानादिना धारयन्तीति चर्षणीधृतो देवाः । avanty ity omāso devāḥ | man ity anuvṛttyā avi-sivi-si-śuṣibhyaḥ kit | u. 1-143 | iti man-pratyayaḥ | jvara-tvara-srivyavi-mavām upadhāyāś ca | pā. 6-4-20 | ity ūṭ | manaḥ kittve 'pi bāhulakatvād guṇaḥ | āj-jaser asuk | pā. 7-1-50 | iti jaser asug-āgamaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | carṣaṇayo manuṣyāḥ | tān sṛṣṭi dānādinā dhārayantīti carṣaṇīdhṛto devāḥ |

Translation: "'Omāsaḥ' — the gods, because they 'protect' ('avanti'): by the continuing sense of 'man' (the Uṇādi-sūtra 'avi-sivi-si-śuṣibhyaḥ kit,' as read on p. 51; numbered in the print, Uṇ. 1-143) the affix 'man' is added; by 'jvara-tvara-srivi-avi-mavām upadhāyāś ca' (Pāṇini 6-4-20) the 'ūṭ' substitution comes; although 'man' is marked 'k' (which would normally bar guṇa), guṇa occurs, because of the Vedic variability ('bāhulaka'). By 'āj-jaser asuk' (Pāṇini 7-1-50) the augment 'asuk' comes to 'jas'; the first syllable is acute by the vocative rule. 'Carṣaṇayaḥ' means human beings; those (gods) who sustain them by creating, by giving and the like, are 'carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ.'" Reading notes: (i) the Uṇādi-number "1-143" is clear in the second scan; (ii) the word before "dānādinā" is printed "sṛṣṭi" (clear in the second scan), and the sense "by creating, by giving, etc." fits; (iii) the Uṇādi-sūtra's wording was first read here as "avi-si-vasi-śuṣibhyaḥ"; p. 51, which quotes it again, prints "avi sivi si śuṣibhyaḥ kit" and lists the roots as "av (rakṣaṇa), …, ṣiñ (bandhane), śuṣ (śoṣaṇe)," so the reading here has been adjusted to that.

॥ The technical accent-debate (characterized, not transcribed) ॥

The remainder of the page (about the last two-thirds) is a scholastic argument on the accent of the vocative words in this verse. I have read it through, but it is pure technical argument whose result does not alter the sense already given above, so, per convention, I summarize it rather than transcribing it line by line. Its course, in outline: Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Mandala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." The grammar at the top is characterized, not transcribed line by line, per the standing convention for dense Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; every sūtra cited is kept in all three layers. Numbers in small Kannada numerals are as read; [?] marks doubt.

  1. The rule and the objection. By the Pāṇinian rule "vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam" (विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् — vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣa-vacane bahuvacanam, पा. ८-१-७४): when an earlier vocative that is a general term is followed by a plural vocative that is a specific term, the earlier one is optionally not treated as "non-existent" (avidyamāna-vat), and so does not lose its accent — hence the preceding vocative here keeps its accent, as being "not a pāda-beginning" (apādādi) it would otherwise take nighāta. An objector asks how the nighāta can still occur (since the "subāmantrite parāṅgavat" rule would make the two words one unit, which would make the later word non-initial in the pāda); the answer given cites the Mahābhāṣya-line "vatkaraṇaṃ svāśrayam api yathā syāt" (वत्करणं स्वाश्रयमपि यथा स्यात् — vatkaraṇaṃ svāśrayam api yathā syāt, म. ८-१-७२ [as printed]), which lets nighāta apply even in a pada-division case, and the rule "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (अनुदात्तं पदमेकवर्जम् — anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam) which ensures nighāta all the more.
  2. A parallel case. A second objection, "dravatpāṇī śubhaspatī" (द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती — a Ṛgvedic phrase used as an example of an unaccented second word), is answered by saying that there the "parāṅgavad-bhāva" is blocked by the rule that says an earlier word, when a vocative follows, is treated as non-existent ("āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat"); here, by contrast, the rule 8-1-74 forbids treating the earlier vocative as non-existent, so the earlier vocative "has existence" and "parāṅgavattva" is accepted.
  3. "Viśve" and "devāsaḥ." "Viśve" has the first-syllable acute because it stands at the beginning of the pāda. Here "viśva" is the name of a gaṇa-devatā (a particular class of deities, the Viśvedevāḥ), not a synonym of "sarva"; being a qualifier that points to a specific noun (viśeṣya), it is a general term in the sense of the rule, and so it does not stand in apposition (sāmānādhikaraṇya) with "omāsaḥ." (If it did, then, the earlier pāda being treated as part of the following word, "mitrāvaruṇau ṛtāvṛdhau"-type examples show the vocative-acute would not occur.) "Devāsaḥ" is the word qualified by "viśve."
  4. "Devāḥ" as a conventional vs. etymological word. "Devāḥ" means "those who shine" (from "div," to shine). An objector cites the Paribhāṣā "nanv avayava-prasiddheḥ samudāya-prasiddhir balīyasī" (नन्ववयवप्रसिद्धेः समुदायप्रसिद्धिर्बलीयसी — nanv avayava-prasiddheḥ samudāya-prasiddhir balīyasī, परि. ९८): "the established whole-word sense is stronger than the sense of its parts," so that the conventional (rūḍha) sense of "deva," not the etymological (yaugika) one, is to be taken; for if the etymological sense were taken, understanding would be delayed by the effort of tracing the parts. The reply begins "samudāya-prasiddhau tu na vikṣepa iti cet na — samudāya-…" and continues on the next page.
original p. 48

Rik 3.7: close of the Bhāṣya's accent-debate and grammar; Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topic

The accent-debate concluded continuing from p. 47, where the objector argued that the conventional (rūḍha) sense of "deva" should be taken, not the etymological "shining one". The reply begins: "when the conventional whole-word sense is the established one, the word 'deva' is a general term and not a specific one, so the condition 'viśeṣa-vacane' is not met; and since the optional rule 'vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣa-vacane bahuvacanam' (8-1-74) does not prohibit it, 'viśve' would be treated as non-existent (avidyamāna-vat), and, like the pair of words 'śubhaspatī,' 'devāsaḥ' would also have first-syllable acute. By the evidence of the accent, then, taking the etymological sense of 'deva,' even at the cost of dropping the conventional one, is perfectly proper." That is the end of the debate; the Bhāṣya's conclusion is that the etymological sense, "those who shine," is the one to be taken.

Remaining word-grammar of the Bhāṣya for Rik 3.7 characterized:

  • "Ā gata" (= "āgacchata"): by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (बहुलं छन्दसि — bahulaṃ chandasi) the "śap" is elided (luk); and the "m" of the root "gam" is dropped under the rule that begins "anudāttopadeśa-…" (अनुदात्तोपदेश… — anudāttopadeśa-…); the word, standing after another word, takes nighāta (loss of accent) — the print here reads "ājaḥ padāt-paratvān nighātaḥ" (clear in the second scan; "ājaḥ" is as printed).
  • "Dāśvāṃsaḥ" (root "dāś" to give): the participial affix "kvasu" is added; by दाश्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्च (dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca, पा. ६-१-१२) the form is a nipātana (irregular formation), so the "iṭ" augment and the doubling that the "kādi-niyama" rule (the rule that restricts "iṭ" to the roots "kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ, stu, dru, śru" — पा. ७-२-१३) would otherwise bring do not occur. By the affix-accent, "kvasu" is acute.
  • "Dāśuṣaḥ": वसोः संप्रसारणम् (vasoḥ samprasāraṇam, पा. ६-४-१३१) — "samprasāraṇa" (the semivowel is replaced by its vowel) for "vasu"; then संप्रसारणाच्च (samprasāraṇāc ca, पा. ६-१-१०८) — the former form (pūrvarūpa) results; and आदेशप्रत्यययोः (ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ, पा. ८-३-५९) — "s" becomes "ṣ." ॥७॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ओमासः (omāsaḥ) — protectors | चर्षणीधृतः (carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ) — those who bear (or nourish) human beings | दाश्वांसः (dāśvāṃsaḥ) — (O you) who give the fruit of the sacrifice | (हे) विश्वे देवासः (he viśve devāsaḥ) — O you who are called the Viśvedevas | दाशुषः (dāśuṣaḥ) — of the sacrificer who gives the oblation | सुतम् (sutam) — the Soma pressed out and made ready (in order to drink it) | आ गत (ā gata) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Viśvedevas! You are the protectors of men (or of those who are fit to perform sacrifice), and the givers of fruit to the sacrificial rites, the nourishers of men. Such as you are, come here, in order to drink the Soma-juice that the sacrificer has prepared for you.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O Viswe devas, protectors and supporters of men, bestowers of rewards come to (drink) the libation of Soma juice of the worshipper."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

From here on, the next three Ṛks are named the "Vaiśvadeva-tṛca" (the triplet addressed to the Viśvedevas). These Ṛks are recited in the Abhijit-savana. And in the sacrifice called Cāturmāsya, on the day on which the Soma-juice is drawn out, the Adhvaryu recites these mantras while he draws out the Soma, with a large wooden vessel called the droṇa-kalaśa. Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The English glosses on the verses are editorial; the source gives none. Reference-numbers are in small Kannada numerals and read with [?] where uncertain.

original p. 49

Special topics on Rik 3.7: "omāsaḥ," "carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ," "viśve devāsaḥ" (opening)

ओमासः (omāsaḥ) — Vocative plural. The word means "protectors, helpers." The word is not used anywhere else in the Ṛgveda.

चर्षणीधृतः (carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ) — The word "carṣaṇī" is read among the twenty-five words that denote "human being" (Nighaṇṭu 2-3). Examples:

य एकश्चर्षणीनां वसूनामिरज्यसि । (ऋ. सं. १-७-९) ya ekaś carṣaṇīnāṃ vasūnām irajyasi | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-7-9) Gloss: "Who alone, of the peoples, of the goods, rules." (The print has "irajyasi," as I read it.)

धर्त्तारा चर्षणीनाम् । (ऋ. सं. १-१७-२) dhartārā carṣaṇīnām | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-17-2) Gloss: "The two upholders of the peoples."

सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनामरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-३२-१५) sedu rājā kṣayati carṣaṇīnām arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-32-15) Gloss: "He alone rules as king over the peoples; as the felly encloses the spokes, he has encompassed them all."

In these Ṛks and others the Bhāṣyakāra and the other commentators have explained "carṣaṇīnām" as "men." Monier Williams holds that "carṣaṇī" derives from the root "kṛṣ" (to plough, to practise agriculture), so that "carṣaṇī" means "those who plough, people who practise agriculture"; this sense, too, seems well-formed. Other Western scholars, in rendering it, use the words "Man, people, race, stock, tribe." In contexts where the word is used as an adjective, they say it has the sense "hastening, brisk, active." Griffith says that since the word comes from the root "car" (to move about), the word "carṣaṇī" signifies "Living beings" (prāṇigaḷu). Many hold the view that, since the Āryas of the Ṛgvedic age were occupied in agriculture, the sense "Cultivating people" is the fitting one. Since the root "dhṛ" has the senses "to hold, to support, to nourish," there is no need for doubt in explaining "carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ" as "those worthy to nourish men, worthy to protect them."

विश्वे देवासः (viśve devāsaḥ) — Among the thirty-one names of the particular classes of deities, beginning with "aśvinau," the name of these deities is read. The Bhāṣyakāra says that they are a distinct, particular class of gods. Some say that they are all the gods. But that the sages worshipped distinct deities named "Viśvedevas" can be stated clearly from what is found in other sūktas. On this question Yāska has written an explanation of this Ṛk:

अवितारो वावनीया वा मनुष्यधृतः सर्वे देवा इहागच्छत दत्तवन्तो दत्तवतः सुतमिति, तदेतदेकमेव वैश्वदेवं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते यत्तु किञ्चिद्बहुदैवतं तद्वैश्वदेवानां स्थाने युज्यते यदेव विश्वलिङ्गमिति शाकपूणिः । (नि. १२-४०) avitāro vāvanīyā vā manuṣyadhṛtaḥ sarve devā ihāgacchata dattavanto dattavataḥ sutam iti, tad etad ekam eva vaiśvadevaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate yat tu kiñcid bahudaivataṃ tad vaiśvadevānāṃ sthāne yujyate yad eva viśva-liṅgam iti śākapūṇiḥ | (ni. 12-40) (Translated on p. 47 above: "Protectors or those to be desired, upholders of men; all the gods, come here … this one Vaiśvadeva Gāyatra tṛca in the daśatayī; whatever many-deitied hymn is fitted into the Vaiśvadevas' place, whatever bears the mark of 'viśva' — so says Śākapūṇi.")

In the discussion of the sense of this Ṛk there is no difference between the sense we have given and Yāska's. But according to Yāska's view "viśve devāḥ" means "all the gods," and "Viśvedevas" — gods called by that name — is, he says, the view of Śākapūṇi… Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Mandala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." This page of the Kannada commentary is full of counts and reference-numbers printed in small Kannada numerals. Many of them are hard to read; the numbers below were re-read in the second scan (one, the Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā range 33-4? to 4?, is still doubtful); they should still be checked against the page before being relied on. The English phrases within the Kannada are printed in English in the source, and are reproduced as printed, with misprints marked [sic].

original p. 50

Special topics on Rik 3.7 (continued): the Viśvedevas; "ā gata," "dāśvāṃsaḥ," "dāśuṣaḥ"

Continuing from p. 49: …"…the view of Śākapūṇi," Yāska himself says. Hence it can be said with confidence that, even in his own time, there was a difference of opinion on this question. Now, if it is said that the Viśvedevas are (as is established practice in the domestic and other rites) not part of the group of ordinary deities, and are a special group of thirteen persons of their own, that too can be understood. Be that as it may, it seems proper to say that the Viśvedevas who are described in the Ṛgveda belong to a group of distinct, particular deities.

आ गत (ā gata) — Second person plural. In present-day Sanskrit this would be "āgacchata."

दाश्वांसः (dāśvāṃsaḥ) — This word, formed from the root "dāś" ("dāśṛ dāne," to give), means "those who give," that is, "those who give the fruit to the men who praise them." Western scholars explain the word with: "Donors, distributors, bestowers of riches," and the like.

दाशुषः (dāśuṣaḥ) — This word is genitive singular: "of one who gives (the oblation to the gods)," or "who is giving." It is formed like the word "dāśvāṃsaḥ." The sense given for it by Western scholars is: "Of the distributors (Ludwig, Benfey), of the worshipper (Rosen, Griffith, Williams), of the offerers" and the like the source's English: "of tne [sic] worshipper".

On the Viśvedevas. Here it is necessary to state a few main points about the Viśvedevas. Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." As on p. 50, the references and counts in small Kannada numerals were re-read in the second scan; the Śatapatha, Nirukta and Bṛhaddevatā numbers are still marked [?] because the Kannada digits 2/3/7 are hard to tell apart; they must be re-checked against the page before being relied on.

  • In the Ṛgveda there are 63 sūktas that praise the Viśvedevas alone.
  • In addition, the first 41 Ṛks of the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164 (second scan; the digits are small, but 1-164 with its first 41 Ṛks is the Viśvedeva portion of the Dīrghatamas hymn) are devoted to the Viśvedevas.
  • In all these — apart from the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-125 — in all the other sūktas, many deities are praised; that is, just as in other sūktas, Agni, Indra and the others are praised, and further, trees, rivers, mountains, cows, horses and the like are also celebrated.
  • Besides these, in sūktas devoted to other deities, there are altogether about 17 Ṛks here and there that are devoted to the Viśvedevas. In all these places the Viśvedevas themselves are stated to be the deities of those Ṛks.
  • And in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-125-1, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are joined with the Viśvedevas.
  • In Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) 2-22, Indra is prayed to come together with the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Maruts and the Viśvedevas. In the same Saṃhitā, in the mantras 33-45 to 47, Indra, Vāyu and other gods are praised along with the Viśvedevas.
  • In the Atharvaveda 20-62-6 the Viśvedevas are referred to in the singular; and many sūktas devoted to the Viśvedevas are found in the Atharvaveda.
  • In the Brāhmaṇas also the name of the Viśvedevas is mentioned in places. In the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa (8-14) and in the mantras 1-20 of the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa, all the deities are given the name "Viśvedevas"…
original p. 51

The Viśvedevas (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.7 begins

Continuing from p. 50: …"…and from that very word they are addressed (in the vocative)." In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (3-9-2-6) the Viśvedevas are called the rays of the Sun; in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (14-2-2-37) they are called the vital airs and the like; in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (7-1-1-42) they are called the sacrificial rites; in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (2-4-4-13) they are called Indra and Agni. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 5-1-6), Indra and Agni are praised together with the Viśvedevas.

In some of the Purāṇas the Viśvedevas are said to be the presiding deities of the directions. In the Nirukta (Ni. 12-39) "Viśvedevas" is said to mean all the gods. Durgācārya, the commentator of the Nirukta, explains "Viśvedevas" as the rays of the Sun. Besides stating his own view that "Viśvedevas" means all the deities, Yāska also reports the view of Śākapūṇi. Śaunaka, speaking of the Viśvedevas in his work Bṛhaddevatā (Bṛ. De. 2-128 to 134), says that Yāska and Śāṇḍilya hold that "Viśvedevāḥ" means all the deities; Śaunaka's own view is the same.

Sāyaṇācārya, in explaining this Ṛk, has stated his own view that the Viśvedevas are the thirty-one groups of gods, beginning with the Aśvins, who, taken together, are called "Viśvedevas."

Among Western scholars, Langlois, Kaegi and Hopkins hold that "Viśvedevas" means all the deities; Wilson, Griffith and Macdonell accept both senses: "all the deities," and "a distinct group of deities named Viśvedevas."

The main conclusion. In earlier times — that is, in very ancient times — the sense "all the deities" was the established sense of "Viśvedevas"; in the course of time it came into use to understand "Viśvedevas" as the name of a distinct group of deities. In many Brāhmaṇas and in the Purāṇas the Viśvedevas are indicated as one distinct group of deities. But from Yāska's own Nirukta it is evident that there was a difference of opinion on this matter even in Yāska's time.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

"Avanti iti omāsaḥ" — because they protect, the gods are called "omāsaḥ." By the Uṇādi-sūtra "अवि सिवि सि शुषिभ्यः कित्" (avi sivi si śuṣibhyaḥ kit, उ. सू. १-१४१), after the roots "av" (to protect, etc.), "sivu" [print: "pivu"] (to sew, to weave together), "ṣiñ" (to bind) and "śuṣ" (to dry up) — roots which the print lists as "pivu tantu saṃtāne," "ṣiñ bandhane," "śuṣa śoṣaṇe" — the affix "man" comes, and it is "k"-marked (kit); so after the root "av," the affix "man"… Source pages 52 (even: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3"), 53 (odd: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6") and 54 (even). These three pages are pure Pāṇinian grammar in Kannada prose: the Kannada rendering of the derivations and the accent-debate that Sāyaṇa gave in Sanskrit on pp. 47–48. Per the standing convention they are characterized in order rather than translated line by line; every sūtra cited is kept in three layers, with its number as printed (small Kannada numerals, read with care but not independently re-verified). Nothing in them alters the sense of the Rik given on p. 48.

original pp. 52–54

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.7 (Kannada), concluded; Saṃhitā and Pada text of Rik 3.8

p. 52 — "omāsaḥ," "carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ," and the first stage of the accent-debate. - "Omāsaḥ" (from "av," to protect): the affix "man" comes, and though "man" is "k"-marked (which would bar guṇa), guṇa and "ūṭ" apply — by ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च (jvara-tvara-srivyavi-mavām upadhāyāś ca, पा. ६-४-२०) the penultimate of the roots "jvar," "tvar," "sriv," "av," "mav" is replaced by "ūṭ" (also "kvi," "jhal" affixes), and the guṇa follows by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, पा. ७-१-८४ [as printed]). Then आज्जसेरसुक् (āj-jaser asuk, पा. ७-१-५०) gives "omāsas"; the vocative is acute on its first syllable; hence "omāsaḥ." - "Carṣaṇayaḥ" = human beings; the gods "support them (by giving rain and the like)," hence "carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ." - The accent-debate (Kannada rendering of Sanskrit pp. 47–48). "Omāsaḥ" is an earlier vocative, a general term; by विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् (vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣa-vacane bahuvacanam, पा. ८-१-७४) it optionally escapes being treated as non-existent. If it is not treated as non-existent, "omāsaḥ" is not accented as a pāda-initial and takes the eighth-chapter vocative-grave (aṣṭamika anudātta); the discussion then compares सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवत्स्वरे (subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare, पा. २-१-२), the Mahābhāṣya rule "vatkaraṇaṃ svāśrayam api yathā syāt" (वत्करणं स्वाश्रयमपि यथा स्यात् — पा. म. ८-१-७२ [as printed]), अनुदात्तं पदमेकवर्जम् (anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam, पा. ६-१-१५८) and the parallel example "dravatpāṇī śubhaspatī" (द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती), exactly as in the Sanskrit on p. 47. Each time the point is that "parāṅgavad-bhāva" (treating the earlier vocative as part of the following word) applies only where the two words are semantically connected (समर्थः पदविधिः, samarthaḥ pada-vidhiḥ, पा. २-१-१). - The page ends in the middle of the argument over "viśve" and "devāsaḥ" ("…in the case of apposition, how would the second pāda-initial 'ṛtāvṛdhau' (in the "mitrāvaruṇau ṛtāvṛdhau" kind of example) get the acute…").

p. 53 — the argument concluded; "devāsaḥ," "ā gata," "dāśvāṃsaḥ." - If there is no apposition (sāmānādhikaraṇya), the prohibition in नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम् (nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānya-vacanam, पा. ८-१-७३) does not apply, so by आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat, पा. ८-१-७२) the earlier vocative is treated as non-existent, and "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" does not apply; hence "viśve" keeps its pāda-initial accent and is acute, with no aṣṭamika-anudātta. "Devāsaḥ" is the qualifier of "viśve," from "divyanti iti devāḥ" ("those who shine"). The earlier objection — that, by the Paribhāṣā "avayava-śakteḥ samudāya-śaktir balīyasī" (परि. ९८), the conventional sense of "deva" should override the etymological one — is answered by saying that if the conventional sense were taken, "deva" would be a general term, and "viśve" could not be given its distinct-class sense; the paribhāṣā rests, the print says, on a maxim about the "delayed understanding" (viḷambita-dhī) that the etymological sense would cause [the maxim's wording is unclear in the print, so I do not quote it]. The conclusion stated: the etymological sense ("shining ones") is to be taken here. "Devāsaḥ" gets its "-asaḥ" by आज्जसेरसुक् (āj-jaser asuk, पा. ७-१-५०). - "Ā gata" (= "āgacchata"): from "ā" + "gam"; the imperative second-person-plural ending "tha" is replaced by "ta" by तस्थस्थमिपां तां तं तामः (tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ, पा. ४-१-१ [as printed]); "śap" by कर्तरि शप् (kartari śap, पा. ६-१-६८ [as printed]) is elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (bahulaṃ chandasi, पा. २-४-७३); the "m" of "gam" is dropped by अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति (anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanotyādīnām anunāsika-lopo jhali kṅiti, पा. ६-४-३७) → "gata"; since "ā" is a particle placed before it, "gata" takes nighāta (loss of accent) as a word following another. - "Dāśvāṃsaḥ": root "dāś" (to give); the participle-affix "kvasu"; by आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ, पा. ७-२-३५) the "iṭ" would come to the "vasu" (a "val"-initial affix), but the "kṛ-sṛ-bhṛ-vṛ-stu-dru-śru" group-rule कृसृभृवृस्तुद्रुश्रुवो लिटि (kṛ-sṛ-bhṛ-vṛ-stu-dru-śru-vo liṭi, पा. ७-२-१३) restricts "iṭ" in the "liṭ" to those roots, and "dāś" is not among them… continues p. 54 Printed references on this page, in order (Oct 2026 numeral pass): Pā. 8-1-73; 8-1-72; 8-1-74; 7-1-50; 4-1-1 [as printed]; 6-1-68 [as printed]; 2-4-73; 6-4-37; 0-2-107 [as printed] (kvasuś ca); 7-2-35; 7-2-8 (neḍ vaśi kṛti); 7-2-13.

p. 54 — "dāśvāṃsaḥ" concluded; "dāśuṣe." continuing …so "iṭ" does not occur; but since Pāṇini's own दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्च (dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca, पा. ६-१-१२) states these forms irregularly (nipātana), "iṭ" does not arise; and from the same statement the doubling prescribed by लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य (liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya, पा. ६-१-८) is also not made (the sūtra is "irregular" with "dāś" described as a root with two syllables…). By the affix-accent "kvasu" is acute. Then the form "dāśuṣe" is derived [the print continues with "dāśuṣe" here, as the dative of "dāśvas"; the Rik has "dāśuṣaḥ," but the derivation is the same]: after "kvasu," the dative singular affix "e" gives "dāśvas + e"; वसोः संप्रसारणम् (vasoḥ samprasāraṇam, पा. ६-४-१३१) — "samprasāraṇa" for "vasu," since it ends in "vas" and is in "bha" (the stem-class before affixes that begin with a vowel, by यचि भम् yaci bham, पा. १-४-१८): the vowels "i, u, ṛ, ḷ" replacing "y, v, r, l" are named "samprasāraṇa" (इग्यणः संप्रसारणम्, ig-yaṇaḥ samprasāraṇam, पा. १-१-४५); then संप्रसारणाच्च (samprasāraṇāc ca, पा. ६-१-१०८) gives the single former form ("pūrvarūpa"): "dāś + us + e"; and आदेशप्रत्यययोः (ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ, पा. ८-३-५९) turns the "s" into "ṣ": "dāśuṣe." ॥७॥

Sūkta 3, The Eighth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒प्तुरः॑ सु॒तमा गं॑त॒ तूर्ण॑यः । उ॒स्रा इ॑व॒ स्वस॑राणि ॥८॥

víśve devā́so aptúraḥ sutámā́ gaṃta tū́rṇayaḥ | usrā́ iva svásarāṇi ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: in the Pada text the print shows a small dividing sign inside "apturaḥ" (read as "ap-turaḥ") and between "usrā" and "iva"; The words are given undivided. विश्वे । देवासः । अप्तुरः । सुतम् । आ । गन्त । तूर्णयः । उस्रा इव । स्वसराणि ॥८॥

original p. 55

Sūkta 3, Eighth Mantra: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विश्वे देवास एतन्नामकगणरूपा देवविशेषाः सुतं सोममा गन्त । आगच्छन्तु । कीदृशाः । अप्तुरः । तत्तत्काले वृष्टिप्रदा इत्यर्थः । तूर्णयः त्वरायुक्ताः । यजमानमनुग्रहीतुमालस्यरहिता इत्यर्थः । विश्वेषां देवानां सोमं प्रत्यागमने उस्रा इत्यादि दृष्टान्तः । उस्राः सूर्यरश्मयः स्वसराण्यहानि प्रत्यालस्यरहिता यथा समागच्छन्ति तद्वत् । viśve devāsa etan-nāmaka-gaṇa-rūpā deva-viśeṣāḥ sutaṃ somam ā gantā | āgacchantu | kīdṛśāḥ | aptuaḥ [sic: apturaḥ] | tat-tat-kāle vṛṣṭi-pradā ity arthaḥ | tūrṇayaḥ tvarā-yuktāḥ | yajamānam anugrahītum ālasya-rahitā ity arthaḥ | viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ somaṃ pratyāgamane usrā ity ādi dṛṣṭāntaḥ | usrāḥ sūrya-raśmayaḥ svasarāṇy ahāni pratyālasya-rahitā yathā samāgacchanti tad-vat |

Translation: "'Viśve devāsaḥ' — the particular class of gods, in the form of a group of that name — come to the pressed Soma. Let them come ('āgacchantu'). What kind are they? 'Apturaḥ' — givers of rain at the proper times. 'Tūrṇayaḥ' — full of haste, that is, free from sloth in order to favour the sacrificer. The words beginning 'usrā iva' give an illustration for the coming of all the gods to the Soma: just as 'usrāḥ' — the rays of the Sun — come each day without sloth to 'svasarāṇi,' the days, so (the gods come)." Correction to the IAST above: the Rik's word is "apturaḥ" — the stray "aptuaḥ" in the line is a slip in the transliteration, not a variant reading.

खेदये इत्यादिषु पञ्चदशसु रश्मिनामसु उस्रा वसव इति पठितम् । वस्तोरित्यादिषु द्वादशसु अहर्नामसु स्वसराणि घ्रंसो घर्म इति पठितम् । तच्छब्दं पदं यास्केन व्याख्यातम् । स्वसराण्यहानि भवन्ति स्वयंसारीण्यपि वा स्वरादित्यो भवति स एतानि सारयति । उस्रा इव स्वसराणीत्यपि निगमो भवति । नि. ५-४ । इति ॥ khedaye ity ādiṣu pañcadaśasu raśmi-nāmasu usrā vasava iti paṭhitam | vastor ity ādiṣu dvādaśasu ahar-nāmasu svasarāṇi ghraṃso gharma iti paṭhitam | tac-chabdaṃ padaṃ yāskena vyākhyātam | svasarāṇy ahāni bhavanti svayaṃ-sārīṇy api vā svar āditya bhavati sa etāni sārayati | usrā iva svasarāṇīty api nigamo bhavati | ni. 5-4 | iti ||

Translation: "Among the fifteen names for 'rays,' beginning with 'khedaye', 'usrāḥ' and 'vasavaḥ' are read; among the twelve names for 'day,' beginning with 'vastoḥ,' 'svasarāṇi,' 'ghraṃsaḥ' and 'gharma' are read. Yāska has explained that word: 'Svasarāṇi are the days — or those that move of themselves; or the Sun is "svar," and he makes these go.' And 'usrā iva svasarāṇi' is also a Vedic quotation (Nirukta [numbers read 5-4 ?])."

॥ Grammar within the Bhāṣya ॥ "Devāsaḥ": formed with the "ac" affix of the "pacādi" class, which is "c"-marked, so the last syllable is acute (पचाद्यच्, pacādy ac; पा. ३-१-१३४). "Apturaḥ": from the root "tur" (to hasten) with the "śluu" (reduplicating) stem, with "kvip" in the sense "those who speed [the rain]," and the preceding word's own accent retained as it is a "gati/kāraka/upapada"-first compound. "Ā ganta": the second-person-plural form used for the third (by vyatyaya), "śap" elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (bahulaṃ chandasi), the ending replaced by "ta" by तस्य तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (tasya tap-tanap-tanathanāś ca, पा. ७-१-४५), the "p"-marked "tap" being non-"ṅit" so that the loss of the nasal does not occur, and nighāta by "tiṅ atiṅaḥ." "Tūrṇayaḥ": root "tvar" (to be agitated), Uṇādi affix "ni[t]" in the list "vahi-śri-śru-yu-dru-glāhā-tvaribhyo ni(t)" (उ. ४-५१); "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute. "Usrā iva": with "iva" the case-ending is not dropped (the compound-rule with its vārttika, पा. २-१-४, with the vārttika as printed "२-१-४-२"), the preceding word keeps its natural accent (पा. ६-२-१, "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam"). "Svasarāṇi": "saratīti saraḥ sūryaḥ" — "sara" is the Sun (root "sṛ," with "ac"); "svaḥ saro yeṣām tāni svasarāṇi ahāni" — the days of which the Sun is the mover — a bahuvrīhi, with the first member "svar" acute by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (पा. ६-२-१).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अप्तुरः (apturaḥ) — givers of rain (those who give rain) | (हे) विश्वे देवासः (he viśve devāsaḥ) — O Viśvedevas | उस्रा इव स्वसराणि (usrā iva svasarāṇi) — as the rays of the Sun reach (us) in the daytime | सुतम् (sutam) — the Soma-juice that has been prepared (for you to drink) | तूर्णयः (tūrṇayaḥ) — those who are speedy (swiftly, quickly) | आ गन्त (ā ganta) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Viśvedevas! You are the givers of rain — that is, you cause the rain to fall. The Soma-juice has been prepared for you. To drink it, come quickly, as the rays of the Sun, at daytime (as soon as the sun has risen), come and reach us. Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." English passages are as printed in the source. Reference-numbers are in small Kannada numerals; where uncertain. Glosses on the verses are editorial.

original p. 56

English rendering of Rik 3.8; Special topics: "apturaḥ," "sutam," "tūrṇayaḥ"

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"May Visvedevas, givers of rain, swift in action, come to the libation (of soma juice) as the (sun's) rays (come) to the days."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अप्तुरः (apturaḥ) — The Bhāṣyakāra and Skandasvāmī both explain this as "vṛṣṭi-pradāḥ" — that is, "those who give rain." Among Western scholars, for this word: "Gloss" [as printed; I take it to be a scholar's name rendered thus] — "Stepping over an expanse of water, commanding over water, overcoming all difficulty"; Griffith — "active, pushing, hardworking"; Ludwig — "Securer of rains, Active, quick, swift"; Williams — "shedder of rains"; Rosen — "rich in rains"; Benfey — "worthy, active, diligent." This word "apturaḥ" is used not only of the Viśvedevas but also of other deities — the Aśvins, Indra, Agni, Pavamāna-Soma and others:

For the Aśvins: ये अप्तुरो दिव्यासो न गृध्रा अभि प्रयो नासत्या वहन्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११८-४) ye apturo divyāso na gṛdhrā abhi prayo nāsatyā vahanti || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-118-4) Gloss: "Those (horses) that are rain-bringers, like heavenly vultures, carry the Nāsatyas to the offering."

For Indra: यज्ञेन गातुमप्तुरो विविद्रिरे धियो हिन्वाना उशिजो मनीषिणः ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-२१-५ तथा ३-५१-२) yajñena gātum apturo vividrire dhiyo hinvānā uśijo manīṣiṇaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 2-21-5 and 3-51-2) Gloss: "By sacrifice the active, wise, eager singers found the path, stirring their thoughts."

For Pavamāna-Soma: इन्द्रं वर्धन्तो अप्तुरः कृण्वन्तो विश्वमार्यम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-६३-५; ९-६१-१३; ९-६३-२१; ९-१०८-७) indraṃ vardhanto apturaḥ kṛṇvanto viśvam āryam || (ṛ. saṃ. 9-63-5; 9-61-13; 9-63-21; 9-108-7) Gloss: "Strengthening Indra, the swift ones, making the whole world noble (Āryan)."

For Agni: अग्निं यन्तुरमप्तुरमृतस्य योगे वनुषः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-२७-११) इत्यादि agniṃ yanturam apturam ṛtasya yoge vanuṣaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-27-11) ity ādi Gloss: "Agni, the controller, the rain-giver, at the yoking of the Order, to the one who honours." [tentative]

सुतम् (sutam) — "Pressed with stones, crushed, the juice squeezed out and filtered so as to be fit for drinking." Along with it the word "somam" sometimes occurs and sometimes does not; in both cases the sense is the Soma-juice.

तूर्णयः (tūrṇayaḥ) — "Tvaramāṇāḥ" — hastening, vigilant, quick: the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "those who come quickly, without sloth, to give the fruit of the sacrifice to the sacrificer." Western scholars too, in various words — "speedy, diligently, hastily, quickly, swift, quick in work" — accept the Bhāṣyakāra's sense. Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā."

original p. 57

Special topics: "usrā iva," "svasarāṇi"; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.8 begins

उस्रा इव (usrā iva) and स्वसराणि (svasarāṇi) — The word "usrā" is read among the fifteen words that denote rays (Nighaṇṭu 2-15), and, in the sense "cows," among the nine words (Nighaṇṭu 3-9); and the word "svasarāṇi" is read among the twelve words that denote "day," and also among the twenty-two names that denote "house." Hence, for the illustrative sentence "usrā iva svasarāṇi," besides the sense the Bhāṣyakāra gives, one may also render it "as cows go to their own homes." Both Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava give both kinds of meaning. Western scholars too explain "svasarāṇi" by "day, cowshed, stall, abode, grazing" and similar words English as printed in the source. The word "svasarāṇi" is used in the Ṛks 1-34-8; 2-19-2; 2-34-5; 3-60-6.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept "Devāsaḥ": by नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः (nandi-grahi-pacādibhyo lyu-ṇiny-acaḥ, पा. ३-१-१३४) the affix "ac" comes after the "pacādi" root "div"; in the nominative plural "āj-jaser asuk" (पा. ७-१-५०) gives the augment "asuk"; the "ac" affix being "c"-marked, the last syllable is acute by चितः (citaḥ, पा. ६-१-१६३). "Apturaḥ": the root "tur" (to hasten) is in the "juhotyādi" group, taking "ślu"; "apaḥ tuturti" — "they make the waters hasten," i.e., cause rain at the proper times; with this intended sense, "kvip" is added after "tur" by क्विप् च (kvip ca, पा. ३-२-७६), all of whose letters are then elided; with "jas" the form "apturaḥ" results; the accent of the second member of the kṛt-compound is retained by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt, पा. ६-२-१३९). "Ā ganta" (= "āgacchantu"): the second-person-plural "tha" stands for the third (vyatyaya); "tha" becomes "ta" by तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्तामः (tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ, पा. ३-४-१०१); the "śap" is elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (bahulaṃ chandasi); "ta" becomes "tap" (तस्य तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च, tasya tap-tanap-tanathanāś ca, पा. ७-१-४५); since "tap" is "p"-marked, the "sārvadhātuka" is not "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, sārvadhātukam apit, पा. १-२-४), so the nasal "m" of "gam" is not elided (अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति, पा. ६-४-३७), and by नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि (naś cāpadāntasya jhali, पा. ८-३-२४) the "n/m" not at the end of a word before a "jhal" becomes anusvāra, which by अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः (anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ, पा. ८-४-५८) takes the nasal of the following consonant's class… Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." The grammar at the top is the Kannada rendering of what Sanskrit p. 55 already gave; characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 58

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.8 concluded; Sūkta 3, Ninth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, and the opening of the Bhāṣya

The grammar of Rik 3.8 concluded continuing from p. 57: "…by अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः (anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ, पा. ८-४-५८) the anusvāra takes the nasal of the class of the following letter — 'n' — giving 'ā gan-ta'; here तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८; the print has १८-१-२८) gives the unaccented form." "Tūrṇayaḥ" (from "tvar"): by the Uṇādi-sūtra वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो णित् (vahi-śri-śru-yu-dru-glā-hā-tvaribhyo ṇit, उ. सू. ४-४-९१ [as printed]) — roots "vah" (to carry), "śriñ" (to serve), "śru" (to hear), "yu" (to mix), "dru" (to go), "glai" (to wither), "ohāk" (to go), "tvarā" (to be agitated) — the affix "ṇi" is added, and it is "nitya"; from "tvarā saṃbhrame" we get "tvar + ṇi"; by ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च (jvara-tvara-srivyavi-mavām upadhāyāś ca, पा. ६-४-२०) "ūṭ" appears and the affix's "n" becomes "ṇ" by रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे (raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samāna-pade, पा. ८-४-१) → "tūrṇi"; being "ṇ"-marked the first syllable is acute; the nominative plural gives "tūrṇayaḥ." "Usrā iva": by "ivena saha nitya-samāso vibhakty-alopaḥ pūrva-pada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ ca" (इवेन सह नित्यसमासो विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च — पा. २-१-४ वा. २ [as printed]) the compound is obligatory, the case-ending is not dropped, and the first member keeps its natural accent. "Svasarāṇi": "saratīti saraḥ sūryaḥ" — "sara" is the Sun ('sṛ,' to go, with "ac" of the pacādi class); "svaḥ saro yeṣāṃ tāni svasarāṇy ahāni" — days of which the Sun is the mover; in this bahuvrīhi, by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, पा. ६-२-१) the first member keeps its accent; hence "sva" is acute on its first syllable. ॥८॥

Sūkta 3, The Ninth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒स्रिध॒ एहि॑मायासो अ॒द्रुहः॑ । मेधं॑ जुषंत॒ वह्न॑यः ॥९॥

víśve devā́so asrídha éhimāyāso adrúhaḥ | médhaṃ juṣaṃta váhnayaḥ ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वे । देवासः । अस्रिधः । एहिमायासः । अद्रुहः । मेधम् । जुषन्त । वह्नयः ॥९॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ opening

विश्वेदेवास एतन्नामका देवविशेषा मेधं हविर्यज्ञसंबद्धं जुषन्ते । सेवन्ताम् । कीदृशाः । अस्रिधः क्षयरहिताः शोषरहिता वा एहिमायासः सर्वतो व्याप्तप्रज्ञाः । यद्वा । सौचीकमग्निमप्सु प्रविष्टमेहि मा यासीरिति यदवोचन् तदनुकरणहेतुकोऽयं विश्वेषां देवानां व्यपदेश एहिमायास इति । अद्रोहः … viśvedevāsa etan-nāmakā deva-viśeṣā medhaṃ havir-yajña-sambaddhaṃ juṣante | sevantām | kīdṛśāḥ | asridhaḥ kṣaya-rahitāḥ śoṣa-rahitā vā ehimāyāsaḥ sarvato vyāpta-prajñāḥ | yad vā | saucīkam agnim apsu praviṣṭam ehi mā yāsīr iti yad avocan tad-anukaraṇa-hetuko 'yaṃ viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ vyapadeśa ehimāyāsa iti | adroho …

Translation: "The Viśvedevas — a particular class of gods of that name — let them enjoy ('juṣantām' = 'sevantām') the 'medha,' the oblation connected with the sacrifice. What kind are they? 'Asridhaḥ' — free from decay, or free from drying-up; 'ehimāyāsaḥ' — those whose wisdom (prajñā) pervades everywhere. Or else: because they said, to Agni the Saucīka who had entered the waters, 'Come! do not go!' ("ehi mā yāsīḥ" — the print on this page shows the second word ambiguously, but the Bhāṣya's own next lines, and the Kannada commentary on p. 60, give "mā"), this designation 'ehimāyāsaḥ' for the Viśvedevas arose from that imitation (of their speech). 'Adrohaḥ' …" Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; where the print is unclear. The grammar is characterized, sūtras kept; the sense is transcribed in full.

original p. 59

Rik 3.9: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (concluded), grammar, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English rendering

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ continuing from p. 58, at "adrohaḥ"

…द्रोहरहिताः । वह्नयो वोढारो धनानां प्रापयितारः ॥ …droha-rahitāḥ | vahnayo voḍhāro dhanānāṃ prāpayitāraḥ ||

Translation: "'Adruhaḥ' — free from malice (droha). 'Vahnayaḥ' — bearers; those who bring about the attaining of riches."

Grammar of Rik 3.9 (characterized): - "Asridhaḥ" — from "sridh," in the sense of decay (or of drying up), "kvip" in the abstract sense after the "sampadādi" class (पा. ३-३-१०८ with its vārttika, printed ३-३-१०८-९); a negative bahuvrīhi; setting aside the first-member's accent, नञ्सुभ्याम् (nañ-subhyām) gives acute on the last syllable of the second member. - "Ehimāyāsaḥ" — "īh" (to strive); "ā samantād īhate" — "he who strives on all sides" = "ehiḥ"; the affix "in" (उ. ४-११२) comes to roots generally, and, being "n"-marked, the first syllable is acute; "ehir māyā prajñā yeṣām" — a bahuvrīhi in which the first member keeps its accent. Alternatively: the word "ehi" is the imperative second-person-singular after the "ā" accented (loṇ-madhyama-ekavacana) with the unaccented ending lost by "tiṅ atiṅaḥ" nighāta, with the fusing vowel "e" acute — and then "ehi" + "mā" of "mā yāsīḥ": "those who have the two syllables 'māyā' in the phrase 'ehi mā yāsīḥ'" = "ehimāyāsaḥ"; the first member keeps its accent. - "Adruhaḥ" — "druh" (to wish to injure), "kvip" by "sampadādi" in the abstract; negative bahuvrīhi; last syllable of the second member acute by "nañ-subhyām." - "Medham" — "medhṛ" (to unite): "that which is united with, approached by the gods" = "medham," oblation; "ghañ" in the object-sense; "ñ"-marked, so first syllable acute. - "Juṣanta" — in the sense "sevantām" ("let them enjoy"), in the Veda the "luṅ, laṅ, liṭ" may stand for the imperative (छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ, पा. ३-४-६); since the sense is joined to the root meanings of "druh" etc., "laṅ" is chosen; by बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि (bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅ-yoge 'pi, पा. ६-४-७५) the augment "aṭ" does not occur. - "Vahnayaḥ" — from "vah" with the Uṇādi "ṇi/ni" (वहिश्री…, vahi-śri-…); "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute. ॥९॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

विश्वे देवासः (viśve devāsaḥ) — O Viśvedevas, (you) | अस्रिधः (asridhaḥ) — free from decay, free from destruction | एहिमायासः (ehimāyāsaḥ) — those who have wisdom (knowledge) in all directions and in all matters | अद्रुहः (adruhaḥ) — those who are free from malice (hostility) | वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ) — those who bring (to those who praise you, wealth and lordship), who carry | (such you) मेधम् (medham) — the oblation that belongs to the sacrifice | जुषन्त (juṣanta) — enjoy (eat).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Viśvedevas! You are free from destruction, complete in wisdom about all matters — that is, all-knowing. You are not those who harbour hostility to another. You are those who bring to the ones who praise you wealth and lordship. Such as you are, partake of the oblation connected with the sacrifice that we offer.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"May the Visve devas, who are immortal, Omniscient, devoid of malice and bearers (of riches), accept the Sacrificial food." Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3."

original p. 60

Special topics on Rik 3.9: "asridhaḥ," "ehimāyāsaḥ," and the legend of Agni in the waters (opening)

अस्रिधः (asridhaḥ) — The Bhāṣyakāra explains this as "one free of decay, or free of drying-up" — in the source's own English, "not causing drought, or dryness." Western scholars have used the words (English as printed): "Unfailing, undecaying, undrying, undaunted, fearless, friendly, harmless," and the like.

एहिमायासः (ehimāyāsaḥ) — This word occurs in the Ṛgveda in this Ṛk alone, nowhere else. The Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "sarvato vyāpta-prajñāḥ" ("those whose understanding pervades everywhere"). Skandasvāmī gives "ahīna-māyāḥ, anyūna-prajñānāḥ" (अहीनमायाः अन्यूनप्रज्ञानाः — "those of undiminished wisdom, of unlessened understanding"). Both of them, and also Veṅkaṭamādhava, in considering the origin of this word, or how it came to be a fixed term, quote a sentence of the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa:

सौचीकमग्निमप्सु प्रविष्टमेहि मा यासीरिति यदवोचन् तदनुकरणहेतुकोऽयं विश्वेषां देवानां व्यपदेश एहिमायास इति । saucīkam agnim apsu praviṣṭam ehi mā yāsīr iti yad avocan tad-anukaraṇa-hetuko 'yaṃ viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ vyapadeśa ehimāyāsa iti |

Translation: "Because they said to Agni Saucīka, who had entered the waters, 'Come! do not go!' — this designation of the Viśvedevas, 'ehimāyāsaḥ,' arises from the imitation of that speech."

That is: seeing the Agni named Saucīka entering the waters, the gods said "ehi mā yāsīḥ" — "come, do not go" — and the word "ehimāyāsaḥ" is thought to have become the fixed word through imitation of those words. This matter is described in detail in the tenth Maṇḍala, sūkta 51 of the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-51-6 [print]):

अग्नेः पूर्वे भ्रातरो अर्थमेतं रथीवाध्वानमन्वावरीवुः । तस्माद्भिया वरुण दूरमायं गौरो न क्षेप्नोरविजे ज्यायाः ॥ कुर्मस्त आयुरजरं यदग्ने यथा युक्तो जातवेदो न रिष्याः । अथा वहासि सुमनस्यमानो भागं देवेभ्यो हविषः सुजात ॥ प्रयाजान्मे अनुयाजांश्च केवलानूर्जस्वन्तं हविषो दत्त भागम् । घृतं चापां पुरुषं चौषधीनामग्नेश्च दीर्घमायुरस्तु देवाः ॥ तव प्रयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल ऊर्जस्वन्तो हविषः सन्तु भागाः । तवाग्ने यज्ञोऽयमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमन्तां प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-५१-६ से ९)

agneḥ pūrve bhrātaro artham etaṃ rathīvādhvānam anvāvarīvuḥ | tasmād bhiyā varuṇa dūram āyaṃ gauro na kṣepnor avije jyāyāḥ || kurmas ta āyur ajaraṃ yad agne yathā yukto jātavedo na riṣyāḥ | athā vahāsi sumanasyamāno bhāgaṃ devebhyo haviṣaḥ sujāta || prayājān me anuyājāṃś ca kevalān ūrjasvantaṃ haviṣo datta bhāgam | ghṛtaṃ cāpāṃ puruṣaṃ cauṣadhīnām agneś ca dīrgham āyur astu devāḥ || tava prayājā anuyājāś ca kevala ūrjasvanto haviṣaḥ santu bhāgāḥ | tavāgne yajño 'yam astu sarvas tubhyaṃ namantāṃ pradiśaś catasraḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 10-51-6 to 9)

Gloss (mine; the source gives no translation of these four verses on this page): "(Agni:) 'Agni's elder brothers went this way, like a charioteer along his road; from fear of that, O Varuṇa, I have come far away, like a buffalo from the archer's shot.' (The gods:) 'We shall make your life unageing, O Agni, so that you, Jātavedas, bound to us, shall not come to harm; and then, well-disposed, you will carry the portion of the oblation to the gods, O well-born one.' (Agni:) 'Give me the fore-offerings and after-offerings, whole, and a strong portion of the oblation; and may ghee (the essence of the waters) and the "puruṣa" of the plants and Agni's long life be [mine], O gods.' (The gods:) 'Yours are the fore-offerings and after-offerings, whole; may the portions of the oblation be full of strength; yours, O Agni, be this whole sacrifice; may the four quarters bow to you.'" [tentative; for orientation only]

This sūkta is a conversation between the gods and Agni. The main point: Agni had three elder brothers, named Bhūpati, Bhuvanapati and Bhūtānāṃpati, who, like Agni, used to carry the oblations to the gods in the sacrifice. When, in the sacrifice, the oblation was made with the thunderbolt-like cry "vaṣaṭ," these three brothers died. Seeing that, the youngest, Agni, frightened, went into the waters and hid. While the gods were searching for Agni, the fish in the water [told] the gods that Agni was in the water… Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The Taittirīya text below is transcribed from the Kannada print letter by letter; It has not been corrected from outside knowledge, and a few of its spellings look irregular; they are left as printed.

original p. 61

The legend of Agni in the waters (concluded); the Taittirīya Saṃhitā version

Continuing from p. 60: "…the fish in the water told the gods that Agni was in the water." Then the gods came and addressed Agni; that very conversation is what is described in this sūkta. The gods asked Agni to come up out of the water and, as before, to carry the oblations for them; but Agni, because his brothers had died, said that the same fate awaited him too, and that therefore he would not come. The gods said, "Do not fear death; we shall so arrange it that you do not have the fear of death." Agni then said: "Very well; but besides keeping the fear of death from me, in the sacrifices the prayāja, anuyāja, ūrjasvat, sviṣṭakṛt, ājyabhāga and other special oblations must be given to me." The gods agreed, gave him the portions of the oblation, and appointed him again as before to the work of oblation-bearing, so that he would carry the chief role in the sacrifice, be worshipped by all, and have long life. This is the main sense of this sūkta.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda the matter stands thus:

अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायाꣳसो भ्रातर आसन्ते देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहन्तः प्रामीयन्त सोऽग्निरबिभेदित्थं वाव स्य आर्तिमार्ष्यतीति स निलायत सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छंस्तं मत्स्यः प्राब्रवीत्तमशपद्धियोधियो त्वा वध्यासुर्यो मा प्रावोचे इति तस्मान्मत्स्यं धियोधियो घ्नन्ति शप्तो हि तमन्वविन्दन्तमब्रुवन्नुप न आ वर्तस्व हव्यं नो वहेति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै यदेव गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बर्हिः परिधिस्कन्दात्तन्मे भ्रातृणां भागधेयमसदिति तस्माद्यद्गृहीतस्याहुतस्य बर्हिः परिधि स्कन्दति तेषां तद्भागधेयं तानेव तेन प्रीणाति परिधीन्परि दधाति रक्षसामपहत्यै ॥ (तै. सं. २-६-६) agnes trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsante devebhyo havyaṃ vahantaḥ prāmīyanta so 'gnir abibhed itthaṃ vāva sya ārtim ārṣyatīti sa nilāyata so 'paḥ prāviśat taṃ devatāḥ praiṣam aicchaṃs taṃ matsyaḥ prābravīt tam aśapad dhiyodhiyo tvā vadhyāsur yo mā prāvoce iti tasmān matsyaṃ dhiyodhiyo ghnanti śapto hi tam anvavindan tam abruvann upa na ā vartasva havyaṃ no vaheti so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai yad eva gṛhītasyāhutasya barhiḥ paridhiskandāt tan me bhrātṛṇāṃ bhāgadheyam asad iti tasmād yad gṛhītasyāhutasya barhiḥ paridhi skandati teṣāṃ tad bhāgadheyaṃ tān eva tena prīṇāti paridhīn pari dadhāti rakṣasām apahatyai || (tai. saṃ. 2-6-6)

Translation (mine, following the Kannada account below; where the Sanskrit is irregular I give the sense of the Kannada): "Agni had three elder brothers, who carried the oblation to the gods; they perished. Agni feared, 'this very distress will reach me,' and hid; he entered the waters. The gods sought him out; a fish told them, and he cursed it — 'may those who kill you (fish), kill you with cleverness (dhiyodhiyo)' — and therefore people kill fish by their wits, for it was cursed. The gods found him and said, 'Come back to us, carry the oblation for us.' He said, 'Let me choose a boon: whatever of the offered oblation, of the barhis, falls (outside) beyond the fire-sticks (paridhi), let that be the share of my brothers.' Therefore whatever of the offered oblation falls beyond the paridhi is their share; with that he satisfies them; he lays the paridhis around, for the driving away of the rākṣasas." (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-6-6, as printed)

The Kannada account (translated): Formerly Agni had three elder brothers; they used to carry to the gods the oblations that the sacrificer gave in the sacrifices. When they died, Agni, fearing that the same fate might reach him too, ran off, entered the water and hid, seen by no one. While the gods were searching for where Agni had gone, a fish in the water told the gods that Agni was hiding in the water. Hearing this tale-bearing of the fish, Agni was angry and cursed it: "From now on, people shall catch the fish that are in the water, by nets and other means, and kill them." So even now people catch fish and eat them. Afterwards the gods said to Agni, "O Agni, come back and be diligent in the work of bearing the oblation for us." To this Agni said — (he asked that) the paridhis used in the sacrifice when oblations are made (special bundles of darbha-grass laid on the four sides around the fire, so that rākṣasas do not come and obstruct the sacrifice), that the share of the ājya and other oblations that falls outside (on the near side) be the oblation-share of his brothers; if this boon were granted, he would come out of the water and carry the oblation to the gods as before. The gods agreed and gave him that boon. Thus the story runs. Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." Reference-numbers in small Kannada numerals are read as well as possible and all marked [?]; English in the source is reproduced as printed, misprints marked [sic].

original p. 62

Special topics on Rik 3.9 (continued): "ehimāyāsaḥ" and "māyā"

Therefore, according to the opinion of some, the word "ehimāyāsaḥ" became a fixed word through imitation of the sentence "ehi mā yāsīḥ" ("Do not go — come!") which the gods addressed to Agni when he was entering the water.

Some hold that "ehimāyāsaḥ" is merely a variant form of the word "ahimāyāḥ." This word, in its different case-forms, ahimāyān (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4), ahimāyāḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-52-15; 10-63-4) and ahimāyasya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-7), is used only in the four Ṛks of which these are the references. For this word Western scholars give, (English as printed):

  • Roth — "Of many shapes or agile like a serpent, tricky as a serpent."
  • Williams — "Having unsurpassable wisdom."
  • Griffith — "Having Superhuman Power."
  • Ludwig — "Having the wiles of serpants [sic]."

— thus various senses are given. For the word "māyā" the following senses can be given in the Ṛgveda English as printed:

  1. Creative power.
  2. Miraculous power (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-3; 2-17-5 &c.)
  3. Power of assuming various shapes (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-8; 5-63-6; 6-22-6 &c.)
  4. Wiles, tactics, tricks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-7; 6-18-9 &c.)
  5. Sorcery, witchcraft, magic (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-16; 8-23-15; 6-45-9 &c.)
  6. Illusion (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-54-2)

Formerly this word may have carried the senses "wisdom, intelligence (buddhi), skill (kuśalate)." In the course of time it appears that its use in other senses became established. In the Purāṇas and the Vedānta as well, senses such as "prakṛti, divine power, creative power, supernatural power" are the established ones for "māyā." In the Ṛgveda, forms of this word — māyā, māyayā, māyāḥ, māyābhiḥ, māyām, māyāvān, māyāvinaḥ, māyāvinam, māyinaḥ, māyinam, māyinā, māyinām, māyā and others — are used in many Ṛks in different senses; their senses will be explained in the places concerned. Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The grammar is the Kannada rendering of Sanskrit p. 59, characterized in order, with the sūtras kept; Where the numbers differ from the Sanskrit page this is noted.

original p. 63

"adruhaḥ"; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 3.9 (Kannada) — characterized

अद्रुहः (adruhaḥ) — This word is derived from the root "druh" ("druha jighāṃsāyām," to wish to injure). The sense of this word is "free from malice"; in the source's English: "not injuring, kindly disposed, without evil, without ill-will, without hostility, Guileless, not deceiving, devoid of malignity." Though different words are used to explain the sense, the chief intention is one.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ - "Asridhaḥ": the root "sridh" (denoting decay, or drying); by संपदादिभ्यः क्विप् (sampadādibhyaḥ kvip, पा. ३-३-१०८, वा. ९) "kvip" in the abstract sense; the negative "nañ" compounded with "sridh" as a bahuvrīhi ("na sridh yeṣām te"); setting aside the first-member accent of बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, पा. ६-२-१), by नञ्सुभ्याम् (nañ-subhyām, पा. ६-२-१७२) the last syllable of the second member is acute — "asridh" is end-acute. - "Ehimāyāsaḥ": "ā" + root "īh ceṣṭāyām" (to strive): "he who strives on all sides" = "ehi"; an Uṇādi affix "in" comes to roots generally (Uṇ. Sū. 2-557 [as printed]; p. 59 cites it as 4-112), and, being "n"-marked, the first syllable is acute; "ehir māyā prajñā yeṣām te ehimāyāsaḥ" — a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent (पा. ६-२-१). Alternatively — as a particle-like first member it is first-syllable acute; behind it the root "iṇ gatau" in the imperative second-person-singular "ihi" (loṇ madhyama-ekavacana), which loses its accent by तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८); with "ā" + "ihi," the guṇa-substitution gives a single "e," which, by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ, पा. ८-२-५), is acute. In that analysis the word is "ehi" together with the two syllables "māyā" of the phrase "ehi mā yāsīḥ": "those who have the two letters 'māyā' with the word 'ehi'" = "ehimāyāsaḥ," a bahuvrīhi keeping its first-member accent. - "Adruhaḥ": the root "druh jighāṃsāyām" is in the "sampadādi" group, so "kvip" comes; with "nañ" as a bahuvrīhi, by नञ्सुभ्याम् the second member is end-acute. - "Medham": from the root "medhṛ saṅgame" (to unite): "medhyate saṅgamyate devaiḥ iti medham" — the oblation, because it is united with the gods; the affix "ghañ" in the object-sense; "ñ"-marked, hence first-syllable acute. - "Juṣanta": since the sense of the root is joined with those of "druh" and the like, छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ, पा. ३-४-६) gives "laṅ" in the sense "sevatām" ("let them enjoy"); and by बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि (bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅ-yoge 'pi, पा. ६-४-७५ [as printed "…-4-75"]) — the augments "aṭ" and "āṭ" come variably, even when there is no "māṅ"; in some places, even where "māṅ" is present, they come; hence here no "āṭ" augment arises. continues on p. 64 Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 1, Sūkta 3." Accent-marks are not reproduced in the Saṃhitā/Pada text; see the note at Rik 3.5.

original p. 64

Rik 3.9 grammar concluded; Sūkta 3, Tenth Mantra (the Sarasvatī tṛca): Saṃhitā, Pada, and the opening of the Bhāṣya

Continuing: …"vahnayaḥ": here the affix "ni" comes by the Uṇādi-sūtra "vahi-śri-…" (as at p. 58); "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute. ॥९॥

Sūkta 3, The Tenth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पा॒व॒का नः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ वाजे॑भिर्वा॒जिनी॑वती । य॒ज्ञं व॑ष्टु धि॒याव॑सुः ॥१०॥

pāvakā́ naḥ sárasvatī vā́jebhirvājínīvatī | yajñáṃ vaṣṭu dhiyā́vasuḥ ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पावका । नः । सरस्वती । वाजेभिः । वाजिनीवती । यज्ञम् । वष्टु । धियावसुः ॥१०॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सारस्वते तृचे या प्रथमा सान्वारम्भणीयेष्ट्या सरस्वत्याः पुरोनुवाक्या । तथा दर्शपूर्णमासारप्स्यमान इत्यस्मिन्कण्डे पावका नः सरस्वती पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः । आ. २-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ sārasvate tṛce yā prathamā sānvārambhaṇīyeṣṭyā sarasvatyāḥ puronuvākyā | tathā darśa-pūrṇamāsārapsyamāna ity asmin kaṇḍe pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ | ā. 2-8 | iti sūtritam ||

Translation: "In the Sārasvata tṛca (the triplet addressed to Sarasvatī), the first Ṛk is the invitatory verse (puronuvākyā) of Sarasvatī in the "sānvārambhaṇīya" sacrificial offering; and likewise, in the section beginning "darśa-pūrṇamāsārapsyamāna" (one about to begin the new- and full-moon sacrifices), the Ṛks "pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī" and "pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ" are laid down in the sūtra (the source reference as printed is "ā. 2-8")."

सरस्वती देवी वाजेभिर्हविर्लक्षणैरन्नैर्निमित्तभूतैः । यद्वा । यजमानेभ्यो दातव्यैरन्नैर्निमित्तभूतैः । नोऽस्मदीयं यज्ञं वष्टु । कामयताम् । कामयित्वा च निर्वहत्वित्यर्थः । तथा चारण्यककाण्डे श्रुत्यैव व्याख्यातम् । यज्ञं वष्टिवति यदाह यज्ञं वहत्विति तदाह । ऐ. आ. १-१-४ । इति । कीदृशी सरस्वती । पावका शोधयित्री वाजिनीवत्यन्नवत्क्रियावती धियावसुः कर्मप्राप्त्यधननिमित्तभूता । वाग्देवतायास्तथाविधं धननिमित्तत्वमारण्यककाण्डे श्रुत्या व्याख्यातम् । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुरिति वाग्वै धियावसुः । ऐ. आ. १-१-४ । इति । श्येनः सोम इत्यादिषु पञ्चत्रिंशत्संख्याकेषु देवताविशेषवाचिषु पदेषु सरमा सरस्वतीति पठितम् । एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । पावका नः सरस्वत्यन्नैरन्नवती यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः कर्मवसुः । नि. ११- … sarasvatī devī vājebhir havir-lakṣaṇair annair nimitta-bhūtaiḥ | yad vā | yajamānebhyo dātavyair annair nimitta-bhūtaiḥ | no 'smadīyaṃ yajñaṃ vaṣṭu | kāmayatām | kāmayitvā ca nirvahatv ity arthaḥ | tathā cāraṇyaka-kāṇḍe śrutyaiva vyākhyātam | yajñaṃ vaṣṭīvati yad āha yajñaṃ vahatv iti tad āha | ai. ā. 1-1-4 | iti | kīdṛśī sarasvatī | pāvakā śodhayitrī vājinīvaty annavat-kriyāvatī dhiyāvasuḥ karma-prāpty-adhana-nimitta-bhūtā | vāg-devatāyās tathāvidhaṃ dhana-nimittatvam āraṇyaka-kāṇḍe śrutyā vyākhyātam | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasur iti vāg vai dhiyāvasuḥ | ai. ā. 1-1-4 | iti | śyenaḥ soma ity ādiṣu pañcatriṃśat-saṃkhyākeṣu devatā-viśeṣa-vāciṣu padeṣu saramā sarasvatīti paṭhitam | etām ṛcaṃ yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | pāvakā naḥ sarasvaty annair annavatī yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ karma-vasuḥ | ni. 11- …

Translation: "'Sarasvatī' — the goddess — 'vājebhiḥ': by the oblation-nature foods that are the occasion (nimitta-bhūta) — or, by the foods to be given to the sacrificers, which are the occasion — 'may she desire our sacrifice ('vaṣṭu': let her desire it); and having desired it, let her carry it through' — such is the sense. And so the Āraṇyaka section itself explains this by Śruti: 'When it says "may she desire the sacrifice" ("yajñaṃ vaṣṭu"), it says "let her carry the sacrifice."' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1-1-4). What kind of Sarasvatī? 'Pāvakā' — the purifier; 'vājinīvatī' — one possessing food, possessing activity; 'dhiyāvasuḥ' — one who is the occasion for the attaining of wealth through ritual action. That the goddess of speech is, in this way, the occasion of wealth, is explained by the Śruti in the Āraṇyaka section: '"yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ" — Speech indeed is "dhiyāvasuḥ."' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1-1-4). Among the thirty-five words denoting particular deities, beginning with 'śyenaḥ soma,' 'saramā' and 'sarasvatī' are read. Yāska explains this Ṛk thus: '"Pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī": Sarasvatī, rich in foods; "yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ": let her desire the sacrifice, she whose wealth is ritual action.' (Nirukta 11-…)" Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; [?] where unclear. Rik 3.10: close of the Bhāṣya (Nirukta quotation), grammar, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English rendering

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ concluding the Nirukta quotation begun on p. 64

…३६ । इति ॥ …36 | iti ||

Translation: "(Nirukta 11-)36. — So much (of Yāska)." The number "36" is the continuation of the reference left open at the foot of p. 64.

Grammar of Rik 3.10 (characterized, with sūtras): - "Pāvakā": "pavanaṃ pāvaḥ śuddhiḥ; pāvaṃ kāyatīti pāvakā" — one who "sings/makes" purity ("kai gai rai śabde"); by आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः (āto 'nupasarge kaḥ, पा. ३-२-३) the affix "ka"; the accent of a kṛt-ending as second member gives an end-acute. Alternatively, in the sense "she purifies," with "ṇvul," the vowel "a" before the affix's "k" would normally become "i" (इदाप्यसुपः, id āpy asupaḥ, पा. ७-३-४४ [as printed "7-3-44"]), but that does not occur here, and the "aṃśa-udātta" accent is to be regarded as Vedic. - "Sarasvatī": "saras" from "sṛ" with the "asun" affix, hence first-syllable acute; "matup" and "ṅīp," being "p"-marked, are unaccented. - "Vājebhiḥ": "vāja" is first-syllable acute as belonging to the "vṛṣādi" class (an "ākṛti-gaṇa," an open-ended list). - "Vājinīvatī": "vājo 'nnam asty āsām" — "those [ritual] actions which possess food" = "vājinyaḥ kriyāḥ" [reading of the print: "vājo 'nnam āstīti vājinyaḥ kriyāḥ" ?]; by अत इनिठनौ (ata iniṭhanau, पा. ५-२-११५) the affix "ini"; "she who has those actions" = "vājinīvatī"; by छन्दसीरः (chandasīraḥ) "matup" gets "va"; since "matup" and "ṅīp" are "p"-marked and unaccented, only the "ini" affix's first-syllable acute remains. - "Yajñam": by यजयाचयतविच्छप्रच्छरक्षो नङ् (yaja-yāca-yata-vicchaprachcha-rakṣo naṅ, पा. ३-३-९०) the affix "naṅ"; end-acute by the affix. - "Vaṣṭu": root "vaś kāntau" (to desire; "kānti" = wish); by आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (ādi-prabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ) "śap" is elided (luk); nighāta. - "Dhiyāvasuḥ": "dhiyā karmaṇā vasu yasyāḥ sakāśād bhavati sā dhiyāvasuḥ" — she from whom wealth comes by ritual action; the case-ending is acute by सावेकाचः (sāv ekācaḥ); in a bahuvrīhi, by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam), the case-accent alone remains; the retention of the instrumental ending (a-luk) is Vedic.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

पावका (pāvakā) — one who purifies (people), or who cleanses | वाजिनीवती (vājinīvatī) — (to the people who praise) one who has food and sustenance and gives them | धियावसुः (dhiyāvasuḥ) — she who is the cause of wealth and the like, the fruit of sacrifice and the other rites | सरस्वती (sarasvatī) — the goddess Sarasvatī (the goddess of speech, or the river named Sarasvatī) | नः (naḥ) — our | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — the sacrifice | वाजेभिः (vājebhiḥ) — through the foods that take the form of the oblation | वष्टु (vaṣṭu) — let her desire (let her bring the sacrifice to completion, with all its parts).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The goddess Sarasvatī is the purifier of people; she gives food and the like to the people who worship her by sacrifice and the like; and she is the cause of the attainment of lordship in the form of wealth. May such a Sarasvatī, satisfied with the foods and the like, in the form of the oblation that we give, bring our sacrifice to its full completion.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"May Saraswati, the purifier, the bestower of food, recompenser of worships with wealth, be attracted to our rite by our offer of sacrificial food." Special topics on Rik 3.10: the Sārasvata tṛca; the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This Ṛk, "pāvakā naḥ," together with the following two Ṛks, form the "sārasvata-tṛcaḥ," that is, three Ṛks that relate to Sarasvatī. Of these three Ṛks, the first, "pāvakā naḥ," is the "puronuvākyā" mantra for invoking Sarasvatī in the special sacrificial offering called the Anvārambhaṇīyeṣṭi. In a sacrifice, when oblation is made to any god, two Ṛks are used; both must relate to that deity. With the first Ṛk — recited aloud — the deity is invoked; this Ṛk is called "puronuvākyā." With another Ṛk the oblation is made to that deity; this mantra is called "yājyā." Likewise, in the Anvārambhaṇīyeṣṭi both Ṛks, "puronuvākyā" and "yājyā," are used. This matter the great sage Āśvalāyana has stated thus in his Śrauta-sūtra (Āśv. Śrau. Sū. 2-8), in the section beginning "darśapūrṇamāsārapsyamāna":

पावका नः सरस्वती पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः । (आश्व. २-८) pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ | (āśv. 2-8) Gloss: "'Pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī' and 'pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ'." (The sūtra simply names the two Ṛks to be used.)

Before performing this Anvārambhaṇīyeṣṭi and the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifice, the sacrificer must first perform the rites called puṇyāhavācana, nāndīśrāddha and udakaśānti, tie a thread called pratisara on his wife's hand, and then, on the day following, after performing the daily rites such as bathing, he must make the resolution: "yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yakṣye" (यावज्जीवं दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां यक्ष्ये — yāvaj-jīvaṃ darśa-pūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yakṣye — "as long as I live I shall sacrifice with the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices"). Next he makes the resolution "anvārambhaṇīyayā yakṣye" (अन्वारम्भणीयया यक्ष्ये — "I shall sacrifice with the anvārambhaṇīyā") and must perform the rite called agnyanayana — bringing in the fire from the Gārhapatya fire by the "agni-viharaṇa." Then, in speaking of the "anvādhāna," the chief ("pradhāna") oblation is made to the principal deities Agnāviṣṇū, Sarasvatī, Sarasvān, and Agnir-bhagī (the last name as printed; I am not sure of it). The offering-materials are: for Agnāviṣṇū, "ekādaśa-kapāla puroḍāśa" (a cake on eleven potsherds); for the deity Sarasvatī, a "caru" (cooked rice-offering); for Sarasvān, a "dvādaśa-kapāla puroḍāśa" (twelve potsherds); and for the deity "Agnir-bhagī," an "aṣṭādaśa-kapāla puroḍāśa" (eighteen potsherds). The "puronuvākyā" and "yājyā" mantras used when making oblation to these deities are these: The page continues on p. 67 with the remaining oblations.
