Special topics on Rik 4.1 (continued): Indra's many forms; "surūpakṛtnum" and "lokakṛtnum"; "ūtaye" (opening)

Continuing from p. 89: In the Ṛk

रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं परि स्वाम् । (ऋ. सं. ३-५३-८) rūpaṃ-rūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānas tanvaṃ pari svām | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-53-8) Gloss: "Maghavan becomes form after form, working his magic arts around his own body."

too it is said that Indra is able to assume many forms. In the Nirukta as well (Ni. 10-17) this Ṛk is explained thus:

विश्वामित्रस्यार्षम् । यावन्ति कानिचिद्रूपाणि मघवा इन्द्रो भवितुमिच्छति तानि सर्वाण्यप्रतिबन्धेन बोभवीति पुनःपुनर्भवतीति । कथम् । मायाः कृण्वानः इदं भवामीदं भवामीत्येवं "तन्वं परि स्वां" स्वां तनुं तत्तदाकृत्यानेकविधां विकुर्वाणः । तेनासावचिन्त्यप्रभावत्वाच्छक्नोति तत्तद्रूपमावेष्टुम् ॥ इत्यादि viśvāmitrasyārṣam | yāvanti kānicid rūpāṇi maghavā indro bhavitum icchati tāni sarvāṇy apratibandhena bobhavīti punaḥ-punar bhavatīti | katham | māyāḥ kṛṇvānaḥ idaṃ bhavāmīdaṃ bhavāmīty evaṃ "tanvaṃ pari svāṃ" svāṃ tanuṃ tat-tad-ākṛtyānekavidhāṃ vikurvāṇaḥ | tenāsāv acintya-prabhāvatvāc chaknoti tat-tad-rūpam āveṣṭum || ity ādi

Translation: "(This Ṛk is) the revelation of Viśvāmitra. Whatever forms Maghavan Indra wishes to become, all of them he becomes without hindrance, again and again. How? 'Working māyās': 'I become this, I become this' — thus 'around his own body' — his own body, in this and that shape, transforming it in many ways. Therefore, through his [a]-inconceivable power ("[a]cintya-prabhāvatvāt" — the first letter of the word is not clear), he is able to enter into this or that form," and so on.

That is, in this Ṛk the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra says this: Indra, by his power of māyā, is able to transform his own body in many ways — that is, to take on, as the occasion requires, many different bodily forms. In the time of slaying enemies he can take a terrible form, and in fulfilling the wishes of the worshipper or of the people who praise him he can take a lovely form; and he has the power of māyā suited to such actions. Therefore, since in the Ṛk in hand the word "surūpakṛtnum" is used in calling Indra, with love, for our protection, the ṛṣi may have used the word to signify that Indra should come here, taking, by his power of māyā, a beautiful — that is, a gracious — form, to guard us. The word "kṛtnu" occurs, as the latter member of a compound, in the word "lokakṛtnum," which is found only in these two Ṛks:

तं ते मदं गृणीमसि वृषणं पृत्सु सासहिम् । उ लोककृत्नुमद्रिवो हरिश्रियम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-१५-४) taṃ te madaṃ gṛṇīmasi vṛṣaṇaṃ pṛtsu sāsahim | u lokakṛtnum adrivo hariśriyam || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-15-4) Gloss: "That exhilaration of yours we praise, the bull, the conqueror in battles, the world-maker, O wielder of the stone, the splendour of the bay horses."

तं त्वा मदाय घृष्वय उ लोककृत्नुमीमहे । तव प्रशस्तयो महीः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-२-८) taṃ tvā madāya ghṛṣvaya u lokakṛtnum īmahe | tava praśastayo mahīḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 9-2-8) Gloss: "Thee, the world-maker, we entreat for the exhilaration, for the bold one; great are your praises."

— This word is, in both Ṛks, applied to Indra, that is, it applies to Indra.

ऊतये (ūtaye) — "For protection; for guarding." This word and its other forms — ūtayaḥ, ūtīḥ, ūtibhiḥ, ūtim, ūtiṣu, ūtī, ūtīḥ, ūtyā — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda. In the Nirukta (Ni. 5-3), "ūtiḥ" is explained as "āvanam" (protection), and… Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Reference-numbers marked [?]; glosses editorial.

original p. 91

Special topics on Rik 4.1 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

Continuing "ūtaye": …and he explains the word "ūtaye" in the Ṛk quoted as an example:

आ त्वा रथं यथोतये सुम्नाय वर्तयामसि । (ऋ. सं. ६-५-१ [as printed]) ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye sumnāya vartayāmasi | (ṛ. saṃ. 6-5-1 [as printed]) Gloss: "As (one turns) a chariot for aid, we turn you hither for favour."

as "avanāya, rakṣaṇāya" (for protecting). Such examples are many in the Ṛgveda. Ṛks in which Indra is entreated to save the worshippers from the harm of enemies, to make them fearless, and to protect them, occur in many places in the Ṛgveda:

त्रातारमिन्द्रमवितारमिन्द्रं हवेहवे सुहवं शूरमिन्द्रम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-११) trātāram indram avitāram indraṃ have-have suhavaṃ śūram indram || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-11) Gloss: "Indra the saviour, Indra the helper, Indra, easily invoked at every call, the hero."

बाधतां द्वेषो अभयं कृणोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-४७-१२) bādhatāṃ dveṣo abhayaṃ kṛṇotu suvīryasya patayaḥ syāma || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-47-12) Gloss: "May he drive off hatred, may he make fearlessness; may we be masters of good heroism."

There are many Ṛks of this kind concerning Indra.

सुदुघामिव गोदुहे (sudughām iva goduhe) — "As one calls a cow for milk." This simile — or similes of the same sense (the source's term: "lupta-upamā") — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda, so it seems that in that age this sentence was a customary one to cite as an illustration:

तं त्वा वयं सुदुघामिव गोदुहो जुहूमसि श्रवस्यवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-५२-४) taṃ tvā vayaṃ sudughām iva goduho juhūmasi śravasyavaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 8-52-4) Gloss: "Thee we call, like milkers a good milch-cow, seeking fame."

इन्द्रं धेनुं सुदुघामन्यामिषमुरुधारामरंकृतम् । (ऋ. सं. ८-१-१०) indraṃ dhenuṃ sudughām anyām iṣam urudhārām araṃkṛtam | (ṛ. saṃ. 8-1-10) Gloss: "Indra — the good milch-cow, another refreshment, broad-streamed, well-fashioned." [tentative; the print gives only this line]

उपह्वये सुदुघां धेनुमेतां सुहस्तो गोधुगुत दोहदेनाम् । (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-२६) upahvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ suhasto godhug uta dohad enām | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-26) Gloss: "I call this good milch-cow near; may the skilful-handed milker milk her."

A cow that gives milk is dear to everyone; likewise Indra, who protects from the harm of enemies, is desired by all — such is the import.

द्यविद्यवि (dyavidyavi) — "Every day." By नित्यवीप्सयोः (nityavīpsayoḥ, पा. ८-१-४) there is doubling: when a single word is read twice, the sense is "each one." Examples: dive-dive ("every day"), āharahaḥ, māsi-māsi ("every month"), yajñe-yajñe ("at every sacrifice"), bhare-bhare ("in every battle"), have-have ("at every call"), dame-dame ("in every house"), and the like.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept 4th Sūkta, Rik 1. "Surūpakṛtnum": a root meaning "to make" ("kṛ"); after the seven roots ṛ-ṣap-śilp-śap-bāp-rūpa-parṣa [?] (the list as printed: "khuṣpa śilpa śaṣpa bāpa rūpa parṣa …" — I read it with doubt; Uṇ. Sū. 3-3[?]8 [?]) — "ṛñ avadāraṇe" (to tear), "śīlasamādhau" (to practise), "śaśu hiṃsāyām" (to kill), "bādhṛ loḍane" (to disturb), "rū śabde" (to sound), "pūpālanapūraṇayoḥ" (to protect and fill), "talapratiṣṭhākaraṇe" — an affix "pa" … Page headers: p. 92 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 93 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, the Kannada rendering of the grammar already given in Sanskrit on p. 88. Per the standing convention they are characterized in order, not translated line by line; each sūtra the pages cite is kept in three layers with its number as read. Sūtra-numbers in small Kannada numerals are marked [?]. Nothing in them changes the sense of the Rik as given on p. 89.

original pp. 92–93

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.1 (Kannada) — characterized

p. 92 — "surūpakṛtnum" and the beginning of "ūtaye." - "Surūpa" — "rūpa" is formed from the root "rūp" (or "rūpa") with the affix "pa" that is added after the seven roots listed in the Uṇādi-sūtra, "khaṣpa-śilpa-śaṣpa-bāṣpa-rūpa-parpa-talpāḥ" (खष्पशिल्पशष्पबाष्परूपपर्पतल्पाः, उ. सू. ६-३०८ [as printed]), and, by nipātana, the lengthening of the vowel gives "rūpa." Explained as "rūpyate (praśasyate) iti rūpam": that which is praised by people. "Śobhanaṃ rūpaṃ yasya tat" — a bahuvrīhi compound — "surūpam." Then the genitive tatpuruṣa "surūpasya kṛtnuḥ." - "Kṛtnu" — "karotīti kṛtnuḥ": the affix "knu" after "kṛ" and "han" (कृहनिभ्यां क्नुः, उ. सू. ३-३-१० [as printed; cited just before as ३-३१०]); "knu" being "k"-marked, there is no guṇa; "han" is stated in the sūtra because the "t" of the affix is added (a Vedic feature). - Accent of the compound. After the "su" the bahuvrīhi would by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) retain the first member's accent; but नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) makes the last member's last syllable acute in a bahuvrīhi after "nañ" or "su"; so "surūpa" is end-acute. In "kṛtnu" the affix's accent is the acute, per धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२) and आद्युदात्तश्च (पा. ३-१-३); with "surūpakṛtnu" as a genitive tatpuruṣa, समासस्य (पा. ६-१-२२३) makes the compound end-acute. The second-case singular ending "am" must be added after "surūpakṛtnu"; by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. ३-१-४) the ending "am" is unaccented. By अमिपूर्वः (पा. ६-१-१०७) the "am" combines in the "pūrvarūpa" with the "u," and by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५) the single substitute is acute. - "Ūtaye" — ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (पा. ३-३-९७) with the word मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६) — the "udātta" of the preceding sūtra being carried over — these words ending in the affix "ktin" are formed irregularly (nipātana) and are end-acute: "ūti" is end-acute. The root "av" (to protect) takes "ktin" by ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च (पा. ६-४-२०) with "ūṭ" replacing "av," giving "ūti"; the accents of the root and of the affix would conflict, and the nipātana's acute on the "i" overrides. "Ū" is unaccented by the "śeṣa-anudātta" rule. …

p. 93 — "ūtaye" concluded; "sudughām," "goduhe," "juhūmasi." - "Ūti" + the dative ending "ṅe": the "ṅī"/"jhi" affixes; since "ūti" is a word ending in short "i" and not "nadī"-labelled, by घेर्ङिति (पा. ७-३-१११) the guṇa is substituted — "ūte" + "e" → by एचोऽयवायावः "ūtaye." The "ṅe" ending is unaccented as "sup"; the accent of the "i" of "ūti" is the "nipātana" acute, and the "ay" substitute is acute as the substitute of an acute; by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. ८-४-६६) the following unaccented syllable becomes svarita. Thus "ūtaye": first syllable unaccented, second acute, third svarita. - "Sudughām" — "suṣṭhu dugdhe iti sudughā" ("she who yields milk well"): the root "duh prapūraṇe" (to fill, to milk) takes "kap" when "su" is an upapada — दुहः कब्घश्च (duhaḥ kab ghaś ca, पा. ३-२-७०) — and the "h" of "duh" becomes "gh"; the "a" of "kap" being "p"-marked, there is no guṇa, and by अनुदात्तोपदेश… the root's accent remains; धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२) gives the root's last vowel — the "u" of "dugh" — the acute. With "su" the compound is a "gati-kāraka-upapada" compound, so by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९) the original accent remains; the feminine "ṭāp"; the second-case singular "sudughām"; and with "iva," by इवेन समासो विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च (the vārttika as on p. 58) the compound keeps the earlier accent. - "Goduhe" — "gāṃ dogdhīti godhuk": सत्सूद्विषद्रुहदुहयुजविदभिदच्छिदजिनीराजामुपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् (पा. ३-२-६१) — after "pad" (to go), "sad," "dviṣ," "druh," "duh," "yuj," "vid," "bhid," "chid," "ji," "nī," "rāj" — "kvip" occurs whether or not an upasarga precedes, when a subanta stands as upapada; the "kvip" is applied to "duh" with "go" as upapada; in the compound, the kṛt-ending second member's accent is kept (कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम्). - "Juhūmasi" — the root "hve" (ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च, "to challenge, to call") is in the bhvādi (first) class; "laṭ" first-person plural "mas" gives "hve + mas"; the "śap" that would come is elided as "ślu" by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. २-४-७६) — in the Veda "ślu" (elision named by the word "ślu") comes variously; then अभ्यस्तस्य च (पा. सू. ६-१-३३) … continues on the next page; re-read from the better scan, Oct 2026 Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; accent-marks not reproduced; see the note at Rik 3.5.

original p. 94

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.1 concluded; Sūkta 4, Second Mantra: Saṃhitā and Pada text

Continuing "juhūmasi" from p. 93: …the root "hve," being the cause, takes "samprasāraṇa" (ह्वेञ् … संप्रसारणम्): "hu + e + mas" → "hu + mas"-type form by संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. ६-१-१०८) — when "samprasāraṇa" is followed by an "ac," the single "pūrvarūpa" replaces both — and then by हलः (पा. ६-४-२, as printed) the stem-final before a consonant is lengthened ("hū"); the doubling by श्लौ (पा. ६-१-१०); the reduplicative syllable is shortened by ह्रस्वः (पा. ७-४-५९) — "hu-hū-mas"; for the "h" of the reduplicative syllable the "c"-class substitute by कुहोश्चुः (kuhoś cuḥ, पा. ७-४-६२) → "ju"; then the "ru/ghosa" substitutions अभ्यासे चर्च (पा. ८-४-५४); "mas" takes the augment "i" by इदन्तो मसिः (पा. ७-१-४६) → "juhūmasi." By the accent of the affix the "ma" is acute.

"Dyavidyavi" — the root "dyut dīptau" (to shine); after it the Uṇādi affix "do" (उणादयो बहुलम्, पा. ३-३-१); because of the word "bahulam" the affix "do" comes. Bhaṭṭoji-dīkṣita, in the Kaumudī, in explaining the Uṇādi-sūtra गमेर्डोः [as printed; "dyoḥ"?] (उ. सू. २-२२६), says that from the "bāhulaka" rule "dyau" too arises; Bhojadeva holds that "do" is the affix after the root "dyu abhigamane" ("to approach"). "Dyoḥ" is end-acute, by the Uṇādi accent rule (फिषः etc. as printed, "Phi. sū. 1"). In the seventh case singular, with the doubling by नित्यवीप्सयोः (पा. ८-१-४), the word is "dyavi-dyavi"; of it, the second part is called "āmreḍita" by परमाम्रेडितम् (पा. ८-१-२), and, by अनुदात्तं च (पा. ८-१-३), the "āmreḍita" is unaccented — so the second "dyavi" is unaccented. ॥१॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 4, The Second Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उप॑ नः॒ सव॒ना ग॑हि॒ सोम॑स्य सोमपाः पिब । गो॒दा इद्रे॒वतो॒ मदः॑ ॥२॥

úpa naḥ sávanā́ gahi sómasya somapāḥ piba | godā́ idreváto mádaḥ ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; [?] where unclear. The sense-lines are transcribed in full; the grammar is characterized, with its sūtras.

उप । नः । सवना । आ । गहि । सोमस्य । सोमऽपाः । पिब । गोऽदाः । इत् । रेवतः । मदः ॥२॥

original p. 95

Rik 4.2: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सोमपाः सोमस्य पातरिन्द्र सोमं पातुं नोऽस्मदीयानि सवना सवनानि त्रीणि प्रत्युप समीप आगहि । आगच्छ । आगत्य च सोमस्य सोमं पिब । रेवतो धनवतस्तव मदो हर्षो गोदा इद्गोप्रद एव । त्वयि हृष्टे सत्यस्माभिर्गावो लभ्यन्त इत्यर्थः ॥ he somapāḥ somasya pātar indra somaṃ pātuṃ no 'smadīyāni savanā savanāni trīṇi praty upa samīpa āgahi | āgaccha | āgatya ca somasya somaṃ piba | revato dhanavatas tava mado harṣo godā id gopradā eva | tvayi hṛṣṭe saty asmābhir gāvo labhyanta ity arthaḥ ||

Translation: "O 'somapāḥ' — O drinker of Soma, Indra! In order to drink the Soma, come near, 'upa āgahi' — come — 'nah savanā' — to our three pressings (savanas). And having come, drink the Soma ('somasya piba' = 'somam piba'). 'Revataḥ' — of you, the wealthy; the 'madaḥ' — the exhilaration — is 'godā id' — a giver of cows indeed: that is, when you are delighted, we obtain cows."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya characterized; the print is somewhat garbled in the middle and only what was read clearly is given: "Upa" — a particle, hence first-syllable acute. "Savanā" — "sūyate somaḥ eṣu iti savanāni": "lyuṭ" in the locative-of-place sense (ल्युट्…, पा. ३-३-११७); the ending "śas/jas" replaced by "ḍā" (सुपो डादेशः, as printed) and the loss of "ṭi"; the accent on the vowel before the affix in the "ṇit/ñit"-marked affix. "Gahi" — from "gam" with the "śap" dropped by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); the root's "m" is dropped by अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७); the "hi" ending by आतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) — the print then discusses why the loss of "m" is to be treated as "asiddha" and the resulting accent, which I do not reproduce. "Somapāḥ" — vocative; the आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८) loss of accent; "piba" has its accent lost by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) with reference to the preceding word, though that word is not itself an existent "pada"-unit by "parāṅgavadbhāva" — the print debates this (the "asāmarthya" argument) and concludes the "nighāta" does apply. "Godāḥ" — "gāṃ dadātīti godāḥ": "kvip" (क्विप् च, पा. ३-२-७६) in the sense of the doer, and the root-final "ā" becomes "i" by आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च (पा. ३-२-७४) [as printed "…vanip"]; "vic" … and "ghu-mā-sthā-…" (घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि, पा. ६-४-६६) — the "ī"-substitution of the final "ā" — would be expected, but "godāḥ" is irregular by Vedic usage. "Revān" — "rayir dhanam asyāstīti": "matup" after "rayi" (रयेर्मतौ बहुलं छन्दसि, पा. ६-१-३७-६ [as printed]), the samprasāraṇa, the guṇa; the "matup" is acute by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. ६-१-१७६); by छन्दसीरः (पा. ८-२-१५) the "va." "Madaḥ" — "mad" (to be glad) with "ap" (मदोऽनुपसर्गे, पा. ३-३-६७); "p"-marked and thus unaccented in the affix; the root-accent remains.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सोमपाः (somapāḥ) — O Indra, who drink the Soma | नः (naḥ) — our | सवना (savanā) — to the morning, midday and third pressings in the sacrifice (or: to the sacrifices that we perform) | उपागहि (upāgahi) — be one who comes near (coming here) | सोमस्य (somasya) — the Soma-juice | पिब (piba) — drink | रेवतः (revataḥ) — (of you) who are endowed with riches, lordship and the like | मदः (madaḥ) — the joy (that arises from drinking the Soma) | गोदाः (godāḥ) — gives (us) cows.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are a drinker of Soma. Therefore, coming to the three pressings of the sacrifice that we are now performing — the morning, the midday and the third — drink the Soma that we have prepared. When you drink it you are made glad; and you, who are endowed with lordship, will be the giver to us of cows (wealth in cows). Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." English as printed. The count of "-dāḥ" words (17) re-read from the better scan.

original p. 96

Rik 4.2: English rendering; Special topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"O Soma-drinker, come hither to our Sacrifices and Partake of the Soma; you being rich the satisfaction you get from drinking Soma is verily the cause of the gift of cattle."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उप आ गहि (upa ā gahi) — "Upa" — near: near the sacrifice we are performing; "ā gahi" — "come," be one who comes.

सवना (savanā) — "sūyate somaḥ eṣu iti savanāni" ("those in which Soma is pressed") — the name "savana" is given to the rite (the sacrifice) that extracts the Soma-juice. "Savana" may be explained as the three pressings beginning with the morning pressing, or as the sacrifice that has the rite of pressing. In either way the chief sense is one.

गोदाः (godāḥ) — "gāṃ dadātīti godāḥ; goprade" — one who gives cows, or wealth in cattle. Similarly "somaṃ pibatīti somapāḥ." In the Ṛgveda there are 17 examples of words ending in the affix "dāḥ":

अश्वदाः । आत्मदाः । ओजोदाः । गोदाः । द्रविणोदाः । धनदाः । बलदाः । भूरिदाः । वस्त्रदाः । वाजदाः । वासोदाः । सहोदाः । सहस्रदाः । सुदाः । स्वस्तिदाः । हिरण्यदाः । भूरिदाः ॥ aśvadāḥ | ātmadāḥ | ojodāḥ | godāḥ | draviṇodāḥ | dhanadāḥ | baladāḥ | bhūridāḥ | vastradāḥ | vājadāḥ | vāsodāḥ | sahodāḥ | sahasradāḥ | sudāḥ | svastidāḥ | hiraṇyadāḥ | bhūridāḥ || (Translation of the word-list, mine: "giver of horses; giver of self; giver of vigour; giver of cows; giver of wealth; giver of riches; giver of strength; giver of plenty; giver of garments; giver of prizes; giver of clothing; giver of might; giver of a thousand; good giver; giver of well-being; giver of gold; giver of plenty." The word "bhūridāḥ" is printed twice in the list, as I read it; I record this without correction.)

इत् (it) — "eva" (indeed). Example: "indraḥ godā id" — "Indra is indeed a giver of cows"; the sentence "indro godā it" means that Indra is a giver of cows only. The word "it" is used in the sense of emphasis (avadhāraṇa).

रेवतः (revataḥ) — "rayir dhanam asyāstīti revān, tasya revataḥ" — one who has wealth: "of the wealthy (Indra)."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized "Upa" — a particle (nipāta), hence, by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (Phiṭ-sūtra 80) first-syllable acute. "Savanā" — "sūyate somaḥ eṣv iti savanāni": करणाधिकरणयोश्च (karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca, पा. ३-३-११७) — "lyuṭ" is added to a root in the sense of instrument or locus; to "ṣuñ" (abhiṣave) comes "lyuṭ," "su + yu"; धात्वादेः षः सः (dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, पा. ६-१-६४) — the initial "ṣ" of the root becomes "s" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, the rendering of the Sanskrit of p. 95; characterized, with sūtras kept; numbers as read, [?] where uncertain.

original p. 97

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.2 — characterized

Continuing "savanā": …युवोरनाकौ (yuvor anākau, पा. ७-१-१) turns "yu" into "ana": "su + ana," then the guṇa and "av" substitutions → "savana." For the second-case plural ending, सुपां सुलुक्… (supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇāccheyāḍādyāyājālaḥ, पा. ७-१-३९) — the "ḍā" substitute — "savana + ā"; the "na" and the following "a" (टेः, पा. ६-४-१४३): the "ṭi" of "savana" is elided before "ḍit" → "savanā." By लिति (liti, पा. ६-१-१९३) the vowel before the "l"-marked affix is acute.

"Gahi" — the root "gam gatau," in the imperative (loṭ) second-person singular, the ending "sip" → "gam + si"; "śap" (कर्तरि शप्, पा. ३-१-६८), which is elided here by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); सेर्ह्यपिच्च (ser hy apic ca, पा. ३-४-८७) — "hi" replaces "si," and it is not "p"-marked — so "hi" is "ṅit"-like and the sārvadhātuka सार्वधातुकमपित् (पा. १-२-४) is "ṅit," whence अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७) drops the "m": "ga + hi." Then अतो हेः (ato heḥ, पा. ६-४-१०५) would drop the "hi" after an "a"-ending stem; but the rule असिद्धवदत्राभात् (asiddhavad atrābhāt, पा. ६-४-२२) makes the "m"-elision "asiddha" with respect to it, so that "hi" is not elided — the print argues this at length with the paribhāṣā about "samānāśraya" rules, and concludes that "hi" is retained: "gahi."

"Somapāḥ" — a vocative; by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ८-१-१९) it is wholly unaccented (sarvānudātta). Although by आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (पा. सू. ८-१-७२) it is treated as non-existent, the following "piba" is made unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. सू. ८-१-२८), taking the word before it as the cause. The preceding word "somasya" is not a vocative; the text debates whether the "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (पा. ८-१-७२) and "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (पा. २-१-२) rules apply between "somapāḥ" and "somasya," and concludes that, because the two words lack a mutual syntactic connection ("asāmarthya"), "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur, and "somasya" is not treated as non-existent.

"Godāḥ" — "gāṃ dadāti iti godāḥ": the root "ḍudāñ dāne" (to give), ending in "ā"; आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः would give "ka," but "kvip" (क्विप् च, पा. ३-२-७६) is the general rule; since the Veda has the specific rule आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च (पा. ३-२-७४), "manin, kvanip, vanip" may come after a root ending in "ā" when a subanta or an upasarga stands as upapada; from the "ca" in that sūtra, "vic" also comes — and so on. The page ends in the middle of this argument about which affix applies to "godāḥ"; it continues on the next page. Page headers: p. 98 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 99 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are an advanced scholastic grammatical debate in Kannada prose about whether the "ī"-substitution of घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि (ghu-mā-sthā-gā-pā-jahāti-sāṃ hali, पा. ६-४-६६) can apply to "godāḥ" (the root "dā" with "kvip"). They have no bearing on the sense of the Rik, already given on pp. 95–96, and per the standing convention the argument is characterized in outline rather than transcribe it line by line, keeping the sūtras the pages name. Numbers as read; [?] where uncertain.

original pp. 98–99

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.2 (continued): the "godāḥ" / "īt" debate; "revataḥ"

The question. The "ghu" labelled roots (the roots "dā" and "dhā") take "ī" before an "ārdhadhātuka" affix that begins with a consonant ("hali") and is "k"- or "ṅ"-marked (ईत्वं हलि…). With "kvip," however, the whole affix is elided (वेरपृक्तस्य, पा. ६-१-६७), and "godāḥ" shows no "ī." The page-98 argument asks whether "kvip" can be regarded as an affix beginning with a consonant ("halādi") so as to call for "ī," and answers that it cannot, since it is entirely elided; yet, because of the "pratyaya-lakṣaṇa" principle (प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम्, पा. १-१-६२ — "when an affix is elided, the operation that depends on the affix still applies"), the objector argues "ī" should still come. Two views are put: that this sūtra is vidhāyaka (enabling) or niyāmaka (restricting). The reply draws on the principle वर्णाश्रये नास्ति प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (varṇāśraye nāsti pratyaya-lakṣaṇam — "where the operation depends on a letter, there is no 'pratyaya-lakṣaṇa'"). Examples are taken from "tṛṇahim" (तृणह इम्, पा. ७-३-९२) and "gaveḥitam," and the page notes that when the chief ground of an operation is a letter (varṇa), the prohibition applies; when the chief ground is the affix itself, "pratyaya-lakṣaṇa" applies.

The Mahābhāṣya line (p. 99). The Mahābhāṣya-kāra's phrase ईर्ध्यायतेर्दधातेर्वा [as printed, "dhīrghyāyater dādhāter vā"; read with doubt] is discussed: if "kvip" were added after "dhā," the "ī" of "ghumāsthā" would need to arise; "hali" would then be read as "an-aji" (not "ajādi"), and the reply says that the rule for "ī" requires a "k/ṅ"-marked or "ārdhadhātuka" affix that does not begin with a vowel; in "godāḥ" the "kvip" is "ajādi," since it is elided; therefore "ī" does not arise, and "vic" is taken instead (the "ca" of the sūtra आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च, पा. ३-२-७४, brings in "vic"). A parallel is "saṃśasthā" (अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते, "…aṃbāgo-bhū-" — the sūtra as printed is garbled), where, if "kvip" were assumed, "ī" would again be required, and so "vic" is again assumed. Vārttikas of Kātyāyana (ईत्वे ह्वयतिप्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः [as read]) and the Padamañjarī are cited in support. The conclusion: in "godāḥ" the affix is "vic" (not "kvip") and no "ī" results. The debate is closed with a remark on the "asiddha"/"samprasāraṇa" rules, and on "pratyayāpratyaya-sādhāraṇa" operations (illustrated by सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी, पा. ६-२-१०२ [?], with "sudṛṣat," "śobhanāḥ dṛṣadaḥ yasya prāsādasya"), which I do not reproduce.

"Revataḥ" p. 99, end — "rayiḥ asya asti iti revān": "matup" after "rayi" (तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्, पा. ५-२-९४); the "m" becomes "v" by छन्दसीरः (पा. ८-२-१५), and by रयेर्मतौ बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. ६-१-३७) the "samprasāraṇa" of "y" (to "i") is variably made in the Veda: "rayi + vat" → "revat" (the "ay" becoming "e" by guṇa: आद्गुणः, पा. ६-१-८७, after the "pūrvarūpa" of संप्रसारणाच्च, पा. ६-१-१०८); the nominative singular "revān"; the "matup" is acute by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. ६-१-१७६) (the print says "the acute when the preceding short vowel has the udātta") … Printed references in the grammar of pp. 98–99, in order: Pā. 6-4-66; 1-1-62; 7-3-92; 6-1-37; 6-2-117; then (p. 99) 5-2-94; 8-2-15; 6-1 vā. 6; 6-1-108; 6-1-87; 6-1-166 (Oct 2026 numeral pass).

original p. 100

Rik 4.2 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Third Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

Continuing "revataḥ" from p. 99: …the "matup" is acute as following a word-final short vowel or the augment "nuṭ" (ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप्, पा. ६-१-१७६). "Madaḥ" — "mad" (to be glad) with "ap" (मदोऽनुपसर्गे, पा. ३-३-६७): when a subanta (not an upasarga) stands as upapada before the root "mad," "ap" comes; being "p"-marked it is unaccented. ॥२॥

Sūkta 4, The Third Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथा॑ ते॒ अंत॑मानां वि॒द्याम॑ सुमती॒नां । मा नो॒ अति॑ ख्य॒ आ ग॑हि ॥३॥

áthā te áṃtamānāṃ vidyā́ma sumatīnā́ṃ | mā no áti khya ā́ gahi ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथ । ते । अन्तमानाम् । विद्याम । सुऽमतीनाम् । मा । नः । अति । ख्यः । आ । गहि ॥३॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अथ सोमपानानन्तरं हे इन्द्र ते तवान्तमानामन्तिकतमानामतिशयेन समीपवर्तिनां सुमतीनां शोभनमतियुक्तानां शोभनप्रज्ञानां पुरुषाणां मध्ये स्थित्वा विद्याम । वयं त्वां जानीयाम । यद्वा । सुमतीनां शोभनबुद्धीनां कर्मानुष्ठानविषयाणां लाभार्थमित्यध्याहारः । बुद्धिलाभाय त्वां स्मरेमेत्यर्थः । त्वमपि नोऽस्मानतिक्रम्यान्येषां त्वत्स्वरूपं मा प्रकथय । किंतु त्वा गह्यस्मानेवागच्छ । atha somapānānantaraṃ he indra te tavāntamānām antikatamānām atiśayena samīpa-vartināṃ sumatīnāṃ śobhana-mati-yuktānāṃ śobhana-prajñānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye sthitvā vidyāma | vayaṃ tvāṃ jānīyāma | yadvā | sumatīnāṃ śobhana-buddhīnāṃ karmānuṣṭhāna-viṣayāṇāṃ lābhārtham ity adhyāhāraḥ | buddhi-lābhāya tvāṃ smarema ity arthaḥ | tvam api no 'smān atikramyānyeṣāṃ tvat-svarūpaṃ mā prakathaya | kiṃ tu tvā [print; "tvam"?] gahy asmān evāgaccha |

Translation: "'Atha' — after the drinking of the Soma — 'O Indra, te' — of you; 'antamānām' — of those nearest, those who stand exceedingly close; 'sumatīnām' — of men of good understanding, of good wisdom — standing in the midst of them, 'vidyāma' — we would know you. Or: 'sumatīnām' — 'of good understanding' — the supplied sense is 'for the obtaining of understanding for those engaged in the performance of rites'; that is, 'we would remember you for the gaining of understanding.' And you, passing us over, do not declare your own form to others; but come to us ('ā gahi')." The print's "tvā gahy" is read as the sentence "kiṃ tu … gahi — come to us alone"; the second word of the clause is slightly unclear, and it is given as printed with the sense the Kannada gives.

अथेति निपात आद्युदात्तः । निपातस्य चेति दीर्घत्वम् । अन्तमानाम् । अतिशयेनान्तिका इत्यतिशायने तमप् । पा. ५-३-५५ । तमो तादेशश्च । पा. ६-४-१५४-९ । इति तादिलोपः । अन्तोऽस्यास्तीत्यन्तिकः समीपः । अत इनिठनाविति ठन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दूरोत्कर्षस्य ह्यवसानं नास्ति । सामीप्योत्कर्षस्य पुनर्यो यस्य समीपः स एव तस्यान्त इत्यन्तवत्त्वात्सामीप्यमन्तिकमुच्यते । विद्याम । वेत्तेर्लिङ् । यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च । पा. ३-४-१०३ । इति यासुडुदात्तः । पादादित्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति न निघातः । सुमतीनाम् । मतिशब्दे क्तिन्नन्तेऽपि मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः । पा. ३-३-९६ । athety nipāta ādyudāttaḥ | nipātasya ceti dīrghatvam | antamānām | atiśayenāntikā ity atiśāyane tamap | pā. 5-3-55 | tamo tādeśaś ca | pā. 6-4-154-9 | iti tādi-lopaḥ | anto 'syāstīty antikaḥ samīpaḥ | ata inithanāv iti ṭhan | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | dūrotkarṣasya hy avasānaṃ nāsti | sāmīpyotkarṣasya punar yo yasya samīpaḥ sa eva tasyānta ity antavattvāt sāmīpyam antikam ucyate | vidyāma | vetter liṅ | yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca | pā. 3-4-103 | iti yāsuḍ udāttaḥ | pādāditvāt tiṅ atiṅa iti na nighātaḥ | sumatīnām | matiśabde ktinnante 'pi mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ | pā. 3-3-96 |

Translation (of the grammar, in outline, with its sūtras): "'Atha' — a particle, hence first-syllable acute; by निपातस्य च (पा. ६-३-१३६) the lengthening in 'athā.' 'Antamānām' — 'atiśayena antikāḥ': the affix 'tamap' in the sense of excess (अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ, पा. ५-३-५५), with the replacement of the 'ti'-portion (तिल्लोपः as printed, "tādi-lopaḥ") — 'anto 'syāstīti antikaḥ' — 'near'; 'ṭhan' by अत इनिठनौ (पा. ५-२-११५); being 'n'-marked (nit) it is first-syllable acute. For there is no limit (avasāna) to 'far-ness'; but in the excellence of 'near-ness' he who is near to someone is that someone's 'anta' (end); thus nearness is called 'antika' on account of the 'anta'-possessing. 'Vidyāma' — 'vid' in the optative (liṅ); 'yāsuṭ' is acute in the parasmaipada (यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च, पा. ३-४-१०३); since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, 'tiṅ atiṅaḥ' does not cause nighāta. 'Sumatīnām' — 'mati' ending in 'ktin' is acute in the Veda by मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६)…" Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; English as printed.

original p. 101

Rik 4.3: grammar concluded; Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

Grammar, continuing "sumatīnām": …the "i" of "mati" is acute (the Sanskrit of p. 100 gives the rule); "śobhanā matir yeṣāṃ te sumatayaḥ" — a bahuvrīhi, in which the first member's natural accent is overridden by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२), so the last syllable of the second member is acute; but where "śobhanā matayaḥ sumatayaḥ" is a karmadhāraya, there is an exception to the first-member accent in the case of an indeclinable prefix, and the second member has the natural accent given by कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् — it is end-acute. After "matup" (as short-final-acute), the genitive-plural "nām" of "sumati" is acute by नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. ६-१-१७७).

"Khyaḥ" — the root "khyā prakathane" (to declare), the aorist (luṅ) second-person singular "sip" → "khyā + si"; च्लि लुङि (cli luṅi, पा. ३-१-४३) puts "cli" after the root in "luṅ"; सिचि … by अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङ् (asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ, पा. ३-१-५२) "aṅ" replaces "cli" after "as," "vac," "khyā"; आतो लोप इटि च (पा. ६-४-६४) elides the final "ā" before "aṅ" — "khya + a + s"; इतश्च (itaś ca, पा. ३-४-१०० [as printed]) elides the final "i" of parasmaipada endings (here of "sip," giving "s"); the "s" is changed to "ru" and visarga: ससजुषो रुः (पा. ८-२-६६) and खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः (पा. ८-३-१५) → "khyaḥ." After "mā," न माङ्योगे (na māṅ-yoge, पा. ६-४-७४) — the augment "aṭ" does not occur → "mā khyaḥ."

"Gahi" — from "gam"; the "śap" is elided by "bahulaṃ chandasi"; because "hi" replaces "si" (सेर्ह्यपिच्च, पा. ३-४-८७) it is not "p"-marked; so the "m" of the root is elided by अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७); the elision, being "asiddha" (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, पा. ६-४-२२), does not permit the "hi"-loss that अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) would otherwise require → "gahi."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अथ (atha) — after the drinking of the Soma | (हे इन्द्र) (he indra) — O Indra | वयम् (vayam) — we | ते (te) — your | अन्तमानाम् (antamānām) — of those who are exceedingly near | सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — of men of good understanding (of the discerning, or of the wise) — in their midst | विद्याम (vidyāma) — we know you (we remember you, or, for the sake of obtaining wisdom for the performance of rites, we remember you) | (त्वम् अपि) नः (naḥ) — us | अति (ati) — passing over (to others) | मा ख्यः (mā khyaḥ) — do not declare (your own form) | आ गहि (ā gahi) — be one who comes (to our side).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! After the drinking of the Soma, we, being near you, remember you for the sake of good understanding in the performance of good works, or for the gaining of excellent wisdom. You must come near us. Do not make your form known to others, and do not cause them to have good understanding.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"We recognize you in the midst of the right-minded who are nearest to you; come to us; do not reveal yourself to others."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this Ṛk, apart from a few special words that are difficult, the ṛṣi's intention is not very clear, though the words are easy and commonly used. The Bhāṣyakāra and others have written the meaning, by using some supplied words (adhyāhāra), in such a way that it can be understood somewhat; but the sense is not quite … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." English as printed.

Special topics on Rik 4.3; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

…it does not fit well. To make clear the sense of the sentences "sumatīnāṃ vidyāma" and "mā no ati khyaḥ," still some more words are needed, and such words are not in the Ṛk. Whether it be because the loss (of words) is a Vedic licence (chandasi), or because the ṛṣi has left out some words that were necessary and chief, thinking that the intention in his own mind would be clear from the words in the Ṛk — it appears so. Hence the sense of this Ṛk and of the next two or three Ṛks remains unclear.

अथा (athā) — the letter "a" of "thā" [the syllable "tha"] of this word is lengthened in accord with Vedic usage. Such examples are needed in the Ṛgveda. For example: sacasva — sacasvā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-9), śrudhi — śrudhī (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1), pṛccha — pṛcchā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-4-4), piba — pibā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-10), and the like.

सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — The explanation of this word has already been given (see p. 81).

मा (mā) — a negative word of prohibition, "do not." This word is used especially in the Veda. अति (ati) — "beyond, besides, passing over" English as printed: "Beyond, besides &c.".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Atha" — a nipāta, so first-syllable acute (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः); निपातस्य च (पा. ६-३-१३६) lengthens the vowel in mantra: "athā." "Antamānām" — "antaḥ asya asti" ("this has an end"), the etymology of "antika": by अत इनिठनौ (पा. ५-२-११५) "ini" or "ṭhan" after a stem ending in short "a"; with "ṭhan," ठस्येकः (ṭhasyekaḥ, पा. ७-३-५०) gives "ika": "anta + ika"; by यस्येति च (पा. ६-४-१४८) the "a" of the stem is elided → "antika." There is no limit to remoteness; but for the excellence of proximity, "that which is near to something has its 'end' there"; because it has an "anta" (limit), the word "antika" means "near." "Atiśayena antikāḥ" — to express excess, अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (पा. ५-३-५५) puts "tamap" after the stem in the sense of excess → "antika + tama"; तमो …: तिकतमः — by टेः / "ti-ka"-loss (as printed: तेस्तादेशश्च, पा. ६-४-१५४ वा. ९) the "tika" portion [as printed: "ti-ka"] is elided before "tamap"; the result is "antama." In the genitive plural, "antamānām." "Vidyāma" — from "vid jñāne" (to know) by liṅ; for the "liṅ" यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — in the parasmaipada the augment "yāsuṭ" comes, which is acute and "ṅit" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; numbers as read.

original p. 103

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.3 concluded

…"yāsuṭ" is acute; because the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) does not bring nighāta. "Sumatīnām" — the word "mati" ends in "ktin," but in the Veda मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. ३-३-९६ [as printed]) makes the affix acute after the roots "vṛṣ" (to shower), "iṣ" (to wish), "duṣ-pac" (to cook), "man" (to think), "vid" (to be), "bhū," "vī" (and "rā" in "rādaḥ"); so after "man," "ktin" is added, and अनुदात्तोपदेश… (पा. ६-४-३७) drops the nasal of "man" → "mati"; the "i" of "ktin" is acute by the preceding sūtra. "Śobhanā matiḥ yeṣāṃ te sumatayaḥ" — as a bahuvrīhi the first member's natural accent is overridden by नञ्सुभ्याम्; "śobhanāś ca tāḥ matayaḥ" — as a karmadhāraya the indeclinable-prefix accent is overridden by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९), and the second member is end-acute. When "matup" is not applied, the genitive-plural "nām" of "sumati" (short-final, end-acute stem) takes the acute by नामन्यतरस्याम् (पा. ६-१-१७७).

"Khyaḥ" — "khyā prakathane": in the aorist (luṅ), second-person singular "sip" — ख्या + सिप्; after the root in "luṅ," "cli" (च्लि लुङि, पा. ३-१-४३); "cli" is replaced by "aṅ" after the roots "as," "vac" and "khyā" (अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङ्, पा. ३-१-५२); "ā" elided (आतो लोप इटि च, पा. ६-४-६४); the "i" of the ending "sip" elided (इतश्च, पा. ३-४-१००) — "khya + a + s"; "s" → "ru" → visarga (ससजुषो रुः, पा. ८-२-६६; रुत्वविसर्गौ) → "khyaḥ." After "mā," न माङ्योगे (पा. ६-४-७४): no "aṭ" (and, by the print, no "āṭ") augment, and the rule लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः (पा. ६-४-७१) which would give the "aḍ" augment does not apply.

"Gahi" — "gam gatau," imperative (loṭ) second-person singular "sip"; "śap" is elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. २-४-७३); सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) puts "hi" in the place of "sip," and the "sārvadhātuka" not being "p"-marked is "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, पा. १-२-४) — by the root's "anudātta-upadeśa" the "m" is dropped (अनुदात्तोपदेश…, पा. ६-४-३७); since the "m"-loss is "asiddha" (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, पा. ६-४-२२), the "hi" does not lose its place by अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) → "gahi." ॥३॥ Re-checked against the better scan: p. 103 ends with the grammar of Rik 4.3, "॥३॥"; it prints no varga-closing line. The seventh varga closes on p. 111.

Sūkta 4, Fourth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pada-meanings (opening)

Sūkta 4, The Fourth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

परे॑हि॒ विग्र॒मस्तृ॑त॒मिंद्रं॑ पृच्छा विप॒श्चितं॑ । यस्ते॒ सखि॑भ्य आ वरं॑ ॥४॥

párehi vígramástṛtamíṃdraṃ pṛcchā vipaścítaṃ | yaste sákhibhya ā váraṃ ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: the Saṃhitā text reads "pṛcchā" with a long final vowel (a Vedic lengthening); the Pada text has "pṛccha." The word "vipaścitam" is divided in the Pada text as "vipaḥ-citam," as read from the printed sign.

परा । इहि । विग्रम् । अस्तृतम् । इन्द्रम् । पृच्छ । विपःऽचितम् । यः । ते । सखिऽभ्यः । आ । वरम् ॥४॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अत्र यजमानं प्रति होता ब्रूते । हे यजमान त्वमिन्द्रं परेहि । इन्द्रस्य समीपे गच्छ । गत्वा च विपश्चितं मेधाविनं होतारं मां पृच्छ । असौ होता सम्यक् स्तुतवान्न चेत्येवं प्रश्नं कुरु । य इन्द्रस्ते तव यजमानस्य सखिभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्यो वरं श्रेष्ठं धनपुत्रादिकमा समन्तात्प्रयच्छतीति शेषः । तादृशमिन्द्रमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । पुनरपि कीदृशम् । विग्रं मेधाविनमस्तृतमहिंसितम् । विप्र इत्यादिषु चतुर्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु मेधाविनामसु विग्रो विपश्चिच्चेति पठितौ । विग्रं वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । अस्तृतम् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । इन्द्रशब्द ऋजेन्द्राग्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सखिभ्यः । समाने ख्यः ... उ. ४-१३६ । इति समान उपपदे ख्यातेरिन् । डिदित्यनुवृत्तेस्तस्य डित्त्वाट्टिलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-१४३ । तत्सन्नियोगेन यलोपः । उपपदस्योदात्तत्वम् । समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु । पा. ६-३-८४ । इति सभावः । अतः सखिशब्द आद्युदात्तः । व्रियत इति वरः । ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च । पा. ३-३-५८ । इत्यप् । तस्य पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वर एव ॥ atra yajamānaṃ prati hotā brūte | he yajamāna tvam indraṃ parehi | indrasya samīpe gaccha | gatvā ca vipaścitaṃ medhāvinaṃ hotāraṃ māṃ pṛccha | asau hotā samyak stutavān na ceti evaṃ praśnaṃ kuru | ya indras te tava yajamānasya sakhibhya ṛtvigbhyo varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhana-putrādikam ā samantāt prayacchatīti śeṣaḥ | tādṛśam indram iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | punar api kīdṛśam | vigraṃ medhāvinam astṛtam ahiṃsitam | vipra ity ādiṣu catur-viṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu medhāvi-nāmasu vigro vipaścic ceti paṭhitau | vigraṃ vṛṣādi-tvād ādyudāttaḥ | astṛtam | avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | indra-śabda ṛjendrāgrety ādinā ran | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | sakhibhyaḥ | samāne khyaḥ … u. 4-136 | iti samāna upapade khyāter in | ḍid ity anuvṛtter tasya ḍittvāṭ ṭilopaś ca | pā. 6-4-143 | tat-sanniyogena yalopaḥ | upapadasyodāttatvam | samānasya chandasy amūrdha-prabhṛty-udarkeṣu | pā. 6-3-84 | iti sabhāvaḥ | ataḥ sakhi-śabda ādyudāttaḥ | vriyata iti varaḥ | grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca | pā. 3-3-58 | ity ap | tasya pittvād dhātusvara eva ||

Translation: "Here the Hotṛ speaks to the sacrificer: 'O sacrificer, go to Indra ("parehi"): go into the presence of Indra; and having gone, ask me, the Hotṛ, 'vipaścitam' — the wise — "Has this Hotṛ praised properly or not?" — put the question thus. That Indra who gives 'varam' — the best, wealth, sons and the like — in full ('ā') to 'te sakhibhyaḥ' — to your friends, the priests (ṛtvijaḥ) of you the sacrificer' — such is the supplied sense. The construction 'such an Indra' connects with what went before. Of what sort again? 'Vigram' — wise; 'astṛtam' — unharmed. Among the twenty-four names for 'wise' beginning with 'vipra,' 'vigra' and 'vipaścit' are read." The Bhāṣya's reading "vipaścitam … pṛccha māṃ hotāram" makes the ṛtvij the one to be asked; It is given as printed.

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Vigram" — first-syllable acute as belonging to the "vṛṣādi" class; "astṛtam" — the first-member accent (an indeclinable prefix) is retained; "Indra" — by the Uṇādi "ṛjrendrāgra-…" (as on p. 39) the affix "ran," "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute; "sakhibhyaḥ" — समाने ख्यः [the Uṇādi sūtra, number garbled: "4-136" ?], from "khyā" after "samāna" as upapada with "in," "ḍit," with elision of "ṭi" (टेः, पा. ६-४-१४३) and of "y"; the upapada's acute; the substitution "sa" for "samāna" by समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु (पा. ६-३-८४); hence "sakhi" is first-syllable acute. "Varam" — "vriyate iti varaḥ": "ap" by ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च (पा. ३-३-५८); "p"-marked, so the root's accent remains.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

In this Ṛk the priest called the Hotṛ speaks, addressing the sacrificer —

(O sacrificer, you) विग्रम् (vigram) — the wise | इन्द्रम् परेहि (indram parehi) — go to Indra's side | (having gone) अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — (about Indra) who is not struck by the harm of enemies | विपश्चितम् पृच्छ (vipaścitam pṛccha) — ask this wise one (whether the Hotṛ has praised you properly or not) | यः (yaḥ) — (the Indra who) | ते (te) — your | सखिभ्यः (sakhibhyaḥ) — to the friendly priests | वरम् (varam) — excellent wealth, sons and the like | आ (yacchati) — gives. Rik 4.4: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Hotṛ speaks thus, addressing the sacrificer: O sacrificer! Go to the side of Indra, who is wise (intelligent) — and ask him whether this Hotṛ has praised you well. Because Indra is pleased with the hymns that the Hotṛ has chanted, he will favour you, and your friends the priests, with the best boons — wealth, sons and the like.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Go (worshipper) to the wise (and) uninjured Indra and ask him of the (fitness of the) learned (priest who recites his praise.) Indra will bestow the best of blessings to your friends (priests)."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

विग्रम्, विपश्चितम् (vigram, vipaścitam) — These words are read among the twenty-four words that indicate "intelligent" (Ni. 3-15). For these words the sense is "buddhimān, medhāvī, vivekin" (one with understanding, intelligent, discerning). The word "vigra" is used in the Ṛgveda in only two places. In the present Ṛk, and also in the Ṛk

ता विग्रं धैथे जठरं पृणध्या आ यत्सद्म सभृतयः पृणन्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-६७-७) tā vigraṃ dhaithe jaṭharaṃ pṛṇadhyā ā yat sadma sabhṛtayaḥ pṛṇanti || (ṛ. saṃ. 6-67-7) Gloss (mine; tentative; the print gives only this line): "You two keep the wise one, to fill the belly, when those who bring together fill the abode."

this word is used. Nowhere else. The word "vipaścit" is used in about 23 places in the Ṛgveda.

अस्तृतम् (astṛtam) — The negative form of the word "stṛta," formed from the root "stṛ"; "na stṛtam = astṛtam" — not struck down, "ahiṃsitam" ("unharmed").

सखिभ्यः (sakhibhyaḥ) — "To the friends" — that is, to the priests who are called the sacrificer's friends. On the point that the priests are the sacrificer's friends:

आ प्यायस्व सखीन्त्सन्या मेधयेत्याहर्त्विजो वा अस्य सखायस्तानेवाप्याययेति ॥ (तै. सं. ६-२-२) ā pyāyasva sakhīn tsanyā medhayety āhartvijo vā asya sakhāyas tān evāpyāyayeti || (tai. saṃ. 6-2-2) Translation (mine, following the Kannada gloss): "'Swell, bring your friends to prosperity with intelligence' — thus he says; the priests, indeed, are his (the sacrificer's) friends; he swells them indeed." — The Kannada adds: here "ṛtvijo vā asya sakhāyaḥ" says plainly that the priests are the sacrificer's friends.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Parā" — a nipāta, first-syllable acute by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); by the "śeṣa-anudātta" the last letter is unaccented. In the saṃhitā, the "ā" of "parā" combines, by guṇa-sandhi, with the unaccented "i" of "ihi," giving "e" as the single substitute; this single substitute, coming in place of unaccented vowels … Page headers: p. 106 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4"; p. 107 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose, the Kannada rendering of the grammar given in Sanskrit on p. 104, with a good deal of added scholastic debate. They do not bear on the sense of the Rik, which was given on pp. 104–105. Per the standing convention they are characterized in outline, not translated line by line; the sūtras the pages name are kept in three layers, numbers as read, [?] where uncertain. Several sentences in the middle of p. 106 and the foot of p. 107 are crowded in the print and are not reproduced.

original pp. 106–107

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 4.4 (Kannada) — characterized

p. 106 — "parā," "ihi," "vigram." - Continuing "parehi" from p. 105. The single substitute "e" replaces the pair of unaccented vowels, and is by स्थानिवदादेशोऽनल्विधौ (sthānivad ādeśo 'nal-vidhau, पा. १-१-५६) treated as the original, hence unaccented; since it comes after the acute "ra," it becomes svarita by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. ८-४-६६). - "Ihi" — "iṇ gatau" (to go); in the imperative second-person singular "sip," सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) puts "hi" for "si"; the "śap" is elided as the root belongs to the "ad" class (अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः, पा. २-४-७२); since "hi" is not "p"-marked, the "sārvadhātuka" is "ṅit" (सार्वधातुकमपित्, पा. १-२-४); hence guṇa is barred by क्ङिति च (पा. १-१-५) and by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "ihi." Since "ihi" stands after "parā," which is not a tiṅanta, तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. ८-१-२८) makes it wholly unaccented. - "Vigram" — two analyses are weighed. (a) From "gṛ śabde" (to sound) with the upasarga "vi" and the affix "ḍa" by अन्येष्वपि दृश्यते (पा. ३-२-१०१) — "ḍa" after any root, since the sūtra says "dṛśyate" ("is seen") — with the "ṭi"-loss debated, and "ṛ" becoming "r" by yaṇ ("vi-gr-a"); the accent then follows the compound rule गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. ६-२-१३९), which would give an end-acute that is not the attested accent. (b) Therefore the word is entered in the "vṛṣādi" class (वृषादीनां च, पा. ६-१-२०३) and is first-syllable acute — "vigra," as in विचिर् पृथग्भावे (the root "vicir pṛthagbhāve") with the intensive/causal sense "viveka": "viśeṣeṇa gṛhṇāti" ("he takes in a special way") = "vigraḥ" (the wise, discerning). Different derivations are offered; the page concludes that either way the sense is "medhāvī."

p. 107 — "vigram" concluded; "astṛtam," "indra," "sakhibhyaḥ." - The Uṇādi affix "ran" is considered for "vigra" (ऋज्रेन्द्राग्रवज्रविप्र…, as on p. 39) — "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute; the second-case singular "am" (an "ap"-class ending) is joined with a pūrvarūpa by अमि पूर्वः (पा. ६-१-१०७). - "Astṛtam" — "na stṛtam"; by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ… (पा. ६-२-२) — with an indeclinable first member the first member's own accent is retained. - "Indra" — by the Uṇādi list "ṛjrendrāgra-vajra-vipra-kubra-cubra-kṣura-khura-bhadrogra-bhera-bhela-śukra-śakla-gaurava-nvera-mālāḥ [?]" (उ. सू. २-२८ [as printed "3-1…"]) "ran" is added; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute; the last letter is unaccented by "śeṣānudātta"; in the saṃhitā it is svarita by उदात्तस्वरितपरस्य सन्नतरः (पा. १-२-४०) in the way already described. - "Sakhibhyaḥ" — समाने ख्य… (Uṇādi-sūtra: the print gives "ṭi-sū. 4-…"; I could not settle the number): after "khyā" with "samāna" as the upapada, the affix "iṇ"; "ḍit" and hence टेः (पा. ६-४-१४३) loss of "ṭi" (the vowel-end) and of "y" (the "ya"-loss); the upapada is acute; समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु (पा. ६-३-८४) substitutes "sa" for "samāna" (the first member, when the second begins with a non-"mūrdhan"-class word) → "sakhi," first-syllable acute. The Uṇādi-sūtra समानेख्यः सश्चोदात्तः [as printed] is also cited, with the remark that the grammarians of the Mādhava school hold that "sa" is substituted in the Veda by the rule "samānasya chandasi mūrdha…," and that in ordinary speech the word "sakhi" is established by Svaramañjarī-kāra and others by other rules. The page ends mid-sentence in this comparison, continuing on p. 108.

original p. 108

Rik 4.4 grammar concluded; Sūkta 4, Fifth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

Continuing "sakhibhyaḥ" from p. 107: …in the system of the Mādhava school the word "sakhi" is established only in the Veda (by the "samānasya chandasi…" rule). "Varam" — "vriyate iti varaḥ": ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च (पा. ३-३-५८) — after "grah," "vṛ," "dṛ," "niścī [print: niści]" and "gam" the affix "ap" comes; "vṛ + a" takes guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "varaḥ"; "ap" is "p"-marked and so unaccented, "va" is acute by धातोः (पा. ६-१-१६२). ॥४॥

Sūkta 4, The Fifth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उ॒त ब्रु॑वंतु नो॒ निदो॒ निर॒न्यत॑श्चिदारत । दधा॑ना इन्द्र इद्दुवः॑ ॥५॥

utá bruvaṃtu no nído níranyátaścidārata | dádhānā indra iddúvaḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading note: the Saṃhitā text reads "indra id duvaḥ"; the Pada text resolves it as "indre it duvaḥ." The printed Pada text shows "ā-rata" as one word.

उत । ब्रुवन्तु । नः । निदः । निः । अन्यतः । चित् । आरत । दधानाः । इन्द्रे । इत् । दुवः ॥५॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नोऽस्माकं संबन्धिन ऋत्विज इति शेषः । ते ब्रुवन्तु । इन्द्रं स्तुवन्तु । उतमपि च हे निदो निन्दितारः पुरुषा निरारत । इतो देशान्निर्गच्छत । अन्यतश्चिदन्यस्मादपि देशान्निर्गच्छत । कीदृशा ऋत्विजः । इन्द्रे दुवः परिचर्यां दधानाः कुर्वाणाः । इच्छब्दोऽवधारणे । सर्वदा परिचर्यां कुर्वन्त एव तिष्ठन्तित्यर्थः । निन्दन्तीति निदः । णिदि कुत्सायाम् । क्विपि नुमभावश्छान्दसः । सुपोऽनुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः । आमन्त्रितत्वेऽपि वाक्यान्तरस्थेन स्ववाक्यगतपदादत्स्वरत्वान्न निघात इत्याद्युदात्तत्वमेव । अन्यतः । लिति प्रत्ययोत्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं चिदित्यपिकबर्थे । तेन न केवलमितः । इतो निर्गत्यान्यतोऽपि निर्गच्छतेति गम्यते । स एष धात्वर्थयोः संबन्ध आरतेति लुजा द्योत्यते । स हि धातुसंबन्धाधिकारे विधीयते । आरत । अर्तेश्छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति लोडर्थे लुङ् । मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तादेशः । सर्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च । पा. ३-१-५६ । इति च्लेरङादेशः । ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः । पा. ७-४-१६ । इति गुणः । आडागमः । दधानाः । शानचश्चित्त्वात्तत्प्राप्तमन्तोदात्तं बाधित्वा परत्वादभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । दुवः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः ॥५॥ no 'smākaṃ sambandhina ṛtvija iti śeṣaḥ | te bruvantu | indraṃ stuvantu | utamapi ca he nido nindi-tāraḥ puruṣā nir ārata | ito deśān nirgacchata | anyataś cid anyasmād api deśān nirgacchata | kīdṛśā ṛtvijaḥ | indre duvaḥ paricaryāṃ dadhānāḥ kurvāṇāḥ | ic chabdo 'vadhāraṇe | sarvadā paricaryāṃ kurvanta eva tiṣṭhantity arthaḥ | nindantīti nidaḥ | ṇidi kutsāyām | kvipi numa-bhāvaś chāndasaḥ | supo 'nudāttatvād dhātusvaraḥ | āmantritatve 'pi vākyāntarasthena sva-vākya-gata-padād-at-svaratvān na nighāta ity ādyudāttatvam eva | anyataḥ | liti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvaṃ cid ity apika-barthe | tena na kevalam itaḥ | ito nirgatyānyato 'pi nirgacchateti gamyate | sa eṣa dhātvarthayoḥ sambandha āratety luñā dyotyate | sa hi dhātu-sambandhādhikāre vidhīyate | ārata | arter chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭa iti loḍarthe luṅ | madhyama-bahuvacanasya tādeśaḥ | sarti-śāsty-arti-bhyaś ca | pā. 3-1-56 | iti cler aṅādeśaḥ | ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ | pā. 7-4-16 | iti guṇaḥ | āḍāgamaḥ | dadhānāḥ | śānacaś cittvāt tat-prāptam antodāttaṃ bādhitvā paratvād abhyastānām ādir ity ādyudāttatvam | duvaḥ | nab-viṣayasyānisantasyety ādyudāttaḥ ||5||

Translation: "'Naḥ' — the supplied sense is 'our priests, those belonging to us.' Let them speak, let them praise Indra. And, O 'nidaḥ' — O revilers, men who blame — 'nirārata' — go out from here, from this place; 'anyataś cit' — go out from any other place as well. What kind of priests? 'Duvaḥ dadhānāḥ' — those who perform service ('paricaryā') in Indra; 'it' is in the sense of emphasis: the sense is 'they remain doing service at all times.' 'Nidaḥ' — 'nindantīti nidaḥ' — those who blame; the root 'ṇidi kutsāyām' (to blame); in the 'kvip' formation the absence of the 'num' augment is Vedic; the accent is that of the root since the case-ending is unaccented; though a vocative, since it stands in a different sentence from the preceding word, there is no nighāta (loss of accent), and so it is first-syllable acute indeed. 'Anyataḥ' — the part before the affix is acute; 'cit' has the sense of 'api' (also): not only from here, but from elsewhere too — 'having gone out from here, go out from other places also' is understood. This connection of the senses of the roots is indicated by the 'luṅ' in 'ārata.' 'Ārata' — the root 'ṛ' in the Veda takes 'luṅ' in the sense of the imperative (छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः, पा. ३-४-६); the second-person plural ending is replaced by 'ta'; the 'cli' is replaced by 'aṅ' (सर्त्तिशास्त्यर्त्तिभ्यश्च, पा. ३-१-५६); guṇa by ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः (पा. ७-४-१६); the augment 'āṭ.' 'Dadhānāḥ' — because 'śānac' is 'c'-marked, the end-acute that this would give is set aside, and, by the later rule अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९), the first syllable is acute. 'Duvaḥ' — first-syllable acute by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (a Phiṭ-sūtra, as on p. 39). ॥५॥" Reading notes: (i) in the second sentence of the Bhāṣya the print has "utamapi ca"; the sense is "uta api ca," as the Rik itself reads "uta"; The print is transcribed as it stands. (ii) "ṇidi kutsāyām" is printed with the root-initial "ṇ," as in the dhātupāṭha. (iii) The reference "pā. 7-4-16" is printed "7-4-16," and it is given so, though it has not been verified. Rik 4.5: Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रे इत् (indre it) — in Indra alone (only in Indra) | दुवः (duvaḥ) — service (that is, worship) | दधानाः (dadhānāḥ) — those who make | नः (naḥ) — our (priests) | ब्रुवन्तु (bruvantu) — let them praise (Indra) | उत (uta) — and | निदः (nidaḥ) — men who blame (Indra) | अन्यतश्चित् (anyataś cit) — from here, and from other places too | निरारत (nirārata) — go out.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Let our priests (and sons and other kinsmen), who are devoted to the service of Indra, praise Indra; and let the men who blame Indra go out from here and from other places as well.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Let our (priests and relatives) engaged in the service of Indra, sing his praises. O revilers, depart from (here and) every other place."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Other commentators, and Western scholars too, have explained the meaning of this Ṛk in various ways English as printed:

  1. Wilson — "Let our ministers earnestly performing his worship exclaim, — depart, ye revilers from hence and every other place (where he is adored)."

  2. Dr. Sitanath — "Let our revilers say — you have estranged yourself from all other (gods) because of your having preference of service only for Indra."

  3. Vedarthayatna — "Whether the revilers may say to us that we might indeed be lost to all other gods by serving Indra alone."

नः (naḥ) — The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word "naḥ" as "our" ("belonging to us, our priests who share in our sacrifice"). Skandasvāmī says "priests, and sons and others." But, rather than supplying the words "priests" or "sons and others," to explain "naḥ" by joining it with the word "nidaḥ" would be more fitting … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 110

Special topics on Rik 4.5 (continued); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins

Continuing "naḥ" from p. 109: …to explain "naḥ" together with "nidaḥ" would be more fitting; that is, "naḥ nidaḥ" — "our revilers, those who revile us." When it is explained thus, it is not necessary to supply a sense such as "let them praise Indra" for the verb "bruvantu"; rather, the sentence "uta bruvantu no nidaḥ" gets the sense "let the revilers of us say (what they will)."

निदः (nidaḥ) — "ṇidi kutsāyām" (to blame): "nindantīti nidaḥ" — since they are those who blame, they are called "nidaḥ."

अन्यतः (anyataḥ) — In this Ṛk the word is only "anyataḥ," "from elsewhere"; therefore the word "itaḥ" ("from here") must be supplied here.

चित् (cit) — "api," "also." इत् (it) — "eva," "indeed": it is used here in the sense of emphasis.

दुवः (duvaḥ) — This word is used in many Ṛks to give various senses. For this word such senses may be given as : "paricaryā (service), sevā, zeal, favour, preference, homage, zeal for service, gift, present" and the like.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ "Nidaḥ" — "nindanti iti nidaḥ"; "kvip" after the root "ṇidi kutsāyām." The root is "i"-marked (iditaḥ), and by इदितो नुम् धातोः (idito num dhātoḥ, पा. ७-१-५८) the augment "num" would be added; but, because of the Vedic variation of all rules ("chandasi vikalpa"), it does not occur here. "Nidaḥ" — the case-ending "sup" is unaccented, and the accent of the root remains (the "i" is acute by the root-accent). "Bruvantu naḥ" — one sentence: "let our priests praise Indra." "Nir ārata anyataś cit" — another sentence: "(you who blame) go out, leaving this place, and leaving other places also." "Nidaḥ" is a vocative that stands at the beginning of the second sentence; so it is not treated as following the preceding word; by the vārttika समानवाक्ये निघातयुष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः [as printed] the nighāta applies only in the same sentence, and thus the vocative does not lose its accent; by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. ६-१-१९८) it is first-syllable acute. "Anyataḥ" — "anyasmāt" with the affix "tasil" by पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (पा. ५-३-७ [as printed "…-3-1"]); since "tasil" is "l"-marked, लिति (पा. ६-१-१९३) puts the acute on the syllable before the affix. "Cit" — has the sense of "api." Hence the meaning: "not only from this place but from other places too — go out." The connection of the senses of the two roots is shown… Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Note on the varga number (re-checked against the better scan): the page headers read "Varga 7" on pp. 89–109 and "Varga 8" on pp. 111–143; the closing note on this page, "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಏಳನೆಯ ವರ್ಗವು ಮುಗಿದುದು" ("here the seventh varga is finished"), is consistent with them (the eighth varga begins on this page with Rik 4.6).

original p. 111

Rik 4.5 grammar concluded; end of the Eighth Varga [as printed "seventh"]; Sūkta 4, Sixth Mantra: Saṃhitā and Pada

Continuing from p. 110: …the connection of the senses of the two roots is shown by the "luṅ" in "ārata," which is laid down in the section on the connection of roots (धातुसंबन्धे प्रत्ययाः, पा. ३-४-१); where the roots' senses are connected, the affixes denoting the three times (past, future, present) may be used optionally for one another; hence "luṅ" comes in the sense of the imperative (loṭ). After "luṅ," "cli" (च्लि लुङि, पा. ३-१-४३) comes; the second-person plural ending "tha" → "ta" (तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्ताम्, पा. ३-४-१०१); by सर्तिशास्त्यर्तिभ्यश्च (पा. ३-१-५६) "cli" is replaced by "aṅ" after "sṛ," "śās" and "ṛ" → "ṛ + a + ta"; ऋदृशोऽङि गुणः (पा. ७-४-१६) gives guṇa → "ar-a-ta"; the augment "āṭ" (आडजादीनाम्, पा. ६-४-७२) → "ā + ar + ata"; the vṛddhi by आटश्च (पा. ६-१-९०) as the single substitute → "ārata." "Dadhānāḥ" — "śānac" is "c"-marked and would give an end-acute; but, by the rule that the later of two conflicting rules prevails (विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम्, पा. १-४-२), अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९) gives first-syllable acute. "Duvaḥ" — नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (a Phiṭ-sūtra): a neuter word not ending in "is/-s" is acute on its first syllable; "duvaḥ" is therefore first-syllable acute. ॥५॥

ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಏಳನೆಯ ವರ್ಗವು ಮುಗಿದುದು — illige ēḷaneya vargavu mugidudu — "Here the seventh varga is finished."

Sūkta 4, The Sixth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उ॒त नः॑ सु॒भगां॑ अ॒रिर्वो॒चेयु॑र्दस्म कृष्टयः॑ । स्यामेदिंद्र॑स्य शर्म॑णि ॥६॥

utá naḥ subhágāṃ arírvocéyurdasma kṛṣṭáyaḥ | syāmedíṃdrasya śármaṇi ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Reading notes: (i) the printed Saṃhitā shows "subhagā" with a mark above the last letter which is read as a nasal sign, giving "subhagāṃ" — standing for the Pada's "subhagān" — but the reading is not certain. (ii) The Pada has "ariḥ" with the "ḥ"; the Saṃhitā "arir" is its sandhi form. (iii) The Pada text, as printed, divides "su-bhagān" with a visible sign; It is given so. उत । नः । सुऽभगान् । अरिः । वोचेयुः । दस्म । कृष्टयः । स्याम । इत् । इन्द्रस्य । शर्मणि ॥६॥

original p. 112

Sūkta 4, Sixth Mantra: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Reading note: the second sentence's "ariḥ uta śatrur" — the print has "ariruta śatrurvo 'pi"; the "vo" that follows "śatruḥ" looks like a printer's slip for the next word's "vocēyuḥ" run on; It is given as read and marked [?]. The final "syāmed … bhavema eva" is printed with an irregular spelling, "bhavemyaiva," which is read as "bhavema eva."

हे दस्म शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितरिन्द्र त्वदनुग्रहादरिरुत शत्रुर्वोऽपि नोऽस्मान्सुभगान्शोभनधनोपेतान्वोचेयुः । उच्यासुः । कृष्टयो मनुष्या अस्मन्मित्रभूता वदन्तीति किमु वक्तव्यमिति शेषः । ततो धनसंपन्ना वयमिन्द्रस्य शर्मणीन्द्रप्रसादलब्धे सुखे स्यामेत् । भवेम्यैव । मघुमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु रयिः क्षत्रं भग इति पठितम् । मनुष्या इत्यादिषु पञ्चविंशतिसंख्याकेषु मनुष्यनामसु कृष्टय इति पठितम् ॥ he dasma śatrūṇām upakṣapayitar indra tvad-anugrahād ariḥ uta śatrur vo 'pi no 'smān subhagān śobhana-dhanopetān vocēyuḥ | ucyāsuḥ | kṛṣṭayo manuṣyā asman-mitra-bhūtā vadantīti kimu vaktavyam iti śeṣaḥ | tato dhana-sampannā vayam indrasya śarmaṇīndra-prasāda-labdhe sukhe syāmed | bhavema eva | maghum ity ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu dhana-nāmasu rayiḥ kṣatraṃ bhaga iti paṭhitam | manuṣyā ity ādiṣu pañcaviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu manuṣya-nāmasu kṛṣṭaya iti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "O 'dasma' — O destroyer of enemies, who bring the enemies to ruin — Indra! By your favour may 'ariḥ' — even an enemy — say of us that we are 'subhagān' — possessed of fine wealth. 'Vocēyuḥ' = 'ucyāsuḥ' (the optative of 'vac,' 'may they say'). 'Kṛṣṭayaḥ' — the people, the men who are our friends, say this — what need is there to say so (of them)! — that is the supplied thought. Therefore, 'syām it' — may we indeed be, 'indrasya śarmaṇi' — in the happiness gained by Indra's grace, endowed with wealth. Among the twenty-eight names of wealth beginning with 'magham,' 'rayiḥ,' 'kṣatram' and 'bhagaḥ' are read; among the twenty-five names of men beginning with 'manuṣyāḥ,' 'kṛṣṭayaḥ' is read."

Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept): "Uta" — a particle, first-syllable acute (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः, Phiṭ-sūtra 4-14). "Subhagān" — "bhaga" ends, in the "kṛtvādi" class, with the first member's accent set aside: नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) would give the end-acute, but "bhaga" is read in the list beginning with "kṛtva" — क्रत्वादयश्च (पा. ६-२-११८) — so the second member is first-syllable acute. In the saṃhitā: दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. ८-३-९) the "n" of "subhagān" becomes "ru" before a vowel; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. ८-३-१७) the "y"; लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. ८-३-१९) the "y" is elided; since the elision is "asiddha," no further sandhi occurs; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. ८-३-३) the "ā" takes the nasal sign. "Ariḥ" — "vacana-vyatyaya" (a change of number: singular for plural); from "ṛ" with the Uṇādi "i" (अर्त्तेरिः, उ. सू. ४-१३७; printed "4-578") with the end-acute by the accent of the affix. "Vocēyuḥ" — "ucyāsuḥ": the root "vac" (to speak) in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ), "jhi → jus" (झेर्जुस्, पा. ३-४-१०८); "liṅ" = "yāsuṭ" (लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य, पा. ७-२-७९); the "ṅit" "yāsuṭ" is acute by यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३); the "ṅit" bars guṇa and, by वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५), the "samprasāraṇa" → "uc"; by Vedic छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) the augment "āṭ" is absent; "s" is elided (लोपोऽनन्त्यस्य, as printed); the accents conflict, the "e" of the "yāsuṭ" being the single substitute of "a + ī" is acute (एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः, पा. ८-२-५). "Dasma" — from "dasu upakṣaye" (to waste away) by the Uṇādi दसेर्णिच्च…मुक् (उ. सू. १-१४४) with the augment "muk"; being a vocative standing after a pada it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् and तिङ्ङतिङः). "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — by क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४) the affix "ktic" in the sense of a name; since it is "c"-marked, it is end-acute. "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be); the "a" of "as" is elided (श्नसोरल्लोपः, पा. ६-४-१११); "yāsuṭ" is acute; the word stands at the beginning of the pāda, so no nighāta. "Śarmaṇi" — "śṝ hiṃsāyām"; "hinasti duḥkham iti śarma" ("that which destroys suffering"); by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. ३-२-७५) "manin" is added; "iṭ" is barred (नेड्वशि कृति, पा. ७-२-८); the "n"-marked affix gives first-syllable acute. ॥६॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) दस्म (he dasma) — O Indra, destroyer of enemies | (तव अनुग्रहात्) (tava anugrahāt) — by your grace | अरिः उत (ariḥ uta) — even enemies | नः (naḥ) — us | सुभगान् (subhagān) — as wealthy, or as lordly | वोचेयुः (vocēyuḥ) — may they say | कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ) — (when our enemies themselves speak well of us, what need to say that) the men who are our friends (say it) | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — Indra's (that arises from his favour) | शर्मणि (śarmaṇi) — in happiness | स्याम इत् (syāma it) — we shall indeed be. Rik 4.6: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening)

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, destroyer of enemies! By your favour, even our enemies will praise us, saying that we are wealthy and lordly. If it is so, what wonder that our other friends, the men of our own side, should say it? Besides this, by your (Indra's) grace we shall be happy indeed.

English Translation (printed in English in the source itself):

"Destroyer of foes, let our enemies say we are prosperous; let men (congratulate us); may we ever live in happiness through your (favour)."

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this Ṛk is, in a small measure, similar to that of the preceding Ṛk; that is, the chief import of the two Ṛks is the same.

सुभगान् (subhagān) — Since the word "bhaga" is read among the twenty-eight words that indicate wealth, beginning with "magha" (Ni. 2-1[?]), "bhaga" here means "wealth." "Subhagān" means "those who have abundant wealth."

अरिः (ariḥ) — Here the singular is used in the sense of the plural. In ordinary speech, when we say "enemy" (the source's English), it is customary to mean the people belonging to the side of our enemy, those who are not our well-wishers. In the same way, here, though the singular "ariḥ — enemy" is used, it must be taken in the plural sense — "our enemies, those who are ill-disposed to us."

दस्म (dasma) — For this word the Bhāṣyakāra says "śatrūṇām upakṣapayitaḥ" and explains it as "destroyer of enemies." The form is derived from the root "dasu upakṣaye." Skandasvāmī explains this word as "darśanīya" — "of beautiful appearance." The Bhāṣyakāra himself, too, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62, its 5th, 11th and 12th Ṛks, explains the word "dasma" as "darśanīya." This word is used in the Ṛgveda not only in the Ṛks mentioned above but also in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-138-4; 2-9-5; 4-1-3; 5-31-7; 6-1-1; 6-18-5; 7-3-4; 7-22-8; 8-92-18; 8-103-7; 10-7-1; 10-43-2; 10-147-5 (re-read from the better scan, Oct 2026). The various forms of the root "meda"-… [the print reads "medan"; I take it to be the stem "daṃs"] — daṃsaḥ, daṃsanā, daṃsobhiḥ, daṃsanābhiḥ, daṃsanaiḥ, daṃsayaḥ, daṃsasā, daṃsāṃsi — are used in many places in the Ṛgveda. Geldner and other scholars explain this word as "master" … Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 4." Nirukta reference-numbers re-read from the better scan. Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.

original p. 114

Special topics on Rik 4.6 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

कृष्टयः (kṛṣṭayaḥ) — This word is read among the twenty-five words that signify "man" (manuṣya), beginning with "manuṣyāḥ" (Ni. 3-8 [as printed]). Because the word is derived from the root "kṛṣ" (to plough, to practise agriculture), the sense is "people who practise agriculture, men who plough" — that is, in general, "people, men."

शर्मणि (śarmaṇi) — The word "śarma" is read among the twenty-two words that signify "house" (Ni. 3-8 [?]); so Skandasvāmī explains "indrasya śarmaṇi" as "in Indra's house" — that is, "in Indra's world." This does not seem to fit very well. Besides this, since "śarma" is read among the twenty words that signify "happiness" (Ni. 3-11), it is fitting to take the sense "happiness" for the word "śarma."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept. - "Uta" — the words that belong to the "eva-ādi" class (एवादीनामन्तः, Phiṭ-sūtra [number as printed "4-1[?]"]) have the last syllable acute; so "uta" is end-acute. Note: the Sanskrit on p. 112 had called "uta" first-syllable acute (by the nipāta rule); the two pages differ, and the discrepancy is recorded without being resolved. - "Subhagān" — "bhaga" belongs to the "kṛtvādi" class; so by नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) the end-acute that a bahuvrīhi after "su" would take is set aside, and by क्रत्वादयश्च (पा. ६-२-११८) the words of the "kratu"-class are first-syllable acute; thus the stem's own accent is prescribed (प्रातिपदोक्त); "subhagān" is an accusative plural. In the saṃhitā: दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. ८-३-९) turns the "n" into "ru" when followed by a vowel in the same pāda; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. ८-३-१७) gives "y" for "ru" after "bho," "bhago," "agho" or a short or long "a"; लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. ८-३-१९) elides the "y" (in Śākalya's view); since the elision is "asiddha" (पूर्वत्रासिद्धम्, पा. ८-२-१), the rule अकःसवर्णे दीर्घः (पा. ६-१-१०१) does not lengthen the vowels; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. ८-३-३) gives the nasal sign to the "ā": "subhagā[ṃ] ariḥ" this is the form whose nasal sign was flagged at p. 111. - "Ariḥ" — a singular where the plural would be expected; from "ṛ" with the Uṇādi "i" (अर्त्तेरिः, उ. सू. ४-५७८ [as printed]); with guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. ७-३-८४) → "ari"; end-acute by the affix-accent. - "Vocēyuḥ" — the root "vac paribhāṣaṇe" (to speak) in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ); the third-person plural "jhi" … Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, the rendering of the Sanskrit of p. 112, characterized in order, sūtras kept; numbers as read, [?] where uncertain. The sense of the Rik is already given on pp. 112–113. Continuing "vocēyuḥ":) …लिङ्याशिषि… (liṅ āśiṣy aṅ, पा. ३-१-८६ [as printed; the usual number is different, and the print is recorded]) puts "aṅ" in the āśīrliṅ; झेर्जुस् (पा. ३-४-१०८) puts "jus" for "jhi"; the "j" of "jus" is an "it" by चुटू (पा. १-३-७) and the "s" ... elided by तस्य लोपः (पा. १-३-९); "vac + a + us" — वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५) and वचेरुम् (पा. ७-४-२०) — before "aṅ" the augment "um" comes to "vac"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) gives guṇa; यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — the augment "yāsuṭ" in the parasmaipada, acute and "ṅit"; किदाशिषि (पा. ३-४-१०४) — "yāsuṭ" in the āśīrliṅ is "kit" (so no guṇa); the Mādhava school adds that by this very sūtra "yāsuṭ" comes. Hence "vac + yās + us." By छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) in the Veda the affix is both "sārvadhātuka" and "ārdhadhātuka"; hence "yās + us" takes the "sārvadhātuka" label, and लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) elides the "s" of "yās" ("s" not at the end); अतो येयः (पा. ७-२-८०) turns the "yā" (after an "a"-final stem) into "iy" → "voc-iy-us"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) → "vocēyuḥ." The "sārvadhātuka" accent is lost by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) and the affix "aṅ" keeps its own acute; the single substitute "ē" of "i + a" … is acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५). - "Dasma" — "dasu upakṣaye" with the Uṇādi ईषियुधीन्धिदसिश्याधूसूभ्योऽमुक् [as printed] (उ. सू. १-१४४) the affix "ma" with the augment "muk"; as a vocative standing after another word it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितस्य च, as printed). - "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४): "ktic" and "kta" in a sense of a name: "ktic" is added to "kṛṣ," meaning "men"; "c"-marked, so the last syllable is acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३). - "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be) in the optative (vidhi-liṅ), first-person plural; "yāsuṭ"; by लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) the "s" is elided; the affix "mas" loses its final "s" (नित्यं ङितः, पा. ३-४-९९); श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. ६-४-१११) the "a" of "as" is elided before an affix that is "k" or "ṅ"-marked; hence "s-yā-ma" → "syāma." (The page ends mid-derivation of "syāma"; it continues on p. 116.
