Rik 6.8: Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics, end of grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Marut-troops are free of fault and have become able to go to the heavenly world. People who seek the fruit of their wishes desire them. May this sacrifice that we are performing for Indra, accompanied by such Marut-troops, gratify him with worship and the like, and make him strong.

English Translation as printed in the source

This sacrifice is performed in adoration of Indra so as to make him powerful, along with the irreproachable, heavenward-tending and amiable bands (of the Maruts).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — Special Topics ॥

The sense of this Ṛk is somewhat strained (kliṣṭa). Its meaning can be stated thus: "May Indra, who is accompanied by the Marut-troops, be well pleased with me by means of this sacrifice that we are performing, and thereby become strong." Of the qualifying words used of the Maruts — "anavadyaiḥ," "abhidyubhiḥ," "kāmyaiḥ" — the meanings are plain.

  • मखः (makhaḥ) — "Among the fifteen sacrifice-names beginning with 'yajña,' the words 'makhaḥ' and 'viṣṇuḥ' are read" (Ni. 3-19).
  • अर्चति (arcati) — "Among the forty-four 'arcati-karma' names beginning with 'arcati, gāyati,' the word 'arcati' is read" (Ni. 3-19).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 244–245, Kannada; characterized "Anavadyaiḥ" — "na vidyate avadyaṃ yeṣāṃ te" (those without fault): नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) makes the second member end-acute. "Abhidyavaḥ" — "abhigatā dyauḥ yais te," "tair abhidyubhiḥ" — those who have set out towards heaven; "abhi" end-acute by the stem accent, kept in the bahuvrīhi. "Makhaḥ" — end-acute by the stem accent. "Sahasvat" — "sahaḥ balam asminn arcanakarmaṇy asti" (in this act of worship there is strength): "matup" by तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् (पा. सू. ५-२-९४); तसौ मत्वर्थे (पा. सू. १-४-१९) — before a matvarthīya affix, stems ending in "t" and "s" are "bha," which sets aside "pada," so ससजुषो रुः (पा. सू. ८-२-६६) gives no "ru"; मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः (पा. सू. ८-२-९) "v" for "m"; "sahas" first-syllable acute by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (फि. सू. २६); "matup," "p"-marked, is unaccented (अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ, पा. सू. ३-१-४), so that accent stays. "Kāmyaiḥ" — कमेर्णिङ् (पा. सू. ३-१-३० [?], the print blurred) "ṇiṅ" in its own sense after "kamu kāntau"; अत उपधायाः (पा. सू. ७-२-११६) vṛddhi: "kāmi"; by the gaṇasūtra "janī-jṝṣ-knasu-rañjo 'mantāś ca" (bhvā. ga. sū.) — "janī prādurbhāve," "jṝṣ vayohānau," "knasu hvaraṇadīptyoḥ" (three divādi roots), "rañja rāge" (in both divādi and bhvādi), and roots ending in "am" — "kam," "gam" etc. would be "mit," and मितां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ६-४-९२) would shorten the penultimate before "ṇi"; but "na kamyamicamām" (bhvā. ga. sū.) withdraws "mit" from them, so there is no shortening. After "kāmi," अचो यत् (पा. सू. ३-१-९७) "yat"; णेरनिटि (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) loss of "ṇi"; in the instrumental plural "kāmyaiḥ," तित्स्वरितम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५) would give svarita, but यतोऽनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) sets it aside: first-syllable acute. ॥८॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. In the second line the svarita strokes stand over "sa" and "gi" in the print; their placement is doubtful, hence [accent ?].

Sūkta 6, The Ninth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Page 246 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 247 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 12". Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; re-read from the better scan. The Pada is printed with accents; not reproduced (Pada unaccented).

अतः॑ परिज्म॒न्ना ग॑हि दि॒वो वा॑ रोच॒नादधि॑ । स॑मस्मिन्नृंजते॒ गि॑रः ॥९॥ [accent ?]

átaḥ parijmannā́ gahi divó vā rocanā́dádhi | samasminnṛṃjate giraḥ ||9|| [accent ?]

original pp. 246–247

Rik 6.9: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English, start of Special Topics

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अतः । परिऽज्मन् । आ । गहि । दिवः । वा । रोचनात् । अधि । सम् । अस्मिन् । ऋञ्जते । गिरः ॥९॥

ataḥ | pari-jman | ā | gahi | divaḥ | vā | rocanāt | adhi | sam | asmin | ṛñjate | giraḥ ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे परिज्मन् परितो व्यापिन्मरुद्गण अतोऽस्मान्मरुद्गणस्थानादन्तरिक्षादा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । दिवो वा । द्युलोकाद्वा समागच्छ । रोचनादधि । दीप्यमानादादित्यमण्डलाद्वा समागच्छ । अस्मदीयकर्मकाले यत्र यत्र तिष्ठसि ततः सर्वस्मादागच्छेत्यर्थः । किमर्थमागमनमिति तदुच्यते । अस्मिन्कर्मणि वर्तमाने ऋत्विग्गिरः स्तुतीः सम्ऋञ्जते । सम्यक् प्रसाधयति । ऋञ्जतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा । नि. ६-२१ । इति यास्कः । एताः स्तुतीः श्रोतुमागच्छेत्यर्थः । यद्यप्यृत्विजा मन्त्रस्य प्रयुज्यमानत्वादृञ्जतिधातोरुत्तमपुरुषेण भवितव्यं तथापि परोक्षकृतत्वेन निर्देशात्प्रथमपुरुषप्रयोगः । परोक्षकृतलक्षणं च यास्क आह । ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिक्यश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य । नि. ७-१ [?] । इति ॥ he parijman parito vyāpin marud-gaṇa ato 'smān marud-gaṇa-sthānād antarikṣād ā gahi | asmin karmaṇy āgaccha | divo vā | dyulokād vā samāgaccha | rocanād adhi | dīpyamānād āditya-maṇḍalād vā samāgaccha | asmadīya-karma-kāle yatra yatra tiṣṭhasi tataḥ sarvasmād āgacchety arthaḥ | kim-artham āgamanam iti tad ucyate | asmin karmaṇi vartamāne ṛtvig-giraḥ stutīḥ sam-ṛñjate | samyak prasādhayati | ṛñjatiḥ prasādhana-karmā | ni. 6-21 | iti yāskaḥ | etāḥ stutīḥ śrotum āgacchety arthaḥ | yady apy ṛtvijā mantrasya prayujyamānatvād ṛñjati-dhātor uttama-puruṣeṇa bhavitavyaṃ tathāpi parokṣa-kṛtatvena nirdeśāt prathama-puruṣa-prayogaḥ | parokṣa-kṛta-lakṣaṇaṃ ca yāska āha | tās tri-vidhā ṛcaḥ parokṣa-kṛtāḥ pratyakṣa-kṛtā ādhyātmikyaś ca | tatra parokṣa-kṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāma-vibhaktibhir yujyante prathama-puruṣaiś cākhyātasya | ni. 7-1 [?] | iti ||

Translation: "O 'parijman' — O Marut-host, pervading on all sides! 'Ataḥ' — from this place of yours, the Marut-host, or from the atmosphere — 'ā gahi' — come to this rite. 'Divo vā' — or come from the world of heaven. 'Rocanād adhi' — or come from the shining disc of the sun. The sense is: at the time of our rite, wherever you are standing, from there come. For what purpose the coming? That is said: while this rite is going on, the priests' voices, the praises, 'sam ṛñjate' — adorn well, that is, accomplish well. 'Ṛñjati' is a verb of accomplishing (Yāska, Nirukta 6-21). The sense: come to hear these praises. Although, since the mantra is being used by the priest, the root 'ṛñj' ought to be in the first person, nevertheless, because the statement is made in the indirect (parokṣa-kṛta) manner, the third person is used. And Yāska gives the mark of the 'parokṣa-kṛta': 'Those verses are of three kinds: indirect, direct, and personal-spiritual. Of these, the indirect are joined with all the case-endings of nouns, and with the third person of the verb' (Nirukta 7-1 [?])." The Nirukta reference for the parokṣa-kṛta definition prints a first digit that looks like 7 but may be 2, hence [?].

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized; references as printed): "Ataḥ" — पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (पा. ५-३-७); एतदोऽश् (पा. ५-३-५), "ś"-marked, so it replaces the whole stem (पा. १-१-५५); "tasil" being "l"-marked, the syllable before the affix is acute ("liti"). "Parijman" — "aja gati-kṣepaṇayoḥ" with "manin" by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. ३-२-७५); the loss of "a" is Vedic; vocative nighāta. "Gahi" — गमेर्बहुलं छन्दसि (as printed; पा. २-४-७३) "luk" of "śap"; "hi" being "ṅit" (पा. ३-४-८७), the "m" is lost by "anudāttopadeśa…" (पा. ६-४-३७); अतो हेः (पा. ६-४-१०५) does not elide "hi," because the loss of "m" is treated as not effected for it by असिद्धवदत्राभात् (पा. ६-४-२२), so the stem does not end in "a." "Divaḥ" — the case-ending acute by "ūḍidam…". "Vā" — चादयोऽनुदात्ताः (फि. ४-१६), unaccented. "Rocanāt" — "ruca dīptau," "yuc" by अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः (पा. ३-२-१४९); युवोरनाकौ (पा. ७-१-१) "ana"; "c"-marked, end-acute. "Adhi" — अधिपरी अनर्थकौ (पा. १-४-९३), a karmapravacanīya, together with the nipāta designation, so first-syllable acute by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ." "Asmin" — as in "parijman" etc., "idam" is replaced, in anvādeśa, by an unaccented "aś" in the third and following cases (पा. २-४-३२), "ś"-marked so replacing the whole stem; the case-ending is unaccented by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. ३-१-४), so the whole word is unaccented. "Ṛñjate" — "ṛji bhṛjī bharjane," with "sam" in the sense of "accomplishing"; nighāta. "Giraḥ" — the stem accent.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated, p. 247

हे परिज्मन् (he parijman) — O Maruts, pervading on every side! अतः (ataḥ) — from your place, the atmosphere | दिवो वा (divo vā) — or from the world of heaven | रोचनात् (rocanāt) — from the shining sun-disc | अस्मिन् (asmin) — to this sacrifice that we are performing, that is, to the sacrificial place | अधि आ गहि (adhi ā gahi) — come | (mattu ṛtvijanu) — (and the priest) | गिरः (giraḥ) — praises | सम्ऋञ्जते (sam-ṛñjate) — recites for your adornment.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Marut-deities, you are all-pervading. At this time of our sacrifice, if you are in the atmosphere, come from there; if in the heavenly world, come from there; or if you are in the sphere of the sun, come from there. Wherever you are now, come from there. Now the priest — that is, the Ṛṣi Madhucchandas, the seer of this mantra — praises you with praises, for your coming.

English Translation as printed

O pervader-on-all-sides, come hither from the regions (of the Maruts) or from the sky or from the radiant solar sphere. For in the rite (the priest) fully recites your praises.

॥ Special Topics ॥ Kannada, translated; continues onto the next page Page 248 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 2, Sū. 6"; p. 249 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 12"; p. 249 also carries a small "32" at the foot, a printer's signature mark. Re-read from the better scan; every printed sūtra number is given.

  • परिज्मन् (parijman) — "going round on all sides"; "moving everywhere." That is, the wind blows always in all places — on earth, in the atmosphere, in heaven, and so on.
  • दिवो वा रोचनादधि (divo vā rocanād adhi) — The commentator says "either from heaven or from the sphere of the sun." Or the word "rocanāt" may be taken to mean "shining," and as a qualifier of "divaḥ" it may be understood as desired. Here, since "adhi" is present, the commentator has explained "rocanāt" as "from the shining sun-sphere." Skandasvāmin says that "adhi" should be construed with the verb "ā gahi."
  • ऋञ्जते (ṛñjate) — "Ṛñjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā" (Nirukta 6-21), says Yāska in the Nirukta. Here the priest who praises, the seer of this mantra, Madhucchandas himself, [text continues on p. 248].
original pp. 248–249

Rik 6.9: end of Special Topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (characterized)

॥ Special Topics (continued from p. 247) ॥

…[the priest] does not use the first-person verb but uses a third-person verb-form. The reason: since the deities being praised, the Maruts, are not present before him, he praises them indirectly (and not directly). Such verses — in which the deities are not addressed, but only their praise, or merely some matter, is stated, with the verbs in the third person — belong to the group of verses called "parokṣa-kṛta" (indirect). Among the Ṛks there are three kinds: parokṣa-kṛta, pratyakṣa-kṛta, and ādhyātmika. This matter, stated by Yāska, we have explained earlier (page 205).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 248–249, Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept, numbers as printed

  1. "Ataḥ." पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (printed "५-७-३" [?], the usual number being 5-3-7): after "kim," the pronouns and "bahu" in the fifth case, other than "dvi" etc., "tasil" comes optionally; so "etasmāt" gives "etad + tasil"; the case-ending is elided by सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (पा. सू. २-४-७१), the taddhita-final being a prātipadika. एतदोऽन् (पा. सू. ५-३-५): this sūtra is split into "etadaḥ" and "an": by the first, "eta" and "ita" replace "etad" before prāgdiśīya affixes beginning with "r" or "th"; by the second, "an" replaces "etad" before prāgdiśīya affixes — so here "an." Since the "nitsvara" concerns affixes, the "n" of "an" needs no "it" designation and gets none; "an," being of more than one letter, replaces the whole of "etad" by अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य (पा. सू. १-१-५५): "an + tasil." स्वादिष्वसर्वनामस्थाने (पा. सू. १-४-१७) gives "an" the pada designation before "tasil"; नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (पा. सू. ८-२-७) drops the "n"; with the "it"-letters of the affix dropped and "ru" and visarga, "ataḥ." The Kāśikā reads the sūtra as "etado 'ś," whose "aś," being "ś"-marked, replaces the whole; the sense is as before; following this reading Mādhavācārya gave the substitute "aś." "Tasil" being "l"-marked, लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) makes the syllable before the affix acute.

  2. "Parijman." "Aja gati-kṣepaṇayoḥ": by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) the affixes "manin, kvanip, vanip, vic" come after roots, so "manin" after "aj"; the "a" of "aj" is lost as a Vedic licence. In "parijmānaṃ sukhaṃ ratham" (ऋ. सं. १-२०-३) "parijman" is derived differently. Unaccented by आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९).

  3. "Gahi." "Gamḷ gatau," "loṭ," second singular "sip": सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. सू. ३-४-८७) "hi" for "si," and it is "apit": "gam + hi." Being "apit," the sārvadhātuka is "ṅit" by सार्वधातुकमपित् (पा. सू. १-२-४), so by अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति (पा. सू. "६-३-३७" as printed) the final nasal of the anudāttopadeśa roots, of "tan" etc. and of "van" is lost before a "jhal"-initial "kit/ṅit" affix: the "m" of "gam" goes. This loss is "ābhīya" — from असिद्धवदत्राभात् (पा. सू. ६-४-२२) to the end of the pāda — and, for another ābhīya rule with the same conditioning, it counts as not effected; so "ga" is treated as ending in "m," not in "a," and अतो हेः (पा. सू. ६-४-१०५) — "luk" of "hi" after a short "a" — does not apply.

  4. "Divaḥ." ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१): the case-ending is acute.

  5. "Vā." In the cādi list, so unaccented by चादयोऽनुदात्ताः (फि. सू. ८४, as printed).

  6. "Rocanāt." अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः (पा. सू. ३-२-१४९): after an intransitive, consonant-initial root marked with an anudātta "it," "yuc": "ruc + yu"; युवोरनाकौ (पा. सू. ७-१-१) "ana" for "yu": "ruc + ana"; guṇa of the light penultimate: "rocana"; ablative singular "rocanāt." The affix is "c"-marked, so चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३), with the vārttika चितः सप्रकृतेर्बह्वकजर्थम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३ वा. १): the end of the whole stem-plus-affix is acute, or else the forms with "bahuc" and "akac" would not come out right. विभाषा सुपो बहुच् पुरस्तात् (पा. सू. ५-३-६८) puts "bahuc" before the stem: "īṣad ūnaḥ paṭuḥ — bahupaṭuḥ"; अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच्प्राक्टेः (पा. सू. ५-३-७१) … continues on p. 250

original pp. 250–251

Rik 6.9: end of grammar; Rik 6.10: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar begins

Page 250 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 1, Sū. 6"; p. 251 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 12". Rik 6.10 is the last Rik of Sūkta 6.

Grammar of Rik 6.9, continued (characterized) Kannada, translated; the page-top continues the "Rocanāt" discussion of p. 249 Final Rik of the sūkta. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

  • "Rocanāt," end of discussion. The affix "akac" coming by अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः (avyaya-sarvanāmnām akac prāk ṭeḥ, पा. ५-३-७१, "'akac' comes before the last 'ṭi' syllable of an indeclinable or a pronoun") comes "behind the 'ṭi'"; the example given is "anyake." The print says that if the Vārttika on "citaḥ" were not taken in this sense, the final letter would not be acute in these two examples; in "rocana," the end of the whole stem-and-affix combination is acute.
  • "Adhi" (अधि, adhi). अधिपरी अनर्थकौ (adhi-parī anarthakau, "'adhi' and 'pari,' when without a distinct sense, are 'karma-pravacanīya,'" पा. १-४-९३): the print says that "adhi" and "pari," not conveying a particular meaning, receive the name "karma-pravacanīya" and also the name "nipāta"; since "adhi" holds the name "nipāta" along with "karma-pravacanīya," it is first-syllable acute by निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (nipātā ādyudāttāḥ, फि. सू. ८०).
  • "Asmin" (अस्मिन्, asmin). When "idam" is followed by the seventh-case ending, by त्यदादीनामः (tyadādīnām aḥ, "of 'tyad' etc. the last letter is replaced by 'a'," पा. ७-२-१०२) the last letter takes "a," and then अतो गुणे (ato guṇe, पा. ६-१-९७) gives the later form ("ida + ṅi"). The print then argues that since "parijman" has pointed to the Marut-troop and "asmin" refers back to it ("asmin" here refers to the sacrifice, which is named to be the very place of coming), this is a case of "anvādeśa" — a reference back — by the definition quoted in the print ("kiñcit kāryaṃ vidhātum upāttasya kāryāntaraṃ vidhātuṃ punar upādānam anvādeśaḥ," "anvādeśa is the repeated mention of what has been mentioned for one purpose, in order to enjoin another operation on it"). Hence इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ (idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau, "in an anvādeśa, 'idam' is replaced by an accent-less 'aś' before the third-case and following endings," पा. २-४-३२): "aś," being "śit," replaces the whole of "idam." The seventh-case ending "ṅi" is replaced by "smin" by जसिङसोः स्मात्स्मिनौ [the print reads "ङसिङ्योः स्मात्स्मिनौ," ṅasi-ṅyoḥ smāt-sminau, पा. ७-१-१५], "'smāt' and 'smin' replace the fifth- and seventh-case endings after an a-ending pronoun"; so "asmin." The ending is accent-less by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (anudāttau sup-pitau, पा. ३-१-४). So "asmin" is wholly accent-less.
  • "Ṛñjate" (ऋञ्जते, ṛñjate). "Ṛji bhṛji bharjane" (the root meaning "to fry"; also, in use, "to adorn"). The root is "idit," so "num" comes by इदितो नुम् धातोः (idito num dhātoḥ, पा. ७-१-५८). Then the anusvāra and parasavarṇa (पा. सू. ८-३-२४ and ८-४-५८) give "ṛñj-." In the present ātmanepada third-person singular, "ṛñjate." It is accent-less by तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८). The print then quotes the verse on the force of the preverb: "उपसर्गे च धात्वर्थो बलादन्यत्र नीयते । प्रहाराहारसंहारविहारपरिहारवत् ॥" (as printed, "upasarge ca"; upasarge ca dhātv-artho balād anyatra nīyate | prahārāhāra-saṃhāra-vihāra-parihāravat ||, "With a preverb the meaning of a root is forcibly led elsewhere — as in 'prahāra,' 'āhāra,' 'saṃhāra,' 'vihāra,' 'parihāra'"). The Kannada explains: the root "hṛ" means "taking," but with "pra" it means "a blow," with "ā" it means "food, eating," with "saṃ" it means "killing, destruction," with "vi" "sport, roaming," with "pari" "abandoning" — thus various meanings appear through the force of the preverb. "In the same way, in other places too, differing meanings arise for roots through the force of the preverb: that is the sense of the verse. Here, although the root 'ṛji' is read in the sense of 'frying,' the preverb 'sam' is joined to it, so the root 'ṛji' conveys the sense of 'adorning.'"
  • "Giraḥ" (गिरः, giraḥ). The stem-accent (prātipadika-svara) comes. ॥९॥

Sūkta 6, The Tenth Mantra

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इ॒तो वा॑ सा॒तिमी॑महे दि॒वो वा॒ पार्थि॑वा॒दधि॑ । इन्द्रं॑ म॒हो वा॒ रज॑सः ॥१०॥

itó vā sātím īmahe divó vā pā́rthivād ádhi | índraṃ mahó vā rájasaḥ ||10||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इतः । वा । सातिम् । ईमहे । दिवः । वा । पार्थिवात् । अधि । इन्द्रम् । महः । वा । रजसः ॥१०॥

itaḥ | vā | sātim | īmahe | divaḥ | vā | pārthivāt | adhi | indram | mahaḥ | vā | rajasaḥ ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Kannada script; re-read from the better scan.

इन्द्रं देवं प्रति सातिं धनदानमीमहे । आधिक्येन याचामहे । कस्माल्लोकादिति तदुच्यते । इतोऽस्मादभिदृश्यमानात्पार्थिवात्पृथिवीलोकाद्वा दिवो वा द्युलोकाद्वा महो महतः प्रौढाद्रजसो वा पक्ष्यादीनां रञ्जकादन्तरिक्षलोकाद्वा । अयमिन्द्रो यतः कुतश्चिदानीयास्मभ्यं धनं प्रयच्छेदित्यर्थः । सप्तदशसु याच्ञाकर्मस्वीमहे यामीति पठितम् ॥ इतः । … indraṃ devaṃ prati sātiṃ dhana-dānam īmahe | ādhikyena yācāmahe | kasmāl lokād iti tad ucyate | ito 'smād abhidṛśyamānāt pārthivāt pṛthivī-lokād vā divo vā dyulokād vā maho mahataḥ prauḍhād rajaso vā pakṣyādīnāṃ rañjakād antarikṣa-lokād vā | ayam indro yataḥ kutaścid ānīyāsmabhyaṃ dhanaṃ prayacched ity arthaḥ | saptadaśasu yācñā-karmasv īmahe yāmīti paṭhitam || itaḥ | …

Translation: "Toward Indra, the god, we 'īmahe' — we ask for in abundance — 'sāti,' the giving of wealth. From which world? That is said: 'itaḥ' — from this earth-world, the 'pārthiva' that is here seen — or 'divo vā' — from the heavenly world — or 'maho vā rajasaḥ' — from the great, expansive 'rajas,' that is, the atmosphere, the region that colours the birds and others ['rañjaka' — 'that which gives colour']. The sense: may this Indra, bringing it from wherever, give us wealth. Among the seventeen verbs of begging, 'īmahe' and 'yāmi' are read."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (begins; characterized, references as printed): "Itaḥ" — from "idam," पञ्चम्यास्तसिल्; इदम इश् (पा. ५-३-३), "ś"-marked, so replacing the whole stem. The rule "ūḍidam…" (पा. ६-१-१७१) has its scope in "ābhyām, ebhiḥ," and "liti" (पा. ६-१-१९३) in "pacanam, pācakaḥ"; both are nitya, so by विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् (पा. १-४-२) the later, "liti," makes the "i" acute. Since by पश्चात्सेशः प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः (as printed; पा. ५-३-१) "tasil" is called "vibhakti," the acute of a non-sarvanāmasthāna case-ending taught by "ūḍidam…" would arise; to the objection that, by "sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitam eva" (परि. ४०), "ūḍidam…" cannot apply again, the answer is no, since repeated application is admitted where the attested forms require it; the argument then turns to "yataḥ, tataḥ," where, though set aside by the "l"-accent, the acute of "tasil" by "sāv ekācaḥ…" … continues on p. 252 Page 252 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 2, Sū. 6"; p. 253 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 12". P. 252 is the end of Sāyaṇa's own grammatical notes, in Kannada script; re-read from the better scan.

original pp. 252–253

Rik 6.10: end of Sanskrit grammar, Pada-meanings, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics; Kannada grammar begins

Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes on Rik 6.10, continued and ended the first lines end the argument about "itaḥ" begun on p. 251 The upshot: the objection is answered by the prohibition "na gośvan-sāv-avarṇa…" (the last digits of its number are not clear), and repeated application is not a general rule, being resorted to only where attested forms require it.

…स्यादिति चेन्न । यत्र च्छब्दयोः सावर्णान्तत्वे न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति । पा. ६-१-१८२ [?] । निषेधात् । न च पुनःप्रसङ्गविज्ञानं चेत्येतत्सार्वत्रिकं लक्ष्यानुरोधेन क्वचिदेव तदाश्रयणादिति । … syād iti cen na | yatra cchabdayoḥ sāvarṇāntatve na gośvansāvavarṇeti | pā. 6-1-182 [?] | niṣedhāt | na ca punaḥprasaṅgavijñānaṃ cety etat sārvatrikaṃ lakṣyānurodhena kvacid eva tadāśrayaṇād iti |

सातिम् । षणु दाने । धात्वादेः षः सः । पा. ६-१-६४ । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः । पा. ६-४-४२ । इति नकारस्यात्वम् । तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च । पा. ७-२-९ । इति निषेधादिण्न भवति । नित्स्वरे प्राप्ते उदात्त इत्यस्य निवृत्त्या ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च । पा. ३-३-९७ । इति निपातनादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । sātim | ṣaṇu dāne | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | pā. 6-1-64 | bhāve ktin | jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ | pā. 6-4-42 | iti nakārasyātvam | titutra-tathasi-susara-kaseṣu ca | pā. 7-2-9 | iti niṣedhād iṇ na bhavati | nit-svare prāpte udātta ity asya nivṛttyā ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca | pā. 3-3-97 | iti nipātanād antodāttatvam |

"Sātim" — from "ṣaṇu dāne"; the initial "ṣ" becomes "s" (धात्वादेः षः सः, dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ, "the initial 'ṣ' of a root becomes 's'," पा. ६-१-६४); "ktin" in the sense of the action (भावे क्तिन्, bhāve ktin); the "n" of the root is replaced by "ā" (जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः, jana-sana-khanāṃ sañjhaloḥ, "'ā' replaces the nasal of 'jan,' 'san,' 'khan' before 'jh'-class sounds and 'san'," पा. ६-४-४२); the augment "iṭ" does not come, by the prohibition तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (titutra-tatha-sisu-sara-kaseṣu ca, पा. ७-२-९); the accent that would come by "n"-marking (the rule for "nit"-affixes) is set aside, and ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (ūti-yūti-jūti-sāti-heti-kīrtayaś ca, पा. ३-३-९७) lists "sāti" as an irregular formation ("nipātana") with the end-acute.

ईमहे । ईङ् गतौ । श्यनोऽपि बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । अस्य धातोर्ङित्त्वात् तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात् । पा. ६-१-१८६ । इति लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । न च तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । चवायोगे प्रथमा । पा. ८-१-५९ । इति निषेधात् । उत्तरवाक्ययोरपि हि वाशब्दयोगादन्यथा वाक्यापरिपूर्तेस्तिङ्विभक्तेरवश्यमध्याहारात्तदपेक्ष्यैषा प्रथमा तिङ्विभक्तिरिति । īmahe | īṅ gatau | śyano 'pi bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | asya dhātor ṅittvāt tāsy-anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāt | pā. 6-1-186 | iti lasārvadhātukasyānudāttatve dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | na ca tiṅ-ṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | cavā-yoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 | iti niṣedhāt | uttara-vākyayor api hi vā-śabda-yogād anyathā vākyāparipūrtes tiṅ-vibhakter avaśyam adhyāhārāt tad-apekṣyaiṣā prathamā tiṅ-vibhaktir iti |

"Īmahe" — "īṅ gatau"; "śyan" is also optionally elided in the Veda (बहुलं छन्दसि, bahulaṃ chandasi), so there is "luk." Since the root is "ṅ"-marked, the personal ending is accent-less by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तम् (tāsy-anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam, पा. ६-१-१८६), only the root's own accent remains. And there is no "nighāta" (lowering of the verb) by तिङ्ङतिङः (tiṅ atiṅaḥ, पा. ८-१-२८), because of the prohibition चवायोगे प्रथमा (cavā-yoge prathamā, "the first [verb] is not lowered when joined with 'ca,' 'vā,' etc.," पा. ८-१-५९): for the two following clauses too are joined with "vā," and since otherwise the sentences would be incomplete, a verb must be supplied in them; in relation to those, this is the "first" verb.

दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । divaḥ | ūḍidam ity ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam |

"Divaḥ" — the case-ending is acute by "ūḍidam…" etc.

पार्थिवात् । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथित इति पृथिवी । प्रथेः षिवन् सम्प्रसारणं च । उ. १-१५० । इति षिवन्प्रत्ययः । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च । पा. ४-१-४१ । इति ङीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । शेषनिघातेनानुदात्तादिः पृथिवीशब्दः । पृथिव्या विकार इत्यर्थे ओरञ् इत्यनुवृत्तावनुदात्तादेश्च । पा. ४-३-१४० । इत्यञ् । यस्येति च । पा. ६-४-१४८ । इतीकारलोपः । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः । पा. ७-२-११७ । इत्यादिवृद्धिः । रपरत्वम् । पा. १-१-५१ । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तः । pārthivāt | pratha prakhyāne | prathita iti pṛthivī | prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca | u. 1-150 | iti ṣivan-pratyayaḥ | ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca | pā. 4-1-41 | iti ṅīṣ | pratyaya-svareṇodāttaḥ | śeṣa-nighātenānudāttādiḥ pṛthivī-śabdaḥ | pṛthivyā vikāra ity arthe oraj ity anuvṛttāv anudāttādeś ca | pā. 4-3-140 | ity añ | yasyeti ca | pā. 6-4-148 | itīkāra-lopaḥ | taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ | pā. 7-2-117 | ity ādi-vṛddhiḥ | raparatvam | pā. 1-1-51 | ñnity ādir nityam ity ādyudāttaḥ |

"Pārthivāt" — from "prath prakhyāne" ("that which is spread out is 'pṛthivī'"); the Uṇādi "prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca" gives the affix "ṣivan" (Uṇādi 1-150); the feminine "ṅīṣ" by षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च (ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca, पा. ४-१-४१); the affix gives the acute, and by the lowering of the rest the stem "pṛthivī" begins accent-less. In the sense "a modification of the earth" ("pṛthivyā vikāraḥ"), the affix "añ" comes by ओरञ् (oraj, "'añ' in the sense of 'its modification' after a stem ending in a short 'u' [here 'o']") carried forward with अनुदात्तादेश्च (anudāttādeś ca, पा. ४-३-१४०); the "ī" is dropped by यस्येति च (yasyeti ca, पा. ६-४-१४८); the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, पा. ७-२-११७); with "r" following (रपरत्वम्, पा. १-१-५१); and by "ñit/ṇit" the first syllable is acute (ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम्, no number printed).

अधि । निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । इन्द्रम् । रन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । महः । महत इत्यस्याकारतकारयोर्लोपश्छान्दसः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । रजसः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥१०॥ adhi | nipātatvād ādyudāttaḥ | indram | ran-pratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | mahaḥ | mahata ity asyākāra-takārayor lopaś chāndasaḥ | sāv ekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam | rajasaḥ | nab-viṣayasyānisantasyety ādyudāttatvam ||10||

"Adhi" — a particle, first-syllable acute. "Indram" — ending in the affix "ran," first-syllable acute. "Mahaḥ" — from "mahat," the "a" and "t" being dropped by Vedic licence; the case-ending is acute by "sāv ekācaḥ…". "Rajasaḥ" — by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (nab-viṣayasyānisantasya, no number printed), first-syllable acute. ॥१०॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ Kannada, translated, p. 252

(वयम् vayam — we) इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | इतः पार्थिवात् वा (itaḥ pārthivāt vā) — either from this earth-world that is seen before our eyes | दिवो वा (divo vā) — or from the heavenly world | महः (mahaḥ) — great | रजसो वा (rajaso vā) — or from the atmosphere that is the refuge of birds and the like | सातिम् (sātim) — for the obtaining of wealth | अधीमहे (adhīmahe, so printed; the "adhi" of the Pada text taken together with "īmahe") — we pray.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Now, before our eyes, whether from this earth-world, from the heavenly world, or from the atmosphere-world, we pray to Indra that he bring wealth and give it to us.

English Translation

We pray to Indra for riches either from this earth, heaven, or from the vast intermediate region.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — Special Topics ॥ Kannada, translated; p. 253

  • सातिम् (sātim) — This word, derived from the root "ṣaṇu dāne," has the sense of "gift," "giving." What is given? Wealth and prosperity, or the other things we need.
  • ईमहे (īmahe) — We pray, we beg. Among the seventeen verbs meaning "to beg," beginning with "yāmi," the word "īmahe" is read.
  • पार्थिवात् (pārthivāt) — "pṛthivyā vikāraḥ pārthivaḥ, tasmāt" — that which is a modification of the earth: that is, the "earth-world."
  • रजसः (rajasaḥ) — The commentator says "pakṣyādīnāṃ rañjakād antarikṣa-lokāt" — "from the atmosphere-world, that which gives colour/delight to the birds and the others." That is, the one that gives joy to the birds, that is, that is their refuge and the main place for them to move about [the Kannada: saṃtoṣavannu uṃṭumāḍuva, eṃdare āśraya-bhūtavāda, mukhya saṃcāra-māḍalu avakāśavuḷḷa].

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā — Grammatical Derivation, Kannada commentary (characterized) ॥ Page 254 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 2, Sū. 6"; p. 255 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 12". Characterized in outline; re-read from the better scan, with the printed numbers.

  • "Itaḥ" (इतः, itaḥ). Since "idam" is a fifth-case word, "tasil" is added by पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (pañcamyās tasil, पा. सू. ५-३-७), and the fifth-case ending is elided (luk) after the "tasil." Then "idam + tasil": by इदम इश् (idama iś, "'iś' replaces 'idam' before a 'prāg-diśīya' affix," पा. ५-३-३) "idam" gets the substitute "iś." Since "iś" is "śit," by the paribhāṣā अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य (anekāl śit sarvasya, पा. १-१-५५) it takes the place of the whole of "idam." Then "i + tas" → with "ru" and visarga: "itaḥ."
  • The print then takes up the accent. ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) — after the substitute "ūṭh," after "idam," after the six "pad"-etc. substitutes taught by पद्दन्नोमास्हृन्निशसन्… (पा. सू. ६-१-६३), and after "ap, pum, rai, div" (monosyllabic and end-acute), a non-sarvanāmasthāna case-ending is acute; this sūtra has its own scope where लिति (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) does not apply, in "ābhyām, ābhiḥ"; "liti" — the syllable before an "l"-marked affix is acute — has its own scope where "ūḍidam…" does not come, in "pacanam" (with "lyu") and "pācakaḥ" (with "ṇvul"). Neither can be called alone "nitya": by "kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgitvaṃ nityatvam" a rule is nitya if it applies whether or not the other has been applied; here "liti" stays applicable whether "ūḍidam" is applied or not, and "ūḍidam" whether "liti" is applied or not; so both are nitya, and neither prevails as the nitya rule. The argument continues onto the next page.
original pp. 254–255

Rik 6.10: Kannada grammar (vipratiṣedha argument; "sātim," "īmahe")

The "itaḥ" accent conflict (continued from p. 253). Both rules reach "itaḥ." Which applies? विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् (पा. सू. १-४-२): "vipratiṣedha" is the simultaneous application, to one form at one time, of two rules each of which has its own scope elsewhere; then the later rule operates. So the later "liti" makes the "i" acute. Next, by प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः (पा. सू. ५-३-१), the affixes taught from there up to दिक्शब्देभ्यः… (पा. सू. ५-३-२७) are called "vibhakti," so "tasil" is a vibhakti, and by ऊडिदम्… (पा. सू. "६-१७१" as printed) the non-sarvanāmasthāna vibhakti "tasil" after "idam" would be acute. But by सकृद्गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्बाधितं तद्बाधितमेव (परिभाषा ४०), what has once been set aside by "vipratiṣedhe param" stays set aside — "param" being read as "param eva," only the later rule — so "ūḍidam" does not apply again. Yet by पुनःप्रसङ्गविज्ञानात्सिद्धम् (परिभा. ३९), "vipratiṣedhe param" is so explained that a set-aside rule may apply again where it is again applicable, so that "ūḍidam" would apply again. The two paribhāṣās do not set each other aside; both operate as the attested forms require, and here "punaḥprasaṅga" decides. Then in "yataḥ, tataḥ": सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६८) — after a word monosyllabic before the locative plural "su," a third-and-following case-ending is acute — and "liti" (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) both arise; "liti," the later, sets "sāv ekācaḥ" aside, but by "punaḥprasaṅga…" (परिभा. ३९) "sāv ekācaḥ" might apply again and make "tasil" acute. But "yat" and "tat," being "a"-ending before the singular "su" (p. 255), fall under the prohibition न गोश्वन्साववर्णराडङ्क्रुङ्कृद्भ्यः (no number printed) for words with "a" before "su," so "sāv ekācaḥ" gives no acute to "tasil"; or rather, as the attested forms require, "sakṛdgatau" decides here: "punaḥprasaṅga…" is not a rule that applies everywhere, only in some places as the forms require; so the set-aside "sāv ekācaḥ" does not apply again, and "yataḥ, tataḥ" are first-syllable acute.

"Sātim" (p. 255). "Ṣaṇu dāne": by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" the initial "ṣ" becomes "s"; when the "ṣ" goes, the "ṇ" it caused reverts to "n": "san." "Ktin" in the sense of the action; जनसनखनां सञ्झलोः (पा. सू. ६-४-४२) — before "san," or a "jhal"-initial "kit/ṅit" affix, "ā" replaces the final of "jan, san, khan": "sa + ā + ti" → "sāti." The "iṭ" of आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (पा. सू. ७-२-३५) is barred for the ten kṛt affixes "ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka, se" by तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (पा. सू. ७-२-९). "Ktin" being "n"-marked, ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१९७) would make the first syllable acute; but ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च (पा. सू. ३-३-९७) forms these "ktin"-words by nipātana as end-acute, so "sāti" is end-acute.

"Īmahe" (p. 255). "Īṅ gatau," "laṭ," first plural "mahiṅ"; टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे (पा. सू. ३-४-७९) "e" for the "i"; the "śyan" of दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (पा. सू. ३-१-६९) is elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. २-४-७३): though that sūtra elides "śap," the word "bahula" extends it to "śyan": "īmahe." Since "īṅ" is "ṅit," तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात्… (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) makes the lasārvadhātuka "mahe" unaccented, and the end-acute of the root taught by धातोः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६२) stays on "ī." तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. सू. ८-१-२८) would make the verb unaccented after a non-verb, but चवायोगे प्रथमा (पा. सू. ८-१-५९) — with "ca" or "vā," the first-uttered verb is not made unaccented — so it is not wholly unaccented. "Ādare…" continues on p. 256 Page 256 header: "Maṇ. 1, A. 2, Sū. 6"; p. 257 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 13". P. 257 also carries a small "33" at the foot, evidently a printer's signature mark. Characterized in outline; sūtras kept.

original pp. 256–257

Rik 6.10: end of grammar; close of Sūkta 6

"Īmahe" — the "cavā-yoge" difficulty (continued from p. 255; characterized). The print raises a doubt: since this mantra contains only one finite verb, how can it be "first-uttered" (prathamoccārita) and hence escape the lowering of accent? The answer given: the Rik really consists of three sentences — (1) "itaḥ pārthivāl lokād vā indraṃ prati sātim adhi īmahe" (from this earth-world, we ask Indra for gain); (2) "indraṃ prati sātim divo vā adhi īmahe" (or from heaven); (3) "rajasaḥ (antarikṣa-lokād vā) indraṃ prati sātim adhi īmahe" (or from the atmosphere). The "īmahe" of the first sentence is the first-uttered one; the "cavā-yoge prathamā" prohibition therefore applies to it (the verb, being first, is not lowered). In the second and third sentences, because of the presence of "vā," the word "īmahe" must be supplied (adhyāhāra) in connection with them; otherwise the sentence would not give a full meaning.

"Divaḥ" (दिवः). By ऊडिदम् (ūḍidam, पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) the case-ending is acute.

"Pārthivāt" (पार्थिवात्, pārthivāt). "Prathate iti pṛthivī" — from "prath prakhyāne," with प्रथेः षिवन् सम्प्रसारणं च (prather ṣivan samprasāraṇaṃ ca, उ. सू. १-१४९) the affix "ṣivan" comes, with "samprasāraṇa" — so "prath + ivan," whence "pṛth + ivan" (the "r" turning to "ṛ"); the "ṣ" is "it"; by षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च (ṣid-gaurādibhyaś ca, पा. ४-१-४१) the feminine "ṅīṣ" comes after a "ṣit" stem and the stems of the "gaura" class. By the maxim अवयवे अचरितार्थं लिङ्गं समुदायोपकारकं भवति ("a marker without use in the part serves the whole"), the "ṣ"-marking, having no use in the affix, qualifies the stem. The "ī" of "ṅīṣ" is acute by the affix-accent (आद्युदात्तश्च, पा. सू. ३-१-३, ādyudāttaś ca, "an affix is first-syllable acute"), and the others are unaccented by अनुदात्तं पदमेकवर्जम् (anudāttaṃ padam eka-varjam, पा. सू. ६-१-१५८), so "pṛthivī" is "anudāttādi" (its first syllable unaccented). To express "a modification of 'pṛthivī'" अनुदात्तादेश्च (पा. सू. ४-३-१४०), with "añ" carried over from ओरञ् (पा. सू. ४-३-१३९), gives "añ" after a genitive stem whose first syllable is unaccented, in the senses "modification" and "part"; since the result ends in a taddhita, it is a stem (कृत्तद्धितसमासाश्च, kṛt-taddhita-samāsāś ca, पा. १-२-४६), and the case-ending is elided by सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (पा. २-४-७१); the "ī" is dropped by यस्येति च (पा. ६-४-१४८); the first vowel takes vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (पा. ७-२-११७) — "ṛ" → "ār," with "r" following by उरण् रपरः (uraṇ raparaḥ, पा. १-१-५१); and by ञ्णित्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. ६-१-१९७) the first syllable is acute. Thus "pārthiva" is first-syllable acute.

"Adhi" (अधि). First-syllable acute as a particle (निपाता आद्युदात्ताः, printed "पा. सू. ८०").

"Indram" (इन्द्रम्, indram). ऋज्रेन्द्राग्र… (ṛjrendrāgra-…, उ. सू. २-१८६) — the word ends with the affix "ran" and is first-syllable acute.

"Mahaḥ" (महः, mahaḥ). From "mahat," the "a" and "t" are dropped by Vedic licence (the printed "(अत्)" marks the dropped part). By सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः (sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, पा. ६-१-१६८) the case-ending is acute.

"Rajasaḥ" (रजसः, rajasaḥ). By नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (nab-viṣayasyānisantasya, फि. सू. २६) first-syllable acute. ॥१०॥

Close of Sūkta 6 (as printed on p. 257). The print marks the end of the sūkta with a ruled line and the statement (Kannada, translated): "Here the sixth sūkta in the first maṇḍala is complete. ॥ ॐ ॥

Sūkta 7 — "indram id gāthino bṛhat" (ಏಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು, "The Seventh Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

इन्द्रमित्यादिकं दशर्चं यत्सूक्तं तत्सुरूपकृत्नुमित्यादिषु चतुर्थम् । ऋषिश्छन्दोदेवता विनियोगश्च पूर्ववत् । विशेषविनियोगस्तूच्यते । महाव्रते निष्केवल्यशस्त्रे इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इति सूक्तम् । तथा च पञ्चमारण्यके सूत्रितम् । शिरोगायत्रमिन्द्रमिद्गाथिनः । ऐ. आ. ५-२-१ । इति । तथा चतुर्विंशेऽहनि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः शस्त्रे इन्द्रमिद्गाथिन इति षळहस्तोत्रियस्तृचः । चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्वेत्युपक्रम्य आयाहि सुषुमा हि त इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनो बृहत् । आ. ७-२ [?] । इति सूत्रितत्वात् । अतिरात्रे प्रथमे पर्यायेऽच्छावाकशस्त्रेऽयमेव तृचोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च इन्द्राय मद्वने सुतमिन्द्रमिद्गाथिनो बृहत् । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥

indram ity-ādikaṃ daśarcaṃ yat sūktaṃ tat surūpakṛtnum ity-ādiṣu caturtham | ṛṣi-chando-devatā viniyogaś ca pūrvavat | viśeṣa-viniyogas tūcyate | mahāvrate niṣkevalya-śastre indram id gāthina iti sūktam | tathā ca pañcamāraṇyake sūtritam | śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ | ai. ā. 5-2-1 | iti | tathā caturviṃśe 'hani brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ śastre indram id gāthina iti ṣaḷaha-stotriyas tṛcaḥ | caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭety upakramya āyāhi suṣumā hi ta indram id gāthino bṛhat | ā. 7-2 [?] | iti sūtritatvāt | atirātre prathame paryāye 'cchāvāka-śastre 'yam eva tṛco 'nurūpaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca indrāya madvane sutam indram id gāthino bṛhat | ā. 6-4 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta of ten riks beginning indram is the fourth among those beginning surūpakṛtnum [i.e., the fourth sūkta of that anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi, meter, deity and application are as before. Its special application is now stated. In the Mahāvrata rite, the sūkta indram id gāthinaḥ is used in the niṣkevalya-śastra. So it is laid down in the Fifth Āraṇyaka: 'śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 5-2-1). Likewise, on the twenty-fourth day [of the Ṣaḷaha-related rite], in the śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the ṣaḷaha-stotriya triplet is indram id gāthinaḥ — as laid down in the (Āśvalāyana) sūtra, which, beginning from 'on the twenty-fourth [day] the hotā …', continues 'āyāhi suṣumā hi ta' and 'indram id gāthino bṛhat' (Āśvalāyana, ref. "7-2" [?], the first digit unclear). In the Atirātra, in the first paryāya, in the Acchāvāka's śastra, this very triplet is the anurūpa; and it is so laid down: 'indrāya madvane sutam, indram id gāthino bṛhat' (ref. "ā. 6-4")."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering of the above) ॥

This sūkta indram id gāthino bṛhat is the fourth (last) sūkta of the second anuvāka, which begins with surūpakṛtnum ūtaye. It has ten riks. Its ṛṣi, deity, meters and application are the same as in the preceding sūkta. It does, however, have a special application: in the sacrifice called Mahāvrata, the sūkta indram id gāthino is recited as the niṣkevalya-śastra mantra. This is stated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (the fifth āraṇyaka — "Pañcamāraṇyaka") in the words śiro-gāyatram indram id gāthinaḥ. And on the twenty-fourth day [of the rite], when the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin — a priest of the hotṛ group — recites the triplet called ṣaḷaha-stotriya, the rik indram id gāthino is to be recited; this is stated in the Āśvalāyana sūtra (Ā. Sū. 7-2 [?]), in the words "caturviṃśe hotājaniṣṭety upakramyāyāhi suṣumā hi ta indram id gāthino bṛhat." That is: in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section hotājaniṣṭa, the rik ā yāhi suṣumā hi te (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-17-1) and the rik indram id gāthino bṛhat (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-7-1) are to be recited, on the twenty-fourth day, in the triplet called ṣaḷaha-stotriya. And in the Āraṇyaka too: "indrāya madvane sutam, indram id gāthino bṛhat" (Āraṇyaka 6-4) — that is, the rik indrāya madvane sutam (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-92-19) and the rik indram id gāthino bṛhat are to be recited together in the triplet mentioned above — so the sūtra directs. The top of this page carries the end of the Kannada anuvāda translated above; its content is given there.

इन्द्र॒मिद्गा॒थिनो॑ बृ॒हदिन्द्र॑म॒र्केभि॑र॒र्किणः॑ । [accent ?] इन्द्रं॒ वाणी॑रनूषत ॥१॥

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya on Rik 1

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

गाथिनो गीयमानसामयुक्ता उद्गातार इन्द्रमिदिन्द्रमेव बृहत् । त्वामिद्धि हवामहे । ऋग्वे. ६-४६-१ । इत्यस्यामृच्युत्पन्नेन बृहन्नामकेन साम्नानूषत । स्तुतवन्तः । अर्किणो ऽर्चनहेतुमन्त्रोपेता होतारो ऽर्केभिर् ऋग्रूपैर्मन्त्रैरिन्द्रमेवानूषत । ये त्ववशिष्टा अध्वर्यवस्ते वाणीर्वाग्भिर्यजूरूपाभिरिन्द्रमेवानूषत । अर्कशब्दस्य मन्त्रपरत्वं यास्केनोक्तम् । अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति । नि. ५-४ । इति । श्लोक इत्यादिषु सप्तपञ्चाशत्सु वाङ्नामसु वाशी वाणीति पठितम् ॥

gāthino gīyamāna-sāma-yuktā udgātāra indram id indram eva bṛhat | tvām id dhi havāmahe | ṛgve. 6-46-1 | ity asyām ṛcy utpannena bṛhan-nāmakena sāmnānūṣata | stutavantaḥ | arkiṇo 'rcana-hetu-mantropetā hotāro 'rkebhir ṛg-rūpair mantrair indram evānūṣata | ye tv avaśiṣṭā adhvaryavas te vāṇīr vāgbhir yajū-rūpābhir indram evānūṣata | arka-śabdasya mantra-paratvaṃ yāskenoktam | arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti | ni. 5-4 | iti | śloka ity-ādiṣu saptapañcāśatsu vāṅ-nāmasu vāśī vāṇīti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "The gāthinaḥ — the udgātṛ priests, who are endowed with sung Sāmans — praised Indra, and Indra alone, with the Bṛhat [Sāman] — that is, with the Sāman named Bṛhat, produced upon the rik tvām id dhi havāmahe (Ṛgveda 6-46-1) — they praised him. The arkiṇaḥ — the hotṛ priests, who are furnished with mantras that are the means of worship — praised Indra, and Indra alone, with the arkas, that is, with mantras in the form of ṛks. And the remaining ones, the adhvaryus, praised Indra alone with vāṇīs — with speech in the form of yajus-formulae. That the word arka denotes 'mantra' is stated by Yāska: 'An arka is a mantra, because with it they offer worship' (Nirukta 5-4). Among the fifty-seven words for 'speech' beginning with śloka, the words vāśī and vāṇī are listed."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed): "Gāthinaḥ" — उषिकुषिगार्तिभ्यस्थन् (उ. २-४) "than" after "gai," "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute: "gāthā"; "gāthā eṣāṃ santi" — व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्च (पा. ५-२-११६) "ini," the "i" acute by the affix accent, which, coming later, remains. "Bṛhat" — for "bṛhatā": the instrumental ending is elided by "supāṃ suluk…"; पृषद्बृहन्महज्जगच्छतृवच्च (उ. २-८४) gives it as end-acute by nipātana. "Arkebhiḥ" — "arca pūjāyām": "arcyate ebhir iti arkā mantrāḥ"; पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेण (पा. ३-३-११८) "gha"; चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः (पा. ७-३-५२) "k"; end-acute by the affix accent; बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. ७-१-१०) — "ais" does not replace "bhis." "Arkiṇaḥ" — "arkāḥ stuti-sādhana-bhūtā mantrā eṣāṃ santi." "Vāṇīḥ" — वृषादीनां च (पा. ६-१-२०३) first-syllable acute; the long vowel, since दीर्घाज्जसि च (पा. ६-१-१०५) — the prohibition of the long "pūrvasavarṇa" — is optional in the Veda (वा छन्दसि, पा. ६-१-१०६); a nominative in the sense of the instrumental. "Anūṣata" — "ṇu stutau," णो नः (पा. ६-१-६५) "n"; "luṅ," ātmanepada by vyatyaya; "at" for "jha" (पा. ७-१-५); no "iṭ" with "sic" and the long "ū" are Vedic; the root being "kuṭādi" (पा. १-२-१), "sic" is "ṅit," so no guṇa (पा. १-१-५).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

गाथिनः (gāthinaḥ) — those who sing, that is, the Sāman-singers beginning with the udgātṛ | इन्द्रम् इत् (indram it) — Indra alone | बृहत् (bṛhat) — with the Sāman-mantra called Bṛhat | अनूषत (anūṣata) — praise, that is, sing | अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — the ṛtvijs, the hotṛ and others, who recite the worship-mantras (the invocatory mantras) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) — with ṛk-mantras | (अनूषत — praise) | (the adhvaryu and the other ṛtvijs) इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) — with the yajurveda mantras that take the form of sentences | (अनूषत — praise).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

At the time of sacrifice, the ṛtvijs praise Indra in many ways. That is: the Sāman-singers, the udgātṛ and others, sing with the mantra called Bṛhat-sāman found in their Sāma Veda (this mantra is the rik at Ṛgveda 6-46-1); the hotṛ group praise him with the ṛks that serve as their śastra; and the adhvaryu and the other ṛtvijs praise Indra with mantras in the form of the sentences of their own Veda, the Yajurveda. In other words, the ṛtvijs praise Indra with the Vedic mantras of all three kinds — Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman.

original p. 260

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

The chanters (of the Sama hymns) praise only Indra with (a Saman called) Brihat; the recetirs [sic] of mantras (Rics) praise Indra with the Ric-Verses; (and the remaning [sic] priest Adhvaryus) praise Indra with prose-like Sentences (of Yajus).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The three Vedas in one rik. Although this rik does not explicitly name the Vedas Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, the Bhāṣyakāra takes the words बृहत् (bṛhat), अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) and वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) to point to the mantras of the three Vedas — Sāma, Ṛg and Yajur respectively. Western scholars do not accept this view. They hold that the Ṛgveda is older than the other Vedas, and so there is no reason for the later Vedas — Yajur and Sāma — to be indicated within it.

Though this argument cannot be dismissed outright, the Ṛgveda's own Puruṣa-sūkta (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-90-9) states the words yajus and sāman explicitly. Moreover:

  1. Most of the Sāma Veda's mantras are themselves Ṛgveda mantras, and even in the Ṛgveda's own period it was the custom to recite many Ṛgveda riks in sung form; so there is nothing impossible in a Sāman-mantra being indicated here.
  2. It is something everyone must grant that the Yajurveda is later than the Ṛgveda and Sāma Veda. But although it did not then exist in its present, systematized form, one may confidently say that many Yajur-mantras — chiefly, the sentences used in the sacrifice — were then in special use. Many such sentences, together with the procedures and rules of sacrificing, may have been gathered together to form the Yajurveda as it now stands.
  3. Further, the Ṛgveda in many places names the Yajurveda's chief priest, the Adhvaryu, explicitly.
  4. And since the word वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) is used in this rik, there is ample room to suppose that it refers to Yajus-sentences that are not bound in meter.

For these reasons, the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation of the words as the Ṛk-Yajus-Sāman mantras of the three Vedas cannot be set aside.

"Gāthinaḥ" — gāthā eṣāṃ santīti gāthinaḥ ("those who have gāthās"). Gāthā is also a name for Sāma-Veda mantras; those who sing these gāthās — that is, the Sāman-mantras — are called gāthinaḥ.

original p. 261

"Bṛhat" — the ordinary sense of bṛhat is "great." But in the Sāma Veda there is the principal Sāman-mantra, sung in sacrifices, called Bṛhat-sāman; and in the Ṛgveda it is this rik:

त्वामिद्धि हवामहे सातौ वाजस्य कारवः । त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥

tvām id dhi havāmahe sātā vājasya kāravaḥ | tvāṃ vṛtreṣv indra satpatiṃ naras tvāṃ kāṣṭhāsv arvataḥ ||

(Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 6-46-1)

Translation (of the rik as cited here): "Indeed we call upon you, O Indra — we the singers — for the winning of strength [or: in the winning of spoil]; you, O Indra, the lord of the good, in battles with Vṛtra [or: against Vṛtras]; the men [call upon] you in the races of the horse." Gloss editorial and tentative; the source gives no translation of it here. "sātā" as printed.

The source adds: this mantra is found in the Sāma Veda at 234; 809; in the Atharvaveda 20-98-1; in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) 27-37; the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) 2-4-14-3; the Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā 7-2-6 [?] (the first digit unclear), and other places. This Bṛhat-sāman is one principal mantra of the Sāma Veda; the Yajurveda explains it in many places.

"Arkebhiḥ" — Yāska, in the Nirukta, gives the sense of the word arka: अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति (arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti) — "an arka is a mantra, because with it they worship" (Nirukta 5-4). The root arc means "to worship" (pūjāyām); because worship is done with it, the mantra is called arka.

"Arkiṇaḥ" — अर्काः स्तुतिसाधनभूता मन्त्रा येषां सन्तीत्यर्किणः (arkāḥ stuti-sādhana-bhūtā mantrā yeṣāṃ santīty arkiṇaḥ) — "those who have arkas, mantras that are the instruments of praise" — that is, those who praise with mantras (arkas) that are the means of praise.

"Vāṇīḥ" — vāṇī is listed among the fifty-seven speech-words beginning with śloka and dhārā (Ni. 2-23 [?], the numerals unclear). Here the Bhāṣyakāra explains vāṇīḥ as Yajurveda sentences. Since the Yajurveda has few mantras bound in meter, it is the custom to call its mantras "sentences" (vākya). In this rik the nominative-case word vāṇīḥ is used in the sense of the instrumental.

"Anūṣata" — the aorist (luṅ) form of the root ṇu stutau ("to praise"). Although the root takes parasmaipada, here, by a Vedic inversion (vyatyaya), it is used as if it were ātmanepada.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

Characterized, not transcribed. This section (pp. 261–263) works through the derivation and accent of each word; sūtra numbers as printed, re-read from the better scan. Continues the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 1 in the same register — the optional-lengthening discussion for vāṇīḥ and the finite-verb analysis of anūṣata, completed on the next page. Characterized as above; not transcribed.

  • गाथिनः (gāthinaḥ) — from the root gai ("to sing") + the than suffix by उषिकुषिगार्तिभ्यस्थन् (उ. सू. २-१६१, so printed here; the Bhāṣya gave "उ. २-४") — after "uṣa dāhe," "kuṣa niṣkarṣe," "gai śabde," "ṛ gatau" — with "ā" for the "ai" by आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति (पा. सू. ६-१-४५), "gātha," first-syllable acute by the "n"-mark; then, "gāthā eṣāṃ santi," व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्च (पा. सू. ५-२-११६) gives "ini" or "than" in the possessive sense after the "vrīhi"-class words, here "ini"; यस्येति च (पा. सू. "६-४-" as printed, the last number missing) drops the "ā"; the "i" acute by the affix accent, the "ā" unaccented by "satiśiṣṭa"; the unaccented "a" of "jas" becomes svarita by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. सू. ८-४-६६).
  • बृहत् (bṛhat) — for "bṛhatā": सुपां सुलुक्… (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) elides the instrumental ending; वर्तमाने पृषद्बृहन्महज्जगच्छतृवच्च (उ. सू. २-२४१ [?], the bhāṣya gave "उ. २-८४") forms these words with the affix "ati" in the present sense, with all the operations of "śatṛ"; end-acute by the affix accent.
  • अर्केभिः (arkebhiḥ) — "arca pūjāyām," "arcyante ebhir iti arkāḥ" (mantras); पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेण (पा. सू. ३-३-११८) "gha" in the instrumental or locative sense; its "gh" is "it" by लशक्वतद्धिते (पा. सू. १-३-८) and dropped by तस्य लोपः (पा. सू. १-३-९); चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः (पा. सू. ७-३-५२) "k" for "c": "arka"; the "ais" of अतो भिस ऐस् (पा. सू. ७-१-९) is barred by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. ७-१-१०); बहुवचने झल्येत् (पा. सू. ७-३-१०३) "e": "arkebhiḥ."
  • अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — "arkāḥ … eṣāṃ santi": अत इनिठनौ (पा. सू. ५-२-११५) "ini"; nominative plural.
  • वाणीः (vāṇīḥ) — वृषादीनां च (पा. सू. ६-१-२०३) first-syllable acute; "vāṇī + as": the long vowel of प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः (पा. सू. ६-१-१०२) is forbidden by दीर्घाज्जसि च (पा. सू. ६-१-१०५), but वा छन्दसि (पा. सू. ६-१-१०६) makes the prohibition optional in the Veda …
  • अनूषत (anūṣata) — root ṇu with n for ṇ; aorist with sic; the augment iṭ absent and the vowel lengthened as Vedic features; guṇa is blocked.
