"Pṛtanyataḥ," concluded: सनाद्यन्ता धातवः (पा. सू. ३-१-३२) the root designation; सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः (पा. सू. २-४-७१) "luk" of "am": "pṛtanā + ya"; कव्यध्वरपृतनस्यर्चि लोपः (पा. सू. ७-४-३९), with क्यचि च (पा. सू. ७-४-३३) carried on: before "kyac" in a Ṛk the final of "kavi, adhvara, pṛtanā" is lost: "pṛtanya," end-acute by "citaḥ"; लटः शतृशानचौ (पा. सू. ३-२-१२४) "śatṛ"; कर्तरि शप् (पा. सू. ३-१-६८), "p"-marked, unaccented; "śatṛ" unaccented by तास्यनुदात्तेत्… (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६); अतो गुणे (पा. सू. ६-१-९७) twice the later form; the single substitute acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. सू. ८-२-५): "pṛtanyat," end-acute; the accusative plural "śas," unaccented by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. सू. ३-१-४), is made acute by शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३), with "antodāttāt" carried from अन्तोदात्तादुत्तरपदादन्यतरस्यामनित्यसमासे (पा. सू. ६-१-१६९). ॥४॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: the strokes stand over "ma" of "mahitvam" and over "tva…"; line 2: a stroke over "dyau," and over "śavaḥ" a stroke joined to a bar; placement doubtful, hence [accent ?].

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

म॒हाँ इन्द्रः॑ प॒रश्च नु म॑हि॒त्वम॑स्तु व॒ज्रिणे॑ । [accent ?] द्यौ॑र्न प्र॑थि॒ना शवः॑ ॥५॥ [accent ?]

mahā́ṁ índraḥ paráś ca nú mahitvám astu vajríṇe | [accent ?] dyaúr ná prathinā́ śávaḥ ||5|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

महान् । इन्द्रः । परः । च । नु । महित्वम् । अस्तु । वज्रिणे ॥ द्यौः । न । प्रथिना । शवः ॥५॥

mahān | indraḥ | paraḥ | ca | nu | mahitvam | astu | vajriṇe || dyauḥ | na | prathinā | śavaḥ ||5||

original p. 320

Rik 5: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अयमिन्द्रो महान् शरीरेण प्रौढः परश्च गुणैरुत्कृष्टो ऽपि । नु किंच वज्रिणे वज्रयुक्तायेन्द्राय महित्वं पूर्वोक्तं द्विविधमाधिक्यं सर्वदास्तु । स्वभावसिद्धस्यापि भक्त्या प्रार्थनमेतत् । किंच द्यौर्न द्युलोक इव शवो बलमिन्द्रस्य सेनारूपं प्रथिना प्रथिम्ना पृथुत्वेन युज्यतामिति शेषः । यथा द्युलोकः प्रभूत एवमस्य सेना प्रभूता ॥ नुशब्दो यद्यपि क्षिप्रनामसु नु मुक्षु इति पठितस्तथाप्यत्र तस्यान्वयाभावात्निपातत्वेनानेकार्थत्वसंभवाच्च समुच्चयार्थो ऽत्र गृहीतः । नुशब्दो लोके प्रतिषेधार्थ एव । स्वाध्याये तु प्रतिषेधार्थ उपमानार्थश्चेति द्विविधः । येन पदेनान्वीयते तस्मात्पूर्वं प्रयुज्यमानः प्रतिषेधार्थ उपरिष्टात्प्रयुज्यमान उपमानार्थः । तथा च यास्क उदाहरति । उभयमन्वध्यायं नेन्द्रं देवममंसतेति प्रतिषेधार्थीयः पुरस्तादुपाचारस्तस्य यत्प्रतिषेधति । दुर्मर्दासो न सुरायामित्युपमार्थीय उपरिष्टादुपाचारस्तस्य येनोपमिमीते । नि. १-४ । इति । अत्रोपमेयवाचिनो द्यौश्शब्दस्यापि प्रयुक्तत्वादुपमार्थः स्वीकृतः । अष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु बलनामसु ओजः पाजः शव इति पठितम् ॥

ayam indro mahān śarīreṇa prauḍhaḥ paraś ca guṇair utkṛṣṭo 'pi | nu kiṃca vajriṇe vajra-yuktāyendrāya mahitvaṃ pūrvoktaṃ dvividham ādhikyaṃ sarvadāstu | svabhāva-siddhasyāpi bhaktyā prārthanam etat | kiṃca dyaur na dyuloka iva śavo balam indrasya senā-rūpaṃ prathinā prathimnā pṛthutvena yujyatām iti śeṣaḥ | yathā dyulokaḥ prabhūta evam asya senā prabhūtā || nu-śabdo yadyapi kṣipra-nāmasu nu mukṣu iti paṭhitas tathāpy atra tasyānvayābhāvāt nipātatvenānekārthatva-saṃbhavāc ca samuccayārtho 'tra gṛhītaḥ | nu-śabdo loke pratiṣedhārtha eva | svādhyāye tu pratiṣedhārtha upamānārthaś ceti dvividhaḥ | yena padenānvīyate tasmāt pūrvaṃ prayujyamānaḥ pratiṣedhārtha upariṣṭāt prayujyamāna upamānārthaḥ | tathā ca yāska udāharati | ubhayam anvadhyāyaṃ nendraṃ devam amaṃsateti pratiṣedhārthīyaḥ purastād upācāras tasya yat pratiṣedhati | durmardāso na surāyām ity upamārthīya upariṣṭād upācāras tasya yenopamimīte | ni. 1-4 | iti | atropameya-vācino dyauś-śabdasyāpi prayuktatvād upamārthaḥ svīkṛtaḥ | aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu bala-nāmasu ojaḥ pājaḥ śava iti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "This Indra is great (mahān) in body, mature, and supreme (paraḥ) — excellent in qualities as well. And may this twofold pre-eminence stated above, mahitvam, be always for the vajra-bearing Indra (vajriṇe): this is a prayer offered in devotion, though [that greatness is] naturally established. Moreover, dyaur na — like the heaven-world — let Indra's śavaḥ, his strength in the form of an army, be joined with prathinā, with breadth (prathimnā), vastness [this is the word to be supplied]: as the heavenly world is vast, so may his army be vast. The word nu — although read among the names for 'quickly' (nu, mukṣu) — here, since it has no construction in that sense and since, being a particle, it can have more than one meaning, is taken in the sense of 'and' (samuccaya). In ordinary speech na is only a negative; in the Veda it is twofold, negative and a particle of comparison: when placed before the word with which it is construed it is negative; when placed after, it means 'like.' So Yāska gives examples: 'ubhayam anvadhyāyaṃ nendraṃ devam amaṃsata' — the negative use is placed before what it negates; 'durmardāso na surāyām' — the comparative use is placed after the word with which it makes the comparison (Nirukta 1-4). Therefore, since the word dyauḥ, expressing the thing compared, is also used here, the comparative sense is accepted. Among the twenty-eight words for 'strength,' ojaḥ, pājaḥ, śavaḥ are read."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed): "Mahān" — in the saṃhitā, दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. ८-३-९) "ru" for the "n"; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. ८-३-३) nasalization of the preceding "ā"; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. ८- -१७, the middle number missing) "y"; its loss by लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. ८-३-१९), which being asiddha (पा. ८-२-१) no vowel sandhi follows. "Mahitvam" — महेरिनण् (as printed; उ. ४-११८) "in": "mahi"; "tva," acute by the affix accent. "Vajriṇe" — the "i" acute by the affix accent. "Dyauḥ" — end-acute by the stem; गोतो णित् (पा. ७-१-९०) the ending "ṇit," so अचो ञ्णिति (पा. ७-२-११५) vṛddhi; end-acute. "Prathinā" — "prathimnā": पृथ्वादिभ्य इमनिज्वा (पा. ५-१-१२२) "imanic"; र ऋतो हलादेर्लघोः (पा. ६-४-१६१) "ra" for the "ṛ"; with "ṭeḥ" (पा. ६-४-१५५) carried from तुरिष्ठेमेयःसु (पा. ६-४-१५४), loss of the "ṭi"; "c"-marked, end-acute; instrumental: अल्लोपोऽनः (पा. ६-४-१३४); the loss of "m" Vedic; the ending acute by अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः. "Śavaḥ" — first-syllable acute by नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य. ॥१५॥ the end of the fifteenth varga

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | महान् (mahān) — great | परः च (paraś ca) — and supreme in qualities | नु (nu) — and | वज्रिणे (vajriṇe) — to Indra, who bears the thunderbolt | महित्वम् (mahitvam) — [this twofold] pre-eminence | अस्तु (astu) — may it be | (for) शवः (śavaḥ) — Indra's strength (in the form of an army) | द्यौः न (dyaur na) — like the heavenly world | प्रथिना (prathinā) — is exceedingly vast (very great).

original p. 321

Rik 5 continued

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra is not great in body alone; he is also supreme in quality. Such pre-eminence in qualities is naturally fitting for the vajra-bearing Indra; for Indra's strength — in the form of an army, or his capacity — is, like the heaven-world, that is, like the vast firmament (the sky), very great.

॥ English Translation ॥

Great is Indra and Supreme. May greatness be ever for the weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt ; May his strength (of the army) be ever vast as the heavens.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Nu" — although the word nu is read among the words for "quickly" (kṣipra) such as nu and mukṣu, that sense does not fit here, and since indeclinables have many senses, the Bhāṣyakāra takes it here in the sense of "and" (samuccaya: muttu).

"Mahitvam astu vajriṇe" — although Indra's qualities are by nature supreme, that the poet says "let his qualities shine with still greater glory" is a prayer made out of devotion.

"Dyauḥ" — dyauḥ means heaven, the sphere of the sky (antarikṣa). Everyone knows that the sky extends very widely, as far as our eyes see and beyond. That is why the poet, when comparing with something very large, offers the simile of the sky.

"Na" — in modern Sanskrit na is a word of negation (na = "not"); in the Ṛgveda it is twofold — negative and comparative (pratiṣedhārtha and upamānārtha); na means "like" (iva): dyaur na = "like the sky." Such usages are plentiful in the Ṛgveda. There is a special point in this usage. As the Bhāṣyakāra says, येन पदेनान्वीयते तस्मात्पूर्वं प्रयुज्यमानः प्रतिषेधार्थ उपरिष्टात्प्रयुज्यमान उपमार्थः (yena padenānvīyate tasmāt pūrvaṃ prayujyamānaḥ pratiṣedhārtha upariṣṭāt prayujyamāna upamārthaḥ) — if na is used before the word to which it relates, it is negative; if it comes after the related word, it is a comparison. For example:

original p. 322

Rik 5: Special Topics (continued) and grammar begins

न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी अनु व्यचो न सिन्धवो रजसो अन्तमानशुः । na yasya dyāvāpṛthivī anu vyaco na sindhavo rajaso antam ānaśuḥ | (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-52-14) (gloss mine and tentative: "He whose breadth neither heaven and earth [match], nor the rivers reach the limit of the space.")

In this rik the word na stands before the related words dyāvāpṛthivī and sindhavaḥ, so na is negative.

न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानाय पित्वः ॥ na sa sakhā yo na dadāti sakhye sacābhuve sacamānāya pitvaḥ || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-117-4) (gloss mine and tentative: "He is no friend who gives not to a friend, to a companion who attends, of his food.")

Here the na stands before the related words sakhā and dadāti; so na is negative.

मा वो मृगो न यवसे जरिता भूदजोष्यः ॥ mā vo mṛgo na yavase jaritā bhūd ajoṣyaḥ || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-38-5) (gloss mine and tentative: "Let not your singer be unwelcome, like a deer in the pasture.")

वाश्रेव विद्युन्मिमाति वत्सं न माता सिषक्ति ॥ vāśreva vidyun mimāti vatsaṃ na mātā siṣakti || (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-38-8) (gloss mine and tentative: "Like a lowing cow, the lightning bellows; as a mother follows her calf.")

In these riks the na comes after the related words mṛgaḥ and vatsam, so it has the comparative sense here.

"Śavaḥ" — although this word is read among the words for water (udaka) such as āṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ (Ni. "2-24" as read [?]), it is read among the twenty-eight words for "strength," ojaḥ, pājaḥ and so on (Ni. "3-9" as read [?]); hence in this rik this sense must be taken.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 322–323, noted briefly

महान् (mahān) — in the saṃhitā, दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. सू. ८-३-९): a final "n" after a long vowel, before an "aṭ" letter in the same pāda, becomes "ru": "mahā + ru + indra"; आतोऽटि नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) — the "ā" before "ru" before an "aṭ" is always nasalized: "mahā̐"; भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि (पा. सू. ८-३-१७) "y" for the "ru" after "bho, bhago, agho" and "a/ā" before an "aś" letter: "mahāy indraḥ"; लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. सू. ८-३-१९) — the final "y, v" of a word after "a/ā" is optionally lost before an "aś" … continues on p. 323

original p. 323

Rik 5 grammar closes

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 323–324, Kannada; page header p. 323 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 15"; characterized, numbers as printed

(Continuing "mahān":) the "y" lost: "mahā̐ indraḥ." Now आद्गुणः (पा. सू. ६-१-८७) would give guṇa of "a" with a following "i, u, ṛ, ḷ"; but by पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् (पा. सू. ८-२-१) what is taught in the last three pādas (the "tripādī," from 8-2-1) is asiddha for the operations of the first seven and a quarter chapters, so for "ād guṇaḥ" (6-1-87) the loss of "y" by लोपः शाकल्यस्य (पा. सू. ८-३-१९) is not effected, the "y" intervenes, and no guṇa sandhi takes place. महित्वम् — "maha pūjāyām" with इन् (उ. सू. ४-५५८ [?], as printed; the Bhāṣya gave "उ. ४-११८") "in"; तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ (पा. सू. ५-१-११९) "tva": "mahitvam"; "tva" end-acute by the affix accent, which remains. वज्रिणे — "vajram asyāsti iti vajrī, tasmai": अत इनिठनौ (पा. सू. ५-२-११५) "ini"; the "i" acute by the affix accent. द्यौः — "dyo," end-acute by फिषः (फि. सू. १); nominative "su"; गोतो णित् (पा. सू. ७-१-९०) — a sarvanāmasthāna after "go" is "ṇit"; by the vārttika ओतो णिदिति वाच्यम्, read "otaḥ" for "gotaḥ," it applies to any "o"-ending stem, so after "dyo" too "su" is "ṇit"; अचो ञ्णिति (पा. सू. ७-२-११५) vṛddhi; by स्थानेऽन्तरतमः (पा. सू. १-१-५०), the nearest substitute in quality — the acute "o" becomes the acute "au": "dyauḥ." प्रथिना — "prathimnā": in the sense "pṛthor bhāvaḥ," पृथ्वादिभ्य इमनिज्वा (पा. सू. ५-१-१२२) "imanic" after a genitive of a word of the "pṛthu" class; र ऋतो हलादेर्लघोः (पा. सू. ६-४-१६१) "ra" for a light "ṛ" after a consonant before "iṣṭhan, imanic, īyasun": "prathu + iman"; टेः (पा. सू. ६-४-१५५) (p. 324) the "ṭi" of a "bha" stem lost: "prathiman"; instrumental "ṭā"; by यचि भम् (पा. सू. १-४-१८) "bha," so अल्लोपोऽनः (पा. सू. ६-४-१३४) loss of the "a" of "an"; the loss of "m" Vedic: "prathinā." "Imanic," "c"-marked, so "prathiman" is end-acute by चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३); before the unaccented "ā" of "ṭā" the acute "a" is lost, so by अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६१) the "ā" becomes acute. शवः — नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य (फि. सू. २६): a word always neuter, not ending in "is" or "as"… (so printed), first-syllable acute. ॥५॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The bar under "sya" of "tokasya" is faint, hence [accent ?].

original p. 324

Sūkta 8, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

स॒मो॒हे वा॒ य आश॑त॒ नर॑स्तो॒कस्य॒ सनि॑तौ । [accent ?] विप्रा॑सो वा धिया॒यवः॑ ॥६॥

samohé vā yá ā́śata náras tokásya sánitau | [accent ?] víprāso vā dhiyāyávaḥ ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सम्ऽओहे । वा । ये । आशत । नरः । तोकस्य । सनितौ ॥ विप्रासः । वा । धियाऽयवः ॥६॥

sam-ohe | vā | ye | āśata | naraḥ | tokasya | sanitau || viprāsaḥ | vā | dhiyā-yavaḥ ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये नरः पुरुषाः समोहे संग्रामे तोकस्यापत्यस्य सनितौ वा लाभे वाशत । व्याप्तवन्तः । इन्द्रं स्तुत्वेति शेषः । वा अथवा विप्रासो मेधाविनो धियायवः प्रज्ञाकामाः सन्त आशत ते सर्वे लभन्त इत्यध्याहारः । रण इत्यादिषु षट्चत्वारिंशत्संग्रामनामसु समोहे समिथ इति पठितम् । पञ्चदशस्वपत्यनामसु तुक् तोकमिति पठितम् ॥

ye naraḥ puruṣāḥ samohe saṃgrāme tokasyāpatyasya sanitau vā lābhe vāśata | vyāptavantaḥ | indraṃ stutveti śeṣaḥ | vā athavā viprāso medhāvino dhiyāyavaḥ prajñā-kāmāḥ santa āśata te sarve labhanta ity adhyāhāraḥ | raṇa ity-ādiṣu ṣaṭcatvāriṃśat-saṃgrāma-nāmasu samohe samitha iti paṭhitam | pañcadaśasv apatya-nāmasu tuk tokam iti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "Those narāḥ, men, who in the samoha — the battle — or in the winning (sanitau) of offspring (tokasya), have āśata — have attained [Indra's favour; the words 'having praised Indra' are to be supplied]; or the viprāsaḥ — the wise — who, being dhiyāyavaḥ — desirous of understanding — have attained: all these obtain [what they seek]: this is the supply of the sentence. Among the forty-six words for 'battle' beginning with raṇa, samohe and samitha are read. Among the fifteen words for 'offspring,' tuk and toka are read."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (p. 325; characterized, references as printed; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16"): "Samohe" — end-acute by the stem accent. "Vā" — unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ." "Āśata" — "aśū vyāptau," "luṅ"; loss of "cli" as Vedic; the augment "āṭ," acute by आडजादीनाम् (पा. ६-४-७२), which, taught later, remains. "Naraḥ" — the stem accent. "Sanitau" — स्त्रियां क्तिन्; by the vārttika "tituträ… grahādīnām iti vaktavyam" (पा. ७-२-९-१) the "iṭ" of "grahādi" roots, and so "iṭ" here. "Viprāsaḥ" — "vipra" formed with "ran" by nipātana in "ṛjrendra…," end-acute. "Dhiyāyavaḥ" — "dhi dhāraṇe": "dhīyate dhāryate 'vabudhyate śrutam artha-jātam anayeti dhīḥ prajñā; tām ātmana icchantīti" — "kyac," क्याच्छन्दसि (पा. ३-२-१७०) the affix "u"; अतो लोपः; end-acute by the affix accent.

original p. 325

Rik 6 continued

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ये नरः (ye naraḥ) — those men (who praise Indra) | समोहे (samohe) — in battle (also for obtaining victory) | वा (vā) — or (and) | तोकस्य (tokasya) — of offspring, sons and so on | सनितौ (sanitau) — also for the gaining | आशत (āśata) — attain Indra | वा (vā) — or | विप्रासः (viprāsaḥ) — wise people | धियायवः (dhiyāyavaḥ) — those desiring understanding or knowledge (too) | आशत (āśata) — attain Indra himself.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Those men who desire victory in battle, and offspring such as sons and grandsons, obtain their desires by praising Indra. And the wise, and those who desire understanding, obtain their desires from Indra himself.

॥ English Translation ॥

Whatever men have recourse to Indra, in battle or for the acquirement of offspring, and the wise who are desirous of understanding (obtain their desires).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Words to be supplied. The sense of this rik can be guessed correctly, but some principal words must be supplied. Since the previous rik declares that Indra's greatness or powers are boundless, in keeping with that purport this rik says that people take refuge in Indra for victory in battle that they desire, for the winning of offspring, and for knowledge, and that, praising him with hymns and the like, they obtain their desires. That is the main sense.

original p. 326

Rik 6: Special Topics (continued); grammar

"Samohe" — the word samohe is read among the forty-six battle-names beginning with raṇa (Ni. 3-9).

"Tokasya" — the word tokam is read among the fifteen words for "offspring" beginning with tuk (Ni. 3-2).

"Āśata" — a form of the root aśū vyāptau ("to pervade, attain"). "To attain Indra" means to entreat Indra with praises and the like.

"Naraḥ" — the nominative plural of the ṛ-ending word nṛ. This word is also used as an a-stem; in that case naraḥ is a nominative singular.

"Viprāsaḥ" — viprāḥ is the ancient form of usage.

"Dhiyāyavaḥ" — धि धारणे । धीयते धार्यत्वेनावबुध्यते श्रुतमर्थजातमनयेति धिया प्रज्ञा । तामात्मन इच्छन्तीति धियायवः (dhi dhāraṇe | dhīyate dhāryatvenāvabudhyate śrutam artha-jātam anayeti dhiyā prajñā | tām ātmana icchantīti dhiyāyavaḥ) — "dhi in the sense of holding; that by which heard matters are held in the mind and understood is dhiyā — insight; those who desire that for themselves are dhiyāyavaḥ." The root dhi means "to hold" or "to know." Because by it one understands matters one has heard or seen, the word dhiyā arises. Those who desire insight or wisdom are called dhiyāyavaḥ.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar page, noted briefly

समोहे (samohe) — by the Phiṭ sūtra "phiṣaḥ" (फि. सू. १) it takes the final accent of the base; वा — unaccented by चादयोऽनुदात्ताः (फि. सू. १४४). आशत (āśata) — root aśū vyāptau with luṅ; cli before luṅ (पा. सू. ३-१-४३); Vedic loss of cli; āṭ augment for luṅ/laṅ/lṛṅ before a root with initial vowel (आडजादीनाम्, पा. सू. ६-४-७२), which is udātta; saty śiṣṭa-svara keeps the accent; vṛddhi of a+a by āṭaś ca (पा. सू. ६-१-९०) as a single substitute; ā is udātta; in the third plural ātmanepada jha → at (पा. सू. ७-१-५), giving āśata. नरः (naraḥ) — final-udātta by base accent. सनितौ (sanitau) — root sana with ktin by "striyāṃ ktin" (पा. सू. ३-३-९४); though तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (पा. सू. ७-२-९) … continues on p. 327

original p. 327

Rik 6 grammar closes; Sūkta 8, Rik 7

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16." Numbers as printed. Continuing सनितौ: … here the "iṭ" would be forbidden; but by the vārttika तितुत्रेष्वग्रहादीनाम् (पा. सू. ७-२-९, भा. वा. १) the prohibition does not apply to "ti, tu, tra" after the "grahādi" roots; the "grahādi" list is an ākṛtigaṇa, so here too the prohibition does not apply, as in "nigṛhītiḥ, nipaṭhitiḥ." विप्रासः — "ṛjrendrāgravipra…" (उ. सू. २-१८६) forms "vipra" with "ran" by nipātana, so first-syllable acute by the "n"-mark; in the nominative plural आज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-५०) "asuk." धियायवः — "dhi dhāraṇe": "dhīyate dhāryate 'vabudhyate śrutam arthajātaṃ sarvam anayā iti dhiyā prajñā"; "dhiyam ātmana icchati": सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (पा. सू. ३-१-८) "kyac"; क्याच्छन्दसि (पा. सू. ३-२-१७०) "u" in the "tācchīlya" senses after roots ending in "kyac, kyaṣ, kyaṅ" and the kaṇḍvādi "yak"; अतो लोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-४८) the loss of "a" before an ārdhadhātuka: "dhiyāyu," end-acute by the affix accent; nominative plural "dhiyāyavaḥ." ॥६॥

original p. 327

Sūkta 8, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यः कु॒क्षिः सो॑म॒पात॑मः समु॒द्र इ॑व॒ पिन्व॑ते । उ॒र्वीरापो॒ न का॒कुदः॑ ॥७॥

yáḥ kukṣíḥ somapā́tamaḥ samudrá iva pínvate | urvī́r ā́po ná kākúdaḥ ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यः । कुक्षिः । सोमऽपातमः । समुद्रः । इव । पिन्वते ॥ उर्वीः । आपः । न । काकुदः ॥७॥

yaḥ | kukṣiḥ | soma-pātamaḥ | samudraḥ | iva | pinvate || urvīḥ | āpaḥ | na | kākudaḥ ||7||

original p. 328

Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यः कुक्षिरस्येन्द्रस्योदरप्रदेशः सोमपातमो ऽतिशयेन सोमस्य पाता स कुक्षिः समुद्र इव पिन्वते । वर्धते । सेचनार्थो धातुरौचित्येन वृद्धिं लक्षयति । काकुदो मुखसंबन्धिन्य उर्वीर्बह्व्य आपो न जलानीव । जिह्वासंबन्धमास्योदकं यथा कदाचिदपि न शुष्यति तथेन्द्रस्य कुक्षिः सोमपूरितो न शुष्यतीत्यर्थः । यद्यपि श्लोक इत्यादिषु सप्तपञ्चाशत्सु वाङ्नामसु काकुज्जिह्वेति पठितं तथाप्युदकसंबन्धसिद्ध्यर्थमत्र काकुच्छब्देन मुखमुपलक्ष्यते । संबन्धवाचिनस्तद्धितस्यात्र छान्दसो लोपो द्रष्टव्यः ॥

yaḥ kukṣir asyendrasyodara-pradeśaḥ somapātamo 'tiśayena somasya pātā sa kukṣiḥ samudra iva pinvate | vardhate | secanārtho dhātur aucityena vṛddhiṃ lakṣayati | kākudo mukha-saṃbandhinya urvīr bahvya āpo na jalānīva | jihvā-saṃbandham āsyodakaṃ yathā kadācid api na śuṣyati tathendrasya kukṣiḥ soma-pūrito na śuṣyatīty arthaḥ | yadyapi śloka ity-ādiṣu saptapañcāśatsu vāṅ-nāmasu kākuj jihveti paṭhitaṃ tathāpy udaka-saṃbandha-siddhy-artham atra kākuc-chabdena mukham upalakṣyate | saṃbandha-vācinas taddhitasyātra chāndaso lopo draṣṭavyaḥ ||

Translation: "That belly (kukṣiḥ) — the region of the stomach — of Indra, somapātamaḥ — which drinks Soma to the utmost — that belly swells (pinvate, grows) like the ocean. The root [pinv] has the sense of sprinkling; by propriety it here indicates growth. Kākudaḥ — [the waters] connected with the mouth: urvīḥ, many āpaḥ, like waters. As the water in the mouth, connected with the tongue, never at any time dries up, so Indra's belly, filled with Soma, does not dry — this is the sense. Although kākut and jihvā are read among the fifty-seven words for speech beginning with śloka, still here, to establish the connection with water, the mouth is indicated by the word kākut. The taddhita suffix of relation has been dropped here by Vedic license."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed): "Somapātamaḥ" — "somaṃ pibatīti somapāḥ"; the "ā" acute by the root accent, kept by the kṛt-final second member's accent; "tamap," "p"-marked, unaccented. "Samudraḥ" — end-acute as a stem. "Iva" — with "iva," no loss of the case-ending and the first member's accent, by the vārttika (पा. २-१-४-२). "Pinvate" — "pivi secane," "i"-marked, so "num" by "idito num dhātoḥ"; "śap," "p"-marked, unaccented, and the lasārvadhātuka, so the root accent remains. "Urvīḥ" — "uru," end-acute; वोतो गुणवचनात् (पा. ४-१-४४) "ṅīṣ"; "y" substitute; उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात् (पा. ६-१-१७४) the "ī" acute; with "jas," the single substitute acute. "Āpaḥ" — the stem accent. "Kākudaḥ" — end-acute by the stem accent.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यः कुक्षिः (yaḥ kukṣiḥ) — which belly of Indra | सोमपातमः (somapātamaḥ) — which drinks Soma (that belly) | समुद्रः इव (samudra iva) — like the ocean | पिन्वते (pinvate) — swells, grows big | (and) काकुदः (kākudaḥ) — [of the tongue] connected with the mouth (that is, within the mouth) | उर्वीः (urvīḥ) — abundant | आपः न (āpo na) — like water (is always moist and not dry).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Because he drinks Soma to excess, Indra's belly swells large like the ocean, and the tongue in his mouth is always moist, as if wetted with water.

॥ English Translation ॥

The belly of Indra which drinks soma-juice most abundantly swells like ocean and like the ample fluids of the palate.

original p. 329

Rik 7: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Here Indra's drinking of Soma is described by hyperbole (utprekṣā): Indra drinks abundant Soma-juice (offered by us), and therefore his belly swells like the ocean; and because he drinks Soma again and again, his palate is always moist with Soma. As the saliva that flows constantly in the human mouth keeps the palate always moist, so Indra's stomach also is always wet with Soma-drinking and never dries. That is the idea.

"Kākudaḥ" — kakut means the palate (English "palate" in the source); kākuda = connected with it. Or, since kākut and jihvā are read among the fifty-seven words for speech beginning with śloka (Ni. 2-23), it is understood to mean "tongue." Everyone knows that the tongue, the mouth, are always moist; that is the comparison the poet draws here. Besides, in the Nirukta there is the statement काकुदं तालु इत्याचक्षते (kākudaṃ tālv ity ācakṣate, "they call the kākuda the palate," Ni. 5-26); and this word also means "mountain peak." On that reading the sense is that streams that flow down from the top of a mountain keep the mountain always wet; "like that" the sense may also be taken.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 329–330, Kannada; page header p. 329 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16"; numbers as printed

सोमपातमः (somapātamaḥ) — somaṃ pibati iti somapāḥ: the "ka" of आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः (पा. सू. ३-२-३) is set aside by आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च (पा. सू. ३-२-७४), whose "ca" brings "vic"; "pā" end-acute by धातोः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६२), kept by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९); then अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (पा. सू. ५-३-५५) "tamap," "p"-marked, unaccented by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. सू. ३-१-४). समुद्रः (samudraḥ) — final-udātta by base accent; with iva the case-ending is dropped and the first member's accent kept ("ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca," पा. सू. २-१-४, म. २). पिन्वते (pinvate) — root pivi secane; num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (पा. सू. ७-१-५८); ātmanepada laṭ, third singular ta; ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere (पा. सू. ३-४-७९) gives te; śap; śap is pit so unaccented; the root keeps its accent.

Rik 7 grammar closes

Kannada, continued; numbers as printed. "Pinvate" (concluded): "te," after an anudāttet root, is unaccented by तास्यनुदात्तेत्… (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६); but यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) — a verb in a clause with the relative "yat" is never unaccented — so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not apply.

उर्वीः — "uru," end-acute; वोतो गुणवचनात् (पा. सू. ४-१-४४) — after a quality-word ending in short "u," "ṅīṣ" optionally in the feminine; "y" substitute: "urvī"; उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात् (पा. सू. ६-१-१७४) — after an acute replaced by "y, v, r, l" preceded by a consonant, the nadī vowel and a "śas"-etc. ending are acute — so the "ī" is acute; "urvī + as": प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः (पा. सू. ६-१-१०२) the long vowel, acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. सू. ८-२-५). आपः — the stem accent. काकुदः — "kākuj jihvā" (निरु. "१-११-३८" as printed [?]): Yāska lists "kākut" among the fifty-seven speech-words beginning "ślokaḥ"; taken so, it does not construe with the water of "āpaḥ," so here the mouth is indicated by "kākut"; by the Mahābhāṣya's भूमनिन्दाप्रशंसासु नित्ययोगेऽतिशायने । संबन्धेऽस्तिविवक्षायां भवन्ति मतुबादयः (पा. सू. ५-२-९४ म. भा.) "matup" in the sense of relation, dropped as Vedic: "kākudaḥ," "connected with the mouth"; end-acute by the stem accent. ॥७॥

Sūkta 8, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ए॒वा ह्य॑स्य सू॒नृता॑ विर॒प्शी गोम॑ती म॒ही । प॒क्वा शाखा॒ न दा॒शुषे॑ ॥८॥

evā́ hy asya sūnṛ́tā virapśī́ gómatī mahī́ | pakvā́ śākhā ná dāśúṣe ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

एव । हि । अस्य । सूनृता । विऽरप्शी । गोऽमती । मही ॥ पक्वा । शाखा । न । दाशुषे ॥८॥

eva | hi | asya | sūnṛtā | vi-rapśī | go-matī | mahī || pakvā | śākhā | na | dāśuṣe ||8||

original p. 331

Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अभिप्लवषडहगतेषूक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एवा ह्यस्य सूनृतेत्यनुरूपस्तृचः । एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि ते इति खण्डे अथ ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इत्युपक्रम्य एवा ह्यसि वीरयुरेवा ह्यस्य सूनृता । आ. ६-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ अस्येन्द्रस्य सूनृता प्रियसत्यरूपा वाग्दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय तदर्थमेवा हि एवं खलु । अनन्तरपदवक्ष्यमाणगुणोपेता भवतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशी । विरप्शी विविधरपणोपेतवाक्ययुक्ता । बहुविधोपचारवादिनीत्यर्थः । गोमती बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेता । गोप्रदेत्यर्थः । अत एव मही महती पूज्या । यथोक्तवाचो दृष्टान्तः । पक्वा शाखा न । यथा बहुभिः पक्वैः फलैरुपेता पनसवृक्षादिशाखा प्रीतिहेतुस्तद्वत् । यद्यपि महन्नामसु व्राधन्विरप्शीति पठितं तथाप्यत्र महीत्यनेन पुनरुक्तिप्रसङ्गादेवमर्थो गृहीतः ॥

abhiplava-ṣaḍaha-gateṣūkthyeṣu tṛtīya-savane brāhmaṇācchaṃsina evā hy asya sūnṛtety anurūpas tṛcaḥ | ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te iti khaṇḍe atha brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ity upakramya evā hy asi vīrayur evā hy asya sūnṛtā | ā. 6-8 | iti sūtritam || asyendrasya sūnṛtā priya-satya-rūpā vāg dāśuṣe havir dattavate yajamānāya tad-artham evā hi evaṃ khalu | anantara-pada-vakṣyamāṇa-guṇopetā bhavatīty arthaḥ | kīdṛśī | virapśī vividha-rapaṇopeta-vākya-yuktā | bahu-vidhopacāra-vādinīty arthaḥ | gomatī bahvībhir gobhir upetā | go-pradety arthaḥ | ata eva mahī mahatī pūjyā | yathokta-vāco dṛṣṭāntaḥ | pakvā śākhā na | yathā bahubhiḥ pakvaiḥ phalair upetā panasa-vṛkṣādi-śākhā prīti-hetus tadvat | yadyapi mahan-nāmasu vrādhan virapśīti paṭhitaṃ tathāpy atra mahīty anena punarukti-prasaṅgād evam artho gṛhītaḥ ||

Translation: "In the ukthya [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, at the third pressing, for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the triplet beginning evā hy asya sūnṛtā is the anurūpa. So it is laid down in the section ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te, beginning 'atha brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ': 'evā hy asi vīrayuḥ, evā hy asya sūnṛtā' (Āśvalāyana 6-8). Asya — of this Indra, the sūnṛtā — speech of the nature of the pleasant and the true — is, to the dāśuṣe, the sacrificer who has given the oblation, [given] for that very purpose; thus [evā hi]: it is endowed with the qualities stated in the next words. What kind? Virapśī — equipped with speech having various utterings; that is, speaking many kinds of courtesies. Gomatī — furnished with many cows; that is, giving cows. Therefore mahī — great, honourable. An illustration of speech so described: Pakvā śākhā na — as a branch of a jackfruit tree or the like, laden with many ripe fruits, is a cause of delight, so [is his speech]. Although vrādhan and virapśī are read among the words for 'great,' here, since mahī would then repeat it, this sense is taken."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16"): "Evā" — end-acute by "evādīnām ante"; long by "nipātasya ca" in the saṃhitā. "Hi" — a nipāta, first-syllable acute. "Asya" — referring back to Indra, "aś" by "idamo 'nvādeśe…," wholly unaccented. "Sūnṛtā" — "ūna parihāṇe": "suṭarām ūnayati apriyam iti sūn"; "sā cāsāv ṛtā satyā ceti sūnṛtā priyasatyā vāk"; the "ṛ" acute by "parādiś chandasi bahulam." "Virapśī" — "vicitraṃ rapaṇaṃ virap," "rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci," "kvip" by "sampadādi"; "tad eṣām astīti virapśāni vākyāni"; "ini"; यस्येति च (पा. ६-४-१४८) loss of "a"; अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते "ṅīp" (पा. ४-१-५); the "i" acute by the affix accent; the loss of "n" Vedic; the single long vowel acute. "Gomatī" — "gāvo 'syāṃ santīti," "matup" and "ṅīp" unaccented, so the stem accent. "Mahī" — "mahatī": उगितश्च (पा. ४-१-६) "ṅīp"; the vārttika "bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam" (पा. ६-१-१७३-१) makes it acute; the loss of "at" Vedic. "Pakvā" — "ḍupacaṣ pāke," निष्ठा (पा. ३-२-१०२) "kta"; पचो वः (पा. ८-२-५२) "v"; चोः कुः (पा. ८-२-३०) "k"; end-acute; with "ṭāp," the long single vowel acute. "Śākhā" — "śākhṛ ślākhṛ vyāptau," "ac" (pacādi), end-acute expected, but as of the vṛṣādi ākṛtigaṇa first-syllable acute. "Dāśuṣe" — "dāśṛ dāne," दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्च (पा. ६-१-१२) by nipātana no "iṭ" and no doubling; यचि भम् (पा. १-४-१८) "bha"; वसोः संप्रसारणम् (पा. ६-४-१३१); the prior form; शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. ८-३-६०) "ṣ"; the "u" acute by the affix accent.

original p. 332

Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अस्य (asya) — of Indra | सूनृता (sūnṛtā) — the pleasant and true (speech) | दाशुषे (dāśuṣe) — to the sacrificer who offers the oblation | पक्वा शाखा न (pakvā śākhā na) — like a branch laden with ripe fruit | विरप्शी (virapśī) — of many kinds (granting what is wished) | गोमती (gomatī) — giving cows | मही (mahī) — worthy of honour | एवा हि (evā hi) — [is] indeed (always so).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Toward the sacrificer who gives the oblation, Indra's word is true and grants many desires. Moreover that word of Indra, like a branch full of ripe fruits, gives the sacrificer his many kinds of desired things, and gives cows as well. Because Indra's word is always worshipful it is deserving of respect; it never turns out false. No "English Translation" block is printed for this rik in the source, as also for Rik 7.6; none is supplied here.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The application. At the time of reciting the mantras in the rite called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the third pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the triplet evā hy asya sūnṛtā. Āśvalāyana says this in his Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 6-8) in the section ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te, beginning atha brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ, directing that the riks evā hy asi vīrayuḥ (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-92-2[?], the last digit unclear) and evā hy asya sūnṛtā (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-8-8) be recited.

The sense of the rik is somewhat involved. Indra always gives each person what they desire when they worship him. His word is pleasant and true; it does not become false. And as a branch of a jackfruit tree laden with fine ripe fruit gives joy to people, so Indra's word is pleasing to people. For Indra gives to the sacrificer who gives him the oblation, and to others like him, cows and many other desired things. Therefore his word is worshipful and deserving of honour. The main idea is that it can never turn out false.

"Sūnṛtā" — ऊन परिहाणे । सुतरामूनयत्यप्रियमिति सून् । सा चासावृता सत्या चेति सूनृता प्रियसत्या वाक् (ūna parihāṇe | sutarām ūnayaty apriyam iti sūn | sā cāsāv ṛtā satyā ceti sūnṛtā priya-satyā vāk) — "[root] ūna, 'to diminish'; that which thoroughly removes the unpleasant is sūn; that, and also ṛtā — true — is sūnṛtā: pleasant and true speech." That is, the root ūna means to remove; because it removes the unpleasant, evil, so well, it is called sūn; ṛta means truth; so the word sūnṛtā means speech that is not unpleasant — that is, pleasant and true. Skandasvāmī, for the word virapśī, gives besides the sense सर्वकामधुक् (sarvakāma-dhuk, "milking all desires": that gives all wished-for things) another: सूनृता गर्जितलक्षणा वाक् । गोमती आपोऽत्र गाव उच्यन्ते (sūnṛtā garjita-lakṣaṇā vāk | gomatī āpo 'tra gāva ucyante) — "sūnṛtā is speech characterized by thundering; gomatī: here the waters are called gāvaḥ [cows]." That is, here the word go is to be taken as "water." Sūnṛtā means a rumbling speech or sound; so the words sūnṛtā gomatī are taken to mean "waters with sound," that is, rain accompanied by the thunder of clouds. Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16." The top of the page ends Skandasvāmī's gloss: "…āpo 'tra gāva ucyante" — here "go" is to be taken as water; "sūnṛtā" means speech accompanied by thunder, or sound; so "sūnṛtā gomatī" means waters with sound, that is, rain with the thunder of clouds.

original p. 333

Rik 8: Special Topics (continued)

"Virapśī" — विविधरपणोपेतवाक्ययुता । बहुविधोपचारवादिनी । रप लप व्यक्तायां वाचि । विचित्रं रपणं यस्यां वाचि अस्तीति सा विरप्शी (vividha-rapaṇopeta-vākya-yutā | bahu-vidhopacāra-vādinī | rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci | vicitraṃ rapaṇaṃ yasyāṃ vāci astīti sā virapśī) — "speech joined with various utterings; speaking many kinds of courtesies. [Roots] rapa, lapa in the sense of clear speech. That speech in which there is varied speaking is virapśī." The root rap means to speak, to talk; vi-rapaṇa means speaking specially, or in a manifold or varied way. A speech having such words is virapśī: speech that embraces many kinds of courtesies. That is: Indra's word gives many kinds of desired things. Although the word virapśī is customarily taken in the sense "great" (mahat), here the word mahī ("great") is also present in the rik, and so it would be a fault of repetition; therefore the Bhāṣyakāra supposes the component-sense for this word.

"Evā" — the vowel ā is lengthened here for the convenience of the meter.

"Gomatī" — बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेता । गोप्रदेत्यर्थः (bahvībhir gobhir upetā | go-pradety arthaḥ) — "furnished with many cows"; i.e., giving cows.

"Pakvā śākhā" — "pakvā śākhā" does not here mean a branch that is itself ripe, but a branch laden with ripe fruits. Since such fruits are wanted by everyone, the poet gives this comparison. Here na means "like" (iva).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 333–335, Kannada; characterized, numbers as printed

एव — एवादीनामन्तः (फि. सू. ८२): the final of "eva" etc. is acute; in the saṃhitā निपातस्य च (पा. सू. "६-३-१-३६" as printed, i.e. 6-3-136) lengthens a particle in a mantra. हि — निपाता आद्युदात्ताः (फि. सू. ८०), first-syllable acute. अस्य — refers back to Indra, already mentioned, so by इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ (पा. सू. २-४-३२) the unaccented "aś" replaces "idam" ("ś"-marked, the whole); "a" unaccented, and "sya" unaccented by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. सू. "३२१-४" as printed, i.e. 3-1-4): wholly unaccented.

सूनृता (p. 334) — "ūna parihāṇe": "sutarām ūnayati apriyam" — "sūn," that which thoroughly removes the unpleasant; "ṛtā," the true; "sūn ca sā ṛtā ca" — pleasant and true speech. In परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१९९), "sakthaṃ" is carried from सक्थं चाक्रान्तात् (पा. सू. ६-२-१९८), so the sense would be that in the Veda the first syllable of "sakthi" as second member is often acute; "vibhāṣā" is carried from विभाषोत्पुच्छे (पा. सू. ६-२-१९६), so "bahula" is not used merely for optionality: by "bahūn arthān lāti iti bahulam" it conveys many senses, as the vārttika says: परादिश्च परान्तश्च पूर्वान्तश्चापि दृश्यते । पूर्वादयश्च दृश्यन्ते व्यत्ययो बहुलं ततः ॥ — so the accent comes even without "sakthi," and in "sūnṛtā" the "ṛ" is acute.

विरप्शी — "vicitraṃ rapaṇaṃ virap," "rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci," with "vi": संपदादिभ्यः क्विप् (पा. सू. ३-३-१०८ वा. ९) "kvip," wholly lost; "virap" = varied speech; "virapa eṣāṃ vākyānām asti iti virapśāni" — sentences with varied words; speech in which such sentences are, "virapśinī"; "virapśāni asyāṃ santi": अत इनिठनौ (पा. सू. ५-२-११५) "ini" in the possessive sense after a short-"a" stem in the first case: "virapśa + in"; यस्येति च (पा. सू. ६-४-१४८) loss of "a": "virapśin"; ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् (पा. सू. ४-१-५) "ṅīp" after "ṛ"- and "n"-ending stems: "virapśin + ī"; the "i" acute by the affix accent; the "n" lost as Vedic; अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (पा. सू. "६-१-६-१-१०१" as printed, i.e. 6-1-101) the long vowel: "virapśī"; the single substitute of the acute "i" and unaccented "ī" acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. सू. ८-२-५).

गोमती — "gāvaḥ asyāṃ santi": तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् (पा. सू. ५-२-९४) "matup"; उगितश्च (पा. सू. ४-१-६) "ṅīp"; both "p"-marked, unaccented; the stem accent of "go" remains. continues on p. 335 Page 334 carries the Kannada grammar of सूनृता and विरप्शी, गोमती as summarized above; its closing lines, continuing on p. 335, treat मही, पक्वा, शाखा and दाशुषे. Kannada; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16"; numbers as printed.

original p. 334
original p. 335

Rik 8 grammar (continued)

मही — "mahatī": after "mahat," उगितश्च (पा. सू. ४-१-६) "ṅīp" after an "ugit" stem in the feminine; "ṅīp," "p"-marked, would be unaccented, but the vārttika बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३-१), under शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (पा. सू. ६-१-१७३), makes the nadī affix and the "śas"-etc. endings after "bṛhat, mahat" acute; the "at" of "mahat" lost as Vedic.

पक्वा — "ḍupacaṣ pāke": निष्ठा (पा. सू. ३-२-१०२) "kta" in the past sense; पचो वः (पा. सू. ८-२-५२) "v" for the "t"; चोः कुः (पा. सू. ८-२-३०) "k" for "c"; end-acute by the affix accent; अजाद्यतष्टाप् (पा. सू. ४-१-४) "ṭāp"; अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (पा. सू. ६-१-१०१): "pakvā"; "ṭāp," "p"-marked, unaccented; the single long "ā" acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. सू. ८-२-५).

शाखा — "śākhṛ ślākhṛ vyāptau," of the pacādi class: नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः (पा. सू. ३-१-१३४) "ac"; end-acute by चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) would apply, but the vṛṣādi class being an ākṛtigaṇa, "śākha" in it is first-syllable acute by वृषादीनां च (पा. सू. ६-१-२०३); with "ṭāp" and the long vowel, the "ā" is unaccented by स्थानेऽन्तरतमः (पा. सू. १-१-५०), then svarita by उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. सू. ८-४-६६).

दाशुषे — by nipātana in दाश्वान्साह्वान्मीढ्वांश्च (पा. सू. ६-१-१२), "dāśṛ dāne" with "kvasu" takes neither "iṭ" nor doubling; dative "ṅe": "dāśvas + e"; यचि भम् (पा. सू. १-४-१८) "bha"; वसोः संप्रसारणम् (पा. सू. ६-४-१३१) "u" for "v"; (p. 336) संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. सू. ६-१-१०८) the prior form: "dāśus + e"; आदेशप्रत्यययोः (पा. सू. ८-३-५९) "ṣ" for the "s" belonging to the affix "vasu": "dāśuṣe." शासिवसिघसीनां च (पा. सू. ८-३-६०) names "vas" — the root "vasa nivāse," not the affix "vasu" — so the "ṣ" does not come from that sūtra here; this was explained before (ऋ. सं. १-६-८). The "u" acute by the affix accent. ॥८॥ Saṃhitā marks as read from the print; Pada unaccented. On this page several strokes seem to stand one syllable early over closely set letters ("ta" of "ūtaya," "dya," "san," "śu"), so the placement is doubtful: [accent ?].

Sūkta 8, Rik 9

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ए॒वा हि ते॒ विभू॑तय ऊ॒त॑य इन्द्र॒ माव॑ते । [accent ?] स॒द्य॑श्चित्स॑न्ति दा॒शु॑षे ॥९॥ [accent ?]

evā́ hi te víbhūtaya ūtaya indra mā́vate | [accent ?] sadyaś cít santi dāśuṣe ||9|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

एव । हि । ते । विऽभूतयः । ऊतयः । इन्द्र । मावते ॥ सद्यः । चित् । सन्ति । दाशुषे ॥९॥

eva | hi | te | vi-bhūtayaḥ | ūtayaḥ | indra | māvate || sadyaḥ | cit | santi | dāśuṣe ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र ते तव विभूतय ऐश्वर्यविशेषा एवा हि एवंविधाः खलु । किंविधा इति तदुच्यते । मावते मत्सदृशाय दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानायोतयस्त्वदीयरक्षारूपाः सद्यश्चित्सन्ति । यदा कर्मानुष्ठितं तदैव भवन्ति ॥ मावते । मत्सदृशाय । वतुप्करणे युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां छन्दसि सादृश्य उपसंख्यानम् । पा. ५-२-३९-१ । इत्यस्मच्छब्दाद्वतुप् । मपर्यन्तस्य प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्च । पा. ७-२-९८ । इति मादेशः । अद्शब्देन सहातो गुणे । पा. ६-१-९७ । इति पररूपत्वम् । दृग्दृशवतुषु । पा. ६-३-८९ । इत्यनुवृत्तावा सर्वनाम्नः । पा. ६-३-९१ । इति दकारस्याकारः । सवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । वतुपः पित्त्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्वर एव शिष्यते । सद्यः । समाने द्यवीत्यर्थे । सद्यः परुत्परार्यैषमः । पा. ५-३-२२ । इत्यादिना निपातितम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । चित् । चादयो ऽनुदात्ताः ॥ सन्ति । अस भुवि । लटः स्थाने झि । झो ऽन्तः । पा. ७-१-३ । आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः । पा. २-४-७२ । इति शपो लुक् । तिङः प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् । पा. १-१-६२ । इति शबकारमाश्रित्य लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वं न भवति । वर्णाश्रयविधौ प्रत्ययलक्षणं नास्ति । परि. २१ । इति निषेधात् । दाशुषे । गतमन्त्रे गतम् ॥

he indra te tava vibhūtaya aiśvarya-viśeṣā evā hi evaṃvidhāḥ khalu | kiṃvidhā iti tad ucyate | māvate mat-sadṛśāya dāśuṣe havir dattavate yajamānāyotayas tvadīya-rakṣā-rūpāḥ sadyaś cit santi | yadā karmānuṣṭhitaṃ tadaiva bhavanti || māvate | mat-sadṛśāya | vatup-karaṇe yuṣmad-asmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam | pā. 5-2-39-1 | ity asmac-chabdād vatup | mapary-antasya pratyayottarapadayoś ca | pā. 7-2-98 | iti mādeśaḥ | ad-śabdena sahāto guṇe | pā. 6-1-97 | iti pararūpatvam | dṛg-dṛśa-vatuṣu | pā. 6-3-89 | ity anuvṛttāv ā sarvanāmnaḥ | pā. 6-3-91 | iti dakārasyākāraḥ | savarṇa-dīrghatvam | vatupaḥ pittvāt prātipadika-svara eva śiṣyate | sadyaḥ | samāne dyavīty arthe | sadyaḥ parut-parāry-aiṣamaḥ | pā. 5-3-22 | ity-ādinā nipātitam | pratyaya-svareṇāntodāttatvam | cit | cādayo 'nudāttāḥ || santi | asa bhuvi | laṭaḥ sthāne jhi | jho 'ntaḥ | pā. 7-1-3 | ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ | pā. 2-4-72 | iti śapo luk | tiṅaḥ pratyayādyudāttatvam | pratyaya-lope pratyaya-lakṣaṇam | pā. 1-1-62 | iti śabakāram āśritya lasārvadhātukānudāttatvaṃ na bhavati | varṇāśraya-vidhau pratyaya-lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti | pari. 21 | iti niṣedhāt | dāśuṣe | gatamantre gatam ||

Translation: "O Indra! Your vibhūtayaḥ — special powers — are indeed (evā hi) of this kind. Of what kind? It is said: māvate — to one like me — dāśuṣe, the sacrificer who has given the oblation — your ūtayaḥ, protections — santi exist sadyaś cit, at once: they exist at the very moment the rite is performed." The grammatical remainder of the Sanskrit explains: māvate — by the vārttika on vatup after yuṣmad / asmad in the Veda in the sense of resemblance (Pā. 5-2-39 vā. 1), the suffix vatup comes after asmad; ma replaces the end of the stem (Pā. 7-2-98); pararūpa of the "a" with "ad" (Pā. 6-1-97); the d becomes ā by "ā sarvanāmnaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-91); savarṇa-dīrgha; vatup is pit, so the base accent stands. Sadyaḥ — formed irregularly (nipātita) in the sense samāne dyavi ("on the same day") by Pā. 5-3-22 and its class; final-udātta by the suffix; cit is unaccented (cādayo 'nudāttāḥ). Santi — root as bhuvi, jhi for laṭ, jh → ant (Pā. 7-1-3), śap dropped (Pā. 2-4-72); the "tiṅ" is first-syllable acute by the affix accent; the lasārvadhātuka unaccentedness, which would come by pratyaya-lakṣaṇa (Pā. 1-1-62) through the "a" of the elided "śap," does not, by the paribhāṣā (pari. 21) that it does not govern a rule based on letters (varṇāśraya); dāśuṣe — "gone [explained] under the earlier mantra." Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16." The top of the page ends the Bhāṣya's grammar, given under p. 336.

original p. 337

Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | ते (te) — your | विभूतयः (vibhūtayaḥ) — special glories | एवा हि (evā hi) — are of this kind (that is) | मावते (māvate) — to one like me | दाशुषे (dāśuṣe) — to the sacrificer who offers the oblation | (your glories are) ऊतयः (ūtayaḥ) — in the form of protections | सद्यश्चित् सन्ति (sadyaś cit santi) — they are at once present.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! The protections you give to a sacrificer like me who offers the oblation are endowed with this kind of greatness: they arrive at the very time we are performing the rite. This very greatness is your special glory.

॥ English Translation ॥

Verily, Indra, your glories are at all times (at once) the protectors of every such worshipper as I am.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

O Indra! You always protect people like us. And in particular, to the sacrificer who offers the oblation, your protection comes at once, while the sacrifice is being performed. Is not this your glory? That is the chief idea.

"Evā" — for the convenience of the meter, the syllable va is lengthened (evā).

"Māvate" — मत्सदृशाय (mat-sadṛśāya) — "like me; one equal to me."

"Sadyaścit" — immediately, at once, on the spot, without delay.

original p. 338

Rik 9: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 338–339, Kannada; characterized, numbers as printed

मावते — "mat-sadṛśāya," like me. Under यत्तदेतेभ्यः परिमाणे वतुप् (पा. सू. "५-२-९" as printed, i.e. 5-2-39) the vārttika वतुप्प्रकरणे युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां छन्दसि सादृश्य उपसंख्यानम् (पा. सू. ५-२-३९-१): in the "vatup" section, after "yuṣmad, asmad" in the Veda "vatup" in the sense of likeness: "asmad + vatup"; प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्च (पा. सू. ७-२-९८) "ma" for "asma": "ma + ad + vatup"; अतो गुणे (पा. सू. ६-१-९७) the later form: "mad + vatup"; आ सर्वनाम्नः (पा. सू. ६-३-९१), with दृग्दृशवतुषु (पा. सू. ६-३-८९) carried on, "ā" for the final of a pronoun before "dṛk, dṛś, vatu": "ma + ā + vat"; अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (पा. सू. ६-१-१०१): "māvat"; dative "ṅe": "māvate"; "vatup," "p"-marked, and "ṅe," a sup, are unaccented by अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. सू. ३-१-४); "mā" end-acute by the stem accent.

सद्यः — "samāne ahani": सद्यःपरुत्परार्यैषमः… (पा. सू. ५-३-२२) forms by nipātana "sa" for "samāna" and the affix "dyas" in the sense "day"; the Mahābhāṣya makes this plain with "samānasya sabhāvo dyaś cāhani"; end-acute by the affix accent.

चित् — चादयोऽनुदात्ताः (फि. सू. "८-४" as printed), unaccented.

सन्ति — "as," "laṭ," third plural "jhi"; झोऽन्तः (पा. सू. "७-२-३" as printed, i.e. 7-1-3) "ant": "as + anti"; कर्तरि शप् (पा. सू. ३-१-६८), elided by अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (पा. सू. २-४-७२); श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-१११) loss of the "a" of "as" before a "kit/ṅit" sārvadhātuka: "santi." Here the "tiṅ" "anti" is first-syllable acute by आद्युदात्तश्च (पा. सू. ३-१-३) … continues on p. 339

original p. 339

Rik 9 grammar closes; Sūkta 8, Rik 10

Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16." सन्ति (concluded): … first-syllable acute. Since "śap" is elided by "luk," the "anti" does not follow an "a"-taught base, so तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात्… (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) does not make the lasārvadhātuka "anti" unaccented. Though "śap" is elided, by प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (पा. सू. १-१-६२) the effect of the affix would still hold; and न लुमताङ्गस्य (पा. सू. १-१-६३) — after a "luk, ślu, lup" loss, operations on the aṅga conditioned by the lost affix do not occur — does not stop it, since the accent rule concerns the lasārvadhātuka, not the aṅga. So one might say the unaccentedness conditioned by "adupadeśa" follows by pratyayalakṣaṇa. That is not right: "adupadeśa" means having a short "a" at the time of teaching — that is "śap"; the unaccentedness would rest on the letter "a" of "śap," and by वर्णाश्रये नास्ति प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (परि. भा. २१) pratyayalakṣaṇa does not apply to an operation resting on a letter; so the sārvadhātuka is not after an "a"-taught base, and no unaccentedness arises. दाशुषे — explained under the earlier mantra. ॥९॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. In the second line strokes stand over "drā," "ma" and the final "ye"; placement doubtful, hence [accent ?].

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ए॒वा ह्य॑स्य॒ काम्या॒ स्तोम॑ उ॒क्थं च॒ शंस्या॑ । इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोम॑पीतये॑ ॥१०॥ [accent ?]

evā́ hy asya kā́myā stóma uktháṃ ca śáṃsyā | índrāya sómapītáye ||10|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

एव । हि । अस्य । काम्या । स्तोमः । उक्थम् । च । शंस्या ॥ इन्द्राय । सोमऽपीतये ॥१०॥

eva | hi | asya | kāmyā | stomaḥ | uktham | ca | śaṃsyā || indrāya | soma-pītaye ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अस्येन्द्रस्य स्तोमः सामसाध्यं स्तोत्रमुक्थं चर्क्साध्यं शस्त्रमुभे एवा ह्येते उभे एवंविधे खलु । किंविधे इति तदुच्यते । काम्या कामयितव्ये शंस्या ऋत्विग्भिः शंसनीये । किमर्थं शंसनमिति तदुच्यते । इन्द्राय सोमपीतये । इन्द्रस्य सोमपानार्थम् ॥ एवा ह्यस्य । व्यवहितमन्त्रे गतम् । काम्या । कमेर्णिङन्तादचो यत् । पा. ३-१-९७ । णेरनिटि । पा. ६-४-५१ । इति णिलोपः । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरिते प्राप्ते यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सुपो डादेशः । स्तोमः । अर्तिस्तुसु… इत्यादिना । उ. १-१४० । मन्प्रत्ययः । उक्थम् । वच परिभाषणे । पातॄतुदिवचिरिचिसिचिभ्यस्थक् । उ. २-७ । इति थक् । कित्त्वात्संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वगुणाभावौ । शंस्या । शंसु स्तुतौ । ण्यन्तादचो यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सुपो डादेशः । सोमस्य पीतिः सोमपीतिः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अथवा सोमस्य पीतिर्यस्येन्द्रस्येति सोमपीतिरिन्द्रः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् । पा. ६-२-१ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

asyendrasya stomaḥ sāma-sādhyaṃ stotram uktham ca ṛk-sādhyaṃ śastram ubhe evā hy ete ubhe evaṃvidhe khalu | kiṃvidhe iti tad ucyate | kāmyā kāmayitavye śaṃsyā ṛtvigbhiḥ śaṃsanīye | kim-arthaṃ śaṃsanam iti tad ucyate | indrāya somapītaye | indrasya soma-pānārtham || evā hy asya | vyavahita-mantre gatam | kāmyā | kamer ṇijantād aco yat | pā. 3-1-97 | ṇer aniṭi | pā. 6-4-51 | iti ṇi-lopaḥ | titsvaritam iti svarite prāpte yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatvam | supo ḍādeśaḥ | stomaḥ | artistusu… ity-ādinā | u. 1-140 | man-pratyayaḥ | uktham | vaca paribhāṣaṇe | pātṝtudivacirici-sicibhyas thak | u. 2-7 | iti thak | kittvāt saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatva-guṇābhāvau | śaṃsyā | śaṃsu stutau | ṇyantād aco yat | yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatvam | supo ḍādeśaḥ | somasya pītiḥ somapītiḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svare prāpte vyatyayenādyudāttatvam | athavā somasya pītir yasyendrasyeti somapītir indraḥ | bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam | pā. 6-2-1 | iti pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||

Translation: "Stoma — the praise sung, achieved through the Sāman — and uktha — the śastra recited, achieved through ṛks — these two are indeed of this kind (evā hi). Of what kind? Kāmyā — to be desired; śaṃsyā — to be recited by the ṛtvijs. For what purpose is the recitation? Indrāya somapītaye — for Indra's drinking of Soma. [The phrase evā hy asya was explained in the earlier mantra, Rik 8.]" The grammar (characterized): "kāmyā" — "yat" after the "ṇiṅ"-ended "kam" (3-1-97), loss of "ṇi" (6-4-51), first-syllable acute by "yato 'nāvaḥ"; "stomaḥ" — "man" (Uṇ. 1-140); "uktham" — "vac" with "thak" (Uṇ. 2-7), samprasāraṇa; "śaṃsyā" — "yat," first-syllable acute; "somapītaye" — first-syllable acute by vyatyaya, or as a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent (6-2-1).

original p. 340

Rik 10: word-meanings, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अस्य (asya) — of this Indra (made in regard to Indra) | स्तोमः (stomaḥ) — the praise in the form of Sāman singing | उक्थं च (uktham ca) — and the praise recited as a śastra from the ṛks (both these two kinds) | काम्या एव हि (kāmyā eva hi) — are indeed granting what is wished | these praises इन्द्राय सोमपीतये (indrāya somapītaye) — for Indra's drinking of Soma | शंस्या (śaṃsyā) — are praised by the ṛtvijs.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The praises in the form of Sāman chants with which the ṛtvijs invite Indra to drink Soma, and the ṛks recited as śastra with ṛk-mantras — both of these kinds of praise are indeed welcome to those people, sacrificers and others, who worship Indra.

॥ English Translation ॥

Verily his chanted and recited praises are to be desired and repeated to Indra, that he may drink the Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Stomaḥ"; "Uktham" — stoma means the Sāma-Veda mantras sung as chant; uktha means recitation as śastra, that is, reciting Ṛgveda mantras plainly, without melody, unlike chanting. We have already explained this matter earlier.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

The words एवा (evā), हि (hi), अस्य (asya) have been treated in the eighth mantra of this same sūkta.

original p. 341

Rik 10 grammar; close of Sūkta 8

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 16"; numbers as printed

काम्या (kāmyā) — root kamu kāntau ("to desire"); ṇic in its own sense by "kameṇiṅ" (पा. सू. ३-१-३०); the penultimate vowel strengthened by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (पा. सू. ७-२-११६); then yat after a vowel-ending root by "ac-o yat" (पा. सू. ३-१-९७); the ṇi dropped by "ṇeraniṭi" (पा. सू. ६-४-५१); yat is t-marked, so svarita would be expected (पा. सू. ६-१-१८५), but by "yato 'nāvaḥ" (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३), with "dvyac" carried from निष्ठा च द्व्यजनात् (पा. सू. ६-१-२०५), a two-vowel word ending in "yat" after a stem other than "nau" is first-syllable acute; the dual au replaced by ḍā (पा. सू. ७-१-३९). स्तोमः (stomaḥ) — root ṣṭuñ stutau with man by अर्तिस्तुसुहुसृधृक्षिक्षुभायावापदियक्षिनीभ्यो मन् (उ. सू. १-१४२ [?], the figures unclear); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (पा. सू. ७-३-८४). उक्थम् (uktham) — root vaca paribhāṣaṇe ("to speak") with thak by पातॄतुदिवचिरिचिसिचिभ्यस्थक् (उ. सू. २-१६४ [?], as printed; the Bhāṣya gave "उ. २-७"); the suffix is kit, so saṃprasāraṇa by वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. सू. ६-१-१५), the prior form by संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. सू. ६-१-१०८); c → k (पा. सू. ८-२-३०); no laghūpadha-guṇa since the suffix is kit. शंस्या (śaṃsyā) — root śaṃsu stutau with ṇic; yat after a ṇic-ending root; ṇi dropped; yato 'nāvaḥ gives initial-udātta; the dual ending by ḍā. सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — somasya pītiḥ ("drinking of Soma"); the compound would take the final-udātta of the second member (kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svara) by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९), but by vyatyaya it takes the initial udātta; or, alternatively, somasya pītir yasya indrasya — "Indra, whose is the drinking of Soma" as a bahuvrīhi, in which the first member keeps its natural accent (Pā. 6-2-1).

॥१०॥

End of Sūkta 8.

॥ ಒಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 9 — "indrehi matsy andhasaḥ" ("The Ninth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

इन्द्रेहीत्यादिकं दशर्चं सूक्तं सुरूपकृत्नुमित्यादिषु षष्ठम् । ऋष्यादयस्तु पूर्ववत् । विशेषस्त्वतिरात्रे द्वितीयपर्याये ऽच्छावाकशस्त्र इन्द्रेहीत्यनुरूपस्तृचः । अतिरात्रे पर्यायाणामिति खण्डे इदं वसो सुतमन्धः इन्द्रेहि मत्स्यन्धसः । आ. ६-४ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥

indrehity-ādikaṃ daśarcaṃ sūktaṃ surūpakṛtnum ity-ādiṣu ṣaṣṭham | ṛṣy-ādayas tu pūrvavat | viśeṣas tv atirātre dvitīya-paryāye 'cchāvāka-śastra indrehity anurūpas tṛcaḥ | atirātre paryāyāṇām iti khaṇḍe idaṃ vaso sutam andhaḥ indrehi matsy andhasaḥ | ā. 6-4 | iti sūtritam ||

Translation: "The ten-rik sūkta beginning indrehi is the sixth among those beginning with surūpakṛtnum. Ṛṣi and the rest are as before. Its special application: in the Atirātra, in the second paryāya, in the Acchāvāka's śastra, the triplet beginning indrehi is the anurūpa. It is laid down in the section 'of the paryāyas in the Atirātra': 'idaṃ vaso sutam andhaḥ, indrehi matsy andhasaḥ' (Āśvalāyana 6-4)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta indrehi has ten riks; among the sūktas beginning surūpakṛtnum it is the sixth. Ṛṣi, deity and meter are as in the preceding sūktas. Special application: in the Atirātra rite, in the second paryāya, the Acchāvāka — a priest of the hotṛ group — recites the triplet indrehi. In the section on the paryāyas of the Atirātra, the riks idaṃ vaso sutam andhaḥ (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-2-1) and indrehi matsy andhasaḥ (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-9-1) are to be recited in the (first and second) paryāyas of the Atirātra rite, as Āśvalāyana says in his Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. Sū. 6-4).

॥ ॐ ॥

Sūkta 9, Rik 1

॥ Sūkta — 9 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 3 ॥ Sūkta — 9 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 17, 18 ॥ ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–10 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Madhucchandā Vaiśvāmitra ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रेहि॒ मत्स्य॑न्धसो॒ विश्वे॑भिः सोम॒पर्व॑भिः । म॒हाँ अ॑भि॒ष्टिरोज॑सा ॥१॥

indrehi mátsy andhaso víśvebhiḥ somapárvabhiḥ | mahā́ṁ abhiṣṭír ójasā ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्र । आ । इहि । मत्सि । अन्धसः । विश्वेभिः । सोमऽपर्वऽभिः ॥ महान् । अभिष्टिः । ओजसा ॥१॥

indra | ā | ihi | matsi | andhasaḥ | viśvebhiḥ | soma-parva-bhiḥ || mahān | abhiṣṭiḥ | ojasā ||1||

original p. 343

Rik 1: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र एहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । आगत्य च विश्वेभिः सर्वैः सोमपर्वभिः सोमरसरूपैरन्धसोऽन्धोभिरन्नैर्मत्सि । माद्य । हृष्टो भव । तत ऊर्ध्वमोजसा बलेन महान्भूत्वाभिष्टिः शत्रूणामभिभविता भवेति शेषः । अष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु बलनामस्वोजः पाज इति पठितम् ॥

he indra ehi | asmin karmaṇy āgaccha | āgatya ca viśvebhiḥ sarvaiḥ somaparvabhiḥ soma-rasa-rūpair andhaso 'ndhobhir annair matsi | mādya | hṛṣṭo bhava | tata ūrdhvam ojasā balena mahān bhūtvābhiṣṭiḥ śatrūṇām abhibhavitā bhaveti śeṣaḥ | aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu bala-nāmasv ojaḥ pāja iti paṭhitam ||

Translation: "O Indra, come (ehi) to this rite. Having come, rejoice (matsi — mādya, be glad) with all (viśvebhiḥ) the somaparvas, the foods (andhasaḥ = andhobhiḥ) in the form of Soma-juice. After that, becoming great (mahān) by your ojas, your strength, be the abhiṣṭi, the overcomer of enemies — this is the sentence to be completed. Among the twenty-eight words for 'strength,' ojaḥ and pājaḥ are read."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17"): "Ā ihi" — आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७); "indra ehi": ओमाङोश्च (पा. ६-१-९५) the later form, since the single substitute counts as "āṅ" (by "antādivac ca," it is treated as the beginning of the next), and the vocative is not "pragṛhya." "Matsi" — "madī harṣaglapanayoḥ," "loṭ," "sip"; by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" the "hi" of सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. ३-४-८७) does not come; दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (पा. ३-१-६९), elided by "bahulaṃ chandasi"; by न लुमताङ्गस्य (पा. १-१-६३) the long vowel of शमामष्टानां दीर्घः श्यनि (पा. ७-३-७४) does not arise; "sip," "p"-marked, so the root accent. "Andhasaḥ" — अदेर्नुम्धौ च (उ. ४-२०४) "asun"; the instrumental plural sense by vyatyaya; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Viśvebhiḥ" — अशिप्रुषि… (उ. १-१५१) "kvan," first-syllable acute; "ais" withheld by "bahulaṃ chandasi." "Somaparvabhiḥ" — "latārūpaṃ somaṃ pṛṇanti pūrayantīti somaparvāṇaḥ somarasāḥ": "pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ," "vanip" by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante," guṇa and "r"; "vanip," "p"-marked, so the root accent, kept by the upapada-compound accent. "Abhiṣṭiḥ" — "abhigantā": "iṣa gatau," मन्त्रे वृषेष… (पा. ३-३-९६) "ktin," acute; though in the action sense it denotes the agent; "k"-marked, no guṇa; "iṭ" barred by "titutratatha…" (पा. ७-२-९); "śakandhvādiṣu pararūpaṃ vaktavyam" (पा. ६-१-९४-६) the later form; in the prādi compound the kṛt-final second member's accent. "Ojasā" — उब्जेर्बले बलोपश्च (उ. ४-१९१) "asun"; first-syllable acute.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | एहि (ehi) — come (to this sacrificial ground where we perform) | विश्वेभिः (viśvebhiḥ) — all | सोमपर्वभिः (somaparvabhiḥ) — in the form of Soma-juice | अन्धसः (andhasaḥ) — with foods | मत्सि (matsi) — be satisfied | (after that) ओजसा (ojasā) — by strength | महान् (mahān) — greater | अभिष्टिः (abhiṣṭiḥ) — one who brings defeat to (enemies).

original p. 344

Rik 1 continued

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Come here, and, being satisfied with the food in the form of Soma that we have prepared — that is, by drinking Soma — become greater, strengthened by it, and defeat the enemies.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Come, O Indra, and regale yourself with Soma-libations and with all viands and mighty in strength be victorious (over your enemies).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Matsi" — the second-person singular loṭ form of the root madī harṣaglapanayoḥ ("to rejoice; to be glad"). The sense: be gratified, attain satisfaction.

"Andhasaḥ" — the word andhaḥ is read among the twenty-eight words for "food" beginning with andhaḥ, vājaḥ (Ni. "3-9" as printed [?]); so andhasaḥ means "with food."

"Somaparvabhiḥ" — लताऽरूपं सोमं पृणन्ति पूरयन्तीति सोमपर्वाणः (latā-rūpaṃ somaṃ pṛṇanti pūrayantīti somaparvāṇaḥ) — "[those that] fill the Soma that is of the form of the creeper are somaparvāṇaḥ": that is, because they fill the vessel after pressing the Soma creeper, they are called somarasa ("Soma-juices"). Skandasvāmī gives for this word the above sense and also another, "gods": सोममयानि पर्वाणि येषां ते सोमपर्वाणो देवाः । यो हि यदाहारो भवति तस्य तन्मयानि पर्वाणि भवन्ति । सोमाहाराश्च देवाः (somamayāni parvāṇi yeṣāṃ te somaparvāṇo devāḥ | yo hi yad-āhāro bhavati tasya tanmayāni parvāṇi bhavanti | somāhārāś ca devāḥ) — "those whose joints are made of Soma are the somaparvāṇas, the gods; for whatever one's food is, one's joints are made of that; and the gods have Soma for their food." The gods too take Soma-juice as their food, so they are called somaparvāṇaḥ. Therefore the sentence indra viśvebhiḥ somaparvabhiḥ ehi in this rik should be understood: "O Indra, come here together with all the gods."

"Abhiṣṭiḥ" — अभिगन्ता (abhigantā) — one who approaches [to defeat] enemies: one who brings defeat on enemies, who conquers enemies.

"Ojasā" — by strength, by capacity. Among the twenty-eight words for strength beginning with ojaḥ, pājaḥ, the word ojaḥ is read (Ni. "3-9" as printed [?]).

original p. 345

Rik 1: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17"; numbers as printed

एहि (ehi) — ā + ihi: by "ād guṇaḥ" (पा. सू. ६-१-८७) guṇa arises as a single substitute; the sūtra "antādivac ca" (पा. सू. ६-१-८५) carried over from "ekaḥ pūrvaparayoḥ" makes the substitute count as both the final of the earlier and the initial of the later item, so that both ā (as an upasarga) and the āṅ-status remain — the source cites the Bhāṣya line "yo 'py ubhayoḥ sthāne labhete 'sāv anyatarato vyapadeśam" to this effect; and "omāṅoś ca" (पा. सू. ६-१-९५) — the rule that pararūpa arises when om or āṅ is followed by a vowel — would give indra + ehi → indrehi. मत्सि (matsi) — madī harṣaglapanayoḥ, loṭ second singular sip; sip → hi by सेर्ह्यपिच्च (पा. सू. ३-४-८७) would come, but by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (परिभा. ३५) it is optional and does not come here; śyan by "divādibhyaḥ śyan" (पा. सू. ३-१-६९), dropped by Vedic bahulam (पा. सू. २-४-७३); by प्रत्ययलोपे प्रत्ययलक्षणम् (पा. सू. १-१-६२) the long vowel of शमामष्टानां दीर्घः श्यनि (पा. सू. ७-३-७४) would come, but न लुमताङ्गस्य (पा. सू. १-१-६३) blocks pratyayalakṣaṇa for an aṅga-operation after a "luk" loss, so no lengthening; "sip," "p"-marked, unaccented, the root accent stays; d → t by "khari ca" (पा. सू. ८-४-५५), giving matsi. अन्धसः (andhasaḥ) — अदेर्नुम्धौ च (उ. सू. ४-६४५ [?], as printed; the Bhāṣya gave "उ. ४-२०४"): after "ada bhakṣaṇe," "asun," the augment "num" and "dh" for "d" … continues on p. 346

अन्धसः (concluded) — "ada bhakṣaṇe" + "asun" etc.: "andhas"; nominative plural "andhasaḥ," to be taken in the sense of the instrumental plural; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. विश्वेभिः — अशूप्रुषिलटिकणिखटिविशिभ्यः क्वन् (उ. सू. १-१४९ [?], the roots glossed one by one) "kvan" after "viś": "viśva," first-syllable acute; with "bhis," बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. "७-१-१०," printed "२-१-१०") withholds "ais." सोमपर्वभिः — "latārūpaṃ somaṃ pṛṇanti pūrayanti iti somaparvāṇaḥ somarasāḥ": "pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ," अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) "vanip"; guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. सू. ७-३-८४) with "r" by उरण् रपरः (पा. सू. १-१-५१): "parvan"; "vanip," "p"-marked, unaccented, the root accent remains; with "soma," उपपदमतिङ् (पा. सू. २-२-१९) the upapada compound, and गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) keeps that accent; instrumental plural: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य (पा. सू. ८-२-७), "ru" and visarga: "somaparvabhiḥ." अभिष्टिः — "abhigantā": "iṣa gatau" with मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः (पा. सू. ३-३-९६) "ktin," acute; though in the action sense, it denotes the agent by implication; the "iṭ" of आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (पा. सू. ७-२-३५) is barred by तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च (पा. सू. ७-२-९); "abhi + iṣ + ti": the vārttika एमन्नादिषु पररूपं वक्तव्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-९४-६) gives the later form instead of the long vowel; ष्टुना ष्टुः (पा. सू. ८-४-४१) "ṭ": "abhiṣṭi"; with "abhi," कुगतिप्रादयः (पा. सू. २-२-१८) the prādi compound, with the kṛt-final second member's accent. ओजसा (p. 347) — उब्जेर्बले बलोपश्च (उ. सू. ४-६३१ [?], as printed) — after "ubja ārjave," "asun" and loss of "b"; guṇa of the light penultimate: "ojas"; instrumental "ojasā," first-syllable acute ("n"-marked). ॥१॥

Sūkta 9, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

एमे॑नं सृजता सु॒ते म॒न्दिमिन्द्रा॑य म॒न्दिने॑ । च॒क्रिं विश्वा॑नि॒ चक्र॑ये ॥२॥

ém enaṃ sṛjatā suté mandím índrāya mandíne | cakríṃ víśvāni cákraye ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । ईम् । एनम् । सृजत । सुते । मन्दिम् । इन्द्राय । मन्दिने ॥ चक्रिम् । विश्वानि । चक्रये ॥२॥

ā | īm | enam | sṛjata | sute | mandim | indrāya | mandine || cakrim | viśvāni | cakraye ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ईमित्यनर्थकः पादपूरणाय प्रयुक्तः । हे अध्वर्यवः सुते ऽभिषुते चमसस्थे सोमे एनं सोममिन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थमा सृजत । पुनरभ्युन्नयत । शुक्रामन्थिचमसगणे पुनरभ्युन्नयनमापस्तम्बेनोक्तम् । होत्रकाणां चमसाध्वर्यवः सकृत्सकृद्धुत्वा शुक्रस्याभ्युन्नीयोपावर्तध्वमिति । आप. १२-२३-४ । इति । कीदृशमेनं मन्दिं हर्षहेतुं चक्रिं साधुकरणशीलम् । कीदृशायेन्द्राय । मन्दिने हर्षयुक्ताय विश्वानि सर्वाणि कर्माणि चक्रये कृतवते । सर्वकर्मनिष्पादनशीलायेत्यर्थः । ईमित्यस्य पादपूरणार्थत्वं यास्क आह । अथ ये प्रवृत्ते ऽर्थे ऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमिमामिद्धीति । नि. १-९ । इति । अस्यायमर्थः । अन्यैरेव पदैर्विवक्षिते ऽर्थे समाप्ते सति ये शब्दा ईमित्यादयः प्रयुक्तास्ते शब्दा अमिताक्षरेषु छन्दोराहित्येन परिमिताक्षररहितेषु ब्राह्मणादिवाक्येषु वाक्यपूरणार्था द्रष्टव्याः । मिताक्षरेषु छन्दोयुक्तेषु ग्रन्थेषु पादपूरणार्थाः । के च कमिमामित्यादय इति । ईमित्यस्य शब्दस्यानर्थक्यैतामृचमुदाजहार । एमेनं सृजता सुते । आसृजतैनं सुते इति ॥

īm ity anarthakaḥ pāda-pūraṇāya prayuktaḥ | he adhvaryavaḥ sute 'bhiṣute camasasthe some enaṃ somam indrāyendrārtham ā sṛjata | punar abhyunnayata | śukrāmanthi-camasa-gaṇe punar abhyunnayanam āpastambenoktam | hotrakāṇāṃ camasādhvaryavaḥ sakṛt sakṛd dhutvā śukrasyābhyunnīyopāvartadhvam iti | āpa. 12-23-4 | iti | kīdṛśam enaṃ mandiṃ harṣa-hetuṃ cakriṃ sādhu-karaṇa-śīlam | kīdṛśāyendrāya | mandine harṣa-yuktāya viśvāni sarvāṇi karmāṇi cakraye kṛtavate | sarva-karma-niṣpādana-śīlāyety arthaḥ | īm ity asya pāda-pūraṇārthatvaṃ yāska āha | atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākya-pūraṇā āgacchanti pada-pūraṇās te mitākṣareṣv anarthakāḥ kam im ām id dhīti | ni. 1-9 | iti | asyāyam arthaḥ | anyair eva padair vivakṣite 'rthe samāpte sati ye śabdā īm ity-ādayaḥ prayuktās te śabdā amitākṣareṣu chando-rāhityena parimitākṣara-rahiteṣu brāhmaṇādi-vākyeṣu vākya-pūraṇārthā draṣṭavyāḥ | mitākṣareṣu chando-yukteṣu grantheṣu pāda-pūraṇārthāḥ | ke ca kam im ām ity-ādaya iti | īm ity asya śabdasyānarthakyaitām ṛcam udājahāra | emenaṃ sṛjatā sute | āsṛjatainaṃ sute iti ||

Translation: "Īm is a particle used merely to fill out the foot (pāda); it has no meaning. O adhvaryus! In the pressed (sute) Soma that stands in the camasa cup, ā sṛjata — pour out again, draw up again — this Soma (enam) for Indra, for his sake. For the group of the śukra-, manthi- and camasa-cups, the drawing up again is stated by Āpastamba: 'The camasa-adhvaryus of the hotrakas, having offered each time, having drawn up [Soma] onto the Śukra, should return' (Āpastamba 12-23-4). What is this Soma like? Mandim — the cause of gladness; cakrim — good at making [bringing about]. And what kind of Indra? Mandine — glad; cakraye — he who has done all (viśvāni) deeds: a doer of all works. That īm is a mere pāda-filler Yāska says: 'Now those [particles] which, where the sense is already in motion, come in works of unmeasured syllables as sentence-fillers, are pāda-fillers in works of measured syllables and meaningless — kam, īm, ām, id, hi' (Nirukta 1-9). The sense of this: when the intended meaning has been completed by other words, those words, īm and the rest, which are used, should be understood as sentence-fillers in unmetrical texts such as the Brāhmaṇas, with no fixed number of syllables, and as pāda-fillers in metrical texts; and what are they? kam, īm, ām and others. For the meaninglessness of the word īm, he quoted this rik: emenaṃ sṛjatā sute — āsṛjatainaṃ sute."

Grammar of the Bhāṣya (pp. 347–348; characterized, references as printed): "Enam" — द्वितीयाटौस्स्वेनः (पा. २-४-३४) "ena" for "idam," and with "anudāttaḥ" carried on, wholly unaccented. "Sṛjata" — अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (पा. ६-३-१३७) the long vowel in the saṃhitā. "Mandim" — "pramodahetum": "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu," "num" by "idito num dhātoḥ"; "mandamānaṃ prayuṅkte" — हेतुमति च (पा. ३-१-२६) "ṇic"; अच इः (उ. ४-१३८) "i"; "ṇer aniṭi," loss of "ṇi"; end-acute by the affix accent. "Mandine" — as before; the "num" of आङो नाऽस्त्रियाम्-type, by vyatyaya, as if neuter (पा. ७-१-७३). "Cakrim" — "ḍukṛñ karaṇe": आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च (पा. ३-२-१७१) "kin" in the "tācchīlya" senses; "k"-marked, no guṇa; "y" substitute; doubling as for "liṭ"; by द्विर्वचनेऽचि (पा. १-१-५९) the substitute counts as the original, so "kṛ" is doubled; for the reduplicate, "a," "r," the velar-to-palatal change and "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Viśvāni" — "viśeḥ kvan," first-syllable acute. "Asya … cakraye" — though joined with a kṛt word, the genitive of कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति (पा. २-३-६५) does not come, since "kin," being treated like "liṭ," falls under the prohibition न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलर्थतृनाम् (पा. २-३-६९). The top of the page ends the Bhāṣya's grammar, characterized under p. 347.
