Rik 2: word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे अध्वर्यवः) ((he adhvaryavaḥ)) — O Adhvaryu and other priests | सुते (sute) — the Soma-juice having been pressed and prepared | मन्दिने (mandine) — to the glad one | विश्वानि (viśvāni) — all deeds | चक्रये (cakraye) — to the doer | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra | मन्दिम् (mandim) — producing joy | चक्रिम् (cakrim) — the instrument for performing good deeds | एनम् (enam) — this Soma-juice | आ सृजत (ā sṛjata) — offer (give).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O ṛtvijs, Adhvaryu and the rest! The Soma-juice has now been pressed from the creeper and prepared fit for drinking. This Soma-juice produces gladness in the one who drinks it; it is the cause of performing good deeds. Offer this Soma-juice to Indra, who is glad and who accomplishes all deeds.

॥ English Translation ॥ The Kannada Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 2 follows on pp. 349–352. Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17."

The soma being extracted, present this exhilarating and efficacious draught to the rejoicing Indra, the accomplisher of all things.

original p. 349

Rik 2: Special Topics

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Īm" — the Bhāṣyakāra and Skandasvāmī both state that the word īm has no meaning and is used merely to fill out the pāda. Yāska too, in the Nirukta (1-9), speaks of this matter as follows:

अथ ये प्रवृत्ते ऽर्थे ऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमिमामिद्धीति ॥ (नि. १-९) atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākya-pūraṇā āgacchanti pada-pūraṇās te mitākṣareṣv anarthakāḥ kam im ām id dhīti || (ni. 1-9) "Now those that, when the sense has set out, come in works of unmeasured syllables as sentence-fillers, are, in works of measured syllables, meaningless pāda-fillers: kam, īm, ām, id, hi."

The Bhāṣyakāra explains this thus: "When the intended meaning has been completed by other words, those words — īm and the like — which are used are to be understood as sentence-fillers in sentences of the Brāhmaṇas and the like, which are not bound by meter and have no fixed number of syllables; in metrical works, with fixed syllables, they serve to fill out the pāda."

That is: the word īm has no meaning; it is used to fill out a pāda. In the Brāhmaṇas and other sentences not bound by meter and with no rule on the number of syllables, words like īm are used to complete sentences. In the same way, in mantras that are metrical and made of syllables of fixed number, these words are used to fill out the pāda. As an example of this, Yāska quotes this very rik, emenaṃ sṛjatā. In this rik the word īm has no use whatsoever in the sense of the mantra, but is used merely so that the pāda has the eight syllables it needs under the rule of the Gāyatrī meter. And:

क्रियावाचकमाख्यातमुपसर्गो विशेषकृत् । सत्त्वाभिधायकं नाम निपातः पादपूरणः ॥ इति ॥ kriyā-vācakam ākhyātam upasargo viśeṣa-kṛt | sattvābhidhāyakaṃ nāma nipātaḥ pāda-pūraṇaḥ || iti || "The verb denotes action; the prefix makes it specific; the noun denotes substance; the particle fills out the pāda."

"Kam im ām id dhīti" — "ete catvāraḥ kam, īm, it, u iti" — these four particles, kam, īm, it, u, are used to fill the deficient number of syllables in a pāda of a metrical rik. They have no fixed sense in such a context. And the words iva, na, cit, nu are likewise used to fill out the pāda, but on some occasions they have a meaning. Hence iva, na, cit, nu are used in two ways: as meaningless and as meaningful.

"Sṛjata" — for the convenience of the meter the ta is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha.

original pp. 350–352

Rik 2 grammar closes; Rik 3

॥ Special Topics (continued, p. 350) ॥

"Mandim" — प्रमोदहेतुम् (pramoda-hetum) — "cause of delight"; madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu. This word is another form of the root mad: one that causes delight, that produces joy.

"Mandine" — the sense is the same as that given for mandim; this is a dative singular.

"Cakrim" and "cakraye" — these words are formed from the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe ("to do"). For their derivation see the grammar section.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 350–352, Kannada; page header p. 351 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17"; numbers as printed

एनम् — "idam + am": द्वितीयाटौस्स्वेनः (पा. सू. २-४-३४) — in anvādeśa, before the accusative, "ṭā" and "os," "ena" replaces "idam" and "etad": "ena + am"; अमि पूर्वः (पा. सू. ६-१-१०७) the prior form: "enam." With 2-4-34, "anudāttaḥ" is carried from इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ (पा. सू. २-४-३२), so the substitute "ena" is unaccented, and "enam" wholly unaccented.

सृजत — अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (पा. सू. ६-३-१३७) the long vowel in the saṃhitā: "sṛjatā."

मन्दिम् — "cause of joy": "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu," "i"-marked, so इदितो नुम् धातोः (पा. सू. ७-१-५८) "num": "mand"; in the sense "mandamānaṃ prayuṅkte," हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ३-१-२६) "ṇic": by तत्प्रयोजको हेतुश्च (पा. सू. १-४-५५) the instigator of the agent is "hetu" and also "kartṛ"; when the activity of such a "hetu" — "preṣaṇa" (command), "adhyeṣaṇa" (request to an equal such as a friend), "anumati" (assent, as of a king), "upadeśa" (as to a patient) — is meant, "ṇic" comes after the root (here in the sense of urging): "mand + i"; being vowel-ending, अच इः (उ. सू. ४-१३८) "i" (p. 351): "mand + i + i"; णेरनिटि (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) loss of "ṇi": "mandi," end-acute by the affix accent; accusative "mandim."

मन्दिने — as for "mandi"; dative "ṅe": इकोऽचि विभक्तौ (पा. सू. ७-१-७३) "num" for a neuter "i/u/ṛ"-ending stem before a vowel-initial ending: "mandine"; though here it qualifies Indra and is masculine, as Vedic it takes "num" by vyatyaya.

चक्रिम् — "ḍukṛñ karaṇe": आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च (पा. सू. ३-२-१७१) — after roots in "ā" and "ṛ," "gam, han, jan," in the "tācchīlya" senses, in the Veda, "ki" and "kin," treated like "liṭ": "kṛ + i." द्विर्वचनेऽचि (पा. सू. १-१-५९): where a vowel conditioning doubling follows, no substitute is made before the doubling; "i," treated as "liṭ," conditions doubling, so by लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य (पा. सू. ६-१-८) doubling is done before इको यणचि (पा. सू. ६-१-७७): "kṛ kṛ + i," then "r" for the second "ṛ." Or, as the Vṛttikāra and others explain 1-1-59, a substitute made before a doubling-conditioning vowel retains the nature of the original: then "y" first: "kr + i," and the "r," standing for "ṛ," takes that form for doubling: "kṛkr + i." Both views give the same result; following the second, the Veda-bhāṣya says "dvirvacane 'ci iti yaṇādeśasya sthānivadbhāvāt kṛśabdo dvir ucyate." उरत् (पा. सू. ७-४-६६) "a" for the reduplicate "ṛ," with "r" by उरण् रपरः (पा. सू. १-१-५१): "kar + kr + i"; हलादिः शेषः (पा. सू. ७-४-६०) only the first consonant of the reduplicate stays: "ka + kr + i"; कुहोश्चुः (पा. सू. ७-४-६२) (p. 352) "c": "cakri"; "kin," "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. "५-४-१९७" as printed, i.e. 6-1-197).

विश्वानि — अशूप्रुषि… (उ. सू. १-१४९) "kvan" after "viś," first-syllable acute; accusative plural "viśvāni." "Viśvāni" is construed with the kṛt "cakraye," so कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति (पा. सू. २-३-६५) would give the genitive; but "kin," by "kikinau liṭ ca," is treated as "liṭ" (a "la"), so न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलर्थतृनाम् (पा. सू. २-३-६९) — with "la," "u," "uka," indeclinables, niṣṭhā, khal-sense affixes and "tṛn," no genitive — forbids it; so by कर्मणि द्वितीया (पा. सू. २-३-२) the accusative. ॥२॥

original p. 352

Sūkta 9, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मत्स्वा॑ सुशिप्र म॒न्दिभिः॒ स्तोमे॑भिर्विश्वचर्षणे । सचै॒षु सव॑ने॒ष्वा ॥३॥

mátsvā suśipra mandíbhiḥ stómebhir viśvacarṣaṇe | sacaiṣú sávaneṣv ā́ ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मत्स्व । सुऽशिप्र । मन्दिऽभिः । स्तोमेभिः । विश्वऽचर्षणे ॥ सचा । एषु । सवनेषु । आ ॥३॥

matsva | su-śipra | mandi-bhiḥ | stomebhiḥ | viśva-carṣaṇe || sacā | eṣu | savaneṣu | ā ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सुशिप्र हे शोभनहनो शोभननासिक वा । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । नि. ६-१७ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् । तादृश हे इन्द्र मन्दिभिर्हर्षहेतुभिः स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैर्मत्स्व हृष्यो भव । हे विश्वचर्षणे सर्वमनुष्ययुक्त । सर्वैर्यजमानैः पूज्येत्यर्थः । तादृशेन्द्र त्वमेषु योगागतेषु त्रिषु सवनेषु सचा देवैरन्यैः सह गच्छेति शेषः ॥ मदि स्तुतीत्यस्य लोट्यनित्यमागमशासनमिति कृत्स्वेदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् न भवति । अनुदात्तेत्त्वात्तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात् । पा. ६-१-१८६ । इति लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव । संहितायां द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः । पा. ६-३-१३५ । इति दीर्घत्वम् । सुशिप्रेत्यामन्त्रितनिघातः । मन्दिभिः । गतमन्त्रे व्याख्यातम् । स्तोमेभिः । मन्प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशो न भवति । विश्वचर्षणे । निघातः । सचा । उक्तम् । एषु । ऊडिदम्-इत्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥

he suśipra he śobhana-hano śobhana-nāsika vā | śipre hanū nāsike vā | ni. 6-17 | iti yāskenoktatvāt | tādṛśa he indra mandibhir harṣa-hetubhiḥ stomebhiḥ stotrair matsva hṛṣyo bhava | he viśvacarṣaṇe sarva-manuṣya-yukta | sarvair yajamānaiḥ pūjyety arthaḥ | tādṛśendra tvam eṣu yogāgateṣu triṣu savaneṣu sacā devair anyaiḥ saha gaccheti śeṣaḥ || madi stutīty asya loṭy anitya-āgama-śāsanam iti kṛtsv edito num dhātor iti num na bhavati | anudāttettvāt tāsy-anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāt | pā. 6-1-186 | iti lasārvadhātukānudāttatvam | dhātu-svara eva | saṃhitāyāṃ dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ | pā. 6-3-135 | iti dīrghatvam | suśipretyāmantrita-nighātaḥ | mandibhiḥ | gatamantre vyākhyātam | stomebhiḥ | man-pratyayasya nittvād ādyudāttatvam | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśo na bhavati | viśvacarṣaṇe | nighātaḥ | sacā | uktam | eṣu | ūḍidam-ityādinā vibhakter udāttatvam ||

Translation: "O suśipra — 'of beautiful jaws' or 'of beautiful nose,' for Yāska says 'śipre means the two jaws or the nose' (Nirukta 6-17). O such Indra, matsva — be glad, be pleased — with mandibhiḥ stomebhiḥ, with praises that cause gladness. O viśvacarṣaṇe — joined with all men: worshipped by all sacrificers. O such Indra, in these three pressings that have come in their turn, sacā — together with the other gods — come (this is the supplied verb). (Grammar: mad in the sense of praise, in the imperative: the augment num does not arise here, since it is optional; the verb matsva is unaccented as a finite verb; its accent remains that of the root; in the Saṃhitā the vowel is lengthened by Pā. 6-3-135 [the "dvyaco 'ta stiṅaḥ" rule]; the vocative suśipra is unaccented as a vocative within the sentence; the base accent of the stoma-word is initial by the suffix; the Vedic bahulam prevents the replacement of bhis by ais; the case-ending of eṣu *is udātta by "ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ.")" Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17." The top of the page ends the Bhāṣya's grammar, given under p. 352.

original p. 353

Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) सुशिप्र ((he) suśipra) — O Indra of beautiful jaws (or nose) | मन्दिभिः (mandibhiḥ) — which cause delight | स्तोमेभिः (stomebhiḥ) — with the praises (that we make) | मत्स्व (matsva) — be glad (be joyful) | (हे) विश्वचर्षणे ((he) viśvacarṣaṇe) — O Indra, accompanied by all men, or honoured by all sacrificers | (त्वम्) — you | एषु सवनेषु (eṣu savaneṣu) — in these three pressings (the morning, midday and third pressings) | सचा (sacā) — together (with the other gods) | आ (gaccha) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Your jaws (or nose) are most handsome. Such as you are, be satisfied with the praises we make. O you who are honoured by all men and sacrificers, come together with the other gods to the three pressings of the sacrifice — the morning, midday and third pressings (savana is the special rite of pressing the Soma-juice and preparing it) — to this sacrificial ground where we are performing the rite.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, with the handsome chin (or nose) be pleased with these pleasing praises; you who are honoured by all men come to these rites (with the gods).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Matsva" — the syllable tsva is lengthened for the convenience of the meter.

"Suśipra" — Yāska explains this word in the Nirukta: suśiprametena vyākhyātam | vāje suśipra gomat (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8-21-8) ity api nigamo bhavati | śipre hanū nāsike vā | hanur hanteḥ — "suśipra is explained by this [the preceding]: there is also a Vedic passage, 'in the contest, O suśipra, rich in cows'; śipre are the two jaws or the nose; the jaw (hanu) is from the root han…" The text breaks off at the page foot; it continues on p. 354.

original pp. 354–355

Rik 3 Special Topics and grammar close; Rik 4

॥ Special Topics (continued, p. 354) ॥

Continuing Yāska on suśipra: नासिका नसतेः । विष्यस्व शिप्रे विसृजस्व धेने (nāsikā nasateḥ | viṣyasva śipre visṛjasva dhene, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-10) ity api nigamo bhavati (Ni. 6-17) — "nāsikā is from nasate; 'loosen, O you of the śipras, let loose the dhenās' — this too is a Vedic text." So śipra means the jaw (hanu) or the nose; Yāska explains it citing two riks of the Ṛgveda. The commentator on the Nirukta too says: शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । ते यस्य प्रशस्ते स शिप्रः (śipre hanū nāsike vā | te yasya praśaste sa śipraḥ) — "śipre are the two jaws or the nose; he whose [jaws/nose] are praiseworthy is śipra"; one who has them is called śiprin. In the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-29-2 —

शिप्रिन्वाजानां पते शचीवस्तव दंसना ॥ śiprin vājānāṃ pate śacīvas tava daṃsanā || (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-29-2)

— the Bhāṣyakāra gives this same sense. Since Yāska himself has explained the word plainly, there is no room for doubt about its meaning.

Occurrences. The word suśipra occurs, besides this Ṛk, at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-10; 3-32-3; 3-50-2; 5-22-4; 5-36-5; 6-46-5; 7-24-4; 8-21-8; 8-69-16; 8-93-12; 8-99-7; other case-forms: suśipraḥ at Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-5; 3-30-3; 2-12-6; 8-66-4; 10-96-3; suśiprāḥ at Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-37-1; suśipram at Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-32-4; 8-66-2.

"Viśvacarṣaṇe" — सर्वमनुष्ययुक्त । सर्वैर्यजमानैः पूज्येत्यर्थः (sarva-manuṣya-yukta | sarvair yajamānaiḥ pūjyety arthaḥ) — "joined with all men; worshipped by all sacrificers." Since carṣaṇi means "man," viśvacarṣaṇe — joined with all men, or worshipped by all men (sacrificers and others) — is the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation. Skandasvāmī, taking carṣaṇi as a verb of seeing (paśyatikarma), explains it as "one who is looked upon by all men." The word viśvacarṣaṇe occurs at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-3; 5-38-1; 8-23-2; 9-66-1; 10-50-4; viśvacarṣaṇi at Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-93-10; viśvacarṣaṇiḥ at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-9 [?]; 2-31-3; 5-6-3; 5-23-4; 6-2-2; 9-1-2; 10-83-4; and viśvacarṣaṇim at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-14; 3-2-15; 5-14-6; 6-44-4; 8-53-6.

"Ā" — in this rik ā is only an upasarga. The Bhāṣyakāra says the verb gaccha ("come") is to be supplied with it.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 354–355, Kannada; page header p. 355 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 17"; numbers as printed

मत्स्व — "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu," "loṭ," ātmanepada second singular "thās": "mad + thās"; though the root is "i"-marked, by आगमशास्त्रमनित्यम् (अनित्यमागमशासनम्, परि. भा. ९३-२) the augment rule is anitya, so the "num" of इदितो नुम् धातोः (पा. सू. ७-१-५८) (p. 355) does not come; "śap" elided by बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. २-४-७३); थासः से (पा. सू. ३-४-८०) "se"; सवाभ्यां वामौ (पा. सू. ३-४-९१) "va" for the "e" of "loṭ" after "s": "mad + sva"; खरि च (पा. सू. ८-४-५५) "t" for "d": "matsva." The root being anudāttet, तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशात्… (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) makes "sva" unaccented; "mad" end-acute by धातोः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६२); उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः (पा. सू. ८-४-६६) makes "sva" svarita; in the saṃhitā द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५) lengthens the final short "a" of a two-syllable verb in a mantra: "matsvā."

सुशिप्र — आमन्त्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९), wholly unaccented. मन्दिभिः — explained under the previous mantra. स्तोमेभिः — अर्तिस्तुसु… (उ. सू. १-१४२) "man" after "stu," "n"-marked, first-syllable acute; with "bhis," बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. ७-१-१०) withholds "ais." विश्वचर्षणे — unaccented by the vocative rule of the eighth chapter. सचा — its derivation is set out in the third mantra of the fifth sūkta. एषु — the locative "su" after "idam" is acute by ऊडिदंपदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१). ॥३॥

असृ॑ग्रमिन्द्र ते॒ गिरः॒ प्रति॒ त्वामुद॑हासत । अजो॑षा वृष॒भं पति॑म् ॥४॥

Rik 4: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र ते गिरस्त्वदीयाः स्तुतीरसृग्रम् । सृष्टवानस्मि । ताश्च गिरः स्वर्गेऽवस्थितं त्वां प्रत्युदहासत । उद्गत्य प्राप्नुवन् । तादृशीर्गिरस्त्वमजोषाः । सेवितवानसि । कीदृशं त्वाम् । वृषभं कामानां वर्षितारं पतिं सोमस्य पातारं यजमानानां पालयितारं वा । पाता वा पालयिता वा । नि. ४-२६ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् ॥ असृग्रम् । असृजम् । सृज विसर्गे । लङो मिप् । तुदादिभ्यः शः । पा. ३-१-७७ । बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. ७-१-८ । इत्यत्र विकरणस्य रुडागमः । जकारस्य गकारः । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्त इत्यडागम उदात्तः । सति शिष्टत्वात्स एव शिष्यते । गिरः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । अहासत । ओहाङ् गतौ । लुङ् । झस्यादादेशः । पा. ७-१-५ । च्लेः सिच् । पा. ३-१-४४ । अडागमो निघातश्च । अजोषाः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । लङस्थास् । तुदादिभ्यः शः । तस्य छन्दस्युभयथा । पा. ३-४-११७ । इत्यार्धधातुकत्वेन ङित्त्वाभावाल्लघूपधगुणः । थासस्थकारलोपश्छान्दसः । सवर्णदीर्घः । अडागमः । सति शिष्टत्वादुदात्तः शिष्यते । वृषभम् । ऋषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । अभिरित्यनुवृत्तौ वृषिवृषिभ्यां कित् । उ. ३-१२३ । इत्यभच्प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । पतिम् । पा रक्षणे । पातेर्डतिः । उ. ४-५७ । डित्त्वाट्टिलोपः । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

he indra te giras tvadīyāḥ stutīr asṛgram | sṛṣṭavān asmi | tāś ca giraḥ svarge 'vasthitaṃ tvāṃ praty ud ahāsata | udgatya prāpnuvan | tādṛśīr giras tvam ajoṣāḥ | sevitavān asi | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | vṛṣabhaṃ kāmānāṃ varṣitāraṃ patiṃ somasya pātāraṃ yajamānānāṃ pālayitāraṃ vā | pātā vā pālayitā vā | ni. 4-26 | iti yāskenoktatvāt || asṛgram | asṛjam | sṛja visarge | laṅo mip | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | pā. 3-1-77 | bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 7-1-8 | ity atra vikaraṇasya ruḍ-āgamaḥ | jakārasya gakāraḥ | luṅ-laṅ-lṛṅkṣv aḍ udātta ity aḍāgama udāttaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvāt sa eva śiṣyate | giraḥ | prātipadika-svaraḥ | ahāsata | ohāṅ gatau | luṅ | jhasyād-ādeśaḥ | pā. 7-1-5 | cleḥ sic | pā. 3-1-44 | aḍāgamo nighātaś ca | ajoṣāḥ | juṣī prīti-sevanayoḥ | laṅas thās | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | tasya chandasy ubhayathā | pā. 3-4-117 | ity ārdhadhātukatvena ṅittvābhāvāl laghūpadha-guṇaḥ | thāsas thakāra-lopaś chāndasaḥ | savarṇa-dīrghaḥ | aḍāgamaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvād udāttaḥ śiṣyate | vṛṣabham | ṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | abhir ity anuvṛttau vṛṣi-vṛṣibhyāṃ kit | u. 3-123 | ity abhac-pratyayaḥ | kittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | cittvād antodāttaḥ | patim | pā rakṣaṇe | pāter ḍatiḥ | u. 4-57 | ḍittvāṭ ṭi-lopaḥ | pratyayādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "O Indra! I have sent forth — created, composed — those speeches, giraḥ, of yours — your hymns. And those words ud ahāsata — rose up, went up and reached — you prati — you who are stationed in heaven. [You, being such,] ajoṣāḥ: you have taken pleasure in (sevitavān asi, have enjoyed) such speeches (the Kannada word-meaning renders it 'be pleased'). What kind of you? Vṛṣabham — the showerer of desires; patim — the drinker of Soma, or the protector of sacrificers: 'pātā vā pālayitā vā' (Ni. 4-26), as Yāska states. Asṛgram — I have made (asṛjam), from sṛja visarge, 'to let go.'" The grammar (characterized): "asṛgram" — "laṅ," "mip," "śa" (3-1-77), the augment "ruṭ" by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (7-1-8), "g" for "j"; the augment "aṭ" acute; "ahāsata" — "ohāṅ gatau," "luṅ," "at" for "jha" (7-1-5), "sic" (3-1-44), nighāta; "ajoṣāḥ" — "juṣī," "laṅ," "thās," "śa" treated as ārdhadhātuka (3-4-117), so guṇa; loss of "th" Vedic; "vṛṣabham" — "abhac" (Uṇ. 3-123), end-acute; "patim" — "ḍati" (Uṇ. 4-57), first-syllable acute.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | ते (te) — your, or for you (concerning you) | गिरः (giraḥ) — words in the form of praise | असृग्रम् (asṛgram) — I have made (composed) | (those praises) वृषभम् (vṛṣabham) — the one who rains the desires | पतिम् (patim) — who drinks Soma, or who protects the people, the sacrificers and others | त्वां प्रति (tvāṃ prati) — to you (stationed in heaven) | उदहासत (udahāsata) — may they go up and reach (and by those praises) | अजोषाः (ajoṣāḥ) — be pleased.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! I have composed and sung praises in your honour. May those praises, joining you who dwell in heaven, who grant all desired ends and protect all, bring you joy.

original p. 357

Rik 4: English, Special Topics, grammar begins

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, I have (composed) praises in your honour; may these praises reach you (in heaven) the showerer of blessings, and the protector of your worshippers and you are pleased with their praises.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Asṛgram" — "I have created" — that is, "I have composed."

"Ut āhāsata" — ut means upward. Since Indra's place is above (in the atmosphere, antarikṣa, or in heaven), the poet offers praise, saying "may [the praises] reach you who are above" (udahāsata).

"Ajoṣāḥ" — जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (juṣī prīti-sevanayoḥ) — "may the praises serve you": that is, "be pleased by the praises."

"Patim" — सोमस्य पातारम् । यजमानानां पालयितारं वा (somasya pātāram | yajamānānāṃ pālayitāraṃ vā) — since the root pā means to drink or to protect, patim can be explained as "one who drinks Soma" or "one who protects the sacrificers." Yāska explains: पाता वा पालयिता वा (pātā vā pālayitā vā; Ni. "4-2-6" as printed, i.e. 4-26). The Vedārtha-yatna author renders patim as "husband" (printed "hnsband" [sic]; Kannada gaṇḍa); this sense does not fit here. Patim may be said to mean "lord" (svāmi).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 357–358, Kannada; page header p. 357 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 18"; numbers as printed

असृग्रम् (asṛgram) — root sṛja visarge, "laṅ" (printed so) parasmaipada first person "mip"; am in its place by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (पा. सू. ३-४-१०१); śa (the śa-vikaraṇa) of the tudādi class by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ" (पा. सू. ३-१-७७); the augment ruṭ by "bahulaṃ chandasy" (पा. सू. ७-१-८); sṛj + ra + am; j → g by "coḥ kuḥ" (पा. सू. ८-२-३०); the augment aṭ (luṅ-laṅ-lṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ, पा. सू. ६-४-७१) is udātta and attaches to the root; a + sṛg + ra + am with pūrvarūpa → asṛgram; the acute of the augment "aṭ," taught later, stays. गिरः (giraḥ) — base accent. अहासत (ahāsata) — root ohāṅ gatau ("to go") with luṅ; the third-person plural ātmanepada jha; आत्मनेपदेष्वनतः (पा. सू. ७-१-५) … continues on p. 358

original p. 358

Rik 4 grammar closes; Sūkta 9, Rik 5 text

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ Kannada; numbers as printed

Closing the grammar of Rik 4: अहासत (ahāsata) — the a of the ātmanepada ending jha is replaced by at; the cli suffix after the root by "cli luṅi" (पा. सू. ३-१-४३); in its place sic by "cleḥ sic" (पा. सू. ३-१-४४); the augment aṭ; so ahāsata; the finite verb is wholly unaccented (पा. सू. ८-१-२८). अजोषाः (ajoṣāḥ) — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ with "laṅ"; the ātmanepada middle-second singular thās; the śa-vikaraṇa of the tudādi class (पा. सू. ३-१-७७), which takes the technical status of ārdhadhātuka by "chandasy ubhayathā" (पा. सू. ३-४-११७) and so is not ṅit; hence no guṇa-prohibition by "kṅiti ca" (पा. सू. १-१-५); puganta-laghūpadhasya ca (पा. सू. ७-३-८६) gives guṇa; the th of thās dropped by Vedic license; joṣ + ās gives a savarṇa-dīrgha (पा. सू. ६-१-१०१), joṣās; the augment "aṭ" is acute, and that accent, taught later, stays; ru-and-visarga give ajoṣāḥ. वृषभम् (vṛṣabham) — ऋषिवृषिभ्यां कित् (उ. सू. ३-४०६ [?], as printed), with "abhac" carried from कॄशॄशलिकलिगर्दिभ्योऽभच् (उ. सू. ३-४०५ [?]): after the roots ṛṣi and vṛṣi the suffix abhac arises, with kit force, so no laghūpadha-guṇa; vṛṣ + abha → vṛṣabha; the suffix is cit, so final-udātta (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३). पतिम् (patim) — root pā rakṣaṇe; पातेर्डतिः (उ. सू. ४-४९८ [?], the figures unclear) — after pā in the sense of protecting, the suffix ḍati; ḍit, so the ā of pā (the ṭi) is dropped; initial-udātta by the suffix.

॥४॥

original p. 358

Sūkta 9, Rik 5

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं चो॑दय चि॒त्रम॒र्वाग्राध॑ इन्द्र॒ वरे॑ण्यम् । अस॒दित्ते॑ वि॒भु प्र॒भु ॥५॥

sáṃ codaya citrám arvā́g rā́dha indra váreṇyam | asad ít te vibhú prabhú ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । चोदय । चित्रम् । अर्वाक् । राधः । इन्द्र । वरेण्यम् ॥ असत् । इत् । ते । विऽभु । प्रऽभु ॥५॥

sam | codaya | citram | arvāk | rādhaḥ | indra | vareṇyam || asat | it | te | vi-bhu | pra-bhu ||5||

original p. 359

Rik 5: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र वरेण्यं श्रेष्ठं राधो धनं चित्रं मणिमुक्तादिरूपेण बहुविधमर्वागस्मदभिमुखं यथा भवति तथा संचोदय । सम्यक् प्रेरय । भोगाय यावत्पर्याप्तं तावद्विभुशब्देनोच्यते । ततोऽप्यधिकं प्रभुशब्देन । तादृशं धनं ते तवैवासदित् । अस्त्येव । तस्मादस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः । मघमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिधननामसु रायो राध इति पठितम् ॥ चोदय । चुद प्रेरणे । ण्यन्ताल्लोट् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । राधः । राध्नुवन्त्यनेनेति राधो धनम् । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । उ. ४-१८८ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वरेण्यम् । वृञ एण्यः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । असत् । अस भुवि । लेट् । तिप् । इतश्च लोपः । पा. ३-४-९७ । इतीकारलोपः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । आगमा अनुदात्ता इत्यटोऽनुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वर एव । विभु । विभवतीति विभु । भुव इत्यनुवृत्तौ विप्रसंभ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् । पा. ३-२-१८० । इति डुप्रत्ययः । डित्त्वाट्टिलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोकार उदात्तः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । एवं प्रभु ॥

he indra vareṇyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rādho dhanaṃ citraṃ maṇi-muktādi-rūpeṇa bahuvidham arvāg asmad-abhimukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathā saṃcodaya | samyak preraya | bhogāya yāvat paryāptaṃ tāvad vibhu-śabdenocyate | tato 'py adhikaṃ prabhu-śabdena | tādṛśaṃ dhanaṃ te tavaivāsad it | asty eva | tasmād asmabhyaṃ prayacchety arthaḥ | magham ity-ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-dhana-nāmasu rāyo rādha iti paṭhitam || codaya | cuda preraṇe | ṇyantāl loṭ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | rādhaḥ | rādhnuvanty aneneti rādho dhanam | sarva-dhātubhyo 'sun | u. 4-188 | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | vareṇyam | vṛña eṇyaḥ | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttaḥ | asat | asa bhuvi | leṭ | tip | itaś ca lopaḥ | pā. 3-4-97 | itīkāra-lopaḥ | leṭo 'ḍāṭāv ity aḍ-āgamaḥ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | āgamā anudāttā ity aṭo 'nudāttatvād dhātu-svara eva | vibhu | vibhavatīti vibhu | bhuva ity anuvṛttau vi-pra-saṃbhyo ḍv asaṃjñāyām | pā. 3-2-180 | iti ḍu-pratyayaḥ | ḍittvāṭ ṭi-lopaḥ | pratyaya-svareṇokāra udāttaḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svareṇa sa eva śiṣyate | evaṃ prabhu ||

Translation: "O Indra! Vareṇyam — choicest — rādhaḥ, wealth, citram — of many kinds, in the form of jewels, pearls and the like — send forth (saṃ codaya; urge well) so that it is arvāk — turned towards us. [Wealth] as much as is sufficient for enjoyment is called by the word vibhu; what is even more than that, by the word prabhu: such wealth is indeed yours (asad it: it exists). Therefore give it to us: this is the sense. Among the twenty-eight words for 'wealth' beginning with magham, rāyaḥ and rādhaḥ are read. Grammar: "codaya," nighāta; "rādhaḥ," "asun" (Uṇ. 4-188), first-syllable acute; "vareṇyam," "eṇya," first-syllable acute as vṛṣādi; "asat," "leṭ," loss of "i" (3-4-97), the augment "aṭ," "śap" elided; the augment being unaccented, the root accent stays; "vibhu," "ḍu" (3-2-180), the "u" acute, kept in the compound; likewise "prabhu.""

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | वरेण्यम् (vareṇyam) — choicest | चित्रम् (citram) — of many kinds | राधः (rādhaḥ) — wealth | अर्वाक् (arvāk) — (let it be) before us (by us) | सं चोदय (saṃ codaya) — impel — (that is, give) | (for) ते (te) — with you | विभु (vibhu) — [wealth] sufficient for enjoyment | (and) प्रभु (prabhu) — still greater than that | असत् इत् (asat it) — wealth indeed exists.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Make the choice and varied wealth available to us. For with you there is wealth enough for the enjoyment of everyone, and much more than that.

original p. 360

Rik 5: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

Place before us, O Indra, precious and different kinds of riches, for you have riches enough and more than enough.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Saṃ codaya" — "impel the wealth": that is, bestow it so that it comes to us; give the wealth.

"Citram" — "of various kinds": that is, wealth consisting of goods, cows, animals, houses, sons and grandsons, and so on, of many kinds.

"Arvāk" — "facing us": that is, so that it is easily obtained by us, in front of us.

"Rādhaḥ" — among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with magham, the words rāyaḥ and rādhaḥ are read (Ni. 3-9); therefore rādhaḥ means wealth.

"Vareṇyam" — choicest, excellent, of great value.

"Asat it" — it means eva: "indeed exists." There is no doubt about the existence of the wealth.

"Vibhu," "prabhu" — भोगाय यावत्पर्याप्तं तावद्विभुशब्देनोच्यते (bhogāya yāvat paryāptaṃ tāvad vibhu-śabdenocyate) — "as much as suffices for enjoyment is called by the word vibhu": that is the meaning of vibhu: "sufficient." Prabhu means "much more than sufficient for wealth." Skandasvāmī explains prabhu as prabhūtam — "abundant, very much."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ pp. 360–361, Kannada; page header p. 361 "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 18"; numbers as printed

चोदय — "cuda preraṇe": हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ३-१-२६) "ṇic"; after the "ṇic"-ended root, "loṭ," parasmaipada second singular "sip"; कर्तरि शप् (पा. सू. ३-१-६८): "cud + i + a + si"; guṇa of the light penultimate before "ṇic," and, before "śap," guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. सू. ७-३-८४): "code + a + si"; "ay" for "e"; सेर्ह्यपिच्च (printed "वा. सू. १-४-८७," i.e. 3-4-87) "hi" for "si"; अतो हेः (पा. सू. ६-४-१०५) "luk" of "hi"; wholly unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. सू. ८-१-२८).

राधः (p. 361) — "rādhnuvanty anena iti rādhaḥ dhanam": सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् (उ. सू. ४-६२८ [?], as printed; the Bhāṣya gave "उ. ४-१८८") "asun" after "rādh"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. वरेण्यम् — वृञ एण्यः (उ. सू. ३-३२८ [?], as printed) "eṇya" after "vṛñ varaṇe"; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (पा. सू. ७-३-८४): "vareṇya"; as of the vṛṣādi class, first-syllable acute by वृषादीनां च (पा. सू. ६-१-२०३). असत् — "asa bhuvi," "leṭ," "tip"; इतश्च लोपः परस्मैपदेषु (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) loss of the "i"; लेटोऽडाटौ (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) the augment "aṭ": "as + at = asat"; "śap" elided by अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (पा. सू. २-४-७२); आगमा अनुदात्ताः (printed "पा. म. ३-१-३-२") — the augment "aṭ" unaccented; "as" end-acute by धातोः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६२), which stays. विभु — "vibhavatīti vibhu": विप्रसंभ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् (पा. सू. ३-२-१८०), with "bhuvaḥ" carried from भुवः संज्ञान्तरयोः (पा. सू. ३-२-१७९): after "bhū" with "vi, pra, sam," when no name is meant, "ḍu"; the "ḍ" is "it" by चुटू (printed "पा. सू. १-०-७," i.e. 1-3-7), leaving "u"; the "ḍ"-mark causes loss of the "ṭi" "ū" of "bhū": "vibhu"; the "u" acute by आद्युदात्तश्च (पा. सू. ३-१-३), kept in the compound by गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९); likewise "prabhu." ॥५॥

original p. 361

Sūkta 9, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ In the Saṃhitā the words asmān su are joined as asmān tsu: a t is inserted between the n and the s by the Vedic sandhi rule, as the Special Topics below explain.

अ॒स्मान्त्सु तत्र॑ चोद॒येन्द्र॑ रा॒ये रभ॑स्वतः । तुवि॑द्युम्न॒ यश॑स्वतः ॥६॥

asmā́nt su tátra codayéndra rāyé rábhasvataḥ | túvidyumna yáśasvataḥ ||6||

original p. 362

Rik 6: Pada text, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अस्मान् । सु । तत्र । चोदय । इन्द्र । राये । रभस्वतः ॥ तुविऽद्युम्न । यशस्वतः ॥६॥

asmān | su | tatra | codaya | indra | rāye | rabhasvataḥ || tuvi-dyumna | yaśasvataḥ ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे तुविद्युम्न प्रभूतधनेन्द्र राये धनसिद्ध्यर्थमस्माननुष्ठातॄन् तत्र कर्मणि सु चोदय । सुष्ठु प्रेरय । कीदृशानस्मान् । रभस्वत उद्योगवतो यशस्वतः कीर्तिमतः ॥ तत्र । तच्छब्दात्सप्तम्यास्त्रल् । पा. ५-३-१० । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । इन्द्र । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । राये । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । रभस्वतः । रभ राभस्ये । राभस्यं कार्योपक्रमः । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । स्वादिष्वसर्वनामस्थाने । पा. १-४-१७ । इति न पदत्वं तसौ मत्वर्थे । पा. १-४-१९ । इति भसंज्ञया बाधितत्वात् । आ कडारादेका संज्ञा । पा. १-४-१ । इति नियमात् तुविद्युम्न । तुवि बहु द्युम्नं धनं यस्य । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । यशस्वतः । यशो ऽस्यास्तीति मतुप् । अस्मायामेधास्रजो विनिः । पा. ५-२-१२१ । इति विनिना न बाध्यते मतुपः सर्वत्र समुच्चयात् । यशश्शब्दो नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः । मतुपः पित्त्वात्तस्य शिष्यते ॥

he tuvidyumna prabhūtadhanendra rāye dhanasiddhyarthamasmānanuṣṭhātṝn tatra karmaṇi su codaya | suṣṭhu preraya | kīdṛśānasmān | rabhasvata udyogavato yaśasvataḥ kīrtimataḥ || tatra | tacchabdātsaptamyāstral | pā. 5-3-10 | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | indra | āmantritādyudāttatvam | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | rāye | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | rabhasvataḥ | rabha rābhasye | rābhasyaṃ kāryopakramaḥ | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | matupaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | svādiṣvasarvanāmasthāne | pā. 1-4-17 | iti na padatvaṃ tasau matvarthe | pā. 1-4-19 | iti bhasaṃjñayā bādhitatvāt | ā kaḍārādekā saṃjñā | pā. 1-4-1 | iti niyamāt tuvidyumna | tuvi bahu dyumnaṃ dhanaṃ yasya | ṣāṣṭhikamāmantritādyudāttatvam | yaśasvataḥ | yaśo 'syāstīti matup | asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ | pā. 5-2-121 | iti vininā na bādhyate matupaḥ sarvatra samuccayāt | yaśaśśabdo nabviṣayasyānisantasyetyādyudāttaḥ | matupaḥ pittvāttasya śiṣyate ||

Translation: "O tuvidyumna — Indra of abundant wealth! For rāye, the achievement of wealth, su codaya — urge well — us, who perform the rites, in that rite. What kind of us? Rabhasvataḥ — enterprising, industrious; yaśasvataḥ — renowned. Grammar: tatra — formed with tral after the word tad in the seventh case (Pā. 5-3-10), the syllable before the suffix being udātta since tral is l-marked; indra — the vocative, initially udātta, but as the first word of a pāda not lowered; rāye — the case-ending udātta by "ūḍidam…"; rabhasvataḥ — root rabha rābhasye, 'the beginning of an act'; the suffix asun, initial-udātta since nit; matup is pit and so unaccented; by Pā. 1-4-17 and 1-4-19 the word is not a pada before matup, but has the technical bha status, which blocks the pada status; tuvidyumna — 'he whose wealth (dyumna) is much (tuvi)', a bahuvrīhi, the vocative initially udātta; yaśasvataḥ — 'who has fame' with matup, not barred by vini (Pā. 5-2-121) since the two are combined everywhere; the word yaśas initial-udātta as a neuter not ending in -isan."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

तुविद्युम्न (tuvidyumna) — O Indra, who are endowed with abundant wealth | (हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | रभस्वतः (rabhasvataḥ) — who are enterprising (engaged in sacrificial and other works) | यशस्वतः (yaśasvataḥ) — who are possessed of fame | अस्मान् (asmān) — us | राये (rāye) — for obtaining wealth | तत्र (tatra) — in that rite | सु चोदय (su codaya) — urge well.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are endowed with abundant wealth — that is, you possess great riches. Therefore urge us, who are always engaged in sacrificial and other works and are renowned, to engage ardently in sacrificial and other rites for obtaining wealth.

original p. 363

Rik 6: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, you are very rich ; encourage us in this rite for the acquirement of wealth, for we are deligent [sic] and renowned.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Asmān + su = asmān tsu" — when s follows the n of a word-ending (here, an accusative-plural n), in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha the two are combined by sandhi and, in pronouncing, a t is inserted between the n and the s, giving nts; this is customary. In this connection:

स गा अविन्दत्सो अविन्ददश्वान्त्स ओषधीः सो अपः सवनानि ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१०३-५) sa gā avindat so avindad aśvānt sa oṣadhīḥ so apaḥ savanāni || (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-103-5) ("He found the cows, he found the horses, he the herbs, he the waters, the pressings." — mine and tentative; the source gives only the citation.)

कविर्गीर्भिः काव्येना कविः सन्त्सोमः पवित्रमत्येति रेभन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-९६-१७) kavir gīrbhiḥ kāvyenā kaviḥ san tsomaḥ pavitram aty eti rebhan || (Ṛg. Saṃ. 9-96-17) ("The seer [Soma], a seer with his songs and poetic power, being [pressed], passes through the filter, murmuring." — mine and tentative.)

Many more examples could be given.

"Rabhasvataḥ" — रभ राभस्ये । राभस्यं कार्योपक्रमः (rabha rābhasye | rābhasyaṃ kāryopakramaḥ) — "[root] rabha in the sense of rābhasya — the beginning of a work." Rābhasya is derived from the root rabh; it means starting an undertaking; being industrious, enterprising. Rabhasvataḥ is the accusative plural of rabhasvān.

"Tuvidyumna" — "of abundant wealth": tuvi is much; dyumna is wealth. So, "he who has much wealth" — a bahuvrīhi. "Of much wealth."

"Yaśasvataḥ" — yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān, "those who have fame"; renowned. Rabhasvataḥ and yaśasvataḥ both qualify the word asmān ("us").

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 363–365, noted briefly

तत्र (tatra) — "in that"; the tral suffix after the seventh-case pronouns tad, kim, sarva etc. (Pā. 5-3-10, "saptamyās tral"); tral is taddhita, so the word is a prātipadika; the sup ending is dropped by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ (Pā. 2-4-71); d → a by tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. 6-2-102 [as printed]); a + a → pararūpa by ato guṇe (Pā. 6-1-97); tral is l-marked, so by liti (Pā. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix is udātta. इन्द्र (indra) — the second pāda's first syllable; since this is the beginning of the pāda, there is no lowering by apādādau; as a vocative it is initial-udātta by āmantritasya ca (Pā. 6-1-198). राये (rāye) — rai + the dative ending e; after the ai-ending word rai, the dative ending is udātta (ūḍidam-pada-ādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ, Pā. 6-1-171). रभस्वतः (rabhasvataḥ) — root rabha rābhasye; asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]) gives rabhas, initial-udātta as nit; matup after it by tad asyāsty asminn iti matup (Pā. 5-2-94), its m → v by mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ (Pā. 8-2-9); the question of whether rabhas is a pada before matup (which would block ruṭ etc.) (by svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne, Pā. 1-4-17) or has bha status (by tasau matvarthe, Pā. 1-4-19) is argued: pada status and bha status are both prescribed, and the source concludes by the maxim "ā kaḍārād ekā saṃjñā" (Pā. 1-4-1) that among the technical names prescribed from there up to kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye (Pā. 2-2-38) only one applies, the later (para) one, bha; so pada-status is inapplicable and the rules (such as ruṭv-rules) that depend on it do not operate. तुविद्युम्न (tuvidyumna) — tuvi (much) + dyumna (wealth) as a bahuvrīhi; a vocative, initial-udātta by the vocative rule of the sixth adhyāya (no number printed). यशस्वतः (yaśasvataḥ) — "yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān": matup, with the m → v as in rabhasvataḥ; the long discussion (pp. 364–365) concerns whether the vini suffix of the sūtra "asmāyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) blocks matup here — answered that, by the carried-over word "anyatarasyām" ("optionally"), vini is only optional — the "nityam" of ekago-pūrvāṭ ṭhañ nityam (Pā. 5-2-118) breaks the carrying-over, but it resumes in tasau matvarthe (Pā. 1-4-19), where the Mahābhāṣya gives the examples yaśasvī / yaśasvān; and by the Vedabhāṣya's general statement that matup has the sense of inclusion everywhere (samuccaya), and by Kaiyaṭa on the Mahābhāṣya on "keśād vo 'nyatarasyām" (Pā. 5-2-109; printed 5-3-109 on p. 365 [as printed]); yaśas is initial-udātta as a neuter noun not ending in -isan (Phiṭ-sūtra 26); matup is pit, hence unaccented; so the initial accent of yaśas stands. Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.

॥६॥

original p. 365

Sūkta 9, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं गोम॑दिन्द्र॒ वाज॑वद॒स्मे पृ॒थु श्रवो॑ बृ॒हत् । वि॒श्वायु॑र्धेह्य॑क्षितम् ॥७॥

saṃ gómad indra vā́javad asmé pṛthú śrávo bṛhát | viśvā́yur dhéhy akṣitam ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । गोऽमत् । इन्द्र । वाजऽवत् । अस्मे इति । पृथु । श्रवः । बृहत् ॥ विश्वऽआयुः । धेहि । अक्षितम् ॥७॥

sam | go-mat | indra | vāja-vat | asme iti | pṛthu | śravaḥ | bṛhat || viśva-āyuḥ | dhehi | akṣitam ||7||

original p. 366

Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र श्रवो धनमस्मे सं धेहि । अस्मभ्यं सम्यक् प्रयच्छ । कीदृशं श्रवः । गोमत् बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेतं वाजवत् प्रभूतेनान्नेनोपेतं पृथु परिमाणेनाधिकं बृहत् गुणैरधिकं विश्वायुः कृत्स्नायुष्यकारणं अक्षितं विनाशरहितम् । गोमत् । वाजवत् । उभयत्र मतुपो ऽनुदात्तत्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्वर एव । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । अस्मे । अस्मच्छब्दाच्चतुर्थीबहुवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना शे आदेशः । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । शेषे लोपः । टिलोप इति पक्षे । पा. ७-२-९० । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अन्त्यलोपपक्षे ऽतो गुण इति पररूपे एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तत्वम् । पृथु । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथिम्रदिभ्रस्जां संप्रसारणं सलोपश्च । उ. १-२९ । इति कुप्रत्ययः । रेफस्य संप्रसारणमृकारः । परपूर्वत्वम् । कोः कित्त्वान्न लघूपधगुणः । श्रूयत इति श्रवो धनम् । असुन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । बृहत् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । विश्वायुः । विश्वमायुर्यस्मिन्धने । विश्वशब्दः क्वन्प्रत्ययान्तः । तस्य बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्याद्युदात्तः । अक्षितम् । क्षि क्षये इत्यस्मादन्तर्णीतण्यर्थात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । तेन स्यदर्थत्वान्निष्ठायामण्यदर्थे [? as printed] । पा. ६-४-६० । इति न दीर्घत्वम् । अत एव क्षियो दीर्घात् । पा. ८-२-४६ । इति न निष्ठानत्वम् । नञ्समासे ऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

he indra śravo dhanamasme saṃ dhehi | asmabhyaṃ samyak prayaccha | kīdṛśaṃ śravaḥ | gomat bahvībhirgobhirupetaṃ vājavat prabhūtenānnenopetaṃ pṛthu parimāṇenādhikaṃ bṛhat guṇairadhikaṃ viśvāyuḥ kṛtsnāyuṣyakāraṇaṃ akṣitaṃ vināśarahitam | gomat | vājavat | ubhayatra matupo 'nudāttatvātprātipadikasvara eva | vājaśabdo vṛṣādirādyudāttaḥ | asme | asmacchabdāccaturthībahuvacanasya supāṃ sulugityādinā śe ādeśaḥ | śittvātsarvādeśaḥ | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttatvam | śeṣe lopaḥ | ṭilopa iti pakṣe | pā. 7-2-90 | udāttanivṛttisvareṇa vibhakterudāttatvam | antyalopapakṣe 'to guṇa iti pararūpe ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttatvam | pṛthu | pratha prakhyāne | prathimradibhrasjāṃ saṃprasāraṇaṃ salopaśca | u. 1-29 | iti kupratyayaḥ | rephasya saṃprasāraṇamṛkāraḥ | parapūrvatvam | koḥ kittvānna laghūpadhaguṇaḥ | śrūyata iti śravo dhanam | asunpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | bṛhat | prātipadikasvaraḥ | viśvāyuḥ | viśvamāyuryasmindhane | viśvaśabdaḥ kvanpratyayāntaḥ | tasya bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamiti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityādyudāttaḥ | akṣitam | kṣi kṣaye ityasmādantarṇītaṇyarthātkarmaṇi niṣṭhā | tena syadarthatvānniṣṭhāyāmaṇyadarthe [? as printed] | pā. 6-4-60 | iti na dīrghatvam | ata eva kṣiyo dīrghāt | pā. 8-2-46 | iti na niṣṭhānatvam | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "O Indra! Śravaḥ — wealth — asme — to us — saṃ dhehi: bestow well. What kind of śravaḥ? Gomat — furnished with many cows; vājavat — furnished with abundant food; pṛthu — larger in measure; bṛhat — superior in qualities; viśvāyuḥ — the cause of a whole lifetime; akṣitam — free of destruction." The accompanying grammar, noted briefly: gomat and vājavat take their stem accent because matup is unaccented; vāja is a vṛṣādi word, initial-udātta; asme is formed by the substitute śe for the plural dative ending after asmad, replacing the whole as it is śit, final-udātta by the stem accent; by śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. 7-2-90) — on the view that the ṭi is dropped, the case-ending is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta; on the view that the final is dropped, the pararūpa by ato guṇe is a single substitute udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ; pṛthu — root prtha prakhyāne with the suffix ku and saṃprasāraṇa of r to ṛ (Uṇ. 1-29); śravaḥ — 'that which is heard' = wealth, with asun, initial-udātta; viśvāyuḥ — a bahuvrīhi 'in which wealth the whole life [is]'; the first-member accent of a bahuvrīhi being displaced by parādiś chandasi bahulam to the end of the first member, and the single substitute udātta, so initial-udātta; akṣitam — from kṣi kṣaye with the causative sense inside, the past-participle suffix in the passive; no lengthening by Pā. 6-4-60 and hence no n-substitution by kṣiyo dīrghāt (Pā. 8-2-46); the nañ compound has the accent of its indeclinable first member. One word, printed syadarthatvāt, is kept as printed [?]."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | अस्मे (asme) — to us | पृथु (pṛthu) — abundant | बृहत् (bṛhat) — superior in qualities | गोमत् (gomat) — endowed with cows (in the form of cattle) | वाजवत् (vājavat) — endowed with food (in the form of food, nourishment) | विश्वायुः (viśvāyuḥ) — the cause of long life | अक्षितम् (akṣitam) — without destruction | श्रवः (śravaḥ) — wealth | धेहि (dhehi) — give.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Give us abundant wealth: the best, in the form of cattle, horses and other animals and wealth, and in the form of grain and nourishing food — wealth that is the means of living a long life and that is imperishable. Give us such wealth in great abundance.

original p. 367

Rik 7: English, Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

Grant us, Indra, wealth beyond measure or calculation, inexhaustible the source of cattle, of food, of all life.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Gomat" — बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेतम् (bahvībhir gobhir upetam) — "furnished with many cows." Or: gāvo yasmin santi tat gomat — "that in which there are cows"; gomat — wealth in the form of animals, with plenty of cows.

"Vājavataḥ" — wealth consisting of food (anna) and the like, of foodstuffs.

"Asme" — means asmabhyam (to us). In the Ṛgveda asme is used in many places in place of asmabhyam.

"Śravaḥ" — among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with magham, the word śravaḥ is read (Nirukta 3-9). "Bṛhat" — excellent, full of substance, excellent in qualities.

"Viśvāyuḥ" — कृत्स्नायुष्यकारणम् (kṛtsnāyuṣya-kāraṇam) — "the cause of a whole lifetime"; the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as wealth that serves for living for a long time. To explain it so, it is better to take viśvāyuḥ as a qualifier of śravaḥ (wealth) than as a qualifier in the sense "one who has a long life": the use of viśvāyuḥ as a viśeṣya word meaning "one who lives long" is more fitting. Skandasvāmī's meaning is likewise.

"Akṣitam" — free from destruction, inexhaustible.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 367–368, noted briefly

गोमत्, वाजवत् (gomat, vājavat) — "gaur asyāsti iti gomat; vājo 'sya asti iti vājavat": in both, matup is pit, hence unaccented, so the stem accent stands; vāja is a vṛṣādi word, so initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203). अस्मे (asme) — asmad + the dative-plural bhyas; this is replaced by śe by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39); the ś of śe is it by "lasakvataddhite" (Pā. 1-3-8), the substitute being śit replaces the whole of bhyas by "anekāl śit sarvasya" (Pā. 1-1-55); asmad is final-udātta by its stem accent; [on the view that the ṭi is dropped,] the e is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta, "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); [on the other view] the final d of asmad is dropped by "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90); asma + e → pararūpa by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), a single substitute that takes the udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). पृथु (pṛthu) — root pṛtha prakhyāne ("to spread"), and the rule "prathimradibhrasjāṃ saṃprasāraṇaṃ salopaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-28 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 366 prints 1-29): the suffix ku after prath, mrad, bhrasj, with saṃprasāraṇa of r to ṛ and loss of s in bhrasj; pṛ + th + u → pṛthu by the pūrvarūpa of "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); ku is kit, so no guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86). श्रवः (śravaḥ) — "śrūyate iti": root śru + asun ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," no number printed); guṇa of u → o by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); ov → av by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78); the nominative/accusative singular ending am/su dropped by "svamor napuṃsakāt" (Pā. 7-1-23); ru-and-visarga; initial-udātta. बृहत् (bṛhat) — stem accent. विश्वायुः (viśvāyuḥ) — a bahuvrīhi "viśvam āyur yasmin dhane"; viśva is formed with kvan (by "aśūpruṣi…", Uṇ. 1-149, from aśū vyāptau) and is nit, so initial-udātta; the bahuvrīhi rule "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) would keep the first-member accent, but with the Vedic "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199) the end of the first member takes the udātta; viśva + āyuḥ → single substitute ā, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). अक्षितम् (akṣitam) — root kṣi kṣaye in the sense including the causative; kta in the passive; by "niṣṭhā-yoṇya-darthe" (Pā. 6-4-60) the lengthening is prohibited since the word does not have the sense "not to be…"; and since the lengthening does not arise, the n-substitution of "kṣiyo dīrghāt" (Pā. 8-2-46) does not arise; the nañ compound with the negative takes the first-member accent of "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) as with indeclinables.

॥७॥

original p. 369

Sūkta 9, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒स्मे धे॑हि॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हद्द्यु॒म्नं स॑हस्र॒सात॑मम् । इन्द्र॒ ता र॒थिनी॒रिषः॑ ॥८॥

asmé dhehi śrávo bṛhád dyumnáṃ sahasrasā́tamam | indra tā́ rathínīr íṣaḥ ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अस्मे इति । धेहि । श्रवः । बृहत् । द्युम्नम् । सहस्रऽसातमम् ॥ इन्द्र । ताः । रथिनीः । इषः ॥८॥

asme iti | dhehi | śravaḥ | bṛhat | dyumnam | sahasra-sātamam || indra | tāḥ | rathinīḥ | iṣaḥ ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र बृहच्छ्रवो महतीं कीर्तिमस्मे धेहि । अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छ । तथा सहस्रसातममतिशयेन सहस्रसंख्यादानोपेतं द्युम्नं धनमस्मे धेहि । तथा ता व्रीहियवादिरूपेण प्रसिद्धा रथिनीर्बहुरथोपेता इषो ऽन्नान्यस्मे धेहि ॥ अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना शे आदेशः । धेहि । घ्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-११९ । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । श्रूयत इति श्रवः । असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सहस्रं सुनुते ददातीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । पा. ३-२-६७ । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् । पा. ६-४-४१ । इत्याकारादेशः । धातुस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । पुनः कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । रथा आसां सन्तीति रथिन्य इति प्रत्ययस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् । पा. ४-१-५ । स च पित्त्वादनुदात्तः । इषो योगिकत्वे धातुस्वरः । रूढत्वे प्रातिपदिकस्वरः ॥

he indra bṛhacchravo mahatīṃ kīrtimasme dhehi | asmabhyaṃ prayaccha | tathā sahasrasātamamatiśayena sahasrasaṃkhyādānopetaṃ dyumnaṃ dhanamasme dhehi | tathā tā vrīhiyavādirūpeṇa prasiddhā rathinīrbahurathopetā iṣo 'nnānyasme dhehi || asme | supāṃ sulugityādinā śe ādeśaḥ | dhehi | ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca | pā. 6-4-119 | ityetvābhyāsalopau | śrūyata iti śravaḥ | asuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | sahasraṃ sunute dadātīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | pā. 3-2-67 | viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt | pā. 6-4-41 | ityākārādeśaḥ | dhātusvareṇāntodāttaḥ | punaḥ kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva śiṣyate | rathā āsāṃ santīti rathinya iti pratyayasyādyudāttatvam | ṛnnebhyo ṅīp | pā. 4-1-5 | sa ca pittvādanudāttaḥ | iṣo yogikatve dhātusvaraḥ | rūḍhatve prātipadikasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra, bṛhac-chravaḥ — O you of great renown: give us (asme dhehi) great fame. And likewise bestow on us sahasra-sātamam — in extreme degree accompanied by gifts reckoned in thousands — dyumnam, wealth. And likewise tāḥ — those famous in the forms of rice, barley and the like — rathinīḥ, furnished with many chariots — iṣaḥ: foods; bestow them on us." Grammar noted briefly: asme as in Rik 7; dhehi — the root dhā with hi, with the substitution of e for ā and loss of the reduplicate (Pā. 6-4-119); śravaḥ with asun; sahasrasā — 'one who gives a thousand': root ṣaṇu dāne with viṭ (Pā. 3-2-67), ā for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41), final-udātta by the root, then the second-member rule; rathinyaḥ — 'those who have chariots,' feminine in ṅīp (Pā. 4-1-5), unaccented because pit; iṣaḥ takes the root accent if taken in its component sense and the stem accent if taken as a settled word.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | अस्मे (asme) — to us | बृहत् (bṛhat) — great, excellent | श्रवः (śravaḥ) — fame | सहस्रसातमम् (sahasrasātamam) — greatly helpful for giving thousands of different things | द्युम्नम् (dyumnam) — wealth | रथिनीः (rathinīḥ) — brought in chariots or carts | ताः (tāḥ) — those in the form of grains such as rice and barley | इषः (iṣaḥ) — foods | धेहि (dhehi) — give.

original p. 370

Rik 8: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Give us exceedingly great fame and thousand-fold wealth, and grain and other food in cartloads (chariot-loads).

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, grant us great fame, and wealth acquired in a thousand ways and those (articles) of food (which are brought from the field) in carts.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is easy to grasp; there are no special difficulties.

"Śravaḥ" — for this word Yāska, in his Nirukta, gives two or three different senses. Since the word śravaḥ is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with magham and reknaḥ (Nirukta 3-9), the sense "wealth" is also possible. In explaining the rik uta svainaṃ (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4-38-5) he says: "śravaś cāpi paśum ucche yūthaṃ praśaṃsāṃ ca yūthaṃ dhanaṃ ca yūthaṃ ceti vā" (as printed) — that is, śravaḥ is "praise (fame)" or "wealth" (Nirukta 4-24); and in the rik amandān stomān (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-126-1; the first digit of the middle number is damaged in the print) he explains the word śrava icchamānāḥ as "wishing for praise" (Nirukta 9-11). In the explanation of the rik pra vo mahe mandamānāya (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-50-1) he explains śravaḥ as mahac chravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ — "great, worthy-of-hearing glory" (Nirukta 11-10). Since in this rik, besides this, the word dyumnam ("wealth") also occurs — a word for wealth — to render śravaḥ as "wealth" would produce the fault of repetition; so to give it the sense of "fame" is quite fitting.

"Sahasrasātamam" — सहस्रं सनुते ददातीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने (sahasraṃ sanute dadātīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne) — "one who gives a thousand; the root ṣaṇu in the sense of giving." Therefore sahasrasātamam means "that which gives thousands, that is, that gives in the greatest abundance."

"Tāḥ" — a feminine accusative plural of tad, and an adjective of the word iṣaḥ. The necessity of this word is not evident in this rik; probably it is used for filling out the pāda.

"Rathinīḥ" — रथा आसां सन्तीति रथिन्यः (rathā āsāṃ santīti rathinyaḥ) — "those that have chariots": [loads] related to chariots — that is, filling the chariots or carts, in great abundance. The grain that a single man carries on his head is not very much; but in a cart, how much more — as many people can carry. Hence the grain that fills a cart is a very great amount of grain.

original p. 371

Rik 8: grammar

"Iṣaḥ" — although the word has the sense "food," here it is used in a general sense, "food or grain." The adjective rathinīḥ supports this sense.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar page, noted briefly

अस्मे (asme) — the plural dative ending after asmad is replaced by śe by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). धेहि (dhehi) — root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ ("to hold, to nourish"); loṭ parasmaipada second singular sip; sip → hi by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-80 [as printed]); the vikaraṇa śap (no number printed), dropped by ślu after the juhotyādi class, "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. 2-4-75); doubling by ślau (Pā. 6-1-10); dhā + hi: by "ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaś ca" (Pā. 6-4-119) the roots called ghu and as, before hi, take e in place of the final ā, and the reduplicate vowel is dropped; so dhehi; wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). श्रवः (śravaḥ) — formed with asun; initial-udātta by the suffix. सहस्रसातमम् (sahasrasātamam) — sahasraṃ sanute dadāti iti sahasrasāḥ; root ṣaṇu dāne; ṣ → s by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; viṭ after jana, sana, khana, krama, gam in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67); the ā substituted for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41); the whole viṭ dropped; sahasra + sā; final-udātta by the root accent, and after compounding the second member's accent stands by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); then tamap in the sense of excess by "atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau" (Pā. 5-3-55), pit and so unaccented. रथिनीः (rathinīḥ) — rathāḥ āsāṃ santi; ini by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); a of ratha dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); ini is initial-udātta by the suffix accent; the stem rathin ends in n; the feminine ṅīp after ṛ- and n-ending stems (Pā. 4-1-5, "ṛnnebhyo ṅīp"); ṅīp is pit, so unaccented. इषः (iṣaḥ) — if taken in its component sense, the root accent stands (i udātta); if taken as a settled word, the stem accent applies.

॥८॥

Sūkta 9, Rik 9

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

वसो॒रिन्द्रं॒ वसु॑पतिं गी॒र्भिर्गृ॒णन्त॑ ऋ॒ग्मियं॑ । होम॒ गन्ता॑रमू॒तये॑ ॥९॥

vasor índraṃ vásupatiṃ gīrbhír gṛṇánta ṛgmíyaṃ | homa gántāram ūtáye ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

वसोः । इन्द्रम् । वसुऽपतिम् । गीःऽभिः । गृणन्तः । ऋग्मियम् ॥ होम । गन्तारम् । ऊतये ॥९॥

vasoḥ | indram | vasu-patim | gīḥ-bhiḥ | gṛṇantaḥ | ṛgmiyam || homa | gantāram | ūtaye ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वसोर्वसुनो ऽस्मदीयस्य धनस्योतये रक्षार्थमिन्द्रं होम । वयमाह्वयामः । किं कुर्वन्तः । गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्गृणन्तः स्तुवन्तः । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । वसुपतिं धनपालकं ऋग्मियं ऋचां मातारं गन्तारं यागदेशे गमनशीलम् ॥ वसोः । वस निवासे । शृस्वृस्निहीत्यादिना । उ १-११ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वसुपतिम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते पत्यावैश्वर्ये । पा. ६-२-१८ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । गीर्भिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । गृणन्तः । गॄ शब्दे । लटः शतृ । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । पा. ३-१-८१ । शतुः सार्वधातुकमपिदिति ङित्त्वात् श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः । पा. ६-४-११२ । इत्याकारलोपः । शतुरकारस्य प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । ऋग्मियम् । ऋचो मिमित [sic: मिमीते] इत्यृग्मीः । तमृग्मियं । माङ् माने शब्दे च । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । घुमास्थेत्यादिना । पा. ६-४-६६ । ईत्त्वं । चकारस्य चोः कुः । झलां जशो ऽन्ते । पा. ८-२-३९ । इति जश्त्वं । गकारः । द्वितीयैकवचने ऽचि श्नुधात्वित्यादिना । पा. ६-४-७७ । इयङादेशः । एरनेकाच इति यणादेशः । पा. ६-४-८२ । सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न भवति । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । होम । आह्वयामः । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । लट् । तस्यास्मदो बहुत्वे ऽपि व्यत्ययेन मिप् । इकारस्य व्यत्ययेनाकारः । शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. ६-१-३४ । इति ह्वः संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वं गुणः । धातोः । पा. ६-१-१६२ । इत्योकार उदात्तः । मिपः पित्स्वरेणानुदात्तत्वम् । गन्तारम् । गम्लृ सृप्लृ गतौ । ताच्छील्ये तृन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ऊतये । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तो निपातितः ॥

vasorvasuno 'smadīyasya dhanasyotaye rakṣārthamindraṃ homa | vayamāhvayāmaḥ | kiṃ kurvantaḥ | gīrbhiḥ stutibhirgṛṇantaḥ stuvantaḥ | kīdṛśamindram | vasupatiṃ dhanapālakaṃ ṛgmiyaṃ ṛcāṃ mātāraṃ gantāraṃ yāgadeśe gamanaśīlam || vasoḥ | vasa nivāse | śṛsvṛsnihītyādinā | u 1-11 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | vasupatim | samāsāntodāttatve prāpte patyāvaiśvarye | pā. 6-2-18 | iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | gīrbhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | gṛṇantaḥ | gṝ śabde | laṭaḥ śatṛ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | pā. 3-1-81 | śatuḥ sārvadhātukamapiditi ṅittvāt śnābhyastayorātaḥ | pā. 6-4-112 | ityākāralopaḥ | śaturakārasya pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | ṛgmiyam | ṛco mimita [sic: mimīte] ityṛgmīḥ | tamṛgmiyaṃ | māṅ māne śabde ca | kvipceti kvip | ghumāsthetyādinā | pā. 6-4-66 | īttvaṃ | cakārasya coḥ kuḥ | jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte | pā. 8-2-39 | iti jaśtvaṃ | gakāraḥ | dvitīyaikavacane 'ci śnudhātvityādinā | pā. 6-4-77 | iyaṅādeśaḥ | eranekāca iti yaṇādeśaḥ | pā. 6-4-82 | sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti na bhavati | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | homa | āhvayāmaḥ | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | laṭ | tasyāsmado bahutve 'pi vyatyayena mip | ikārasya vyatyayenākāraḥ | śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 6-1-34 | iti hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvaṃ guṇaḥ | dhātoḥ | pā. 6-1-162 | ityokāra udāttaḥ | mipaḥ pitsvareṇānudāttatvam | gantāram | gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau | tācchīlye tṛn | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | ūtaye | ūtiyūtītyādinā ktinnudātto nipātitaḥ ||

Translation: "For the ūtaye — the protection — of our vasu, our wealth, we call (homa) Indra. What are we doing? Gīrbhiḥ gṛṇantaḥ — praising with hymns. What kind of Indra? Vasupatim — the guardian of wealth; ṛgmiyam — the measurer (mātṛ) of the ṛks; gantāram — the one who is in the habit of going to the place of sacrifice." Grammar, noted briefly: vasoḥ — root vasa nivāse with the suffix u (Uṇ. 1-11); vasupatim — the first-member accent by Pā. 6-2-18 when pati means 'lord'; gṛṇantaḥ — root gṝ śabde, śatṛ with śnā, the ā of śnā dropped before the śatṛ since it is treated as ṅit; ṛgmiyam — 'one who measures the ṛks' (ṛco mimīte): root māṅ māne śabde ca with kvip, the ī by Pā. 6-4-66, the voicing of the final consonant (Pā. 8-2-39); before the accusative ending the iyaṅ substitute (Pā. 6-4-77), not the yaṇ of Pā. 6-4-82; the i udātta by the second-member accent; homa — root hveñ with the first-person plural mip by Vedic exchange, śap dropped, the saṃprasāraṇa of hve (Pā. 6-1-34), giving homa, the o udātta by dhātoḥ (Pā. 6-1-162); gantāram — root gamlṛ with tṛn in the sense of habit, initial-udātta since nit; ūtaye — the ktin of ūti, udātta by the irregular formation."

original p. 373

Rik 9: word-meanings, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वसोः (vasoḥ) — (our) wealth's | ऊतये (ūtaye) — for protection | वसुपतिम् (vasupatim) — the lord of wealth and splendour | ऋग्मियम् (ṛgmiyam) — worthy of being praised by ṛks | गन्तारम् (gantāram) — one who goes to the sacrificial ground (for the protection of the sacrificer) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | गीर्भिः (gīrbhiḥ) — with hymns in the form of speech | गृणन्तः (gṛṇantaḥ) — praising | होम (homa) — we call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra is the lord of wealth and splendour; he is worthy of being praised with ṛks (Vedic mantras); he goes to the sacrificial ground and protects the sacrificers and others. We call such an Indra with hymns for the protection of our wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Praising with songs we invoke Indra, the lord of riches, who deserves to be praised and who goes (to protect his worshipper).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Vasupatim" — vasu is wealth, pati is lord; the lord of wealth, the master of wealth. Although the word vasoḥ is already in this rik, the word vasupatim is used again — would there not then be a fault of repetition? No: such usages are found especially often in the Ṛgveda. When using a customary (settled) group of words, one need not attend to whether it is faulty by repetition or contrary to the rules of grammar. Because everyone uses what is settled in usage, its use is regarded as right; for the rules of grammar and the like are composed following the established practice of the language. The root of grammar is language, not the root of language grammar. Such usages with repetition are needed in the Ṛgveda in plenty. We give a couple of examples:

ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥ ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tam ā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnām || (ऋ. सं. ३-३०-१९ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-30-19) ("As if like an expanse my desire has spread [for me]; fill it, O lord of riches, of the riches." — mine and tentative.)

आ तू भर माकिरेतत्परिष्ठाद्विद्मा हि त्वा वसुपतिं वसूनाम् ॥ ā tū bhara mākir etat pariṣṭhād vidmā hi tvā vasupatiṃ vasūnām || (ऋ. सं. ३-३६-९ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-36-9) ("Bring [it] now; let none hinder this; for we know you as lord of riches of riches." — mine and tentative.)

original p. 374

Rik 9: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

The page opens with the end of the second quoted rik from p. 373, and a third:

सत्राभवो वसुपतिर्वसूनां दत्रे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कृष्टीः ॥ satrābhavo vasupatir vasūnāṃ datre viśvā adhithā indra kṛṣṭīḥ || (ऋ. सं. ४-१७-६ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4-17-6) ("You were the lord of riches, of riches in giving; you held all the peoples, O Indra." — mine and tentative.)

"…and so on." All these riks are addressed to Indra. So it may be said that calling Indra vasupati is an established usage.

"Ṛgmiyam" — ऋचो मिमीत इत्यृग्मियः । ऋचां मातारम् (ṛco mimīta ity ṛgmiyaḥ | ṛcāṃ mātāram) — "one who measures the ṛks is ṛgmiya; the 'maker' of the ṛks": the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "one who is praised by ṛks," i.e., one who is hymned. Skandasvāmī: ऋग्मियं । ऋचि स्तुतौ । अर्चना ऋक् । संपदादित्वात् क्विप् । तद्वन्तं स्तुतियोग्यमित्यर्थः (ṛgmiyaṃ | ṛci stutau | arcanā ṛk | saṃpadāditvāt kvip | tadvantaṃ stuti-yogyam ity arthaḥ) — "ṛgmiya: [root] ṛc in the sense of praise; ṛk is worship (arcanā), with kvip as it belongs to the saṃpadādi group; [the one] possessed of it, that is, worthy of praise." That is, ṛgmiya means "worthy of being praised." Veṅkaṭamādhava says ṛgarham — "worthy of ṛks," that is, worthy of being praised with ṛks.

"Homa" — āhvayāmaḥ, "we invoke, we call." The word is the first-person plural laṭ of the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca. For its derivation see the grammar section.

"Gantāram" — the accusative singular of the ṛ-ending word gantṛ. The meaning is "one who goes." Where does he go? The Bhāṣyakāra says to supply the words यागदेशे गमनशीलम् (yāgadeśe gamanaśīlam) — "in the habit of going to the place of sacrifice" — to make the sense: one who goes to the sacrificial ground to protect the sacrificer.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 374–376, noted briefly

वसोः (vasoḥ) — root vasa nivāse; the Uṇādi sūtra "śṝ-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-klidi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-10) gives the suffix u after the roots śṝ hiṃsāyām, svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ, ṣṇiha upatāpe [as printed], trapūṣ lajjāyām, asu kṣepaṇe, vasa nivāse, hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, klidū ārdrībhāve, bandha bandhane, mana jñāne; the suffix is nit, so vasu is initial-udātta. वसुपतिम् (vasupatim) — compound accent: by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223) final-udātta would be expected; this is set aside by "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-1-18 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 372 prints 6-2-18) — when pati in the sense of lordship is the second member, the first member keeps its natural accent. गीर्भिः (gīrbhiḥ) — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168): the case ending is udātta. गृणन्तः (gṛṇantaḥ) — root gṝ śabde ("to sound; praise") with laṭ, replaced by śatṛ by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau" (Pā. 3-2-124); śnā after the kryādi class (Pā. 3-1-81); the root vowel shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80); śatṛ, being apit, is ṅit by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4), so the ā of śnā is dropped by "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-112); the n of śnā becomes ṇ by the vārttika "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" (vārttika 8-4-1); num before jas by "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70); the suffix-accent makes the a of śatṛ udātta. ऋग्मियम् (ṛgmiyam) — "ṛco mimīte": root māṅ māne śabde ca + kvip by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76); by "ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali" (Pā. 7-4-66 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 372 prints 6-4-66) the ā → ī; "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. 6-1-67) removes the v — with a discussion of antaraṅga and bahiraṅga (paribhāṣā 50, "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge"), sthānivad ādeśo 'nalvidhau (Pā. 1-1-56) and "varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam" (paribhāṣā 21), concluding that in Vedic usage sthānivadbhāva sometimes applies even in an al-rule; c → k by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30) and k → g by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. 8-2-39); accusative singular am; the ī before the vowel becomes iy (iyaṅ, "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau", Pā. 6-4-77), with a discussion of the rule "er anekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya" (Pā. 6-4-82) (yaṇ for the final i/ī of a root of more than one syllable) and why it does not arise here (by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante", paribhāṣā 35); finally "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the ī-syllable the udātta. होम (homa) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ first plural mas, replaced by mip by Vedic inversion; i of mip → a; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 2-4-73); saṃprasāraṇa of hve by the "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) that follows "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. 6-1-32); pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108) and guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) give homa; the o is udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-162); mip is pit, so the ma is unaccented. गन्तारम् (gantāram) — root gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau with tṛn in the sense of habitual action (Pā. 3-2-135); nit, initial-udātta. ऊतये (ūtaye) — the irregular ktin of "ūtiyūtijūti…" (Pā. 3-3-97), udātta.

॥९॥

Sūkta 9, Rik 10 (the last)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सु॒तेसु॑ते॒ न्यो॑कसे बृ॒हद्बृ॑ह॒त एद॒रिः । इन्द्रा॑य शू॒षम॑र्चति ॥१०॥

suté-sute nyokase bṛhád bṛhatá ed aríḥ | índrāya śūṣám arcati ||10||

सुतेऽसुते । निऽओकसे । बृहत् । बृहते । आ । इत् । अरिः ॥ इन्द्राय । शूषम् । अर्चति ॥१०॥

sute-sute | ni-okase | bṛhat | bṛhate | ā | it | ariḥ || indrāya | śūṣam | arcati ||10||
