Rik 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

आकार इच्छब्दश्च पादपूरणौ । यद्वा । व्याप्तिवचन आकारः । आङीषदर्थे ऽभिव्याप्तौ । अमु. ३-४-३२ । इत्यभिधानात् । इच्छब्दो ऽपिशब्दार्थः । इयर्ति गच्छत्यनुष्ठेयं कर्म प्राप्नोतीत्यरिर्यजमानः । एदरिः सर्वो ऽपि यजमान इन्द्राय सुते सुत इन्द्रार्थमभिषुते तत्र तत्र सोमे शूषं बलमर्चति स्तौति । इन्द्रस्य पराक्रमं प्रशंसतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशं शूषम् । बृहत् प्रौढम् । कीदृशायेन्द्राय । न्योकसे नियतस्थानाय बृहते प्रौढाय ॥ सुते सुते । षुञ् अभिषवे । क्तप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमिति द्वितीयस्याम्रेडितत्वेनानुदात्तं च । पा. ८-१-३ । इत्यनुदात्तत्वम् । न्योकसे । नियतमोको यस्य तस्मै । निशब्दो निपाता आद्युदात्ता इत्युदात्तः । तस्य यणादेश उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितो ऽनुदात्तस्य । पा. ८-२-४ । इत्योकारः स्वरितः । बृहते । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् । पा. ६-१-१७३-१ । इत्यजादिविभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अरिः । ऋ गतौ । अच इः । उ. ४-१३८ । इतीकारप्रत्ययः । गुणो रपरत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । इन्द्राय । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन्प्रत्यय इकार उदात्तः । शूषम् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । अर्चति । निघातस्वरः ॥ १८ ॥

ākāra icchabdaśca pādapūraṇau | yadvā | vyāptivacana ākāraḥ | āṅīṣadarthe 'bhivyāptau | amu. 3-4-32 | ityabhidhānāt | icchabdo 'piśabdārthaḥ | iyarti gacchatyanuṣṭheyaṃ karma prāpnotītyariryajamānaḥ | edariḥ sarvo 'pi yajamāna indrāya sute suta indrārthamabhiṣute tatra tatra some śūṣaṃ balamarcati stauti | indrasya parākramaṃ praśaṃsatītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ śūṣam | bṛhat prauḍham | kīdṛśāyendrāya | nyokase niyatasthānāya bṛhate prauḍhāya || sute sute | ṣuñ abhiṣave | ktapratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | nityavīpsayoriti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ | tasya paramāmreḍitamiti dvitīyasyāmreḍitatvenānudāttaṃ ca | pā. 8-1-3 | ityanudāttatvam | nyokase | niyatamoko yasya tasmai | niśabdo nipātā ādyudāttā ityudāttaḥ | tasya yaṇādeśa udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya | pā. 8-2-4 | ityokāraḥ svaritaḥ | bṛhate | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam | pā. 6-1-173-1 | ityajādivibhakterudāttatvam | ariḥ | ṛ gatau | aca iḥ | u. 4-138 | itīkārapratyayaḥ | guṇo raparatvam | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | indrāya | ṛjrendretyādinā ranpratyaya ikāra udāttaḥ | śūṣam | prātipadikasvaraḥ | arcati | nighātasvaraḥ || 18 ||

Translation: "The syllable ā and the word it are pāda-fillers. Or: the ā has the sense of 'pervading', according to the statement [of the Amarakośa], 'āṅ in the sense of "a little" and of "pervading"' (Amara 3-4-32); the word it has the sense of api ('also'). Ariḥ is the sacrificer: 'he who goes (iyarti) — attains — the rite to be performed.' Ed ariḥ: every sacrificer, sute-sute, in each Soma that is pressed for Indra's sake, arcati — praises — śūṣam, [his] strength, that is, extols Indra's prowess. What kind of śūṣa? Bṛhat — vast. For what kind of Indra? Nyokase — one whose dwelling is fixed; bṛhate — great." Grammar, noted briefly: sute-sute — root ṣuñ abhiṣave with kta, udātta by the suffix; doubled in the distributive sense ("nityavīpsayoḥ"), the second, as āmreḍita, unaccented (Pā. 8-1-3); nyokase — "he whose abode (okas) is fixed"; the particle ni initial-udātta; with yaṇ, the o becomes svarita (Pā. 8-2-4); bṛhate — the case ending udātta by the upasaṃkhyāna "bṛhanmahatoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-173, vārttika 1); ariḥ — root ṛ gatau with i (Uṇ. 4-138), guṇa and r, the i udātta; indrāya — the suffix ran (by "ṛjrendra…"), the i udātta; śūṣam — stem accent; arcati — unaccented as a finite verb. The bhāṣya ends "॥ १८ ॥", the close of the eighteenth varga.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अरिः (ariḥ) — the sacrificer who performs the rite, or who offers praise | न्योकसे (nyokase) — to the one who dwells in his appointed place | बृहते (bṛhate) — mighty, of great capacity | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra | सुतेसुते (sute-sute) — in each pressing, for Indra, of the Soma-juice prepared | बृहत् (bṛhat) — vast | शूषम् (śūṣam) — (Indra's) strength (power of capacity) | आ अर्चति इत् (ā arcati it) — praises indeed.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The strength, or capacity, of Indra is exceedingly great. The sacrificer who performs the rite praises with hymns and the like, in each pressing — the morning pressing and the other two — Indra's strength and capacities, and calls him.

original p. 378

Rik 10: English, Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

The sacrificer glorifies the vast prowess of Indra, the mighty, the dweller in his permanent abode in every rite where soma is prepared.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this rik, although a third-person verb has been used — "the sacrificer praises Indra" — the poet indirectly states the sense of a first-person usage: "I praise Indra."

"Sute sute" — "at each pressing." By "nityavīpsayoḥ" (no number printed) a word is doubled to show "each one." Using a single word twice to convey "each" is established usage in the Ṛgveda and in other texts: bhare-bhare, have-have, aharahaḥ, etc. Sute-sute means "in the rite of each pressing, and in each rite where Soma-juice is drawn."

"Nyokase" — ni + okase. Here ni is a prefix (upasarga). The word okaḥ, ending in s, means a dwelling, one's own place, a place where one always lives: permanent dwelling, abode, etc. [the source's own English]. For the word divaukasaḥ — "those who dwell in heaven," as their own place — means "gods." Similarly in ni-okase = nyokase, the ni is a particle (upasarga), here meaning "fixed." So nyokase means "one whose place is fixed."

"Ā it" — these words have no necessary meaning in this rik; they are used for filling out the pāda. Or the Bhāṣyakāra's view is that the word ā may be given the sense of api ("also").

"Bṛhate" — महते, महतः शरीरेण वीर्येण वा (mahate, mahataḥ śarīreṇa vīryeṇa vā) — "great — great in body or in valour"; that is, great in body and also in prowess.

"Ariḥ" — ऋ गतौ । इयर्ति गच्छतीत्यनुष्ठेयं कर्म प्राप्नोतीत्यरिर्यजमानः (ṛ gatau | iyarti gacchatīty anuṣṭheyaṃ karma prāpnotīty arir yajamānaḥ) — the root ṛ means "to go, to attain": the one who attains the rite to be performed, i.e., one who performs the rite, the sacrificer.

"Śūṣam" — strength, capacity. Among the twenty-eight words for strength beginning with ojaḥ, pājaḥ, the word śūṣam is read (Nirukta 2-9). Indra's powers, valour, glory, and so on. Although śūṣa has this sense, when the word is used with Indra in view, the sense "hymn" (stotra) generally fits best. A few examples are given on this point:

original p. 379

Rik 10: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

प्र मन्महे शवसानाय शूषमाङ्गूषं गिर्वणसे अङ्गिरस्वत् । pra manmahe śavasānāya śūṣam āṅgūṣaṃ girvaṇase aṅgirasvat | (ऋ. सं. १-६२-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-62-1) ("We offer a hymn — a śūṣa, an āṅgūṣa — to the powerful one, the hymn-loving, as the Aṅgirases did." — mine and tentative.)

इनम् महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुः । inam mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ śaśvat-kṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruḥ | (ऋ. सं. ३-५४-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-54-1) ("To the great lord, worthy of the assembly, worthy of praise, they have brought a hymn, perpetually acting." — mine and tentative.)

उप व एषे वन्द्येभिः शूषैः प्र यह्वी दिवश्चितयद्भिरर्कैः । upa va eṣe vandyebhiḥ śūṣaiḥ pra yahvī divaś citayadbhir arkaiḥ | (ऋ. सं. ५-४१-६ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 5-41-6) ("I approach you with praiseworthy hymns, with hymns that make [the heavens] shine." — mine and tentative.)

आ यं पृणन्ति हरिभिर्न धेनव इन्द्राय शूषं हरिवन्तमर्चत ॥ ā yaṃ pṛṇanti haribhir na dhenava indrāya śūṣaṃ harivantam arcata || (ऋ. सं. १०-९६-२ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-96-2) ("…whom [the hymns] fill as milch-cows [fill a calf]; sing a hymn to Indra, the lord of bay horses." — mine and tentative.)

Many more examples could be given.

"Arcati" — arcati is read among the forty-four verbs [roots] of the sense "to worship, praise," beginning with arcati, gāyati (Nirukta 3-19); so arcati means gāyati, stauti — "he praises, he extols."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 379–380, noted briefly

सुतेसुते (sute-sute) — root ṣuñ abhiṣave ("to press") + kta; initial/final-udātta by the suffix; locative singular ṅi → e; doubling by "nityavīpsayoḥ" (Pā. 8-1-4); for the second member the technical name āmreḍita arises ("tasya paramāmreḍitam," Pā. 8-1-2), and "anudāttaṃ ca" (8-1-3, printed "va. sū." [sic]) makes it unaccented. न्योकसे (nyokase) — "niyatam okaḥ yasya": ni is a nipāta, initial-udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); the udātta i is replaced by y ("iko yaṇ aci," Pā. 6-4-77 [as printed]), and the o after the udātta y is svarita by "udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (Pā. 8-2-4). बृहते (bṛhate) — "bṛhan-mahator upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. 6-1-173, vārttika 1): after bṛhat and mahat the case-ending that has nadī status (and the vowel-initial endings) is udātta; so the e in bṛhate is udātta; although the sūtra "vartamāne pṛṣad-bṛhan-mahaj-jagac-chatṛvac ca" (Uṇ. 2-2-42 [?], as printed in three parts) says śatṛvat (treated like śatṛ), by which "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. 6-1-173) would already give the udātta, a vārttika is needed to fix the rule so that it applies only after bṛhat and mahat and not after pṛṣat and jagat; hence "bṛhan-mahator upasaṃkhyānam" is necessary. अरिः (ariḥ) — root ṛ gatau + the suffix i by "aca iḥ" (Uṇ. 4-578 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 377 prints 4-138); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) and raparatva by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51); ari is final-udātta by the suffix. इन्द्राय (indrāya) — ran by "ṛjrendrāgra-vajra…" (Uṇ. 2-186); the suffix is nit, so initial-udātta. शूषम् (śūṣam) — base accent by the Phiṭ-sūtra "phiṣaḥ" (Phiṭ 1). अर्चति (arcati) — wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

॥१०॥

इति नवमं सूक्तं समाप्तम् । iti navamaṃ sūktaṃ samāptam | "Thus the ninth sūkta is completed." Printed in Sanskrit at the end of the grammar, p. 380.

End of Sūkta 9.

original p. 380

॥ ಹತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 10 — "gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ" ("The Tenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

गायन्तीति सूक्तस्य मन्त्रसंख्या छन्दोविशेषश्चैवमनुक्रम्यते । गायन्ति द्वादशानुष्टुभं त्विति । तुहिहवेत्यादिपरिभाषायाम् । अनु १२-३ । तुशब्दस्य सूक्तद्वये परिभाषितत्वादस्य सूक्तस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्य चानुष्टुभत्वं द्रष्टव्यम् । ऋषिदेवते पूर्ववत् । अभिप्लवषडहस्योक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवने ऽच्छावाकस्य गायन्तीति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । एह्यूष्विति खण्डे गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिण आ त्वा गिरो रथीरिव । आ. ७-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥

gāyantīti sūktasya mantrasaṃkhyā chandoviśeṣaścaivamanukramyate | gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tviti | tuhihavetyādiparibhāṣāyām | anu 12-3 | tuśabdasya sūktadvaye paribhāṣitatvādasya sūktasya vakṣyamāṇasya cānuṣṭubhatvaṃ draṣṭavyam | ṛṣidevate pūrvavat | abhiplavaṣaḍahasyokthyeṣu tṛtīyasavane 'cchāvākasya gāyantīti stotriyastṛcaḥ | ehyūṣviti khaṇḍe gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇa ā tvā giro rathīriva | ā. 7-8 | iti sūtritam ||

Translation: "The number of mantras and the special meter of the sūkta gāyanti are laid down in the Anukramaṇī thus: 'gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tv iti' ("gāyanti: twelve, in Anuṣṭubh — tu"); and by the rule beginning tuhihava in the Paribhāṣā (Anukramaṇī 12-3), since the word tu is declared to apply to two sūktas, this sūkta and the next are both to be understood as Anuṣṭubh. Ṛṣi and deity are as before. Its special application: in the ukthya [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, in the third pressing, the opening triplet (stotriya) of the Acchāvāka is gāyanti. In the section ehy ū ṣu it is laid down: 'gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ, ā tvā giro rathīr iva' (Āśvalāyana 7-8)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The mantra-count and the meter of the sūkta gāyanti tvā are given in the Sūkta-anukramaṇī as "gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tv iti" — twelve riks, in the Anuṣṭubh meter (Anu. 12-3). Here the word tu [in the Paribhāṣā] is used so as to make known that this sūkta and the next share the same meter, Anuṣṭubh, as the two sūktas it governs. The ṛṣi and deity of this sūkta are as in the previous sūkta. Its application: in the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the third pressing, when the ukthya mantras are recited, the Acchāvāka priest [recites] the triplet gāyanti, as a stotriya [opening triplet] śastra-mantra. Āśvalāyana says in his Śrauta-sūtra, in the section ehy ū ṣu (Āś. Sū. 7-8), that the riks gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1; Sāma 342; 1344) and ā tvā giro rathīr iva (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-95-1; Sāma 349) are to be recited.

original p. 381

Sūkta 10, Rik 1

॥ Sūkta — 10 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 3 ॥ Sūkta — 10 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 19, 20 ॥ ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–12 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Madhucchandā Vaiśvāmitra ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Anuṣṭubh ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गाय॑न्ति त्वा गाय॒त्रिणो ऽर्च॑न्त्य॒र्कम॒र्किणः॑ । ब्र॒ह्मा॑णस्त्वा शतक्र॒त उद्वं॒शमि॑व येमिरे ॥१॥

gā́yanti tvā gāyatríṇó 'rcanty arkám arkíṇaḥ | brahmāṇas tvā śatakratá ud vaṃśám iva yemire ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गायन्ति । त्वा । गायत्रिणः । अर्चन्ति । अर्कम् । अर्किणः ॥ ब्रह्माणः । त्वा । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । उत् । वंशम्ऽइव । येमिरे ॥१॥

gāyanti | tvā | gāyatriṇaḥ | arcanti | arkam | arkiṇaḥ || brahmāṇaḥ | tvā | śatakrato iti śata-krato | ut | vaṃśam-iva | yemire ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन्बहुप्रज्ञ वेन्द्र त्वां गायत्रिण उद्गातारो गायन्ति । स्तुवन्ति । अर्किणो ऽर्चनहेतुमन्त्रयुक्ता होतारो ऽर्कमर्चनीयमिन्द्रमर्चन्ति । शस्त्रगतैर्मन्त्रैः प्रशंसन्ति । ब्रह्माणो ब्रह्मप्रभृतय इतरे ब्राह्मणास्त्वामुद्येमिरे । उन्नतिं प्रापयन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वंशमिव । यथा वंशाग्रे नृत्यन्तः शिल्पिनः प्रौढं वंशमुत्पन्नं कुर्वन्ति । यथा वा सन्मार्गवर्तिनः स्वकीयं कुलमुन्नतं कुर्वन्ति तद्वत् । एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः प्रार्चन्ति ते ऽर्कमर्किणो ब्रह्माणस्त्वा शतक्रत उद्येमिरे वंशमिव । वंशो वनशयो भवति वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा । नि. ५-५ । अर्कशब्दं च बहुधा व्याचष्टे । अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्त्यर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्त्यर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतान्यर्को वृक्षो भवति स वृतः कटुकिम्ना । नि. ५-४ । इति ॥ गायन्ति । शप्तिङौ पित्त्वात्सार्वधातुकत्वाच्चानुदात्तौ । धातुरुदात्तः । गायत्रिणः । गायत्रं साम येषामुद्गातॄणामस्ति ते । अत इनिठनौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । अर्चन्ति । अर्च पूजायाम् । भौवादिकः । शप्तिङावनुदात्तौ धातुस्वर एव । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । अर्कम् । अर्चन्त्येभिरित्यर्का मन्त्राः । तैरर्चनीयतया तदात्मक इन्द्रो ऽपि लक्षणयार्कः । पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेण । पा. ३-३-११८ । इति करणे घः । चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः । पा. ७-३-५२ । इति चकारस्य कुत्वम् । ककारः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । अर्का मन्त्रा एषां सन्तीत्यर्किणो होतारः । एकाक्षरात्कृतो जातेः सप्तम्यां च न तौ स्मृतौ । पा. ५-२-११५-२ । इति कृदन्तादिनिठनौ यद्यपि प्रतिषिद्धौ तथाप्यत्र व्यत्ययादिनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । ब्रह्माणः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । शतक्रतो । निघातः । संहितायामवादेशे लोपः शाकल्यस्य । पा. ८-३-१९ । इति वकारलोपः । वंशशब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च । पा. २-१-४-२ । इति स एव शिष्यते । येमिरे । यम उपरमे । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

he śatakrato bahukarmanbahuprajña vendra tvāṃ gāyatriṇa udgātāro gāyanti | stuvanti | arkiṇo 'rcanahetumantrayuktā hotāro 'rkamarcanīyamindramarcanti | śastragatairmantraiḥ praśaṃsanti | brahmāṇo brahmaprabhṛtaya itare brāhmaṇāstvāmudyemire | unnatiṃ prāpayanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vaṃśamiva | yathā vaṃśāgre nṛtyantaḥ śilpinaḥ prauḍhaṃ vaṃśamutpannaṃ kurvanti | yathā vā sanmārgavartinaḥ svakīyaṃ kulamunnataṃ kurvanti tadvat | etāmṛcaṃ yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ prārcanti te 'rkamarkiṇo brahmāṇastvā śatakrata udyemire vaṃśamiva | vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananācchrūyata iti vā | ni. 5-5 | arkaśabdaṃ ca bahudhā vyācaṣṭe | arko devo bhavati yadenamarcantyarko mantro bhavati yadenenārcantyarkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtānyarko vṛkṣo bhavati sa vṛtaḥ kaṭukimnā | ni. 5-4 | iti || gāyanti | śaptiṅau pittvātsārvadhātukatvāccānudāttau | dhāturudāttaḥ | gāyatriṇaḥ | gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣāmudgātṝṇāmasti te | ata iniṭhanau | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | arcanti | arca pūjāyām | bhauvādikaḥ | śaptiṅāvanudāttau dhātusvara eva | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | arkam | arcantyebhirityarkā mantrāḥ | tairarcanīyatayā tadātmaka indro 'pi lakṣaṇayārkaḥ | puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa | pā. 3-3-118 | iti karaṇe ghaḥ | cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ | pā. 7-3-52 | iti cakārasya kutvam | kakāraḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | arkā mantrā eṣāṃ santītyarkiṇo hotāraḥ | ekākṣarātkṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau | pā. 5-2-115-2 | iti kṛdantādiniṭhanau yadyapi pratiṣiddhau tathāpyatra vyatyayādiniḥ | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | brahmāṇaḥ | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | śatakrato | nighātaḥ | saṃhitāyāmavādeśe lopaḥ śākalyasya | pā. 8-3-19 | iti vakāralopaḥ | vaṃśaśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca | pā. 2-1-4-2 | iti sa eva śiṣyate | yemire | yama uparame | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O śatakrato — O Indra of many deeds, of much wisdom — the gāyatriṇaḥ, the udgātṛ priests, sing of you (gāyanti): they praise. The arkiṇaḥ, the hotṛ priests, equipped with the mantras that are the means of worship, worship (arcanti) Indra, the arka — the worshipful one: they praise [him] with the mantras of the śastra. The brahmāṇaḥ — Brahmā and the other brāhmaṇas — ud yemire: raise you aloft, they bring about your elevation. The illustration: vaṃśam iva — as craftsmen dancing at the tip of a bamboo pole set the grown bamboo upright, or as those who follow the good path raise their own family high, so [they raise you]. This rik Yāska explains thus: 'gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ, prārcanti te 'rkam arkiṇaḥ, brahmāṇas tvā śatakrata udyemire vaṃśam iva; a vaṃśa (bamboo) is "that which lies in the forest" (vanaśaya), or "that which is heard of (śrūyate) because of its being enjoyed (vananāt)"' (Nirukta 5-5). And he explains the word arka in many ways: 'arka is a god, because they worship him (arcanti); arka is a mantra, because with it they worship; arka is food, because beings honour it; arka is a tree (vṛkṣa): it is covered with pungency' (Nirukta 5-4)." Grammar, noted briefly: gāyanti — the root accent stands, śap and tiṅ being unaccented; gāyatriṇaḥ — "those udgātṛs who have the gāyatra sāman", with ini, the i udātta; arcanti — root arca pūjāyām, root accent, not lowered as first in the pāda; arkam — "the mantras with which they worship", hence by implication Indra; the suffix gha in the instrumental sense (Pā. 3-3-118), c → k (Pā. 7-3-52), final-udātta; arkiṇaḥ — the hotṛs "who have the arka-mantras", with ini by Vedic exchange though the vārttika (Pā. 5-2-115-2) forbids it after a kṛt stem; brahmāṇaḥ — stem accent; śatakrato — vocative, lowered; the v dropped in the Saṃhitā (Pā. 8-3-19); vaṃśam iva — no loss of the case ending, first-member accent (Pā. 2-1-4-2); yemire — root yama uparame, lowered as a finite verb.

original p. 382

Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) शतक्रतो ((he) śatakrato) — O Indra, who perform many daring deeds, or who are of much wisdom | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | गायत्रिणः (gāyatriṇaḥ) — the priests called udgātṛ, singers of the Sāman | गायन्ति (gāyanti) — praise with Sāma-Veda mantras | अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — the priests called hotṛ, who praise with ṛks of the Ṛgveda | अर्कम् (arkam) — Indra, worthy of worship or praise | अर्चन्ति (arcanti) — extol with the śastra mantras | ब्रह्माणः (brahmāṇaḥ) — the other brāhmaṇas, headed by Brahmā | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | वंशम् इव (vaṃśam iva) — like a bamboo | उत् येमिरे (ut yemire) — raise aloft (praise specially).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You do many daring deeds or are of much wisdom. In sacrifices and other rites the priests called udgātṛ praise you by singing Sāmans; the priests called hotṛ, who are worthy to be worshipped with the mantras of their own Veda, the Ṛgveda, praise you; Brahmā and the other brāhmaṇas praise you with hymns and the like, as one raises a bamboo aloft, and so increase your fame.

original p. 383

Rik 1: English and Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Indra, with many daring deeds or great knowledge, the chanters of the Sama sing about you, the reciters of the Riks praise you who are worthy of praise, and the (priests called) Brahmanas raise you aloft like a bamboo pole.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This rik is found, besides in this sūkta, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1-6-12-2), the Sāma-Veda (342; 1344) and the Nirukta (5-5). The sense of this rik, or the matter stated in it, is almost the same as the sense of the first rik of the seventh sūkta. The sense of the first half (that is, the first and second pādas) is clear, but what is said in the third pāda is somewhat strained. Here the sense of the word brahmāṇaḥ does not fit well. In the sacrificial rite, the three priest-groups — hotṛ, adhvaryu and udgātṛ — need one priest, called brahmā, to see to it that their duties are properly carried out. He must know all three Vedas and the order of performance of the sacrifice. Although he does not take a special part in the actual duties of the rite, he takes care that the sacrifice proceeds properly, and gives permission for the necessary actions of the other priests, so that the sacrifice goes on with all its limbs: he is the supervisor. The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word brahmāṇaḥ as the priests of the brahma class and the other brāhmaṇas. Or, brahma has the sense of "praise (stotra)," and so one may give the word brahmāṇaḥ the sense "those who praise."

The comparison vaṃśam iva in the third pāda is also strained. Vaṃśa is a kind of tree: bamboo, reed. The comparison "like raising [or lifting high] a bamboo" is not well fitted. [The meaning:] those who raise you as one raises a bamboo — that is, they praise you and so increase your fame and renown; by singing of your qualities they provide you with a high station: this may be taken as the poet's idea. Or, since vaṃśa has another meaning — family, lineage — then "as those who raise their family's honour by right conduct, or raise the esteem of the family by special deeds of daring, so [they raise you]": this is the sense one may give. The Bhāṣyakāra gives both of these senses.

original p. 384

Rik 1: Special Topics (continued)

"Gāyatriṇaḥ" — गायत्रं साम येषामुद्गातॄणामस्ति ते (gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣām udgātṝṇām asti te) — "those udgātṛs who have the Gāyatra Sāman": those who sing the Sāman called Gāyatra; or, since many of the mantras sung in the Sāma-Veda are Ṛgveda mantras in the Gāyatrī meter, it is the customary usage to call the udgātṛ priests who sing them gāyatriṇaḥ — "singers of Gāyatrī-meter ṛks."

"Arcanti" — arca pūjāyām — the root arc: to worship; that is, to praise.

"Arkam" — अर्चन्त्येभिरित्यर्काः मन्त्राः (arcanty ebhir ity arkāḥ mantrāḥ) — "those with which they worship are arkas, the mantras": since they are used for praising, mantras are called arkas. Here arkam means Indra, who is praised by such arkas or mantras.

For this rik the sage Yāska has given, in his Nirukta, an explanation in this manner:

अर्कः ॥ अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्ति ॥ अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति ॥ अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि ॥ अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥ arkaḥ || arko devo bhavati yad enam arcanti || arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti || arkam annaṃ bhavaty arcati bhūtāni || arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā || (No reference is printed with this block; the bhāṣya on p. 382 cites it as Ni. 5-4, reading sa vṛtaḥ.)

Four different senses of the word arka are stated:

Devaḥ — तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यत्-यस्मात् एनं-देवम् अर्चन्ति स्तोतारः (tāvat sarva evārka ity ucyate yat-yasmāt enaṃ-devam arcanti stotāraḥ) — "first, every [god] is called arka, because (yat = yasmāt) the praisers worship him (enam = the god)" — arka is the god; for the worshippers, using this word, say "arka" of whom they worship. That is, the deity worshipped by the devotees is called arka.

अर्को मन्त्रो भवति — यत्-यस्मात्, अनेन-मन्त्रेण, अर्चन्ति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः (arko mantro bhavati — yat-yasmāt, anena-mantreṇa, arcanti stotāraḥ tasmād arkaḥ) — "arka is a mantra, because with it (= the mantra) the praisers worship; therefore arka"; those who praise worship the deity with this (the arka, or mantra); hence arka means "mantra."

अर्कमन्नं भवति — तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि, यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, पूज्यं च सर्वस्यैवान्नम् (arkam annaṃ bhavati — tad dhi arcati bhūtāni, yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnam api saṃskāra-viśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate, pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyaivānnam) — "arka is food, for it honours (sustains) beings; for whoever is worthy of honour, his food too is prepared with special care and used in worship; and food is honoured by everyone": food (āhāra) is necessary to all living beings, and everyone honours and seeks it with respect and love; so arka also means food.

अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन भवति (arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭuka-bhāvena bhavati) — "that well-known tree arka [the Calotropis, in Kannada ಎಕ್ಕ] is covered all round with pungency (kaṭu)." The name arka for a tree (vṛkṣa) is well established, too.

original p. 385

Rik 1: Special Topics (continued)

…"Arka" means ekka tree, in Kannada. Its twigs are used in the homa rites, and it is also well known to all as a herbal medicine; therefore the arka tree is a thing known to all. As its sap is acrid, he says kaṭukimnā ("by pungency").

As an example to explain the word arka, Yāska has quoted this very rik gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ, and in it has also given an explanation of the meaning of the word vaṃśa in it:

गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः प्रार्चन्ति ते ऽर्कमर्किणो ब्राह्मणास्त्वा शतक्रतो उद्येमिरे वंशमिव वंशो वनशयो भवति वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा ॥ gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ prārcanti te 'rkamarkiṇo brāhmaṇāstvā śatakrato udyemire vaṃśamiva vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananācchrūyata iti vā || (नि. ५-४ — Nirukta 5-4 as printed; the bhāṣya on p. 382 cites it as 5-5) (Yāska's text reads brāhmaṇās tvā śatakrato for the Saṃhitā's brahmāṇas tvā śatakrata.)

Durgācārya's commentary on this runs:

गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः — स्तुवन्ति त्वां सामगाः सामभिः । अर्चन्त्यर्कमर्किणः — पूजयन्ति त्वां ऋग्भिः होतारो मन्त्रिणः । एवमनेन प्रकारेण सर्व एते ब्राह्मणा यज्ञे कर्मणि हे शतक्रतो उद्वंशमिव येमिरे — उद्येमिरे वंशमिव त्वां स्तुतिभिः हविर्भिश्च यज्ञेषु तवैव महिमानं वर्धयन्तीत्यर्थः । वंशो वनशयो भवति वने शयित इवास्ते, वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा संभजनाद्वा वल्लिभिः ॥ एवमत्र देवः अर्कशब्देनोच्यते मन्त्रस्यार्कशब्दवाच्यत्वे अर्चन्त्यर्कमर्किण इत्येष एव निगमः । अर्किणो हि मन्त्रिण एवाभिप्रेताः । वृक्षस्तु प्रसिद्ध एव । तेन निगमस्तदभिधायको नैवास्ति ॥ gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ — stuvanti tvāṃ sāmagāḥ sāmabhiḥ | arcantyarkamarkiṇaḥ — pūjayanti tvāṃ ṛgbhiḥ hotāro mantriṇaḥ | evamanena prakāreṇa sarva ete brāhmaṇā yajñe karmaṇi he śatakrato udvaṃśamiva yemire — udyemire vaṃśamiva tvāṃ stutibhiḥ havirbhiśca yajñeṣu tavaiva mahimānaṃ vardhayantītyarthaḥ | vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vane śayita ivāste, vananācchrūyata iti vā saṃbhajanādvā vallibhiḥ || evamatra devaḥ arkaśabdenocyate mantrasyārkaśabdavācyatve arcantyarkamarkiṇa ityeṣa eva nigamaḥ | arkiṇo hi mantriṇa evābhipretāḥ | vṛkṣastu prasiddha eva | tena nigamastadabhidhāyako naivāsti ||

— "Gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ: the Sāma-singers praise you with Sāmans. Arcanty arkam arkiṇaḥ: the hotṛs, with mantras, worship you with ṛks. In this way all these brāhmaṇas, in the sacrificial rite, O śatakrato, ud yemire — raise you aloft like a bamboo; with praises and offerings in sacrifices they increase your greatness. A vaṃśa is vanaśaya, lying in the forest; or, vananāc chrūyate — it is heard of because of being enjoyed, or because creepers resort to it. Thus here the god is meant by the word arka; for arka meaning the mantra, this very passage arcanty arkam arkiṇaḥ is the instance, for by arkiṇaḥ those who have the mantras are meant; the tree is well known, and so there is no passage naming it."

Here Yāska gives the word brahmāṇaḥ the sense brāhmaṇāḥ: brāhmaṇa means those of the brāhmaṇa caste and also the priests, headed by Brahmā, who take part in sacrifices and the like. For vaṃśa he says: vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananāc chrayata iti vā — "because it lies in the forest it is called vaṃśa; or because, when the wind blows, the bamboos rub against one another and make a sound, it is called vaṃśa; or because creepers climb it, it is called vaṃśa": so he explains.

"Arkiṇaḥ" — अर्चनहेतुमन्त्रयुक्ताः होतारः । अर्का मन्त्रा एषां सन्तीत्यर्किणः होतारः (arcana-hetu-mantra-yuktāḥ hotāraḥ | arkā mantrā eṣāṃ santīty arkiṇaḥ hotāraḥ) — "the hotṛs, equipped with the mantras that are the means of worship; those who have arka mantras are arkiṇaḥ, the hotṛs." Since arka has the sense "mantra," those who praise with them are called arkiṇaḥ — that is, the priests of the hotṛ group who recite the ṛks in the form of śastra.

"Brahmāṇaḥ" — the Bhāṣyakāra gives this word the sense of priests headed by Brahmā, and other brāhmaṇas. Yāska gives it a general sense, "brāhmaṇas."

"Śatakrato" — the explanation of this word was already given earlier.

"Vaṃśam iva" — the explanation of this word is also in Yāska's exposition above.

original p. 386

Rik 1: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 386–387, noted briefly

गायन्ति (gāyanti) — root gai śabde with laṭ parasmaipada third plural jhi; jh → ant by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); śap; since the suffix is śit, "ād eca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. 6-1-45) does not give ā for the ai; "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78) gives āy, so gāyanti; śap is pit, hence unaccented; the ending anti, a lasārvadhātuka, follows śap, an adupadeśa, and so is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); the ā of gā takes the root accent, udātta. गायत्रिणः (gāyatriṇaḥ) — gāyatra is the name of a Sāman; "gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣām udgātṝṇām asti te" ("those udgātṛs who have the Gāyatra Sāman") — in the compound analysis ini by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); a of gāyatra dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); nominative plural gāyatriṇaḥ; the i is udātta by the suffix. अर्चन्ति (arcanti) — root arca pūjāyām (bhvādi class); śap is pit, so unaccented; the anti is unaccented as a lasārvadhātuka following the adupadeśa śap; the root accent stands; since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda there is no lowering of the verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). अर्कम् (arkam) — "arcanty ebhiḥ iti arkāḥ, mantrāḥ" ("the mantras with which they worship"); Indra, worshipped with them, is by implication also called arka; from arc with gha by "puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa" (Pā. 3-3-118), in the sense of instrument or location, in a masculine name; gha is ghit (its gh is it), so by "cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-52) the c takes the k-class before a ghit or ṇyat suffix, giving arka; final-udātta by the suffix accent. अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ) — "arkāḥ mantrāḥ eṣāṃ santi" — "the hotṛs": the ini suffix by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); although arka is a kṛdanta, and the Mahābhāṣya's "ekākṣarāt kṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau" (pā. ma. 5-2-115-1) says that ini and ṭhan do not come after a one-syllable word, a kṛdanta, a word for a class, or in the locative sense, ini arises here by Vedic inversion (continued on p. 387); the i is udātta by the suffix.

Rik 1 grammar closes; Rik 2

ब्रह्माणः (brahmāṇaḥ) — final-udātta by the stem accent. शतक्रतो (śatakrato) — unaccented as a vocative by "āmantritasya ca" (8-1-19); in the Saṃhitā, with u before a vowel, the o → av by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78), then the v is lost by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19); and since this loss is treated as not having taken place (pūrvatrāsiddham, Pā. 8-2-1), the guṇa of "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) does not occur. वंशमिव (vaṃśam iva) — vaṃśa is final-udātta by the stem accent; with iva it becomes a compound and the case-ending is dropped, the first member's accent staying ("ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ ca," Pā. 2-1-4). येमिरे (yemire) — root yamu uparame ("to restrain; to hold up") with liṭ ātmanepada third plural jha; jha → irec by "liṭas tajhayor eśirec" (3-4-81, printed "pā. sada." [sic]); doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8); by "ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi" (Pā. "6-4-1-20" as printed, i.e. 6-4-120), before a kit liṭ the short a between single consonants of a root whose initial is not changed in reduplication takes e, with loss of the reduplicate; so yemire; although the root yam is parasmaipadī in the bhvādi class, here it is ātmanepada by Vedic inversion; wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

Rik 2: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यद्यदा सानोः सानुमारुहत् यजमानः सोमवल्लीसमिदाद्याहरणायैकस्मात्पर्वतभागादपरं पर्वतभागमारूढवान् । तथा भूरि प्रभूतं कर्त्वं कर्म सोमयागरूपमस्पष्ट स्पृष्टवान् । उपक्रान्तवानित्यर्थः । तत्तदानीमिन्द्रो ऽर्थं यजमानस्य प्रयोजनं चेतति । जानाति । ज्ञात्वा च वृष्णिः कामानां वर्षिता सन् यूथेन मरुद्गणेन सहैजति । कम्पते । स्वस्थानाद्यज्ञभूमिमागन्तुमुद्युक्त इत्यर्थः ॥ सानोः । षणु दाने । सनोति ददाति निवसतामवकाशमिति सानुः । दृसनिजनिचरिचटिरहिभ्यो ञुण् । उ. १-३ । णित्त्वादुपधाया वृद्धिः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं च । अरुहत् । रुहेर्लुङि तिपि शपि संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः । परि ९३-१ । इति लघूपधगुणो न भवति । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । सति शिष्टत्वात्स एव शिष्यते । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति । पा. ८-१-३० । निषेधान्निघातो न भवति । भूरि । अदिशदिभूशुभिभ्यः क्रिन् । उ. ४-६५ । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अस्पष्ट । स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः । स्वरितञित इत्यात्मनेपदम् । लङः प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनं त । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । व्रश्चादिषत्वष्टुत्वे । पा. ८-२-३६ ; ८-४-४१ । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्त इत्यडागम उदात्तः । स एव शिष्यते । अनुषङ्गेण यच्छब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः । कर्त्वम् । डुकृञ् करणे । अन्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्ते । पा. ३-२-७५ । इति विच् । गुणो रपरत्वम् । विचः सर्वापहारी लोपः । करो भावः कर्त्वम् । अर्थम् । अर्तेरुषिकुषिगार्तिभ्यस्थन् । उ. २-४ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । यूथेन । तिथपृष्ठगूथयूथप्रोथाः । उ. २-१२ । इति थक्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । वृष्णिः । निरित्यनुवृत्तौ सृवृषिभ्यां कित् । उ. ४-४९ । इति निप्रत्ययान्तः । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । एजति । एजृ कम्पने । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

yadyadā sānoḥ sānumāruhat yajamānaḥ somavallīsamidādyāharaṇāyaikasmātparvatabhāgādaparaṃ parvatabhāgamārūḍhavān | tathā bhūri prabhūtaṃ kartvaṃ karma somayāgarūpamaspaṣṭa spṛṣṭavān | upakrāntavānityarthaḥ | tattadānīmindro 'rthaṃ yajamānasya prayojanaṃ cetati | jānāti | jñātvā ca vṛṣṇiḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitā san yūthena marudgaṇena sahaijati | kampate | svasthānādyajñabhūmimāgantumudyukta ityarthaḥ || sānoḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | sanoti dadāti nivasatāmavakāśamiti sānuḥ | dṛsanijanicaricaṭirahibhyo ñuṇ | u. 1-3 | ṇittvādupadhāyā vṛddhiḥ | ñittvādādyudāttatvaṃ ca | aruhat | ruherluṅi tipi śapi saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranityaḥ | pari 93-1 | iti laghūpadhaguṇo na bhavati | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudāttaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvātsa eva śiṣyate | nipātairyadyadihanteti | pā. 8-1-30 | niṣedhānnighāto na bhavati | bhūri | adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin | u. 4-65 | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | aspaṣṭa | spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ | svaritañita ityātmanepadam | laṅaḥ prathamapuruṣaikavacanaṃ ta | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vraścādiṣatvaṣṭutve | pā. 8-2-36 ; 8-4-41 | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudātta ityaḍāgama udāttaḥ | sa eva śiṣyate | anuṣaṅgeṇa yacchabdayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | kartvam | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante | pā. 3-2-75 | iti vic | guṇo raparatvam | vicaḥ sarvāpahārī lopaḥ | karo bhāvaḥ kartvam | artham | arteruṣikuṣigārtibhyasthan | u. 2-4 | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | yūthena | tithapṛṣṭhagūthayūthaprothāḥ | u. 2-12 | iti thakpratyayānto nipātitaḥ | vṛṣṇiḥ | nirityanuvṛttau sṛvṛṣibhyāṃ kit | u. 4-49 | iti nipratyayāntaḥ | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | ejati | ejṛ kampane | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Yad — when — the sacrificer sānoḥ sānum āruhat: in order to fetch Soma-creepers, fuel-sticks and the like, climbs from one part of the mountain to another part. And bhūri — a great — kartvam, a work (karma) in the form of a Soma-sacrifice, aspaṣṭa — has touched: has begun. Tat — then — Indra artham cetati: knows the sacrificer's purpose. Having known it, being vṛṣṇiḥ, the showerer of desires, he ejati — stirs, is set in motion — yūthena, together with the troop of Maruts: he is ready to come from his own place to the sacrificial ground." Grammar, noted briefly: sānoḥ — root ṣaṇu dāne, "that which gives room to those who dwell", suffix ñuṇ (Uṇ. 1-3), vṛddhi, initial-udātta; aruhat — luṅ of ruh, no guṇa since the rule is not obligatory (paribhāṣā 93-1); the augment aṭ udātta, not lowered after yat (Pā. 8-1-30); bhūri — suffix krin (Uṇ. 4-65), initial-udātta; aspaṣṭa — root spaśa , ātmanepada, laṅ third singular, śap dropped, ṣ and ṭ by Pā. 8-2-36 and 8-4-41, the augment udātta; kartvam — root ḍukṛñ with vic (Pā. 3-2-75), "the doing"; artham — suffix than (Uṇ. 2-4); yūthena — an irregular thak formation (Uṇ. 2-12); vṛṣṇiḥ — suffix ni, kit (Uṇ. 4-49), final-udātta; ejati — root ejṛ kampane, lowered as a finite verb.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यत् (yat) — when | the sacrificer, to fetch the Soma-creeper and the fuel-sticks सानोः (sānoḥ) — from one mountain-top | सानुम् (sānum) — to another peak | आ अरुहत् (ā aruhat) — climbs | and भूरि (bhūri) — a great | कर्त्वम् (kartvam) — Soma-sacrificial work | अस्पष्ट (aspaṣṭa) — has begun | तत् (tat) — then | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | अर्थम् (artham) — the sacrificer's wish | चेतति (cetati) — knows | after knowing वृष्णिः (vṛṣṇiḥ) — Indra, the granter of desires, the giver of rain | यूथेन (yūthena) — together with the troop of Maruts | एजति (ejati) — leaves (that is, leaving his own dwelling, sets out to come near the sacrificer).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The sacrificer goes to the mountain, and there climbs from one peak to another, to bring the Soma-creeper that has grown on the hills and the fuel-sticks required for the sacrifice; thereby he begins the sacrifice. Indra, knowing this, since he grants the desired ends of the sacrificer, sets out from his own place for the sacrificial ground, together with his friendly troop of Maruts.

original p. 389

Rik 2: English and Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

When Indra the showerer of blessings knows the object of the worshipper who has wandered from one ridge of the mountain to the other in quest of soma plant and who has just begun the sacrifice, he (Indra) approaches the sacrificial place with the troop of (Maruts).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

To give the sense of this rik, many words have to be supplied. "Sānoḥ sānum āruhat" — "climbs from one peak [or table-land] of the mountain to another": that is, the question of "who climbs?" and "why?" arises. To fit the sense, the Bhāṣyakāra supplies the words "the sacrificer — for fetching the Soma-creeper, fuel-sticks and the other means of sacrifice." And since the word yūtha means a herd, a group, the word "Maruts" is supplied: "the troop (gaṇa) of Maruts." The word vṛṣṇi means varṣitā, "giver of rain": though "he comes with the Maruts who are helpers for rain" would fit, the Bhāṣyakāra explains vṛṣṇi as kāmānāṃ varṣitā — "the one who rains desired ends," and so a doubt arises as to whether the help of the Maruts is necessary for giving desired things other than rain. Hence it is doubtful whether yūthena in this rik is the poet's intended "with the troop of Maruts." Veṅkaṭamādhava gives the sense vasusamūhena — "with the assembly of the Vasus"; so it seems more fitting to say "with the assembly of the gods."

"Yat," "tat" — here these words are not the relative-demonstrative words yad and tad in any case or number; they are indeclinables. For them the sense yadā, "when," and tadā, "then," must be given.

"Sānoḥ, sānum" — the mountain-peak or the table-land of the hill. Since the Soma-creeper grows especially in the hill regions, and since the creeper growing in the high regions of the hills gives a more abundant and better juice than the creeper that grows on the level ground, it was then the custom to go to the higher hills, often, to bring the Soma-creeper. This matter is mentioned in many places in the Ṛgveda.

original p. 390

Rik 2: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Aspaṣṭa" — spaśa bādhana-sparśanayoḥ — "has touched"; that is, "has begun."

"Kartvam" — karma, "work." Among the twenty-six words for "work" beginning with apaḥ and apnaḥ, the word kartvam is read (Ni. 3-2).

"Vṛṣṇiḥ" — कामानां वर्षिता अथवा वर्षिता (kāmānāṃ varṣitā athavā varṣitā) — "the showerer of desires, or the giver of rain." The word vṛṣṇi is used in many places in the Ṛgveda, in passages describing Indra's qualities.

"Ejati" — ejṛ kampane — the root ej, to tremble, to move. Here "moves" means "sets out from his own place to come to the sacrificer's side."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 390–391, noted briefly

सानोः (sānoḥ) — root ṣaṇu dāne ("to give"): sanoti dadāti nivasatām avakāśam iti sānuḥ ("that which gives room to those who dwell") — ñuṇ suffix by "dṛsanijanicaricaṭirahibhyo ñuṇ" (Uṇ. 1-3), after dṛ vidāraṇe, ṣaṇu dāne, jana janane, cara gatau, caṭa bhedane, raha tyāge; ṣ → s by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64), and with the ṣ gone the ṇ it caused goes too; "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. 7-2-116) gives the vṛddhi; the suffix is ñit, so initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). आरुहत् (āruhat) — root ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca with laṅ, third singular tip; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); since "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā 93-1), the laghūpadha-guṇa of "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86) does not apply; the i of tip is dropped by "itaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-100); the aṭ augment is udātta by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71), and being taught later (satiśiṣṭa) it alone stands; "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) would make the verb unaccented, but because yat ("when"), yadi, hanta, kuvit, neta, cet, caṇ, kaccit, yatra and other particles occur, the lowering is prohibited by "nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnetcetcaṇkaccidyatrayuktam" (Pā. 8-1-30); so the verb stays accented. भूरि (bhūri) — "adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin" (Uṇ. 4-505 [as printed]; the bhāṣya prints 4-65): after the roots ada bhakṣaṇe, śadḷ śātane, bhū sattāyām, śubha śumbha śobhārthe the suffix krin; kit, so by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) the guṇa of "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) does not apply; the suffix is nit, so initial-udātta. अस्पष्ट (aspaṣṭa) — root spaśa bādhana-sparśanayoḥ ("to touch"), anudātta-it by the marker iṅ-like; it is svarita-marked, so the ātmanepada by "svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale" (1-3-72, printed "sā. sū." [sic]); laṅ, third singular ta; śap dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); ś → ṣ by "vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājachaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) and ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41); the aṭ augment is udātta by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71) and its accent stands; the word yat carried over from the first half brings the prohibition of lowering by "nipātair yadyadi…" (Pā. 8-1-30). कर्त्वम् (kartvam) — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe with vic ("anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante," Pā. 3-2-75); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) with raparatva by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51); all the letters of vic drop, giving kar; in the sense karor bhāvaḥ ("the doing"), tva by "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (Pā. 5-1-119), giving kartvam. अर्थम् (artham) — root ṛ gatau with than ("uṣikuṣigārtibhyas than," printed "pā. sū. 2-161" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 2-4), after uṣa dāhe, kuṣa niṣkarṣe, gai śabde and ṛ gatau; guṇa and raparatva; initial-udātta (nit). यूथेन (yūthena) — "tithapṛṣṭhagūthayūthaprothāḥ" (printed "pā. sū. 2-169" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 2-12): an irregular formation with thak. वृष्णिः (vṛṣṇiḥ) — "sṛvṛṣibhyāṃ kit" (Uṇ. 4-486 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 4-49) after sṛ (to go) and vṛṣu secane, the suffix ni; kit, so no guṇa; final-udātta by the suffix. एजति (ejati) — root ejṛ kampane; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

Sūkta 10, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यु॒क्ष्वा हि के॒शिना॒ ह॒री वृष॑णा कक्ष्यप्रा । अथा॑ न इन्द्र सोमपा गि॒रामु॒प॑श्रुतिं चर ॥३॥

yukṣvā́ hi keśínā harī́ vṛ́ṣaṇā kakṣyaprā | áthā na indra somapā girā́m upaśrutiṃ cara ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युक्ष्व । हि । केशिना । हरी इति । वृषणा । कक्ष्यऽप्रा ॥ अथ । नः । इन्द्र । सोमऽपाः । गिराम् । उपऽश्रुतिम् । चर ॥३॥

yukṣva | hi | keśinā | harī iti | vṛṣaṇā | kakṣya-prā || atha | naḥ | indra | soma-pāḥ | girām | upa-śrutim | cara ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सोमपाः सोमपानयुक्तेन्द्र हरी त्वदीयावश्वौ युक्ष्वा हि । सर्वथा संयोजय । अथानन्तरं नो ऽस्मदीयानां गिरां स्तुतीनामुपश्रुतिं समीपे श्रवणमुद्दिश्य चर । तत्प्रदेशं गच्छ । कीदृशौ हरी । केशिना स्कन्धप्रदेशे लम्बमानकेशयुक्तौ वृषणा सेचनसमर्थौ युवानौ कक्ष्यप्रा । अश्वस्योदरबन्धनरज्जुः कक्ष्या तस्याः पूरकौ । पुष्टाङ्गावित्यर्थः ॥ युक्ष्व । श्नमो लोपश्छान्दसः । सति शिष्टत्वेन प्रत्ययस्वरः शिष्यते । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् । केशिना । प्रशस्ताः केशा अनयोः सन्तीति मत्वर्थीय इनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना द्विवचनस्याकारादेशः । वृषणा । पृषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तः । वा षपूर्वस्य निगमे । पा. ६-४-९ । इत्युपधायाः पक्षे दीर्घाभावः । पूर्ववदाकारः । कक्ष्यप्रा । कक्ष्ययोर्भवं कक्ष्यं सूत्रम् । तत्प्रातः पूरयतः पुष्टत्वादिति कक्ष्यप्रौ । प्रा पूरणे । आतो ऽनुपसर्गे कः । पा. ३-२-३ । इति कप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । आकारः पूर्ववत् । अथ । निपातस्येति संहितायां दीर्घः । नः । अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादावित्यनुवृत्तौ बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ । पा. ८-१-२१ । इति नसादेशो ऽनुदात्तः । इन्द्र सोमपा । उभावामन्त्रितस्य चेति सर्वानुदात्तौ । गिराम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिरिति विभक्तिरुदात्ता । उपशब्दो निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । श्रुतिशब्देन प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ । पा. ६-२-५० । इति तुवर्जिततादिपरत्वाद्गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः । चर । निघातः ॥

he somapāḥ somapānayuktendra harī tvadīyāvaśvau yukṣvā hi | sarvathā saṃyojaya | athānantaraṃ no 'smadīyānāṃ girāṃ stutīnāmupaśrutiṃ samīpe śravaṇamuddiśya cara | tatpradeśaṃ gaccha | kīdṛśau harī | keśinā skandhapradeśe lambamānakeśayuktau vṛṣaṇā secanasamarthau yuvānau kakṣyaprā | aśvasyodarabandhanarajjuḥ kakṣyā tasyāḥ pūrakau | puṣṭāṅgāvityarthaḥ || yukṣva | śnamo lopaśchāndasaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvena pratyayasvaraḥ śiṣyate | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam | keśinā | praśastāḥ keśā anayoḥ santīti matvarthīya iniḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | supāṃ sulugityādinā dvivacanasyākārādeśaḥ | vṛṣaṇā | pṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | ñnityādirnityamityādyudāttaḥ | vā ṣapūrvasya nigame | pā. 6-4-9 | ityupadhāyāḥ pakṣe dīrghābhāvaḥ | pūrvavadākāraḥ | kakṣyaprā | kakṣyayorbhavaṃ kakṣyaṃ sūtram | tatprātaḥ pūrayataḥ puṣṭatvāditi kakṣyaprau | prā pūraṇe | āto 'nupasarge kaḥ | pā. 3-2-3 | iti kapratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇāntodāttatvam | ākāraḥ pūrvavat | atha | nipātasyeti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | naḥ | anudāttaṃ sarvamapādādāvityanuvṛttau bahuvacanasya vasnasau | pā. 8-1-21 | iti nasādeśo 'nudāttaḥ | indra somapā | ubhāvāmantritasya ceti sarvānudāttau | girām | sāvekācastṛtīyādirvibhaktiriti vibhaktirudāttā | upaśabdo nipātatvādādyudāttaḥ | śrutiśabdena prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte tādau ca niti kṛtyatau | pā. 6-2-50 | iti tuvarjitatādiparatvādgateḥ prakṛtisvaraḥ | cara | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O somapāḥ — O Indra, drinker of Soma! Harī — your two horses (tvadīyāv aśvau) — yukṣvā hi: yoke [them] fully. Athā — thereafter — cara: go to the place, with a view to upaśruti — listening near at hand — of naḥ girām, our praises. What kind of two horses? Keśinā — having manes hanging down on the shoulder region; vṛṣaṇā — able to sprinkle (to rain), young; kakṣyaprā — kakṣyā is the rope that binds the horse's belly; they are prā, 'fillers' of it: that is, of well-nourished (full) bodies." (Grammar noted briefly: yukṣva — the loss of śnam is Vedic, the suffix accent stands, and the final is lengthened in the Saṃhitā ("dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ"); keśinā — "having handsome manes," with ini; vṛṣaṇā — root vṛṣu secane with kanin (Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta; optionally no lengthening (Pā. 6-4-9); dual in ā by "supāṃ suluk…"; kakṣyaprā — "those who fill the kakṣya (the girth-cord) because they are well fed," root prā pūraṇe with ka (Pā. 3-2-3), final-udātta by the second-member rule; athā — the particle lengthened in the Saṃhitā; naḥ — substitute nas for asmān/asmākam (Pā. 8-1-21), unaccented; indra, somapā — vocatives, both unaccented; girām — case-ending udātta; upaśrutim — the prefix upa is initial-udātta as a particle, and by "tādau ca niti kṛty atau" (Pā. 6-2-50) the prefix keeps its accent; cara *— unaccented.)

original p. 393

Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सोमपाः (somapāḥ) — O Indra who drink Soma (so absorbed in it) | केशिना (keśinā) — having manes (the long hair that grows upright on the neck) | वृषणा (vṛṣaṇā) — able to sprinkle, that is, in the prime of youth | कक्ष्यप्रा (kakṣyaprā) — with fully nourished bodies, such that the girth-rope tied about the belly is filled out | हरी (harī) — your two horses | युक्ष्व हि (yukṣva hi) — yoke [them to the chariot] | अथ (atha) — then | नः (naḥ) — our | गिराम् (girām) — of the words in the form of praise | उपश्रुतिम् (upaśrutim) — to hear them (for hearing) near at hand | चर (cara) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, absorbed in drinking Soma! Your horses have manes — long hair grown upright on the neck — are youthful, and have bodies so well nourished that the girth-rope tied about the belly is filled out. Yoke such horses to your chariot, and then come to us to hear, near at hand, our words of praise.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, drinker of soma, harness your pair of long-maned youthful and well-conditioned horses and then come to hear our praises.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Yukṣvā" — for the convenience of the meter the final vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha. The word means "join, yoke to the chariot."

"Keśinā" — स्कन्धप्रदेशे लम्बमानकेशयुक्तौ (skandha-pradeśe lambamāna-keśa-yuktau) — "furnished with manes hanging in the region of the shoulder": pralamba-keśarau, i.e., with manes grown up on the neck, long-maned.

"Vṛṣaṇā" — रेतःसेचनसमर्थौ (retaḥ-secana-samarthau) — "able to impregnate": that is, in the prime of life, in youth.

"Kakṣyaprā" — कक्ष्यप्रा अश्वस्योदरबन्धनरज्जुः कक्ष्या । तस्याः पूरकौ । पुष्टाङ्गावित्यर्थः (kakṣyaprā aśvasyodara-bandhana-rajjuḥ kakṣyā | tasyāḥ pūrakau | puṣṭāṅgāv ity arthaḥ) — "kakṣyā is the rope that binds the belly of the horse: the two are 'fillers' of it: well-nourished in body." Kakṣyā is the girth tied round the belly when a horse is yoked to a chariot; horses whose bellies have grown stout (filling out their girth) are meant.

"Somapāḥ" — सोमस्य पाता (somasya pātā), "drinker of Soma"; this is a vocative singular, an epithet of the word indra.

original p. 394

Rik 3: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Girām" — gīḥ is the genitive plural. The use of words like gīḥ, girām, gīrbhiḥ in the senses of hymns, praises and eulogies is customary in the Ṛgveda. So naḥ girām means "of the hymns that we make."

"Upaśrutim" — समीपे श्रवणमुद्दिश्य । श्रुतेः समीपम् (samīpe śravaṇam uddiśya | śruteḥ samīpam) — "with a view to hearing near at hand": for the sake of hearing, [coming] near, standing near to hear.

"Cara" — "come": be the one who comes.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 394–395, noted briefly

युक्ष्व (yukṣva) — root yujir yoge ("to join"), ubhayapadī, with loṭ ātmanepada middle-second singular thās; thās → se by "thāsaḥ se" (Pā. 3-4-80); "savābhyāṃ vāmau" (Pā. 3-4-91) replaces e by va; yuj + sva; the vikaraṇa śnam is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73) — the source notes that this sūtra prescribes luk for śap, but in Ṛ. Saṃ. Aṣṭaka 1, Sūkta 9, mantra 1 (the word matsi) the Bhāṣyakāra gives the same luk for śyan by this sūtra, so the luk of śnam may be said here too, by the word bahula; j → g by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30), g → k by "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55), and s → ṣ by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59), giving yukṣva; the suffix accent stands, being taught later (satiśiṣṭa); in the Saṃhitā the final is lengthened by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135). केशिना (keśinā) — "praśastāḥ keśā anayor santi": ini in the possessive sense by "ata iniṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the a of keśa dropped by "yasyeti ca" (6-4-148); suffix accent; the accusative dual ending au replaced by ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). वृषणा (vṛṣaṇā) — root pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane; kanin by "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 1-156); "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197) gives initial-udātta; "vā ṣapūrvasya nigame" (Pā. 6-4-9): the lengthening of the penultimate vowel before the sarvanāmasthāna suffix is optional after ṣ, and so does not arise here; the accusative dual ending → ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). कक्ष्यप्रा (kakṣyaprā) — kakṣyayor bhavaṃ kakṣyam (that which is in the kakṣyā): the girth; "that which fills it" — root prā pūraṇe with ka ("āto 'nupasarge kaḥ," Pā. 3-2-3); ā dropped before ka by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (printed "6-2-139" [as printed], the number of the next sūtra; usually 6-4-64); final-udātta by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); the dual ending as above. अथ (atha) — the particle is lengthened in the Saṃhitā (athā) by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136). नः (naḥ) — the rule "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21) with the carried-over "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. 8-1-18): nas replaces the plural genitive of asmad, unaccented, since the word is not at the beginning of the pāda. इन्द्र, सोमपाः (indra, somapāḥ) — both are vocatives, wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). गिराम् (girām) — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168) — the case-ending is udātta. उप (upa) — a nipāta, initial-udātta (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); with śruti it forms a prādi-compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the second member's accent, but by "tādau ca niti kṛty atau" (6-2-50) — before a kṛt suffix beginning with t (other than tu) the preceding gati keeps its own accent — upa retains its natural accent. चर (cara) — wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

॥३॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: the stroke in सचेन्द्र stands between चे and न्द्र; read as on चे — [accent ?].

Sūkta 10, Rik 4

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

एहि॒ स्तोमाँ॑ अ॒भि स्व॑रा॒भि गृ॑णी॒ह्या रु॑व । ब्रह्म॑ च नो वसो॒ सचे॑न्द्र य॒ज्ञं च॑ वर्धय ॥४॥ [accent ?]

ehi stómām̐ abhí svarābhí gṛṇīhy ā́ ruva | bráhma ca no vaso sácendra yajñáṃ ca vardhaya ||4|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । इहि । स्तोमान् । अभि । स्वर । अभि । गृणीहि । आ । रुव ॥ ब्रह्म । च । नः । वसो इति । सचा । इन्द्र । यज्ञम् । च । वर्धय ॥४॥

ā | ihi | stomān | abhi | svara | abhi | gṛṇīhi | ā | ruva || brahma | ca | naḥ | vaso iti | sacā | indra | yajñam | ca | vardhaya ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विशेषविनियोगस्तु यत्र श्रौतो न सूत्रितः । स्मार्तं तत्र विजानीयादृग्विधानादिसूत्रतः ॥ एहि स्तोमानित्येषा सूत्रे विशेषाकारेण न विनियुक्ता । साधारणविनियोगस्तु ब्रह्मयज्ञादौ सर्वत्रानुसंधेयः ॥

viśeṣaviniyogastu yatra śrauto na sūtritaḥ | smārtaṃ tatra vijānīyādṛgvidhānādisūtrataḥ || ehi stomānityeṣā sūtre viśeṣākāreṇa na viniyuktā | sādhāraṇaviniyogastu brahmayajñādau sarvatrānusaṃdheyaḥ ||

हे वसो निवासकारणभूतेन्द्र एहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । आगत्य च स्तोमानुद्गातृप्रयुक्तानि स्तोत्राण्यभि स्वर । अभिलक्ष्य प्रशंसारूपं शब्दं कुरु । तथाध्वर्युमभिलक्ष्य गृणीहि । शब्दं कुरु । तथा होतृप्रयुक्तानि शस्त्राण्यालक्ष्य रुव । शब्दं कुरु । परितोषेण सर्वानृत्विजः प्रशंसेत्यर्थः । तत ऊर्ध्वं नो ऽस्माकं ब्रह्म चान्नं च यज्ञं चानुष्ठीयमानं कर्म च सचा सह वर्धय । सांगत्वसंपादनेन यज्ञं वर्धयित्वा तत्फलमन्नं च प्रवृद्धं कुरु । अन्ध इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशत्यन्ननामसु ब्रह्म वर्ज इति पठितम् ॥ इहि । इण् गतौ । सेर्हिः । हेरपित्त्वेन ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । निघातः । आङा सह गुण एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । स्तोमान् । अर्तिस्तुसु इत्यादिना मन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । उत्तरपदेन संहितायां नकारस्य दीर्घादटि समानपादे इति रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्याकारस्यानुनासिकः । भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य यो ऽशीति यत्वम् । तस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः । तस्यासिद्धत्वात्स्वरसन्धिर्न भवति । अभि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तः । स्वर । स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः । निघातः । अभि । गतम् । गृणीहि । गॄ शब्दे । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हिः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । ई हल्यघोः । पा. ६-४-११३ । इतीत्त्वम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । पा. ७-३-८० । इत्यृकारस्य ऋकारः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ८-४-१-१ । इति णत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । रुव । रु शब्दे । सेर्ह्यपिच्च । शपि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन शः । तस्य ङित्त्वेन गुणाभावादुवङादेशः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । ब्रह्म । तृहि वृहि वृद्धौ । मनिन्नित्यनुवृत्तौ वृंहेरम् न लोपश्च । उ. ४-१४५ । इति मनिन् । तत्संनियोगेन नलोपः । अमागमश्च । मिदचो ऽन्त्यात्परः । पा. १-१-४७ । इत्यृकारात्परः । यणादेशः । मनिनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । वसो । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । यज्ञम् । यजयाचेत्यादिना । पा. ३-३-९० । नङ् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वर्धय । निघातः । अत्र चकारद्वयश्रवणादियमेव तिङ्विभक्तिः पूर्ववाक्ये ऽप्यनुषज्यते । अतो ऽनुषक्तैव प्रथमा न श्रुतेत्यश्रुतायाश्च वायोगे प्रथमा । पा. ८-१-५९ । इति निघातनिषेधो न भवति ॥

he vaso nivāsakāraṇabhūtendra ehi | asminkarmaṇyāgaccha | āgatya ca stomānudgātṛprayuktāni stotrāṇyabhi svara | abhilakṣya praśaṃsārūpaṃ śabdaṃ kuru | tathādhvaryumabhilakṣya gṛṇīhi | śabdaṃ kuru | tathā hotṛprayuktāni śastrāṇyālakṣya ruva | śabdaṃ kuru | paritoṣeṇa sarvānṛtvijaḥ praśaṃsetyarthaḥ | tata ūrdhvaṃ no 'smākaṃ brahma cānnaṃ ca yajñaṃ cānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ karma ca sacā saha vardhaya | sāṃgatvasaṃpādanena yajñaṃ vardhayitvā tatphalamannaṃ ca pravṛddhaṃ kuru | andha ityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatyannanāmasu brahma varja iti paṭhitam || ihi | iṇ gatau | serhiḥ | herapittvena ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nighātaḥ | āṅā saha guṇa ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | stomān | artistusu ityādinā man | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | uttarapadena saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya dīrghādaṭi samānapāde iti rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityākārasyānunāsikaḥ | bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śīti yatvam | tasya lopaḥ śākalyasyeti lopaḥ | tasyāsiddhatvātsvarasandhirna bhavati | abhi | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttaḥ | svara | svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ | nighātaḥ | abhi | gatam | gṛṇīhi | gṝ śabde | serhyapicceti hiḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | ī halyaghoḥ | pā. 6-4-113 | itīttvam | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | pā. 7-3-80 | ityṛkārasya ṛkāraḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyam | kā. 8-4-1-1 | iti ṇatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | ruva | ru śabde | serhyapicca | śapi prāpte vyatyayena śaḥ | tasya ṅittvena guṇābhāvāduvaṅādeśaḥ | ato heriti herluk | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | brahma | tṛhi vṛhi vṛddhau | maninnityanuvṛttau vṛṃheram na lopaśca | u. 4-145 | iti manin | tatsaṃniyogena nalopaḥ | amāgamaśca | midaco 'ntyātparaḥ | pā. 1-1-47 | ityṛkārātparaḥ | yaṇādeśaḥ | manino nittvādādyudāttatvam | vaso | āmantritanighātaḥ | yajñam | yajayācetyādinā | pā. 3-3-90 | naṅ | pratyayasvaraḥ | vardhaya | nighātaḥ | atra cakāradvayaśravaṇādiyameva tiṅvibhaktiḥ pūrvavākye 'pyanuṣajyate | ato 'nuṣaktaiva prathamā na śrutetyaśrutāyāśca vāyoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 | iti nighātaniṣedho na bhavati ||

Translation: "Where the special application has not been laid down in the Śrauta [texts], one is to know the Smārta one, from the Ṛgvidhāna and other texts. This rik ehi stomān has not been assigned a special application in the sūtra; its general application is to be understood everywhere, in the Brahmayajña and so on. O vaso — O Indra, the cause of dwelling: ehi — come to this rite. Having come, stomān abhi svara: make a sound of praise toward the stomas, the hymns sung by the udgātṛs. Likewise, gṛṇīhi: with the adhvaryu in view, make a sound. Likewise, ā ruva: with the śastras recited by the hotṛs in view, make a sound — praise all the priests with pleasure. After that, sacā — together — vardhaya: make grow naḥ brahma — our food — and the sacrifice, that is, the rite being performed. Having made the sacrifice grow by getting it completed with all its limbs, make its fruit — food — abundant. Among the twenty-eight words for food beginning with andhaḥ, brahma is read [the print reads "brahma varja"]." Grammar, noted briefly: ihi — root iṇ gatau with hi, which is ṅit-like, so no guṇa; with ā a single substitute udātta; stomān — suffix man ("artistusu…"), initial-udātta; in the Saṃhitā the final n becomes ru, the ā nasalised, the r → y and dropped ("lopaḥ śākalyasya"), without vowel sandhi; abhi — final-udātta; svara — root svṛ, lowered; gṛṇīhi — root gṝ śabde, śnā, ī by "ī halyaghoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-113), the root vowel shortened (Pā. 7-3-80), ṇ by the Kāśikā's addition to 8-4-1; ruva — root ru śabde, śa for śap by Vedic exchange, uvaṅ, loss of hi; brahma — root bṛhi vṛddhau with manin (Uṇ. 4-145), the n dropped and am inserted after the last vowel (Pā. 1-1-47), initial-udātta; vaso — vocative, lowered; yajñam — naṅ (Pā. 3-3-90); vardhaya — lowered; since ca is used twice, this verb is understood in the earlier clause as well, so the rule "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59) does not prevent the lowering. The first lines of the page finish Sāyaṇa's grammar, given in full with p. 396 above.

Rik 4: grammar close, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वसो (vaso) — O Indra, you who are excellent (or the cause of our dwelling-places) | (हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | एहि (ehi) — come (to this sacrificial ground that we perform) | स्तोमान् (stomān) — the hymns that the priests called udgātṛ, singers of the Sāman, recite, or sing | अभि स्वर (abhi svara) — listen with attention and give praise (that is, express approval) | अभि गृणीहि (abhi gṛṇīhi) — praise (the rites, that the adhvaryu performs) | आ रुव (ā ruva) — listen to the śastra mantras recited by the priests of the hotṛ group and signify your approval | then नः (naḥ) — to us | ब्रह्म च (brahma ca) — food too | यज्ञं च (yajñaṃ ca) — our sacrifice too | सचा (sacā) — being together (that is, being here) | वर्धय (vardhaya) — increase (that is, bring our sacrifice to completion, along with all its limbs, and bestow on us the food and the other foodstuffs that are its fruit).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are the cause of our dwellings — that is, it is you who give us the places where we live. Such as you are, O Indra, endowed with the quality of excellence! Come here, to the sacrifice we are performing; listen to the hymns sung with Sāmans by the priests called udgātṛ, to the adhvaryu, and to the śastra-mantras recited by the priests of the hotṛ group — to the hymns that each of them performs — and signify your approval of them by sound. Then grant that our sacrifice grows and is completed; and bestow upon us food and other nourishment.

॥ English Translation ॥

Come hither, O good Indra, applaud our prayers, praise them, receive them approvingly. O Indra, bless our sacrifice and bestow upon us abundant food.

original p. 398

Rik 4: Special Topics

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

On the matter of the special application of this rik, the Bhāṣyakāra, following the rule —

विशेषविनियोगस्तु यत्र श्रौतो न सूत्रितः । स्मार्तं तत्र विजानीयादृग्विधानादिसूत्रतः ॥ viśeṣa-viniyogas tu yatra śrauto na sūtritaḥ | smārtaṃ tatra vijānīyād ṛgvidhānādi-sūtrataḥ || "Where the special application [of a mantra] has not been laid down in the Śrauta [texts], one is to know the Smārta one from the Ṛgvidhāna and other texts."

— says that where the special application of a mantra is not stated in the Śrauta sūtras, in the performance of Smārta rites one must learn the application of that mantra from works such as the Ṛgvidhāna; and since no special application has been stated in the Śrauta sūtras for this rik ehi stomān, its general application in rites such as the Brahmayajña is to be understood.

In this rik there are three verbs, svara, gṛṇīhi, ruva: svara — root svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ; gṛṇīhi — root gṝ śabde; ruva — root ru śabde. Since these are given in the Dhātupāṭha, all three have the one meaning "make a sound." When one adds the prefix abhi — abhilakṣya — and renders it "make a sound of praise," that is, "praise, approve by sound (or by speech)," Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava likewise give this same sense; so it is this that should be accepted.

"Vaso" — nivāsakāraṇabhūtendra — "O Indra, the cause of dwelling-places": the Bhāṣyakāra's sense. Skandasvāmī: वसो । शतपथे वसिष्ठ इति वसुशब्दस्यातिशयितप्रत्ययान्तस्य "यद्वै नः श्रेष्ठस्तेन वसिष्ठः" इति प्रशस्यतमेन वचनेन श्रेष्ठशब्देनार्थविवरणदर्शनात् वसुशब्दः प्रशस्यनाम (vaso | śatapathe vasiṣṭha iti vasuśabdasyātiśayitapratyayāntasya "yadvai naḥ śreṣṭhastena vasiṣṭhaḥ" iti praśasyatamena vacanena śreṣṭhaśabdenārthavivaraṇadarśanāt vasuśabdaḥ praśasyanāma) — "vaso: since in the Śatapatha the word vasiṣṭha — vasu with the superlative suffix — is explained by the word śreṣṭha in the statement 'he is our best, therefore Vasiṣṭha', the word vasu is a name for 'excellent'": as stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa of the Śukla Yajurveda, vasu is explained as śreṣṭha ("best") and praśasya ("praiseworthy"). Or, since vasu also means wealth, the sense "O Indra, who are wealthy" may be given as well.

"Brahma" — andhaḥ — among the twenty-eight words for food beginning with vājaḥ, the word brahma is read (Ni. 3-9 as printed); so brahma means food. It is customary to call anything fit to be eaten "food." Besides, Yāska in the Nirukta says: अन्नं कस्मादानतं भूतेभ्यो ऽत्तेर्वा अभिमुख्येन ह्येतत् नतं प्रह्वीभूतं भवति भोजनाय भूतानाम् । अत्तेर्वा । … अद्यते ऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यत इति (annaṃ kasmādānataṃ bhūtebhyo 'ttervā abhimukhyena hyetat nataṃ prahvībhūtaṃ bhavati bhojanāya bhūtānām | attervā | … adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyata iti) the source breaks the quotation after atter vā with "having said", then continues — "Why is it anna (food)? It is ānata, bowed down towards beings, or from ad ('to eat'): for it is bent, humbled, before beings for their eating; or from ad: it is eaten and it eats beings; therefore it is called anna." Thus he gives the etymology of the word.

original p. 399

Rik 4: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Sacā" — "together" — sahitaḥ. In this rik no use of this word seems evident; the sense may be given: "being together, that is, directly (in person)."

"Vardhaya" — "increase; bring to completion; fulfil without obstacle." The usage of this root is special in the Ṛgveda. Besides the general sense "increase," it must be given a meaning according to context in many places. For example, in the sentence tvāṃ vardhantu no giraḥ the word vardhantu has the sense "let them praise." In this rik brahma ca vardhaya — "increase the food" — means "give us abundant food"; likewise yajñaṃ ca vardhaya — "increase the sacrifice" — means "grant that the sacrifice be completed without obstacle."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 399–401, noted briefly

एहि (ehi) — root iṇ gatau ("to go"), loṭ second singular sip; sip → hi by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); the śap vikaraṇa is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); hi is not pit, hence by "sārvadhātukam apit" (printed "1-6-4" [as printed], i.e. 1-2-4) it is ṅit, and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) prevents guṇa; "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) makes it unaccented; with the prefix ā, the guṇa arises as a single substitute and gives ehi; ā is a nipāta, hence udātta, and the single substitute e takes the udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). स्तोमान् (stomān) — root ṣṭuñ stutau with man ("arti-stu-su…," Uṇ. 1-142); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); accusative plural stomān. The Saṃhitā sandhi — with the following word: "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9): the n after a long vowel, when followed by an aṭ-letter in the same pāda, is replaced by ru; stomār + abhi: by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. 8-3-3) the long ā before that ru is always nasalized, giving stomā̐; "bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17): y replaces ru after bho, bhago, agho and a/ā before a voiced sound; then "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) drops the y; the source argues that by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1) the savarṇa-dīrgha of "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-101) does not apply (the y having been "unseen" — the elision of y is in the last three pādas and invisible to the earlier rule), so stomā̐ + abhi stays as two syllables. अभि (abhi) — final-udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ" (Phiṭ-sūtra 82). स्वर (svara) — root svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ, loṭ second singular with the ending dropped, unaccented. गृणीहि (gṛṇīhi) — root gṝ śabde, loṭ second singular sip; sip → hi by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); the vikaraṇa śnā by "kryādibhyaḥ śnā" (Pā. 3-1-81); "ī halyaghoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-113): the ā of śnā and of an abhyasta other than a ghu root becomes ī before a consonant-initial kit/ṅit ending, giving gṝ + nī + hi; "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80): before a śit suffix pūñ and the like shorten, so gṛ; ṇatva by "raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade" (Pā. 8-4-1) with the vārttika "raṣābhyāṃ ṇatve ṛkāragrahaṇam", which the Mahābhāṣya states as "ṛkārāc ceti vaktavyam"; where the vārttika is set aside, the Mahābhāṣya divides "chandasy avagrahāt" (Pā. 8-4-26) into "ṛtaḥ" and "chandasy avagrahāt", the first part giving ṇ after ṛ: gṛṇīhi; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). रुव (ruva) — root ru śabde, loṭ second singular sip, → hi by "seryapicca" (adādi class, hence the vikaraṇa śap is dropped by "ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; the source notes that, by Vedic inversion, a śa-type vikaraṇa arises here instead) continues on p. 400.

original pp. 400–401

Rik 4 grammar closes

Grammar page, noted briefly. रुव (ruva) — ru śabde (adādi), loṭ second singular sip, sip → hi by "seryapicca". The adādi vikaraṇa śap ought to be dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); here instead, by Vedic inversion, the vikaraṇa śa arises, which by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) is ṅit, so no guṇa; the u of ru takes uvaṅ by "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77), giving ruv + a + hi; hi is dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. 6-4-105), so ruva; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). ब्रह्म (brahma) — root bṛha vṛddhau ("to grow"), an idit root, so num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (printed "6-1-58" [as printed], i.e. 7-1-58), giving bṛnh; then manin (carried from "sarvadhātubhyo manin") by "bṛṃher am nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 3-585 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 4-145), with the augment am and loss of the n of num; the am goes after the last vowel by "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ" (Pā. 1-1-47); some read the Uṇādi sūtra as "bṛṃher no 'c ca" (Uṇ. 4-585 [as printed]), the n becoming a; the ṛ → r by "iko yaṇ aci" (6-1-77, printed "jā. sū." [sic]), giving brahman; manin is nit, so initial-udātta. वसो (vaso) — a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). यज्ञम् (yajñam) — naṅ by "yajayācayatavicchapracharakṣo naṅ" (Pā. 3-3-90) after yaj; j + n → jñ by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-40). वर्धय (vardhaya) — a finite verb, unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28); but since in this mantra two ca's are heard (brahma ca vardhaya, yajñaṃ ca vardhaya), the verb is connected with the earlier clause too — so that the vardhaya of the earlier clause is the first finite verb of the joined sentence, and the rule "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59) prevents the lowering of the first verb in a sentence joined by ca and vā; hence no lowering applies where the first-uttered verb is concerned.

अभिप्लवषडहगतोक्थ्येष्वच्छावाकस्य तृतीयसवन उक्थमिन्द्राय शंस्यमित्यनुरूपस्तृचः । एह्यूष्विति खण्ड इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नुक्थमिन्द्राय शंस्यम् । आ. ७-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ इन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं वर्धनं Translation: "In the ukthya [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, in the Acchāvāka's third pressing, the triplet beginning uktham indrāya śaṃsyam is the anurūpa. In the section ehy ū ṣu it is laid down: 'indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan, uktham indrāya śaṃsyam' (Āśvalāyana 7-8). Indrāya — for Indra's sake — vardhanam — the means of increase — uktham, the śastra — is śaṃsyam, to be recited by us. For what kind of Indra? Puruniṣṣidhe — for him who bars many enemies. Śakraḥ — Indra — yathā — in whatever manner — rāraṇat would, in the highest degree, make a sound [of approval] regarding naḥ, our suteṣu (sons) and sakhyeṣu (friendships) — so [the śastra] is to be recited: this is the connection with what precedes. The sense is: Indra, pleased with our śastra, praises our sons and our friends in many ways." Grammar, noted briefly: uktham — from vac with thak (Uṇ. 2-2); śaṃsyam — root śaṃsu stutau with yat, initial-udātta; vardhanam — lyuṭ in the instrumental sense (Pā. 3-3-117), the syllable before the suffix udātta; puruniṣṣidhe — root ṣidha gatyām with kvip after nis (Pā. 2-2-18), the ṣ by Pā. 8-3-65 and 8-4-41, compounded with puru as its object, the root accent standing; śakraḥ — with rak (Uṇ. 2-13); yathā — thāl (Pā. 5-3-23); suteṣu — with kta; ṇaḥ — the ṇ in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 8-4-27; rāraṇat — root raṇa with yaṅ (Pā. 3-1-22) dropped (Pā. 2-4-74), doubling, lengthening (Pā. 7-4-83), the leṭ in the sense of liṅ (Pā. 3-4-7, 3-3-156), not lowered after yathā (Pā. 8-1-36); sakhyeṣu — "the acts of a friend", suffix ya (Pā. 5-1-126), the i dropped (Pā. 6-4-148).
