Rik 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र त्वां विद्म । जानीमः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । वृषन्तमं कामानामतिशयेन वर्षितारं वाजेषु संग्रामेषु हवनश्रुतमस्मदीयस्याह्वानस्य श्रोतारम् । वृषन्तममस्यातिशयेन कामादीनां वर्षितुस्तवोतिं रक्षामस्मद्विषयामुद्दिश्य हूमहे । त्वामाह्वयामः । कीदृशीमूतिम् । सहस्रसातमामतिशयेन धनसहस्राणां दात्रीम् ॥ विद्म । विदो लटो वा । पा. ३-४-८३ । इति मसो मादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । वृषन्तमम् । पृषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तमपः पित्त्वात्स एव शिष्यते । अयस्मयादीनि छन्दसि । पा. १-४-२० । इति भत्वेन पदत्वाभावान्नलोपाभावः । पा. ८-२-७ । वाजेषु । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । हवनश्रुतम् । हू इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति ल्युटि संप्रसारणम् । हवनं शृणोतीति क्विप् । तुगागमः । वृषन्तमस्य । उक्तम् । हूमहे । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । शप इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । ऊतिम् । ऊतियूतीत्यादिनान्तोदात्तो निपातितः । सहस्रसातमाम् । सहस्रं सनोतीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । पा. ३-२-६७ । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् । पा. ६-४-४१ । इत्याकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । तमपः पित्त्वात्स एव शिष्यते ॥

he indra tvāṃ vidma | jānīmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | vṛṣantamaṃ kāmānāmatiśayena varṣitāraṃ vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu havanaśrutamasmadīyasyāhvānasya śrotāram | vṛṣantamamasyātiśayena kāmādīnāṃ varṣitustavotiṃ rakṣāmasmadviṣayāmuddiśya hūmahe | tvāmāhvayāmaḥ | kīdṛśīmūtim | sahasrasātamāmatiśayena dhanasahasrāṇāṃ dātrīm || vidma | vido laṭo vā | pā. 3-4-83 | iti maso mādeśaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | vṛṣantamam | pṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | tamapaḥ pittvātsa eva śiṣyate | ayasmayādīni chandasi | pā. 1-4-20 | iti bhatvena padatvābhāvānnalopābhāvaḥ | pā. 8-2-7 | vājeṣu | vājaśabdo vṛṣādirādyudāttaḥ | havanaśrutam | hū ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti lyuṭi saṃprasāraṇam | havanaṃ śṛṇotīti kvip | tugāgamaḥ | vṛṣantamasya | uktam | hūmahe | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | śapa ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | ūtim | ūtiyūtītyādināntodātto nipātitaḥ | sahasrasātamām | sahasraṃ sanotīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | pā. 3-2-67 | viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt | pā. 6-4-41 | ityākārādeśaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | tamapaḥ pittvātsa eva śiṣyate ||

Translation: "O Indra! Tvāṃ vidma — we know you. What kind? Vṛṣantamam — the one who rains desires to the utmost; vājeṣu — in battles; havanaśrutam — the one who hears our invocation. For the protection (ūtim) of you, the vṛṣantama — the supreme showerer of desires and the like — directed at us, hūmahe: we call you. What kind of protection? Sahasrasātamām — that which, to the utmost, gives thousands of riches." The grammar of vidma, vṛṣantamam, havanaśrutam, hūmahe, ūtim, sahasrasātamām follows in the Sanskrit and is noted briefly: vidma — the substitute ma for mas in the laṭ of vid (Pā. 3-4-83), with the Saṃhitā lengthening; vṛṣantamam — root vṛṣu secane with kanin (Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta, then tamap (unaccented since pit); no loss of n because in the Veda the stem has bha status and so is not a pada; havanaśrutam — the lyuṭ from root hve with saṃprasāraṇa, then kvip with tuk; hūmahe — with saṃprasāraṇa, and the loss of śap by bahulaṃ chandasi; ūtim — final-udātta by the irregular formation "ūtiyūti…"; sahasrasātamām — root ṣaṇu dāne with viṭ, the ā for the nasal, the second-member accent, and tamap unaccented as pit.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | वृषन्तमम् (vṛṣantamam) — (as the bestower of desired things) the giver of rain | वाजेषु (vājeṣu) — in battles | हवनश्रुतम् (havanaśrutam) — one who hears our invocation (our cry for help) | विद्म (vidma) — we know | हि (hi) — indeed | वृषन्तमस्य (vṛṣantamasya) — of you, who rain down desires | सहस्रसातमाम् (sahasrasātamām) — which gives in thousands of ways | ऊतिम् (ūtim) — protection (or, for our protection) | हूमहे (hūmahe) — we call (we pray for).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! We know you as the giver of desired things and as one who hears our call in battles. Therefore, for your manifold protection, you who are the giver of rain in the form of desired things, we call upon you.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, we know you, the rainer of blessings, the hearer of our call in battles; we invoke the thousand-fold protection of you, the showerer of bounties.

original pp. 437–438

Rik 10: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is easy to understand. There are no special difficulties, and no words that need supplying.

"Vidma" — the final syllable is lengthened for the convenience of the meter in the Saṃhitā.

"Vṛṣantamam," "vṛṣantamasya" — vṛṣṭi-prada, "bestower of rain"; that is, the one who gives us the rain in the form of desired ends.

"Havanaśrutam" — one who hears our invocation, who attends to our cry.

"Sahasrasātamām" — the explanation of this word was already given earlier (see "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-9" as printed [?]; the word was explained at Sūkta 9, Ṛk 8).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 437–438, noted briefly

विद्म (vidma) — root vida jñāne ("to know") with laṭ; in the parasmaipada the first-person plural mas; śap is dropped by luk ("adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," Pā. 2-4-72); "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83): for the nine parasmaipada endings of laṭ after vid the substitutes ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, ma are optionally given, so mas → ma, giving vidma; the Saṃhitā lengthening by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135), vidmā. वृषन्तमम् (vṛṣantamam) — root pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane; kanin by "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 1-156); the k and n of kanin are lost as it, leaving vṛṣ + an → vṛṣan; initial-udātta since nit; then tamap in the sense of excess, unaccented since pit (so the initial-udātta stands); by "ayasmayādīni chandasi" (Pā. 1-4-20) the bha status prevents the pada status, so the n is not dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7). वा (vā) — vāja is a vṛṣādi word, so initial-udātta. हवनश्रुतम् (havanaśrutam) — root hveñ with lyuṭ; lyuṭ → ana; hve + ana: by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34), with "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. 6-1-32) carried over, the saṃprasāraṇa of hve — hu — arises; with pūrvarūpa, guṇa and av, havana; "havanaṃ śṛṇoti iti": kvip after the root śru with havana as upapada; by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. 6-1-71), tuk, giving havanaśrut; the accusative singular am gives havanaśrutam. वृषन्तमस्य (vṛṣantamasya) — the derivation of vṛṣantama was given earlier in this mantra; genitive singular. हूमहे (hūmahe) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ ātmanepada first plural mahiṅ; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79 [?], printed digits unclear) gives e; śap, which is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); "bahulaṃ chandasi" (printed "6-4-34" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-34) carries saṃprasāraṇa; then pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca"; "halaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-2) lengthens the saṃprasāraṇa at the end of an aṅga after a consonant: hūmahe. ऊतिम् (ūtim) — "ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-97): these ktin words are irregularly udātta on the end. सहस्रसातमाम् (sahasrasātamām) — "sahasraṃ sanoti iti sahasrasāḥ": root ṣaṇu dāne; ṣ → s (Pā. 6-1-64), ṇ → n; viṭ after jana, sana, khana, krama, gama in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67); the nasal replaced by ā before viṭ and van (Pā. 6-4-41); savarṇa-dīrgha, sahasrasā; second-member accent; tamap is pit, so unaccented; sahasrasā keeps the accent of the earlier formation; being feminine, tamā + ṭāp ("ajādyataṣṭāp," no number printed); ṭāp is pit; savarṇa-dīrgha (by "antaratamaḥ" the ā in place of the two) is unaccented; accusative singular am, pūrvarūpa by "ami pūrvaḥ" (printed "8-1-23" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-107): sahasrasātamām.

॥१०॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: a stroke over स of सहस्र followed by a bar under ह, as printed — [accent ?].

original p. 439

Sūkta 10, Rik 11

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ तू न॑ इन्द्र कौशिक मन्दसा॒नः सु॒तं पि॑ब । न॒व्यमायुः॒ प्र सू ति॑र कृ॒धी स॑ह॒स्रसामृ॑षिम् ॥११॥ [accent ?]

ā tū́ na indra kauśika mandasānáḥ sutáṃ piba | navyám āyuḥ prá sū́ tira kṛdhī́ sahasrásā́m ṛṣim ||11|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । कौशिक । मन्दसानः । सुतम् । पिब ॥ नव्यम् । आयुः । प्र । सु । तिर । कृधि । सहस्रऽसाम् । ऋषिम् ॥११॥

ā | tu | naḥ | indra | kauśika | mandasānaḥ | sutam | piba || navyam | āyuḥ | pra | su | tira | kṛdhi | sahasra-sām | ṛṣim ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र तु क्षिप्रं नो ऽस्मान्प्रत्या गच्छेति शेषः । हे कौशिक कुशिकस्य पुत्रेन्द्र मन्दसानो हृष्यो भूत्वा सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिब । यद्यपि विश्वामित्रः कुशिकस्य पुत्रस्तथापि तद्रूपेणेन्द्रस्यैवोत्पन्नत्वात्कुशिकपुत्रत्वमविरुद्धम् । अयं वृत्तान्तो ऽनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तः । कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छन्ब्रह्मचर्यं चकार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे । अनु. ऋग्वे. ३-१ । इति । हे इन्द्र नव्यं सर्वैर्देवैः स्तुत्यं कर्मानुष्ठानपरमायुर्जीवितं प्र सू तिर । प्रकर्षेण सुष्ठु वर्धय । ततो मां सहस्रसां सहस्रसंख्याकलाभोपेतमृषिमतीन्द्रियद्रष्टारं कृधि । कुरु ॥ तु । संहितायामृचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणामिति दीर्घः । नः । संहितायामुदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः । इन्द्र । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । कौशिक । निघातः । मन्दसानः । हृष्यन् । मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकान्तिगतिषु । आसानजित्यनुवृत्तौ वञ्जिवृधिमन्दिसहिभ्यः कित् । उ. २-८६ । इत्यसानच्प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । सुतम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । नव्यम् । णु स्तुतौ । अचो यत् । गुणः । वान्तो यि प्रत्यये । पा. ६-१-७९ । इत्यवादेशः । यतो ऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । आयुः । उसिनिदित्यनुवृत्तावेतेर्णिच्च । उ. २-११९ । इत्युसिप्रत्ययः । णित्त्वाद्वृद्ध्यायादेशौ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सु । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् । तिर । तरतेर्व्यत्ययेन शः । ऋत इद्धातोः । पा. ७-१-१०० । इतीत्त्वम् । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । कृधि । डुकृञ् करणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसीति हेर्धिरादेशः । सहस्रसाम् । उक्तम् । ऋषिम् । ऋषी गतौ । इन्नित्यनुवृत्तावि गुपधात्कित् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

he indra tu kṣipraṃ no 'smānpratyā gaccheti śeṣaḥ | he kauśika kuśikasya putrendra mandasāno hṛṣyo bhūtvā sutamabhiṣutaṃ somaṃ piba | yadyapi viśvāmitraḥ kuśikasya putrastathāpi tadrūpeṇendrasyaivotpannatvātkuśikaputratvamaviruddham | ayaṃ vṛttānto 'nukramaṇikāyāmuktaḥ | kuśikastvaiṣīrathirindratulyaṃ putramicchanbrahmacaryaṃ cakāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe | anu. ṛgve. 3-1 | iti | he indra navyaṃ sarvairdevaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaparamāyurjīvitaṃ pra sū tira | prakarṣeṇa suṣṭhu vardhaya | tato māṃ sahasrasāṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākalābhopetamṛṣimatīndriyadraṣṭāraṃ kṛdhi | kuru || tu | saṃhitāyāmṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇāmiti dīrghaḥ | naḥ | saṃhitāyāmudāttādanudāttasya svaritaḥ | indra | āmantritanighātaḥ | kauśika | nighātaḥ | mandasānaḥ | hṛṣyan | madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu | āsānajityanuvṛttau vañjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit | u. 2-86 | ityasānacpratyayaḥ | cittvādantodāttaḥ | sutam | pratyayasvaraḥ | navyam | ṇu stutau | aco yat | guṇaḥ | vānto yi pratyaye | pā. 6-1-79 | ityavādeśaḥ | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | āyuḥ | usinidityanuvṛttāveterṇicca | u. 2-119 | ityusipratyayaḥ | ṇittvādvṛddhyāyādeśau | nittvādādyudāttatvam | su | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam | tira | taratervyatyayena śaḥ | ṛta iddhātoḥ | pā. 7-1-100 | itīttvam | ato heriti herluk | kṛdhi | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaśchandasīti herdhirādeśaḥ | sahasrasām | uktam | ṛṣim | ṛṣī gatau | innityanuvṛttāvi gupadhātkit | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "O Indra, tu — quickly — come to us (this is to be supplied). O kauśika — O Indra, son of Kuśika — mandasānaḥ — being glad — sutam piba: drink the pressed Soma. Although Viśvāmitra is the son of Kuśika, yet since Indra himself was born in that form, his being Kuśika's son is not contradictory. This story is told in the Anukramaṇikā: 'Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing for a son equal to Indra, practised celibacy; Indra himself was born to him as his son Gāthin' (Anu. Ṛgve. 3-1). O Indra, navyam āyuḥ pra sū tira: increase greatly and well [our] āyuḥ, life, navyam — praiseworthy by all the gods, devoted to the performance of rites. Then kṛdhi — make — me sahasrasām — endowed with gains reckoned in thousands — a ṛṣi, a seer of what is beyond the senses." Grammar, noted briefly: tū — lengthened in the Saṃhitā; naḥ — svarita after an udātta in the Saṃhitā; indra, kauśika — vocatives, lowered; mandasānaḥ — root madi with asānac (Uṇ. 2-86), final-udātta; navyam — root ṇu stutau with yat, av before y (Pā. 6-1-79), initial-udātta; āyuḥ — from iṇ with usi (Uṇ. 2-119), vṛddhi and āy, initial-udātta; sū — lengthened as a particle; tira — root tṝ with śa by Vedic exchange, i (Pā. 7-1-100), loss of hi; kṛdhi — śap dropped, hi → dhi; ṛṣim — root ṛṣī gatau with in, kit, initial-udātta.

original p. 440

Rik 11: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | तु (tu) — quickly | नः (naḥ) — our (to our side) | आ (gaccha) — come | (हे) कौशिक ((he) kauśika) — O Indra, son of Kuśika | you मन्दसानः (mandasānaḥ) — being glad | सुतम् (sutam) — the Soma-juice, pressed and prepared | पिब (piba) — drink | नव्यम् (navyam) — [which is] requested (that is, desired) | आयुः (āyuḥ) — life | प्र सु तिर (pra su tira) — increase specially (for me) | सहस्रसाम् (sahasrasām) — [one who is] winning thousands of gains | ऋषिम् (ṛṣim) — a seer | कृधि (kṛdhi) — make (me).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! Come quickly to us, and drink with delight this Soma-juice that we have pressed. Increase our life, and make me, an ordinary person, one who gains thousands of benefits.

॥ English Translation ॥

Come quickly, Indra, son of Kusika, and drink the soma libation with delight; prolong the life which we merit and make me a Rishi abnndantly [sic] endowed with thousands of benefits.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Tu," "su," "kṛdhi" — the final syllables of these words in this rik are lengthened for the convenience of the meter.

"Ā" — in this rik only the prefix ā occurs; with it the verb gaccha ("come") has to be supplied. Such usages are needed in the Ṛgveda.

"Kauśika" — here Indra is addressed as the son of Kuśika. In this connection the Bhāṣyakāra cites an account from the Anukramaṇikā:

कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छन् ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे ॥ (ऋ. अनु. ३-१) kuśikas tv aiṣīrathir indra-tulyaṃ putram icchan brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe || (ṛ. anu. 3-1) "Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born as his son, Gāthin."

Skandasvāmī, on this subject:

अत्र चेतिहासमाचक्षते । इषीरथपुत्रः कुशिको नाम राजा पुत्रमिन्द्रतुल्यं कामयमानो ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्य गाथी नामेन्द्र एव स्वयं पुत्रो जात इति ॥ atra cetihāsam ācakṣate | iṣīrathaputraḥ kuśiko nāma rājā putram indra-tulyaṃ kāmayamāno brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasya gāthī nāmendra eva svayaṃ putro jāta iti || "Here they tell a legend: a king named Kuśika, son of Iṣīratha, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born to him as a son named Gāthin."

original p. 441

Rik 11: Special Topics (continued)

Veṅkaṭamādhava:

पुत्रमिन्द्रसमम् इच्छन् कुशिको ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्रः स्वयमेव पुत्रो ऽभूत् । सास्य कौशिकता ॥ putram indra-samam icchan kuśiko brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendraḥ svayam eva putro 'bhūt | sāsya kauśikatā || "Desiring a son equal to Indra, Kuśika practised celibate austerity; Indra himself became his son. That is his Kauśika-hood."

The chief point is this: in ancient times a king named Iṣīratha had a son called Kuśika. He, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity. Then Indra himself was born as his son, under the name Gāthin. The sage Viśvāmitra was the son of King Gāthin; and since Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this rik, was born in the family of Viśvāmitra, he addresses Indra, born in his own family — that is, in the family of Kuśika — as "Kauśika."

"Navyam" — the Bhāṣyakāra says that the word navya is another form of the root ṇu stutau, and explains it as sarvair devaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaparam — "that is to be praised by all gods, devoted to the performance of rites," or, as the Kannada gloss gives it, "that is wanted by all, even the gods": that is, long life, as everyone naturally desires to live long. Or, as Skandasvāmī says, if the word navyam is given the sense "new" (navam — fresh), then the sense would be: a new vitality for the words navyam āyuḥ — or, to bring out the underlying idea, a still greater lifespan henceforth. In sum: "make us live long; increase our life — prolong our life" [the source's own English].

"Sahasrasām" — thousands of gains, benefits, or many kinds of desired things.

"Ṛṣim" — the root ṛṣī gatau ("to go") has the senses of motion and knowledge; so ṛṣi means one who knows, one endowed with wisdom, or — as the Bhāṣyakāra says — अतीन्द्रियद्रष्टारम् (atīndriyadraṣṭāram): a great person with the power to know things beyond the reach of the outer senses. Here "ṛṣi" means Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this mantra. When he prays to Indra, "give me long life and make me an excellent seer," he does not use a first-person verb but a third-person usage.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 441–443, noted briefly

तु (tu) — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "ṛcitunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. 6-3-133); a nipāta, initial-udātta ("nipātā ādyudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 80). The grammar continues on p. 442.

original pp. 442–443

Rik 11 grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 442–443, noted briefly

नः (naḥ) — nas replaces asmān by "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21); unaccented as a substitute; in the Saṃhitā it becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66) after an udātta. इन्द्र (indra), कौशिक (kauśika) — vocatives, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). मन्दसानः (mandasānaḥ) — hṛṣyan ("rejoicing"); root madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu; by "ṛñjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. 2-244 [as printed]), with asānac carried over from "chandasy asānac chujyābhyām" (Uṇ. 2-243 [as printed]), the suffix asānac, kit, comes after ṛji bharjane, vṛdhu vṛddhau, madi stuti… and ṣaha marṣaṇe; the source remarks that the Bālamanoramā reads the roots there as ṛji gatau and madī harṣe, but ṛji gatau is not found in the Dhātupāṭha (only ṛja gatau), and madī harṣe is not idit and so takes no num; so "mandi" in the sūtra would not fit, and the reading may be due to a copyist's or proof-reader's slip; the suffix is cit, so final-udātta ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163). सुतम् (sutam) — kta-ending; the suffix accent. नव्यम् (navyam) — root ṇu stutau; ṇ → n ("ṇo naḥ," Pā. 6-1-65); yat after a vowel-ending root ("aco yat," printed "3-1-96" [as printed], i.e. 3-1-97), nu + ya; since ya is an ārdhadhātuka, guṇa ("sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ"), u → o; then "vānto yi pratyaye" (Pā. 6-1-79): before a y-initial suffix o and au become av and āv, so no → nav; navya; "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-213) gives initial-udātta; accusative singular navyam. आयुः (āyuḥ) — by "eter ṇic ca" (Uṇ. 2-283 [?] as printed), with usi carried over from "janer usiḥ" (Uṇ. 2-286 [as printed]) and nit from "artipṛvapiyajitanidhanitapibhyo nit" (Uṇ. 2-284 [as printed]), the suffix usi comes after iṇ gatau, being both ṇit and nit; i + us: vṛddhi by "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. 7-2-115) — i → ai; then ai → āy ("eco 'yavāyāvaḥ," Pā. 6-1-78), āyus; ru and visarga, āyuḥ; initial-udātta, "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). सु (su) — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136). तिर (tira) — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ (bhvādi); loṭ second singular sip; sip → hi by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); śap should arise but by Vedic inversion the vikaraṇa śa arises, which is apit and so ṅit-like; hence "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) and no guṇa by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100): i in place of the ṛ, the final, by "alo 'ntyasya" (Pā. 1-1-52); then "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51): tir; hi is dropped after a stem ending in a ("ato heḥ," Pā. 6-4-105); tira. कृधि (kṛdhi) — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe, loṭ, sip, hi; the śap is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); hi → dhi by "śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi" (6-4-102). सहस्रसाम् (sahasrasām) — explained in the earlier mantra (Rik 10). ऋषिम् (ṛṣim) — root ṛṣī gatau; by "igupadhāt kit" (Uṇ. 4-559 [as printed]) with in carried from "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. 4-557 [as printed]), the suffix in, kit, after a root with ik in the penultimate position, so ṛṣ + in; the suffix is kit, so no guṇa; nit, so initial-udātta ("ñnityādir nityam," Pā. 6-1-197); the accusative singular am with pūrvarūpa gives ṛṣim.

pari | tvā | girvaṇaḥ | giraḥ | imāḥ | bhavantu | viśvataḥ || vṛddha-āyum | anu | vṛddhayaḥ | juṣṭāḥ | bhavantu | juṣṭayaḥ ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रवर्ग्ये परि त्वेत्यभिष्टुयात् । स्पृष्ट्वोदकमिति खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिरो ऽधि द्वयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वचः । आ. ४-६ । इति सूत्रितम् । तथा हविर्धानप्रवर्तने सेयं परिधानीया । हविर्धाने प्रवर्तयन्तीति खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इति परिदध्यात् । आ. ४-९ । इति सूत्रितम् । तथा ब्राह्मणं च । परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । ऐ. ब्रा. १-२९ । इति ॥

pravargye pari tvetyabhiṣṭuyāt | spṛṣṭvodakamiti khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇo giro 'dhi dvayoradadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ | ā. 4-6 | iti sūtritam | tathā havirdhānapravartane seyaṃ paridhānīyā | havirdhāne pravartayantīti khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇo gira iti paridadhyāt | ā. 4-9 | iti sūtritam | tathā brāhmaṇaṃ ca | pari tvā girvaṇo gira ityuttamayā paridadhāti | ai. brā. 1-29 | iti ||

हे गिर्वणो ऽस्मदीयस्तुतिभागिन्द्र विश्वतः सर्वेषु कर्मसु प्रयुज्यमाना इमा गिरो ऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतयस्त्वां परि भवन्तु । सर्वतः प्राप्नुवन्तु । कीदृश्यो गिरः । वृद्धायुमनु प्रवृद्धेनायुष्येणोपेतं त्वामनुसृत्य वृद्धयो वर्धमानाः । किंचैता गिरो जुष्टास्त्वया सेविताः सत्यो जुष्टयो ऽस्माकं प्रीतिहेतवो भवन्तु ॥ गिर्वणः । गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । गिर उपधाया दीर्घाभावश्छान्दसः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । विश्वतः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । वृद्धायुम् । वृधु वृद्धौ । क्तप्रत्ययः । उदितो वा । पा. ७-२-५६ । इतीटः क्त्वाप्रत्यये विकल्पितत्वाद्यस्य विभाषा । पा. ७-२-१५ । इति निष्ठायामिडभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । इण् गतौ । छन्दसीणः । उ. १-२ । इत्युण् । णित्त्वाद्वृद्धिः । आयादेशश्च । वृद्धमायुर्यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वृद्धयः । वृधेः क्तिनि तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च । पा. ७-२-९ । इतीडभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । जुष्टाः । श्वीदितो निष्ठायाम् । पा. ७-२-१४ । इतीडभावः । जुष्टार्पिते चेत्यनुवृत्तौ नित्यं मन्त्रे । पा. ६-१-२१० । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । जुष्टयः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । क्तिन् । तितुत्रेतीडभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥ २० ॥

he girvaṇo 'smadīyastutibhāgindra viśvataḥ sarveṣu karmasu prayujyamānā imā giro 'smadīyāḥ stutayastvāṃ pari bhavantu | sarvataḥ prāpnuvantu | kīdṛśyo giraḥ | vṛddhāyumanu pravṛddhenāyuṣyeṇopetaṃ tvāmanusṛtya vṛddhayo vardhamānāḥ | kiṃcaitā giro juṣṭāstvayā sevitāḥ satyo juṣṭayo 'smākaṃ prītihetavo bhavantu || girvaṇaḥ | gīrbhirvanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | gira upadhāyā dīrghābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | viśvataḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | vṛddhāyum | vṛdhu vṛddhau | ktapratyayaḥ | udito vā | pā. 7-2-56 | itīṭaḥ ktvāpratyaye vikalpitatvādyasya vibhāṣā | pā. 7-2-15 | iti niṣṭhāyāmiḍabhāvaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | iṇ gatau | chandasīṇaḥ | u. 1-2 | ityuṇ | ṇittvādvṛddhiḥ | āyādeśaśca | vṛddhamāyuryasya | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vṛddhayaḥ | vṛdheḥ ktini titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca | pā. 7-2-9 | itīḍabhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | juṣṭāḥ | śvīdito niṣṭhāyām | pā. 7-2-14 | itīḍabhāvaḥ | juṣṭārpite cetyanuvṛttau nityaṃ mantre | pā. 6-1-210 | ityādyudāttatvam | juṣṭayaḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | ktin | titutretīḍabhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ || 20 ||

Translation: "In the pravargya one should praise with pari tvā: in the section beginning spṛṣṭvodakam it is laid down, 'pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ, adhi dvayor adadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ' (Āśvalāyana 4-6). Likewise, in the moving forward of the havirdhāna carts this [ṛk] is the closing verse: in the section havirdhāne pravartayanti it is laid down, 'one should close with pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ' (Āśvalāyana 4-9). And the Brāhmaṇa too: 'he closes with the last [ṛk], pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ' (Ai. Brā. 1-29). O girvaṇaḥ — O Indra, sharer in our praises — imāḥ giraḥ, these our praises, used viśvataḥ, in all rites, tvāṃ pari bhavantu: may they reach you on all sides. What kind of praises? Vṛddhāyum anu — following you, who are endowed with grown life; vṛddhayaḥ — growing. And further: may these praises, juṣṭāḥ — enjoyed by you — become juṣṭayaḥ, the causes of our delight." Grammar, noted briefly: girvaṇaḥ — "he who is served with praises", root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau with asun, no lengthening of gir as a Vedic form, lowered as a vocative; viśvataḥ — the syllable before the suffix udātta; vṛddhāyum — vṛddha from vṛdhu with kta, no iṭ (Pā. 7-2-56, 7-2-15); āyu from iṇ with uṇ (Uṇ. 1-2); a bahuvrīhi with the first-member accent; vṛddhayaḥ — ktin, no iṭ (Pā. 7-2-9), initial-udātta; juṣṭāḥ — no iṭ (Pā. 7-2-14), initial-udātta by "nityaṃ mantre" (Pā. 6-1-210); juṣṭayaḥ — root juṣī with ktin, initial-udātta. The bhāṣya closes "॥ २० ॥", the twentieth varga.

original p. 445

Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) गिर्वणः ((he) girvaṇaḥ) — O Indra, worthy of being praised by us | विश्वतः (viśvataḥ) — in all (that is, in all the rites in which we make use of them) | इमाः गिरः (imāḥ giraḥ) — these words in the form of praise | त्वा (tvā) — you | परि भवन्तु (pari bhavantu) — may they come from every side and join (you) | वृद्धायुम् (vṛddhāyum) — you who have long life | अनु (anu) — following | वृद्धयः (vṛddhayaḥ) — growing | जुष्टाः (juṣṭāḥ) — [the words] served (accepted) by you | जुष्टयः (juṣṭayaḥ) — [may they be] the means of giving us delight | भवन्तु (bhavantu) — may they be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, lover of praise! May these words of praise that we make come to you from every side and bring you delight. As these words give you delight, may your life-span (your strength) increase; and as these words of ours bring you delight, may they bring delight to us as well.

॥ English Translation ॥

O deserver of praise, may these our praises be on all occasions around you (accepted by you); may they increase your power, O long-lived, and being agreeable to you, may they become our enjoyments.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is very involved (difficult); the intention does not fit together properly, and what the seer means is not clearly known.

"Girvaṇaḥ" — गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ । अस्मदीयस्तुतिभाक् (gīrbhir vanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | asmadīya-stuti-bhāk) — "one who is served with praises; the root vana/ṣaṇa in the sense of sharing: one who partakes of our praise": that is, one who is worshipped with our words, who is praised, who is worthy of praise.

"Viśvataḥ" — in all places, or on all occasions.

"Vṛddhāyum" — प्रवृद्धेनायुष्येणोपेतम् (pravṛddhenāyuṣyeṇopetam) — "endowed with increased lifespan": endowed with a life that is great or growing, one who lives for a long time. Skandasvāmī explains this word as vṛddhān śatrūn atigantāram — "one who overcomes enemies that have grown great," one who subdues enemies.

"Anu" — anusṛtya, prāpya — "following," "reaching": that is, may the hymns we make reach you; may you hear them.

original p. 446

Rik 12: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Vṛddhayaḥ" — vardhamānāḥ — growing; much, specially, flourishing, abundant.

"Juṣṭāḥ," "juṣṭayaḥ" — the root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ has the senses "to be fond of" and "to serve"; so these words mean "that which gives delight, that which is an object of delight."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 446–447, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

गिर्वणः (girvaṇaḥ) — "gīrbhir vanyate iti girvaṇāḥ": root gṝ śabde (kryādi) with kvip ("kvip ca," Pā. 3-2-76); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100) gives i in place of ṛ, which, as an alo 'ntyasya substitute, comes at the end; root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau with asun ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-638 [?] [as printed]); gir + bhis + vanas receive the technical name prātipadika, and by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) bhis is dropped; by pratyaya-lakṣaṇa gir counts as a pada; so "vor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-76): the penultimate ik of a stem ending in r or v is lengthened at the end of a pada, which would lengthen the i of gir; but "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (Paribhāṣā 35) makes this optional, so it does not arise; the vocative singular su is added to girvaṇas, the su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68); ru and visarga: girvaṇaḥ; a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). विश्वतः (viśvataḥ) — from tasil, which is l-marked, so the vowel before it is udātta ("liti," Pā. 6-1-193). वृद्धायुम् (vṛddhāyum) — root vṛdhu vṛddhau with kta; vṛdh + ta; vṛdh is udit, so by "udito vā" (Pā. 7-2-56) the iṭ augment before ktvā is optional (the print then discusses whether kta too takes iṭ, citing "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. 7-2-15): a suffix beginning kt-/ktavat does not take iṭ after a root to which iṭ is optional); so the iṭ that "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35) would give is barred; vṛdh + ta → by "jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-40) t → dh after a jhaṣ; then dh + dh → ddh by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" (Pā. 8-4-53): vṛddha; the root iṇ gatau, with uṇ in the Veda ("chandasīṇaḥ," Uṇ. 1-2), uṇ being ṇit, so vṛddhi ("aco ñṇiti," Pā. 7-2-115) gives ai + u, then "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78) gives āy + u → āyu; vṛddham āyur yasya saḥ: vṛddhāyuḥ, a bahuvrīhi, with the first member's accent ("bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam," Pā. 6-2-1); accusative singular vṛddhāyum. वृद्धयः (vṛddhayaḥ) — ktin ("striyāṃ ktin," Pā. 3-3-94) after vṛdh; the iṭ augment does not arise by "ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka, seṣu ca" (Pā. 7-2-9); th → dh and j-type changes as before: vṛddhi; initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-17 [as printed]); nominative plural vṛddhayaḥ. जुष्टाः (juṣṭāḥ) — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, idit; kta; "śvīditaḥ niṣṭhāyām" (Pā. 7-2-14): after śvi and idit roots, niṣṭhā does not take iṭ, so kta has no augment; the suffix accent would arise but is set aside by "nityaṃ mantre" (Pā. 6-1-210), and juṣṭa and arpita are, by the previous sūtra's carried-over words "juṣṭārpite ca chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-209), always initial-udātta in the mantra. जुष्टयः (juṣṭayaḥ) — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, ktin; the augment iṭ barred by "ti-tu-tra…." (Pā. 7-2-9); "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) turns t → ṭ: juṣṭi; initial-udātta by the nit accent; nominative plural juṣṭayaḥ.

॥१२॥

Close of Sūkta 10

॥ इति दशमं सूक्तं समाप्तम् ॥ iti daśamaṃ sūktaṃ samāptam | "Thus the tenth sūkta is completed."

Kannada colophon: ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಥಮಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಮುಗಿದುದು । "Here the tenth sūkta in the first maṇḍala is concluded."

original p. 448

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ ಹನ್ನೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 11 — "indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan" ("The Eleventh Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

इन्द्रं विश्वा इत्यष्टर्चस्य सूक्तस्य मधुच्छन्दसः पुत्रो जेतैनामक ऋषिः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । इन्द्रमष्टौ जेता माधुच्छन्दस इति । छन्दस्त्वानुष्टुभमिति पूर्वसूत्रोक्तम् । इन्द्रो देवतानुवर्तते ॥ विनियोगस्तु । महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये कृत्स्नसूक्तं शंसनीयम् । ऊरू इति खण्डे शौनकेन सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधनित्यानुष्टुभं तस्य प्रथमायाः पूर्वमर्धर्चं शस्त्वोत्तरेणार्धर्चेनोत्तरस्याः पूर्वमर्धर्चं व्यतिषजति पाद्यैः पादाननुष्टुप्कारं प्रागुत्तमायाः । ऐ. आ. ५-३-१ । इति । ब्राह्मणं च प्रथमारण्यके पश्यते [?] प्र वो मह इति खण्डे । इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्निति पदानुषङ्गः । ऐ. आ. १-५-२ । इति । तथा पृष्ठ्यस्य पञ्चमे ऽहनि निष्केवल्ये शस्त्र इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नित्यनुरूपस्तृचः । स्तोमो वर्धमान इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । उप नो हरिभिः सुतमिन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन् । आ. ७-१२ [?] । इति ॥

indraṃ viśvā ityaṣṭarcasya sūktasya madhucchandasaḥ putro jetaināmaka ṛṣiḥ | tathā cānukrāntam | indramaṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasa iti | chandastvānuṣṭubhamiti pūrvasūtroktam | indro devatānuvartate || viniyogastu | mahāvrate niṣkevalye kṛtsnasūktaṃ śaṃsanīyam | ūrū iti khaṇḍe śaunakena sūtritam | indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhanityānuṣṭubhaṃ tasya prathamāyāḥ pūrvamardharcaṃ śastvottareṇārdharcenottarasyāḥ pūrvamardharcaṃ vyatiṣajati pādyaiḥ pādānanuṣṭupkāraṃ prāguttamāyāḥ | ai. ā. 5-3-1 | iti | brāhmaṇaṃ ca prathamāraṇyake paśyate [?] pra vo maha iti khaṇḍe | indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhanniti padānuṣaṅgaḥ | ai. ā. 1-5-2 | iti | tathā pṛṣṭhyasya pañcame 'hani niṣkevalye śastra indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhannityanurūpastṛcaḥ | stomo vardhamāna iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | upa no haribhiḥ sutamindraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan | ā. 7-12 [?] | iti ||

Translation: "The ṛṣi of the eight-rik sūkta beginning indraṃ viśvā is Jetā, son of Madhucchandas. So the Anukramaṇī says: 'indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasaḥ' — indram [is the sūkta of] eight [riks; see the note below], seer Jetā, son of Madhucchandas. That the meter is Anuṣṭubh was stated in the preceding sūtra. The deity, Indra, continues. Its application: in the Mahāvrata, in the niṣkevalya [śastra], the whole sūkta is to be recited; Śaunaka lays this down in the section ūrū: 'indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan — Anuṣṭubh; having recited the first half of its first rik, with the second half he interweaves the first half of the next, making Anuṣṭubhs of the pādas pāda by pāda, up to the last [rik]' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 5-3-1, as printed). And the Brāhmaṇa, in the first Āraṇyaka, in the section paśyate [?] pra vo maha: 'the words indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan are to be appended' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1-5-2). Again, on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya rite, in the niṣkevalya śastra, the triplet indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan is the anurūpa: in the section stomo vardhamānaḥ it is laid down: 'upa no haribhiḥ sutam; indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan' (Āśvalāyana 7-12 [?])." The printed reference reads "ā 7-12"; its first digit could be 6 or 7. The Anuvāda below gives the first Āraṇyaka reference as "ai. ha. 5-2-1" [sic], against "5-3-1" in the Sanskrit.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The ṛṣi of the sūkta indraṃ viśvā is Jetā, son of the sage Madhucchandas. The Anukramaṇikā too says "indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasaḥ" — that is, "of the [eight] riks indraṃ viśvā, the ṛṣi is Jetā, son of Madhucchandas." The meter, Anuṣṭubh, was stated earlier. The deity is Indra. Application: in the sacrifice called Mahāvrata, when reciting the mantras of the niṣkevalya-śastra, this whole sūkta is to be recited; Śaunaka says so in the section ūrū of the Śrauta-sūtra, and the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (5-2-1 [as printed]) gives the order of application of this sūkta, and the Brāhmaṇa-portion that explains it is in the same Āraṇyaka (1-5-2) in the section pra vo mahe. And on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya sacrifice, when reciting the niṣkevalya-śastra, the three riks beginning indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan are to be used for the stomāvāpa; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra says so in the sūtra upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 11, Rik 1

॥ Sūkta — 11 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 3 ॥ Sūkta — 11 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 21 ॥ a single numeral, clearly printed; the earlier headings gave two numerals each ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 8 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Jetā Mādhucchandasa ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Anuṣṭubh ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रं॒ विश्वा॑ अवीवृधन्त्समु॒द्रव्य॑चसं॒ गिरः । र॒थीत॑मं॒ र॒थीनां॒ वाजा॑नां॒ सत्प॑तिं॒ पतिं॑ ॥१॥

indraṃ víśvā avīvṛdhant samudrávyacasaṃ gíraḥ | rathī́tamaṃ rathī́nāṃ vā́jānāṃ sátpatiṃ pátiṃ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रम् । विश्वाः । अवीवृधन् । समुद्रऽव्यचसम् । गिरः ॥ रथिऽतमम् । रथीनाम् । वाजानाम् । सत्ऽपतिम् । पतिम् ॥१॥

indram | viśvāḥ | avīvṛdhan | samudra-vyacasam | giraḥ || rathi-tamam | rathīnām | vājānām | sat-patim | patim ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विश्वाः सर्वा गिरो ऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतय इन्द्रमवीवृधन् । वर्धितवत्यः । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । समुद्रव्यचसं समुद्रवद्व्याप्तवन्तं रथीनां रथयुक्तानां योद्धॄणां मध्ये रथीतमम् अतिशयेन रथयुक्तं वाजानामन्नानां पतिं स्वामिनं सत्पतिं सतां सन्मार्गवर्तिनां पालकम् ॥ विश्वाः । विशेः क्वन् । नित्स्वरः । अवीवृधन् । वृधेर्णिचि चङ्युपधाया ऋदित्यनुवृत्तौ नित्यं छन्दसि । पा. ७-४-८ । इत्यृकारस्य ऋकारविधानाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । निघातस्वरः । समुद्रव्यचसम् । व्यचेरसुन् । गाङ्कुटादिभ्यो ऽञ्णिन्ङित् । पा. १-२-१ । इति प्राप्तस्य ङित्त्वस्य व्यचेः कुटादित्वमनसि । पा. १-२-१-१ । इत्यसि निषेधाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना ङिति विधीयमानं संप्रसारणम् । पा. ६-१-१६ । न भवति । समुद्रव्यच इव व्यचो यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । रथीतमं रथीनाम् । रथशब्दादुत्पन्नस्येनश्छान्दसं दीर्घत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वं च । वाजानाम् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सत्पतिम् । पत्यावैश्वर्ये । पा. ६-२-१८ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

viśvāḥ sarvā giro 'smadīyāḥ stutaya indramavīvṛdhan | vardhitavatyaḥ | kīdṛśamindram | samudravyacasaṃ samudravadvyāptavantaṃ rathīnāṃ rathayuktānāṃ yoddhṝṇāṃ madhye rathītamam atiśayena rathayuktaṃ vājānāmannānāṃ patiṃ svāminaṃ satpatiṃ satāṃ sanmārgavartināṃ pālakam || viśvāḥ | viśeḥ kvan | nitsvaraḥ | avīvṛdhan | vṛdherṇici caṅyupadhāyā ṛdityanuvṛttau nityaṃ chandasi | pā. 7-4-8 | ityṛkārasya ṛkāravidhānāllaghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | nighātasvaraḥ | samudravyacasam | vyacerasun | gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñṇinṅit | pā. 1-2-1 | iti prāptasya ṅittvasya vyaceḥ kuṭāditvamanasi | pā. 1-2-1-1 | ityasi niṣedhādgrahijyetyādinā ṅiti vidhīyamānaṃ saṃprasāraṇam | pā. 6-1-16 | na bhavati | samudravyaca iva vyaco yasya | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | rathītamaṃ rathīnām | rathaśabdādutpannasyenaśchāndasaṃ dīrghatvam | pratyayasvareṇodāttatvaṃ ca | vājānām | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvam | satpatim | patyāvaiśvarye | pā. 6-2-18 | iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "All (viśvāḥ) our praises (giraḥ) have magnified (avīvṛdhan) Indra. What kind of Indra? Samudravyacasam — pervading like the ocean; rathītamam — among rathīs, warriors who fight from chariots, the one most endowed with chariots; vājānām patim — lord of foods; satpatim — protector of the good, of those who follow the right path." Note: (The grammatical tail, which runs onto p. 450: viśvāḥ from viś with kvan, nit accent; avīvṛdhan, the causative caṅ-aorist of vṛdh, where "nityaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 7-4-8) gives ṛ for the penultimate, so there is no guṇa; unaccented (nighāta); samudravyacasam from vyac with asun: the ṅit-status that "gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit" (Pā. 1-2-1) would give is barred before as by the vārttika "vyaceḥ kuṭāditvam anasi" (printed "1-2-1-1"), so the samprasāraṇa of "grahi-jyā…" (Pā. 6-1-16) does not arise; the bahuvrīhi "samudravyaca iva [sic] vyaco yasya" keeps the first member's accent; rathītamam, rathīnām: the Vedic lengthening of in after ratha, with the suffix accent; vājānām initial-udātta as one of the vṛṣādi words; satpatim: "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18) keeps the first member's accent.)

original p. 450

Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

विश्वाः (viśvāḥ) — all | गिरः (giraḥ) — the words in the form of praise that we make | समुद्रव्यचसम् (samudravyacasam) — pervading like the ocean | रथीनाम् (rathīnām) — among the warriors who fight from chariots (in battle) | रथीतमम् (rathītamam) — [the one] exceedingly endowed with a chariot | वाजानाम् (vājānām) — of food and other nourishment | पतिम् (patim) — the lord | सत्पतिम् (satpatim) — the protector of good people | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | अवीवृधन् (avīvṛdhan) — have made [him] grow, that is, have praised.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra pervades everything as the ocean does; among warriors who fight seated in chariots he is by far the best; he is the lord of foods and other nourishment; he is the protector of the good. All the words of praise that we utter praise such an Indra.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

All our praises have glorified Indra who is as great as the ocean, who is the best chariateer [sic] of all charioteers, the lord of food, the protector of the virtuous.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Avīvṛdhan" — the root vṛdh is generally used in the Ṛgveda in the sense of "praise" (stuti). In this rik, giraḥ indraṃ avīvṛdhan means "our words praise Indra, extol him."

"Samudravyacasam" — "pervading like the ocean." This comparison is not exactly apt, for the ocean does not pervade everywhere. But since the ocean is very wide and unfathomable, the seer may have given the ocean comparison with just this idea in mind.

original p. 451

Rik 1: Special Topics (continued) and grammar begins

"Rathītamam," "rathīnām" — such doubled expressions are numerous in the Ṛgveda: vasor indraṃ vasupatim; somapā somapītaye; and many other examples can be given. These words mean "excellent among charioteers."

"Satpatim" — सतां पतिं पालकम् (satāṃ patiṃ pālakam) — "the protector, the guardian, of the good": that is the sense.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 451–452, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

विश्वाः (viśvāḥ) — root viśa praveśane; kvan by "aśūpruṣi-laṭi-kaṇi-khaṭi-viśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. 1-149): viśva; initial-udātta by the nit accent. अवीवृधन् (avīvṛdhan) — root vṛdhu vardhane with ṇic; from the ṇic-ending root, luṅ; third plural jhi; jh → ant by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); the i dropped by "itaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-100), then loss of the final of the cluster: an; cli by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43), replaced by caṅ by "ṇi-śri-dru-srubhyaḥ kartari caṅ" (Pā. 3-1-48); doubling by "caṅi" (Pā. 6-1-11); "ur at" gives a (with r) for the ṛ of the reduplicate; "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-60) removes the dh and r there; guṇa of the penultimate ṛ would arise by "puganta-laghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86), but "nityaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 7-4-8) with "ur ṛt" (printed "7-47") carried over always gives ṛ in the Veda, so no guṇa; "sanval laghuni caṅpare 'naglope" (Pā. 7-4-93) treats it like san, so "sanyataḥ" (Pā. 7-4-79) gives i for the reduplicate's a, lengthened by "dīrgho laghoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-94); the augment aṭ by "luṅ-laṅ-lṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71); ṇi dropped by "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. 6-4-51); pararūpa by "ato guṇe": avīvṛdhan; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). समुद्रव्यचसम् (samudravyacasam) — root vyaca vyājīkaraṇe; asun by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. 4-638 [?]); "vyaceḥ kuṭāditvam anasi" (Kā. vā. 1-2-1-1) —

original p. 452

Rik 1 grammar (continued)

[samudravyacasam, continued:] vyac is kuṭādi except before as, so here it is not, and "gāṅ-kuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit" (Pā. 1-2-1) does not make the suffix ṅit; hence the samprasāraṇa of "grahi-jyā-vayi-vyadhi-vaṣṭi-vicati-vṛścati-pṛcchati-bhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca" (Pā. 6-1-16) does not arise; the bahuvrīhi "samudrasya vyaca iva vyacaḥ yasya saḥ" keeps the first member's accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1). रथीतमम् (rathītamam) — "rathaḥ asya asti iti rathī": ini by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the a of ratha dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); "atiśayitaḥ rathī": tamap by "atiśāyane tamab-iṣṭhanau" (Pā. 5-3-55); rathin + su + tama, su dropped; pada status by pratyaya-lakṣaṇa, so the n is dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7); Vedic lengthening of the i: rathītama; accusative singular rathītamam; tamap, being pit, is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. 3-1-4), and the word is udātta on in by the suffix accent. रथीनाम् (rathīnām) — genitive plural ām after rathin, Vedic lengthening of the i; udātta on in by the suffix accent; ām, being sup, unaccented, then svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66). वाजानाम् (vājānām) — initial-udātta as one of the vṛṣādi words, "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (printed "pā. rū." [sic] 6-1-203). सत्पतिम् (satpatim) — "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18): before pati in the sense of lordship the first member keeps its own accent; sat from as bhuvi with laṭ → śatṛ; the śap dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (no number printed); the root's a dropped by "śnasor allopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-111): sat, final-udātta by the suffix accent; "satāṃ patiḥ satpatiḥ," a genitive tatpuruṣa.

Sūkta 11, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

स॒ख्ये त॑ इन्द्र वा॒जिनो॒ मा भे॑म शवसस्पते । त्वाम॒भि प्र णो॑नुमो॒ जेता॑र॒मप॑राजितम् ॥२॥

sakhyé ta indra vājíno mā́ bhema śavasas pate | tvām abhí prá ṇonumo jétāram áparājitam ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सख्ये । ते । इन्द्र । वाजिनः । मा । भेम । शवसः । पते ॥ त्वाम् । अभि । प्र । नोनुमः । जेतारम् । अपराऽजितम् ॥२॥

sakhye | te | indra | vājinaḥ | mā | bhema | śavasaḥ | pate || tvām | abhi | pra | nonumaḥ | jetāram | aparā-jitam ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पालकेन्द्र ते तव सख्ये ऽनुग्रहप्रयुक्ते सखित्वे वर्तमाना वयं वाजिनो ऽन्नवन्तो भूत्वा मा भेम । शत्रुभ्यो भीतिं प्राप्ता मा भूम । अतस्त्वामुभयहेतुमभि प्र णोनुमः । सर्वतः प्रकर्षेण स्तुमः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । जेतारं युद्धेषु जयशीलम् अपराजितं क्वापि पराजयरहितम् ॥ सख्ये । सख्युः कर्म सख्यम् । सख्युर्यः । पा. ५-१-१२६ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वाजिनः । वाजो ऽन्नमेषामस्तीति वाजिनः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । भेम । ञिभी भये । लुङुत्तमबहुवचनं मस् । नित्यं ङितः । पा. ३-४-९९ । इति सलोपः । बहुलं छन्दसीति च्लेर्लुक् । छन्दस्युभयथेति तिङ आर्धधातुकत्वेन ङित्त्वाभावाद्गुणः । न माङ्योगे । पा. ६-४-७४ । इत्यडागमप्रतिषेधः । शवसस्पते । शवसः षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रपृष्ठपारपदपयस्पोषेषु । पा. ८-३-५३ । इति विसर्जनीयस्य संहितायां सत्वम् । सुबामन्त्रितपराङ्गवद्भावेन । पा. २-१-२ । पदद्वयनिघातः । नोनुमः । णु स्तुतौ । णो नः । पा. ६-१-६५ । इति नत्वम् । यङो लुक् । प्रत्ययलक्षणेन सन्यङोरिति द्विर्भावः । गुणो यङ्लुकोः । पा. ७-४-८२ । इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणः । प्रत्ययलक्षणेन धातुसंज्ञायां लटो मस् । अदादिवद्भावाच्छपो लुक् । उपसर्गादसमासे ऽपि णोपदेशस्य । पा. ८-४-१४ । इति संहितायां णत्वम् । जेतारम् । जि जये । ताच्छील्यादिषु तृन् । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् । पा. ६-१-१९७ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । अपराजितम् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन नञ उदात्तत्वम् ॥

he śavasaspate balasya pālakendra te tava sakhye 'nugrahaprayukte sakhitve vartamānā vayaṃ vājino 'nnavanto bhūtvā mā bhema | śatrubhyo bhītiṃ prāptā mā bhūma | atastvāmubhayahetumabhi pra ṇonumaḥ | sarvataḥ prakarṣeṇa stumaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | jetāraṃ yuddheṣu jayaśīlam aparājitaṃ kvāpi parājayarahitam || sakhye | sakhyuḥ karma sakhyam | sakhyuryaḥ | pā. 5-1-126 | pratyayasvaraḥ | vājinaḥ | vājo 'nnameṣāmastīti vājinaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | bhema | ñibhī bhaye | luṅuttamabahuvacanaṃ mas | nityaṃ ṅitaḥ | pā. 3-4-99 | iti salopaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti clerluk | chandasyubhayatheti tiṅa ārdhadhātukatvena ṅittvābhāvādguṇaḥ | na māṅyoge | pā. 6-4-74 | ityaḍāgamapratiṣedhaḥ | śavasaspate | śavasaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayaspoṣeṣu | pā. 8-3-53 | iti visarjanīyasya saṃhitāyāṃ satvam | subāmantritaparāṅgavadbhāvena | pā. 2-1-2 | padadvayanighātaḥ | nonumaḥ | ṇu stutau | ṇo naḥ | pā. 6-1-65 | iti natvam | yaṅo luk | pratyayalakṣaṇena sanyaṅoriti dvirbhāvaḥ | guṇo yaṅlukoḥ | pā. 7-4-82 | ityabhyāsasya guṇaḥ | pratyayalakṣaṇena dhātusaṃjñāyāṃ laṭo mas | adādivadbhāvācchapo luk | upasargādasamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya | pā. 8-4-14 | iti saṃhitāyāṃ ṇatvam | jetāram | ji jaye | tācchīlyādiṣu tṛn | ñnityādirnityam | pā. 6-1-197 | ityādyudāttatvam | aparājitam | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvena naña udāttatvam ||

Translation: "O śavasaspate, O Indra, protector of strength! We, abiding in your sakhya — friendship, born of your grace — being vājinaḥ, possessed of food, mā bhema: let us not be afraid; let us not be overcome by fear of enemies. Therefore tvām, the cause of both, abhi pra ṇonumaḥ: we praise everywhere and exceedingly. What kind of you? Jetāram — victorious in battles; aparājitam — never defeated anywhere." (Grammatical tail: sakhyam "the act of a friend" with ya by "sakhyur yaḥ" (Pā. 5-1-126), suffix accent; vājinaḥ "those who have food," suffix accent; bhema: ñibhī bhaye, luṅ first plural mas, its s dropped by "nityaṃ ṅitaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-99), the cli dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi", and since "chandasy ubhayathā" makes the ending ārdhadhātuka, it is not ṅit, so guṇa; the augment aṭ barred by "na māṅyoge" (Pā. 6-4-74); śavasaspate: the visarga becomes s in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 8-3-53, and both words lose their accent, the genitive being treated as part of the vocative (Pā. 2-1-2); nonumaḥ: ṇu stutau, n by "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. 6-1-65), yaṅ-luk, doubling, guṇa of the reduplicate by "guṇo yaṅlukoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-82), laṭ mas, śap dropped as in the adādi class, and ṇ in the Saṃhitā after pra by Pā. 8-4-14; jetāram: ji jaye with tṛn in the sense of habit, initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197); aparājitam: nañ udātta as the indeclinable first member.)

original p. 454

Rik 2: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) शवसस्पते ((he) śavasaspate) — O Indra, lord of strength and capacity (that is, O one of great strength) | ते (te) — your | सख्ये (sakhye) — in friendship that is joined with favour (we who abide) | वाजिनः (vājinaḥ) — being possessed of food and other nourishment | मा भेम (mā bhema) — we do not fear (enemies); for that very reason | जेतारम् (jetāram) — who conquers in battles | अपराजितम् (aparājitam) — never defeated | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | अभि प्र णोनुमः (abhi pra ṇonumaḥ) — we praise in all places, specially.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! You are the lord of strength and capacity — that is, of great might. Because we are in friendship with you, we do not lack food and other nourishment, and so we need not fear enemies on any account. And you are ever victorious in battle; there is no such thing as defeat for you. We praise you, such as you are, specially.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, lord of strength, supported by your friendship, we have no fear but glorify you the conqueror and the unoonquered [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Sakhye" — अनुग्राहकयुक्ते सखित्वे (anugrāhaka-yukte sakhitve) — "in friendship joined with favour": the state of friendship that is accompanied by [your] graciousness — your protection. Since you are in friendship with us, we have no fear of enemies; there is no lack of food and the like; you are the one who is victorious in battle and never defeated; so we praise you. That is the chief idea. In this rik there are no difficult words and no strained connections of meaning.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 454–456, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

सख्ये (sakhye) — after sakhi, the suffix yat in the sense of "act" by "sakhyur yaḥ" (Pā. 5-1-126); the i dropped by "yasyeti ca"; the suffix accent puts the udātta on ya. वाजिनः (vājinaḥ) — vāja means food; "vājo 'eṣām asti": ini by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the a dropped; the suffix accent. The grammar continues on p. 455.

original p. 455

Rik 2 grammar continued (to the top of p. 456)

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar page, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

भेम (bhema) — root ñibhī bhaye; luṅ, in its place the first-person plural mas; the s dropped by "nityaṃ ṅitaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-99); the cli that arises by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43) is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); the tiṅ ending ma gets the name ārdhadhātuka by "chandasy ubhayathā", so it does not become ṅit by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4), and "kṅiti ca" gives no bar to guṇa; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84): bhema; with mā (māṅ), "na māṅyoge" (Pā. 6-4-74) bars the augment aṭ. शवसस्पते (śavasaspate) — śavas ends in s; genitive singular "jas" [sic, for ṅas]: śavas + as = śavasas; ru and visarga: śavasaḥ, followed by pati; so in the Saṃhitā "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ pati-putra-pṛṣṭha-pāra-pada-payas-poṣeṣu" (printed "8-4-53"; the bhāṣya gives 8-3-53) makes the genitive visarga s before pati and the rest: śavasaspate; pate is a vocative, and the śavasaḥ before it becomes like a part of it by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. 2-1-2), so by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19) both words are unaccented. णोनुमः (ṇonumaḥ) — root ṇu stutau; ṇ → n by "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. 6-1-65); yaṅ by "dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ" (Pā. 3-1-22), dropped by "yaṅo 'ci ca" (Pā. 2-4-74) but still counted by pratyaya-lakṣaṇa, so doubling by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-9): nunu; guṇa of the reduplicate's i/u by "guṇo yaṅlukoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-82): nonu; as a yaṅ-ending it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32); laṭ parasmaipada first plural mas; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); by "carkarītaṃ parasmaipadam adādivac ca draṣṭavyam" it is treated as adādi (carkarīta means the yaṅluk form), so the śap is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); ru and visarga: nonumaḥ; after the upasarga pra, "upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya" (Pā. 8-4-14) gives ṇ for the n of a ṇopadeśa root after an upasarga with r, compound or not. [p. 456] The print explains upadeśa as the first utterance of Pāṇini, Patañjali and Vararuci, and a ṇopadeśa root as one that has ṇ in that first utterance. जेतारम् (jetāram) — root ji jaye; tṛn by Pā. 3-2-135 in the senses "having that habit," "having that nature," "doing it well"; guṇa by Pā. 7-3-84: jetṛ; initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197), the suffix being n-marked; accusative singular am: "ṛto ṅi-sarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110) gives guṇa a with r by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51): jetar + am; "ap-tṛn-tṛc-svasṛ-naptṛ-neṣṭṛ-tvaṣṭṛ-kṣattṛ-hotṛ-potṛ-praśāstṝṇām" (Pā. 6-4-11) lengthens the penultimate before a sarvanāmasthāna other than the vocative: jetāram. अपराजितम् (aparājitam) — "na parājitaḥ = aparājitaḥ"; the n of nañ dropped by "nalopo nañaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-73); by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) the indeclinable first member keeps its accent, so the a is udātta.

॥२॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: a stroke over ज of वाजस्य followed by a bar under स्य, as printed.

Sūkta 11, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पूर्वीरिन्द्र॑स्य रा॒तयो॒ न वि द॑स्यन्त्यू॒तयः॑ । यदी॒ वाज॑स्य॒ गोम॑तः स्तो॒तृभ्यो॒ मंह॑ते म॒घम् ॥३॥

pūrvīr índrasya rātáyo ná ví dasyanty ūtáyaḥ | yadī vā́jasya gómataḥ stotṛ́bhyo máṃhate maghám ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ The Saṃhitā prints यदी with a long final vowel; the Pada prints यदि.

पूर्वीः । इन्द्रस्य । रातयः । न । वि । दस्यन्ति । ऊतयः ॥ यदि । वाजस्य । गोऽमतः । स्तोतृऽभ्यः । मंहते । मघम् ॥३॥

pūrvīḥ | indrasya | rātayaḥ | na | vi | dasyanti | ūtayaḥ || yadi | vājasya | go-mataḥ | stotṛ-bhyaḥ | maṃhate | magham ||3||

original p. 457

Rik 3: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रस्य संबन्धिन्यो रातयो धनदानानि पूर्वीरनादिकालसिद्धाः प्रभूता वा । अस्येन्द्रस्य सर्वदा यष्टृभ्यो धनदानमेव स्वभाव इत्यर्थः । एवं सतीदानीन्तनो ऽपि यजमानः स्तोतृभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्यो गोमतो गोसहितस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य पर्याप्तं मघं धनं यदि मंहते दक्षिणारूपेण ददाति तदानीमूतयो बहुधनदानपूर्वकाणीन्द्रस्यास्मद्विषयाणि रक्षणानि न वि दस्यन्ति । विशेषेण नोपक्षीयन्ते । मघं रेक्ण इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु मघशब्दः पठितः । दाति दाशतीत्यादिषु दशसु दानकर्मसु मंहत इति पठितम् ॥ पूर्वीः । पुरुशब्दस्य वोतो गुणवचनादिति ङीष् । आद्यस्योकारस्य दीर्घश्छान्दसः । जसि दीर्घाज्जसि चेति निषेधं बाधित्वा वा छन्दसि । पा. ६-१-१०६ । इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । ङीषः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । रातयः । मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः । पा. ३-३-९६ । इति क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् । दस्यन्ति । दसु उपक्षये । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् । निघातः । ऊतयः । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः । यदि । निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । संहितायां निपातस्य चेति दीर्घत्वम् । स्तोतृभ्यः । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । धात्वादेः षः सः । तृचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । मंहते । शपः पित्त्वादुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति निषेधात् ॥

indrasya saṃbandhinyo rātayo dhanadānāni pūrvīranādikālasiddhāḥ prabhūtā vā | asyendrasya sarvadā yaṣṭṛbhyo dhanadānameva svabhāva ityarthaḥ | evaṃ satīdānīntano 'pi yajamānaḥ stotṛbhya ṛtvigbhyo gomato gosahitasya vājasyānnasya paryāptaṃ maghaṃ dhanaṃ yadi maṃhate dakṣiṇārūpeṇa dadāti tadānīmūtayo bahudhanadānapūrvakāṇīndrasyāsmadviṣayāṇi rakṣaṇāni na vi dasyanti | viśeṣeṇa nopakṣīyante | maghaṃ rekṇa ityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu dhananāmasu maghaśabdaḥ paṭhitaḥ | dāti dāśatītyādiṣu daśasu dānakarmasu maṃhata iti paṭhitam || pūrvīḥ | puruśabdasya voto guṇavacanāditi ṅīṣ | ādyasyokārasya dīrghaśchāndasaḥ | jasi dīrghājjasi ceti niṣedhaṃ bādhitvā vā chandasi | pā. 6-1-106 | iti pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | ṅīṣaḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | rātayaḥ | mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ | pā. 3-3-96 | iti ktina udāttatvam | dasyanti | dasu upakṣaye | divādibhyaḥ śyan | nighātaḥ | ūtayaḥ | ūtiyūtītyādinā ktinnudāttaḥ | yadi | nipātatvādādyudāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasya ceti dīrghatvam | stotṛbhyaḥ | ṣṭuñ stutau | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | tṛcaścittvādantodāttatvam | maṃhate | śapaḥ pittvādudāttatvam | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati nipātairyadyadihanteti niṣedhāt ||

Translation: "The rātayaḥ — gifts of wealth — of Indra are pūrvīḥ: established from beginningless time, or abundant. The sense: to give wealth to those who sacrifice is always this Indra's very nature. This being so, if even the present-day sacrificer gives to the stotṛs, the priests, as sacrificial fee, magham — sufficient wealth — of vāja, food, accompanied by cows, then Indra's ūtayaḥ — protections, preceded by many gifts of wealth — directed to us na vi dasyanti, are not specially diminished. Among the twenty-eight words for 'wealth' beginning with magham and rekṇaḥ, magha is read; among the ten words for acts of giving beginning with dāti, dāśati, maṃhate is read." (Grammatical tail: pūrvīḥ — ṅīṣ after puru by "voto guṇavacanāt", the first u lengthened as a Vedic form, and "vā chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-106) sets aside the bar of "dīrghāj jasi ca" so the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening applies; ṅīṣ udātta by the suffix accent; rātayaḥ — ktin udātta by "mantre vṛṣeṣa-paca-mana-vida-bhū-vīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96); dasyanti — dasu upakṣaye, śyan by "divādibhyaḥ śyan", unaccented; ūtayaḥ — ktin udātta by "ūti-yūti…"; yadi — initial-udātta as a particle, long in the Saṃhitā by "nipātasya ca"; stotṛbhyaḥ — ṣṭuñ stutau, ṣ → s, final-udātta because tṛc is cit; maṃhate — the śap being pit, "udātta" [sic, as printed; read anudātta], the ending by the lasārvadhātuka accent; not unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" because of the bar "nipātair yadyadi-hanta…".)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

स्तोतृभ्यः (stotṛbhyaḥ) — the sacrificer to the priests who praise Indra | गोमतः (gomataḥ) — accompanied by cows | वाजस्य (vājasya) — in return for food | मघम् (magham) — wealth | यदि मंहते (yadi maṃhate) — if he gives, at the time when he gives as the sacrificial fee | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — of Indra | रातयः (rātayaḥ) — gifts of wealth and the like | ऊतयः (ūtayaḥ) — protections | पूर्वीः (pūrvīḥ) — [those] that have been from ancient times | न वि दस्यन्ति (na vi dasyanti) — do not diminish.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

When the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice gives to the priests who praise Indra cows, food and wealth as the sacrificial fee, then, however much Indra has given that sacrificer before, he does not reduce in the least his giving of wealth, protection and the like now.

॥ English Translation ॥

The former liberalities of Indra and his protection will not be wanting to him who presents wealth, food, and cattle to the reciters of the hymns.

original p. 458

Rik 3: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is somewhat strained. To the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, Indra has many times given wealth and the like, and protection in battle. Even so, when that sacrificer gives wealth, food, cows and the like to the priests who praise Indra, Indra will again give that sacrificer food and other nourishment, wealth and protection. What he gave before he gives again now, and there is no diminution at all: that is the idea.

"Pūrvīḥ" — this word may be given the sense pūrvasya sambandhinyaḥ — "those connected with former times," "of former relation" — or puru = many; pūrvyaḥ = "many": abundant, plentiful, much.

"Rātayaḥ" — rāti is read among the ten words for acts of giving beginning with dāti (Ni. 3-19); so rātayaḥ may be given the senses "gifts, bestowal, giving."

"Na vi dasyanti" — nopakṣīyante: they are not exhausted, they do not diminish.

"Maṃhate" — maṃhate is read among the ten words for the act of giving beginning with dāti; so it means "gives" (Ni. 3-19).

"Magham" — magha is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with magham, rekṇaḥ; so magha means wealth (Ni. 3-9 [as printed]).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 458–459, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

पूर्वीः (pūrvīḥ) — after puru (adjective), "voto guṇavacanāt" (Pā. 4-1-44): after a quality-word ending in u the feminine suffix ṅīṣ is optional, so ṅīṣ arises; the first u is lengthened in the Veda; the second u is replaced by v (yaṇ-substitution): pūrvī; then the nominative plural jas, giving pūrvī + as; pūrvasavarṇadīrgha ("prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ," Pā. 6-1-102) is barred by "dīrghājjasi ca" (Pā. 6-1-105): after a long vowel, if jas or a vowel of the ic group follows, no pūrvasavarṇa-lengthening applies; yet "vā chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-106) makes the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening optional in the Veda, so the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening arises; with ru and visarga the form is pūrvīḥ; the ṅīṣ suffix is udātta by the suffix accent.

original p. 459

Rik 3 grammar closes

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

रातयः (rātayaḥ) — a ktin-ending word; by "mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96) the ktin suffix is udātta in the mantra. दस्यन्ति (dasyanti) — root dasu upakṣaye ("to waste away"); laṭ third plural jhi, jh → ant; śyan by "divādibhyaḥ śyan" (Pā. 3-1-69); unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ". ऊतयः (ūtayaḥ) — the ktin is udātta by irregular formation, "ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-97). यदि (yadi) — a nipāta, initial-udātta ("nipātā ādyudāttāḥ"); in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136), yadī. स्तोतृभ्यः (stotṛbhyaḥ) — root ṣṭuñ stutau; ṣ → s by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64); tṛc by "nvul-tṛcau" (Pā. 3-1-133); the suffix is cit, so final-udātta ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163); dative plural bhyas. मंहते (maṃhate) — root mahi vṛddhau (idit), so the augment num; laṭ ātmanepada third singular ta; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79) gives e; śap; "naścāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. 8-3-24) turns the n of num into anusvāra: maṃhate; śap is pit and unaccented; te is unaccented ("tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt…," Pā. 6-1-186); the root accent stands; "nipātair yad-yadi-hanta-kuvin-nec-ceccaṇ-kaccid-yatra-yuktam" (Pā. 8-1-30) bars the loss of accent, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (8-1-28) does not make it unaccented.

॥३॥

original p. 459

Sūkta 11, Rik 4

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पु॒रां भि॒न्दुर्युवा॑ क॒विरमि॑तौजा अजायत । इ॒न्द्रो विश्व॑स्य॒ कर्म॑णो ध॒र्ता व॒ज्री पु॑रुष्टु॒तः ॥४॥

purā́ṃ bhindúr yúvā kavír ámitaujā ajāyata | indró víśvasya kármaṇo dhartā́ vajrī́ puruṣṭutáḥ ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पुराम् । भिन्दुः । युवा । कविः । अमितऽओजाः । अजायत ॥ इन्द्रः । विश्वस्य । कर्मणः । धर्ता । वज्री । पुरुऽस्तुतः ॥४॥

purām | bhinduḥ | yuvā | kaviḥ | amita-ojāḥ | ajāyata || indraḥ | viśvasya | karmaṇaḥ | dhartā | vajrī | puru-stutaḥ ||4||

Rik 4: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अभिप्लवषडहस्योक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवने ऽच्छावाकस्य पुरां भिन्दुर्युवा कविरिति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । तथा च सूत्रितम् । ऐह्यू ष्वित्युपक्रम्य [?] पुरां भिन्दुर्युवा कविर्वृषा ह्यसि राधसे । आ. ७-८ । इति ॥

abhiplavaṣaḍahasyokthyeṣu tṛtīyasavane 'cchāvākasya purāṃ bhinduryuvā kaviriti stotriyastṛcaḥ | tathā ca sūtritam | aihyū ṣvityupakramya [?] purāṃ bhinduryuvā kavirvṛṣā hyasi rādhase | ā. 7-8 | iti ||

अयमिन्द्र उच्यमानगुणयुक्तो ऽजायत । संपन्नः । कीदृग्गुणक इति तदुच्यते । पुरामसुरपुराणां भिन्दुर्भेत्ता । युवा कदाचिदपि वलीपलितादिवार्धकरहितः । कविर्मेधावी । अमितौजाः प्रभूतबलः । विश्वस्य कर्मणः कृत्स्नस्य ज्योतिष्टोमादेर्धर्ता पोषकः । वज्री यजमानरक्षणार्थं सर्वदा वज्रयुक्तः । पुरुष्टुतो बहुविधे तत्तत्कर्मणि स्तुतः ॥ भिन्दुः । भिदिर् विदारणे । कुरित्यनुवृत्तौ पॄभिदिव्यधिगृधिधृषिदृशिभ्यः [?] । उ. १-२४ । इति कुप्रत्ययः । तस्य छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकसंज्ञायां रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । पा. ३-१-७८ । मित्त्वादन्त्यादचः परो भवति । पा. १-१-४७ । श्नसोरल्लोपः । अनुस्वारपरसवर्णौ । पा. ८-४-५८ । अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ । पा. १-१-५७ । इति प्राप्तस्य स्थानिवद्भावस्य न पदान्तेत्यादिना । पा. १-१-५८ । निषेधः । युवा । यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । कविः । कु शब्दे । अच इः । उ. ४-१३९ । इतीः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अमितौजाः । अमितशब्दस्याव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते । विश्वस्य । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना । उ. १-१४९ । क्वन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । कर्मणः । अन्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । नित्स्वरः । धर्ता । तृच् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । वज्री । मत्वर्थीय इनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पुरुष्टुतः । स्तुतस्तोमयोश्छन्दसि । पा. ८-३-१०५ । इति षत्वम् । बहुषु प्रदेशेषु स्तुतः । थाथघञ्क्ताजबित्रकाणाम् । पा. ६-२-१४४ । इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं तृतीयासमासे हि थाथादिस्वरापवादस्तृतीया कर्मणि । पा. ६-२-४८ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः स्यात् ॥

ayamindra ucyamānaguṇayukto 'jāyata | saṃpannaḥ | kīdṛgguṇaka iti taducyate | purāmasurapurāṇāṃ bhindurbhettā | yuvā kadācidapi valīpalitādivārdhakarahitaḥ | kavirmedhāvī | amitaujāḥ prabhūtabalaḥ | viśvasya karmaṇaḥ kṛtsnasya jyotiṣṭomāderdhartā poṣakaḥ | vajrī yajamānarakṣaṇārthaṃ sarvadā vajrayuktaḥ | puruṣṭuto bahuvidhe tattatkarmaṇi stutaḥ || bhinduḥ | bhidir vidāraṇe | kurityanuvṛttau pṝbhidivyadhigṛdhidhṛṣidṛśibhyaḥ [?] | u. 1-24 | iti kupratyayaḥ | tasya chandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukasaṃjñāyāṃ rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | pā. 3-1-78 | mittvādantyādacaḥ paro bhavati | pā. 1-1-47 | śnasorallopaḥ | anusvāraparasavarṇau | pā. 8-4-58 | acaḥ parasminpūrvavidhau | pā. 1-1-57 | iti prāptasya sthānivadbhāvasya na padāntetyādinā | pā. 1-1-58 | niṣedhaḥ | yuvā | yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | kaviḥ | ku śabde | aca iḥ | u. 4-139 | itīḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | amitaujāḥ | amitaśabdasyāvyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tadeva śiṣyate | viśvasya | aśipruṣītyādinā | u. 1-149 | kvan | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | karmaṇaḥ | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | nitsvaraḥ | dhartā | tṛc | cittvādantodāttaḥ | vajrī | matvarthīya iniḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | puruṣṭutaḥ | stutastomayośchandasi | pā. 8-3-105 | iti ṣatvam | bahuṣu pradeśeṣu stutaḥ | thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām | pā. 6-2-144 | ityantodāttatvaṃ tṛtīyāsamāse hi thāthādisvarāpavādastṛtīyā karmaṇi | pā. 6-2-48 | iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ syāt ||

Translation: "In the ukthya [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, in the third pressing, the opening triplet (stotriya) of the Acchāvāka is purāṃ bhindur yuvā kaviḥ; so it is laid down, beginning with ehy ū ṣu [?]: 'purāṃ bhindur yuvā kaviḥ, vṛṣā hy asi rādhase' (Āśvalāyana 7-8). This Indra ajāyata — has come to be, is endowed — with the qualities now to be told. Of what qualities? Purām bhinduḥ — the breaker of the cities of the asuras; yuvā — young, never marked by the old age of wrinkles and grey hair; kaviḥ — wise; amitaujāḥ — of abundant strength; viśvasya karmaṇaḥ dhartā — the sustainer, the nourisher, of the whole of every rite such as the Jyotiṣṭoma; vajrī — always bearing the thunderbolt, for the protection of the sacrificer; puruṣṭutaḥ — praised in many ways in various rites." (Grammatical tail: bhinduḥ — bhidir vidāraṇe with ku (Uṇ. 1-24), which counts as sārvadhātuka by "chandasy ubhayathā", so śnam by "rudhādibhyaḥ śnam" (Pā. 3-1-78), placed after the last vowel as mit (Pā. 1-1-47); a of śna dropped by "śnasor allopaḥ"; anusvāra and the homorganic nasal (Pā. 8-4-58); the sthānivadbhāva of "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. 1-1-57) is barred by "na padānta…" (Pā. 1-1-58); yuvā — yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ with kanin (Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta as nit; kaviḥ — ku śabde with i by "aca iḥ" (Uṇ. 4-139), suffix accent; amitaujāḥ — in the bahuvrīhi the first member amita keeps the accent it has as a compound with an indeclinable first member; viśvasya — kvan (Uṇ. 1-149), initial-udātta; karmaṇaḥ — manin by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante", nit accent; dhartā — tṛc, final-udātta as cit; vajrī — the possessive ini, suffix accent; puruṣṭutaḥ — ṣ by "stutastomayoś chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-105); "praised in many places": final-udātta by "thātha-ghañ-ktāj-abitra-kāṇām" (Pā. 6-2-144), for in a third-case compound "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. 6-2-48), an exception to the thātha accent, would give the first member's accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — this Indra | पुराम् (purām) — of the cities of enemies | भिन्दुः (bhinduḥ) — the destroyer (the one who breaks down) | युवा (yuvā) — one who is always in the stage of youth, free from the changes of old age such as senility | कविः (kaviḥ) — wise | अमितौजाः (amitaujāḥ) — of immense prowess | विश्वस्य कर्मणः (viśvasya karmaṇaḥ) — of all rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma | धर्ता (dhartā) — the nourisher | वज्री (vajrī) — the bearer of the thunderbolt | पुरुष्टुतः (puruṣṭutaḥ) — praised exceedingly in many rites | endowed with these qualities अजायत (ajāyata) — he has become.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra's qualities are many. He destroys the cities of enemies; he is free from changes such as senility and is always in the stage of youth; he is very wise, of great might; he sustains, by his protection, all the rites of sacrifice; he bears the thunderbolt for the protection of the sacrificer. People praise this Indra abundantly in many rites.

original p. 461

Rik 4: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra is the destroyer of (enemies') cities, he is ever young, wise, of unbounded strength, the sustainer of pious acts, the weilder [sic] of thunderbolt and praised by many.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

A special application for this rik has been stated: in the rite called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, on the special ukthya day, at the third pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite the triplet purāṃ bhindur yuvā kaviḥ in the stotra-mantra recitation; in this connection the Āśvalāyana sūtra, in the section ehy ū ṣv iti [?], says that the triplets purāṃ bhindur yuvā kaviḥ and vṛṣā hy asi rādhase are to be recited.

"Bhinduḥ" — bhidir vidāraṇe — "one who splits, destroys, demolishes." Here the word purām is explained as "of the cities of enemies."

"Yuvā" — one who is in the stage of youth; one whose bodily strength does not wane with old age, who is always in the stage of youth. The words yuvā and kaviḥ are used especially in praising Agni.

"Ajāyata" — although this word means "became, was born," here only the sense "he is such, endowed with such qualities" is to be given.

"Viśvasya karmaṇaḥ" — the Bhāṣyakāra explains this as kṛtsnasya jyotiṣṭomādeḥ; it may also be given the sense "all deeds — rites such as sacrifices and the activities of worldly life."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 461–463, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

भिन्दुः (bhinduḥ) — root bhidir vidāraṇe; "pṝ [?]-bhidi-vyadhi-gṛdhi-dhṛṣi-dṛśibhyaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-23; the bhāṣya gives 1-24), with kuḥ carried over from "kur bhraś ca" (printed "pā. sū. 1-22")

original p. 462

Rik 4 grammar (continued)

— the roots pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, bhidir vidāraṇe, vyadha tāḍane, gṛdhu abhikāṅkṣāyām, ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye take ku; k is it and dropped: bhid + u; by "chandasy ubhayathā" (Pā. 3-4-117) the u is sārvadhātuka, so "rudhādibhyaḥ śnam" (Pā. 3-1-78) gives śnam, placed after the last vowel by "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ" (Pā. 1-1-47); "śnasor allopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-111) drops the a of śna before a kit/ṅit sārvadhātuka: bhin + d + u; "naś cāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. 8-3-24) gives anusvāra, and "anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-58) the homorganic n. The print then argues that the dropped a would, by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. 1-1-57), be sthānivat and intervene, so that anusvāra and parasavarṇa could not apply; but "na padānta-dvirvacana-vare-yalopa-svara-savarṇānusvāra-dīrgha-jaś-car-vidhiṣu" (1-1-58) denies the sthānivadbhāva in rules of anusvāra and savarṇa, so there is no intervention: bhinduḥ, with the suffix accent. युवा (yuvā) — root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ + kanin by "kanin yu-vṛṣi-takṣi-rāji-dhanvi-dyu-pratidivaḥ" (printed Uṇ. "1-154"; the bhāṣya gives 1-156); the suffix being nit, initial-udātta.

original p. 463

Rik 4 grammar closes

कविः (kaviḥ) — root ku śabde + i by "aca iḥ" (printed Uṇ. "4-578" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 4-139), after a vowel-ending root; ku + i, guṇa and av: kavi; the suffix accent. अमितौजाः (amitaujāḥ) — "na mitam amitam; amitam ojaḥ yasya saḥ"; in amita the indeclinable first member keeps its accent by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2); in the bahuvrīhi that follows, "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) keeps that same accent. विश्वस्य (viśvasya) — (headed "viśvataḥ" [sic]) kvan by "aśūpruṣi…" (Uṇ. 1-149); the nit accent. कर्मणः (karmaṇaḥ) — root ḍukṛñ karaṇe + manin by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75); guṇa with r; karman initial-udātta by the nit accent; genitive singular, ṇ by "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam"; ru and visarga: karmaṇaḥ. धर्ता (dhartā) — root dhṛñ avasthāne + tṛc by "ṇvul-tṛcau" (Pā. 3-1-133); guṇa with r: dhartṛ; final-udātta by "citaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-163); nominative singular dhartā. वज्री (vajrī) — "vajram asya asti iti vajrī": ini by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the suffix accent. पुरुष्टुतः (puruṣṭutaḥ) — root pṝ [?] pālanapūraṇayoḥ + ku by "pṝ-bhidi…" (Uṇ. 1-23); "ud oṣṭhyapūrvasya" (Pā. 7-1-102) gives ur for the ṝ: puru; root ṣṭuñ stutau, ṣ → s by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64), the ṭ reverting; "puruṣu stutaḥ," a locative tatpuruṣa — "praised in many places"; the case ending dropped by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71): purustuta; "stutastomayoś chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-105) makes the s after an iṇ or kavarga in the first member ṣ, and "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) the t after it ṭ: puruṣṭuta; final-udātta by "thātha-ghañ-ktāj-abitra-kāṇām" (printed "6-1-144"; the bhāṣya gives 6-2-144): after a gati or kāraka, words ending in tha, atha, ghañ, kta, ac, ap, itra, ka are final-udātta. If it were analysed as "purubhiḥ stutaḥ," a third-case tatpuruṣa, "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. 6-2-48) would give the first member's accent; so the locative tatpuruṣa has to be accepted.
