Sūkta 11, Rik 5

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

त्वं व॒लस्य॒ गोम॒तो ऽपा॑वरद्रिवो॒ बिलं॑ । [accent ?] त्वां दे॒वा अबि॑भ्युषस्तु॒ज्यमा॑नास आविषुः ॥५॥

tvaṃ valásya gómató 'pāvar adrivo bílaṃ | [accent ?] tvāṃ devā́ ábibhyuṣas tujyámānāsa āviṣuḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ The saṃhitā word ऽपावर् joins apa and avaḥ, with avaḥ written as ar before adrivaḥ by the visarga rule; the pada text separates them.

त्वम् । वलस्य । गोऽमतः । अप । अवः । अद्रिऽवः । बिलम् ॥ त्वाम् । देवाः । अबिभ्युषः । तुज्यमानासः । आविषुः ॥५॥

tvam | valasya | go-mataḥ | apa | avaḥ | adri-vaḥ | bilam || tvām | devāḥ | abibhyuṣaḥ | tujyamānāsaḥ | āviṣuḥ ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वलनामकः कश्चिदसुरो देवसंबन्धिनीर्गा अपहृत्य कस्मिंश्चिद्बिले गोपितवान् । तदानीमिन्द्रस्तद्बिलं स्वसैन्येन समावृत्य तस्माद्बिलाद्गा निःसारयामास । तदिदमुपाख्यानमिन्द्रो वलस्य बिलमपौर्णोत् । तै. सं. २-१-५-१ । इत्यादिब्राह्मणेषु मन्त्रान्तरेषु च प्रसिद्धम् । तदेतद्वृधि [?] निधायायं मन्त्रः प्रवर्तते ॥ हे अद्रिवो वज्रयुक्तेन्द्र त्वं गोमतो वलस्य गोभिर्युक्तस्य वलनामकस्यासुरस्य संबन्धि बिलमपावः । स्वसैन्यमुखेनापावृतवानसि । तदानीं तुज्यमानासो वलेन हिंस्यमाना देवा अभिभ्युषस्त्वदीयरक्षया वलादभीताः सन्तस्त्वामाविषुः । प्राप्तवन्तः ॥ अप । निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । अवः । वृञ् वरणे । लङ् । सिप् । इतश्च लोपः । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । गुणो रपरत्वं हल्ङ्यादिलोपः । विसर्जनीयः । अडागमः । अद्रिवः । अद्रिरस्यास्तीति मतुप् । छन्दसीर इति षत्वम् । संबोधन उगिदचामिति नुम् । हल्ङ्यादिसंयोगान्तलोपौ । मतुवसो रु संबुद्धौ छन्दसि । पा. ८-३-१ । इति रुत्वम् । बिलम् । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । अभिभ्युषः । ञिभी भये । लिट् । द्विर्भावः । अभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वजश्त्वे । क्वसुश्चेति लिटः क्वसुरादेशः । क्रादिनियमात्प्राप्त इट् वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमान्निवर्तते । जसि सर्वनामस्थाने ऽपि व्यत्ययेन भत्वाद्वसोः संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वम् । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वम् । अचि श्नुधात्वित्यादिना । पा. ६-४-७७ । प्राप्तमियङादेशं बाधित्वा एरनेकाच इति यणादेशः । नञ्समासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । तुज्यमानासः । तुजेर्हिंसार्थात्परस्य कर्मणि लटः स्थाने शानच् । सार्वधातुके यक् । पा. ३-१-६७ । इति यक् । कस्माददुपदेशादुत्तरस्य [?] लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वम् । यक एव प्रत्ययस्वरः शिष्यते । आविषुः । अव रक्षणादिषु । अस्माद्गत्यर्थाल्लुङो झिः । तस्य सिजभ्यस्तविदिभ्यश्च । पा. ३-४-१०९ । इति जुस् । सिच इडागमः । आडजादीनाम् । पा. ६-४-७२ । इत्याडागमः । आदेशप्रत्यययोरिति षत्वम् ॥

valanāmakaḥ kaścidasuro devasaṃbandhinīrgā apahṛtya kasmiṃścidbile gopitavān | tadānīmindrastadbilaṃ svasainyena samāvṛtya tasmādbilādgā niḥsārayāmāsa | tadidamupākhyānamindro valasya bilamapaurṇot | tai. saṃ. 2-1-5-1 | ityādibrāhmaṇeṣu mantrāntareṣu ca prasiddham | tadetadvṛdhi [?] nidhāyāyaṃ mantraḥ pravartate || he adrivo vajrayuktendra tvaṃ gomato valasya gobhiryuktasya valanāmakasyāsurasya saṃbandhi bilamapāvaḥ | svasainyamukhenāpāvṛtavānasi | tadānīṃ tujyamānāso valena hiṃsyamānā devā abhibhyuṣastvadīyarakṣayā valādabhītāḥ santastvāmāviṣuḥ | prāptavantaḥ || apa | nipātatvādādyudāttaḥ | avaḥ | vṛñ varaṇe | laṅ | sip | itaśca lopaḥ | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | guṇo raparatvaṃ halṅyādilopaḥ | visarjanīyaḥ | aḍāgamaḥ | adrivaḥ | adrirasyāstīti matup | chandasīra iti ṣatvam | saṃbodhana ugidacāmiti num | halṅyādisaṃyogāntalopau | matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi | pā. 8-3-1 | iti rutvam | bilam | nabviṣayasyānisantasyetyādyudāttatvam | abhibhyuṣaḥ | ñibhī bhaye | liṭ | dvirbhāvaḥ | abhyāsasya hrasvajaśtve | kvasuśceti liṭaḥ kvasurādeśaḥ | krādiniyamātprāpta iṭ vasvekājādghasāmiti niyamānnivartate | jasi sarvanāmasthāne 'pi vyatyayena bhatvādvasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatvam | śāsivasighasīnāṃ ceti ṣatvam | aci śnudhātvityādinā | pā. 6-4-77 | prāptamiyaṅādeśaṃ bādhitvā eranekāca iti yaṇādeśaḥ | nañsamāsaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | tujyamānāsaḥ | tujerhiṃsārthātparasya karmaṇi laṭaḥ sthāne śānac | sārvadhātuke yak | pā. 3-1-67 | iti yak | kasmādadupadeśāduttarasya [?] lasārvadhātukasyānudāttatvam | yaka eva pratyayasvaraḥ śiṣyate | āviṣuḥ | ava rakṣaṇādiṣu | asmādgatyarthālluṅo jhiḥ | tasya sijabhyastavidibhyaśca | pā. 3-4-109 | iti jus | sica iḍāgamaḥ | āḍajādīnām | pā. 6-4-72 | ityāḍāgamaḥ | ādeśapratyayayoriti ṣatvam ||

Translation: "An asura named Vala, having stolen the cows belonging to the gods, hid them in a cave. Then Indra, surrounding that cave with his own army, drove the cows out of it. This legend — 'indro valasya bilam apaurṇot' (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-1-5-1) — is well known in the Brāhmaṇas and in other mantras. With this in mind [vṛdhi [?] nidhāya] this mantra proceeds. O adrivaḥ, thunderbolt-bearing Indra! You apāvaḥ — uncovered — the cave of gomataḥ valasya, of the asura named Vala who possessed cows; you opened it by means of your own army. Then the gods, tujyamānāsaḥ — oppressed by Vala — being abhibhyuṣaḥ [sic] — without fear of Vala, thanks to your protection — and āviṣuḥ: came to you, attained you." (Grammatical tail, partly on p. 465: apa initial-udātta as a particle; avaḥ — vṛñ varaṇe, laṅ, sip, i dropped by "itaś ca", the śnu of the svādi class dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi", guṇa with r, the s dropped by "hal-ṅyādi", visarga, augment aṭ; adrivaḥ — matup, "chandasīraḥ" (printed "ṣatvam" [sic] for vatvam), num in the vocative by "ugid-acām", loss of the final consonants, ru by "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-1); bilam initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya"; abhibhyuṣaḥ [sic] — ñibhī bhaye, liṭ replaced by kvasu, the iṭ due by the krādi restriction withdrawn by the restriction "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām", samprasāraṇa of vas (treated as bha by exception even before jas), ṣ by "śāsi-vasi-ghasīnāṃ ca", and yaṇ by "er anekācaḥ" overriding the iyaṅ of Pā. 6-4-77; a nañ-compound with the indeclinable's accent; tujyamānāsaḥ — passive śānac after tuj "to hurt", yak by "sārvadhātuke yak" (Pā. 3-1-67), the lasārvadhātuka after the a-ending being unaccented, so the accent of yak stands; āviṣuḥ — ava in the sense of going, luṅ jhi → jus by "sij-abhyasta-vidibhyaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-109), iṭ for sic, āṭ by "āḍ ajādīnām" (Pā. 6-4-72), ṣ by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ".)

original p. 465

Rik 5: word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अद्रिवः ((he) adrivaḥ) — O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt | त्वम् (tvam) — you | गोमतः (gomataḥ) — who had taken the cows | वलस्य (valasya) — of the asura Vala | बिलम् (bilam) — the cave | अप अवः (apa avaḥ) — have laid siege to and opened (with the help of your army) | then तुज्यमानासः (tujyamānāsaḥ) — [those] oppressed by the asura Vala | देवाः (devāḥ) — the gods | अबिभ्युषः (abibhyuṣaḥ) — made fearless by your protection, that is, not afraid of the asura Bala [sic] | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | आविषुः (āviṣuḥ) — took shelter in.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt! The asura Vala had stolen the gods' cows and hidden them in a cave. To free them you laid siege to his cave with the help of your army, opened its door and set the cows free. The gods who had been oppressed by the asura Bala [sic], having your protection, no longer feared him in the least, and came to you and took refuge in you.

॥ English Translation ॥

O weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt, you opened the cave of Vala, who had concealed the cattle (cows) and the gods whom he had oppressed no longer feared when they had obtained your protection.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In explaining this rik the Bhāṣyakāra relates an ancient legend (legend — the source's own English): the asura Vala stole the gods' cows and hid them in a cave; then Indra, with the help of his army, laid siege to the cave and freed the cows that were in it. This is told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (printed "2-1-1-1"; the bhāṣya gives 2-1-5-1) in the following way: The passage runs onto p. 466. Gloss editorial and tentative: "Indra opened Vala's cave; the best animal that was there he seized by the back and drew out; a thousand animals came up after it; it became raised (unnata). One who desires cattle should offer this raised [animal] to Indra; he approaches Indra with his own share; Indra gives him cattle; he becomes rich in cattle, he becomes raised."

इन्द्रो वलस्य बिलमपौर्णोत्स य उत्तमः पशुरासीत्तं पृष्ठं प्रति संगृह्योदक्षिदत्तग्ं सहस्रं पशवो ऽनूदायन्त्स उन्नतो ऽभवद्यः पशुकामः स्यात्स एतमैन्द्रमुन्नतमालभेतेन्द्रमेव स्वेन भागधेयेनोप धावति स एवास्मै पशून्प्रयच्छति पशुमानेव भवत्युन्नतो भवति ॥

indro valasya bilamapaurṇotsa ya uttamaḥ paśurāsīttaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ prati saṃgṛhyodakṣidattagṃ sahasraṃ paśavo 'nūdāyantsa unnato 'bhavadyaḥ paśukāmaḥ syātsa etamaindramunnatamālabhetendrameva svena bhāgadheyenopa dhāvati sa evāsmai paśūnprayacchati paśumāneva bhavatyunnato bhavati ||

Rik 5: Special Topics (continued) and grammar begins

This subject is also described here and there in other mantras of the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas. In the Ṛgveda this matter of Vala is set out in the riks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-4; 2-11-20; 2-14-3; 2-15-8; 2-12-3; 2-24-3; 3-30-10; 3-34-10; 4-50-5; 6-18-5; 6-39-2; 8-14-7 [?]; 8-24-30; 10-62-2; 10-67-6; 10-68-5; 10-68-6; 10-68-9; 10-68-10; 10-138-1. There is a tradition that Vala's soldiers are called Paṇis; in many places it is said that they stole the cows and hid them in caves. We have explained this subject earlier, at the fifth rik of the sūkta Ṛ. Sa. 1-2-6 (see Part 2, page 228). Besides this, the matter of the asuras called Paṇi is described in many riks of the Ṛgveda; these will be explained in their places.

Skandasvāmī's explanation of this rik is different: vala is a cloud (megha) and go is water (udaka); Indra used his thunderbolt on the clouds and caused the held-back rain to fall. And tujyamānāḥ he renders as tvaramāṇāḥ ("hastening"), āviṣuḥ as anugatavantaḥ ("followed"), and devāḥ as "Maruts"; so the idea is that the rain, with the help of the wind, came falling swiftly.

"Gomataḥ" — gobhir yuktasya, "who possesses cows" — which cows? — one has to consider what is said elsewhere, that they are the stolen cows.

"Bilam" — a cave, a hollow that cannot be seen by anyone: cave [the source's own English].

"Tujyamānāsaḥ" — balena hiṃsyamānāḥ — oppressed by the asura Bala [sic].

"Āviṣuḥ" — ava rakṣaṇādiṣu — "[those] who have reached, who have taken shelter for protection."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 466–470, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

अप (apa) — a nipāta, initial-udātta ("nipātā ādyudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 80).

original p. 467

Rik 5 grammar (continued)

अवः (avaḥ) — root vṛñ varaṇe, of the svādi class; laṅ, replaced by the second-person singular parasmaipada sip; its p is it by "halantyam" (Pā. 1-3-3) and dropped; the i dropped by "itaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-100) (the final of an i-ending parasmaipada ending in place of a ṅit lakāra); "itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-4-97), which makes that loss optional in leṭ, does not apply here; śnu by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. 3-1-73), dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); vṛ + s: guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84), with r by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51): var + s; the s dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68); visarga for the r; the augment aṭ by "luṅ-laṅ-lṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71): avaḥ. अद्रिवः (adrivaḥ) — "adriḥ asya asti": matup by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); m → v by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. 8-2-15); vocative singular su: adrivat + su; num after the v by "ugid-acāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70): adrivant + su; su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68); the t dropped by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-23), which by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1) is not effective for the loss of n, so "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7) does not apply; "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-1) gives ru for the n, and "kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-15) the visarga: adrivaḥ. बिलम् (bilam) — initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (printed Phiṭ-sū. "26"). अबिभ्युषः (abibhyuṣaḥ) — root ñibhī bhaye; liṭ; doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8): bhī + bhī; the first shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-59); jaś in the reduplicate by "abhyāse car ca" (Pā. 8-4-54), bh → b: bibhī; parasmaipada by "śeṣāt kartari parasmaipadam" (Pā. 1-3-78); liṭ → kvasu by "kvasuś ca" (Pā. 3-2-107); kvasu being kit, no guṇa: bibhī + vas; vas is ārdhadhātuka, so iṭ would come by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35).

original p. 468

Rik 5 grammar (continued)

But "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. 7-2-10) bars iṭ before a val-initial ārdhadhātuka after a root that in the upadeśa is monosyllabic and anudātta. bhī is monosyllabic; and by the verse "ūd-ṛdantair yauti-ru-kṣṇu-śīṅ-snu-nu-kṣu-śvi-ḍīṅ-śribhiḥ | vṛṅ-vṛñbhyāṃ ca vinaikāco 'janteṣu nihatāḥ smṛtāḥ ||" — among vowel-ending roots, all except those ending in ū and ṝ and yu, ru, kṣṇu, śīṅ, snu, nu, kṣu, śvi, ḍīṅ, śri, vṛṅ, vṛñ are anudātta — bhī, not being in the list, is anudātta, so iṭ is barred for vas. Then the krādi restriction makes iṭ arise again: "kṛ-sṛ-bhṛ-vṛ-stu-dru-sru-śruvo liṭi" (Pā. 7-2-13) bars iṭ before liṭ after these roots. For kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, monosyllabic and anudātta, the bar already follows from 7-2-10; vṛ is in the verse and so not anudātta, but being monosyllabic and u-ending (uk) it is barred by "śryukaḥ kiti" (Pā. 7-2-11); so naming them in 7-2-13 would be useless, and by the maxim "siddhe saty ārabhyamāṇo vidhir niyamāya bhavati" the sūtra is a restriction: the bars of iṭ before liṭ, whether depending on the root (prakṛtyāśraya, as ekācaḥ) or on the suffix (pratyayāśraya, as śryukaḥ kiti), apply only after kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ; after other roots neither bar applies. stu, dru, sru, śru are u-ending; by "ṛto bhāradvājasya" (Pā. 7-2-63), in Bhāradvāja's view the bar of iṭ before thal applies only to ṛ-ending roots among those always aniṭ before tās, so after stu etc. iṭ would arise before thal; naming stu etc. is needed both for that bar and for the bar before va, ma and the like that the krādi restriction would otherwise produce;

original p. 469

Rik 5 grammar (continued)

so they have a prescriptive role, and by the maxim "vidhi-niyama-saṃbhave vidhir eva jyāyān" the four roots stu etc. are taken as prescriptive, not restrictive. Thus by the krādi restriction iṭ is not barred for the vas (of liṭ) after bhī, which is outside the krādi list, and iṭ would arise; it is withdrawn by the restriction "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām" (Pā. 7-2-67): iṭ comes before vas only after roots monosyllabic after reduplication, roots ending in ā, and ghas. vas is a kṛt beginning with vaś, so "neḍ vaśi kṛti" (Pā. 7-2-8) would bar iṭ, and the krādi restriction would give it; giving iṭ again is for restriction — only after those roots does vas take iṭ, not after others; so after bibhī, which is not among them, vas takes no iṭ. bibhīvas + jas: though jas is a sarvanāmasthāna, by Vedic exception bibhīvas is treated as bha; samprasāraṇa by "vasoḥ samprasāraṇam" (Pā. 6-4-131) and pūrvarūpa by "samprasāraṇāc ca": bibhī + us + as; the iyaṅ that "aci śnu-dhātu-bhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅ-uvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77) would give is set aside by "er anekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya" (Pā. 6-4-82), giving yaṇ: ī → y; the s of the suffix vas → ṣ by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59); "śāsi-vasi-ghasīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 8-3-60) was shown earlier not to apply here; "na bibhyuṣaḥ abibhyuṣaḥ," a nañ-compound; by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) the indeclinable first member keeps its accent. तुज्यमानासः (tujyamānāsaḥ) — root tuja hiṃsāyām; passive laṭ, replaced by śānac by "laṭaḥ śatṛ-śānacau…" (Pā. 3-2-124); yak by "sārvadhātuke yak" (Pā. 3-1-67) before a sārvadhātuka expressing bhāva or karman: tuj + ya + āna; yak is kit, so no laghūpadha-guṇa; muk by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82): tujyamāna; nominative plural jas with asuk by "āj-jaser asuk" (Pā. 7-1-50); yak ends in a in the upadeśa, so the śānac after it is unaccented by "tāsy anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāt…" (Pā. 6-1-186), jas is unaccented as a sup, and the udātta of yak by its suffix accent stands. आविषुः (āviṣuḥ) — root ava rakṣaṇādiṣu, here taken in the sense of going;

original p. 470

Rik 5 grammar closes

luṅ after av, replaced by jhi; cli by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43), sic by "cleḥ sic" (Pā. 3-1-44); av + s + jhi: "sij-abhyasta-vidibhyaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-109) gives jus for the jhi of a ṅit lakāra after sic, a reduplicated root or vid: av + s + us; iṭ for sic by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35); the augment āṭ by "āḍ ajādīnām" (Pā. 6-4-72), vṛddhi by "āṭaś ca" (Pā. 6-1-90): āvisus; ṣ for the s of sic by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59); ru and visarga for the final s: āviṣuḥ; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

Sūkta 11, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तवा॒हं शू॑र रा॒तिभिः॒ प्रत्या॑यं॒ सिन्धु॑मा॒वद॑न् । उपा॑तिष्ठन्त गिर्वणो वि॒दुष्टे॒ तस्य॑ का॒रवः॑ ॥६॥

tavāháṃ śūra rātíbhiḥ práty āyaṃ síndhum āvádan | úpātiṣṭhanta girvaṇo vidúṣ ṭe tásya kārávaḥ ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तव । अहम् । शूर । रातिऽभिः । प्रति । आयम् । सिन्धुम् । आऽवदन् ॥ उप । अतिष्ठन्त । गिर्वणः । विदुः । ते । तस्य । कारवः ॥६॥

tava | aham | śūra | rāti-bhiḥ | prati | āyam | sindhum | ā-vadan || upa | atiṣṭhanta | girvaṇaḥ | viduḥ | te | tasya | kāravaḥ ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शूर संग्रामे शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र तव रातिभिः कर्मसु त्वदीयैर्धनदानैर्निमित्तभूतैरहं होता प्रत्यायम् । त्वां पुनरागतो ऽस्मि । पुरा बहुषु कर्मसु त्वत्तो धनस्य लब्धत्वादस्मिन्कर्मणि प्रत्यागमनमित्युच्यते । किं कुर्वन् । सिन्धुं स्यन्दमानं सोममावदन् सर्वतः कथयन् । अस्मिन्सोमयागे त्वदीयां धनदानकीर्तिं प्रकटयन्नित्यर्थः । हे गिर्वणो गीर्भिर्वननीयेन्द्र कारवः कर्तार ऋत्विग्यजमाना उपातिष्ठन्त । पुरा धनलाभार्थं त्वामुपस्थितवन्तः । उपस्थाय च तस्य तादृशस्यौदार्योपेतस्य ते तव धनदानं विदुः । जानन्ति । गिर्वणश्शब्दं यास्क इत्थं निब्रूते । गिर्वणा देवो भवति गीर्भिरेनं वनयन्ति । नि. ६-१४ । इति । रेभो जरितेत्यादिषु त्रयोदशसु स्तोतृनामसु कारुशब्दः पठितः ॥ तव । युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसीत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । रातिभिः । मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः । आयम् । इणो लङ् । तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्तामः । पा. ३-४-१०१ । इत्यमादेशः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । आडागमः । वृद्ध्यायादेशौ । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । सिन्धुम् । स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे । नित्यनुवृत्तौ स्यन्देः संप्रसारणं धश्च । उ. १-१२ । इत्युप्रत्ययो धकारश्चान्तादेशः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । आवदन् । वद व्यक्तायां वाचि । लटः शतृ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । आङा सह कुगतिप्रादयः । पा. २-२-१८ । इति समासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अतिष्ठन्त । उपान्मन्त्रकरणे । पा. १-३-२५ । इत्यात्मनेपदम् । गिर्वणः । वन षण संभक्तौ । असुन् । आमन्त्रितस्य चेति निघातः । विदुः । विद ज्ञाने । लट् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । विदो लटो वा । पा. ३-४-८३ । इति झेरुस् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । संहितायां युष्मत्ततक्षुःष्वन्तःपादम् । पा. ८-३-१०३ । इति षत्वम् । ष्टुना ष्टुरित्युत्तरस्य तकारस्य ष्टुत्वम् । तस्य । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं प्राप्तं न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति निषिध्यते । कारवः । कृवापाजीत्यादिना । उ. १-१ । उण् । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

he śūra saṃgrāme śauryayuktendra tava rātibhiḥ karmasu tvadīyairdhanadānairnimittabhūtairahaṃ hotā pratyāyam | tvāṃ punarāgato 'smi | purā bahuṣu karmasu tvatto dhanasya labdhatvādasminkarmaṇi pratyāgamanamityucyate | kiṃ kurvan | sindhuṃ syandamānaṃ somamāvadan sarvataḥ kathayan | asminsomayāge tvadīyāṃ dhanadānakīrtiṃ prakaṭayannityarthaḥ | he girvaṇo gīrbhirvananīyendra kāravaḥ kartāra ṛtvigyajamānā upātiṣṭhanta | purā dhanalābhārthaṃ tvāmupasthitavantaḥ | upasthāya ca tasya tādṛśasyaudāryopetasya te tava dhanadānaṃ viduḥ | jānanti | girvaṇaśśabdaṃ yāska itthaṃ nibrūte | girvaṇā devo bhavati gīrbhirenaṃ vanayanti | ni. 6-14 | iti | rebho jaritetyādiṣu trayodaśasu stotṛnāmasu kāruśabdaḥ paṭhitaḥ || tava | yuṣmadasmadorṅasītyādyudāttatvam | rātibhiḥ | mantre vṛṣetyādinā ktinnudāttaḥ | āyam | iṇo laṅ | tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ | pā. 3-4-101 | ityamādeśaḥ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | āḍāgamaḥ | vṛddhyāyādeśau | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | sindhum | syandū prasravaṇe | nityanuvṛttau syandeḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ dhaśca | u. 1-12 | ityupratyayo dhakāraścāntādeśaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | āvadan | vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci | laṭaḥ śatṛ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | āṅā saha kugatiprādayaḥ | pā. 2-2-18 | iti samāsaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | atiṣṭhanta | upānmantrakaraṇe | pā. 1-3-25 | ityātmanepadam | girvaṇaḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | asun | āmantritasya ceti nighātaḥ | viduḥ | vida jñāne | laṭ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | vido laṭo vā | pā. 3-4-83 | iti jherus | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ yuṣmattatakṣuḥṣvantaḥpādam | pā. 8-3-103 | iti ṣatvam | ṣṭunā ṣṭurityuttarasya takārasya ṣṭutvam | tasya | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ prāptaṃ na gośvansāvavarṇeti niṣidhyate | kāravaḥ | kṛvāpājītyādinā | u. 1-1 | uṇ | pratyayasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "O śūra, O Indra, hero in battle! By your rātibhiḥ — your gifts of wealth that have been the cause in the rites — I, the hotṛ, prati āyam, have come back to you. In many earlier rites I received wealth from you; hence in this rite it is called a coming back. Doing what? Sindhum āvadan: proclaiming on all sides the flowing Soma — publishing, at this Soma-sacrifice, your fame of giving wealth. O girvaṇaḥ — O Indra, to be served with praises — kāravaḥ, the doers: the priests and sacrificers, upātiṣṭhanta: stand near [you]. Formerly they came near you for the gain of wealth; and, having come near, they viduḥ — know — the giving of wealth of you, who are so endowed with generosity. Yāska explains the word girvaṇas thus: 'girvaṇas is a god; because they serve him with girs (praises)' (Ni. 6-14). Among the thirteen words for 'praiser,' beginning with rebhaḥ and jaritā, the word kāru is read." (Grammatical tail, on p. 471: tava initial-udātta by "yuṣmadasmador ṅasi"; rātibhiḥ — ktin udātta by "mantre vṛṣa…"; āyam — laṅ of iṇ, am for mip by "tas-thas-tha-mipāṃ tān-tan-tāmaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-101), śap dropped, augment āṭ, vṛddhi and āy, unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ"; sindhum — syandū prasravaṇe, with nit carried over, u by "syandeḥ samprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-12), dh for the final, initial-udātta; āvadan — śatṛ after vad, the root accent alone remaining, compounded with ā by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18), the kṛt second member keeping its accent; atiṣṭhanta — ātmanepada by "upān mantrakaraṇe" (Pā. 1-3-25); girvaṇaḥ unaccented as a vocative; viduḥ — us for jhi by "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83), not unaccented as it begins a pāda; in the Saṃhitā ṣ by "yuṣmat-tat-takṣuḥṣv antaḥpādam" (Pā. 8-3-103) and ṭ by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ"; tasya — the case-ending udātta of "sāv ekācaḥ" barred by "na go-śvan-sāv-avarṇa…"; kāravaḥ — uṇ by "kṛ-vā-pā-ji…" (Uṇ. 1-1), suffix accent.)

original p. 471

Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) शूर ((he) śūra) — O Indra, endowed with prowess (in battle) | तव (tava) — your | रातिभिः (rātibhiḥ) — by gifts of wealth | (अहम्) (aham) — I | सिन्धुम् आवदन् (sindhum āvadan) — praising the Soma-juice that is to be offered to you | प्रति आयम् (prati āyam) — have come again to you | (हे) गिर्वणः ((he) girvaṇaḥ) — O Indra, praised by words | कारवः (kāravaḥ) — priests, sacrificers and others who perform the rites | उप अतिष्ठन्त (upa atiṣṭhanta) — stand near you (pray to you) | and ते (te) — your | (धनप्रदानम्) (dhanapradānam) — giving of wealth | विदुः (viduḥ) — have known.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, hero! Moved by the gifts of wealth and the like that you gave before, I have come to you again, praising the virtues of the Soma-juice I offer you; and the priests, sacrificers and others who perform sacrificial rites also stand near you, having known your generosity.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Hero, attracted by your bounties, I again come praising the Soma libation to be offered to you; the performers of the rite approach you who are worthy of praise, for they have known your liberalities.

original p. 472

Rik 6: Special Topics and grammar begins

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Sindhum ā vadan" — the word sindhu is derived from the root syandū prasravaṇe ("to flow"); the sense is "the Soma-juice that, when the creeper is pressed, is born and flows out in streams." Āvadan means "praising": describing the delights and the like that come from drinking Soma.

"Upa atiṣṭhanta" — "we are near, we come near; approach you" [the source's own English]: that is, we pray to you.

"Viduḥ te" — if the word dhanadānam ("giving of wealth") is not supplied with these words, no proper sense results. The usage viduṣṭe occurs also in the next rik.

"Kāravaḥ" — kartāraḥ, "those who do"; what they do has to be explained: they perform sacrificial rites or make hymns.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 472–474, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

तव (tava) — yuṣmad + genitive singular "jas" [sic, for ṅas]; before it "tava-mamau ṅasi" (Pā. 7-2-96) replaces yuṣm, the part up to the m, by tava: tava + ad + ṅas; pararūpa by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97): tavad + ṅas; aś for ṅas by "yuṣmad-asmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś" (printed "7-1-32" [?]); tavad + a: the ṭi dropped by "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90): tava; or, if "śeṣe lopaḥ" drops only the final d, pararūpa by "ato guṇe" again gives tava; initial-udātta by "yuṣmad-asmador ṅasi" (Pā. 6-1-211). रातिभिः (rātibhiḥ) — root rā "ādāne" [as printed]; ktin, udātta, by "mantre vṛṣeṣa-paca-mana-vida-bhū-vīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96); the following bhis unaccented. आयम् (āyam) — root iṇ gatau; laṅ, first singular mip; "tas-thas-tha-mipāṃ tān-tan-tāmaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-101): for tas, thas, tha, mip in place of a ṅit lakāra, tām, tam, ta, am: i + am; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68), dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); the augment āṭ by "āḍ ajādīnām" (Pā. 6-4-72), vṛddhi by "āṭaś ca" (Pā. 6-1-90),

original p. 473

Rik 6 grammar (continued)

and āy for ai by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78): āyam; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). सिन्धुम् (sindhum) — root syandū prasravaṇe; "syandeḥ samprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-11), with nit carried over from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. "1-9" [?]): after syand the suffix u, which is nit, with samprasāraṇa of the y and dh for the d: sindhu; initial-udātta by the nit accent; accusative singular sindhum. आवदन् (āvadan) — root vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci; laṭ → śatṛ; śap: vad + a + at; śap, being pit, unaccented; śap ends in a in the upadeśa, so the lasārvadhātuka after it is unaccented by "tāsy anudātten-ṅid-ad-upadeśāt…" (Pā. 6-1-186), and the root accent stands; vadat compounded with āṅ by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18): āvadat, the kṛt second member keeping the accents already stated; with su, num by "ugid-acāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70), su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68), the t dropped by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-23), which being asiddha by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1) does not let "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7) drop the n: āvadan. अतिष्ठन्त (atiṣṭhanta) — root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau, here after the upasarga upa, so "upān mantrakaraṇe" (Pā. 1-3-25): after upa, sthā in the sense of addressing with a mantra takes ātmanepada; laṅ, third plural jha; śap by "kartari śap"; sthā → tiṣṭha by "pā-ghrā-dhmā…" (Pā. 7-3-78); ant for jh by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); the augment aṭ by Pā. 6-4-71; pararūpa of the second a by "ato guṇe" (6-1-97): atiṣṭhanta. गिर्वणः (girvaṇaḥ) — gṝ śabde + kvip; i with r by "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (7-1-100): gir; "gīrbhiḥ vanyate": vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau with asun: girvanas; vocative singular,

Rik 6 grammar closes

su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ", ru, visarga and ṇ: girvaṇaḥ; as a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). विदुः (viduḥ) — root vida jñāne, adādi; laṭ → jhi; śap dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83): for the parasmaipada endings of laṭ after vid, the nine substitutes ṇal etc. optionally, so us for jhi: vidus, ru and visarga; viduḥ stands at the beginning of the fourth pāda, so it is not unaccented. In the Saṃhitā viduḥ + te: "visarjanīyasya saḥ" (Pā. 8-3-34) gives s for the visarga before a khar letter; then "yuṣmat-tat-takṣuḥṣv antaḥpādam" (Pā. 8-3-103): ṣ for an s before the t-initial substitutes of yuṣmad, before tat and takṣu, within a pāda; and "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) turns the t into ṭ: viduṣṭe. तस्य (tasya) — "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168): after a word that is monosyllabic before the locative plural su, the case endings from the third onward are udātta; this would make the genitive sya udātta, but "na go-śvan-sāv-avarṇa-rāḍ-aṅ-kruṅ-kṛdbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-182 [?]) bars it after go, śvan, a word ending in a in the nominative singular, rāṭ, aṅ, kruṅ and kṛt; so by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. 3-1-4) sya is unaccented. कारवः (kāravaḥ) — "kṛ-vā-pā-ji-mi-svadi-sādhy-aśūbhya uṇ" (Uṇ. 1-1): after ḍukṛñ karaṇe, vā gatigandhanayoḥ, pā pāne, ji abhibhave, ḍumiñ prakṣepaṇe, svada āsvādane, sādha saṃsiddhau, aśū vyāptau, the suffix uṇ; ṇit, so vṛddhi by "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. 7-2-115), with r by "uraṇ raparaḥ": kāru; the suffix accent.

॥६॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: a bar under वां and a stroke over स्यु of श्रवांस्युत्तिर, as printed — [accent ?].

Sūkta 11, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मा॒याभि॑रिन्द्र मा॒यिनं॒ त्वं शुष्ण॒मवा॑तिरः । वि॒दुष्टे॒ तस्य॒ मेधि॑रा॒स्तेषां॒ श्रवां॒स्यु॑त्तिर ॥७॥ [accent ?]

māyā́bhir indra māyínaṃ tváṃ śuṣṇam ávātiraḥ | vidúṣ ṭe tásya médhirās téṣāṃ śrávāṃsy ut tira ||7|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मायाभिः । इन्द्र । मायिनम् । त्वम् । शुष्णम् । अव । अतिरः ॥ विदुः । ते । तस्य । मेधिराः । तेषाम् । श्रवांसि । उत् । तिर ॥७॥

māyābhiḥ | indra | māyinam | tvam | śuṣṇam | ava | atiraḥ || viduḥ | te | tasya | medhirāḥ | teṣām | śravāṃsi | ut | tira ||7||

Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र त्वं मायिनं नानाविधकपटोपेतं शुष्णं भूतानां शोषणहेतुमेतन्नामकमसुरं मायाभिस्तत्प्रतिकूलैः कपटविशेषैः । यद्वा । तद्विधोपायगोचरप्रज्ञाभिः । अवातिरः । हिंसितवानसि । एतच्च यास्केनोक्तम् । इन्द्रः शुष्णं जघान । नि. ३-११ । इति । शुष्णं पिप्रुम् । ऋग्वे. १-१०३-८ । इत्यादिमन्त्रे चायमर्थो विस्पष्टः । मेधिरा मेधावन्तो ऽनुष्ठातारस्तस्य तादृशस्य ते तव महिमानं विदुः । जानन्ति । तेषां जानतामनुष्ठातॄणां श्रवांस्यन्नान्युत्तिर । वर्धय । केतः केतुरित्यादिष्वेकादशसु प्रज्ञानामसु माया वयुनमिति पठितम् । श्रवःशब्दं यास्को निर्वक्ति । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सतः । नि. १०-३ । इति ॥ मायाभिः । माङ् माने । माच्छाससिसूभ्यो यः । उ. ४-१०९ । इति यप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मायिनम् । मायास्यास्तीति मायी । व्रीह्यादित्वादिनिप्रत्ययः । पा. ५-२-११६ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । शुष्णम् । शुष शोषणे । अस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थान्निदित्यनुवृत्तौ तृषिशुषिरसिभ्यः कित् । उ. ३-१२ । इति नप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अतिरः । तरतेर्लङि व्यत्ययेन शः । तस्य ङित्त्वेन गुणाभावादृत इद्धातोरितीत्त्वम् । रपरत्वम् । विदुष्टे तस्य । गतं मन्त्रे गतम् । मेधिराः । मिधृ मेधृ मेधाहिंसनयोः । औणादिक इरन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । श्रवांसि । नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

he indra tvaṃ māyinaṃ nānāvidhakapaṭopetaṃ śuṣṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ śoṣaṇahetumetannāmakamasuraṃ māyābhistatpratikūlaiḥ kapaṭaviśeṣaiḥ | yadvā | tadvidhopāyagocaraprajñābhiḥ | avātiraḥ | hiṃsitavānasi | etacca yāskenoktam | indraḥ śuṣṇaṃ jaghāna | ni. 3-11 | iti | śuṣṇaṃ piprum | ṛgve. 1-103-8 | ityādimantre cāyamartho vispaṣṭaḥ | medhirā medhāvanto 'nuṣṭhātārastasya tādṛśasya te tava mahimānaṃ viduḥ | jānanti | teṣāṃ jānatāmanuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ śravāṃsyannānyuttira | vardhaya | ketaḥ keturityādiṣvekādaśasu prajñānāmasu māyā vayunamiti paṭhitam | śravaḥśabdaṃ yāsko nirvakti | śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ | ni. 10-3 | iti || māyābhiḥ | māṅ māne | mācchāsasisūbhyo yaḥ | u. 4-109 | iti yapratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | māyinam | māyāsyāstīti māyī | vrīhyāditvādinipratyayaḥ | pā. 5-2-116 | pratyayasvaraḥ | śuṣṇam | śuṣa śoṣaṇe | asmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthānnidityanuvṛttau tṛṣiśuṣirasibhyaḥ kit | u. 3-12 | iti napratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | atiraḥ | taraterlaṅi vyatyayena śaḥ | tasya ṅittvena guṇābhāvādṛta iddhātoritīttvam | raparatvam | viduṣṭe tasya | gataṃ mantre gatam | medhirāḥ | midhṛ medhṛ medhāhiṃsanayoḥ | auṇādika iran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | śravāṃsi | nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra! You avātiraḥ — slew — śuṣṇam, the asura of that name, māyin — possessed of various kinds of trickery — and the cause of the drying up of beings, māyābhiḥ — with special devices of deceit opposed to his; or [alternatively] with prajñās, insights into such means. This Yāska says: 'indraḥ śuṣṇaṃ jaghāna' (Ni. 3-11); and this sense is clear in the mantra beginning śuṣṇaṃ pipruṃ (Ṛgveda 1-103-8). Medhirāḥ — the wise performers — viduḥ te — know your greatness, of such a one. For those who thus know, uttira — increase — śravāṃsi, foods. Among the eleven words for 'wisdom' beginning with ketaḥ and ketuḥ, māyā and vayunam are read. Yāska explains the word śravas: 'śravas is a name for food; because it is heard (śrūyate)' (Ni. 10-3)." (Grammatical tail: māyā — māṅ māne with ya by "mācchā-sasi-sūbhyo yaḥ" (Uṇ. 4-109), suffix accent; māyinam — "māyā asya asti," ini as one of the vrīhyādi (Pā. 5-2-116), suffix accent; śuṣṇam — śuṣa śoṣaṇe with causative sense, na by "tṛṣi-śuṣi-rasibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. 3-12) with nit carried over, initial-udātta; atiraḥ — laṅ of tṝ with śa by exception, no guṇa because it is ṅit, so i by "ṛta id dhātoḥ", with r; viduṣ ṭe tasya — as in the previous mantra; medhirāḥ — midhṛ medhṛ medhāhiṃsanayoḥ, the Uṇādi iran, initial-udātta as nit; śravāṃsi initial-udātta as a nab-viṣaya word.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra) — O Indra | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मायिनम् (māyinam) — endowed with many kinds of trickery | शुष्णम् (śuṣṇam) — the asura named Śuṣṇa who harms people | मायाभिः (māyābhiḥ) — by deceitful stratagems suited to the occasion, or by [your] intelligence and capacity | अव अतिरः (ava atiraḥ) — have destroyed | मेधिराः (medhirāḥ) — wise people | विदुः (viduḥ) — know | तेषाम् (teṣām) — to those | that is, to those who perform sacrifices and the like, being wise श्रवांसि (śravāṃsi) — foods (food and other nourishment) | उत् तिर (ut tira) — increase (give in abundance).

original p. 476

Rik 7: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra! The asura named Śuṣṇa was exceedingly deceitful. You killed that asura of deceitful nature by deceitful stratagems, or by your own intelligence and power. Wise people know this greatness of yours. Give them food and other nourishment in abundance.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, you killed the wily Sushna by your stratagems; the wise men have known this your greatness; bestow upon them abundant food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Māyābhiḥ," "māyinam" — māyā means a special kind of deceit, a device, a means, power and capacity: wile, stratagem, etc. [the source's English]. A couple of riks that explain this sense of the word māyā are given below: Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-8; the "१" after तन्वं is printed so. "Maghavan becomes form after form, making māyās about his own body" — editorial and tentative. Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18. "Indra goes about, of many forms, by his māyās; for his ten hundred bay horses are yoked" — editorial and tentative.

रूपं रूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं१ परि स्वाम् ॥

rūpaṃ rūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānastanvaṃ1 pari svām ||

इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥

indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ||

There are many such examples. Since the word māyā is read among the eleven words for "wisdom" beginning with ketaḥ, ketuḥ (Ni. 3-13), māyā also means prajñā, understanding, intelligence, a means, and so on. In considering this sense prajñā, the sage Yāska in the Nirukta, explaining the rik Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6.

मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् । माया मू तु यज्ञियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् ॥

mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyan | māyā mū tu yajñiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇiścarati prajānan ||

says

मूर्धा मूर्तमस्मिन्धीयते मूर्धा यः सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन्स एव प्रज्ञां त्वेतां मन्यन्ते यज्ञियानां देवानां यज्ञसंपादिनामपो यत्कर्म चरति प्रजानन्सर्वाणि स्थानान्यनुसंचरते त्वरमाणः

mūrdhā mūrtamasmindhīyate mūrdhā yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyansa eva prajñāṃ tvetāṃ manyante yajñiyānāṃ devānāṃ yajñasaṃpādināmapo yatkarma carati prajānansarvāṇi sthānānyanusaṃcarate tvaramāṇaḥ

(Ni. "7-27" [?]) — thus plainly giving the word māyā the sense prajñā; and also — Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1. "Bright is one [form] of yours, worshipful the other; you are like the sky, with the two days of different form; for you protect all māyās, O self-powered one; may your bounty be auspicious here, O Pūṣan" — editorial and tentative.

original p. 477

Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि । विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥

śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ||

in the explanation of this rik too —

शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्यज्ञियं ते अन्यद्विषमरूपे ते अहनी कर्म द्यौरिव चासि सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन्भाजनवती ते पूषन्निह दत्तिरस्तु ॥

śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadyajñiyaṃ te anyadviṣamarūpe te ahanī karma dyauriva cāsi sarvāṇi prajñānānyavasyannavanbhājanavatī te pūṣanniha dattirastu ||

(Ni. "12-17" [?]) — he explained the word māyā as prajñā.

"Śuṣṇam" — the asura named Śuṣṇa. The word śuṣṇa also means strength (Ni. 3-9). There are many riks that tell of Indra's killing the asura Śuṣṇa: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-8. "When, O Indra, you slew Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, Vṛtra, [you broke] apart the forts of Śambara" — editorial and tentative.

शुष्णं पिप्रुं कुयवं वृत्रमिन्द्र यदावधीर्वि पुरः शम्बरस्य ॥

śuṣṇaṃ pipruṃ kuyavaṃ vṛtramindra yadāvadhīrvi puraḥ śambarasya ||

In this rik it is said that when Indra destroyed the city of the asura Śambara he killed four asuras, Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava and Vṛtra. Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-11. "The mighty one let out the rushing waters with a stream; he shook apart the firm forts of Śuṣṇa" — editorial and tentative.

उग्रो ययिं निरपः स्रोतसासृजद्वि शुष्णस्य दृंहिता ऐरयत्पुरः ॥

ugro yayiṃ nirapaḥ srotasāsṛjadvi śuṣṇasya dṛṃhitā airayatpuraḥ ||

In this rik it is said that Indra laid siege to the city of the asura Śuṣṇa. There are many riks suggesting such a sense. Besides this, the word śuṣṇa can be given the sense śoṣayitṛ, "one who dries up." In such contexts the sense can be given that Indra, by his power, strikes the cloud that does not pour rain and makes the earth parch, and so brings about rain. In considering this sense Yāska, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-5.

नियुद्व्वणक्षि [?] श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद्व्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना ॥

niyudvvaṇakṣi [?] śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cidvrandino roruvadvanā ||

in explaining this rik, explained the word śuṣṇa as śoṣayituḥ, "one who dries up": "शुष्णस्यादित्यस्य च शोषयितुः" (śuṣṇasyādityasya ca śoṣayituḥ) (Ni. 5-16); and also, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-12.

न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृङ्गिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः ॥

nyāvidhyadilībiśasya dṛḷhā vi śṛṅgiṇamabhinacchuṣṇamindraḥ ||

in this rik too, "निरविध्यदिलाबिलशयस्य दृढानि व्यभिनच्छृङ्गिणं शुष्णमिन्द्रः" (niravidhyadilābilaśayasya dṛḍhāni vyabhinacchṛṅgiṇaṃ śuṣṇamindraḥ): that is, he explained that Indra struck the cloud that stays over the mountain top and, not pouring rain, makes the earth dry up (Ni. "6-20" [?]).

original p. 478

Rik 7: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Ava atiraḥ" — hiṃsitavān asi: "you have struck, smitten, killed."

"Viduḥ te" — "they know you or yours": that is, they know your greatness, or your power and capacity.

"Medhirāḥ" — medhāvantaḥ puruṣāḥ: wise, discerning people and the like.

"Śravāṃsi" — foods, food and nourishment. In explaining the rik āsasrāṇāsaḥ śavasā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-3 [?]) Yāska gives the word śravas the sense of food: "śrava ity annanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ" (Ni. 10-3).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 478–479, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

मायाभिः (māyābhiḥ) — root māṅ māne; "mācchāsasi(sū)bhyo yaḥ" (Uṇ. "4-549" [?]): after māṅ māne, cho chedane, ṣasa svapne, the suffix ya: māya, final-udātta by the suffix accent; for the feminine, ṭāp by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. 4-1-4), unaccented as pit; savarṇa-lengthening, and the single substitute udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5); then bhis, ru and visarga; bhis unaccented, made svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ". मायिनम् (māyinam) — "māyā asya asti": "vrīhyādibhyaś ca" (Pā. 5-2-116) gives ini and ṭhan in the possessive sense after the words of the vrīhi group: ini; the ā dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); accusative singular am: māyinam; the suffix accent. शुष्णम् (śuṣṇam) — root śuṣa śoṣaṇe, with the causative sense included; "tṛṣi-śuṣi-rasibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. "3-292" [?]): after ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām, śuṣa śoṣaṇe, rasa śabde the suffix na, kit and nit; kit, so no laghūpadha-guṇa; the nit accent; ṇ by "raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade" (Pā. 8-4-1): śuṣṇa. अतिरः (atiraḥ) — root tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, bhvādi; laṅ, second singular sip; śap, replaced by Vedic exception by śa: tṝ + a + s; "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) makes śa ṅit, so no guṇa;

Rik 7 grammar closes

स्तोमाः स्तोतार ऋत्विज ओजसा बलेनेशानं जगतो नियामकमिन्द्रमभ्यनूषत । सर्वत्र स्तुतवन्तः । यस्येन्द्रस्य रातयो धनदानानि सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्योपेतानि सन्ति । उत वाथवा भूयसीः सहस्रसंख्याया अप्यधिकाः सन्ति । तमिन्द्रमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ इन्द्रम् । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ईशानम् । लटः शानच् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । धातोरनुदात्तेत्त्वात्तास्यनुदात्तेत्यादिना शानचो ऽनुदात्तत्वम् । ओजसा । नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः । स्तोमाः । अर्तिस्तुस्वित्यादिना मन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अनूषत । णु स्तुतौ । णो नः । लुङ् । व्यत्ययेन झः । तस्यादादेशः । पा. ७-१-५ । च्लेः सिच् । अस्य धातोः कुटादित्वेन सिचो ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । इडभावश्छान्दसः । दीर्घत्वं च । अडागमः । सहस्रम् । कर्दमादीनां च । फि. ३-१० । इति द्वितीयाक्षरमुदात्तम् । रातयः । मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः । उत । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । वा । चादिरनुदात्तः । सन्ति । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति प्रतिषेधात् । स हि व्यवहिते ऽपि भवतीत्युक्तम् । भूयसीः । सहस्रादतिशयेन बह्व्यो भूयस्यः । अत्र विभक्तव्यस्य सहस्रस्य संनिधिबलादुपपदत्वप्रतीतेर्द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ । पा. ५-३-५७ । इति बहुशब्दादीयसुन् । बहोर्लोपो भू च बहोः । पा. ६-४-१५८ । इतीकारलोपः । प्रकृतेर्भू इत्यादेशश्च । ईयसुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । उगितश्चेति ङीप् ॥२१॥

stomāḥ stotāra ṛtvija ojasā baleneśānaṃ jagato niyāmakamindramabhyanūṣata | sarvatra stutavantaḥ | yasyendrasya rātayo dhanadānāni sahasraṃ sahasrasaṃkhyopetāni santi | uta vāthavā bhūyasīḥ sahasrasaṃkhyāyā apyadhikāḥ santi | tamindramiti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || indram | ṛjrendretyādinā ran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | īśānam | laṭaḥ śānac | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | dhātoranudāttettvāttāsyanudāttetyādinā śānaco 'nudāttatvam | ojasā | nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ | stomāḥ | artistusvityādinā manpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | anūṣata | ṇu stutau | ṇo naḥ | luṅ | vyatyayena jhaḥ | tasyādādeśaḥ | pā. 7-1-5 | cleḥ sic | asya dhātoḥ kuṭāditvena sico ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | iḍabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | dīrghatvaṃ ca | aḍāgamaḥ | sahasram | kardamādīnāṃ ca | phi. 3-10 | iti dvitīyākṣaramudāttam | rātayaḥ | mantre vṛṣetyādinā ktinnudāttaḥ | uta | prātipadikasvaraḥ | vā | cādiranudāttaḥ | santi | pratyayādyudāttatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati yadvṛttānnityamiti pratiṣedhāt | sa hi vyavahite 'pi bhavatītyuktam | bhūyasīḥ | sahasrādatiśayena bahvyo bhūyasyaḥ | atra vibhaktavyasya sahasrasya saṃnidhibalādupapadatvapratīterdvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau | pā. 5-3-57 | iti bahuśabdādīyasun | bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ | pā. 6-4-158 | itīkāralopaḥ | prakṛterbhū ityādeśaśca | īyasuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | ugitaśceti ṅīp ||21||

Translation: "The stomāḥ — the praisers, the priests — with ojas, strength, abhy anūṣata: praised on all sides Indra, īśānam, the ruler who governs the world; yasya — of which Indra — the rātayaḥ, gifts of wealth, sahasraṃ santi, are a thousand in number; uta vā — or — bhūyasīḥ, are more even than a thousand. 'That Indra' is the connection with what precedes." (Grammatical tail: indram — ran by "ṛjrendra…", initial-udātta as nit; īśānam — śānac for laṭ, śap dropped, the śānac unaccented because the root is anudātta-marked ("tāsy anudātta…"); ojasā initial-udātta as a nab-viṣaya word; stomāḥ — man by "arti-stu-su…", initial-udātta; anūṣata — ṇu stutau, n by "ṇo naḥ", luṅ, jha by exception, at for it (Pā. 7-1-5), sic for cli, no guṇa because, the root being kuṭādi, sic is ṅit, the absence of iṭ and the lengthening Vedic, augment aṭ; sahasram — second syllable udātta by "kardamādīnāṃ ca" (Phi. 3-10); rātayaḥ — ktin udātta by "mantre vṛṣa…"; uta — the stem accent; vā unaccented as one of the cādi; santi — initial-udātta of the suffix, and not unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" because of the bar "yad-vṛttān nityam", which applies even with words between; bhūyasīḥ — "more than a thousand": since sahasra, the thing to be divided, is near, it is felt as an upapada, so īyasun after bahu by "dvivacana-vibhajyopapade tarab-īyasunau" (Pā. 5-3-57); "bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-158) drops the ī and gives bhū for the stem; initial-udātta as nit; ṅīp by "ugitaś ca".)

original p. 480

Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यस्य (yasya) — of which Indra | रातयः (rātayaḥ) — gifts of wealth | सहस्रम् (sahasram) — as many as thousands | उत वा (uta vā) — or | भूयसीः (bhūyasīḥ) — still more | सन्ति (santi) — are such | ईशानम् (īśānam) — who governs the world | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | स्तोमाः (stomāḥ) — the priests who praise | ओजसा (ojasā) — with all the strength they have | अभि अनूषत (abhi anūṣata) — praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra gives to those who praise him wealth and the like to the number of a thousand, or even more. The priests and other people praise such an Indra using all their strength.

॥ English Translation ॥

The reciters of Sacred hymns praise with all their might Indra, the ruler of the world whose bounties are counted by thousends [sic] or even more.

Īśānam — the lord, the master of the world: "Thr [sic] ruler of the world" [the source's English].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Ojasā" — balena: "with strength, with all the strength they have; with enthusiasm too," and so on.

"Stomāḥ" — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra gives the meaning stotāra ṛtvijaḥ, "priests who praise." When the word stoma is neuter it means "hymn"; when it is masculine, "those who praise."

"Sahasram" — a thousand in number; many.

"Bhūyasīḥ" — more than a thousand; more than can be counted; exceedingly, and so on.

original p. 481

Rik 8 grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 481–482, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

इन्द्रम् (indram) — the suffix ran by "ṛjrendrāgra…" (Uṇ. 2-186); initial-udātta as nit. ईशानम् (īśānam) — root īśa aiśvarye, anudātta-marked, hence ātmanepada; laṭ → śānac by "laṭaḥ śatṛ-śānacau…": īś + āna; śap dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); the śānac, a sārvadhātuka in place of a lakāra, unaccented by "tāsy anudātteṭ…" (Pā. 6-1-186). ओजसा (ojasā) — initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (Phiṭ-sū. "26"). स्तोमाः (stomāḥ) — man after stu by "arti-stu-su…" (Uṇ. "1-138" [?]); the nit accent, initial-udātta. अनूषत (anūṣata) — root ṇu stutau; n for ṇ by "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. 6-1-65); luṅ, cli by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43), sic by "cleḥ sic" (3-1-44); the root is parasmaipada, so the third plural should properly be jhi, but here by exception the ātmanepada jha comes; at for jh by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. 7-1-5): nu + s + ata; the root is in the kuṭādi list, so by "gāṅ-kuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit" (Pā. 1-2-1) sic is ṅit and there is no guṇa; by Vedic procedure no iṭ; the lengthening of the root vowel is also Vedic; augment aṭ: anūṣata. सहस्रम् (sahasram) — by "kardamādīnāṃ ca" (Phiṭ-sū. "59" [?]) the first or the second syllable is udātta: here the second. रातयः (rātayaḥ) — after rā, the udātta ktin by "mantre vṛṣeṣa-paca-mana-vida-bhū-vīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96). उत (uta) — the stem accent. वा (vā) — unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ" (Phiṭ-sū. 84). सन्ति (santi) — root as bhuvi; laṭ, jhi, ant for jh; śap dropped; a of the root dropped by "śnasor allopaḥ" (printed "vā. sū." [sic] 6-4-111): santi, with the accent of the tiṅ suffix. The bar "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66), as was explained earlier, applies even when words stand between, because pūjita is taken again in the sūtra "pūjanāt pūjitam…"; so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not make it unaccented.

original p. 482

Rik 8 grammar closes; close of Sūkta 11

भूयसीः (bhūyasīḥ) — "sahasrād api atiśayena bahvyaḥ." "dvivacana-vibhajyopapade tarab-īyasunau" (Pā. 5-3-57): when a word meaning two or a word for the thing to be divided is the upapada, tarap and īyasun come in their own sense after a subanta or tiṅanta that expresses superiority of one over the other and denotes the property that makes the division. By upapada is meant a word spoken nearby; "tatropapadaṃ saptamīstham" (Pā. 3-1-92) is not meant, since that applies only within the section on roots. The word expressing duality or the thing to be divided need be used only in the analytical phrase; in the taddhita formation its meaning is included, so it need not be used. The sense of the second half of the mantra is that Indra has wealth and grain to the number of a thousand, or wealth exceeding a thousand. With sahasra, the thing to be divided, as the upapada, this sūtra gives īyasun after bahu: bahu + īyas; "bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-158): after bahu, the suffixes iman, iṣṭhan, īyasun lose [their initial] and bahu is replaced by bhū; by "ādeḥ parasya" (Pā. 1-1-54) the loss falls on the first letter of what follows, so the ī is dropped, and by the same sūtra bhū replaces the stem: bhūyas; īyasun is nit, so bhūyas is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197); bhūyas is an ugit stem, so "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6) gives ṅīp in the feminine; in bhūyas + ṅīp, the ṅ is it by "laśakv ataddhite" and the p by "halantyam" (Pā. 1-3-3), dropped by "tasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-9); ṅīp is pit, so unaccented by "anudāttau sup-pitau" (Pā. 3-1-4).

॥८॥

End of Sūkta 11.

original p. 483

॥ ಹನ್ನೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 12 — "agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe" ("The Twelfth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)

चतुर्थानुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्राग्निं दूतमित्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य प्रथमस्य सूक्तस्य कण्वपुत्रो मेधातिथिर्ऋषिः । अपवादाभावादनुवर्तमानं प्राग्घिरण्यस्तूपादित्युक्तं गायत्रमेव छन्दः । अग्निदेवताकत्वं विस्पष्टम् । अत एवानुक्रम्यते । अग्निं द्वादश मेधातिथिः काण्व आग्नेयमग्निनेति पादो द्व्यग्निदैवतो निर्मथ्य आहवनीयश्चेति ॥ विनियोगस्तु । प्रातरनुवाक आग्नेये क्रतौ गायत्रे छन्दस्यग्निं दूतमिति सूक्तम् । अथैतस्या रात्रेर्विवासकाल इति खण्डे ऽग्निमीळे ऽग्निं दूतम् । आ. ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ तथा पृष्ठ्यषडहस्य द्वितीये ऽहनीदमेव सूक्तमाज्यशस्त्रम् । पृष्ठ्यस्याभिप्लवेनोक्ते अहनी इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अग्निं दूतमिति द्वितीये । आ. ७-१० । इति ॥ दर्शपूर्णमासयोः सामिधेनीष्वग्निं दूतमित्येका नमः प्रवक्त्र इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । ईळेन्यो नमस्यस्तिरो ऽग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे ॥ आ. १-२ । इति ॥

caturthānuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatrāgniṃ dūtamityādikasya dvādaśarcasya prathamasya sūktasya kaṇvaputro medhātithirṛṣiḥ | apavādābhāvādanuvartamānaṃ prāgghiraṇyastūpādityuktaṃ gāyatrameva chandaḥ | agnidevatākatvaṃ vispaṣṭam | ata evānukramyate | agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇva āgneyamagnineti pādo dvyagnidaivato nirmathya āhavanīyaśceti || viniyogastu | prātaranuvāka āgneye kratau gāyatre chandasyagniṃ dūtamiti sūktam | athaitasyā rātrervivāsakāla iti khaṇḍe 'gnimīḷe 'gniṃ dūtam | ā. 4-13 | iti sūtritam || tathā pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahasya dvitīye 'hanīdameva sūktamājyaśastram | pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | agniṃ dūtamiti dvitīye | ā. 7-10 | iti || darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sāmidhenīṣvagniṃ dūtamityekā namaḥ pravaktra iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | īḷenyo namasyastiro 'gniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe || ā. 1-2 | iti ||

Translation: "In the fourth anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of these, of the first sūkta, of twelve riks, beginning agniṃ dūtam, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva. Since there is no exception, the meter is the Gāyatrī that continues, as was said, 'up to Hiraṇyastūpa.' That Agni is the deity is clear. Therefore the Anukramaṇī says: 'agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇva āgneyam agnineti pādo dvyagnidaivato nirmathya āhavanīyaś ca' — [the sūkta] agnim, twelve [riks], Medhātithi Kāṇva, to Agni; the pāda agninā has two Agnis as deity, the churned [fire] and the Āhavanīya. Its application: in the morning litany (prātaranuvāka), in the Āgneya rite, in the Gāyatrī meter, the sūkta agniṃ dūtam; laid down in the section athaitasyā rātrer vivāsakāle: 'agnim īḷe, agniṃ dūtam' (Āś. 4-13). Likewise on the second day of the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha this same sūkta is the ājya-śastra; laid down in the section pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī: 'agniṃ dūtam on the second' (Āś. 7-10). In the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa, among the sāmidhenīs, the single [rik] agniṃ dūtam; laid down in the section namaḥ pravaktre: 'īḷenyo namasyas tiro, agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe' (Āś. 1-2)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The fourth anuvāka begins with the twelfth sūkta; this anuvāka has six sūktas. Of these six sūktas, of the first, the sūkta of twelve riks called agniṃ dūtam, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva; the meter is Gāyatrī; the deity is Agni. This is said in the Anukramaṇikā in the section agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ. The order of application: at the time of reciting the mantras of the prātaranuvāka of the Āgneya rite, when the riks in the Gāyatrī meter are recited, this sūkta agniṃ dūtam is to be recited; this is said in the Śrautasūtra of Āśvalāyana in the section athaitasyā rātrer vivāsakāle (Ā. 4-13). And on the second day of the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha rite this sūkta is recited as the ājya-śastra mantras; this is said in Āśvalāyana's sūtra 7-10, in the section pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī, as "agniṃ dūtam iti dvitīye." And in the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, when the riks called sāmidhenī are recited, the rik agniṃ dūtam is to be recited, as is said in the section namaḥ pravaktre; this too is said in section 1-2 of Āśvalāyana's Śrautasūtra: "īḷenyo namasyas tiro 'gniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe." Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 12, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 12 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 12 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 22, 23 ॥ ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–12 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ printed "1–12 medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ" ॥ Devatā — Agni; 6 — Agni Nirmathya and Agni Āhavanīya ॥ printed "agniḥ | 6 — agnir nirmathyo 'gnir āhavanīyaś ca" ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒ग्निं दू॒तं वृ॑णीमहे॒ होता॑रं वि॒श्ववे॑दसम् । अ॒स्य य॒ज्ञस्य॑ सु॒क्रतु॑म् ॥१॥

agníṃ dūtáṃ vṛṇīmahe hótāraṃ viśvávedasam | asyá yajñásya sukrátum ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्निम् । दूतम् । वृणीमहे । होतारम् । विश्वऽवेदसम् ॥ अस्य । यज्ञस्य । सुऽक्रतुम् ॥१॥

agnim | dūtam | vṛṇīmahe | hotāram | viśva-vedasam || asya | yajñasya | su-kratum ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अग्नेर्दूतत्वमेतन्मन्त्रव्याख्याने तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणे समाम्नायते । अग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीदुशनाः काव्यो ऽसुराणाम् । तै. सं. २-५-८-५ । इति । तादृशं देवदूतमग्निमस्मिन्कर्मणि वृणीमहे । संभजामः । कीदृशम् । होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं विश्ववेदसं सर्वधनोपेतम् अस्य प्रवर्तमानस्य यज्ञस्य निष्पादकत्वेन सुक्रतुं शोभनकर्माणं शोभनप्रज्ञं वा ॥ मघमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु वेदस्शब्दः पठितः ॥ होतारम् । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । तृन् । ताच्छील्यादिषु । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणे । परपूर्वत्वे गुणः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । विश्ववेदसम् । बहुव्रीहौ । विश्वं संज्ञायाम् । पा. ६-२-१०६ । इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तः । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सुक्रतुम् । क्रत्वादयश्च । पा. ६-२-११८ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

agner dūtatvam etan-mantra-vyākhyāne taittirīya-brāhmaṇe samāmnāyate | agnir devānāṃ dūta āsīd uśanāḥ kāvyo 'surāṇām | tai. saṃ. 2-5-8-5 | iti | tādṛśaṃ deva-dūtam agnim asmin karmaṇi vṛṇīmahe | saṃbhajāmaḥ | kīdṛśam | hotāraṃ devānām āhvātāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ sarva-dhanopetam asya pravartamānasya yajñasya niṣpādakatvena sukratuṃ śobhana-karmāṇaṃ śobhana-prajñaṃ vā || magham ity-ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu dhana-nāmasu vedas-śabdaḥ paṭhitaḥ || hotāram | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | tṛn | tācchīlyādiṣu | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇe | parapūrvatve guṇaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | viśvavedasam | bahuvrīhau | viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām | pā. 6-2-106 | iti pūrvapadāntodāttaḥ | asya | ūḍidam ity-ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam | sukratum | kratv-ādayaś ca | pā. 6-2-118 | ity-ādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "That Agni is a messenger is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, in explanation of this mantra: 'Agni was the messenger of the gods; Uśanas Kāvya, of the asuras' (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-5-8-5). Such an Agni, messenger of the gods, we vṛṇīmahe — choose, serve — in this rite. What kind? Hotāram — the caller of the gods; viśvavedasam — endowed with all wealth; sukratum — as the accomplisher of this rite now in progress, of excellent action, or of excellent wisdom. Among the twenty-eight words for 'wealth' beginning with magham, vedas is read." Grammar noted briefly: that hotṛ is from hveñ with tṛn in the habitual sense, with saṃprasāraṇa, pūrvarūpa and guṇa, initial-udātta since nit; that viśvavedasam is a bahuvrīhi in which viśva, in a name, ends in udātta (Pā. 6-2-106); that the case-ending of asya is udātta by ūḍ-idam…; and that sukratu has initial accent by Pā. 6-2-118.

original p. 485

Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

दूतम् (dūtam) — the messenger of the gods | होतारम् (hotāram) — one who invokes the gods for sacrifices and the like | विश्ववेदसम् (viśvavedasam) — endowed with all wealth | अस्य यज्ञस्य (asya yajñasya) — of this sacrifice | सुक्रतुम् (sukratum) — the performer of the rite, or one who knows well the procedure of this sacrifice | अग्निम् (agnim) — the deity named Agni | we वृणीमहे (vṛṇīmahe) — choose and invoke (call).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Agni is the messenger of the gods, and he brings them to the sacrificial rites that we perform. This Agni has abundant wealth, and is the chief performer in this sacrifice, or one who knows well the nature of the rite. Such an Agni we choose (we pray to).

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

We select (invoke) Agni, the messenger of Gods, their invoker, the possessor of riches, the perfector of this rite or the highly wise.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

From this 12th sūkta up to the 23rd sūkta, too, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva. These sūktas are not, like the sūktas of the ṛṣi Madhucchandas explained so far, full of tangles; there is no need to supply special words; they are in a fairly easy style and can be understood by all. The style of language of some ṛṣis is very involved; the style of others is easy to understand. In the order stated earlier, at the beginning there are sūktas addressed to Agni, then sūktas addressed to Indra, and after that sūktas of other deities. The descendants of this ṛṣi are the seers of Sūktas 36–50 in this maṇḍala, of the sūktas of the 8th maṇḍala, and of the 2nd sūkta of the 9th maṇḍala. The rik agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe is read in these places: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-5-8-5 and 5-5-6-1 [?]; Tai. Brā. 3-5-2-3; Sāmaveda 1-3; Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā 4-10-2. The dūtam note begins at the foot of p. 485.

original p. 486

Rik 1: Special Topics (continued) and grammar begins

"Dūtam" — in explaining the word dūta, the Bhāṣyakāra cites the Yajurveda sentence "agnir devānāṃ dūta āsīd uśanāḥ kāvyo 'surāṇām" (printed "Tai. Saṃ. 3-5-8-5"; the bhāṣya gives 2-5-8-5): that is, Agni was the messenger of the gods, and Uśanas, son of Kavi, the messenger of the asuras. And the Yajurveda śruti says "parokṣaṃ vā anye devāḥ" — the other gods (those other than Agni) are not visible to us directly. When we humans pour into Agni the oblations we offer, so that they reach the gods, Agni stands between humans and gods, and it is believed that he carries the oblations to the gods. Hence Agni is called the messenger of the gods, as is customary.

"Vṛṇīmahe" — "we choose; we select; select, choose" and so on [the source's own English]. Skandasvāmī explains it as "we pray."

"Viśvavedasam" — sarvadhanopetam — "endowed with all wealth"; the word ratnadhātamam in the first rik of the Ṛgveda, agnim īḷe, supports this sense. Vedas is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with magham (printed "2-3-9" [?]); so vedas is to be given the sense of wealth.

"Sukratum" — śobhana-karmāṇam or śobhana-prajñam: one who has good deeds or good wisdom; that is, one who performs the needed acts of sacrifice and brings the sacrificial rite to completion with all its limbs; one of excellent wisdom; one who knows well the nature of the rites of sacrifice and the like. The word kratu is read both among the twenty-six words for 'work' beginning with apaḥ (Ni. "3-1" [as printed]), and among the eleven words for 'wisdom' beginning with ketaḥ (Ni. 3-13), so kratu has two senses, work and wisdom.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 486–487, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

होतारम् (hotāram) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; tṛn by "tṛn" (Pā. 3-2-135) in the senses of habit, duty and doing it well: hve + tṛ; "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) gives samprasāraṇa, u for the v; pūrvarūpa by "samprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); hu + tṛ: "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) gives guṇa to an ik-final stem before these suffixes; by "tiṅ-śit sārvadhātukam" (Pā. 3-4-113) the tiṅ endings and ś-marked suffixes are sārvadhātuka, and by "ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-114) the other suffixes taught under "dhātoḥ" (Pā. 3-1-91) are ārdhadhātuka; tṛn is neither tiṅ nor śit, so it is ārdhadhātuka, and the u of hu takes guṇa: hotṛ; then the accusative singular am:

original p. 487

Rik 1 grammar closes

"ṛto ṅi-sarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110) gives guṇa of the ṛ with r: hotar + am; "ap-tṛn-tṛc…" (Pā. 6-4-11) lengthens the penultimate: hotāram; hotṛ initial-udātta by the nit accent. विश्ववेदसम् (viśvavedasam) — "viśvaṃ vedo yasya saḥ": a bahuvrīhi; "bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. 6-2-106) — viśva as the first member in a name-bahuvrīhi ends in udātta; without this sūtra viśva would be initial-udātta, being a kvan word, and "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) would keep that; the sūtra overrides it, so the final syllable is udātta. अस्य (asya) — after idam, the genitive ending is udātta by "ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-171). सुक्रतुम् (sukratum) — "kratvādayaś ca" (Pā. 6-2-118): words of the kratu class after su are initial-udātta, so the kratu in sukratu is initial-udātta.

Page 487 (lower) — Sūkta 12, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒ग्निम॑ग्निं॒ हवी॑मभिः॒ सदा॑ हवन्त वि॒श्पति॑म् । ह॒व्य॒वाहं॑ पुरुप्रि॒यम् ॥२॥

agním-agniṃ hávīmabhiḥ sádā havanta viśpátim | havyavā́haṃ purupriyám ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्निम्ऽअग्निम् । हवीमऽभिः । सदा । हवन्त । विश्पतिम् ॥ हव्यऽवाहम् । पुरुऽप्रियम् ॥२॥

agnim-agnim | havīma-bhiḥ | sadā | havanta | viśpatim || havya-vāham | puru-priyam ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The bhāṣya runs onto p. 488.

यद्यप्यग्निः स्वरूपेणैक एव तथापि प्रयोगभेदादाहवनीयादिस्थानभेदात्पावकादिविशेषणभेदाद्वा बहुविधत्वमभिप्रेत्याग्निमग्निमिति वीप्सा । तं हवीमभिराह्वानकरणैर्मन्त्रैः सदा हवन्ते । निरन्तरमनुष्ठातार आह्वयन्ति । कीदृशम् । विश्पतिं विशां प्रजानां होत्रादीनां पालकं हव्यवाहं यजमानसमर्पितस्य हविषो देवान्प्रति वोढारं अत एव पुरुप्रियं बहूनां प्रीत्यास्पदम् ॥ अग्निमग्निम् । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमित्युत्तरस्याम्रेडितसंज्ञायामनुदात्तं चेत्यनुदात्तम् । हवीमभिः । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । आह्वानकरणभूतेषु मन्त्रेषु स्वव्यापारस्वातन्त्र्यात्कर्तृत्वविवक्षयान्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्त इति कर्तरि मनिन् । तस्य छान्दस ईडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति धातोः संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वं गुणावादेशौ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सदा । सर्वैकान्येत्यादिना । पा. ५-३-१५ । सर्वशब्दाद्दाप्रत्ययः । सर्वस्य सो ऽन्यतरस्यां दि । पा. ५-३-६ । इति सभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हवन्त । ह्वेञो लट् । झस्यान्तादेशः । टेरेत्वाभावश्छान्दसः । शपि बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । विश्पतिम् । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हव्यवाहम् । वह प्रापणे । वहश्च । पा. ३-२-६४ । इति ण्विप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पुरुप्रियम् । पुरूणां प्रियम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

yadyapyagniḥ svarūpeṇaika eva tathāpi prayogabhedādāhavanīyādisthānabhedātpāvakādiviśeṣaṇabhedādvā bahuvidhatvamabhipretyāgnimagnimiti vīpsā | taṃ havīmabhirāhvānakaraṇairmantraiḥ sadā havante | nirantaramanuṣṭhātāra āhvayanti | kīdṛśam | viśpatiṃ viśāṃ prajānāṃ hotrādīnāṃ pālakaṃ havyavāhaṃ yajamānasamarpitasya haviṣo devānprati voḍhāraṃ ata eva purupriyaṃ bahūnāṃ prītyāspadam || agnimagnim | nityavīpsayoriti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ | tasya paramāmreḍitamityuttarasyāmreḍitasaṃjñāyāmanudāttaṃ cetyanudāttam | havīmabhiḥ | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | āhvānakaraṇabhūteṣu mantreṣu svavyāpārasvātantryātkartṛtvavivakṣayānyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti kartari manin | tasya chāndasa īḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti dhātoḥ saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatvaṃ guṇāvādeśau | nittvādādyudāttatvam | sadā | sarvaikānyetyādinā | pā. 5-3-15 | sarvaśabdāddāpratyayaḥ | sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di | pā. 5-3-6 | iti sabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvam | havanta | hveño laṭ | jhasyāntādeśaḥ | ṭeretvābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | śapi bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | viśpatim | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | havyavāham | vaha prāpaṇe | vahaśca | pā. 3-2-64 | iti ṇvipratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | purupriyam | purūṇāṃ priyam | samāsāntodāttatvam ||

Translation: "Although Agni is one in his own nature, nevertheless, with a view to his manifoldness — by differences of use, by differences of place such as the āhavanīya [fire] and the rest, or by differences of epithets such as pāvaka [the purifier] — the repetition agnim agnim ('Agni, Agni') is used. Him, havīmabhiḥ — with mantras that serve as the means of invocation — the performers sadā havante — constantly call. What kind of Agni? Viśpatim — protector of the viś, the people: the hotṛ priests and others; havyavāham — the carrier, to the gods, of the oblation offered by the sacrificer; and therefore purupriyam — the dear one of many."

original p. 488

Rik 2: grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

(Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya: agnim agnim — doubled in the sense of vīpsā by "nitya-vīpsayoḥ"; the second member is āmreḍita by "tasya param āmreḍitam" and unaccented by "anudāttaṃ ca"; havīmabhiḥ — hveñ, manin in the agent sense by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante", since the mantras that are instruments of calling are spoken of as independent agents; Vedic ī augment, samprasāraṇa by "bahulaṃ chandasi", pūrvarūpa, guṇa and av; initial-udātta as nit; sadā — dā after sarva (Pā. 5-3-15), sa for sarva by "sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di" (Pā. 5-3-6), initial-udātta by exception; havanta — laṭ of hveñ, ant for jha, no e for the ṭi (Vedic), samprasāraṇa before śap, unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ"; viśpatim — instead of the first-member accent of "patyāv aiśvarye", "parādiś chandasi bahulam" makes the second member initial-udātta; havyavāham — ṇvi by "vahaś ca" (Pā. 3-2-64), the kṛt second member keeping its accent; purupriyam — "purūṇāṃ priyam," the compound final-udātta.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

विश्पतिम् (viśpatim) — the lord, the protector, of the people (the hotṛ priests and others) | हव्यवाहम् (havyavāham) — [the one] who carries to the gods the oblations offered by the sacrificer | पुरुप्रियम् (purupriyam) — dear to all | अग्निमग्निम् (agnim-agnim) — to Agni (who is seen in places such as the āhavanīya) | हवीमभिः (havīmabhiḥ) — with the mantras used for invocation | सदा (sadā) — always | हवन्त (havanta) — [the performers of sacrifices] invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Although Agni is one, he appears separately in different places — the āhavanīya, the gārhapatya and others. He is the protector of all people, beginning with the sacrificer; he carries to the gods the oblations offered in the sacrifice; he is dear to all. The people who perform sacrifices always invoke such an Agni with mantras of invocation.

॥ English Translation ॥

They (offerers of oblations) constantly invoke Agni and Agni again, the lord of men, the bearer of offerings, the beloved of many.

original p. 489

Rik 2: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Agnim-agnim" — "nityavīpsayor iti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ": by pronouncing one word twice the sense "each one" is conveyed. Here it means each Agni: the āhavanīya, the dakṣiṇāgni, the gārhapatya and the others established in different places in the sacrifices.

"Viśpatim" — viśāṃ prajānāṃ patim: the lord, the master, of the subjects or people: "Ruler of men, progeny" [the source's English].

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 489–490, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

अग्निमग्निम् (agnim-agnim) — "nitya-vīpsayoḥ" (Pā. 8-1-4): the word nitya-vīpsayoḥ names the two senses nitya and vīpsā; since there is an expectation of what comes in which sense — an expectation of the place and of what is enjoined — the sūtra "sarvasya dve" (Pā. 8-1-1) is in force as a heading, and the later sūtra "padasya" (Pā. 8-1-16) is connected too. Dve is a numeral, so it expects a counted thing, and since this is a grammar of words, "words" is understood. Nitya means ābhīkṣṇya, repetition; vīpsā means the wish to pervade; in verbal cognition only pervasion appears. When repetition or pervasion is to be shown, two words come in place of the whole word: so, with pervasion meant, two words agnim come in place of the one agnim — agnim agnim, "each Agni." Repetition is a property of an action, so the doubling in that sense comes with a tiṅanta and with a kṛdanta that is an indeclinable. By "tasya param āmreḍitam" (Pā. 8-1-2) the second form of the doubled word is named āmreḍita, and by "anudāttaṃ ca" (Pā. 8-1-3) it is unaccented. हवीमभिः (havīmabhiḥ) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; manin in the agent sense by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75). Although the mantras are instruments in calling, by the maxim "vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti" — as in sthālī pacati, where the pot gets the name of agent — their independence in their own activity is meant, so nothing bars manin in the agent sense: hve + man; the Vedic augment ī: hve + īman; "bahulaṃ chandasi"

original p. 490

Rik 2 grammar closes

(Pā. 6-1-34) gives samprasāraṇa, u for the e-ending root's v, pūrvarūpa, guṇa, av: havīman; instrumental plural bhis; by "svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne" (Pā. 1-4-17) [pada status], loss of n, ru and visarga: havīmabhiḥ; initial-udātta by the nit accent. सदा (sadā) — "sarvaikānya-kiṃ-yat-tadaḥ kāle dā" (Pā. 5-3-15): after sarva, eka, anya, kim, yad, tad in the locative sense of time, dā in its own sense: sarva + dā; "sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di" (Pā. 5-3-6): before a d-initial suffix of the prāgdiśīya group, sa optionally replaces sarva: sadā; "sarvasmin kāle"; properly the suffix accent would make sadā final-udātta, but by exception it is initial-udātta. हवन्त (havanta) — root hveñ; laṭ, jha; ant for jh by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); the e that "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (printed "3-4-79" [?]) would give is absent as a Vedic form; śap: hve + a + anta; "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) gives samprasāraṇa, then pūrvarūpa, guṇa, av: havanta; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). विश्पतिम् (viśpatim) — "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18) would give the first member's accent; setting it aside, "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (printed "pā. sada." [sic] 6-2-199) makes the second member pati initial-udātta. हव्यवाहम् (havyavāham) — "havyaṃ vahati iti havyavāhaḥ, tam"; root vaha prāpaṇe; "vahaś ca" (Pā. 3-2-64): in the Veda, with a subanta as upapada, ṇvi after vah: havya + am + vah + ṇvi; properly the non-surface analysis should be shown as havya + as vah + ṇvi; as a kṛdanta it is a prātipadika, the sup dropped; ṇvi lost part by part; vṛddhi of the penultimate: havyavāha, with the accent of the kṛt second member; accusative singular am: havyavāham. पुरुप्रियम् (purupriyam) — "purūṇāṃ priyas tam": a genitive tatpuruṣa; final-udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223).
