Sūkta 12, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्ने॑ दे॒वाँ इ॒हा व॑ह जज्ञा॒नो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषे । असि॒ होता॑ न॒ ईड्यः॑ ॥३॥

ágne devā́m̐ ihā́ vaha jajñānó vṛktábarhiṣe | asi hótā na ī́ḍyaḥ ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्ने । देवान् । इह । आ । वह । जज्ञानः । वृक्तऽबर्हिषे ॥ असि । होता । नः । ईड्यः ॥३॥

agne | devān | iha | ā | vaha | jajñānaḥ | vṛkta-barhiṣe || asi | hotā | naḥ | īḍyaḥ ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने जज्ञानो ऽरण्योरुत्पन्नस्त्वं वृक्तबर्हिष आस्तरणार्थं छिन्नेन बर्हिषा युक्ताय तं यजमानमनुग्रहीतुमिह कर्मणि हविर्भुजो देवाना वह । सो ऽस्मदर्थं होता देवानामाह्वाता त्वमीड्यः स्तुत्यो ऽसि ॥ देवानित्यत्र संहितायां दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्यनुनासिकभावः । जज्ञानः । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । लिटः कानच् । गमहनेत्युपधालोपः । द्विर्वचने ऽचि । पा. १-१-५९ । इति तस्य स्थानिवद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनम् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । वृक्तबर्हिषे । ओव्रश्चू छेदने । निष्ठेति क्तप्रत्ययः । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । वृक्तं बर्हिर्यस्मै यजमानाय येन वा ऋत्विजा । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । असि । अस्तेः सिप् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । तासस्त्योर्लोपः । पा. ७-४-५० । इति सकारस्य लोपः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । होता । ह्वयतेस्ताच्छील्यादिषु तृन् । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ईड्यः । ईड स्तुतौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । पा. ३-१-१२४ । तित्स्वरिते प्राप्त ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः । पा. ६-१-२१४ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

he agne jajñāno 'raṇyorutpannastvaṃ vṛktabarhiṣa āstaraṇārthaṃ chinnena barhiṣā yuktāya taṃ yajamānamanugrahītumiha karmaṇi havirbhujo devānā vaha | so 'smadarthaṃ hotā devānāmāhvātā tvamīḍyaḥ stutyo 'si || devānityatra saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityanunāsikabhāvaḥ | jajñānaḥ | janī prādurbhāve | liṭaḥ kānac | gamahanetyupadhālopaḥ | dvirvacane 'ci | pā. 1-1-59 | iti tasya sthānivadbhāvāddvirvacanam | cittvādantodāttaḥ | vṛktabarhiṣe | ovraścū chedane | niṣṭheti ktapratyayaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vṛktaṃ barhiryasmai yajamānāya yena vā ṛtvijā | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | asi | asteḥ sip | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | tāsastyorlopaḥ | pā. 7-4-50 | iti sakārasya lopaḥ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | hotā | hvayatestācchīlyādiṣu tṛn | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | īḍyaḥ | īḍa stutau | ṛhalorṇyat | pā. 3-1-124 | titsvarite prāpta īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ | pā. 6-1-214 | ityādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "O Agni! Jajñānaḥ — born of the two araṇis — you, vṛktabarhiṣe, for [the sacrificer] who is equipped with barhis cut for strewing, in order to favour that sacrificer, bring here, to this rite, the gods who eat the oblation. You, hotā, the caller of the gods on our behalf, are īḍyaḥ — worthy of praise." (Grammatical tail: devān — in the Saṃhitā ru by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde", and nasalization by "āto 'ṭi nityam"; jajñānaḥ — janī prādurbhāve, kānac for liṭ, loss of the penultimate by "gama-hana…", doubling because by "dvirvacane 'ci" (Pā. 1-1-59) the lost vowel counts as present, final-udātta as cit; vṛktabarhiṣe — ovraścū chedane with kta, iṭ barred by "yasya vibhāṣā"; "for whom or by whom the barhis has been cut", a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; asi — sip after as, śap dropped, the s of the root dropped by "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-50), not unaccented because it begins the pāda; hotā — tṛn after hve, samprasāraṇa, initial-udātta; īḍyaḥ — īḍa stutau, ṇyat by "ṛhalor ṇyat" (Pā. 3-1-124), where the tit svarita would arise "īḍa-vanda-vṛ-śaṃsa-duhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. 6-1-214) gives initial-udātta.)

Page 491 (lower) — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | जज्ञानः (jajñānaḥ) — [you] born in the araṇi | वृक्तबर्हिषे (vṛktabarhiṣe) — for the sacrificer who has spread the cut sacred grass as seats [for the gods] | इह (iha) — in this rite (sacrifice) | देवान् (devān) — the gods | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring | नः (naḥ) — for us | होता (hotā) — [you] who bring the gods | ईड्यः (īḍyaḥ) — worthy of praise | असि (asi) — you are.

original p. 492

Rik 3: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! You are born (in the araṇi). Such as you are, to favour the sacrificer who has spread and made ready the cut darbha for the gods to come and sit on, bring the gods here. For, since you bring the gods, you are worthy of being praised by all of us.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, when born, bring hither the gods for him who has prepared their seats with the clipped sacred grass; you are their invoker for us and are to be adored.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Jajñānaḥ" — born, arisen: born [the source's English]. "Born Agni" means: in sacrifices people produce fire by rubbing together two pieces of wood called araṇi; hence the usage that Agni is born in the araṇi.

"Vṛktabarhiṣe" — this word has been explained earlier. Barhis is cut darbha. The sense is "for the sacrificer who has spread and made ready such darbha for the gods to come and sit on."

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 492–494, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

देवान् (devān) — in the Saṃhitā an i follows, so "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9): when the n and the aṭ letter are in the same pāda, the n after a long vowel is replaced by ru: devār i; "āto 'ṭi nityam" (printed "8-3-3"): before an aṭ letter, the long ā before the ru is always nasalized; then "bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17) gives y for the r, and "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) drops the y: devām̐ iha. जज्ञानः (jajñānaḥ) — root janī prādurbhāve; liṭ, replaced by kānac by "liṭaḥ kānaj vā" (Pā. 3-2-106); "gama-hana-jana-khana-ghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi"

original p. 493

Rik 3 grammar (continued)

(Pā. 6-4-98): before a vowel-initial kit or ṅit suffix other than aṅ, the penultimate of gam etc. is dropped, so the a after j is dropped: jn + āna; "dvirvacane 'ci" (Pā. 1-1-59): when a vowel that causes doubling follows, a substitute for a vowel counts as that vowel for doubling, so the dropped a counts as present and "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8) gives doubling: jan jn āna; "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-60) removes the n of the reduplicate; by ścutva the dental nasal n becomes the palatal nasal ñ: jajñāna; the suffix being cit, final-udātta. वृक्तबर्हिषे (vṛktabarhiṣe) — root ovraścū chedane, ūdit; "svarati-sūti-sūyati-dhūñ-ūdito vā" (Pā. 7-2-44): after svṛ etc. and ūdit roots the iṭ augment before a val-initial ārdhadhātuka is optional; so after kta by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102), "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. 7-2-15) bars iṭ: vraśc + ta; "oditaś ca" (Pā. 8-2-45): after an o-marked root the t of kta becomes n: vraśc + na; "grahi-jyā-vayi-vyadhi-vaṣṭi-vicati-vṛścati-pṛcchati-bhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca" (Pā. 6-1-16) gives samprasāraṇa, ṛ for the r, and pūrvarūpa: vṛśc + na; "skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca" (Pā. 8-2-29): the s or k at the start of a cluster at the end of a pada or before a jhal is dropped — so the s is dropped. In doing this, the n of the niṣṭhā substitute given by "oditaś ca" (8-2-45) is asiddha by "pūrvatrāsiddham", so the cluster counts as standing before a jhal. By the verse "nakārajāv anusvāra-pañcamau jhali dhātuṣu | sakārajaḥ śakāraś ce ṣāṭ ṭavargas tavargajaḥ" — in roots, an anusvāra or fifth-of-class before a jhal comes from n; ś before c comes from s; and ṣ with a ṭ-class letter comes from the t-class — the ś before c in vraśc is known to come from s: vras + c, with ścutva by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-40). When the cluster-initial loss is made, that ś from ścutva is asiddha by "pūrvatrāsiddham", so the cluster-initial s is found [and dropped]. With the cluster-initial loss, vṛc + na; "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā.

original p. 494

Rik 3 grammar closes

8-2-30): before a jhal or at the end of a pada a palatal becomes a velar, so c → k; here too, in making the velar, the n is asiddha by "pūrvatrāsiddham". One may ask why, the n being asiddha, "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) does not make the c of vraśc ṣ; but by "niṣṭhādeśaḥ ṣatva-svara-pratyaya-iḍvidhiṣu siddho vācyaḥ" (printed "8-2-6 vā. 6") the niṣṭhā substitute counts as effective for rules of ṣatva and the like, so the n is not asiddha and no ṣ arises. This is made clear in the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti and in the Siddhāntakaumudī. Since nṛnamana is read in the kṣubhnādi group to bar that ṇatva, the ṛ gives ṇatva by "aṭ-kupv-āṅ-num-vyavāye 'pi" (Pā. 8-4-2); so by the sūtra mentioned the n would become ṇ, and the form should be vṛkṇaḥ. Here it must be said that, by Vedic procedure, neither the niṣṭhā-natva given by "oditaś ca" nor the ṣatva given by "vraśca-bhrasja…" (Pā. 8-2-36) applies. So vṛc + ta, and with the velar the form vṛkta is obtained. Vṛkta is final-udātta by the suffix accent. As a bahuvrīhi, "vṛktaṃ barhiḥ yasmai yajamānāya" or "vṛktaṃ barhiḥ yena ṛtvijā", it takes the first member's accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1). असि (asi) — root asa bhuvi; laṭ → sip; the śap dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (2-4-72); "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-50): before an s-initial suffix the final s of tās and as is dropped: asi; standing at the beginning of the pāda, it is not unaccented. होता (hotā) — root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; tṛn by "tṛn" (Pā. 3-2-135) in the senses of habit etc.; samprasāraṇa by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34), pūrvarūpa by "samprasāraṇāc ca", guṇa; nominative singular hotā; initial-udātta by the nit accent. ईड्यः (īḍyaḥ) — root īḍa stutau; "ṛhalor ṇyat" (Pā. 3-1-124): after roots ending in ṛ or a consonant, ṇyat; the svarita that "tit svaritam" (Pā. 6-1-185) would give is set aside by "īḍa-vanda-vṛ-śaṃsa-duhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. 6-1-214), which gives initial-udātta.

॥३॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. No svarita is printed on the final syllables of दूत्यम् and बर्हिषि.

Sūkta 12, Rik 4

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ताँ उ॑श॒तो वि बो॑धय॒ यद॑ग्ने॒ यासि॑ दू॒त्यम् । दे॒वैरा स॑त्सि ब॒र्हिषि ॥४॥

tā́m̐ uśató ví bodhaya yád agne yā́si dūtyám | deváir ā́ satsi barhíṣi ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तान् । उशतः । वि । बोधय । यत् । अग्ने । यासि । दूत्यम् ॥ देवैः । आ । सत्सि । बर्हिषि ॥४॥

tān | uśataḥ | vi | bodhaya | yat | agne | yāsi | dūtyam || devaiḥ | ā | satsi | barhiṣi ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने यद्यस्मात्कारणाद्दूत्यं यासि देवानां दूतकर्म प्राप्नोषि तस्मात्कारणादुशतो हविः कामयमानांस्तान्देवान् हविःस्वीकारार्थं वि बोधय । विबोध्य च बर्हिष्यस्मिन्कर्मणि तैर्देवैः सह आ सत्सि । आसीद । आगत्योपविश ॥ तान् । दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति संहितायां रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्यनुनासिकभावः । उशतः । वश कान्तौ । लटः शतृ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणम् । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । यासि । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । दूत्यम् । दूतस्य भागः कर्म वा दूत्यम् । दूतस्य भागकर्मणी । पा. ४-४-१२० । इति यत् । तस्य तित्स्वरितापवादत्वेन यतो ऽनाव इति प्राप्तमाद्युदात्तत्वं सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति निवर्तते । अतस्तित्स्वरितमित्येव भवति । शेषनिघातः । सत्सि । सीदसि । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । लटः सिपि शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । न लुमताङ्गस्येति प्रत्ययलक्षणप्रतिषेधात् पाघ्रेत्यादिना । पा. ७-३-७८ । सीदादेशो न भवति । बर्हिषि । बृह बृहि वृद्धौ । बृंहेर्नलोपश्च । उ. २-११० । इतीसिप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः ॥

he agne yadyasmātkāraṇāddūtyaṃ yāsi devānāṃ dūtakarma prāpnoṣi tasmātkāraṇāduśato haviḥ kāmayamānāṃstāndevān haviḥsvīkārārthaṃ vi bodhaya | vibodhya ca barhiṣyasminkarmaṇi tairdevaiḥ saha ā satsi | āsīda | āgatyopaviśa || tān | dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti saṃhitāyāṃ rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityanunāsikabhāvaḥ | uśataḥ | vaśa kāntau | laṭaḥ śatṛ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | grahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇam | śaturanumo nadyajādī iti vibhakterudāttatvam | yāsi | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | dūtyam | dūtasya bhāgaḥ karma vā dūtyam | dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī | pā. 4-4-120 | iti yat | tasya titsvaritāpavādatvena yato 'nāva iti prāptamādyudāttatvaṃ sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti nivartate | atastitsvaritamityeva bhavati | śeṣanighātaḥ | satsi | sīdasi | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu | laṭaḥ sipi śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | na lumatāṅgasyeti pratyayalakṣaṇapratiṣedhāt pāghretyādinā | pā. 7-3-78 | sīdādeśo na bhavati | barhiṣi | bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau | bṛṃhernalopaśca | u. 2-110 | itīsipratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ ||

Translation: "O Agni! Because you yāsi dūtyam — attain the work of messenger of the gods — therefore uśataḥ — those gods who desire the oblation — vi bodhaya: awaken them, so as to make them accept the oblation; and having awakened them, ā satsi — sit down — with those gods on the barhis in this rite; come and be seated." (Grammatical tail: tān — ru in the Saṃhitā by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde", nasalization by "āto 'ṭi nityam"; uśataḥ — vaśa kāntau, śatṛ, śap dropped, samprasāraṇa by "grahi-jyā…", the case ending udātta by "śatur anumo nady-ajādī"; yāsi — not unaccented, by "yad-vṛttān nityam"; dūtyam — "the share or the work of a messenger", yat by "dūtasya bhāga-karmaṇī" (Pā. 4-4-120); the initial accent of "yato 'nāvaḥ", which would set aside the tit svarita, is withdrawn by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante", so "tit svaritam" holds, the rest unaccented; satsi — = sīdasi: ṣadḷ, the śap after sip dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi", and since "na lumatāṅgasya" bars pratyaya-lakṣaṇa, the sīd of "pā-ghrā…" (Pā. 7-3-78) does not come; barhiṣi — bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau, isi by "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 2-110), the i udātta by the suffix accent.)

Page 495 (lower) — Rik 4: word-meanings

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | यत् (yat) — for which reason | दूत्यम् (dūtyam) — the state of being a messenger of the gods | यासि (yāsi) — you have attained | for that reason उशतः (uśataḥ) — [the gods] who desire the oblation | तान् (tān) — those gods | वि बोधय (vi bodhaya) — awaken (urge) | then देवैः (devaiḥ) — together with the gods | बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — on the darbha grass spread out for seats | आ सत्सि (ā satsi) — sit down.

original p. 496

Rik 4: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! You are the gods' messenger. Therefore rouse those gods who desire the oblation (in the sacrifices), bring them here, and sit with them on the cut darbha made ready for seats.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, as you go as messenger of Gods, awaken them desirous of oblations; sit down with them on the sacred grass.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Barhiṣi" — "for seats": it is the custom to spread darbha cut with its tips so that the gods may sit. Vessels of ghee and the oblations, too, are placed on such spread darbha; this is held to be best and the custom.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 496–497, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

तान् (tān) — by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9) the n becomes ru in the Saṃhitā; by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (printed "8-3-3") the long ā is nasalized; y by "bho-bhago…" (Pā. 8-3-17), and the y dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19): tām̐ uśataḥ. उशतः (uśataḥ) — root vaśa kāntau; laṭ → śatṛ by "laṭaḥ śatṛ…" (Pā. 3-2-124); the śap dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); "grahi-jyā-vayi-vyadhi-vaṣṭi…" (Pā. 6-1-16) gives samprasāraṇa, u for the v, pūrvarūpa by "samprasāraṇāc ca": uśat, accusative plural; the case ending udātta by "śatur anumo nady-ajādī" (Pā. 6-1-173). यासि (yāsi) — root yā prāpaṇe; laṭ, second singular; "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66): a tiṅanta after a word containing yad is not unaccented, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not apply. दूत्यम् (dūtyam) — "dūtasya bhāvaḥ [sic] karma vā"; bhāga means a share, karma an act; in the sense of share it is masculine, in the sense of act neuter, accusative singular. "dūtasya bhāga-karmaṇī" (Pā. 4-4-120): after the genitive of dūta, yat in the senses of share and act;

original p. 497

Rik 4 grammar closes

yat is t-marked, so by "tit svaritam" (Pā. 6-1-185) the svarita would come; setting it aside, "yato 'nāvaḥ" (printed "6-1-213") would give initial-udātta; that is optional by the paribhāṣā "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (printed "Paribhā. 35" [?]), so it does not apply, and the svarita stands; the remaining dū is unaccented by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158). सत्सि (satsi) — meaning sīdasi; root ṣadḷ viśaraṇa-gaty-avasādaneṣu; laṭ → second singular sip: sad + si; the śap dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); "na lumatāṅgasya" (Pā. 1-1-63) bars pratyaya-lakṣaṇa, so the sīda of "pā-ghrā-dhmā…" (Pā. 7-3-78) does not come; car by "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55); wholly unaccented. बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — root bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau; "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. "2-266" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-110): after bṛṃh the suffix isi, with loss of the n; the n is that of the num augment, bṛhi being idit, by "idito num dhātoḥ" (printed "7-1-58"); bṛh + is: laghūpadha-guṇa with r: barhis; the i udātta by the suffix accent; locative singular barhiṣi.

Rik 5: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The bhāṣya and its long grammatical tail fill p. 498.

हे घृताहवन घृतेनाहूयमान दीदिवो दीप्यमानाग्ने त्वं रक्षस्विनो रक्षोयुक्तान्रिषतो हिंसकाञ्छत्रून्प्रत्यस्माकं प्रतिकूलान्दह स्म । सर्वथा भस्मीकुरु ॥ घृतेनाहूयते ऽस्मिन्निति करणाधिकरणयोश्चेत्यधिकरणे ल्युट् । अत्र जुहोतेरविवक्षितकर्मत्वेनाकर्मकत्वाद्घृतस्य करणत्वमेव न तु कर्मत्वम् । अतो नैषा तृतीया च होश्छन्दसि । पा. २-३-३ । इति कर्मणि तृतीया । किंतु कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया । पा. २-३-१८ । इति करणवाचिन्येव । अतः कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् । पा. २-१-३२ । इति समासः । तत्र पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरापवादे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते प्रातिपदिकावस्थायामेव कृते सति पश्चाद्विभक्त्युत्पन्नायामामन्त्रितस्य चेत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । दीदिवः । दीव्यतेर्लिटः क्वसुः । तस्य वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमादिडभावः । द्विर्वचनम् । हलादिः शेषः । उत्तरवकारस्य लोपो व्योर्वलीति लोपः । क्वसुः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । तुजादीनां दीर्घो ऽभ्यासस्य । पा. ६-१-७ । इति दीर्घत्वमभ्यासस्य । संबुद्धावुगिदचामिति नुम् । संयोगान्तस्य लोपः । पा. ८-२-२३ । इति सकारलोपे नकारस्य मतुवसो रु संबुद्धौ छन्दसीति रुत्वम् । विसर्गः । पदात्परत्वादामन्त्रितनिघातः । ननु पूर्वामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वात्तत्पादादित्वेन न निघातोपपत्तिः । न च नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम् । पा. ८-१-७३ । इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधः । उभयोरग्निपदविशेषणत्वेन विशेषवचनत्वात् । अत एव परस्परमनन्वयेनासामर्थ्यात्समर्थः पदविधिः । पा. २-१-१ । इति च नियमात्पूर्वस्य न पराङ्गवद्भावो येनैकपद्येन निघातः स्यात् । अत एवेडे रन्ते ऽदिते सरस्वतीत्यादौ । तै. सं. ७-१-६-८ । पृथक्पृथगाद्युदात्तत्वमिति । उच्यते । अत्र दीदिव इति नाग्निपदस्य विशेषणं किंतु घृताहवनपदस्यैव द्योतनार्थम् । घृताहवन इति विशेष्यत्वेन विवक्षितत्वात् । विशिष्टस्य तु पश्चादग्निविशेषणता । तत्र दीदिवः पदं प्रति घृताहवनपदस्य विशेष्यत्वान्नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरण इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधान्निघातोपपत्तिः । अत एव परस्परविशेषणविशेष्यभावेन सामर्थ्यात्सुबामन्त्रित इति पराङ्गवद्भावे शेषनिघातेनापि स्वरोपपत्तिरिति । इडे रन्त इत्यादौ तु नैवं परस्परान्वय इति वैषम्यम् । रिषतः । रुष रिष हिंसार्था इति भौवादिकस्य लटः शत्रादेशे शपि छान्दसो गुणाभावः । तौदादिकस्य वा रुश रिश हिंसायामित्यस्य छान्दसं षत्वम् । विकरणस्य शस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । रक्षस्विनः । रक्षःशब्दादस्मायामेधास्रजो विनिः । पा. ५-२-१२१ । इति मत्वर्थीयो विनिः । तस्य प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

Translation: "O ghṛtāhavana — O Agni, called with ghee; dīdivaḥ — blazing! You, prati daha sma: burn on every side — turn into ashes completely — the enemies who are rakṣasvinaḥ, accompanied by rākṣasas, riṣataḥ, injurious, hostile to us." (Grammatical tail: ghṛtāhavana — "in whom one is called with ghee": lyuṭ in the locative sense by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca"; since juhoti is here intransitive, its object not being meant, the ghee is an instrument, not an object, so not the object-sense third case of "tṛtīyā ca hoś chandasi" (Pā. 2-3-3) but the instrumental of "kartṛ-karaṇayos tṛtīyā" (Pā. 2-3-18); compound by "kartṛ-karaṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-32); the kṛt second-member accent, which sets aside the first-member accent, is made at the stem stage, and after the ending the vocative is initial-udātta by "āmantritasya ca"; dīdivaḥ — kvasu for liṭ of div, no iṭ by the restriction "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām", doubling, "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ", the second v dropped by "lopo vyor vali", no guṇa as kit, the reduplicate lengthened by "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-7), num in the vocative, the s dropped (Pā. 8-2-23), ru for the n by "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi", visarga; unaccented as a vocative after a word. Objection: the first vocative being treated as absent, dīdivaḥ would begin the pāda and could not be unaccented; and the bar "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) does not apply, since both are specific qualifiers of agni; for the same reason, lacking mutual connection, "samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ" (Pā. 2-1-1) prevents the first from being treated as part of the next, as in "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (T.S. 7-1-6-8), where each is initial-udātta. Answer: here dīdiva qualifies not agni but ghṛtāhavana, which is meant as the qualified term, and the whole then qualifies agni; so the bar of 8-1-73 applies and the loss of accent is in order, and by the qualifier-qualified relation "subāmantrite…" also works; in iḍe rante there is no such mutual connection — hence the difference. riṣataḥ — śatṛ after ruṣa riṣa hiṃsārthāḥ (bhvādi), the absence of guṇa with śap Vedic; or from ruśa riśa hiṃsāyām (tudādi) with Vedic ṣ, no guṇa because śa is ṅit; rakṣasvinaḥ — vini by "as-māyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121), initial-udātta of the suffix.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

घृताहवन (ghṛtāhavana) — [you] called by offering ghee | दीदिवः (dīdivaḥ) — shining | (हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | रक्षस्विनः (rakṣasvinaḥ) — accompanied by rākṣasas | रिषतः (riṣataḥ) — who do harm | प्रति (prati) — to us | विरोधिनः (virodhinaḥ) — the enemies | दह स्म (daha sma) — burn them to ashes.

original p. 499

Rik 5: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar begins

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni! When we call you, we make offerings with ghee. Therefore you shine blazing. As such, burn to ashes those enemies of ours who are accompanied by rākṣasas and who do us harm.

॥ English Translation ॥

Resplendent Agni, invoked by oblations of clarified butter burn down our adversaries defended by evil spirits (Rakshas).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Ghṛtāhavana," "dīdivaḥ" — to call Agni by pouring ghee into him is the custom in sacrifices; and since Agni, when ghee is offered, blazes brightly, the word dīdivaḥ is used here.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 499–502, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

घृताहवन (ghṛtāhavana) — with the analysis "ghṛtena hūyate asmin", "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (printed "pā. sū. sū." [sic] 3-3-117): after a root, lyuṭ in the senses of instrument and locus; so lyuṭ after hu dānādanayoḥ; ana by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. 7-1-1), guṇa, av: havana. Although the root is transitive, its object is not meant, so it is intransitive; hence the ghee is an instrument in the action of hu, not an object; not being an object, the third case of "tṛtīyā ca hoś chandasi" (Pā. 2-3-3) — in the Veda the third, and by ca the second, case after the object of the action of hu — does not come; "kartṛ-karaṇayos tṛtīyā" (Pā. 2-3-18) gives the third case in the instrumental sense: ghṛtena. This is compounded with the kṛdanta havana by "kartṛ-karaṇe kṛtā bahulam" (printed "Pā. 2-1-3" at a line end, the last digit not printed; the bhāṣya gives 2-1-32): a third-case subanta in the sense of agent or instrument is compounded with a connected kṛdanta: ghṛtahavana [sic]. Now "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) would give the first member's accent, but setting it aside "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139)

original p. 500

Rik 5 grammar (continued)

gives the accent of the kṛt second member at the stem stage itself. Then, on adding the vocative singular, "eṅ-hrasvāt saṃbuddheḥ" (Pā. 6-1-69) drops the consonant of the vocative ending after a stem ending in eṅ or a short vowel; ghṛtahavana [sic] becomes a vocative, initial-udātta by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198). दीदिवः (dīdivaḥ) — root divu krīḍā-vijigīṣā-vyavahāra-dyuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu; liṭ, replaced by kvasu by "kvasuś ca" (Pā. 3-2-107): div + vas; "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām" (Pā. 7-2-67): only after roots that are monosyllabic after doubling, roots in ā, and ghasḷ does vas take iṭ; after other roots it does not, so here none; doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8): div div + vas; "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (printed "(Pā. sū.) 7-4-60") removes the v of the reduplicate; "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-7): tujādi is an ākṛtigaṇa, and the reduplicate of its roots is lengthened in the Veda: dīdiv + vas; "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. 6-1-66) drops v or y before a val letter, so the v of the second div: dīdivas; kvasu is kit, so "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) gives no guṇa. Then the vocative singular su; "ugid-acāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70) gives num before a sarvanāmasthāna to ugit non-root stems and to añc that has lost its n: dīdivans + su; su dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68); "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-23) drops the s: dīdivan; "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-1) gives ru for the final of a matup- or vasu-stem before the vocative in the Veda; visarga by "kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-15): dīdivaḥ. It stands after the word ghṛtāhavana, so "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19) makes it wholly unaccented. But here ghṛtāhavana and dīdivaḥ are both vocatives, and "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. 8-1-72) treats the earlier vocative as absent; then the second vocative does not stand after a word, so how could the eighth-chapter loss of accent apply? [For] "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) — sāmānyavacana means the word for the qualified —

original p. 501

Rik 5 grammar (continued)

when a vocative in apposition expressing a qualifier follows, the vocative that expresses the qualified is not treated as absent; so the bar would apply, and with the "absent" treatment not arising, the word would follow another word and the eighth-chapter loss of accent would be in order — but this cannot be said, because here both vocatives ghṛtāhavana and dīdivaḥ qualify agne: agne is the general term and both are specific terms, so the bar does not apply. In the same way both vocatives are connected with agne, not with each other; lacking mutual connection, they lack sāmarthya, the capacity of conveying a joint sense. The treatment of a subanta before a vocative as part of the following vocative for accent, given by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. 2-1-2), is a rule about words, and by the paribhāṣā "samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ" (Pā. 2-1-1) it applies only where there is sāmarthya; here neither has it, so the parāṅgavat treatment does not arise either, and one cannot say that, treating ghṛtāhavana dīdiva as one word, the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198) makes ghṛ udātta and "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158) the rest unaccented. Hence, just as in the mantra "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-6-8), where there is no mutual connection, each vocative is initial-udātta by the sixth-chapter sūtra, so here too each should be separately initial-udātta — how then is the eighth-chapter loss of accent justified? So one may object. The answer: here dīdivaḥ is not a qualifier of agne but of ghṛtāhavana; ghṛtāhavana is meant as the qualified term, and then the qualified-plus-qualifier dīdivaḥ ghṛtāhavana becomes a qualifier of agne. With reference to dīdivaḥ, ghṛtāhavana is the qualified, hence the general term; so "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) bars the "absent" treatment, the word follows another word, and the eighth-chapter loss of accent is in order. In this way dīdivaḥ and ghṛtāhavana are mutually connected and have sāmarthya, so "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. 2-1-2) gives the parāṅgavat treatment too; with it, ghṛtāhavana dīdivaḥ count as one word, so the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" makes ghṛ udātta and "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158) the rest unaccented; in this way too dīdivaḥ is wholly unaccented. In "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-6-8) there is no such mutual connection, so the full loss of accent does not arise there, and each vocative by the sixth-chapter sūtra

original p. 502

Rik 5 grammar closes

is initial-udātta. Thus between ghṛtāhavana dīdivaḥ and iḍe rante there is the difference of the presence and absence of mutual connection. रिषतः (riṣataḥ) — root ruṣa riṣa hiṃsārthāḥ, in the bhvādi (first) class; laṭ, replaced by śatṛ by "laṭaḥ śatṛ-śānacau…" (Pā. 3-2-124); the vikaraṇa śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); with it the laghūpadha-guṇa of "puganta-laghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86) would arise, but by Vedic procedure there is no guṇa: riṣ + a + at; pararūpa of the two a's by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97): riṣat. Or the root ruśa riśa hiṃsāyām, in the tudādi class: with śatṛ for laṭ, the vikaraṇa śa by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-77); it is apit, so ṅit by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4), and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) bars the laghūpadha-guṇa; the ṣ here comes by Vedic procedure; pararūpa: riṣat; either way the accusative plural is riṣataḥ. रक्षस्विनः (rakṣasvinaḥ) — rakṣas ends in as, so "as-māyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) gives vini in the possessive sense after words in as and after māyā, medhā, sraj: rakṣasvin; accusative plural śas: rakṣasvinaḥ, initial-udātta by the suffix accent.

Rik 6: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ the closing "॥२२॥" is the varga number

अग्निमन्थने ऽग्निनाग्निः समिध्यत इत्येषानुवचनीया । प्रातर्वैश्वदेव्यां प्रैषित इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना । आ. २-१६ । इति ॥ एषैवाग्निमत इत्यस्यानुवाक्या । अथाग्नेय्या इति खण्डे ऽग्नावग्निप्रणयन इत्युपक्रम्य सूत्रितम् । यद्वो वयं प्रमिनाम व्रतान्यग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते । आ. ३-१३ । इति ॥

agnimanthane 'gnināgniḥ samidhyata ityeṣānuvacanīyā | prātarvaiśvadevyāṃ praiṣita iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | agnināgniḥ samidhyate tvaṃ hyagne agninā | ā. 2-16 | iti || eṣaivāgnimata ityasyānuvākyā | athāgneyyā iti khaṇḍe 'gnāvagnipraṇayana ityupakramya sūtritam | yadvo vayaṃ pramināma vratānyagnināgniḥ samidhyate | ā. 3-13 | iti ||

अग्निराहवनीयाख्यस्तस्मिन्नुपक्षिप्यमाणेनाग्निना निर्मथ्येन प्रणीतेन वा सह समिध्यते । सम्यग्दीप्यते । कीदृशो ऽग्निः । कविर्मेधावी गृहपतिर्यजमानगृहस्य पालको युवा नित्यतरुणो हव्यवाट् हविषो वोढा जुह्वास्यो जुहूरूपेण मुखेन युक्तः ॥ गृहपतिः । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । युवा । यु मिश्रणे । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिव इति कनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । हव्यं वहतीति हव्यवाट् । वहश्चेति ण्विप्रत्ययः । णित्त्वादुपधावृद्धिः । गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जुह्वास्यः । हूयते ऽनयेति जुहूः । हुवः श्लुवच्च । उ. २-६० । इति क्विप् । तत्संनियोगाद्दीर्घः । श्लुवद्भावाद्द्विर्भावः । चुत्वजश्त्वे । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । जुहूरास्यं यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । शेषनिघातः । यणादेश उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितो ऽनुदात्तस्य । पा. ८-२-४ । इत्याकारः स्वरितः ॥२२॥

agnirāhavanīyākhyastasminnupakṣipyamāṇenāgninā nirmathyena praṇītena vā saha samidhyate | samyagdīpyate | kīdṛśo 'gniḥ | kavirmedhāvī gṛhapatiryajamānagṛhasya pālako yuvā nityataruṇo havyavāṭ haviṣo voḍhā juhvāsyo juhūrūpeṇa mukhena yuktaḥ || gṛhapatiḥ | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yuvā | yu miśraṇe | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidiva iti kanin | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | havyaṃ vahatīti havyavāṭ | vahaśceti ṇvipratyayaḥ | ṇittvādupadhāvṛddhiḥ | gatikārakopapadātkṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | juhvāsyaḥ | hūyate 'nayeti juhūḥ | huvaḥ śluvacca | u. 2-60 | iti kvip | tatsaṃniyogāddīrghaḥ | śluvadbhāvāddvirbhāvaḥ | cutvajaśtve | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | juhūrāsyaṃ yasyeti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | śeṣanighātaḥ | yaṇādeśa udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya | pā. 8-2-4 | ityākāraḥ svaritaḥ ||22||

Translation: "In the rite of the churning of fire, this [rik] agninā agniḥ samidhyate is the anuvacanīya; in the section 'prātarvaiśvadevyāṃ praiṣite' it is laid down: 'agninā agniḥ samidhyate; tvaṃ hy agne agninā' (Āśv. 2-16); and this very rik is the anuvākyā of the Agnimat [offering]; in the section 'athāgneyyāḥ,' beginning with the agnipraṇayana, it is laid down: 'yad vo vayaṃ pramināma vratāni; agninā agniḥ samidhyate' (Āśv. 3-13). The fire called Āhavanīya is samidhyate — well kindled — together with the fire, churned or brought forward, that is being put into it. What is the fire like? Kaviḥ — wise; gṛhapatiḥ — the protector of the sacrificer's house; yuvā — ever young; havyavāṭ — the bearer of the oblation; juhvāsyaḥ — having as its mouth the juhū, the sacrificial ladle." (Grammatical tail: gṛhapatiḥ — the first member's accent by "patyāv aiśvarye"; yuvā — yu miśraṇe with kanin, initial-udātta as nit; havyavāṭ — "he carries the oblation", ṇvi by "vahaś ca", vṛddhi of the penultimate as ṇit, the kṛt second-member accent by "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt"; juhvāsyaḥ — juhū "that with which one offers": kvip by "huvaḥ śluvac ca" (Uṇ. 2-60), the lengthening that goes with it, doubling as if after ślu, c-series and jaś, final-udātta by the stem accent; in the bahuvrīhi "whose mouth is the juhū" that accent alone remains, the rest unaccented; after the yaṇ substitute the ā is svarita by "udātta-svaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (Pā. 8-2-4).)

Page 503 (lower) — Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्निः (agniḥ) — the fire called Āhavanīya | अग्निना (agninā) — by the fire churned out of the araṇi | सम् इध्यते (sam idhyate) — is kindled, blazes well | such a fire कविः (kaviḥ) — wise, discerning | गृहपतिः (gṛhapatiḥ) — protector of the sacrificer's house | युवा (yuvā) — ever youthful | हव्यवाट् (havyavāṭ) — one who carries the oblation to the gods | जुह्वास्यः (juhvāsyaḥ) — one whose mouth is the juhū [ladle].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

At the beginning of the sacrifice, they produce fire by churning in the araṇi; with that fire they kindle the other fires, the Gārhapatya and the rest. Such a fire is very wise, a protector of the sacrificer's house, ever youthful, a bearer of the oblation to the gods; the instrument of offering called juhū is his mouth.

original p. 504

Rik 6: English, Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni is kindlod [sic] by Agni, the ever young and wise, the gaurdian [sic] of the dwelling (of the Sacrificer) the bearer of offerings, whose mouth is the sacrificial spoon.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Agninā, agniḥ" — one fire being kindled from another means: at the start of the sacrifice, with the fire produced by rubbing and churning the piece of wood called araṇi, they kindle the other fires. In the sacrifice the fire must be produced from the araṇi itself, while reciting this rik; fire already produced and kept ready in some other way is not used in the sacrifice.

The order of application of this rik is as follows: at the time of the churning of fire, the rik agninā agniḥ samidhyate is to be recited. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section prātarvaiśvadevyāṃ praiṣite, which says that the riks agninā agniḥ samidhyate (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-12-6) and tvaṃ hy agne agninā are to be recited; and this rik is also used as the puronuvākyā. And the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section athāgneyyāḥ, in the sūtra agnāv agnipraṇayane, says that the rik yad vo vayaṃ pramināma (Ṛg. Saṃ. 10-2-4) is to be used as the yājyā mantra, and the rik agninā agniḥ samidhyate (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-12-6) is the puronuvākyā mantra.

"Kaviḥ" — wise, intelligent, discerning: the wise etc. [the source's English].

"Gṛhapatiḥ" — yajamāna-gṛhasya pālakaḥ — the protector of the sacrificer's house: it is the āhitāgni — one who performs sacrifices and has established the sacred fires — who is meant. An āhitāgni is one who has produced fire at the start of his sacrificial life by the rite called agnyādhāna and used it in the sacrifices that follow. The fire thus consecrated must be protected as long as he lives. Therefore, since Agni is always in the sacrificer's house and is favourable to the sacrifices he performs, the custom of calling Agni gṛhapati may have arisen. The word gṛhapatiḥ is read in the riks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6; 1-36-5; 1-60-4; 2-1-2; 4-9-4; 6-15-13; 6-48-8; 7-16-5; 8-60-19; 10-122-1; the word gṛhapatim in the riks Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-11-5; 5-8-1; 5-8-2; 6-16-42; 6-53-2; 6-1-1 [?]; 10-118-6; and the word gṛhapate in the rik 6-15-19.

original p. 505

Rik 6: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

"Yuvā" — nityataruṇa: always young. Since Agni is always blazing, kindled by oblations such as ghee and samidh sticks and other sacrificial substances, he is always shining with flames. Because he always shines in the same way, it is customary to call Agni yuvā, young.

"Havyavāṭ" — havyaṃ vahatīti havyavāṭ: because he carries to the gods the oblations offered in the fire, he is havyavāṭ: "he who carries the oblation."

"Juhvāsyaḥ" — juhū is the wooden vessel shaped like a ladle (sauṭu), of a stated length, used when offering ghee in sacrifices; the method of making this sacrificial instrument, its shape and dimensions, the material and manner of its making, and such things are explained in the Śulba-sūtras. When the juhū is filled with ghee and poured out, the flames of Agni, called his seven tongues, lap it up; so Agni is juhvāsyaḥ: "one whose mouth is the juhū," or "one who has a juhū-vessel in his mouth," or "one whose mouth takes the form of the vessel juhū" — it is customary to call him so.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 505–506, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

गृहपतिः (gṛhapatiḥ) — "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18): in a tatpuruṣa, when pati in the sense of lordship is the second member, the first member keeps its own accent. Gṛha here: "gehe kaḥ" (printed "Pā. sū. 3-1 44" [sic]): when a house is the agent, ka after grah; so with ka after grah, samprasāraṇa by "grahi-jyā-vayi…" (Pā. 6-1-16) gives gṛha. Or the root gṛhū grahaṇe, in the bhvādi class, with ka conditioned by the penultimate ik by "igupadha-jñā-prī-kiraḥ kaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-135), also gives gṛha. Either way gṛha is final-udātta by the suffix accent, and "patyāv aiśvarye" keeps that accent. युवा (yuvā) — root yu miśraṇe; "kanin yu-vṛṣi-takṣi-rāji-dhanvi-dyu-pratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. "1-154") gives kanin after yu; yuvan initial-udātta by the nit accent; in the nominative singular, loss of su, lengthening of the penultimate and loss of n: yuvā. हव्यवाट् (havyavāṭ) — "havyaṃ vahati iti havyavāṭ": with havya as upapada, after the root vah "vahaś ca" (printed "Pā. sū. 4-2-64" [sic]; the bhāṣya says vahaś ca, Pā. 3-2-64) gives ṇvi in the Veda when a subanta is the upapada; some hold that this ṇvi is used in the classical language too, as the Śekharakāra states;

original p. 506

Rik 6 grammar closes

the suffix being ṇit, "ata upadhāyāḥ" (printed "71-116" [sic]) gives vṛddhi of the penultimate; all the letters of ṇvi are lost: havyavāh; vāh is final-udātta by the root accent; even after compounding, "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) keeps that accent as that of the kṛt second member. Then the nominative singular su is dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68); "ho ḍhaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-31) gives ḍh for an h before a jhal or at the end of a pada: havyavāḍh; jaśtva by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. 8-2-39), ḍ; car by "vāvasāne" (Pā. 8-4-56): havyavāṭ. जुह्वास्यः (juhvāsyaḥ) — "hūyate 'nena iti juhūḥ": "huvaḥ śluvac ca" (Uṇ. "2-215" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-60): after hu dānādanayoḥ, kvip, the lengthening of the root and ślu-like treatment of the suffix: hu + kvip, the lengthening by this sūtra itself: hū; the kvip being like ślu, doubling by "ślau" (Pā. 6-1-10); the reduplicate shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-59); for its h, "kuhoś cuḥ" (Pā. 7-4-62) gives a palatal — jh, the voiced aspirate matching h; jaś by "abhyāse car ca" (Pā. 8-4-54): j: juhū; the kvip is lost; final-udātta by the stem accent. In the bahuvrīhi "juhūḥ āsyaṃ yasya saḥ juhvāsyaḥ", "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) keeps the first member's accent; by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158) the rest except the ū are unaccented; the udātta ū becomes v by "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. 6-1-77); and "udātta-svaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (Pā. 8-2-4) makes the unaccented vowel after a yaṇ that replaced an udātta or svarita svarita: so the ā is svarita.

॥६॥

original p. 506

Sūkta 12, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

क॒विम॒ग्निमुप॑ स्तुहि स॒त्यध॑र्माणमध्व॒रे । दे॒वम॑मीव॒चात॑नम् ॥७॥

kavím agním úpa stuhi satyádharmāṇam adhvaré | devám amīvacā́tanam ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

कविम् । अग्निम् । उप । स्तुहि । सत्यऽधर्माणम् । अध्वरे ॥ देवम् । अमीवऽचातनम् ॥७॥

kavim | agnim | upa | stuhi | satya-dharmāṇam | adhvare || devam | amīva-cātanam ||7||

original p. 507

Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे स्तोतृसंघ अध्वरे क्रतावग्निमुपस्तुहि । उपेत्य स्तुतिं कुरु । कीदृशम् । कविं मेधाविनं सत्यधर्माणं सत्यवदनरूपेण धर्मेणोपेतं देवं द्योतमानममीवचातनममीवानां हिंसकानां शत्रूणां रोगाणां वा घातकम् ॥ सत्यं धर्मो यस्येति सत्यधर्मा । धर्मादनिच् केवलात् । पा. ५-४-१२४ । इत्यनिच् समासान्तः । अन्तःपदेन तस्य समासत्वाभिधानाद्बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे शेषनिघातेनानुदात्तत्वम् । अमीवशब्दो ऽम रोग इत्यस्मात् शेवायहूजिह्वाग्रीवाप्वामीवाः । उ. १-१५४ । इति वन्प्रत्यय ईडागमश्च निपातितः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । चतेः चदे याचने चेत्यस्माद्धिंसार्थात् । णिजन्तान्नन्द्यादित्वात् ल्युः । पा. ३-१-१३४ । योरनादेशः । पा. ७-१-१ । णेरनिटीति णेर्लोपः । लितीति धातोरकारस्योदात्तत्वम् । न च स्वरे कर्तव्ये णिलोपस्य स्थानिवद्भावः । न पदान्तद्विर्वचनेत्यादिना प्रतिषेधात् । पा. १-१-५८ । अमीवानां चातन इति समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते ॥

he stotṛsaṃgha adhvare kratāvagnimupastuhi | upetya stutiṃ kuru | kīdṛśam | kaviṃ medhāvinaṃ satyadharmāṇaṃ satyavadanarūpeṇa dharmeṇopetaṃ devaṃ dyotamānamamīvacātanamamīvānāṃ hiṃsakānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ rogāṇāṃ vā ghātakam || satyaṃ dharmo yasyeti satyadharmā | dharmādanic kevalāt | pā. 5-4-124 | ityanic samāsāntaḥ | antaḥpadena tasya samāsatvābhidhānādbahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve śeṣanighātenānudāttatvam | amīvaśabdo 'ma roga ityasmāt śevāyahūjihvāgrīvāpvāmīvāḥ | u. 1-154 | iti vanpratyaya īḍāgamaśca nipātitaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | cateḥ cade yācane cetyasmāddhiṃsārthāt | ṇijantānnandyāditvāt lyuḥ | pā. 3-1-134 | yoranādeśaḥ | pā. 7-1-1 | ṇeraniṭīti ṇerlopaḥ | litīti dhātorakārasyodāttatvam | na ca svare kartavye ṇilopasya sthānivadbhāvaḥ | na padāntadvirvacanetyādinā pratiṣedhāt | pā. 1-1-58 | amīvānāṃ cātana iti samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva śiṣyate ||

Translation: "O company of praisers! In the adhvara, the sacrifice, upa stuhi — approaching, sing praise to Agni. What kind of Agni? Kavim — wise; satyadharmāṇam — endowed with the nature of speaking truth; devam — shining; amīvacātanam — the destroyer of the amīvas, of those who harm, of enemies or of diseases." (Grammatical tail: satyadharmā — "whose dharma is truth": the samāsānta anic by "dharmād anic kevalāt" (Pā. 5-4-124); since it is taught as part of the compound, the bahuvrīhi keeps the first member's accent and the rest is unaccented; amīva — from ama roge, formed irregularly with van and the augment ī by "śevā-yahū-jihvā-grīvā-pvāmīvāḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154), initial-udātta as nit; cātana — from cate/cade yācane in the sense of hurting, with ṇic, lyu as one of the nandyādi (Pā. 3-1-134), ana for yu (Pā. 7-1-1), ṇi dropped by "ṇer aniṭi", the root's a udātta by "liti"; the loss of ṇi is not treated as present for accent, by the bar "na padānta-dvirvacana…" (Pā. 1-1-58); in the compound "amīvānāṃ cātanaḥ" the kṛt second member keeps that accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

O priests and others who sing praise! कविम् (kavim) — the wise one | सत्यधर्माणम् (satyadharmāṇam) — whose nature is truth and dharma | देवम् (devam) — shining | अमीवचातनम् (amīvacātanam) — the destroyer of enemies, or the destroyer of diseases | अग्निम् (agnim) — Agni | अध्वरे (adhvare) — in the sacrificial rite | उपस्तुहि (upastuhi) — standing near, praise [him].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests and others! This Agni whom you are praising is very wise, of the nature of truth and dharma (or whose dharma — conduct — is truth itself), shining, a destroyer of enemies or a remover of diseases and such troubles. Stand near this Agni in the rite we perform and praise him.

original p. 508

Rik 7: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

Praise, in the sacr'fice [sic], Agni, the wise, the observer of truth, the radiant, the remover of disease.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This rik is addressed to the priests who are praising Agni.

"Satyadharmāṇam" — satyaṃ dharmo yasya: truth itself is his nature; or satyavadana-rūpeṇa dharmeṇopetam — one whose nature is to speak only the truth.

"Amīvacātanam" — amīvānāṃ hiṃsakānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ rogāṇāṃ vā ghātakam — "the destroyer of enemies or of diseases." This word occurs not only in this rik but in these riks too:

विप्रः स उच्यते भिषग्रक्षोहामीवचातनः । vipraḥ sa ucyate bhiṣag rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-6) ("He is called the sage, the physician, slayer of rākṣasas, driver-out of disease." — mine and tentative.)

आपो इद्वा उ भेषजीरापो अमीवचातनीः । āpo id vā u bheṣajīr āpo amīvacātanīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-137-6) ("The waters are indeed healing, the waters are expellers of disease." — mine and tentative.)

In the first example, the words bhiṣak and rakṣohā support the sense of "destroyer of diseases and of enemies." In the second example the word bheṣajīḥ indicates the removal of disease; hence for this word the sense "remover of disease" fits well.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 508–509, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

सत्यधर्माणम् (satyadharmāṇam) — "satyaṃ dharmaḥ yasya saḥ satyadharmā", a bahuvrīhi. "dharmād anic kevalāt" (Pā. 5-4-124): after a bahuvrīhi ending in dharma that follows a bare (kevala) first member, anic comes and becomes the final part of the compound; kevala means not accompanied by any word other than the second member: satyadharma + an; the final a of dharma dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148): satyadharman. By "samāsāntāḥ" (Pā. 5-4-68) anic is joined to the compound as its final part, so the first member keeps its accent and the rest is unaccented by the rule for the remainder. अमीवचातनम् (amīvacātanam) — the word amīva: after the root ama roge, "śeva-yahva-jihvā-grīvā-pvāmīvāḥ" (Uṇ. "1-152"; the bhāṣya gives 1-154): these words are formed irregularly with van.

original p. 509

Rik 7 grammar closes

After śīṅ svapne, van with guṇa gives śeva; here final-udātta is laid down irregularly; otherwise, by "iṇ-śībhyāṃ van" (Uṇ. 1-150) van would come and the nit accent would make it initial-udātta. "yānti anena iti yahvaḥ": after yā prāpaṇe, van with the huk augment and shortening, irregularly: yahva. "lihanti anayā iti jihvā": after liha āsvādane, van with j for the l and no guṇa, irregularly. "giranti anayā iti grīvā": after gṝ nigaraṇe, van with the augment ī, irregularly; gṛ + īva with yaṇ: grīva. After āpḷ vyāptau, van: āpva. After ama, van with the augment ī, irregularly: amīva; van is nit, so initial-udātta by the nit accent. Cātana: the root cate cade yācane ca is also in the sense of hurting; after it ṇic; vṛddhi of the penultimate by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (printed "7-1-116" [sic]): cāt + i; lyu by "nandi-grahi-pacādibhyo lyu-ṇiny-acaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-134); ana for it by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. 7-1-1); ṇic dropped by "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. 6-4-51): cātana; by "liti" (Pā. 6-1-193) the vowel before an l-marked suffix is udātta, so the ā of cāt is udātta. Here, in making the accent, the loss of ṇi, conditioned by what follows, would by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. 1-1-57) count as present — a substitute for a vowel, conditioned by what follows, counts as the original when an operation is made on what precedes it; that sthānivadbhāva is barred by "na padānta-dvirvacana-vare-yalopa-svara-savarṇānusvāra-dīrgha-jaś-car-vidhiṣu" (Pā. 1-1-58), so it does not arise. As the genitive tatpuruṣa "amīvānāṃ cātanaḥ", by "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) the kṛt second member keeps that accent.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यस्त्वाम॑ग्ने ह॒विष्प॑तिर्दू॒तं दे॑व सप॒र्यति॑ । तस्य॑ स्म प्रावि॒ता भ॑व ॥८॥

yas tvā́m agne havíṣpatir dūtáṃ deva saparyáti | tásya sma prāvitā́ bhava ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यः । त्वाम् । अग्ने । हविःऽपतिः । दूतम् । देव । सपर्यति ॥ तस्य । स्म । प्रऽअविता । भव ॥८॥

yaḥ | tvām | agne | haviḥ-patiḥ | dūtam | deva | saparyati || tasya | sma | pra-avitā | bhava ||8||

original p. 510

Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने देव यो हविष्पतिर्यजमानो देवदूतं त्वां सपर्यति परिचरति तस्य यजमानस्य प्राविता भव स्म । अवश्यं रक्षको भव ॥ हूयत इति हविः । अर्चिशुचीत्यादिना । उ. २-१०९ । इसिः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । हविषः पतिर्हविष्पतिः । नित्यं समासे ऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य । पा. ८-३-४५ । इति षत्वम् । पत्यावैश्वर्ये इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सपरशब्दात्कण्ड्वादिभ्यो यक् । पा. ३-१-२७ । इति यक् । धातुप्रकरणाद्गुणप्रतिषेधाद्यर्थात्कः कित्त्वाच्च सपरशब्दस्य धातुत्वात्ततो विहितस्य यक आर्धधातुकत्वे सत्यतो लोप इति लोपः । सनाद्यन्ता धातव इति धातुसंज्ञायां तिप् । कर्तरि शप् । तस्मिन्पूर्वस्यातो गुण इति पररूपत्वम् । यकः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । शपा सह यकैकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति प्रतिषेधात् ॥

he agne deva yo haviṣpatiryajamāno devadūtaṃ tvāṃ saparyati paricarati tasya yajamānasya prāvitā bhava sma | avaśyaṃ rakṣako bhava || hūyata iti haviḥ | arciśucītyādinā | u. 2-109 | isiḥ | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | haviṣaḥ patirhaviṣpatiḥ | nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya | pā. 8-3-45 | iti ṣatvam | patyāvaiśvarye iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | saparaśabdātkaṇḍvādibhyo yak | pā. 3-1-27 | iti yak | dhātuprakaraṇādguṇapratiṣedhādyarthātkaḥ kittvācca saparaśabdasya dhātutvāttato vihitasya yaka ārdhadhātukatve satyato lopa iti lopaḥ | sanādyantā dhātava iti dhātusaṃjñāyāṃ tip | kartari śap | tasminpūrvasyāto guṇa iti pararūpatvam | yakaḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | śapā saha yakaikādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati yadvṛttānnityamiti pratiṣedhāt ||

Translation: "O Agni, O god! The sacrificer who is haviṣpati — lord of the oblation — and saparyati, serves you, the messenger of the gods: of that sacrificer, prāvitā bhava sma — be the protector; surely be his protector." Grammar noted briefly: that haviḥ is "that which is offered," with isi (Uṇ. 2-109); haviṣpati has the visarga turned to ṣ by Pā. 8-3-45, keeping the first member's accent; saparyati is a denominative from sapara in the kaṇḍvādi class with yak (Pā. 3-1-27); and the verb is not lowered because a relative word yaḥ precedes it.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

देव (deva) — shining | (हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | हविष्पतिः (haviṣpatiḥ) — the sacrificer who offers you oblations | दूतम् (dūtam) — messenger of the gods | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | सपर्यति (saparyati) — worships (serves) | तस्य (tasya) — of that sacrificer | प्राविता (prāvitā) — as chief protector | भव स्म (bhava sma) — be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O shining Agni! The sacrificer who offers oblations to you worships you, the messenger of the gods. Protect such a sacrificer without fail.

॥ English Translation ॥

Be the protector, O Agni of the master (offerer] [sic] of sacrificial food, who worships you O God, as his messenger.

original p. 511

Rik 8: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

"Haviṣpatiḥ" — haviṣaḥ patiḥ — "the master of the oblation", that is, one who offers the oblation: offerer of oblations [the source's English].

"Prāvitā" — [protector] in a special way, or the chief protector.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 511–512, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

हविष्पतिः (haviṣpatiḥ) — "hūyate iti haviḥ": "arci-śuci-hu-sṛpi-chādi-chardibhya isiḥ" (Uṇ. "2-265" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-109): after arca pūjāyām, śuca śoke, hu dānādanayoḥ, sṛpḷ gatau, chadi apavāraṇe in its ṇic form, and charda vamane, the suffix isi; so isi after hu: hu + is, guṇa and av: havis; nominative singular haviḥ; the i udātta by the suffix accent. "haviṣaḥ patiḥ", a genitive tatpuruṣa; ru and visarga for the s: haviḥ patiḥ. Now "nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya" (Pā. 8-3-45): in a compound, before a k- or p-class letter, the visarga of is or us not in the second member always becomes ṣ; so the visarga of the suffix is before the p: haviṣpatiḥ; the first member's accent by "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18). सपर्यति (saparyati) — the word sapara is read in the kaṇḍvādi group, so "kaṇḍvādibhyo yak" (printed "vā. 3-1-27"): after the roots read in the kaṇḍvādi group the suffix yak; so yak after sapara. The words in the kaṇḍvādi group have both the name dhātu and the name prātipadika; this is clear in the Mahābhāṣya:

धातुप्रकरणाद्धातुः कस्य चासञ्जनादपि । आह चायमिमं दीर्घं मन्ये धातुर्विभाषितः ॥

dhātuprakaraṇād dhātuḥ kasya cāsañjanād api | āha cāyam imaṃ dīrghaṃ manye dhātur vibhāṣitaḥ ||

(printed "pā. sū. ma. 3-1-27"). Because the group is in the section on roots, the kaṇḍvādi are roots; and because the k is attached to yak, they are roots too: if one grants that they are roots, the yak added to them is ārdhadhātuka, and when guṇa would arise, the k serves to bar it — otherwise the k would be useless. If they are simply roots, the long vowel in kaṇḍūya would come by "akṛt-sārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ" (printed "7-4-2" [sic]; the sūtra is 7-4-25), so the long vowel read in the gaṇapāṭha as kaṇḍū would be useless; if the root-name is optional, then when it does not apply yak does not come, and the long vowel read is useful for being heard. So the conclusion is that the kaṇḍvādi words take the name dhātu optionally, and the name prātipadika when that is absent.

original p. 512

Rik 8 grammar closes

Here, taking sapara as a root, the yak added to it is ārdhadhātuka by "ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-114); so "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-48) drops the final a of sapara: saparya; it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32); then laṭ, replaced by third singular tip; the vikaraṇa śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68): saparya + a + ti; "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97) gives pararūpa of the root's final a and the a of śap: saparyati; udātta by the suffix accent of yak; the a formed as a single substitute with the a of śap is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). Since "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66) bars it, "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) does not make it wholly unaccented; the other vowels are unaccented by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158), and the i of ti becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66).

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यो अ॒ग्निं दे॒ववी॑तये ह॒विष्माँ॑ आ॒विवा॑सति । तस्मै॑ पावक मृळय ॥९॥

yo agníṃ devávītaye havíṣmām̐ āvívāsati | tásmai pāvaka mṛḷaya ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यः । अग्निम् । देवऽवीतये । हविष्मान् । आऽविवासति ॥ तस्मै । पावक । मृळय ॥९॥

yaḥ | agnim | deva-vītaye | haviṣmān | ā-vivāsati || tasmai | pāvaka | mṛḷaya ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ runs onto p. 513

गार्हपत्याहवनीययोः परस्परसंसर्गे विहितस्य हविषो याज्या यो अग्निं देववीतय इत्येषा । अथाग्नेय्या इष्टय इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । यो अग्निं देववीतये कुवित्सु नो गविष्टये । आ. ३-१३ । इति ॥

gārhapatyāhavanīyayoḥ parasparasaṃsarge vihitasya haviṣo yājyā yo agniṃ devavītaya ityeṣā | athāgneyyā iṣṭaya iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | yo agniṃ devavītaye kuvitsu no gaviṣṭaye | ā. 3-13 | iti ||

हविष्मान्हविर्युक्तो यो यजमानो देववीतये देवानां हविर्भक्षणहेतुयोगार्थमग्निमाविवासति अग्नेः समीपे विशेषेणागत्य परिचर्यां करोति हे पावकाग्ने तस्मै मृळय । तं यजमानं सुखय ॥ देववीतये । वी गतिप्रजनकान्त्यशनखादनेष्वित्यस्मादशनार्थात्क्तिन् । देवानां वीतिर्यस्मिन्यागे स देववीतिः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । हविष्मान् । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येति पर्युदासाद्धविःशब्दो ऽन्तोदात्तः । मतुपः सर्वानुदात्तत्वात्स एव शिष्यते । आविवासति । वा गतिगन्धनयोः । अस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थादागमयितुमिच्छतीत्यर्थे सन् । आह्वाने चाप [?] परिचर्यायां पर्यवस्यतीति विवासतिशब्दः परिचर्यार्थे निघण्टौ पठितः । द्विर्भावः । अभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वः । सन्यतः । पा. ७-४-७९ । इतीत्त्वम् । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति प्रतिषेधात् । तिङि चोदात्तवति । पा. ८-१-७१ । इत्याङो निघातः । सह सुपा । पा. २-१-४ । इत्यत्र सहेति योगविभागादाङस्तिङा सह समासे समासान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तस्मै । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यम् । पा. १-४-३२-१ । इति संप्रदाने चतुर्थी ॥

haviṣmānhaviryukto yo yajamāno devavītaye devānāṃ havirbhakṣaṇahetuyogārthamagnimāvivāsati agneḥ samīpe viśeṣeṇāgatya paricaryāṃ karoti he pāvakāgne tasmai mṛḷaya | taṃ yajamānaṃ sukhaya || devavītaye | vī gatiprajanakāntyaśanakhādaneṣvityasmādaśanārthātktin | devānāṃ vītiryasminyāge sa devavītiḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | haviṣmān | nabviṣayasyānisantasyeti paryudāsāddhaviḥśabdo 'ntodāttaḥ | matupaḥ sarvānudāttatvātsa eva śiṣyate | āvivāsati | vā gatigandhanayoḥ | asmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthādāgamayitumicchatītyarthe san | āhvāne cāpa [?] paricaryāyāṃ paryavasyatīti vivāsatiśabdaḥ paricaryārthe nighaṇṭau paṭhitaḥ | dvirbhāvaḥ | abhyāsasya hrasvaḥ | sanyataḥ | pā. 7-4-79 | itīttvam | ñnityādirnityamityādyudāttatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati | yadvṛttānnityamiti pratiṣedhāt | tiṅi codāttavati | pā. 8-1-71 | ityāṅo nighātaḥ | saha supā | pā. 2-1-4 | ityatra saheti yogavibhāgādāṅastiṅā saha samāse samāsāntodāttatve prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | tasmai | kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam | pā. 1-4-32-1 | iti saṃpradāne caturthī ||

Translation: "For the oblation prescribed at the mutual contact of the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya [fires], this [rik] yo agniṃ devavītaye is the yājyā; laid down in the section athāgneyyā iṣṭayaḥ: 'yo agniṃ devavītaye; kuvit su no gaviṣṭaye' (Āśv. 3-13). The sacrificer who, haviṣmān — having an oblation — devavītaye, for the purpose of the gods' eating of the oblation, āvivāsati Agni — comes specially near Agni and serves him: O pāvaka, Agni, tasmai mṛḷaya — make that sacrificer happy." (Grammatical tail, on p. 513: devavītaye — ktin after vī in the sense of eating; "that sacrifice in which there is the eating of the gods", a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; haviṣmān — havis is final-udātta, being excluded by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya", and since matup is wholly unaccented that accent alone remains; āvivāsati — from vā gatigandhanayoḥ with the causative sense included, san in the sense "wishes to bring"; ending in calling and service, vivāsati is read in the Nighaṇṭu among words for service; doubling, shortening of the reduplicate, i by "sanyataḥ" (Pā. 7-4-79), initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam"; not unaccented, by "yad-vṛttān nityam"; the āṅ unaccented by "tiṅi codāttavati" (Pā. 8-1-71); by splitting off saha in "saha supā" (Pā. 2-1-4) āṅ compounds with the tiṅanta, and instead of the compound-final udātta "parādiś chandasi bahulam" makes the second member initial-udātta; tasmai — the dative of the sampradāna by the vārttika "kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam" (Pā. 1-4-32-1).)

Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हविष्मान् (haviṣmān) — endowed with the oblation | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | देववीतये (devavītaye) — in order to offer the oblation to the gods | अग्निम् (agnim) — Agni, you | आविवासति (āvivāsati) — draws near and serves | तस्मै (tasmai) — for that sacrificer | O पावक (pāvaka) — Agni, who purifies all | मृळय (mṛḷaya) — grant happiness.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, you purify all things! To offer the oblation to the gods through you, the sacrificer comes to you and serves you. Give such a sacrificer happiness.

॥ English Translation ॥

Be merciful, O purifier, to the man who, presenting oblations for the gratification of gods, approaches Agni.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

When the sacrificer has come to the fires in the two fire-pits, the Gārhapatya and the Āhavanīya, he recites this rik and, offering the oblation, performs the homa. At that time this rik is used as a yājyā mantra. In this connection the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra

original p. 514

Rik 9: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

(Ā. 3-13), in the section athāgneyyā iṣṭayaḥ, says that the riks yo agniṃ devavītaye (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-9) and kuvit su no gaviṣṭaye (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-11) are to be used as the yājyā and puronuvākyā mantras.

"Devavītaye" — devānāṃ havir-bhakṣaṇa-hetu-yogārtham — "for the sake of bringing about the gods' eating of the oblation": to make an offering to the gods. Since the gods other than Agni are not seen by the eye, one must offer the oblation to them through Agni by pouring it into fire; therefore the sacrificer brings the oblation near Agni, serves him, and prays: this is the idea. Skandasvāmī gives for this word devān prati gamanāya, devānāṃ vā havir-bhakṣaṇāya: that is, for going to the gods as messenger on the sacrificer's behalf, and for calling the gods to eat the oblation.

"Haviṣmān" — one who has prepared the oblation to be offered to the gods and has brought it along.

"Āvivāsati" — samīpe viśeṣeṇāgatya paricaryāṃ karoti — "comes near and serves specially" [the source's English: "Approaches you for presenting oblations"].

"Pāvaka" — one who purifies; purifier; or one who blazes brilliantly: resplendent [the source's English]. The word is used especially in addressing Agni.

"Mṛḷaya" — sukhaya, sukham utpādaya: give happiness.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 514–515, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print

देववीतये (devavītaye) — root vī gati-prajana-kānty-aśana-khādaneṣu; after this root in the sense of eating, ktin by "striyāṃ ktin" (Pā. 3-3-94); the suffix being kit, no guṇa: vīti. "devānāṃ vītiḥ yasmin yāge saḥ devavītiḥ", a bahuvrīhi, keeps the first member's accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1). The word haviḥ, although neuter, ends in is, so, being excluded by the word anisantasya, it does not become initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (Phiṭ-sū. "26"); it is final-udātta by the suffix accent. हविष्मान् (haviṣmān) — "haviḥ asya asti": matup after it by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); being pit, it is unaccented by "anudāttau sup-pitau" (Pā. 3-1-4); so the final udātta of haviḥ alone remains.

original p. 515

Rik 9 grammar closes

आविवासति (āvivāsati) — root vā gatigandhanayoḥ; with the causative sense included, in the sense "wishes to bring", "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samāna-kartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" (Pā. 3-1-7) gives san; the wish to call ends in the sense of service; therefore in the Nighaṇṭu (Ni. "3-5-10") the word vivāsati is read in the sense of service. vā + sa: doubling by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-9); the reduplicate shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-59); "sanyataḥ" (Pā. 7-4-79): before san the a of the reduplicate becomes i: vivāsa; san is nit, so by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197) vivāsa is initial-udātta; root-name by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32); then laṭ, tip, the vikaraṇa śap and pararūpa: vivāsati. Since "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66) bars it, "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented. The preverb ā is unaccented by "tiṅi codāttavati" (Pā. 8-1-71) — a word with the name gati is unaccented before a tiṅanta that has an udātta; this is an exception to "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ". In "saha supā" (Pā. 2-1-4) the sūtra is split at saha, so the āṅ is compounded with the tiṅanta; the final-udātta of "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223) would arise, but "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (printed "6-2-19" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-2-199) sets it aside and makes the first syllable of the second member udātta. तस्मै (tasmai) — "karmaṇā yam abhipraiti sa sampradānam" (Pā. 1-4-32): the one the doer wishes to connect with the object of the act of giving takes the name of the kāraka sampradāna — in effect, the one for whom the thing given is meant. On this sūtra the Bhāṣyakāra says "kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam" (printed "pā. sū. ma. 1-4-32-1"): the vārttika means that the one for whom an action is meant takes the name sampradāna. Here, since tat is the one for whom the act of making happy, expressed by the root mṛḍaya, is meant, it is sampradāna, and "caturthī sampradāne" (printed "5-2-3-1-13" [sic]; the sūtra is 2-3-13) gives the dative. मृळय (mṛḷaya) — root mṛḍa sukhane, ṇic-ending; loṭ, second singular sip, replaced by hi; the vikaraṇa śap, guṇa, ay; hi dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. 6-4-105); ḷ for the ḍ: mṛḷaya.
