द्र॒वि॒णो॒दा द्रवि॑णसो॒ ग्राव॑हस्तासो अध्व॒रे । [accent ?] य॒ज्ञेषु॑ दे॒वमी॑ळते ॥७॥

draviṇodā́ dráviṇaso grā́vahastāso adhvaré | [accent ?] yajñéṣu devám īḷate ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणःऽदाः । द्रविणसः । ग्रावऽहस्तासः । अध्वरे ॥ यज्ञेषु । देवम् । ईळते ॥७॥

draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | draviṇasaḥ | grāva 'hastāsaḥ | adhvare || yajñeṣu | devam | īḷate ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अध्वरे ऽग्निष्टोमे प्रकृतिरूपे यज्ञेषु विकृतिरूपेषूक्थ्यादिषु च देवमग्निमीळते । ऋत्विजः स्तुवन्ति । कीदृशा ऋत्विजः । द्रविणसो धनार्थिनो ग्रावहस्तासो ऽभिषवसाधनपाषाणधारिणः । कीदृशं देवं । द्रविणोदा धनप्रदं । यद्वा । धनप्रदो ऽग्निः सोमं पिबत्विति शेषः । तमेतं मन्त्रं यास्क एवं निराह । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति तस्य दाता द्रविणोदास्तस्यैषा भवति । द्रविणोदा द्रविणस इत्यादि । नि. ८-१ । सो ऽयं यास्कोक्तो निर्वचनप्रपञ्चस्तस्मिन्नेव ग्रन्थे ऽवगन्तव्यः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । द्रुदक्षिभ्यामिनन् । उ. २-५० [?] । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो द्रविणशब्दः । तद्ददातीति द्रविणोदाः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । पूर्वपदस्य सकारोपजनश्छान्दसः । रुत्वोत्वे । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । देवविशेषणत्वेनैकवाक्यतापक्षे द्वितीयायाः स्वादेशः । अथवा द्रविणमात्मन इच्छन्ति द्रविणस्यन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो

adhvare 'gniṣṭome prakṛtirūpe yajñeṣu vikṛtirūpeṣūkthyādiṣu ca devamagnimīḷate | ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti | kīdṛśā ṛtvijaḥ | draviṇaso dhanārthino grāvahastāso 'bhiṣavasādhanapāṣāṇadhāriṇaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ devaṃ | draviṇodā dhanapradaṃ | yadvā | dhanaprado 'gniḥ somaṃ pibatviti śeṣaḥ | tametaṃ mantraṃ yāska evaṃ nirāha | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate yadenadabhidravanti balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravanti tasya dātā draviṇodāstasyaiṣā bhavati | draviṇodā draviṇasa ityādi | ni. 8-1 | so 'yaṃ yāskokto nirvacanaprapañcastasminneva granthe 'vagantavyaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | drudakṣibhyāminan | u. 2-50 [?] | nittvādādyudātto draviṇaśabdaḥ | taddadātīti draviṇodāḥ | kvipceti kvip | pūrvapadasya sakāropajanaśchāndasaḥ | rutvotve | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | devaviśeṣaṇatvenaikavākyatāpakṣe dvitīyāyāḥ svādeśaḥ | athavā draviṇamātmana icchanti draviṇasyanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | sarvaprātipadikebhyo

original p. 651

Rik 7: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English

लालसायां सुग्वक्तव्यः । म. ७-१-५१-२ । इति क्यचि परतः सुगागमः । द्रविणस्यतेः सम्पदादित्वाद्भावे क्विप् । अतो लोपः । क्वौ लुप्तं न स्थानिवद्भवति । म. १-१-५८-२ । इति तस्य स्थानिवत्त्वप्रतिषेधाद्यलोपः । एवं द्रविणस्शब्दो धनेच्छावचनः । द्रविणेच्छां दस्यति यथेष्टधनप्रदानेनोपक्षपयतीत्यर्थे दसु उपक्षये इत्यस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप्चेति क्विप् । एवं द्रविणोदःशब्दः सकारान्तो भवति । तथा द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्तीति नैरुक्तो व्यवहार उपपद्यते । नि. ८-२ । अतो द्रविणोदस्शब्दो भिन्नवाक्यत्वे स्वार्थे प्रथमा । एकवाक्यत्वे तु व्यत्ययेन द्वितीयार्थो भवति । द्रविणस इत्यत्रापि वाक्यभेदपक्षे द्रविणसः सोमस्येत्यर्थे सकारोपजनश्छान्दसः । आद्युदात्तत्वं तु नियमेन स्थितं । ऋत्विग्विशेषणत्वेनैकवाक्यत्वपक्षे तु क्यजन्तात्क्विप् । अतो लोपादि पूर्ववत् । अत्र तु पक्षे क्यचश्चित्त्वेनान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वं । ग्रावयुक्ता हस्ता येषां ते ग्रावहस्तासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । ग्रावशब्दो वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अध्वरे । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । ईळते । अनुदात्तेत्त्वादात्मनेपदं । अदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक् । झस्यादादेशः ॥

lālasāyāṃ sugvaktavyaḥ | ma. 7-1-51-2 | iti kyaci parataḥ sugāgamaḥ | draviṇasyateḥ sampadāditvādbhāve kvip | ato lopaḥ | kvau luptaṃ na sthānivadbhavati | ma. 1-1-58-2 | iti tasya sthānivattvapratiṣedhādyalopaḥ | evaṃ draviṇasśabdo dhanecchāvacanaḥ | draviṇecchāṃ dasyati yatheṣṭadhanapradānenopakṣapayatītyarthe dasu upakṣaye ityasmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvipceti kvip | evaṃ draviṇodaḥśabdaḥ sakārānto bhavati | tathā draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavantīti nairukto vyavahāra upapadyate | ni. 8-2 | ato draviṇodasśabdo bhinnavākyatve svārthe prathamā | ekavākyatve tu vyatyayena dvitīyārtho bhavati | draviṇasa ityatrāpi vākyabhedapakṣe draviṇasaḥ somasyetyarthe sakāropajanaśchāndasaḥ | ādyudāttatvaṃ tu niyamena sthitaṃ | ṛtvigviśeṣaṇatvenaikavākyatvapakṣe tu kyajantātkvip | ato lopādi pūrvavat | atra tu pakṣe kyacaścittvenāntodāttatve prāpte vyatyayenādyudāttatvaṃ | grāvayuktā hastā yeṣāṃ te grāvahastāsaḥ | ājjaserasuk | grāvaśabdo vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | adhvare | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | īḷate | anudāttettvādātmanepadaṃ | adiprabhṛtibhya iti śapo luk | jhasyādādeśaḥ ||

Translation: "At the adhvara, the Agniṣṭoma in its model form, and at the yajñas, the modified forms such as the Ukthya, the priests īḷate, praise, the god Agni. What are the priests like? Draviṇasaḥ, seeking wealth; grāvahastāsaḥ, holding the stones that are the means of pressing. What is the god like? Draviṇodāḥ, the giver of wealth. Or: 'may Agni, the giver of wealth, drink the soma' is to be supplied. Yāska explains this mantra so: 'Draviṇodāḥ: why? Wealth is called draviṇa because they run towards it; or strength is draviṇa, because by it they run towards (the foe); its giver is draviṇodāḥ; this Ṛk is about him: draviṇodā draviṇasaḥ…' (Ni. 8-1). That etymological account of Yāska is to be learnt from that very work." (Grammatical tail: draviṇa with inan (Uṇ. "2-50" [?]), initial udātta; draviṇodāḥ, "who gives it", kvip, the Vedic insertion of s in the first member, ru and u, the accent of the kṛt second member; taken with devam as one sentence, the accusative is replaced by the nominative; or draviṇasyanti "they desire wealth for themselves", kyac with the augment s (MB 7-1-51-2), kvip in the action sense, the a and then the y dropped (the kvip loss not sthānivat, MB 1-1-58-2), so draviṇas means desire for wealth; draviṇodas, "who removes that desire by giving wealth", from das 'to waste' with the inner causative and kvip, ending in s, which fits Yāska's draviṇodasaḥ pravādāḥ (Ni. 8-2); in separate sentences a nominative in its own sense, in one sentence by vyatyaya in the accusative sense; draviṇasaḥ, on the separate-sentence view "of the soma" with a Vedic s, initial udātta as a rule; as an epithet of the priests, kvip after the kyac form, final udātta (cit) overridden by vyatyaya to initial udātta; grāvahastāsaḥ, a bahuvrīhi with asuk, grāvan initial udātta as of the vṛṣādi class; adhvare final udātta by nañsubhyām; īḷate, ātmanepada, śap dropped, at for jh.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणसः (draviṇasaḥ) — the priests who seek wealth | ग्रावहस्तासः (grāvahastāsaḥ) — holding in their hands the stones (the means of pressing the soma juice) | द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — the giver of wealth (or the one named Draviṇodas) | देवम् (devam) — Agni, the god | अध्वरे (adhvare) — at the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice in its model form | यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu) — and at the sacrifices such as the Ukthya in their modified forms | ईळते (īḷate) — praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The priests who seek wealth, holding in their hands the stones that are the means of pressing the soma juice, at the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, the model, and at the Ukthya and other sacrifices, the modifications, invoke and praise Agni called Draviṇodas so that he drinks the soma juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

The priests desirous of wealth, with the soma-pressing stones in their hands praise the divine (Agni) Dravinodas who is the giver of riches, in the Soma and other sacrifices.

original p. 652

Rik 7: Special Topics

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Draviṇodāḥ: Yāska has written a full explanation of this word:

द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते । यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति । बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः ॥

draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate | yadenadabhidravanti | balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravanti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ ||

Ni. 8-1. Here the word draviṇodāḥ is derived as draviṇaṃ dadāti iti draviṇodāḥ. The word draviṇa has two senses, wealth and strength; so draviṇodāḥ means the giver of wealth or of strength. This is the sense of the parts of the word. Besides, Yāska gives the etymological explanation of this Ṛk thus:

द्रविणोदा यस्त्वं । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसानिन इति वा द्रविणसस्तस्मात्पिबत्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचन्ति स्तुवन्ति वर्धयन्ति पूजयन्तीति वा ॥

draviṇodā yastvaṃ | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasānina iti vā draviṇasastasmātpibatviti vā | yajñeṣu devamīḷate | yācanti stuvanti vardhayanti pūjayantīti vā ||

That is, the priests who look for wealth, oblations and the like pray to you, called Draviṇodas, to drink the soma at the sacrifices: this is the chief sense. Though draviṇodāḥ here is a nominative singular, how does it qualify the accusative singular devam? Words must be supplied so that the sense is draviṇodā yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devam, "the god who is the giver of wealth: that god". Draviṇasaḥ: since they pray to the god for wealth or oblations for the worship of the gods, draviṇasaḥ means the priests. And īḷate may be given many senses: they beg, they praise, they extol, they worship.

तत्को द्रविणोदा इन्द्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः । स बलधनयोर्दातृतमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥

tatko draviṇodā indra iti krauṣṭukiḥ | sa baladhanayordātṛtamastasya ca sarvā balakṛtiḥ ||

original p. 653

Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

So much for the sense of the parts of the word draviṇodāḥ. But who is the deity draviṇodāḥ? Indra is the one called draviṇodāḥ, for it is Indra who gives most the strength and wealth that the word draviṇa points to; so Indra himself should be called draviṇodāḥ: this is Krauṣṭuki's view.

अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहैष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते । यो अश्मनोरन्तरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥

athāpyagniṃ draviṇodasamāhaiṣa punaretasmājjāyate | yo aśmanorantaragniṃ jajāna ityapi nigamo bhavati ||

And they give this word another sense: Indra created heaven and earth, and created Agni too between them; so the word draviṇodāḥ may also be said to mean Agni; to support this sense they give the Ṛk "aśmanor antar agniṃ jajāna" as an example.

अथाप्यृतुयाजेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्यैन्द्रपानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति । अथाप्याह द्रविणोदाः पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥

athāpyṛtuyājeṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti | teṣāṃ punaḥ pātrasyaindrapānamiti bhavati || athāpyenaṃ somapānena stauti | athāpyāha draviṇodāḥ pibatu draviṇodasa iti ||

Since it is said that at the sacrifices made with the Ṛtus in view Indra drinks the soma from the vessel in the priests' hands, and since Indra is praised with mantras about drinking soma, there is the custom of calling the priests draviṇodasaḥ: all this is Krauṣṭuki's view.

अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः । आग्नेयेष्वेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति ॥

ayamevāgnirdraviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ | āgneyeṣveva hi sūkteṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti ||

That Agni himself is draviṇodāḥ is Śākapūṇi's view; for in the sūktas about Agni, when the priests praise Agni, they use the word draviṇodāḥ as an epithet of Agni.

यथो एतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतम इति सर्वासु देवतास्वैश्वर्यं विद्यते । यथो एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनमिति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्निरोजसा बलेन मथ्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं सहसो यहुं ॥

yatho etatsa baladhanayordātṛtama iti sarvāsu devatāsvaiśvaryaṃ vidyate | yatho etadojaso jātamutamanya enamiti cāhetyayamapyagnirojasā balena mathyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yahuṃ ||

In all deities there is lordship; so Agni too gives strength and wealth. Since he gives strength and wealth, Agni too can be called draviṇodāḥ. Besides, it is clear that the word draviṇa means strength. Since in kindling Agni one churns using strength, there is the notion that Agni is born of strength. That is why they praise Agni with the words sahasas putram (the son of strength), sahasaḥ sūnum, sahaso yahum: Ṛ. Saṃ. "2-7-6" [?]; the print reads द्र्वन्नः for the first word.) ("Eating wood, receiving ghee as his libation, the ancient Hotṛ, choice-worthy, the son of strength, the wonderful" — editorial and tentative.

द्र्वन्नः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः । सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥

drvannaḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ | sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ||

original p. 654

Rik 7: Special Topics (end) and grammar

त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुतः । ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥

tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnavāhutaḥ | ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ||

Ṛ. Saṃ. "8-23-3" [?]; the middle digits are small.) ("When you, youngest, son of strength, are offered to, you become true to order and worthy of worship" — editorial and tentative. Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4.) ("O Agni, lord of strength rich in cattle, son of strength, give us great fame, O Jātavedas" — editorial and tentative.

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥

agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ||

In these Ṛks the words sahasas putra, sahasaḥ sūnu and sahaso yahu are used in turn in praising Agni. So, though other deities too give strength and wealth, it is Agni above all who is set forth by the word draviṇodāḥ.

Grāvahastāsaḥ: those who hold stones in their hands to crush the soma creeper.

Adhvare, yajñeṣu: though the words adhvara and yajña generally denote the same thing, sacrifice, here the Bhāṣyakāra, fearing the fault of repetition, gives adhvara the sense of the Agniṣṭoma in its model form and yajña the sense of the particular sacrifices such as the Ukthya in their modified forms. The model (prakṛti) is the basic sacrificial rite that contains the procedures common to all sacrifices. The modification (vikṛti) is a sacrificial rite carried out with some changes here and there as the occasion requires; that is, in a modified sacrifice all the acts are as in the model sacrifice, with a slight difference in only one or two matters. We have explained the model and modified sacrifices earlier.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 654–656, noted briefly

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ): "drudakṣibhyām inan" (Uṇ. sū. "2-50" [?]; dru gatau, dakṣa vṛddhau): after these roots the suffix inan; with inan after dru: dru + ina; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), o for the u; av for the o by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): dravina; ṇ for the n by "aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2): draviṇa. Draviṇaṃ dadāti iti draviṇodāḥ: with the subanta draviṇam as upapada, kvip after dā by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); kvip drops; a prātipadika by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-2-46); the am dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71); the first member, as a Vedic form,

original p. 655

Rik 7: grammar (continued)

takes the augment suk, joining an s: draviṇas + dā; ru for the s by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66): draviṇar + dā; u for the ru by "haśi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-114): draviṇa + u + dā; guṇa by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87): draviṇodā. Dā is final udātta by the root accent of "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162); after compounding, the kṛt second-member accent comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) and remains. Draviṇodāḥ qualifies the accusative singular devam; so if one sentence is meant, for the accusative am after draviṇodā the replacement su comes by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39): draviṇodās, ru, visarga: draviṇodāḥ. Or, with the analysis draviṇam ātmanaḥ icchanti, it becomes draviṇasyanti: in this case kyac by "supa ātmanaḥ kyac" after draviṇam in the sense "they desire for themselves"; the kyac-form is called a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-32); the sup inside the root is dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71); by "sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyāṃ sug vaktavyaḥ" (Pā. sū. Ma. Bhā. 7-1-51-2) (lālasā is atiśayenābhyavajihīrṣā, as the Kaiyaṭa explains; utkaṭecchā, eager desire, says the Tattvabodhinī), when eager desire is shown before kyac all stems take the augment suk: draviṇasya. After it, by "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. sū. vārtti. 3-3-108-9) kvip in the action sense: draviṇasya + v; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48): the a of what ends in a at the time the ārdhadhātuka suffix is taught drops; so the a before the suffix drops: draviṇasy + v. In this a-loss view, when the y is to be dropped, "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57) would give sthānivadbhāva, but by "kvau luptaṃ na sthānivad bhavati" (Pā. Ma. 1-1-58-2) what is dropped with reference to the kvip suffix is not sthānivat; so sthānivadbhāva is barred. "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66): before a val letter v and y drop; so the y drops. "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-67): apṛkta is a suffix of a single letter; the apṛkta v drops. Though the loss of the apṛkta v, having no outside cause, is antaraṅga, and the loss before val, having an outside cause, is bahiraṅga, so that by "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" (paribhāṣā 50) the val-loss would count as not done when the apṛkta loss is made, and then, once the apṛkta loss came first, the bar of sthānivadbhāva in the al-rule would make the val-loss not come: yet by "ver apṛktalopād vali lopo balīyān", the val-loss comes first, then the apṛkta loss: draviṇas. This means desire for wealth. Draviṇecchāṃ dasyati: one who, by giving

original p. 656

Rik 7: grammar (end)

wealth as desired, removes the desire for wealth: with this sense meant, kvip by "kvip ca" after the root dasu upakṣaye with the inner causative; the kvip drops. In this way the word draviṇodas ends in s. By this derivation Yāska's usage draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti (Ni. 8-2) fits. So if draviṇodāḥ is taken as not qualifying devam, two sentences arise; on this view the nominative singular su comes in its own sense, giving draviṇodāḥ; on the one-sentence view the nominative must be taken in the sense of the accusative by vyatyaya.

द्रविणसः (draviṇasaḥ): here too, on the separate-sentence view, draviṇasaḥ means "of the soma juice"; in this sense, by a Vedic process, the augment s comes, giving draviṇasaḥ. By "ñnityādir nityam" it is initial udātta as a rule. On the view that draviṇasaḥ qualifies the priests and there is one sentence, as said before, kvip after the kyac form, and by "ato lopaḥ" and the other rules the loss of a and the other operations come as before. On this view the kyac suffix is cit, so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) final udātta would come, but by vyatyaya it is initial udātta. On the one-sentence view the construction is adhvare yajñeṣu ca draviṇaso grāvahastāso ṛtvijaḥ draviṇodā devam īḷate. On the separate-sentence view the constructions are draviṇasaḥ grāvahastāsaḥ ṛtvijaḥ adhvare yajñeṣu ca devam īḷate, draviṇodāḥ agniḥ somaṃ pibatu, and grāvahastāsaḥ ṛtvijaḥ adhvare yajñeṣu ca devam īḷate, draviṇodāḥ agniḥ draviṇasaḥ somasya pātā bhavatu.

ग्रावहस्तासः (grāvahastāsaḥ): grāvayuktāḥ hastāḥ yeṣāṃ te grāvahastāsaḥ, a bahuvrīhi compound. After grāvahasta, jas; by "ājjaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) jas takes the augment asuk. The word grāvan belongs to the vṛṣādi class, so it is initial udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); even after compounding, by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the first-member accent comes.

अध्वरे (adhvare): na vidyate dhvaraḥ hiṃsā yasmin saḥ adhvaraḥ; overriding the first-member accent, by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172) the second member is final udātta.

ईळते (īḷate): īḍa stutau; the root is anudāttet, so by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12) the ātmanepada. Laṭ, 3rd plural jha. The vikaraṇa śap is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72). By "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5) at for the jh. By "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79) e for the ṭi: īḍate; ḷ for the ḍ by "ajmadhyasya ḍakārasya…".

॥७॥

original p. 657

Sūkta 15, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्र॒वि॒णो॒दा द॑दातु नो॒ वसू॑नि॒ यानि॑ शृण्वि॒रे । दे॒वेषु॒ ता व॑नामहे ॥८॥

draviṇodā́ dadātu no vásūni yā́ni śṛṇviré | devéṣu tā́ vanāmahe ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणःऽदाः । ददातु । नः । वसूनि । यानि । शृण्विरे ॥ देवेषु । ता । वनामहे ॥८॥

draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | dadātu | naḥ | vasūni | yāni | śṛṇvire || deveṣu | tā | vanāmahe ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्रविणोदा देवो नो ऽस्मभ्यं वसूनि धनानि ददातु । यानि धनानि शृण्विरे हविरुपयुक्तत्वेन श्रूयन्ते । ता तानि च सर्वाणि धनानि देवेषु निमित्तभूतेषु वनामहे । सम्भजामः । धनैर्देवान्यष्टुं तानि स्वीकुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । गतं । वसूनि । शृस्वृस्निहीत्यादिना । उ. १-११ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः । शृण्विरे । श्रु श्रवणे । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लिट् । झ इरेच् । पा. ३-४-८१ । छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वे व्यत्ययेन श्नुः । तत्सन्नियोगेन शृभावश्च । उवङि प्राप्ते हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके । पा. ६-४-८७ । इति यणादेशः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । ता । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य । पा. ८-२-७ । इति नलोपः । वनामहे । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥

draviṇodā devo no 'smabhyaṃ vasūni dhanāni dadātu | yāni dhanāni śṛṇvire havirupayuktatvena śrūyante | tā tāni ca sarvāṇi dhanāni deveṣu nimittabhūteṣu vanāmahe | sambhajāmaḥ | dhanairdevānyaṣṭuṃ tāni svīkurma ityarthaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | gataṃ | vasūni | śṛsvṛsnihītyādinā | u. 1-11 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtterādyudāttaḥ | śṛṇvire | śru śravaṇe | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne liṭ | jha irec | pā. 3-4-81 | chandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukatve vyatyayena śnuḥ | tatsanniyogena śṛbhāvaśca | uvaṅi prāpte huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke | pā. 6-4-87 | iti yaṇādeśaḥ | cita ityantodāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | tā | śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya | pā. 8-2-7 | iti nalopaḥ | vanāmahe | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | vyatyayenātmanepadaṃ ||

Translation: "May the god Draviṇodas give us vasūni, riches. The riches that śṛṇvire, are heard of, as fit for oblations: tā, all those riches, devesu, for the sake of the gods, vanāmahe, we accept; that is, we take them in order to worship the gods with riches." (Grammatical tail: draviṇodāḥ gone through; vasūni with u (Uṇ. 1-11), initial udātta (nit carried on); śṛṇvire: śru, liṭ in the present, irec for jha (Pā. 3-4-81), by chandasy ubhayathā sārvadhātuka status and so by vyatyaya śnu with śṛ for śru, yaṇ for the uvaṅ by Pā. 6-4-87, final udātta (cit), not lowered because of the relative yāni; tā: the śi dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam, the n dropped (Pā. 8-2-7); vanāmahe, van 'to share', ātmanepada by vyatyaya.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — the god who gives wealth (Agni) | यानि (yāni) — the riches which | शृण्विरे (śṛṇvire) — are well known as fit for oblations | ता वसूनि (tā vasūni) — those riches | नः (naḥ) — to us | ददातु (dadātu) — may he give | ता (tā) — all those riches | देवेषु (devesu) — for the sake of the gods | वनामहे (vanāmahe) — we take.

original p. 658

Rik 8: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We look for wealth for the works of the gods, such as sacrifices. May Agni, the giver of wealth, graciously grant us all the wealth known to be for these works.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Dravinodas give us riches that may be heard of; we ask them towards the service of the gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Yāni śṛṇvire: all such things, of whatever kinds of wealth and lordship we have heard there are. Since it is said here devesu tā vanāmahe, those things must be fit to be offered to the gods; so the Bhāṣyakāra says they are things fit for offering oblations.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 658–659, noted briefly

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ): explained in the previous mantra.

वसूनि (vasūni): by "śṛsvṛsnihitrapyasivasihanikledibandhimanibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "1-10" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 1-11) the suffix u after vasa nivāse. In this sūtra nit is carried on from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. sū. 1-9); so the suffix u is nit, and by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) initial udātta comes.

शृण्विरे (śṛṇvire): śru śravaṇe; by "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-6) liṭ in the present sense; 3rd plural jha; by "liṭas tajhayor eśirec" (Pā. sū. 3-4-81) irec for the jha. By "chandasy ubhayathā" (Pā. sū. 3-4-117) it also has sārvadhātuka status; so by "śruvaḥ śṛ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-74) śṛ comes for śru, together with the suffix śnu: śṛ + nu + ire. Now "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) would give yaṇ; overriding it, "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) would give uvaṅ; overriding that too, "huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke" (Pā. sū. 6-4-87): before a vowel-initial sārvadhātuka suffix, the u of hu and of a stem ending in śnu with several vowels,

original p. 659

Rik 8: grammar (end)

not preceded by a conjunct, takes yaṇ; so yaṇ. By "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" (Pā. sū. 8-4-1 vā. 1) ṇ for the n: śṛṇvire. The suffix irec is cit, so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) it is final udātta. By "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) the full lowering is barred, so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) does not make it wholly unaccented.

ता (tā): tad in the neuter, with śas after it; a for the d by "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); pararūpa by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97). "jaśśasoḥ śiḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-20): for jas and śas after a neuter stem, the replacement śi; so śi for śas. By "śi sarvanāmasthānam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-42) śi is a sarvanāmasthāna. "napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-72): a neuter stem ending in a jhal or a vowel takes the augment num before a sarvanāmasthāna; so num: tan + i; by "sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8) the penultimate is lengthened: tān + i. By "śeś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-70) the śi drops; by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7) the n drops: tā. It means tāni.

वनामहे (vanāmahe): vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau. In "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85), in the kārikā suptiṅupagraha…, upagraha is explained as parasmaipada and ātmanepada; so there is interchange between parasmaipada and ātmanepada. The word vyatyaya is made from the root iṇ gatau with the two upasargas vi and ati, with ac in the action sense; it means "going beyond". So it is settled that where there is a cause for parasmaipada, going beyond it the ātmanepada comes, and where there is a cause for ātmanepada, going beyond it the parasmaipada comes, in some places. Though the root van is parasmaipadin, going beyond that, the ātmanepada comes by "vyatyayo bahulam" (3-1-85). Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

॥८॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The print joins नेष्ट्रादृतुभिः.

द्र॒वि॒णो॒दाः पि॑पीषति जु॒होत॒ प्र च॑ तिष्ठत । ने॒ष्ट्रादृ॒तुभि॑रिष्यत ॥९॥ [accent ?]

draviṇodā́ḥ pipīṣati juhóta prá ca tiṣṭhata | neṣṭrā́d ṛtúbhir iṣyata ||9|| [accent ?]

original p. 660

Rik 9: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

द्रविणःऽदाः । पिपीषति । जुहोत । प्र । च । तिष्ठत ॥ नेष्ट्रात् । ऋतुऽभिः । इष्यत ॥९॥

draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | pipīṣati | juhota | pra | ca | tiṣṭhata || neṣṭrāt | ṛtu 'bhiḥ | iṣyata ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्रविणोदा देव ऋतुभिः सह नेष्ट्रान्नेष्टृसम्बन्धिपात्रात्पिपीषति । सोमं पातुमिच्छति । ततो हे ऋत्विज इष्यत । होमस्थाने गच्छत । गत्वा च जुहोत । होमं कुरुत । हुत्वा प्र तिष्ठत च । होमस्थानात्स्थानान्तरं प्रति प्रस्थानमपि कुरुत ॥ द्रविणोदाः । गतं । पिपीषति । पा पाने । पातुमिच्छतीति सन् । छान्दस ईकारः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । जुहोत । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं । तस्य लङ्वद्भावात्तादेशः । तस्य तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तबादेशः । तस्य पित्त्वाद्गुणः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्यनुवृत्तावनुदात्ते च । पा. ६-१-१९० । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते भीह्रीभृहुमदजनधनदरिद्राजागरां प्रत्ययात्पूर्वं पिति । पा. ६-१-१९२ । इति होकार उदात्तः । तिष्ठत । ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य थस्य लङ्वद्भावात्तादेशः । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना तिष्ठादेशः । समवप्रविभ्यः स्थः । पा. १-३-२२ । इत्यात्मनेपदं न भवति । तत्रानुवृत्तस्य निर्दिष्टग्रहणस्यानन्तर्यार्थत्वात् । अत्र चशब्देन व्यवधानात्ते प्राग्धातोः । पा. १-४-८० । इत्युपसर्गत्वेन प्राक्प्रयोक्तव्यस्यापि प्रशब्दस्य व्यवहिताश्चेति छन्दसि व्यवहितप्रयोगः । अत्र चशब्दो जुहोतेति पूर्वेण सह समुच्चयार्थः । न पुनरिष्यतेत्युत्तरेण । तेनाप्रथमत्वाच्चवायोगे प्रथमा । पा. ८-१-५९ । इति निषेधाभावात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । नेष्ट्रात् । पोत्राद्यज्ञं पुनीतन । ऋग्वे. १-१५-२ । इत्यत्र पोत्रशब्देन यदुक्तं तदत्र द्रष्टव्यं । इष्यत । इष गतौ । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं ॥

draviṇodā deva ṛtubhiḥ saha neṣṭrānneṣṭṛsambandhipātrātpipīṣati | somaṃ pātumicchati | tato he ṛtvija iṣyata | homasthāne gacchata | gatvā ca juhota | homaṃ kuruta | hutvā pra tiṣṭhata ca | homasthānātsthānāntaraṃ prati prasthānamapi kuruta || draviṇodāḥ | gataṃ | pipīṣati | pā pāne | pātumicchatīti san | chāndasa īkāraḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | juhota | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ | tasya laṅvadbhāvāttādeśaḥ | tasya taptanaptanathanāśceti tabādeśaḥ | tasya pittvādguṇaḥ | abhyastānāmādirityanuvṛttāvanudātte ca | pā. 6-1-190 | ityādyudāttatve prāpte bhīhrībhṛhumadajanadhanadaridrājāgarāṃ pratyayātpūrvaṃ piti | pā. 6-1-192 | iti hokāra udāttaḥ | tiṣṭhata | ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanasya thasya laṅvadbhāvāttādeśaḥ | śapi pāghretyādinā tiṣṭhādeśaḥ | samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ | pā. 1-3-22 | ityātmanepadaṃ na bhavati | tatrānuvṛttasya nirdiṣṭagrahaṇasyānantaryārthatvāt | atra caśabdena vyavadhānātte prāgdhātoḥ | pā. 1-4-80 | ityupasargatvena prākprayoktavyasyāpi praśabdasya vyavahitāśceti chandasi vyavahitaprayogaḥ | atra caśabdo juhoteti pūrveṇa saha samuccayārthaḥ | na punariṣyatetyuttareṇa | tenāprathamatvāccavāyoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 | iti niṣedhābhāvāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | neṣṭrāt | potrādyajñaṃ punītana | ṛgve. 1-15-2 | ityatra potraśabdena yaduktaṃ tadatra draṣṭavyaṃ | iṣyata | iṣa gatau | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ ||

Translation: "The god Draviṇodas, with the Ṛtus, pipīṣati, wishes to drink the soma, from the neṣṭra, the vessel belonging to the Neṣṭṛ. So, O priests, iṣyata, go to the place of the homa; having gone, juhota, make the homa; having made it, pra tiṣṭhata ca, also set out from the place of the homa to another place." (Grammatical tail: draviṇodāḥ gone through; pipīṣati, san after pā 'to drink' in the sense of wishing, the ī Vedic, lowered; juhota: loṭ 2nd plural, ta by laṅvadbhāva, tap for it, guṇa (pit); the initial udātta of Pā. 6-1-190 is overridden by Pā. 6-1-192, so the o is udātta; tiṣṭhata: tiṣṭha for sthā; the ātmanepada of Pā. 1-3-22 does not come, the immediate sequence being required there and ca intervening; pra, which as an upasarga should come before the root (Pā. 1-4-80), is used separated in the Veda; ca joins juhota with what precedes, not with iṣyata; so, tiṣṭhata not being the first, the bar of Pā. 8-1-59 does not apply and it is lowered; neṣṭrāt as said for potra at Ṛ. 1-15-2; iṣyata, iṣ 'to go', loṭ 2nd plural.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ) — Agni, the giver of wealth | ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) — with the Ṛtu deities | नेष्ट्रात् (neṣṭrāt) — from the Neṣṭṛ's vessel | पिपीषति (pipīṣati) — wishes to drink (the soma juice); (so, O priests) | इष्यत (iṣyata) — go (to the place of sacrifice) | जुहोत (juhota) — make the homa; (then) | प्र तिष्ठत च (pra tiṣṭhata ca) — leave the place of the homa and go back to your own places.

original p. 661

Rik 9: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests, Agni, the giver of wealth and the self of the gods, looks to drink the soma juice from the Neṣṭṛ's vessel. So all of you come to the place of sacrifice, make the homa, and then go out.

॥ English Translation ॥

Dravinodas desires to drink with the Ritu's from the cup of Neshtri; hasten, priests, present the oblation and depart.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Pipīṣati:

पा पाने । पातुमिच्छति ॥

pā pāne | pātumicchati ||

he looks to drink.

Neṣṭrāt: the soma juice from the vessel in the hand of the priest called Neṣṭṛ.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 661–663, noted briefly

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ): explained in the seventh mantra.

पिपीषति (pipīṣati): the root pā pāne; analysed pātum icchati. "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-7): the root iṣu icchāyām; after a root expressing an activity that has the same agent as this iṣ and is the object of the iṣ, the suffix san comes in the sense of wishing: that is the sense of the sūtra. Here the one who wishes is Agni; Agni is the agent of iṣ; the same Agni is the agent in the activity favourable to contact with the throat, which is the sense of pā; so the activity of pā has the same agent as the wishing, and this activity is the object of iṣ. So san comes after pā, denoting such an activity, in the sense of wishing: pā + sa; reduplication by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9): pā + pā + sa; the reduplicate shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59); i for the a of the reduplicate by "sanyataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-79): pipāsati. Now the ā becomes ī as a Vedic form. Ṣ for the s by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59): pipīṣati. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" ("8-12-28" [as printed, for 8-1-28]).

जुहोत (juhota): hu dānādanayoḥ (juhotyādi); loṭ, 2nd plural tha; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the laṅvadbhāva; so

original p. 662

Rik 9: grammar (continued)

by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) ta for tha; tap for it by "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-45); the vikaraṇa śap by "kartari śap", dropped (ślu) by "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-75); reduplication of the root by "ślau" (Pā. sū. 6-1-10): hu + hu + ta; by "kuhoś cuḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-62), for the h, closed, with great breath, a jh of that kind; by "abhyāse carc ca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-54) j for the jh: ju + hu + ta. Tap is pit, so by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it is not ṅit; so "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) does not bar guṇa; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84): juhota. The sārvadhātuka ta standing for the lakāra is pit, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). With "abhyastānām ādiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-189) carried on in "anudātte ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-190), na vidyate udāttaḥ yasmin saḥ anudāttaḥ, tasmin anudātte: before an unaccented sārvadhātuka in the place of a lakāra, the first syllable of a reduplicated stem is udātta; so the initial udātta would come; but overriding it, "bhīhrībhṛhumadajanadhanadaridrājāgarāṃ pratyayāt pūrvaṃ piti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-192): ñibhī bhaye, hrī lajjāyām, ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, hu dānādanayoḥ, madī harṣe (a divādi root, but by a Vedic process śap gets ślu), jana janane, dhana dhānye, daridrā durgatau, jāgṛ nidrākṣaye. Daridrā and jāgṛ are reduplicated by "jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ" (Pā. sū. "6-1-6" [?]), by which jakṣ and the six roots after it are called reduplicated; the others are reduplicated by "ubhe abhyastam" (Pā. sū. "6-1-5" [?]). Before a pit sārvadhātuka in the place of a lakāra, in the roots bhī and the rest that are reduplicated, the syllable before the suffix is udātta; so the o before the suffix ta is udātta.

तिष्ठत (tiṣṭhata): the root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; s for the ṣ by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64); with the ṣṭutva gone, the ṭh reverts: sthā. Loṭ, 2nd plural tha: sthā + tha; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the laṅvadbhāva; by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) ta for tha; by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) śap: sthā + a + ta; by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78) tiṣṭha for sthā: tiṣṭhata. "samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-22): after the upasargas sam, ava, pra, vi, the root sthā takes the ātmanepada in the place of the lakāra; but here, though there is an upasarga, the ātmanepada does not come, since samavapravibhyaḥ is a fifth-case statement. So by "tasmād ity uttarasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-67), the paribhāṣā

original p. 663

Rik 9: grammar (end)

means: the operation enjoined in a rule that names a fifth-case form comes for what immediately follows. By this paribhāṣā, the ātmanepada is enjoined when sthā immediately follows sam and the other upasargas. Here, in pra ca tiṣṭhata, ca intervenes between them; so the ātmanepada does not come. Pra is an upasarga; so by "te prāg dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-4-80) the gati and upasarga words must be used immediately before the root, and pra ought to be used immediately before the root. But by "vyavahitāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-82) in the Veda the gati and upasarga words may be used separated too; so here pra is used separated. Here ca conveys the joining with the earlier action: juhota, pratiṣṭhata ca, "make the homa, and having made it go to another place". It does not convey joining with iṣyata as pratiṣṭhata iṣyata ca. So, with reference to the action joined by ca, tiṣṭhata is not the first tiṅanta. So "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. sū. 8-1-59): when joined with ca or vā, the first tiṅanta is not unaccented; this bar does not apply, and by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" it is wholly unaccented.

नेष्ट्रात् (neṣṭrāt): the derivation must be given here as for the word potra in the mantra potrād yajñaṃ punītana (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-2).

इष्यत (iṣyata): iṣa gatau (divādi), loṭ, 2nd plural tha; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the laṅvadbhāva; by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) ta for tha; by "divādibhyaḥ śyan" the vikaraṇa śyan: iṣyata. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे द्रविणोदो देव यद्यस्मात्कारणादृतुभिः सह त्वां यजामहे । अधेत्ययं निपातस्तच्छब्दार्थः । तस्मात्कारणान्नो ऽस्मभ्यं ददिर्धनस्य दाता भव स्म । अवश्यं भव । तुरीयं चतुर्णां पूरणं ॥ तुरीयं । चतुरश्छयतावाद्यक्षरलोपश्च । पा. ५-२-५१-१ । इति छप्रत्ययः । तस्य प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तात्प्रागेवायनेयीनीत्यादिना । पा. ७-१-२ । ईयादेशः । आयनादिषूपदेशिवद्वचनं स्वरसिद्ध्यर्थं । पा. ७-१-२-१ । इति वचनात्कृत आदेशे प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । द्रविणोदः । उक्तं । पादादित्वादामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । यजामहे । अत्र शपः पित्त्वेन तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव । पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वाद्यद्वृत्तयोगाद्वा न निघातः । व्यवहितयोगे ऽपि हि स निषेध इत्युक्तं । अध । छान्दसो धकारः । स्म । चादिरनुदात्तः । संहितायां निपातस्य चेति दीर्घः । ददिः । डुदाञ् दाने । आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च । पा. ३-२-१७१ । इति किप्रत्ययः । लिड्वद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनादि । आतो लोप इटि च । पा. ६-४-६४ । इत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

he draviṇodo deva yadyasmātkāraṇādṛtubhiḥ saha tvāṃ yajāmahe | adhetyayaṃ nipātastacchabdārthaḥ | tasmātkāraṇānno 'smabhyaṃ dadirdhanasya dātā bhava sma | avaśyaṃ bhava | turīyaṃ caturṇāṃ pūraṇaṃ || turīyaṃ | caturaśchayatāvādyakṣaralopaśca | pā. 5-2-51-1 | iti chapratyayaḥ | tasya pratyayasvareṇodāttātprāgevāyaneyīnītyādinā | pā. 7-1-2 | īyādeśaḥ | āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyarthaṃ | pā. 7-1-2-1 | iti vacanātkṛta ādeśe pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | draviṇodaḥ | uktaṃ | pādāditvādāmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | yajāmahe | atra śapaḥ pittvena tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva | pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvādyadvṛttayogādvā na nighātaḥ | vyavahitayoge 'pi hi sa niṣedha ityuktaṃ | adha | chāndaso dhakāraḥ | sma | cādiranudāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasya ceti dīrghaḥ | dadiḥ | ḍudāñ dāne | ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca | pā. 3-2-171 | iti kipratyayaḥ | liḍvadbhāvāddvirvacanādi | āto lopa iṭi ca | pā. 6-4-64 | ityākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "O god Draviṇodas, yat, since, we worship you with the Ṛtus, adha, a particle in the sense of tad, for that reason be dadiḥ, the giver of wealth, naḥ, to us: bhava sma, be so without fail. Turīyam: the filler of four, the fourth." (Grammatical tail: turīyam with cha and the loss of the first syllable by the vārttika 5-2-51-1, the replacement īya (Pā. 7-1-2) made first, before the suffix accent, by the vārttika 7-1-2-1, so the ī is udātta; draviṇodaḥ as said, initial udātta at the head of the pāda; yajāmahe, the root accent, not lowered, the earlier vocative counting as absent, or because of the relative yat, for the bar holds even when yat is not adjacent; adha, the dh Vedic; sma, unaccented as of the cādi class, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by nipātasya ca; dadiḥ, ki after dā (Pā. 3-2-171), reduplication as in liṭ, the ā dropped (Pā. 6-4-64), the suffix accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

द्रविणोदः (draviṇodaḥ) — O Agni, giver of wealth | यत् (yat) — for the reason that | ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ) — with the Ṛtu deities | तुरीयम् (turīyam) — for the fourth time | त्वा (tvā) — you | यजामहे (yajāmahe) — we worship | अध (adha) — so | नः (naḥ) — to us | ददिः (dadiḥ) — as the giver of wealth | भव स्म (bhava sma) — be, without fail.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, seeking wealth, we worship you, the fourth, with the Ṛtu deities. So surely accept our worship and become the giver of wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Dravinodas, Since we adore you for the fourth time along with the Ritus; therefore be a giver (of riches) to us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Turīyam: for the fourth time. In this sūkta there are four Ṛks praising Agni called Draviṇodas (the Ṛks from 7 to 10); among them this is the fourth. So here turīyam means "for the fourth time", or "we praise with the fourth Ṛk".

original p. 665

Rik 10: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 665–666, noted briefly

तुरीयम् (turīyam): analysed caturṇāṃ pūraṇam. "caturaś chayatāv ādyakṣaralopaś ca" (Pā. sū. "5-2-51" [as printed; the bhāṣya gives 5-2-51-1]): in the sense of filling, after catur the suffixes cha and yat come alternately, and the first syllable also drops; so the suffix cha after catur: catur + cha; by this vārttika itself the first akṣara drops. Akṣara should not be explained as the first consonant with its vowel, nor as the first vowel with its consonant. If it is so explained, by the maxim "naṭabhāryāvad vyañjanāni bhavanti" it would mean the first vowel with the consonants before and after it, and then in catur the cat would have to drop. So ādyakṣara means the first consonant with its vowel. Thus ca drops: tur + cha. "āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyartham" (Pā. Ma. "2-1-2-1" [as printed, for 7-1-2-1]): before the initial udātta comes by "ādyudāttaś ca", by "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. "2-1-2" [as printed, for 7-1-2]) īya replaces the suffix cha; after this replacement, by the suffix accent the ī of īya becomes udātta.

द्रविणोदः (draviṇodaḥ): its formation is set out in the 7th mantra. Here draviṇodaḥ is a vocative singular, so it is a vocative. Being at the head of the pāda, it is not made unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19); by the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) it is initial udātta.

यजामहे (yajāmahe): yaja devapūjādau, laṭ, ātmanepada 1st plural mahiṅ; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68): yaj + a + mahi; e for the ṭi by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); lengthening by "ato dīrgho yañi" (Pā. sū. 7-3-101): yajāmahe. Here śap is pit, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). The sārvadhātuka mahe in place of the lakāra follows the śap of adupadeśa, so it is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttet…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186). So the root accent remains. The earlier vocative draviṇodaḥ is treated as absent by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. "8-1-27" [as printed, for 8-1-72]); so yajāmahe counts as at the head of the pāda, and "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" ("8-8-28" [as printed]) does not make it wholly unaccented. Or the bar comes by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66). Since pūjita is mentioned again in "pūjanāt pūjitam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-67), it is made known that "in this section, though there is a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required", as was set out before. So, though yat is not adjacent, there is no obstacle to the bar of yadvṛttān nityam.

original p. 666

Rik 10: grammar (end)

अध (adha): atha is a nipāta; the th becomes dh as a Vedic form. Initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 80).

स्म (sma): unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 84). In the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-136).

ददिः (dadiḥ): the root ḍudāñ dāne. "ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-171): after roots ending in ā and in ṛ, and after gam and the others, the suffixes ki and kin come, and they behave as liṭ; so the suffix ki after the ā-final root dā. Since it behaves as liṭ, reduplication by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8); shortening by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59): da + dā + i; by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-64) the ā drops: dadi. By the suffix accent it is final udātta.

अश्वि॑ना॒ पिब॑तं॒ मधु॒ दीद्य॑ग्नी शुचिव्रता । [accent ?] ऋ॒तुना॑ यज्ञवाहसा ॥११॥

áśvinā píbataṃ mádhu dī́dyagnī śucivratā | [accent ?] ṛtúnā yajñavāhasā ||11||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अश्विना । पिबतम् । मधु । दीद्यग्नी इति दीदिऽअग्नी । शुचिऽव्रता ॥ ऋतुना । यज्ञऽवाहसा ॥११॥

aśvinā | pibatam | madhu | dīdyagnī iti dīdi 'agnī | śuci 'vratā || ṛtunā | yajña 'vāhasā ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अश्विनौ मधु माधुर्योपेतं सोमं पिबतं । कीदृशौ । दीद्यग्नी द्योतमानाहवनीयाद्यग्नियुक्तौ शुचिव्रता शुद्धकर्माणौ ऋतुना ऋतुदेवतया सह यज्ञवाहसा यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकौ ॥ अश्विना । सम्बोधनद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तः । पिबतं । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्व-

he aśvinau madhu mādhuryopetaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ | kīdṛśau | dīdyagnī dyotamānāhavanīyādyagniyuktau śucivratā śuddhakarmāṇau ṛtunā ṛtudevatayā saha yajñavāhasā yajñasya nirvāhakau || aśvinā | sambodhanadvivacanasya supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | āmantritādyudāttaḥ | pibataṃ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārva-

Rik 11: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English

-धातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । मधु । फलिपाटीत्यादिना । उ. १-१९ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दीद्यग्नी । दिवु क्रीडादौ । अन्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्त इति विच् । वेरपृक्तलोपाद्वलि लोपो बलीयानिति प्रथमं वकारस्य लोपः । पा. ६-१-६६, ६७ । प्रथमं प्रत्ययलोपे हि वर्णाश्रये विधौ प्रत्ययलक्षणं नास्ति । परि. ९१ । इति निषेधाद्वलि लोपो न स्यात् । छान्दसं द्विर्वचनं । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वं । यङ्लुगन्ताद्वा संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः । दीदिरग्निर्ययोस्तौ दीद्यग्नी । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । शुचिव्रता । शुचि व्रतं ययोस्तौ । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दीद्यग्निशब्दस्य सामान्यवचनत्वेन नामन्त्रित इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधादाष्टमिकनिघातत्वं । पूर्वस्य पराङ्गवद्भावाद्वैकस्वर्यं । यज्ञवाहसा । वह प्रापणे । यज्ञं वहत इति यज्ञवाहसौ । वहिहाधाञ्भ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. ४-२२० । इत्यसुन् । तत्र हि गतिकारकयोरपि पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेति वचनात्सोपपदानामपि भवति । उ. ४-२२६ । इत्युक्तं । णिदित्यनुवृत्तेरुपधावृद्धिः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । असामर्थ्यात्पूर्वस्य न पराङ्गवद्भावः ॥

-dhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | madhu | phalipāṭītyādinā | u. 1-19 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | dīdyagnī | divu krīḍādau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vic | verapṛktalopādvali lopo balīyāniti prathamaṃ vakārasya lopaḥ | pā. 6-1-66, 67 | prathamaṃ pratyayalope hi varṇāśraye vidhau pratyayalakṣaṇaṃ nāsti | pari. 91 | iti niṣedhādvali lopo na syāt | chāndasaṃ dvirvacanaṃ | tujāditvādabhyāsasya dīrghatvaṃ | yaṅlugantādvā saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranitya ityabhyāsasya guṇābhāvaḥ | dīdiragniryayostau dīdyagnī | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | śucivratā | śuci vrataṃ yayostau | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | dīdyagniśabdasya sāmānyavacanatvena nāmantrita ityavidyamānavattvapratiṣedhādāṣṭamikanighātatvaṃ | pūrvasya parāṅgavadbhāvādvaikasvaryaṃ | yajñavāhasā | vaha prāpaṇe | yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau | vahihādhāñbhyaśchandasi | u. 4-220 | ityasun | tatra hi gatikārakayorapi pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ceti vacanātsopapadānāmapi bhavati | u. 4-226 | ityuktaṃ | ṇidityanuvṛtterupadhāvṛddhiḥ | supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterākāraḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | asāmarthyātpūrvasya na parāṅgavadbhāvaḥ ||

Translation: "O Aśvins, drink the madhu, the soma that is full of sweetness. What are you like? Dīdyagnī, joined with the shining fires, the Āhavanīya and the others; śucivratā, of pure rites; ṛtunā, with the Ṛtu deity, yajñavāhasā, carriers through of the sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: aśvinā, ā for the vocative dual by supāṃ suluk…, initial udātta; pibatam, the root accent; madhu with u (Uṇ. 1-19), initial udātta; dīdyagnī: div 'to play' with vic; by ver apṛktalopād vali lopo balīyān the v drops first (Pā. 6-1-66, 67), since if the suffix dropped first, by "varṇāśraye vidhau pratyayalakṣaṇaṃ nāsti" (pari. 91) the loss before val would not come; Vedic reduplication, the reduplicate lengthened as of the tujādi class, or from the yaṅluk form, its guṇa not made by saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ; "whose fire is shining", initial udātta, not lowered at the head of the pāda; śucivratā, "whose rite is pure", ā for the ending, lowered by the eighth-adhyāya rule, since dīdyagnī, being a general term, is not treated as absent (nāmantrite…), and the earlier word is joined to it as part of the following (one accent); yajñavāhasā, "who carry the sacrifice", asun (Uṇ. 4-220), which applies with an upapada too by the statement on the first-member accent (Uṇ. 4-226), vṛddhi of the penultimate, ā for the ending, lowered as a vocative; the earlier word is not joined to it, not being connected in sense.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī) — shining with the fires, the Āhavanīya and the others | शुचिव्रता (śucivratā) — having pure rites | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — with the Ṛtu deity | यज्ञवाहसा (yajñavāhasā) — who carry through the sacrifice | अश्विना (aśvinā) — O Aśvin deities | मधु (madhu) — the sweet soma juice | पिबतम् (pibatam) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Aśvin deities, you always shine together with the fires, the Āhavanīya and the others. With the Ṛtu deity you carry the sacrifice through. Kindly drink the sweet soma juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Aswins, performers of pious acts, accepters of the sacrifice with the Ritus, and accompained [sic] by brilliant Agni, drink the sweet draught.

original p. 668

Rik 11: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Dīdyagnī:

दिवु क्रीडादौ । दीदिरग्निर्ययोस्तौ ॥

divu krīḍādau | dīdiragniryayostau ||

"joined with the shining Āhavanīya and other fires": that is, since the homa is made in the Āhavanīya and other fires with these Aśvin deities in view, they are said to have shining fires.

Śucivratā:

शुचि व्रतं ययोस्तौ

śuci vrataṃ yayostau

"having pure rites": that is, the rites they perform are pure.

Yajñavāhasā:

वह प्रापणे । यज्ञं वहत इति यज्ञवाहसौ । यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकौ ॥

vaha prāpaṇe | yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau | yajñasya nirvāhakau ||

those who carry the sacrifice through, who make it go on without obstacle.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 668–670, noted briefly

अश्विना (aśvinā): for the vocative dual, the replacement ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); initial udātta by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198). Being at the head of the pāda, the eighth-adhyāya lowering does not come.

पिबतम् (pibatam): pā pāne; loṭ, 2nd dual thas; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the laṅvadbhāva; so by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) tam for thas: pā + tam; by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap; by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78) piba for pā: piba + a + tam; pararūpa by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97): pibatam. On the view that the replacement piba ends in a, piba is made initial udātta by nipātana in the sūtra; the Vārttikakāra says this under "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162): "pibater nipātanāt". On this view the laghūpadha-guṇa of "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) has no scope. This is the settled view. On the view that the replacement enjoined in pāghrādhmā… is pib, ending in b, the final-udātta accent follows easily by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162). By "aṅgavṛtte punar vṛttāv avidhiḥ" (paribhāṣā 93) the guṇa must be barred so that it does not come after the pib replacement. This view is the one taken in the Vedabhāṣya as dhātusvara eva śiṣyate. Śap is pit, so unaccented; the sārvadhātuka tam in the place of the lakāra is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttet…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186); so the i of pib is udātta by the root accent.

original p. 669

Rik 11: grammar (continued)

मधु (madhu): the formation of this is set out in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-2 [as printed "1-1-3-2"]; here it is given briefly. After the root mana jñāne, the suffix u by "phalipāṭi…" (Uṇ. sū. 1-18); nit is carried on here, so the suffix u is nit; so madhu is initial udātta by the nit accent.

दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī): the root divu krīḍādau; after it, by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. sū. 3-2-75) the suffixes manin, kvanip, vanip and vic come after roots; so vic after div: div + v. By "ver apṛktalopād vali lopo balīyān", the loss before val enjoined by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66) is stronger than the loss of the v enjoined by "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. sū. "6-1-62" [as printed, for 6-1-67]); so, though the apṛkta loss is antaraṅga, the first v drops first by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66). On the view that the suffix drops first by "ver apṛktasya", by "varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam" (paribhāṣā "93-1" [?]), when an operation based on a letter is made, pratyayalakṣaṇa does not apply; so the following val could not be had, and the loss of the first v would not come. So first the first v drops as said, then the second v drops by "ver apṛktasya". As a Vedic form di is reduplicated: didi. Now by "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-7) the first di is lengthened: dīdi. Or, after the root div, by "dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-22) yaṅ; by "yaṅo 'ci ca" (Pā. sū. 2-4-74) yaṅ takes luk; by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: div div; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60) the v of the reduplicate goes: didiv. "guṇo yaṅlukoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-82): in yaṅ and in yaṅluk an ik-final reduplicate takes guṇa; so the first di would get guṇa. But by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā "93-1" [?]) the guṇa rule is not binding, so it does not come here. "dīrgho 'kitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-83): a vowel-final reduplicate that is not kit is lengthened in yaṅ and yaṅluk; so dīdiv. With vic as before, dīdi. Dīdiḥ agniḥ yayoḥ tau dīdyagnī, a bahuvrīhi compound. Though the lowering would come by the eighth-adhyāya sūtra, being at the head of the pāda it does not come here; by the sixth-adhyāya sūtra it is initial udātta.

शुचिव्रता (śucivratā): analysed śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ tau. By "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. "3-1-39" [as printed, for 7-1-39]) ā for the vocative-nominative dual. The two vocatives dīdyagnī and śucivratā are described as construed with aśvinā. So aśvinā is the general term,

original p. 670

Rik 11: grammar (end)

and the other two vocatives, being qualifiers, are themselves particular terms. So "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. sū. "8-1-23" [as printed, for 8-1-73]) has no scope. Since the two vocatives are not construed with each other, there is no connection of sense, so "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. "3-1-2" [as printed, for 2-1-2]) gives no joining as part of the following either. So the doubt rightly arises how the full lowering in śucivratā fits. But here we take dīdyagnī itself as the qualified, and say that śucivratā is its qualifier, and that this qualified pair is construed with aśvinā. Now dīdyagnī is a general term, so by "nāmantrite…" (Pā. sū. "8-1-23" [as printed]) the treatment as absent that "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. "8-1-62" [as printed, for 8-1-72]) would give is barred; so śucivratā is not at the head of the pāda, and by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) it is wholly unaccented. Or, in this explanation, since dīdyagnī and śucivratā are construed with each other, there is a connection of sense, so by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. "3-1-2" [as printed]) the earlier is joined as part of the following; so the notion arises that dīdyagnī śucivratā is one word. So by the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) the first letter dī is initial udātta. Then by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. sū. "6-1-148" [as printed, for 6-1-158]) the other letters are unaccented. The unaccented di after the udātta becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" ("8-4-66"); the unaccented syllables after the svarita are pracaya by "svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām".

यज्ञवाहसा (yajñavāhasā): yajñaṃ vahataḥ iti yajñavāhasau; the root vaha prāpaṇe. "vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi" (Uṇ. sū. "4-660" [?]; vaha prāpaṇe, ohāk tyāge, ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ): after these roots the suffix asun comes, and it is ṇit; so the suffix asun after vah with the object-kāraka yajñam as upapada. Since by "gatikārakayor api pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca" (Uṇ. sū. "4-666" [?]) it is said that these suffixes come after roots with gati or kāraka upapadas, though in the sūtra vahihā… a root without upapada is named, the suffix asun comes after roots with an upapada too: yajña + am + vah + as. The suffix is ṇit, so vṛddhi of the penultimate by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116). Being a kṛdanta, it is called a prātipadika; so the am inside the prātipadika takes luk. For the vocative dual au, the replacement ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39). The two words ṛtunā and yajñavāhasā are not construed with each other; so "subāmantrite…" does not join the earlier ṛtunā as part of the following. By "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) it is wholly unaccented.

॥११॥

original p. 671

Sūkta 15, Rik 12 (last rik of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ The strokes over गा, ना, नी and दे are clear; the bars under ऋ, ज्ञ, दे and य of देवयते are read from the print and the Pada; not all certain.

गार्ह॑पत्येन सन्त्य ऋ॒तुना॑ यज्ञ॒नीर॑सि । [accent ?] दे॒वान्दे॑व॒य॒ते य॑ज ॥१२॥ [accent ?]

gā́rhapatyena santya ṛtúnā yajñanī́r asi | [accent ?] devā́n devayaté yaja ||12|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

गार्हऽपत्येन । सन्त्य । ऋतुना । यज्ञऽनीः । असि ॥ देवान् । देवऽयते । यज ॥१२॥

gārha 'patyena | santya | ṛtunā | yajña 'nīḥ | asi || devān | deva 'yate | yaja ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सन्त्य फलप्रदाग्निदेव गार्हपत्येन गृहपतिसम्बन्धिना रूपेण युक्तः सन्नृतुना ऋतुदेवेन सह यज्ञनीर्यज्ञस्य निर्वाहको ऽसि । तस्मात्त्वं देवयते देवविषयकामनायुक्ताय यजमानाय देवान्यज ॥ गार्हपत्येन । गृहपतिना संयुक्ते ञ्यः । पा. ४-४-९० । यस्येति लोपः । ञित्त्वादादिवृद्धिराद्युदात्तत्वं च । गृहपतित्वमित्यर्थे पत्यन्तपुरोहितादिभ्यः । पा. ५-१-१२८ । इति यकि त्वन्तोदात्तत्वं स्यात् । सन्त्य । सनने भव । षणु दाने । क्तिच्क्तौ चेति क्तिच् । न क्तिचि दीर्घश्च । पा. ६-४-३९ । इति दीर्घनलोपाभावः । भवे छन्दसि । पा. ४-४-११० । इति यत् । तत्र साधुः । पा. ४-४-९८ । इति वा । निघातः । यज्ञं नयतीति यज्ञनीः । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । देवयते । देवानात्मन इच्छतीति देवयन् । तस्मै । क्यचि चेतीत्वं न भवति । न च्छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येति निषेधात् । अश्वाघस्य । पा. ७-४-३७ । इत्यात्वविधानादीत्वनिषेधे प्राप्तस्य दीर्घस्याप्येष निषेध इत्युक्तं । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । अत्र क्यचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणोभयोः क्यचा सहैकादेश एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । तस्मादन्तोदात्तात्परस्या विभक्तेः शतुरनुमो नद्यजादीत्युदात्तत्वं ॥ २९ ॥

he santya phalapradāgnideva gārhapatyena gṛhapatisambandhinā rūpeṇa yuktaḥ sannṛtunā ṛtudevena saha yajñanīryajñasya nirvāhako 'si | tasmāttvaṃ devayate devaviṣayakāmanāyuktāya yajamānāya devānyaja || gārhapatyena | gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ | pā. 4-4-90 | yasyeti lopaḥ | ñittvādādivṛddhirādyudāttatvaṃ ca | gṛhapatitvamityarthe patyantapurohitādibhyaḥ | pā. 5-1-128 | iti yaki tvantodāttatvaṃ syāt | santya | sanane bhava | ṣaṇu dāne | kticktau ceti ktic | na ktici dīrghaśca | pā. 6-4-39 | iti dīrghanalopābhāvaḥ | bhave chandasi | pā. 4-4-110 | iti yat | tatra sādhuḥ | pā. 4-4-98 | iti vā | nighātaḥ | yajñaṃ nayatīti yajñanīḥ | satsūdviṣetyādinā kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | devayate | devānātmana icchatīti devayan | tasmai | kyaci cetītvaṃ na bhavati | na cchandasyaputrasyeti niṣedhāt | aśvāghasya | pā. 7-4-37 | ityātvavidhānādītvaniṣedhe prāptasya dīrghasyāpyeṣa niṣedha ityuktaṃ | śaturanumo nadyajādī iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | atra kyacaścittvādantodāttatvaṃ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇobhayoḥ kyacā sahaikādeśa ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | tasmādantodāttātparasyā vibhakteḥ śaturanumo nadyajādītyudāttatvaṃ || 29 ||

Translation: "O santya, Agni, god who gives the fruit, joined with the form belonging to the master of the house, gārhapatyena, you are with the Ṛtu god yajñanīḥ, the one who carries the sacrifice through. So, devayate, for the sacrificer who longs for the gods, worship the gods." (Grammatical tail: gārhapatyena, ñya by Pā. 4-4-90 "joined with the master of the house", the i dropped, initial vṛddhi and initial udātta (ñit); with yak by Pā. 5-1-128 in the sense of mastership it would be final udātta; santya, "who is in the giving", san with ktic, no lengthening or loss of n (Pā. 6-4-39), then yat by Pā. 4-4-110 or 4-4-98, lowered; yajñanīḥ, "who leads the sacrifice", kvip, the kṛt second-member accent; devayate, "who desires the gods for himself", no ī before kyac by na chandasy aputrasya, which bars the lengthening too, as shown by Pā. 7-4-37 enjoining ā; the ending udātta by śatur anumo nadyajādī; kyac final udātta (cit), śap and śatṛ unaccented, the single replacements udātta. The closing "29" is the varga number.)

original p. 672

Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सन्त्य (santya) — O Agni, able to give fruit, (you) | गार्हपत्येन (gārhapatyena) — joined with the gārhapatya fire | ऋतुना (ṛtunā) — with the Ṛtu god | यज्ञनीः (yajñanīḥ) — as the one who carries the sacrifice through | असि (asi) — you are; (so) | देवयते (devayate) — for the sacrificer who seeks the gods for the sacrifice | देवान् (devān) — the gods | यज (yaja) — worship.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O god Agni, you give what is desired. In the form of the gārhapatya fire, you carry through the sacrificer's rites with the Ṛtu god. So, for the sacrificer who always seeks the worship of the gods, carry the sacrifice through.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, giver of rewards, being the lord of the house, and partaker with Ritu of the sacrifice, perform the sacrifice on behalf of the worshipper.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Santya:

षणु दाने । सनने भव ॥

ṣaṇu dāne | sanane bhava ||

The root ṣaṇu means to give; so the word santya, formed from this root, means giver. Giver of what? Giver of the fruit of sacrificial rites; or, as said in words like ratnadhātamaḥ, giver of wealth and lordship.

Yajñanīḥ:

यज्ञं नयतीति यज्ञनीः । यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकः ॥

yajñaṃ nayatīti yajñanīḥ | yajñasya nirvāhakaḥ ||

one who carries the sacrifice through.

Devayate:

देवानात्मन इच्छतीति देवयन् तस्मै यजमानाय ॥

devānātmana icchatīti devayan tasmai yajamānāya ||

that is, for the sake of the sacrificer who longs for the gods to come to the sacrifice he performs.

original p. 673

Rik 12: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 673–676, noted briefly

गार्हपत्येन (gārhapatyena): "gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-4-90): after the fitting instrumental of gṛhapati, in the sense "joined", the suffix ñya; so ñya after gṛhapatinā: gṛhapati + ṭā + ñya. By "cuṭū" (Pā. sū. 1-3-7) the ñ at the beginning of the suffix is it; dropped by "tasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-9). The ṭā, a sup inside a taddhita-ending stem, takes luk by "supo dhātu…" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71): gṛhapati + ya. The i drops by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); the suffix is ñit, so initial vṛddhi by "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-117); r after it by "uraṇ raparaḥ": gārhapatya. The suffix is ñit, so initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). "patyantapurohitādibhyo yak" (Pā. sū. 5-1-128): after the fitting genitive of stems ending in pati or read in the purohitādi class, in the senses of state and act, yak; if one explained that yak comes after gṛhapati, ending in pati, in the sense gṛhapater bhāvaḥ, the form gārhapatya would indeed be got. But then by the suffix accent gārhapatya would be final udātta, and the initial udātta would not be got. So the suffix ñya is set out.

सन्त्य (santya): sanane bhava: "being in giving the fruit". The root ṣaṇu dāne. "ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 3-3-174): when a blessing or a name is meant, the suffixes ktic and kta come after a root; so ktic. S for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; the ṇ that came by "raṣābhyām…" reverts: san + ti. "na ktici dīrghaś ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-39): before ktic, the anudāttopadeśa roots, that is, the aniṭ roots, and the roots vana, tanoti and the rest get neither the lengthening nor the loss of the nasal: that is the sense of the sūtra. By "anunāsikasya kvijhaloḥ kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-15), before kvi and before a jhal-initial kit or ṅit suffix, the penultimate of a root ending in a nasal is lengthened; that lengthening, and the loss of the n by "anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-37), which drops the final nasal of tanoti and the others and of the root van before a jhal-initial kit or ṅit suffix, are both barred by na ktici dīrghaś ca. So santi. In fact here

original p. 674

Rik 12: grammar (continued)

"sanaḥ ktici lopaś cāsyānyatarasyām" (Pā. sū. "6-4-46" [as printed, for 6-4-45]): before ktic the n of the root san drops and ā comes, both optionally; since ā and the loss of n are enjoined as optional, it is fitting to explain that where neither comes the form santi is got. Under "sarva evāyaṃ yogaḥ śakyo 'vaktum" (Pā. Mabhā. "6-4-45" [?]), on the view that the whole sūtra can be dropped, the Kaiyaṭa says that sanaḥ ktici ity eva lopasya prakaraṇāt siddhatvāl lopaś ca ity api na vaktavyam. Since many words are rejected, the Bhāṣya says "sarva evāyaṃ yogaḥ". It is explained that lopaḥ, ca, asya, anyatarasyām, many words, are rejected as unnecessary, so the Bhāṣya "sarva evāyam" begins; and rejecting the whole sūtra is not the Bhāṣya's intention; it is explained that the sūtra sanaḥ ktici alone is enough. On this view, since the ā and the loss of n enjoined by sanaḥ ktici are optional, it is fitting to explain that where they do not come the form santi is got. If the analysis santyāṃ bhavaḥ is meant, by "bhave chandasi" (Pā. sū. "4-41-10" [as printed, for 4-4-110]) the suffix yat comes in the Veda after the fitting locative of a stem in the sense of being; with yat, santi + ṅi + ya. Or if the analysis santyāṃ sādhuḥ is made, by "tatra sādhuḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-4-98) yat in the sense sādhu after the fitting locative; with yat, santi + ṅi + ya. In both places the sup inside the taddhita-ending stem takes luk. By "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the i drops: santya. Nominative singular santyaḥ, vocative singular santya. Wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19).

यज्ञनीः (yajñanīḥ): yajñaṃ nayati iti yajñanīḥ. "satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidacchidajinīrājām upasarge 'pi kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-61): ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau; the root sū is threefold: ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane (adādi), ṣūṅ prāṇiprasave (divādi), ṣū preraṇe (tudādi). Here by "sahacaritāsahacaritayoḥ sahacaritasyaiva grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā 113) the adādi root is taken, being in company with the adādi root dviṣ; dviṣa aprītau, druha jighāṃsāyām, duha prapūraṇe, yujir yoge, yuja samādhau; vida is taken in all three, vida jñāne (adādi), vida sattāyām (divādi), vida vicāraṇe (tudādi); since vida is named ending in a, the tudādi root vidḷ lābhe is not taken; bhidir vidāraṇe, chidir dvaidhīkaraṇe, ji jaye, ji abhibhave, ṇīñ prāpaṇe, rājṛ dīptau: after these roots, with or without an upasarga, when a subanta is upapada, the suffix kvip comes; so kvip after ṇīñ with the subanta yajñam as upapada; by "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. sū. "6-1-64" [as printed]) n for ṇ. The sup inside

original p. 675

Rik 12: grammar (continued)

the prātipadika takes luk, the kvip drops: yajñanī; nominative singular su; ru, visarga: yajñanīḥ. The second member nī is final udātta by the root accent. After compounding, the kṛt second-member accent comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) and that accent remains.

देवयते (devayate): when analysed devān ātmanaḥ icchati (who desires the gods for himself), it becomes devayan. Thus: by "supa ātmanaḥ kyac" (Pā. sū. 3-1-8) kyac after devam; by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-32) it is called a root. The sup inside the root takes luk by "supo dhātu…" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71): deva + ya. Now by "kyaci ca" (Pā. sū. 7-4-33) ī would come for the a before kyac; but "na chandasy aputrasya" (Pā. sū. 7-4-35): before kyac, short a-final words other than putra get neither ī nor lengthening: that is the sense of the sūtra, carefully drawn out. By "anantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā" (paribhāṣā 61) this bar might seem to bar only the immediately preceding kyaci ca. Then, though no ī came, the lengthening by "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-25) would have to come; for kyaci ca is an exception to akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ, and when the exception does not come, the general rule comes without obstacle. So na chandasi must be explained to mean that whatever would come before kyac for an a-final word other than putra does not come; the anantarasya paribhāṣā is not relied on. The proof on this point is "aśvāghasyāt" (Pā. sū. 7-4-37): the very prescription of ā for aśva and agha before kyac in the Veda is the proof. In aśvāyantaḥ and aghāyavaḥ the ā is prescribed so that a long ā is heard. If na chandasy aputrasya barred only the ī by the anantara maxim, the lengthening would come by akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ itself, and the forms aśvāyantaḥ, aghāyavaḥ would be got. Then the sūtra aśvāghasyāt would be useless. By the maxim vyarthaṃ sat kiṃcid arthaṃ jñāpayati, this sūtra makes known that the bar is not only of the ī of kyaci ca but of the lengthening too. Now without this sūtra the forms aśvāyantaḥ and the rest would not be got; so the sūtra has its purpose. Thus na chandasi… is settled as barring both ī and lengthening. So in the present case, in deva + ya, no lengthening by akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ comes either. Devaya is a root; after it, by "vartamāne laṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-123) laṭ; in its place by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau…" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) śatṛ: devaya + at; śap by "kartari śap": devaya + a + at; by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97) pararūpa twice: devayat.

original p. 676

Rik 12: grammar (end); close of Sūkta 15

Here the suffix kyac is cit, so final udātta by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163). Śap is pit, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). The suffix at, śatṛ, has come in the place of the lakāra laṭ; being śit, it is a sārvadhātuka by "tiṅśit sārvadhātukam" (Pā. sū. 3-4-113); it follows śap, an a-final upadeśa. So by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186) at is unaccented. The a that came by the single pararūpa with the a of śap is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5); the a that came by pararūpa of this udātta and the unaccented a of at is udātta in the same way. So in devayat the ya is udātta, and it is settled as final udātta. After it, the dative singular ṅe: devayat + e; "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173): after a final-udātta word ending in a śatṛ suffix without the augment num, a nadī letter and a vowel-initial ending from śas on are also udātta; so the ending e is udātta.

॥१२॥ The sūkta ends here; the print has no separate colophon for Sūkta 15; the bhāṣya closes with the varga number "29", agreeing with the heading's 28, 29.

॥ ಹದಿನಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 16 — "ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ" ("The Sixteenth Sūkta")

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 676, after the close of Sūkta 15; re-read from the print

आ त्वा वहन्त्विति पञ्चमं नवर्चं सूक्तम् । ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । अनुवर्तते विशेषादेशाभावादिन्द्रो देवता ॥ विनियोगस्तु । प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणस्योन्नीयमाने सूक्तमा त्वा वहन्तु हरय इति । तथा च द्विदेवत्यैश्चरन्तीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । उन्नीयमानेभ्यो ऽन्वाहा त्वा वहन्तु । आ. ५-५ । इति ॥ तथा षोडशिशस्त्र आ त्वा वहन्तु हरय इति तिस्रः । तथा सूत्रितमथ षोडशीति खण्डे । आ त्वा वहन्तु हरय इति तिस्रो गायत्र्यः । आ. ६-२ । इति ॥

ā tvā vahantviti pañcamaṃ navarcaṃ sūktam | ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | anuvartate viśeṣādeśābhāvādindro devatā || viniyogastu | prātaḥsavane maitrāvaruṇasyonnīyamāne sūktamā tvā vahantu haraya iti | tathā ca dvidevatyaiścarantīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | unnīyamānebhyo 'nvāhā tvā vahantu | ā. 5-5 | iti || tathā ṣoḍaśiśastra ā tvā vahantu haraya iti tisraḥ | tathā sūtritamatha ṣoḍaśīti khaṇḍe | ā tvā vahantu haraya iti tisro gāyatryaḥ | ā. 6-2 | iti ||

Translation: "The nine-rik sūkta beginning ā tvā vahantu is the fifth [of this anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. Since no special deity is stated, Indra, the deity carried on [from before], is the deity. Its application: at the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana), when the Maitrāvaruṇa priest is having the soma drawn up (unnayana), the sūkta ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ is recited. And so it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section beginning dvidevatyaiś caranti: 'for those [cups] being drawn up, it recites after: ā tvā vahantu' (Āśv. 5-5). Likewise, in the ṣoḍaśi-śastra, the three riks ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ are used; and it is laid down in the section beginning atha ṣoḍaśī: 'the three Gāyatrīs ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ' (Āśv. 6-2)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta ā tvā vahantu, with nine riks, is the fifth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka. The ṛṣi and meter are as in the earlier sūktas; the deity is Indra. Application: at the morning pressing, in the rite called unnayana done by the priest named Maitrāvaruṇa, this sūkta is to be recited. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra says in the section dvidevatyaiś caranti that for the unnayana the sūkta ā tvā vahantu is to be used (Āś. sū. 5-5). Moreover, in the section ṣoḍaśī, for the ṣoḍaśi-śastra recitation the tṛca [three riks] of this sūkta beginning ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ is to be recited, as the same Sūtra says (Āś. Sū. 6-2).

original p. 677

Sūkta 16, Rik 1

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 16 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 16 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 30, 31 ॥ as printed; Sūkta 15 closed with varga 29 ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indra ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ त्वा॑ वहन्तु॒ हर॑यो॒ वृष॑णं॒ सोम॑पीतये । इन्द्र॑ त्वा॒ सूर॑चक्षसः ॥१॥

ā́ tvā vahantu hárayo vṛ́ṣaṇaṃ sómapītaye | índra tvā sū́racakṣasaḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । त्वा । वहन्तु । हरयः । वृषणम् । सोमऽपीतये ॥ इन्द्र । त्वा । सूरऽचक्षसः ॥१॥

ā | tvā | vahantu | harayaḥ | vṛṣaṇam | soma 'pītaye || indra | tvā | sūra 'cakṣasaḥ ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र वृषणं कामानां वर्षितारं त्वां सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं हरयस्त्वदीया अश्वा आ वहन्तु । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यानयन्तु । तथा सूरचक्षसः सूर्यसमानप्रकाशयुक्ता ऋत्विजस्त्वां मन्त्रैः प्रकाशयन्त्विति शेषः ॥ हरन्तीति हरयः । इन् सर्वधातुभ्यः । उ. ४-११८ । इतीन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वृषणं । कनिन्युवृषितक्षीत्यादिना कनिन् । कित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । वा षपूर्वस्य निगमे । पा. ६-४-९ । इति विकल्पितमुपधादीर्घत्वं । सोमपीतये । ऐभिरग्न इत्यत्रोक्तं । ऋग्वे. १-१४-१ । सूरचक्षसः । चक्षिङ् व्यक्तायां वाचि । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । चक्षिङः ख्याञ् । पा. २-४-५४ । इति न भवति । असनयोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्य इति निषेधात् । षू प्रेरणे । सुवतीति सूरः । सुसूधागृधिभ्यः क्रन् । उ. २-२४ । इति क्रन् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सूरवत्ख्यानं प्रकाशो येषां । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

he indra vṛṣaṇaṃ kāmānāṃ varṣitāraṃ tvāṃ somapītaye somapānārthaṃ harayastvadīyā aśvā ā vahantu | asminkarmaṇyānayantu | tathā sūracakṣasaḥ sūryasamānaprakāśayuktā ṛtvijastvāṃ mantraiḥ prakāśayantviti śeṣaḥ || harantīti harayaḥ | in sarvadhātubhyaḥ | u. 4-118 | itīn | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | vṛṣaṇaṃ | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣītyādinā kanin | kittvāllaghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | vā ṣapūrvasya nigame | pā. 6-4-9 | iti vikalpitamupadhādīrghatvaṃ | somapītaye | aibhiragna ityatroktaṃ | ṛgve. 1-14-1 | sūracakṣasaḥ | cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ | pā. 2-4-54 | iti na bhavati | asanayoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavya iti niṣedhāt | ṣū preraṇe | suvatīti sūraḥ | susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran | u. 2-24 | iti kran | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | sūravatkhyānaṃ prakāśo yeṣāṃ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "O Indra, may the harayaḥ, your horses, ā vahantu, bring you, the vṛṣan, rainer of desires, for the drinking of soma, to this rite. And may the sūracakṣasaḥ, the priests endowed with a radiance like the sun's, make you manifest with mantras: this is to be supplied." (Grammatical tail: harayaḥ, "they carry", in (Uṇ. 4-118), initial udātta; vṛṣaṇam with kanin, no guṇa (kit), the optional lengthening of the penultimate (Pā. 6-4-9) not made; somapītaye as said at Ṛ. 1-14-1; sūracakṣasaḥ: cakṣ with asun, no khyāñ (Pā. 2-4-54) before as/ana by the vārttika; sūra "who urges", kran after sū (Uṇ. 2-24), initial udātta; "whose shining is like the sun's", a bahuvrīhi with the first-member accent.)

original p. 678

Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | वृषणम् (vṛṣaṇam) — who rains (gives) what is desired | त्वा (tvā) — you | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | हरयः (harayaḥ) — (your) horses | आ वहन्तु (ā vahantu) — may they bring (to the place where this rite is going on) | सूरचक्षसः (sūracakṣasaḥ) — the radiant priests, shining like the sun | त्वा (tvā) — you (may they praise).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, you give all that is desired. The radiant priests praise you. Come with your horses to our sacrificial hall to drink soma.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Indra, let your horses bring you, bestower of riches, to drink the Soma-Juice; May the priests radiant as the Sun, praise you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Sūracakṣasaḥ:

सूर्यसमानप्रकाशयुक्ता ऋत्विजस्त्वां मन्त्रैः प्रकाशयन्तु ॥

sūryasamānaprakāśayuktā ṛtvijastvāṃ mantraiḥ prakāśayantu ||

that is, "may the priests, radiant like the sun, praise you with mantras, make you known".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 678–679, noted briefly

हरयः (harayaḥ): the root hṛñ haraṇe. By "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. sū. "4-552" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 4-118) the suffix in after all roots: hṛ + i; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84); r after it by "uraṇ raparaḥ": hari.

original p. 679

Rik 1: grammar (end)

After it, jas; guṇa by "jasi ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-109): hare + as; ay by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): harayas, ru, visarga. Hari is initial udātta by the nit accent.

वृषणम् (vṛṣaṇam): the root vṛṣu secane; after it, by "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 1-154) the suffix kanin. The suffix is kit, so "kṅiti ca" bars the guṇa, and the penultimate guṇa of "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" does not come: vṛṣan. After it the accusative singular am: vṛṣan + am. "vā ṣapūrvasya nigame" (Pā. sū. 6-4-9): before a sarvanāmasthāna suffix other than the vocative, the vowel in the penultimate after a ṣ is lengthened optionally; since the lengthening is enjoined as optional, it does not come here. By "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" (Pā. sū. vā. 8-4-1-1) ṇ for the n: vṛṣaṇam.

सोमपीतये (somapītaye): set out at aibhir agne (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-1).

सूरचक्षसः (sūracakṣasaḥ): the root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci. By "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]) the suffix asun; by "ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-114) asun is an ārdhadhātuka suffix; so by "cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-54), before an ārdhadhātuka suffix, khyāñ would replace cakṣiṅ. But after saying "varjane pratiṣedhaḥ" (Pā. sū. "2-4-54-9" [?]), that khyāñ does not come for cakṣiṅ when avoidance is meant, the Vārttikakāra says "asanayoś ca" (Pā. sū. vā. 2-4-54-10): before the suffixes as and ana, khyāñ does not come for cakṣiṅ. So here, as following, khyāñ does not come for cakṣiṅ. Ṣū preraṇe, a tudādi root; suvati iti sūraḥ: one who urges people to their works. By "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64) s for ṣ. "susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran" (Uṇ. sū. "2-173" [?]; ṣuñ abhiṣave, ṣū preraṇe, ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, gṛdhu abhikāṅkṣāyām): after these roots kran; so kran after sū: sū + ra; the suffix is kit, so "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) bars it, and guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) does not come: sūra. It is initial udātta by the nit accent. Sūravat cakṣaḥ khyānaṃ = prakāśaḥ yeṣāṃ te sūracakṣasaḥ, a bahuvrīhi compound. By "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the first-member accent comes.
