Sūkta 16, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इ॒मा धा॒ना घृ॑त॒स्नुवो॒ हरी॑ इ॒होप॑ वक्षतः । इन्द्रं॑ सु॒खत॑मे॒ रथे॑ ॥२॥

imā́ dhānā́ ghṛtasnúvo hárī ihópa vakṣataḥ | índraṃ sukhátame ráthe ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इमाः । धानाः । घृतऽस्नुवः । हरी इति । इह । उप । वक्षतः ॥ इन्द्रम् । सुखऽतमे । रथे ॥२॥

imāḥ | dhānāḥ | ghṛta 'snuvaḥ | harī iti | iha | upa | vakṣataḥ || indram | sukha 'tame | rathe ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हरिशब्द इन्द्ररथस्य वोढारावश्वावाचष्टे । तथा च श्रुत्यन्तरं । हर्योः स्थातेति । हरिभ्यां त्वेन्द्रो देवतां गमयत्विति च । एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य निघण्टुकार आह । हरी इन्द्रस्येति । तादृशौ हरी इमा यागार्थं वेद्यामासादितत्वेन पुरोवर्तिनीर्धाना भृष्टयवतण्डुलाननुद्दिश्य सुखतमे रथ इन्द्रमवस्थाप्येहास्मिन्कर्मण्युप वक्षतः । वेदिसमीपे वहतां । कीदृशीर्धानाः । घृतस्नुवो ऽलंकरणोपस्तरणाभिघारणेन घृतस्राविणीः ॥ धीयन्त इति धानाः । धाप्यावस्यज्यतिभ्यो नः । उ. ३-६ । इति नः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । घृतस्नुवः । घृतं स्नुवन्तीति घृतस्नुवः । क्विपि तुगभावश्छान्दसः । धातुस्वरः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । स्नोः संयोगपूर्वत्वेन यणभावादुवङादेशः । हरी । हृञ् हरणे । सर्वधातुभ्य इन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । प्रगृह्यत्वात्संहितायां प्रकृतिभावः । वक्षतः । प्रार्थनायां लिङर्थे लेट् । तस्य प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचनं तस् । लेटो ऽडाटावित्यडागमः । शपि प्राप्ते सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् । ढत्वकत्वषत्वानि । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । सुखतमे । गतं ॥

hariśabda indrarathasya voḍhārāvaśvāvācaṣṭe | tathā ca śrutyantaraṃ | haryoḥ sthāteti | haribhyāṃ tvendro devatāṃ gamayatviti ca | etadevābhipretya nighaṇṭukāra āha | harī indrasyeti | tādṛśau harī imā yāgārthaṃ vedyāmāsāditatvena purovartinīrdhānā bhṛṣṭayavataṇḍulānanuddiśya sukhatame ratha indramavasthāpyehāsminkarmaṇyupa vakṣataḥ | vedisamīpe vahatāṃ | kīdṛśīrdhānāḥ | ghṛtasnuvo 'laṃkaraṇopastaraṇābhighāraṇena ghṛtasrāviṇīḥ || dhīyanta iti dhānāḥ | dhāpyāvasyajyatibhyo naḥ | u. 3-6 | iti naḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | ghṛtasnuvaḥ | ghṛtaṃ snuvantīti ghṛtasnuvaḥ | kvipi tugabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | dhātusvaraḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | snoḥ saṃyogapūrvatvena yaṇabhāvāduvaṅādeśaḥ | harī | hṛñ haraṇe | sarvadhātubhya in | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | pragṛhyatvātsaṃhitāyāṃ prakṛtibhāvaḥ | vakṣataḥ | prārthanāyāṃ liṅarthe leṭ | tasya prathamapuruṣadvivacanaṃ tas | leṭo 'ḍāṭāvityaḍāgamaḥ | śapi prāpte sibbahulaṃ leṭīti sip | ḍhatvakatvaṣatvāni | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | sukhatame | gataṃ ||

Translation: "The word hari denotes the two horses that draw Indra's chariot; so another Śruti says 'haryoḥ sthātā', 'standing on the two bays', and 'haribhyāṃ tvendro devatāṃ gamayatu', 'may Indra with the two bays lead you to the gods'; with this in mind the author of the Nighaṇṭu says 'harī indrasya', 'the two bays are Indra's'. May such harī, with Indra set in the sukhatama, most comfortable, chariot, iha upa vakṣataḥ, bring him here to this rite, near the altar, towards imāḥ dhānāḥ, these roasted barley grains set out on the altar for the sacrifice and lying in front. What are the grains like? Ghṛtasnuvaḥ, oozing ghee from being adorned, spread and sprinkled with it." (Grammatical tail: dhānāḥ, "what are set down", na (Uṇ. 3-6), the suffix accent; ghṛtasnuvaḥ, "which drip ghee", kvip without tuk (Vedic), the root accent, then the kṛt second-member accent, uvaṅ since snu follows a conjunct; harī, in, initial udātta, pragṛhya, so natural form in the Saṃhitā; vakṣataḥ, leṭ in the sense of prayer, tas, the augment a, sip, ḍh, k, ṣ, lowered; sukhatame gone through.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हरी (harī) — Indra's two horses | इमाः (imāḥ) — these (made ready on the altar for the sacrifice) | घृतस्नुवः (ghṛtasnuvaḥ) — sprinkled with ghee, that is, soaked in ghee | धानाः (dhānāḥ) — for receiving the grains, barley, rice and the like | सुखतमे (sukhatame) — comfortable | रथे (rathe) — in the chariot | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra (seated) | इह (iha) — here (to the place where this sacrifice goes on) | उप वक्षतः (upa vakṣataḥ) — may they bring.

original p. 681

Rik 2: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The grains, barley, rice and the like, well soaked in ghee for the homa in the sacrifice, are scattered round the sacrificial fire-pit when it is adorned and strewn. May Indra's two horses called Harī, to eat them, bring Indra, seated in the comfortable chariot, near this place of sacrifice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Let the horses convey Indra in an easy-moving chariot hither where these grains of parched barely [sic] steeped in clarified butter are being prepared for the Sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Dhānāḥ: the grains, barley, rice and the like, made ready for the homa in the fire. In the work of consecrating the fire, when the acts of adorning, strewing and so on are done with barley, rice and the like, the grains of that corn are scattered round the fire-pit. They are the share of the sacrifice to be given to Indra's horses. The intention is: may Indra's horses come with Indra to eat it.

Ghṛtasnuvaḥ:

घृतं स्नुवन्तीति घृतस्नुवः

ghṛtaṃ snuvantīti ghṛtasnuvaḥ

well soaked in ghee, or dripping ghee.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 681–683, noted briefly

धानाः (dhānāḥ): dhīyante iti dhānāḥ; the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ. "dhāpṝvasyajyatibhyo naḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "3-296" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 3-6; ḍudhāñ dhāraṇādau, pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, vasa nivāse, aja gatau, ata sātatyagamane): after these roots the suffix na; so na after dhā: dhāna. Since the feminine is meant, ṭāp by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-4): dhāna + ā, lengthening of like vowels; accusative plural dhānāḥ. The na is initial udātta by "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3); the single replacement, lengthening with the suffix ṭā, is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ". So the word dhānā is final udātta.

घृतस्नुवः (ghṛtasnuvaḥ): the root ṣṇu prasravaṇe, adādi. Ghṛtaṃ snuvanti iti ghṛtasnuvaḥ; with the subanta ghṛtam as upapada, kvip after snu by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76),

original p. 682

Rik 2: grammar (continued)

kvip drops; s for ṣ by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64). The am, a sup inside the kṛdanta prātipadika, takes luk: ghṛtasnu. Now, though the kvip, a pit kṛt, has dropped, by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-62) it counts as following; so the augment tuk would come by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk". But by a Vedic process it does not come; or it does not come by "āgamaśāstram anityam" (paribhāṣā 94). Snu being a root, it is final udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162); after compounding too, by the kṛt second-member accent of "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) that accent remains. After ghṛtasnu, śas: ghṛtasnu + as; the u stands after the conjunct sn. So by "oḥ supi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-83), before a vowel-initial sup, a stem of several vowels ending in a root that ends in u, not preceded by a conjunct belonging to the root itself, takes yaṇ: so yaṇ does not come. By "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. "6-9-22" [as printed, for 6-4-77]) uvaṅ for the u: ghṛtasnuvam.

हरी (harī): hṛñ haraṇe; by "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. sū. "4-5-552" [?]) the suffix in, guṇa, r after it; by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) hari is initial udātta. After it the nominative-accusative dual au: hari + au; by "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-102) pūrvasavarṇa-dīrgha: harī. Since by "antādivac ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-85) the ī counts as the end of the earlier word, it is a dual ending in ī. So "īdūded dvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-11): duals ending in ī, ū and e are called pragṛhya; it has this name. So in the Saṃhitā, in harī + iha, with a vowel following, by "plutapragṛhyā aci nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-125), before a vowel pluta and pragṛhya always keep their natural form, so natural form comes. Prakṛtyā svabhāvena nirvikārasvarūpeṇa bhavanaṃ sthitiḥ prakṛtibhāvaḥ: natural form means staying without change.

वक्षतः (vakṣataḥ): vaha prāpaṇe; after it, by "liṅarthe leṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-7), leṭ in the sense of liṅ, that is, prayer; its 3rd dual tas: vah + tas; by "leṭo 'ḍāṭau" (Pā. sū. 3-4-94) the augment a for leṭ: vah + a + tas; though śap would come by "kartari śap", overriding it, by "sib bahulaṃ leṭi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-34) sip: vah + s + atas. By "ho ḍhaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-31) ḍh for h; by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" (Pā. sū. 8-2-41) k for ḍh: vak + s + atas; by "ādeśa-

original p. 683

Rik 2: grammar (end)

pratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for the s: vakṣatas; ru and visarga: vakṣataḥ. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

सुखतमे (sukhatame): explained at agne sukhatame rathe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-4).

॥२॥

Page 683 (lower) — Sūkta 16, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Line 1: the bars under प्रा, ह and य and under ध्व are read as printed; the stroke over त्य, the svarita of the yaṇ, as the grammar on p. 686 explains.

इन्द्रं॑ प्रा॒तर्ह॑वामह॒ इन्द्रं॑ प्रय॒त्य॑ध्व॒रे । [accent ?] इन्द्रं॒ सोम॑स्य पी॒तये॑ ॥३॥

índraṃ prātár havāmaha índraṃ prayaty adhvaré | [accent ?] indraṃ sómasya pītáye ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रम् । प्रातः । हवामहे । इन्द्रम् । प्रऽयति । अध्वरे ॥ इन्द्रम् । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥३॥

indram | prātaḥ | havāmahe | indram | pra 'yati | adhvare || indram | somasya | pītaye ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रातः कर्मारम्भे प्रातःसवन इन्द्रं हवामहे । आह्वयामः । तथैवाध्वरे सोमयागे प्रयति प्रगच्छति प्रारभ्य वर्तमाने सति माध्यन्दिने सवने तमिन्द्रं हवामहे । तथा यज्ञसमाप्त्यवसरे तृतीयसवने सोमस्य पीतये सोमपानार्थं हवामहे ॥ प्रातः । स्वरादिष्वन्तोदात्तो निपातितः । हवामहे । ह्वेञो लटि शपि परतो ह्वः सम्प्रसारणमित्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणं । परपूर्वत्वं । गुणावादेशौ । प्रयति । इण् गतौ । लटः शतृ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । शतुर्ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्रादिसमासः । कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणं । परि. २८ । इति वचनात्प्रत्ययग्रहण इति नियमाभावाच्छतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । अध्वरे । उक्तं । संहितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितो ऽनुदात्तस्य । पा. ८-२-४ । इत्यकारस्य स्वरितत्वं । पीतये । पा पाने । क्तिनि छान्दसमन्तोदात्तत्वं ॥

prātaḥ karmārambhe prātaḥsavana indraṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | tathaivādhvare somayāge prayati pragacchati prārabhya vartamāne sati mādhyandine savane tamindraṃ havāmahe | tathā yajñasamāptyavasare tṛtīyasavane somasya pītaye somapānārthaṃ havāmahe || prātaḥ | svarādiṣvantodātto nipātitaḥ | havāmahe | hveño laṭi śapi parato hvaḥ samprasāraṇamityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇaṃ | parapūrvatvaṃ | guṇāvādeśau | prayati | iṇ gatau | laṭaḥ śatṛ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | śaturṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | prādisamāsaḥ | kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇaṃ | pari. 28 | iti vacanātpratyayagrahaṇa iti niyamābhāvācchaturanumo nadyajādī iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | adhvare | uktaṃ | saṃhitāyāmudāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya | pā. 8-2-4 | ityakārasya svaritatvaṃ | pītaye | pā pāne | ktini chāndasamantodāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "Prātaḥ, at the start of the rite, at the morning pressing, havāmahe, we call, Indra. In the same way, adhvare, at the soma sacrifice, prayati, as it goes on, having begun, at the midday pressing, we call that Indra. And at the time of the sacrifice's close, at the third pressing, we call him somasya pītaye, to drink soma." (Grammatical tail: prātaḥ, made final udātta by nipātana in the svarādi class; havāmahe: hve, laṭ, śap, saṃprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi, pūrvarūpa, guṇa, av; prayati: iṇ 'to go', śatṛ, śap dropped, no guṇa (ṅit), a prādi compound; by "kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (pari. 28) the restriction to the bare suffix does not apply, so the ending is udātta by śatur anumo nadyajādī; adhvare as said; in the Saṃhitā the a becomes svarita after the yaṇ by Pā. 8-2-4; pītaye, pā with ktin, final udātta as Vedic.)

original p. 684

Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

प्रातः (prātaḥ) — at the morning pressing (held at the start of the rite) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call | अध्वरे (adhvare) — the soma sacrifice | प्रयति (prayati) — while it is going on (at the midday pressing that comes) | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | havāmahe — we call | and likewise, at the third pressing held at the close of the sacrifice सोमस्य (somasya) — of the soma juice | पीतये (pītaye) — for drinking (Indra) | .

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

At all three pressing times that are parts of the soma sacrifice, the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing, we call Indra to drink soma.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke Indra at the morning rite, we invoke Indra at the succeeding Sacrifice, we invoke Indra to drink the Soma-Juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In a sacrificial rite the procedure is to crush the soma creeper and make the soma juice ready for drinking at all three times, morning, midday and evening. These acts are named in order the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. Though only the morning is named in this Ṛk, since Indra is called to drink soma at the sacrifice that goes on afterwards too, the ṛṣi's meaning is that Indra is called at all three pressings mentioned.

Prayati: iṇ gatau; pragacchati: when the sacrificial rite is going on, or proceeding, that is, at the midday and third pressings held at midday and evening: that is the sense.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 684–686, noted briefly

प्रातः (prātaḥ): made final udātta by nipātana in the svarādi class.

हवामहे (havāmahe): the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; after it laṭ; in its place the ātmanepada 1st plural mahiṅ: hve + mahi; by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere"

original p. 685

Rik 3: grammar (continued)

(Pā. sū. 3-4-79) e for the ṭi; śap by "kartari śap": hve + a + mahe. With "hvaḥ samprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) carried on, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34) hveñ takes saṃprasāraṇa variously in the Veda: saṃprasāraṇa, u for the v: hu + e + a + mahe; pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108): hu + a + mahe. By "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ", with the sārvadhātuka śap as cause, the u takes guṇa, o. By "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78) av for the o: hava + mahe. By "ato dīrgho yañi" (Pā. sū. 7-3-101) the a before the m is lengthened: havāmahe. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

प्रयति (prayati): the root iṇ gatau, adādi; after it laṭ; in its place, by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) śatṛ; the śap that comes by "kartari śap" takes luk by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72): i + at. By "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) the suffix at is ṅit; so the guṇa that "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" would give is barred by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5). "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) would give yaṇ; overriding it, "aci śnudhātubhruvām…" (Pā. sū. "6-4-22" [as printed, for 6-4-77]) would give iyaṅ; overriding that too, "iṇo yaṇ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-81): before a vowel-initial suffix the root iṇ takes yaṇ; so yaṇ: yat. By "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18) pra is compounded with it: prayat; locative singular ṅi: prayati. The suffix śatṛ is udātta by the suffix accent; after compounding too, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the kṛt second-member accent comes and that accent remains. So prayat is final udātta; so by "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173), after a final-udātta word ending in a śatṛ suffix without the augment num, a nadī letter and a vowel-initial ending from śas on are also udātta; so the locative singular ṅi becomes udātta. But how does prayat, a, end in the śatṛ suffix? By "pratyayagrahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tadādes tadantasya grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā 23), the word with the śatṛ suffix whose first member is the base and whose last member is śatṛ is the śatṛ-ending word. Here śatṛ is enjoined after the root iṇ, so yat ends in śatṛ, but prayat does not. So how does the ending get udātta? Thus: śatṛ is a kṛt suffix; so by "kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā 28), where the kṛt is named with the property of being kṛt, which pervades it, there forms with a gati or kāraka before them are taken too: so this paribhāṣā tells.

original p. 686

Rik 3: grammar (end)

In śatur anumaḥ the kṛt is named with the property of being śatṛ, which pervades the kṛt. So here forms with gati and kāraka before them are taken too; that is, the paribhāṣā on naming a suffix does not apply in the case of gati and kāraka. So "ending in the śatṛ suffix" means only "having the śatṛ suffix as its last member". Prayat too has the śatṛ suffix as its last member, so it ends in the śatṛ suffix. So by śatur anumaḥ the ending after it becomes udātta. Yat ends in śatṛ, so, even without the use of the kṛt-naming paribhāṣā, there is no obstacle to the ending after it being udātta. But it should be understood that the sense set out here is the reasonable one.

अध्वरे (adhvare): its derivation is given at draviṇodāḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-7). In prayati + adhvare, in the Saṃhitā, by "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77), with the unaccented a after the udātta i as cause, yaṇ comes: prayatyadhvare. Now by "udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-4) the a after the y becomes svarita.

पीतये (pītaye): the root pā pāne; by "striyāṃ ktin" (Pā. sū. 3-3-94) the suffix ktin: pā + ti; by "ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali" (Pā. sū. 6-4-66) ī for the ā: pīti. The suffix being nit, initial udātta would come by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); but as a Vedic form it is final udātta. After it the dative singular ṅe: pīti + e. By "ṅiti hrasvaś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-6), before a ṅit suffix, the ī/ū-final words that are fit for iyaṅ/uvaṅ, other than strī, that always denote the feminine, and the short i/u-final words denoting the feminine, are optionally called nadī; since the nadī name is optional, on the view where it does not come, by "śeṣo ghy asakhi" (Pā. sū. 1-4-7) the ghi name comes. By "gher ṅiti" (Pā. sū. "1-3-111" [as printed, for 7-3-111]) guṇa, e for the i: pīte + e; by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78) ay: pītaye.

॥३॥

उप॑ नः सु॒तमा ग॑हि॒ हरि॑भिरिन्द्र के॒शिभिः॑ । [accent ?] सु॒ते हि त्वा॒ हवा॑महे ॥४॥ [accent ?]

original p. 687

Rik 4: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उप । नः । सुतम् । आ । गहि । हरिऽभिः । इन्द्र । केशिऽभिः ॥ सुते । हि । त्वा । हवामहे ॥४॥

upa | naḥ | sutam | ā | gahi | hari 'bhiḥ | indra | keśi 'bhiḥ || sute | hi | tvā | havāmahe ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र केशिभिः केसरयुक्तैर्हरिभिरश्वैस्त्वं नो ऽस्मदीयं सुतमभिषुतं सोमं प्रत्युप समीप आ गहि । आगच्छ । सुते ऽभिषुते सोमे निमित्तभूते सति यस्मात्कारणात्त्वा हवामहे त्वामाह्वयामः । तस्मादागच्छेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ गहि । गमेर्लोटः सेर्हिः । शप इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । इषुगमियमां छः । पा. ७-३-७७ । इति छत्वं न भवति । न लुमताङ्गस्येति प्रतिषेधात् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभात् । पा. ६-४-२२ । इत्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति हेर्लुग्न भवति । केशिभिः । क्लिशेरन् लो लोपश्च । उ. ५-३३ । इत्यन् । मत्वर्थीय इनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हवामहे । ह्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणं । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव । तिङ्ङतिङ इति न निघातो हि चेति प्रतिषेधात् ॥

he indra keśibhiḥ kesarayuktairharibhiraśvaistvaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ sutamabhiṣutaṃ somaṃ pratyupa samīpa ā gahi | āgaccha | sute 'bhiṣute some nimittabhūte sati yasmātkāraṇāttvā havāmahe tvāmāhvayāmaḥ | tasmādāgaccheti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || gahi | gamerloṭaḥ serhiḥ | śapa ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ | pā. 7-3-77 | iti chatvaṃ na bhavati | na lumatāṅgasyeti pratiṣedhāt | anudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhāt | pā. 6-4-22 | ityasiddhatvādato heriti herlugna bhavati | keśibhiḥ | kliśeran lo lopaśca | u. 5-33 | ityan | matvarthīya iniḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | havāmahe | hva ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇaṃ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva | tiṅṅatiṅa iti na nighāto hi ceti pratiṣedhāt ||

Translation: "O Indra, with your keśin, maned, hari, horses, upa ā gahi, come near to our sutam, the pressed soma. For since, the soma being pressed, sute, we call you, therefore come: that is the construction with what precedes." (Grammatical tail: gahi: hi for si, the śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, no ch (Pā. 7-3-77), barred by na lumatāṅgasya; the m dropped; that loss counting as not done (Pā. 6-4-22), hi is not dropped by ato heḥ; keśibhiḥ, an after kliś with loss of the l (Uṇ. 5-33), ini in the possessive sense, the suffix accent; havāmahe, saṃprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi, the root accent, not lowered because of hi.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सुते (sute) — when the soma has been made ready | त्वा (tvā) — you | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call; (so) | केशिभिः (keśibhiḥ) — with manes | हरिभिः (haribhiḥ) — together with the horses | नः (naḥ) — our | सुतम् (sutam) — the soma made ready (to drink) | उप आ गहि (upa ā gahi) — come near us.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, we have made the soma juice ready for you and call you. Come near us with your maned horses to drink that soma juice.

॥ English Translation ॥

Come Indra to our extracted soma libation by means of your long-maned horses. For we invoke you as soon as the soma is prepared.

original p. 688

Rik 4: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Keśibhiḥ: with long manes. The mane is the long hair grown on the horses' necks.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 688–689, noted briefly

गहि (gahi): the root gamḷ gatau; loṭ, parasmaipada 2nd singular sip; by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87) hi for the si standing for loṭ, and it is apit; so hi for si; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68): gam + a + hi. In "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73) śapaḥ is carried on from "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ"; śap takes luk variously, so śap takes luk. The pratyayalakṣaṇa that "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-62) would give is barred by "na lumatāṅgasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-63). So a śit suffix does not count as following. So "iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-77), which gives ch for the final of iṣu icchāyām, gamḷ gatau and yamu uparame before a suffix with ś as it, does not apply. In "anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-37), anunāsika is a sixth case, a qualifier of the others apart from vanati; since there is nothing else it could exclude, it does not qualify vanati. There is the maxim "sambhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syād viśeṣaṇam arthavat": a qualifier has a purpose when the connection is possible and it excludes others. Sambhava is fitness, vyabhicāra exclusion of others: in kṛṣṇaḥ haṃsaḥ the swan is only white, never black, so, lacking fitness, kṛṣṇaḥ cannot be given as a qualifier of haṃsaḥ. In kṛṣṇaḥ kākaḥ all crows are black; so though the fitness for kṛṣṇaḥ to be construed with the crow exists, there is no exclusion of others. So in kākaḥ the qualifier kṛṣṇaḥ is unnecessary; likewise here the qualifier anunāsika is unnecessary for vanati. Before a jhal-initial kit or ṅit suffix the nasal of the nasal-final anudāttopadeśa roots and of the tanoty-ādi roots, and the nasal of the root van, drop; so the nasal m drops. Gam is read in the kārikā of the anudāttopadeśa class, "gamir namir yamo ramiḥ", so it is anudāttopadeśa. With ga + hi, by "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105), after a stem ending in a the hi would take luk; but by "asiddhavad atrābhāt" (Pā. sū. 6-4-22), when an operation of the ābhīya section with the same basis is made, an operation of that section with the same basis counts as not done; so when the luk based on hi is made, the loss of m by anudāttopadeśa…, based on hi, counts as not done. So the stem ends in m, not in a; so hi does not take luk.

original p. 689

Rik 4: grammar (end)

केशिभिः (keśibhiḥ): "kliśer an lo lopaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "5-2-11" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 5-33): after kliśū vibādhane the suffix an, and the l of the root drops; so with the suffix an and the loss of l, kiś + a; by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" the laghūpadha-guṇa: keśa. By "ata iniṭhanau" (Pā. sū. 5-2-115) the suffix ini: keśa + in; by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the a drops: keśin. It is final udātta by the suffix accent. After it the instrumental plural bhis: keśin + bhis. By "svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne" (Pā. sū. 1-4-17) keśin is called pada; so by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7) the n drops; with ru and visarga, keśibhiḥ.

हवामहे (havāmahe): the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; after it laṭ, ātmanepada 1st plural mahiṅ; e for the ṭi by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. "3-4-28" [as printed, for 3-4-79]); śap by "kartari śap": hve + a + mahe; with "hvaḥ samprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) carried on, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34) saṃprasāraṇa; pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ"; av by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): hav + a + mahe; by "ato dīrgho yañi" (Pā. sū. 7-3-101) the a lengthened: havāmahe. Śap is pit, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau"; the tiṅ suffix mahe after the śap, an adupadeśa, is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttet" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186); so the root accent remains. By "hi ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-34), a tiṅanta joined with the word hi is not unaccented; and since in sute hi tvā havāmahe the word hi is used, "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented. From the mention of pūjita in the sūtra pūjanāt pūjitam it is made known that "in this section, though there is a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required"; so, though tvā intervenes, there is no obstacle to the bar of hi ca. This point was set out before.

॥४॥

सेमं नः॒ स्तोम॒मा ग॒ह्युपे॒दं सव॑नं सु॒तम् । गौ॒रो न तृ॑षितः पि॑ब ॥५॥ [accent ?]

semaṃ naḥ stómam ā́ gahy úpedáṃ sávanaṃ sutám | gauró ná tṛṣitáḥ piba ||5|| [accent ?]

original p. 690

Rik 5: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । इमम् । नः । स्तोमम् । आ । गहि । उप । इदम् । सवनम् । सुतम् ॥ गौरः । न । तृषितः । पिब ॥५॥

saḥ | imam | naḥ | stomam | ā | gahi | upa | idam | savanam | sutam || gauraḥ | na | tṛṣitaḥ | piba ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ उडन्तात् is as printed; the grammar page (p. 691) has ल्युडन्त, so ल्युडन्तात् is probably meant. "म." before ७-१-३९ is as printed. ॥३०॥ closes Varga 30.

हे इन्द्र स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं स्तोमं स्तुतिं प्रत्या गहि । आगच्छ । आगमने हेतुरुच्यते । उप देवयजनसमीपे सुतमभिषुतसोमयुक्तमिदानीमनुष्ठीयमानं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्म वर्तते । तस्माद्गौरो न गौरमृग इव तृषितः सन्निमं सोमं पिब ॥ सः इममित्यत्र संहितायां सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम् । पा. ६-१-१३४ । इति सुलोपः । गहि । गतम् । सवनम् । सूयतेऽस्मिन्सोम इत्यधिकरणे ल्युट् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । उडन्तात्सप्तम्याः [?] सुपां सुपो भवन्तीति वक्तव्यम् । म. ७-१-३९ । इति वचनाद्द्वितीया । अभिषुतसोमयुक्तमिदं सवनमिति कर्मण्येव वा द्वितीया । तदा सुतशब्दादर्शआदित्वादच् । पा. ५-२-१२७ । तृषितः । ञितृष पिपासायाम् । निष्ठेति क्तः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । पश्चादिटि आगमा अनुदात्ता इत्यनुदात्तत्वम् ॥३०॥

he indra sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyamimaṃ stomaṃ stutiṃ pratyā gahi | āgaccha | āgamane heturucyate | upa devayajanasamīpe sutamabhiṣutasomayuktamidānīmanuṣṭhīyamānaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādirūpaṃ karma vartate | tasmādgauro na gauramṛga iva tṛṣitaḥ sannimaṃ somaṃ piba || saḥ imamityatra saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cetpādapūraṇam | pā. 6-1-134 | iti sulopaḥ | gahi | gatam | savanam | sūyate 'sminsoma ityadhikaraṇe lyuṭ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | uḍantātsaptamyāḥ [?] supāṃ supo bhavantīti vaktavyam | ma. 7-1-39 | iti vacanāddvitīyā | abhiṣutasomayuktamidaṃ savanamiti karmaṇyeva vā dvitīyā | tadā sutaśabdādarśaāditvādac | pā. 5-2-127 | tṛṣitaḥ | ñitṛṣa pipāsāyām | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | paścādiṭi āgamā anudāttā ityanudāttatvam ||30||

Translation: "O Indra, such as you are, come to this our stoma, praise. Come: the reason for coming is stated. Near (upa) the place of sacrifice a rite (savana) in the form of the morning pressing and so on, joined with the pressed soma (sutam), is now being performed. Therefore, like a gaura, a gaura deer, being thirsty, drink this soma." (Grammatical tail: sa imam, the loss of su in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 6-1-134; gahi, explained before; savanam, lyuṭ in the sense of place, "in it the soma is pressed", the accent before the suffix by liti; the accusative for the locative by the statement supāṃ supo bhavanti (म. 7-1-39), or the accusative of object, suta then taking ac as one of the arśa-ādi (Pā. 5-2-127); tṛṣitaḥ, kta after ñitṛṣa pipāsāyām, udātta by the suffix accent, the augment iṭ unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सः (saḥ) — you | नः (naḥ) — our | इमम् (imam) — this | स्तोमम् (stomam) — praise (to hear it) | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come | उप (upa) — near (the sacrificial altar) | सुतम् (sutam) — joined with the prepared soma juice | इदम् (idam) — this (now to be performed) | सवनम् (savanam) — the rite in the form of the morning pressing (is going on) | तृषितः (tṛṣitaḥ) — thirsty | गौरः न (gauraḥ na) — like a light-coloured deer | पिब (piba) — drink (the soma juice).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The soma juice needed for the morning pressing is ready. Come, pleased with the praise we make as a part of that rite, and drink the soma juice as a thirsty animal (a deer) drinks water.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, accept this our praise and come to this our sacrifice of the expressed soma ; drink like a thirsty stag.

original p. 691

Rik 5: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Gauraḥ: a light-coloured deer. Here the word na indicates comparison; gauro na means "like a deer".

Tṛṣitaḥ: thirsty. The sense is: as a deer worn out by thirst drinks water eagerly, so you should drink our soma juice eagerly, as much as you wish.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 691–692, noted briefly

सः इमम् (saḥ imam): here, with sas + imam in the Saṃhitā, by "so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-134), in the case where the loss makes up the pāda, the su suffix of sas is dropped when a vowel follows; so, the su dropped, sa + imam; by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) in place of a and i, born in the throat and the palate, comes e, born in the throat and palate together and called guṇa: semam. From the Pāṇinīya-śikṣā statement The verses are as printed: तालव्यावोष्ठजा and कण्ठतालव्यावो औ show a printed v glide.

कण्ठ्यावहाविचुयशास्तालव्यावोष्ठजावुपू । स्युर्मूर्धन्या ऋटुरषा दन्त्या लृतुलसाः स्मृताः ॥१७॥ जिह्वामूले तु कुः प्रोक्तः दन्त्योष्ठ्यो वस्स्मृतो बुधैः । ए ऐ तु कण्ठतालव्यावो औ कण्ठोष्ठजौ स्मृतौ ॥१८॥

kaṇṭhyāvahāvicuyaśāstālavyāvoṣṭhajāvupū | syurmūrdhanyā ṛṭuraṣā dantyā lṛtulasāḥ smṛtāḥ ||17|| jihvāmūle tu kuḥ proktaḥ dantyoṣṭhyo vassmṛto budhaiḥ | e ai tu kaṇṭhatālavyāvo au kaṇṭhoṣṭhajau smṛtau ||18||

("The a, ku, h and visarga are of the throat; i, cu, y and ś of the palate; u and pu of the lips; ṛ, ṭu, r and ṣ are of the head; ḷ, tu, l and s are held to be of the teeth. Ku is said to be at the root of the tongue; v is held by the wise to be of the teeth and lips; e and ai are of the throat and palate, o and au of the throat and lips": my rendering, editorial and tentative.) it is established that a is of the throat, i of the palate and e of the throat and palate. In the case where by so 'ci lope (Pā. sū. 6-1-134) the loss of su does not come, in sas + imam there is ru by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66), y for it by "bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. sū. 6-3-18 [as read; ?]), then the y is dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-19). By "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1), when guṇa is to be made by ād guṇaḥ, the loss of y counts as not done; so there is no room for guṇa. Thus it would have to stay sa imam, and the pāda would not be made up.

गहि (gahi): explained in the previous mantra.

सवनम् (savanam): meant as "sūyate asmin somaḥ", in it the soma is pressed: the root ṣūñ prāṇiprasave; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; after sū, in the sense of place, lyuṭ by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-117); the substitute ana by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1): sū + ana; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-44 [as printed, for 7-3-84]); the substitute av by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): savana. The a before the suffix ana is udātta by "liti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-193). Savana is a lyuḍanta in the sense of place. After it comes the locative singular suffix ṅi.

Page 692 (upper) — Rik 5: grammar (end)

In its place, by "supāṃ supo bhavanti" (Pā. sū. Vā. 3-1-39-1 [as printed; the vārttika is on 7-1-39]), stated in the sūtra "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) (in place of sup endings the intended sup endings come), the accusative singular am comes. Savana + am: by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the pūrvarūpa: savanam. Savane sutam idaṃ piba: in this alternative the sense is "O Indra, drink the soma pressed in the rite in the form of the morning pressing and so on". Or, meant as "sutam asya asti", by "arśaādibhyo 'c" (Pā. sū. 5-2-127) the suffix ac: suta + a; by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the a is dropped. Sutam means "joined with the pressed soma juice". In this alternative sutam idaṃ savanaṃ piba means "enjoy this rite of the morning pressing and so on, joined with the pressed soma juice". Since savana denotes the object marked by the action conveyed by the root pā, the justification can be given that the accusative comes by "karmaṇi dvitīyā" (Pā. sū. 2-9-2 [as read; for 2-3-2] [?]). In the Vedabhāṣya, explaining the sense, savanam is taken as a nominative and the verb is supplied; in that alternative it must be said that am is substituted for the nominative singular suffix by supāṃ suluk.

तृषितः (tṛṣitaḥ): the root ñitṛṣa pipāsāyām; the suffix kta in the object sense by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. sū. 2-2-36 [as printed, for 3-2-102]); the augment iṭ by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-35): tṛṣita. After the kta suffix is made initial udātta by ādyudāttaś ca, the augment iṭ that comes is unaccented by āgamā anudāttāḥ.

॥५॥

Page 692 (lower) — Sūkta 16, Rik 6

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The earlier reading अधिकेन is corrected from the print: यज्ञेऽध्याधिक्येन, i.e. adhi glossed by ādhikyena.

इन्दुशब्द उन्दी क्लेदन इति धातोरुत्पन्नः । इन्दवः क्लेदनयुक्ता इमे वेद्यामवस्थिताः सोमासस्तत्तत्पात्रगताः सोमा बर्हिषि यज्ञेऽध्याधिक्येन सुतासः । अभिषुताः । हे इन्द्र सहसे बलार्थं तान् सोमान् पिब ॥ सोमासः । आज्जसेरसुगिति जसोऽसुगागमः । इन्दवः । उक्तम् । सुतासः । पूर्ववदसुक् । संहितायां प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपर इति प्रकृतिभावात्स्वरपूर्वत्वं न भवति । बर्हिषि । बृंहेर्नलोपश्च । उ. २-१०० । इतीस् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । ताँ इन्द्रेत्यत्र दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वम् । यत्वयलोपौ । अनुनासिकः । सहसे । षह मर्षणे । असुनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

induśabda undī kledana iti dhātorutpannaḥ | indavaḥ kledanayuktā ime vedyāmavasthitāḥ somāsastattatpātragatāḥ somā barhiṣi yajñe 'dhyādhikyena sutāsaḥ | abhiṣutāḥ | he indra sahase balārthaṃ tān somān piba || somāsaḥ | ājjaserasugiti jaso 'sugāgamaḥ | indavaḥ | uktam | sutāsaḥ | pūrvavadasuk | saṃhitāyāṃ prakṛtyāntaḥpādamavyapara iti prakṛtibhāvātsvarapūrvatvaṃ na bhavati | barhiṣi | bṛṃhernalopaśca | u. 2-100 | itīs | pratyayasvaraḥ | tām̐ indretyatra dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti rutvam | yatvayalopau | anunāsikaḥ | sahase | ṣaha marṣaṇe | asunanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "The word indu is formed from the root undī kledane, to wet. Indavaḥ, wet: these somāsaḥ, soma juices standing on the altar and held in their several vessels, are sutāsaḥ, pressed, at the sacrifice, barhiṣi, in abundance, adhi. O Indra, drink those soma juices for strength, sahase." (Grammatical tail: somāsaḥ, asuk for jas by āj jaser asuk; indavaḥ, explained; sutāsaḥ, asuk as before, and in the Saṃhitā no loss of the following vowel, by the prakṛtibhāva of prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare; barhiṣi, is by bṛṃher nalopaś ca (Uṇ. 2-100), the suffix accent; tām̐ indra, ru by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde, y and its loss, the nasal; sahase, ṣaha marṣaṇe, an asun form, initial udātta as nit.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सुतासः (sutāsaḥ) — prepared | इन्दवः (indavaḥ) — liquid (or, dripping) | इमे (ime) — these (on the altar) | सोमासः (somāsaḥ) — soma juices (in the several vessels) | बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — in the sacrifice | अधि (adhi) — in abundant measure (in a pure, special way) are placed | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सहसे (sahase) — for the increase of strength | तान् (tān) — those soma juices | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The soma juice in the various vessels on this altar was not squeezed out in an ordinary way; it has been prepared with mantras as a part of the sacrifice. O Indra, drink it for the increase of your strength.

॥ English Translation ॥

These dripping Soma juices are effused upon the sacred grass; drink them Indra, to recruit your strength.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Indavaḥ: when the soma plant is crushed with stones and the juice squeezed out, the juice oozes in drops. Soma juice dripping in this way is by usage called indavaḥ. The word is formed from the root undī kledane.

original p. 694

Rik 6: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 694–695, noted briefly

सोमासः (somāsaḥ): ṣuñ abhiṣave; s for ṣ by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64); after su, man by "arti-stu-su-…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-13[?]" [?]); guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ: soma, initial udātta by the nit accent. After it jas: soma + as; by "āj jaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) the augment asuk for jas, which, being kit, comes as its first part by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46): soma + asas; lengthening of the like vowel; somāsas, ru and visarga.

इन्दवः (indavaḥ): explained at the mantra "pra vo bhriyanta indavaḥ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-14-4).

सुतासः (sutāsaḥ): the root ṣuñ; s for ṣ; kta by niṣṭhā; the augment iṭ, due by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ, is barred by "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt". After suta, jas; asuk as before; lengthening; ru and visarga: sutāsaḥ. In the Saṃhitā, with sutāsas adhi, ru for s by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. "8-2-6[?]" [?]): sutāsar + adhi; u for ru by ato ror aplutād aplute; guṇa by ād guṇaḥ: sutāso + adhi. By "eṅaḥ padāntād ati" (Pā. sū. 6-1-109) the pūrvarūpa would come; but by "prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare" (Pā. sū. 6-1-115) e and o in the middle of a pāda keep their form before a vowel, unless that vowel is followed by v or y; so here they keep it, and there is no pūrvarūpa.

बर्हिषि (barhiṣi): the root bṛhi vṛddhau; being idit, it takes the augment num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-58): bṛnh. By "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "2-[?]" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-100), after bṛhi the suffix isi comes and the n is dropped: bṛh + is; the laghūpadha-guṇa by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca, followed by r by uraṇ raparaḥ: barhis, final udātta by the suffix accent. Locative singular ṅi; by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. "8-3-5[?]" [?]) ṣ for the s belonging to the suffix: barhiṣi.

ताँ इन्द्र (tām̐ indra): with tān + indra in the Saṃhitā, ru for the n by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. sū. 8-3-9); by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-3-3)

Page 695 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

the nasal for the ā; by "bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. sū. 8-3-17) y for ru: tām̐y + indra; the y dropped by lopaḥ śākalyasya: tām̐ indra.

सहसे (sahase): ṣaha marṣaṇe; s for ṣ by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64); the suffix asun by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-[?]" [?]): sahas, initial udātta by the nit accent. Dative singular ṅe: sahase.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒यं ते॒ स्तोमो॑ अग्रि॒यो हृ॑दि॒स्पृग॑स्तु॒ शंत॑मः । अथा॒ सोमं॑ सु॒तं पि॑ब ॥७॥

ayáṃ te stómo agriyó hṛdispṛ́g astu śáṃtamaḥ | athā sómaṃ sutáṃ piba ||7||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अयम् । ते । स्तोमः । अग्रियः । हृदिऽस्पृक् । अस्तु । शम्ऽतमः ॥ अथ । सोमम् । सुतम् । पिब ॥७॥

ayam | te | stomaḥ | agriyaḥ | hṛdi 'spṛk | astu | śam 'tamaḥ || atha | somam | sutam | piba ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र अयमस्माभिः क्रियमाणः स्तोमः स्तोत्रविशेषोऽग्रियः श्रेष्ठः सन् ते तव हृदिस्पृक् मनस्यङ्गीकृतः शंतमः सुखतमोऽस्तु । अथ स्तुतेरनन्तरं सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिब ॥ अग्रियः । अग्रादित्यनुवृत्तौ घच्छौ च । पा. ४-४-११७ । इति घच् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । हृदि स्पृशतीति हृदिस्पृक् । स्पृशोऽनुदके क्विन् । पा. ३-२-५८ । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् । पा. ६-३-१४ । इत्यलुक् । क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः । पा. ८-२-६२ । इति शकारस्य कुत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । शंतमः । सुखकरद्रव्यवचनोऽत्र शंशब्दः ततस्तमप् । अत्र सुखप्रकर्षस्य गुणद्वारा गुणिनिष्ठद्रव्ये संक्रान्तत्वादद्रव्यप्रकर्ष इति निषेधात् किमेत्तिङव्ययेत्यादिना । पा. ५-४-११ । आम् न भवति द्रव्यस्य स्वतः प्रकर्षाभावात् । ईदृगर्थ एव हि स निषेधः । अथा सोमम् । संहितायां निपातस्येति दीर्घः ॥

he indra ayamasmābhiḥ kriyamāṇaḥ stomaḥ stotraviśeṣo 'griyaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ san te tava hṛdispṛk manasyaṅgīkṛtaḥ śaṃtamaḥ sukhatamo 'stu | atha stuteranantaraṃ sutamabhiṣutaṃ somaṃ piba || agriyaḥ | agrādityanuvṛttau ghacchau ca | pā. 4-4-117 | iti ghac | cittvādantodāttaḥ | hṛdi spṛśatīti hṛdispṛk | spṛśo 'nudake kvin | pā. 3-2-58 | tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam | pā. 6-3-14 | ityaluk | kvinpratyayasya kuḥ | pā. 8-2-62 | iti śakārasya kutvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | śaṃtamaḥ | sukhakaradravyavacano 'tra śaṃśabdaḥ tatastamap | atra sukhaprakarṣasya guṇadvārā guṇiniṣṭhadravye saṃkrāntatvādadravyaprakarṣa iti niṣedhāt kimettiṅavyayetyādinā | pā. 5-4-11 | ām na bhavati dravyasya svataḥ prakarṣābhāvāt | īdṛgartha eva hi sa niṣedhaḥ | athā somam | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasyeti dīrghaḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra, may this stoma, this particular hymn being made by us, being agriya, the best, be hṛdispṛk to you, taken to heart, and śaṃtama, most pleasing. Atha, after the praise, drink the sutam, pressed, soma." (Grammatical tail: agriyaḥ, ghac by ghacchau ca (Pā. 4-4-117), with agrāt carried on, final udātta as cit; hṛdispṛk, "it touches the heart", kvin by Pā. 3-2-58, the case kept by Pā. 6-3-14, the guttural for ś by Pā. 8-2-62, the accent of the kṛt final member; śaṃtamaḥ, śam here naming a thing that gives happiness, then tamap; since the excess of happiness passes through the quality to the thing that has it, the bar "adravyaprakarṣe" in kim-et-tiṅ-avyaya… (Pā. 5-4-11) applies and ām does not come, a thing having no excess of its own; athā somam, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by nipātasya.)

original p. 696

Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे इन्द्र (he indra) — O Indra) | अग्रियः (agriyaḥ) — excellent | अयम् (ayam) — this (being made by us) | स्तोमः (stomaḥ) — hymn of praise | ते (te) — your | हृदिस्पृक् (hṛdispṛk) — touching the heart (and agreeable to the mind) | शंतमः (śaṃtamaḥ) — giving happiness | अस्तु (astu) — may it be | अथ (atha) — after the praise is over | सुतम् (sutam) — made ready | सोमम् (somam) — the soma juice | पिब (piba) — drink.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, may this hymn that we are making about you touch your heart, gladden you and give you joy. Then drink this soma juice that we have prepared.

॥ English Translation ॥

May this excellent hymn touching you [sic] heart be most agreeable to you. Drink, then Indra, the extracted Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Agriyaḥ: best (agre bhavaḥ, being at the front); excellent, highest.

Hṛdispṛk: hṛdi spṛśatīti hṛdispṛk, it touches the heart: touching the heart, melting the heart, striking the mind, "touching your heart, etc." The intent is: may the hymn we make strike your mind.

Śaṃtamaḥ: causing happiness; the sense is: may the hymn we make give you joy.

Atha: the last syllable of this word is long in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha to suit the metre.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 696–698, noted briefly

अग्रियः (agriyaḥ): in "ghacchau ca" (Pā. sū. 4-4-117) the word agrāt is carried on from the preceding sūtra "agrād yat" (Pā. sū. 4-4-116). After the stem agra ending in the locative, in the sense "bhava",

original p. 697

Rik 7: grammar

the suffixes gha, cha and yat come; so here, agre bhavaḥ being meant, ghac comes. The sup inside the taddhita-final stem takes luk. By "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām" (Pā. sū. "1-3-6" [as printed, for 7-1-2]), for ph, ḍh, kh, ch and gh at the start of a suffix come āyan, ey, īn, īy and iy; so iy for gh: agra + iya; the a dropped by yasyeti ca: agriya. The suffix ghac is cit; so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) agriya is final udātta. Nominative singular su; ru and visarga: agriyaḥ.

हृदिस्पृक् (hṛdispṛk): hṛdi spṛśati iti hṛdispṛk. By "spṛśo 'nudake kvin" (Pā. sū. 3-2-58), when a subanta other than the word udaka is the upapada, the suffix kvin comes after the root spṛś; all its letters drop. By "tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-3-14), when a kṛdanta final member follows, the locative in a tatpuruṣa compound is not dropped; so the luk due by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" does not come. After hṛdispṛś the suffix su, dropped by "halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68). The guttural enjoined by "kvinpratyayasya kuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-62) (in the pada-final position a word after which kvin came takes a guttural as its final substitute) counts as not done when the ṣ for a final ś is made by "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-36). So first ṣ comes by this sūtra: spṛṣ; then jaś, ḍ for ṣ, by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. sū. 8-2-39). Now by kvinpratyayasya kuḥ the guttural: for ḍ, the third of the ṭ-class, g, the third of the k-class; ghṛtaspṛg; by "vā śari" (Pā. sū. 8-3-36 [as printed]) car optionally: ghṛtaspṛk [as printed: the word worked here is ghṛtaspṛk, not hṛdispṛk]. Spṛk is final udātta by the root accent. After compounding too, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), the accent of the kṛt final member comes; the root accent stays.

शंतमः (śaṃtamaḥ): the word śam conveys "a thing that gives happiness". Atiśayitaḥ śam being meant, tamap by "atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau" (Pā. sū. 5-3-55): śam + tama. Here the excess of happiness is of the form happiness; through the quality it comes to rest in the excess of the thing marked by the quality happiness. So, because of the bar "adravyaprakarṣe" in "kim-et-tiṅ-avyaya-ghād ām v adravyaprakarṣe" (Pā. sū. 5-4-11) (after a word ending in a suffix called gha that follows kim, an e-final word, a tiṅanta or an avyaya, āmu comes, but not when an excess of a thing is shown), āmu does not come here. A thing has no excess of its own; so the excess of the thing must be explained by putting first the excess of quality and so on.

Page 698 (upper) — Rik 7: grammar (end)

This point Kaiyaṭa states in the tamap sūtra:

अद्रव्यप्रकर्षे इति निषेध उपचरितगुणक्रियागतप्रकर्षद्रव्यविषयो द्रष्टव्यः

adravyaprakarṣe iti niṣedha upacaritaguṇakriyāgataprakarṣadravyaviṣayo draṣṭavyaḥ

("The bar 'adravyaprakarṣe' is to be seen as concerning a thing whose excess lies in a quality or action figuratively ascribed to it": my rendering, editorial and tentative.) In the present case, since an excess of the thing that has happiness is shown through the excess of the quality happiness, the bar adravyaprakarṣe applies, and the suffix ām does not come. By "taraptamapau ghaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-22) the suffixes tarap and tamap are called gha: this is how the name gha is stated.

अथा सोमम् (athā somam): lengthened in the Saṃhitā by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-136).

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्व॒मित्सव॑नं सु॒तमिन्द्रो॒ मदा॑य गच्छति । वृ॒त्र॒हा सोम॑पीतये ॥८॥

viśvam ít sávanaṃ sutám indro mádāya gacchati | vṛtrahā́ sómapītaye ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वम् । इत् । सवनम् । सुतम् । इन्द्रः । मदाय । गच्छति ॥ वृत्रऽहा । सोमऽपीतये ॥८॥

viśvam | it | savanam | sutam | indraḥ | madāya | gacchati || vṛtra 'hā | soma 'pītaye ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वृत्रहा शत्रुघातक इन्द्रः सोमपीतये सोमपानाय मदाय तत्पानजन्यहर्षाय च विश्वमित्सर्वमपि सुतमभिषुतसोमयुक्तं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्म गच्छति ॥ विश्वम् । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सवनं सुतम् । पूर्ववत् । मदाय । मदोऽनुपसर्गे । पा. ३-३-६७ । इत्यप्प्रत्ययः । पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । गच्छति । इषुगमियमां छः । वृत्रहा । वृत्रं हतवान् । ब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्रेषु क्विप् । पा. ३-२-८७ । इन्हन्नित्यादिना निवृत्तं दीर्घत्वं सौ च । पा. ६-४-१२, १३ । इति प्रतिप्रसवाद्भवति । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सोमपीतये । व्यधिकरणबहुव्रीहिरित्युक्तम् । तत्पुरुषे वा दासीभारादित्वात् । पा. ६-२-४२ । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

vṛtrahā śatrughātaka indraḥ somapītaye somapānāya madāya tatpānajanyaharṣāya ca viśvamitsarvamapi sutamabhiṣutasomayuktaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādirūpaṃ karma gacchati || viśvam | aśipruṣītyādinā kvan | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | savanaṃ sutam | pūrvavat | madāya | mado 'nupasarge | pā. 3-3-67 | ityappratyayaḥ | pittvāddhātusvaraḥ | gacchati | iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ | vṛtrahā | vṛtraṃ hatavān | brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip | pā. 3-2-87 | inhannityādinā nivṛttaṃ dīrghatvaṃ sau ca | pā. 6-4-12, 13 | iti pratiprasavādbhavati | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | somapītaye | vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhirityuktam | tatpuruṣe vā dāsībhārāditvāt | pā. 6-2-42 | pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "Indra, vṛtrahā, the slayer of enemies, goes for somapīti, the drinking of soma, and for mada, the joy born of drinking it, to viśvam it, every, savana, rite in the form of the morning pressing and so on, sutam, joined with pressed soma." (Grammatical tail: viśvam, kvan by aśipruṣi…, initial udātta as nit; savanaṃ sutam, as before; madāya, the suffix ap by mado 'nupasarge (Pā. 3-3-67), the root accent since ap is pit; gacchati, ch by iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ; vṛtrahā, "he killed Vṛtra", kvip by Pā. 3-2-87; the lengthening, cancelled by in-han-…, comes back by the counter-rule sau ca (Pā. 6-4-12, 13); the accent of the kṛt final member; somapītaye, a vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi, as said, or a tatpuruṣa with the accent of the first member, as one of the dāsībhāra-ādi (Pā. 6-2-42).)

Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā) — who destroys enemies, or who destroyed the demon Vṛtra | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | मदाय (madāya) — and for the joy (that comes from drinking soma) | विश्वम् (viśvam) — all | सुतम् (sutam) — where the soma juice is made ready | सवनम् (savanam) — to the rites (in the form of the morning pressing and so on) | गच्छति इत् (gacchati it) — surely goes.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra, who destroys the demons or Vṛtra, goes to every rite of the morning pressing and so on where the soma juice is pressed out, drinks the soma, and is pleased by it.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, the killer of Vritra (or of enemies) goes to every ceremoney [sic] where Soma is prepared that he may drink the Soma and be intoxicated.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Vṛtrahā: though the word vṛtra denotes many things, cloud, strength, water, the demon Vṛtra and so on, here the commentator takes it as "enemy". It may also be taken as the demon Vṛtra if wished. Accordingly vṛtrahā means destroyer of enemies, or slayer of the demon Vṛtra.

Madāya: for the mada (intoxication) or joy that comes from drinking soma, "Intoxication".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 699–703, noted briefly

विश्वम् (viśvam): the root viśa praveśane; after it the suffix kvan by "aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. sū. 1-149); by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) the nit accent: viśva is initial udātta. Savanaṃ sutam are explained at "semaṃ naḥ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-16-5).

मदाय (madāya): by "mado 'nupasarge" (Pā. sū. 3-3-67), when a subanta other than a preverb is the upapada, the suffix ap comes after the root mad; so after the root mad

original p. 700

Rik 8: grammar

the suffix ap. It is pit, that is, has p as it; so it is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4), and the root accent stays.

गच्छति (gacchati): gamḷ gatau. By "iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-77), when laṭ, tip and śap have come after the root gam, the substitute ch.

वृत्रहा (vṛtrahā): the analysis is vṛtraṃ hatavān; the root hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ. By "brahma-bhrūṇa-vṛtreṣu kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-87), when the words brahma, bhrūṇa and vṛtra, denoting the object, are the upapada, the suffix kvip comes after the root han in the past sense. Here, though kvip would come anyway by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76), this sūtra is needed as a restriction, by the maxim

सिद्धे सत्यारभ्यमाणो विधिर्नियमाय भवति

siddhe satyārabhyamāṇo vidhirniyamāya bhavati

("A rule stated when the result is already obtained serves as a restriction.") Here the Kāśikā gives the restriction in four ways. Since they are heard in the sūtra, the words brahma and so on are to be used first, then, as the base, the root han, then, by elimination, bhūte, and kvip, being what is enjoined, comes last of all; so it reads

ब्रह्मादिषु उपपदेषु हन्तेः भूते क्विप्

brahmādiṣu upapadeṣu hanteḥ bhūte kvip

("When brahma and the rest are the upapada, kvip after han in the past.") By the maxim

यत एवकारस्ततोऽन्यत्र नियमः

yata evakārastato 'nyatra niyamaḥ

("The restriction applies to what is other than where the eva stands"), the restriction falls on what stands next to the word it is attached to. So if the restriction is stated as

ब्रह्मादिष्वेव हन्तेः भूते क्विप्

brahmādiṣveva hanteḥ bhūte kvip

("Only when brahma and the rest are upapada, kvip after han in the past"), what stands next to it is the root han; so it is a prakṛti-niyama, a restriction on the base, whose result is to exclude other upapadas from that root.

स्वसजातीयेतरव्यावर्तकत्वं नियमत्वम्

svasajātīyetaravyāvartakatvaṃ niyamatvam

("Being a restriction is excluding what is other than its own kind.") By this restriction it is settled that if there is connection with an upapada other than brahma and the rest, kvip does not come after the root han in the past sense. Example: for puruṣaṃ hatavān, the form puruṣahā is not used. Though not used in the past sense, in the present and future senses, puruṣaṃ hanti, puruṣaṃ haniṣyati, kvip does come, and in those senses puruṣahā is correct. This restriction is called prakṛti-niyama; the name comes because its result is to exclude other upapadas from the base. Next, when the restriction is stated as

ब्रह्मादिषु उपपदेषु हन्तेरेव भूते क्विप्

brahmādiṣu upapadeṣu hantereva bhūte kvip

("When brahma and the rest are upapada, kvip in the past only after han"), the upapada and bhūte, the word for the time, both stand equally near; yet since the upapada is named first, it is called an upapada-niyama. By it, when this upapada is connected, kvip does not come in the past sense after other roots. Example: for vṛtraṃ jitavān, with vṛtra as upapada, kvip does not come after the root ji in the past sense, so vṛtrajit is not a correct usage in that sense. When the present and future times are meant, vṛtraṃ jayati, vṛtraṃ jeṣyati, with brahma and the rest as upapada,

original p. 701

Rik 8: grammar

since the exclusion that kvip does not come in the past sense after a root other than han is settled, the usage vṛtrajit is correct. Thus there are two restrictions, prakṛti-niyama and upapada-niyama. Next, if the restriction takes the form

ब्रह्मादिषु उपपदेषु हन्तेः भूते क्विबेव

brahmādiṣu upapadeṣu hanteḥ bhūte kvibeva

("When brahma and the rest are upapada, after han in the past only kvip"), here hanteḥ and kvip both stand equally near; though they are equal, the suffix is the principal thing, so this is a pratyaya-niyama. By it it is settled that, with brahma and the rest as upapada, kvip does not come after the root han at a time other than the past. Example: in the senses brāhmaṇaṃ hanti, brāhmaṇaṃ haniṣyati, present and future time being understood, kvip does not come; so in these senses brahmahā is not formed. With these upapadas absent, even if kvip does not come after han in the past sense, when there is connection with another upapada it does come after han in the past sense: for puruṣaṃ hanti or haniṣyati, puruṣahā is formed. When the restriction is

ब्रह्मादिषु उपपदेषु हन्तेः भूत एव क्विप्

brahmādiṣu upapadeṣu hanteḥ bhūta eva kvip

("When brahma and the rest are upapada, kvip after han only in the past"), since bhūte stands next to it, it is a kāla-niyama, a restriction of time, by the maxim yata evakāraḥ. By it it is settled that, with brahma and the rest as upapada, no suffix other than kvip comes after the root han in the past sense. So for brāhmaṇaṃ hatavān the suffix ṇini in the past sense by "karmaṇi hanaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-86) does not come, and the usage brahmaghātī is not correct. But since the restriction contains "brahmādiṣu", when other words are the upapada, kvip does come after the root han in the past sense [as printed; the example is a ṇini form]: example, pitṛvyaṃ hatavān, pitṛvyaghātī. The Kāśikā's view is that the sūtra "brahma-bhrūṇa-vṛtreṣu kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-87) is needed to obtain these four restrictions, the prakṛti-niyama, upapada-niyama, pratyaya-niyama and kāla-niyama. In the Mahābhāṣya it reads:

उभयतो नियमोऽयम् । ब्रह्मादिष्वेव । क्विबेव ।

ubhayato niyamo 'yam | brahmādiṣveva | kvibeva |

("This is a restriction both ways: only with brahma and the rest; only kvip.") So the two restrictions accepted by the Bhāṣya are the prakṛti-niyama and the kāla-niyama. Readers will not fail to ask what the Bhāṣya's intention may be in relying on two restrictions in this way. In the sūtra "brahma-bhrūṇa-vṛtreṣu kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-87) the upapada and the suffix are both heard; the root han and the time-word bhūte are not heard. They are obtained from the context; and by

श्रुतिलिङ्गवाक्यप्रकरणस्थानसमाख्यानां पारदौर्बल्यमर्थविप्रकर्षात्

śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ pāradaurbalyamarthaviprakarṣāt

("Of direct statement, indication, syntactic connection, context, position and name, each later one is weaker, because its meaning is more remote"), context is much weaker than direct statement. So the Mahābhāṣyakāra's view is that it is proper to restrict the base and the time, supplied by a weaker means of knowledge, and not proper to restrict the upapada and the suffix, which are heard. Kaiyaṭa makes it clear that, since it conflicts with the Bhāṣya, which follows this reasoning, the view of the Vṛttikāra is to be disregarded. Haradatta says here:

धातूपपदविषयं नियमद्वयं भाष्ये प्रदर्शितम्

dhātūpapadaviṣayaṃ niyamadvayaṃ bhāṣye pradarśitam

("The two restrictions, concerning the root and the upapada, are shown in the Bhāṣya.") Instead of saying here

धातुकालविषयम्

dhātukālaviṣayam

("concerning the root and the time"), [the text continues on p. 702:]

original p. 702

Rik 8: grammar

Jñānendra Sarasvatī (the ascetic) has shown that the word upapada has slipped in through an oversight. Thus the sūtra brahma-bhrūṇa… is needed to obtain the restrictions. In vṛtraṃ hatavān, when by it the form ends in kvip, it is called prātipadika by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-2-46); by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71) the am inside the stem takes luk; the whole of kvip drops. After vṛtrahan the nominative singular su: vṛtrahan + su. By "sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8), before a sarvanāmasthāna suffix other than the vocative, the penultimate of an n-final stem is lengthened; so lengthening is due. But the sense of "in-han-pūṣāryamṇāṃ śau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-12) is that the penultimate of a stem ending in in, han, pūṣan or aryaman is lengthened before the suffix śi. By sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau (Pā. sū. 6-4-8) the lengthening of their penultimate is already established; so by siddhe satyārabhyamāṇo vidhir niyamāya bhavati this sūtra is a restriction: for stems ending in in, han, pūṣan and aryaman, the lengthening of the penultimate comes only before śi. By it it is settled that without śi following, the penultimate of a stem ending in in and the rest is not lengthened. So in vṛtrahan + su, śi not following, there would be no lengthening. Yet by "sau ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-13), when the suffix su follows, the penultimate of a stem ending in in, han, pūṣan or aryaman is lengthened; so the lengthening comes. Pratiprasava means a bar to a bar. Here the lengthening due by sarvanāmasthāne ca was in effect barred by in-han-pūṣā…; and sau ca (Pā. sū. 6-4-13) in effect bars that bar. So the Bhāṣya says

दीर्घत्वं सौ चेति प्रतिप्रसवाद्भवति

dīrghatvaṃ sau ceti pratiprasavādbhavati

("The lengthening comes by the counter-rule sau ca.") With vṛtrahān + su, the su drops by "halṅyābbhyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68); the n drops by "na lopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7): vṛtrahā. Hā is udātta by the root accent; after compounding too the same accent comes by the accent of the kṛt final member, that is, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. "7-2-139" [as read; for 6-2-139] [?]).

सोमपीतये (somapītaye): a bahuvrīhi compound is made of words ending in the nominative; when words in other cases enter a bahuvrīhi, it is called a vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi. At "aibhir agne duvo giraḥ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-14-1) somapītaye was shown to be a vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi. The word soma is initial udātta by the nit accent; in the bahuvrīhi the same accent comes by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1). Even if a tatpuruṣa is made, somasya pītiḥ somapītiḥ, tasyai somapītaye, then, by samāsasya

Page 703 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

overriding the final udātta that would come, since dāsībhāra-ādi is an ākṛtigaṇa, somapīti, which belongs to that group, takes the accent of its first member by

कुरुगार्हपततरिक्तगुर्वसूतजरत्यश्लीलदृढरूपापारेवडवातैतिलकद्रूःपण्यकम्बलो दासीभाराणां च

kurugārhapatatariktagurvasūtajaratyaślīladṛḍharūpāpārevaḍavātaitilakadrūḥpaṇyakambalo dāsībhārāṇāṃ ca

(Pā. sū. 6-2-42). Since recourse to a vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi is a last resort, the tatpuruṣa has been described.

॥८॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सेमं नः॒ काम॒मा पृ॑ण॒ गोभि॒रश्वैः॑ शतक्रतो । स्तवा॑म त्वा स्वा॒ध्यः॑ ॥९॥

semaṃ naḥ kā́mam ā́ pṛṇa góbhir áśvaiḥ śatakrato | stávāma tvā svādhyaḥ ||9||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । इमम् । नः । कामम् । आ । पृण । गोभिः । अश्वैः । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो ॥ स्तवाम । त्वा । सुऽआध्यः ॥९॥

saḥ | imam | naḥ | kāmam | ā | pṛṇa | gobhiḥ | aśvaiḥ | śatakrato iti śata 'krato || stavāma | tvā | su 'ādhyaḥ ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥३१॥ closes Varga 31.

हे शतक्रतो स त्वं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं कामं काम्यमानं फलं गोभिरश्वैश्च सहा पृण । सर्वतः पूरय । वयमपि स्वाध्यः सुष्ठु सर्वतो ध्यानयुक्ताः सन्तस्त्वां स्तवाम ॥ सेमम् । संहितायां सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणमिति सुलोपः । कामम् । कमेर्घञ् । कर्षात्वतो घञोऽन्त उदात्तः । पा. ६-१-१५९ । इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वृषादिषु पाठादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । पृण । पृण प्रीणने । लोटः सेर्हिः । तुदादिभ्यः शः । तस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । गोभिः । सावेकाच इति प्राप्तं विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषिध्यते । अश्वैः । क्वनन्त इत्युक्तम् । असामर्थ्यान्न पराङ्गवद्भावः । स्तवाम । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । धात्वादेः षः सः । लोडुत्तमबहुवचनस्य लोटो लङ्वदिति लङ्वद्भावान्नित्यं ङितः ।

he śatakrato sa tvaṃ no 'smadīyamimaṃ kāmaṃ kāmyamānaṃ phalaṃ gobhiraśvaiśca sahā pṛṇa | sarvataḥ pūraya | vayamapi svādhyaḥ suṣṭhu sarvato dhyānayuktāḥ santastvāṃ stavāma || semam | saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cetpādapūraṇamiti sulopaḥ | kāmam | kamerghañ | karṣātvato ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ | pā. 6-1-159 | ityantodāttatve prāpte vṛṣādiṣu pāṭhādādyudāttatvam | pṛṇa | pṛṇa prīṇane | loṭaḥ serhiḥ | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | tasya ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | ato heriti herluk | gobhiḥ | sāvekāca iti prāptaṃ vibhakterudāttatvaṃ na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣidhyate | aśvaiḥ | kvananta ityuktam | asāmarthyānna parāṅgavadbhāvaḥ | stavāma | ṣṭuñ stutau | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | loḍuttamabahuvacanasya loṭo laṅvaditi laṅvadbhāvānnityaṃ ṅitaḥ |
