Rik 9: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

पा. ३-४-९९ । इति सकारस्य लोपः । आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च । पा. ३-४-९२ । इत्याडागमः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव । स्वाध्यः । ध्यै चिन्तायाम् । स्वाङोरुपसर्गयोः प्राक्प्रयोगः । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते । पा. ३-२-१७८ । इति क्विप् । दृशिग्रहणस्य विध्यन्तरोपसंग्रहणार्थत्वादत्र संप्रसारणे सति परपूर्वत्वम् । हल इति दीर्घः । जस्येरनेकाचः । पा. ६-४-८२ । इति यणादेशः । गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदिति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति जस उदात्तत्वं न भवति तत्रासर्वनामस्थानमित्यनुवृत्तेः । अत उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्येति स्वरितत्वमेव भवति ॥३१॥

pā. 3-4-99 | iti sakārasya lopaḥ | āḍuttamasya picca | pā. 3-4-92 | ityāḍāgamaḥ | pratyayasya pittvādanudāttatvam | dhātusvara eva | svādhyaḥ | dhyai cintāyām | svāṅorupasargayoḥ prākprayogaḥ | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate | pā. 3-2-178 | iti kvip | dṛśigrahaṇasya vidhyantaropasaṃgrahaṇārthatvādatra saṃprasāraṇe sati parapūrvatvam | hala iti dīrghaḥ | jasyeranekācaḥ | pā. 6-4-82 | iti yaṇādeśaḥ | gatikārakopapadātkṛditi kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi jasa udāttatvaṃ na bhavati tatrāsarvanāmasthānamityanuvṛtteḥ | ata udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasyeti svaritatvameva bhavati ||31||

Translation: "O Śatakratu, such as you are, ā pṛṇa, fill up on all sides, this our kāma, the fruit we desire, with cows and horses. We too, svādhyaḥ, well and wholly given to meditation, praise you." (Grammatical tail: semam, the loss of su in the Saṃhitā by so 'ci lope…; kāmam, ghañ after kam; final udātta due by Pā. 6-1-159, initial udātta because it is read in the vṛṣa-ādi; pṛṇa, pṛṇa prīṇane, hi for si, śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, no guṇa as it is ṅit, hi dropped by ato heḥ; gobhiḥ, the case-ending accent due by sāv ekācaḥ barred by na gośvan…; aśvaiḥ, a kvan form, as said; for lack of syntactic connection [with śatakrato], no parāṅgavadbhāva; stavāma, ṣṭuñ stutau, s for ṣ, the loss of s by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ (Pā. 3-4-99) since the loṭ is treated as laṅ, the augment āṭ by Pā. 3-4-92, the root accent; svādhyaḥ, dhyai cintāyām, su and āṅ used before it, kvip by Pā. 3-2-178, saṃprasāraṇa since dṛśi takes in other rules, lengthening by halaḥ, yaṇ by Pā. 6-4-82, the accent of the kṛt final member; the jas is not udātta by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt, since asarvanāmasthāna is carried on there, and becomes svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ….)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे शतक्रतो (he śatakrato) — O Indra | सः त्वम् (saḥ tvam) — you | नः (naḥ) — our | इमम् (imam) — this | कामम् (kāmam) — desired fruit (the object wished for) | गोभिः अश्वैः (gobhiḥ aśvaiḥ) — with cows and horses | आ पृण (ā pṛṇa) — fill up | (वयम् अपि (vayam api) — we too) | स्वाध्यः (svādhyaḥ) — being well given to meditation | त्वा (tvā) — you | स्तवाम (stavāma) — praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra, give us cows, horses and the like and fulfil our desire. We too, always given to meditation, praise you.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Satakratu (Indra) fulfil this our desire by giving us cows and horses. Profoundly meditating we praise yon [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Gobhir aśvaiḥ āpṛṇa: fill with cows and horses; that is, give us cows and horses and fulfil our desire.

Svādhyaḥ: dhyai cintāyām;

सुष्ठु सर्वतो ध्यानयुक्ताः सन्तः ॥

suṣṭhu sarvato dhyānayuktāḥ santaḥ ||

("Well and wholly given to meditation.") The sense is: meditating well in the mind (on you, Indra).

original p. 705

Rik 9: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 705–707, noted briefly

सेमम् (semam): after the word tad the nominative singular su. By "tadoḥ saḥ sāv anantyayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-106) s comes for a non-final t or d of the words of the tyad-ādi group before su: s for t, sad + s; by "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102) a for the d: sa + a + s; by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97) the pararūpa. These points are to be taken at "semaṃ na stomam ā" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-16-5) too. Sas + imam: by "so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-134) the s is dropped; guṇa: semam. The rest of its explanation is at the mantra semaṃ na stomam ā.

कामम् (kāmam): the root kamu kāntau; after it the suffix ghañ by "halaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-121): kam + a; vṛddhi of the penultimate by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116): kāma. Ghañ being ñit, initial udātta would come by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); overriding it, by "karṣātvato ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-159) (after the root karṣ and roots having ā, the last letter of a word ending in ghañ is udātta) final udātta comes. Overriding that too, by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203) (the first syllable of words read in the vṛṣa-ādi group is udātta), kāma, read in that group, is initial udātta.

पृण (pṛṇa): pṛṇa prīṇane, a root of the tud-ādi class; after it loṭ, 2nd singular sip. By "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87) the substitute hi; by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-77) the vikaraṇa śa: pṛṇ + a + hi. By "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) a sārvadhātuka without p as it counts as ṅit, so the suffix śa is ṅit; so by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) guṇa is barred, and guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) does not come. By "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105) hi takes luk: pṛṇa. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented. In the Saṃhitā, the pṛ after the udātta ā becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-66). The unaccented ṇa after it, since the udātta go follows, takes the anudātta tone by "udāttasvaritaparasya sannataraḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-2-40).

गोभिः (gobhiḥ): by "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-168), after a word of one vowel the case-endings from the instrumental on are udātta when the locative plural sup follows; so in gobhiḥ,

original p. 706

Rik 9: grammar

the base go having one vowel, udātta is due for the bhis after it. But by "na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkṛdbhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-182) it is barred that the accent just stated comes for a case-ending or matup after go and the rest; so the case-ending is not udātta.

अश्वैः (aśvaiḥ): aśva ends in the suffix kvan by "aśūpruṣi…" (Uṇ. sū. 1-149); initial udātta by the nit accent. After it stands the vocative śatakrato. Aśvaiḥ and śatakrato have no mutual syntactic connection, so there is no sāmarthya. For that reason it is not treated as one word by parāṅgavadbhāva through "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. 2-1-2), and so it does not become wholly unaccented by the eighth-chapter "āmantritasya ca".

स्तवाम (stavāma): the root ṣṭuñ stutau; s for ṣ by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64); loṭ, 1st plural mas: stu + mas. By "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) it is treated as laṅ; so by "nityaṃ ṅitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-99) the final s of the 1st person of a ṅit drops. Śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68); luk for it by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72). By "āḍ uttamasya pic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-92) the augment āṭ for ma: stu + āma; the tiṅ āma now begins with a vowel. So the optional augment īṭ enjoined by "turustuśamyamaḥ sārvadhātuke" (Pā. sū. 7-3-95) for a consonant-initial tiṅ called sārvadhātuka after these roots does not come. Guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), o for u, and the substitute av by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): stavāma. The suffix, being pit, is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4); so the root accent stays.

स्वाध्यः (svādhyaḥ): the root dhyai cintāyām; the preverbs su and āṅ used before it; ā for the final by "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-45): su + ā + dhyā; yaṇ: svā + dhyā. By "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate" (Pā. sū. 3-2-178) (kvip is seen after roots other than bhrāj and the rest too) kvip, and all of it drops. Here the mention of dṛśi in the sūtra serves to take in operations not got from other rules; so in the present case saṃprasāraṇa comes: svādh + i + a; by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108) the pūrvarūpa for i + a: svādhi. With the dropped suffix kvi as the condition, by "yasmāt pratyayavidhis tadādi pratyaye 'ṅgam" (Pā. sū. 1-4-13) (the word beginning with the base after which a suffix is enjoined, and ending before the suffix,

original p. 707

Rik 9: grammar (end)

is called aṅga when that suffix follows) the name aṅga applies. So by "halaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-2) (a stem ending in a saṃprasāraṇa that follows a consonant belonging to the stem is lengthened) the lengthening: svādhī. After it jas: svādhī + as. Now the substitute iyaṅ, due by "aci śnudhātu…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77), is overridden by "er anekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya" (Pā. sū. 6-4-82) (an aṅga of more than one vowel, ending in a root that ends in an i-vowel not preceded by a conjunct formed of root letters alone, takes yaṇ before a vowel-initial suffix), so yaṇ comes. For in svādhī the ī does not follow a conjunct, still less a conjunct of root letters alone; the root it ends in is dhī, the aṅga ending in it is svādhī, and it has more than one vowel. So yaṇ comes, and by the paribhāṣā "alo 'ntyasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-52) for the last letter ī: svādhyas; ru and visarga: svādhyaḥ. Dhī is final udātta by the root accent; after compounding with the preverbs the accent of the kṛt final member stays by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139). The yaṇ stands in place of the udātta ī, and it is preceded by a consonant. Yet by "udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt" (Pā. sū. 6-1-174) the jas ending is not udātta, because into this sūtra "asarvanāmasthānam" is carried on from "añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-170). So the sense of udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt is: after a yaṇ that stands in place of an udātta and is preceded by a consonant, a suffix called nadī and a case-ending that is not sarvanāmasthāna are udātta. The present jas is a sarvanāmasthāna by "suḍ anapuṃsakasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-43) (the five suffixes su, au, jas, am, auṭ, not after a neuter word, are called sarvanāmasthāna); it is not asarvanāmasthāna. So the udātta accent does not come for the jas by udāttayaṇaḥ. By "udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (after a yaṇ standing in place of an udātta or svarita, an unaccented vowel becomes svarita), the jas, unaccented by anudāttau suppitau, gets only the svarita tone.

॥९॥ An ornament closes Sūkta 16 at the foot of p. 707; no colophon is printed. Printed p. 708 opens with the title ಹದಿನೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Seventeenth Sūkta") and an ornament.

॥ ಹದಿನೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 17 — "indrāvaruṇayor aham" ("The Seventeenth Sūkta")

original p. 708

Sūkta 17: introduction, heading, Rik 1 Saṃhitā

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note) वनुक्रम्यते is as printed, probably for ऽनुक्रम्यते.

इन्द्रावरुणयोरित्यादिकं नवर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तम् । अत एव नवशब्दानुवृत्त्यावनुक्रम्यते । इन्द्रावरुणयोरैन्द्रावरुणं युवाकु पादनिचृताविति । अत्र देवता विस्पष्टा । ऋषिच्छन्दसी तु पूर्ववदनुवर्तेते । अयं तु विशेषः । युवाकु हीत्यादिके द्वे ऋचौ पादनिचृन्नामकच्छन्दोयुक्ते ॥ विनियोगस्तु स्मार्तो लैङ्गिको वा कश्चिदवगन्तव्यः ॥

indrāvaruṇayorityādikaṃ navarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktam | ata eva navaśabdānuvṛttyāvanukramyate | indrāvaruṇayoraindrāvaruṇaṃ yuvāku pādanicṛtāviti | atra devatā vispaṣṭā | ṛṣicchandasī tu pūrvavadanuvartete | ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ | yuvāku hītyādike dve ṛcau pādanicṛnnāmakacchandoyukte || viniyogastu smārto laiṅgiko vā kaścidavagantavyaḥ ||

Translation: "The sūkta beginning indrāvaruṇayoḥ, of nine ṛks, is the sixth. So, with the word 'nine' carried on, the Anukramaṇī states: 'indrāvaruṇayoḥ, to Indra and Varuṇa; yuvāku, two in pādanicṛt'. Here the deity is plain; the ṛṣi and the metre continue as before. This, however, is special: the two ṛks beginning yuvāku hi have the metre called pādanicṛt. The application is to be understood as some smārta or laiṅgika one."

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): Indrāvaruṇayoḥ is the sixth sūkta in this fourth anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā the 4th and 5th ṛks are said to be ṛks of the metre called pādanicṛt. Indra and Varuṇa are the deities. The ṛṣi and metre are as in the previous sūkta; but the two ṛks yuvāku hi śacīnām and indraḥ sahasradāvnām alone have the metre named pādanicṛt. The application may be learnt by looking at the smārta usage.

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 17 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 4 ॥ Sūkta — 17 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 32, 33 ॥ ॥ Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣiḥ — Medhātithiḥ Kāṇvaḥ ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indrāvaruṇau ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — 1–3, 6–9, Gāyatrī; 4, 5, Pādanicṛt ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 17, Rik 1

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रा॒वरु॑णयोर॒हं स॒म्राजो॒रव॒ आ वृ॑णे । ता नो॑ मृळात ई॒दृशे॑ ॥१॥

indrāváruṇayor aháṃ samrā́jor áva ā́ vṛṇe | tā́ no mṛḷāta īdṛ́śe ||1||

original p. 709

Rik 1: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणयोः । अहम् । सम्ऽराजोः । अवः । आ । वृणे ॥ ता । नः । मृळातः । ईदृशे ॥१॥

indrāvaruṇayoḥ | aham | sam 'rājoḥ | avaḥ | ā | vṛṇe || tā | naḥ | mṛḷātaḥ | īdṛśe ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ समो before मोऽनुस्वारः is as read; the first letter may be स or a misprint.

अहमनुष्ठाता सम्राजोः समीचीनराज्योपेतयोः सम्यग्दीप्यमानयोर्वेन्द्रावरुणयोर्देवयोः संबन्ध्यवो रक्षणमा वृणे । सर्वतः प्रार्थये । ता तौ देवावीदृशे एवंविधेऽस्मदीयवरणे निमित्तभूते सति मृळातः । अस्मान्सुखयतः ॥ इन्द्रशब्दो रन्प्रत्ययान्तः । वरुणशब्द उनन्प्रत्ययान्तः । उभौ नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तौ । समासे देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानङादेशः । उभे युगपदित्यनुवृत्तौ देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति युगपदुभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सम्राजोः । राजृ दीप्तौ । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । समो[?] मोऽनुस्वारः । पा. ८-३-२३ । इत्यनुस्वारे प्राप्ते मो राजि समः क्वौ । पा. ८-३-२५ । इति मकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति । पा. २-३-६५ । इति कर्तरि षष्ठी । अवः । अव रक्षणादिषु । भावेऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ता । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना द्विवचनस्य डादेशः । टिलोपे विभक्तेरुदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरः । मृळातः । मृड सुखने । प्रार्थनायां लिङर्थे लेट् । द्विवचनं तस् । लेटोऽडाटावित्याडागमः । तुदादिभ्यः शः । ङित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । ईदृशे । त्यदादिषु दृशोऽनालोचने कञ्च । पा. ३-२-६० । इतीदंशब्द उपपदे दृशेः कञ् । उपपदसमास इदंकिमोरीश्की । पा. ६-३-९० । इतीदम ईश् । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । कञः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । ञित्त्वादुत्तरपदस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । उपपदसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते ॥

ahamanuṣṭhātā samrājoḥ samīcīnarājyopetayoḥ samyagdīpyamānayorvendrāvaruṇayordevayoḥ saṃbandhyavo rakṣaṇamā vṛṇe | sarvataḥ prārthaye | tā tau devāvīdṛśe evaṃvidhe 'smadīyavaraṇe nimittabhūte sati mṛḷātaḥ | asmānsukhayataḥ || indraśabdo ranpratyayāntaḥ | varuṇaśabda unanpratyayāntaḥ | ubhau nittvādādyudāttau | samāse devatādvandve ceti pūrvapadasyānaṅādeśaḥ | ubhe yugapadityanuvṛttau devatādvandve ceti yugapadubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | samrājoḥ | rājṛ dīptau | satsūdviṣetyādinā kvip | samo[?] mo 'nusvāraḥ | pā. 8-3-23 | ityanusvāre prāpte mo rāji samaḥ kvau | pā. 8-3-25 | iti makārādeśaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti | pā. 2-3-65 | iti kartari ṣaṣṭhī | avaḥ | ava rakṣaṇādiṣu | bhāve 'sun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | tā | supāṃ sulugityādinā dvivacanasya ḍādeśaḥ | ṭilope vibhakterudāttanivṛttisvaraḥ | mṛḷātaḥ | mṛḍa sukhane | prārthanāyāṃ liṅarthe leṭ | dvivacanaṃ tas | leṭo 'ḍāṭāvityāḍāgamaḥ | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | ṅittvāllaghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | īdṛśe | tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañca | pā. 3-2-60 | itīdaṃśabda upapade dṛśeḥ kañ | upapadasamāsa idaṃkimorīśkī | pā. 6-3-90 | itīdama īś | śittvātsarvādeśaḥ | kañaḥ kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | ñittvāduttarapadasyādyudāttatvam | upapadasamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tadeva śiṣyate ||

Translation: "I, the performer, ā vṛṇe, pray from all sides for the avaḥ, protection, belonging to the two gods Indra and Varuṇa, samrājau, possessed of excellent sovereignty, or shining well. May those two gods, īdṛśe, on such an occasion, our choosing [them] being the cause, mṛḷātaḥ, make us happy." (Grammatical tail: indra ends in ran, varuṇa in unan, both initial udātta as nit; in the compound ānaṅ for the first member by devatādvandve ca, and, with ubhe yugapat carried on, both members keep their own accent at once by devatādvandve ca; samrājoḥ, rājṛ dīptau, kvip by satsūdviṣa…, the anusvāra due by Pā. 8-3-23 replaced by m by Pā. 8-3-25, the accent of the kṛt final member, the genitive of agent by Pā. 2-3-65; avaḥ, ava rakṣaṇādiṣu, asun in the sense of the action, initial udātta as nit; tā, ḍā for the dual ending by supāṃ suluk…, with the loss of the ṭi the case-ending takes the accent of the lost udātta; mṛḷātaḥ, mṛḍa sukhane, leṭ in the sense of liṅ, of a prayer, dual tas, the augment āṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau, śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, no guṇa of the light penultimate as it is ṅit; īdṛśe, kañ after dṛś with idam as upapada by Pā. 3-2-60, īś for idam in the upapada compound by Pā. 6-3-90, replacing the whole as it is śit, no guṇa as kañ is kit, initial udātta of the final member as ñit, and that alone stays by the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अहम् (aham) — I (the performer of the sacrifice) | सम्राजोः (samrājoḥ) — who shine well, or who have good sovereignty | इन्द्रावरुणयोः (indrāvaruṇayoḥ) — of Indra and Varuṇa | अवः (avaḥ) — protection | आ वृणे (ā vṛṇe) — I pray for (on all sides) | ता (tā) — those two deities | ईदृशे (īdṛśe) — in this matter of our prayer | नः (naḥ) — to us | मृळातः (mṛḷātaḥ) — may they give happiness.

original p. 710

Rik 1: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

I, who have begun the sacrifice, with the aim that my sacrifice be completed in all its parts, take refuge with Indra and Varuṇa, who are very radiant and possessed of sovereignty. May they fulfil this prayer of mine and give me joy.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I seek the protection of the sovereign rulers Indra and Varuna; may they both favour us accordingly.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The deities of this sūkta are the two, Indra and Varuṇa. In the Ṛgveda, the calling of two deities together and their praise together is especially to be seen. Mantras setting forth such pairs of deities (devatādvandvas) are called saṃstavika mantras. The chief deities in them are fourteen: Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Brahmaṇaspati, Parvata, Kutsa, Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Mitra, Rudra, Vāta and Parjanya. For example:

इन्द्राग्नी (indra + agni):

इन्द्राग्नी रोचना दिवः (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-12-9)

indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-12-9)

("Indra and Agni, the bright realms of heaven": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्रासोमा (indra + soma):

इन्द्रासोमा समघशंसम् (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-104-2)

indrāsomā samaghaśaṃsam (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-104-2)

("Indra and Soma, [burn] the one who speaks evil": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्रावरुणा (indra + varuṇa):

इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नः (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-82-1)

indrāvaruṇā yuvamadhvarāya naḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-82-1)

("Indra and Varuṇa, you two, for our sacrifice": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्रापूषणा (indra + pūṣan):

इन्द्रपूषणा वयम् (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-57-1)

indrapūṣaṇā vayam (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-57-1)

("Indra and Pūṣan, we …": editorial and tentative. इन्द्रपूषणा, without the long ā, is as printed; the heading has इन्द्रापूषणा.)

इन्द्राबृहस्पती (indra + bṛhaspati):

इदं वामास्ये हविः प्रियमिन्द्राबृहस्पती (Ṛ. saṃ. 4-49-1)

idaṃ vāmāsye haviḥ priyamindrābṛhaspatī (Ṛ. saṃ. 4-49-1)

("This dear offering in your mouth, Indra and Bṛhaspati": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पती (indra + brahmaṇaspati):

अच्छेन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पती हविर्नः (Ṛ. saṃ. 2-24-12)

acchendrābrahmaṇaspatī havirnaḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 2-24-12)

("Towards our offering, Indra and Brahmaṇaspati": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 711

Rik 1: Special Topics (continued)

इन्द्रापर्वता (indra + parvata):

इन्द्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-53-1)

indrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-53-1)

("Indra and Parvata, with your great chariot": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्राकुत्सा (indra + kutsa):

इन्द्राकुत्सा वहमाना रथेन (Ṛ. saṃ. 5-31-9)

indrākutsā vahamānā rathena (Ṛ. saṃ. 5-31-9)

("Indra and Kutsa, riding on the chariot": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्राविष्णू (indra + viṣṇu):

इन्द्राविष्णू दृंहिताः शम्बरस्य (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-99-5)

indrāviṣṇū dṛṃhitāḥ śambarasya (Ṛ. saṃ. 7-99-5)

("Indra and Viṣṇu, the strongholds of Śambara": editorial and tentative.)

इन्द्रवायू (indra + vāyu):

इन्द्रवायू इमे सुताः (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-2-4)

indravāyū ime sutāḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-2-4)

("Indra and Vāyu, these [soma juices] are pressed": editorial and tentative.)

मित्रावरुणा (mitra + varuṇa):

आ नो मित्रावरुणा (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-62-16)

ā no mitrāvaruṇā (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-62-16)

("[Come] to us, Mitra and Varuṇa": editorial and tentative.)

सोमापूषणा (soma + pūṣan):

somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇām (Ṛ. saṃ. 2-40-1)

("Soma and Pūṣan, begetters of riches": editorial and tentative.)

सोमारुद्रा युवमेतान्यस्मे (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-74-3)

somārudrā yuvametānyasme (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-74-3)

("Soma and Rudra, you two, these [remedies] for us": editorial and tentative.)

धर्तारो दिव ऋभवः सुहस्ता वातापर्जन्या महिषस्य तन्यतोः (Ṛ. saṃ. 10-66-10)

dhartāro diva ṛbhavaḥ suhastā vātāparjanyā mahiṣasya tanyatoḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 10-66-10)

("The upholders of heaven, the skilful-handed Ṛbhus, Vāta and Parjanya of the roaring buffalo [thunder]": editorial and tentative.)

अग्नीषोमौ (agni + soma):

अग्नीषोमाविमं सु मे (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-93-1)

("Agni and Soma, [hear] well this [call] of mine": editorial and tentative.)

अग्नीपर्जन्या (agni + parjanya):

अग्नीपर्जन्याववतं धियं मे (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-52-16)

agnīparjanyāvavataṃ dhiyaṃ me (Ṛ. saṃ. 6-52-16)

("Agni and Parjanya, favour my prayer": editorial and tentative.)

अग्नाविष्णू (agni + viṣṇu):

अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसा (Tai. saṃ. 4-7-1)

agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā (Tai. saṃ. 4-7-1)

("Agni and Viṣṇu, of one accord": editorial and tentative.)

Such saṃstava mantras are many in the Ṛgveda. There are also many ṛks in which, in naming a pair of deities, the dual is not used, but the singular is used for each separately. For example:

अग्न इन्द्रश्च दाशुषे दुरोणे (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-25-4)

agna indraśca dāśuṣe duroṇe (Ṛ. saṃ. 3-25-4)

("Agni, and Indra, in the house of the worshipper": editorial and tentative.)

त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान् (Ṛ. saṃ. 4-1-4)

tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān (Ṛ. saṃ. 4-1-4)

("You, Agni, knowing Varuṇa, [for] us": editorial and tentative.)

मरुतः पिबत ऋतुना (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-15-2)

marutaḥ pibata ṛtunā (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-15-2)

("Maruts, drink with the season": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 712

Rik 1: Special Topics (end) and grammar

and so on. In these ṛks, though the pairs of deities Agni + Indra, Agni + Varuṇa and the Maruts + Ṛtu are named, the dual is not used; the deities are named each separately, in the singular.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 712–714, noted briefly

इन्द्रावरुणयोः (indrāvaruṇayoḥ): the dvandva compound indraś ca varuṇaś ca indrāvaruṇau, tayoḥ. After the root idi paramaiśvarye the suffix ran by "ṛjrendrāgra…" (Uṇ. sū. 2-186); the root being idit, the augment num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-58): indra. By "kṝvṝdāribhya unan" (Uṇ. sū. "3-333" [as read; ?]) the suffix unan comes after kṝ vikṣepe, vṛñ varaṇe and dṝ vidāraṇe; so after the root vṛñ, unan: vṛ + una; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), followed by r by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51): varuna; by "aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for n: varuṇa. Both words end in a suffix with n as it; so both are initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). In their dvandva, by "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26), in a dvandva of two words naming deities, the first member takes the substitute ānaṅ when the second follows; being ṅit, it replaces the final by "ṅic ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-53); the n is dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7). In "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-2-141) the two words ubhe and yugapat are carried on from "ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat" (Pā. sū. 6-2-140); so the sūtra means that in a dvandva of words naming deities, the first and second members both keep their own accent at the same time; so both members keep their accent.

सम्राजोः (samrājoḥ): the root rājṛ dīptau. By "satsūdviṣa…janirājām upasarge 'pi kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-61) the suffix kvip. With sam + rāj, the anusvāra is due for the m of sam by "mo 'nusvāraḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-23) (before a consonant the final m of a word becomes anusvāra). But by "mo rāji samaḥ kvau" (Pā. sū. 8-3-25), when the root rāj ending in kvip follows, the m of sam stays m: samrāj.

अवः (avaḥ): the root ava rakṣaṇādau. By "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]) the suffix asun in the sense of the action; initial udātta by the nit accent. So avaḥ is a kṛdanta;

original p. 713

Rik 1: grammar

since there is connection with this kṛdanta, in indrāvaruṇayoḥ the genitive comes by "kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti" (Pā. sū. 2-3-65) (the genitive comes after a word that is the agent or object in the action denoted by the root that is the base of a kṛt suffix). For the kṛt is the suffix asun, its base is the root av, its sense is the action, an activity leading to warding off the unwanted and gaining the wanted; Indra and Varuṇa are the substrate of that activity, so they are the agents in the action meant by the root av; after the word indrāvaruṇa, naming the agents, the genitive comes by the sūtra just stated. On the view "kārakāṇāṃ kriyayaivānvayaḥ" (the kārakas are construed with the action alone), in samrājoḥ too the genitive comes in the same way.

ता (tā): after the word tad the nominative dual au: tad + au. By "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ḍā for au; by force of its being marked with ḍ, though it is not called bha, the ṭi ad drops. By "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-161), the accent of the lost udātta, the ending ā is udātta.

मृळातः (mṛḷātaḥ): the root mṛḍa sukhane. After the root mṛḍ, by "liṅarthe leṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-7), leṭ comes in the sense of liṅ, of a prayer; in its place the 3rd dual tas: mṛḍ + tas. By "leṭo 'ḍāṭau" (Pā. sū. 3-4-94) the augment āṭ; being ṭit, it comes as the first part by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (paribhāṣā, Pā. sū. 1-1-46). Mṛḍ + ātas: the vikaraṇa suffix śa by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-77). It is a sārvadhātuka without p, so by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it is ṅit; so guṇa is barred by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5), and the laghūpadha-guṇa by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) does not come. [After] the lengthening of like vowels, since by "antādivac ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-85) the result counts as the end of what precedes, the śa vikaraṇa can count as following, so guṇa does not come. Mṛḍātaḥ: by "ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ" (the Ṛgvedins pronounce ḍ between vowels as ḷ), ḷ for ḍ.

ईदृशे (īdṛśe): idam iva paśyati iti īdṛśaḥ, tasmin īdṛśe. By "tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-60), when words of the tyad-ādi group are the upapada, the suffix kañ comes after the root dṛś not in the sense of seeing; by the ca, optionally kvin too; so after the root dṛś with the word idam as upapada, the suffix kañ. By "upapadam atiṅ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-19) compounding; the sup inside the compound takes luk: idam + dṛśa. By "idaṃkimor īśkī" (Pā. sū. 6-3-90), when dṛk, dṛśa or vatu follow, īś is substituted for idam and kī for kim; so īś for idam; being śit, by "anekālśit sarvasya" (Pā. sū.

Page 714 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

1-1-55) it replaces the whole: īdṛśa; in the locative singular īdṛśe. The suffix kañ being kit, laghūpadha-guṇa does not come in dṛśa. The suffix is ñit; so by "ñnityādir nityam" dṛśa is initial udātta. After compounding, the accent of the kṛt final member coming by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), dṛśa stays initial udātta. So īdṛśe is udātta in the middle.

॥१॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The Saṃhitā prints स्थोवसे without the avagraha.

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa, avase, to protect the performer, you are indeed gantārau, given to coming, to the havam, the call, of a vipra, a brahmin priest, māvataḥ, like me. Of what kind? Dhartārau, upholders, of carṣaṇi, men, by bringing about their yogakṣema." (Grammatical tail: gantārā, tṛn after gam in the sense of habit, ā for the dual by supāṃ suluk…, guṇa by ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ (Pā. 7-4-16), the penultimate lengthened by aptṛn…, initial udātta as tṛn is nit; sthaḥ, asa bhuvi, 2nd dual thas, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ, the lowering barred by hi ca; avase, ava rakṣaṇe, asen in the sense of the infinitive (Pā. 3-4-9), initial udātta as nit; havam, hveñ with saṃprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi, ap by ṛdor ap, guṇa and av, ap unaccented as pit, the root accent; viprasya, ḍuvap bījatantusaṃtāne, ran by ṛjrendra…, initial udātta as nit; māvataḥ, vatup in the sense of likeness after asmad in the Veda (Pā. 5-2-39-1), ma for the part up to m (Pā. 7-2-98), ā for the d (Pā. 6-3-91), lengthening, the suffix unaccented as pit, and the stem-final udātta stays; dhartārā, dhṛñ dhāraṇe, tṛc (Pā. 3-1-133), no iṭ by ekāca upadeśe…, guṇa with r, lengthening, ā for the dual, final udātta as tṛc is cit; carṣaṇīnām, ani by kṛṣer ādeś ca caḥ (Uṇ. 2-104), c for k with it; overriding the suffix-initial udātta, a Vedic final udātta; so the ending is udātta by nām anyatarasyām, explained there as "nām after what ends in a short vowel before matup".)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे इन्द्रावरुणौ (he indrāvaruṇau) — O Indra and Varuṇa) | चर्षणीनाम् (carṣaṇīnām) — of men | धर्तारौ (dhartārau) — upholders (of their yogakṣema) (you are) | अवसे (avase) — for protection (of the sacrificer) | मावतः (māvataḥ) — of one like me | विप्रस्य (viprasya) — of the priest (a brahmin) | हवम् (havam) — the call (honouring it) | गन्तारा स्थः हि (gantārā sthaḥ hi) — you are indeed of the nature of coming.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa, you look after the yogakṣema of men. So you are of the nature to come here without fail, honouring my call, for the protection of a priest like me.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra and Varuna, you are the protectors of the people and you go at the call of a minister like me to protect him.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Viprasya: though the word vipra means "wise", here the sense "one who is praising" fits well.

Māvataḥ:

मद्विधस्य

madvidhasya

("Of one like me.") Like me: that is, to the sacrificer who praises you as I do.

Dhartārā:

धृञ् धारणे । योगक्षेमसंपादनेन धारयितारौ ।

dhṛñ dhāraṇe | yogakṣemasaṃpādanena dhārayitārau |

("Dhṛñ, to hold; who uphold by bringing about yogakṣema.") Those who uphold the yogakṣema of men, that is, who care for it, who bear the burden of yogakṣema.

original p. 716

Rik 2: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 716–718, noted briefly

गन्तारा (gantārā): the root gamḷ gatau. After it tṛn comes in the sense "tacchīla" by "tṛn" (Pā. sū. 3-2-135): gam + tṛ. By "naś cāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. sū. 8-3-24) anusvāra for the m; by "anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-58), with the help of the paribhāṣā sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ, in place of the anusvāra comes n, homorganic with what follows and nasal: gantṛ. After it the nominative dual au; for it the substitute ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39): gantṛ + ā. Guṇa by "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-110), followed by r by uraṇ raparaḥ: gantar + ā. Here, by "ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-16), the guṇa enjoined for ṛ-final roots and dṛś comes when aṅ follows; here there is no suffix aṅ, so this sūtra does not apply. So it should be understood that the derivation of guṇa here from the sūtra ṛdṛśo 'ṅi [in the bhāṣya] is an oversight. By "aptṛntṛc…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-11) the penultimate is lengthened: gantāram [as printed]. The suffix tṛn is nit; so gantṛ is initial udātta by ñnityādir nityam.

स्थः (sthaḥ): the root asa bhuvi, of the ad-ādi class; after it laṭ, 2nd dual thas: as + thas; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68), luk for it by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72); thas is ṅit by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4). By "śnasor allopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-111) the a of as drops; ru and visarga: sthaḥ. By "hi ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-34) a tiṅanta joined with hi is not unaccented; since stha, joined with hi as hi stha, is barred from being wholly unaccented, it does not become wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

अवसे (avase): the root ava rakṣaṇe. By the statement "tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kse-kasen-adhyai-adhyain-kadhyai-kadhyain-śadhyai-śadhyain-tavai-taveṅ-tavenaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-9), with avyayakṛto bhāve, the infinitive sense is the action, and in it the suffixes named come; so the suffix asen: av + ase = avase, initial udātta by the nit accent.

हवम् (havam): the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; with "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) carried on, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34) saṃprasāraṇa without a condition, that is, u for v; the pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108): hu. By "ṛdor ap" (Pā. sū. 3-3-57) (after roots ending in ṝ or u comes the suffix ap), after hu the suffix ap; guṇa, o for u, by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84); by "eco 'ya-

original p. 717

Rik 2: grammar

vāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78) the substitute av: hava. The suffix ap being pit, it is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau; so the root accent stays. After it the suffix am; the pūrvarūpa by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107): havam.

विप्रस्य (viprasya): the root ḍuvap bījasantāne. For it the suffix ran is given as a ready-made form by the sūtra "ṛjrendrāgravipra…" (Uṇ. sū. 2-186). Initial udātta by the nit accent.

मावतः (māvataḥ): "yattadetebhyaḥ parimāṇe vatup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-39). By the statement on this sūtra, "vatupprakaraṇe yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. sū. 5-2-39-1) (in the Veda, vatup in the sense of likeness after yuṣmad and asmad is to be stated in the vatup section), vatup comes after asmad in the sense of likeness: asmad + vat. By "pratyayottarapadayoś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-98), when a suffix or a final member follows, the part of yuṣmad and asmad up to the m takes tva and ma; so ma for asm: ma + ad + vat. The pararūpa by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97): mad + vat. By "ā sarvanāmnaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-91), when dṛk, dṛśa or vatu follow, the final of a pronoun takes ā: ma + ā + vat; lengthening of like vowels by "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-101): māvat. The suffix vatup being pit, it is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau. Mā is final udātta by the stem accent; that accent stays.

धर्तारा (dhartārā): the root dhṛñ dhāraṇe; tṛc by "ṇvultṛcau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-133). The root dhṛ is anudātta in the upadeśa and has one vowel; so by "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. sū. 7-2-10) the augment iṭ due by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ is barred for the tṛ. With tṛc as the condition, guṇa for dhṛ by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, followed by r: dhartṛ. After it the suffix au; for it the substitute ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); in dhartṛ guṇa by ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ, followed by r, and the penultimate lengthened by the sūtra aptṛntṛc…: dhartārā. The suffix tṛc being cit, dhartṛ is final udātta by citaḥ.

चर्षणीनाम् (carṣaṇīnām): the root kṛṣa vilekhane. After it, by "kṛṣer ādeś ca caḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "2-26" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-104), the suffix ani comes after the root kṛṣ, and c for the first letter k; so with the suffix ani and c for k: cṛṣ + ani; by "puganta-

Page 718 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar (end)

laghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) the laghūpadha-guṇa, followed by r: carṣani; by "aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for n: carṣaṇi. After it the genitive plural ām: carṣaṇi + ām. By "hrasvanadyāpo nuṭ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-54) the augment nuṭ; by "nāmi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-3), before nām, a vowel-final aṅga is lengthened: carṣaṇīnām. Though the suffix-initial udātta is due for ani by ādyudāttaś ca, a Vedic final udātta comes. Because it is final udātta, the ending is udātta by "nām anyatarasyām" (Pā. sū. "6-1-77" [as printed, for 6-1-177]). Carṣaṇī, though final udātta, does not end in a short vowel; so how does the udātta come? The sense of nām anyatarasyām is: after what is short-final and final udātta when the suffix matup follows, the nām is optionally udātta. If matup is placed after carṣaṇi, it is short-final and final udātta; so, though it is now long-final, the ending may be udātta.

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ अनुकाममस्मदीयाभिलाषमनु रायो धनस्य प्रदानेन तर्पयेथाम् । सर्वतोऽस्मांस्तृप्तान्कुरुतम् । वयं यदा यदा धनं कामयामहे तदा तदा प्रयच्छतमित्यर्थः । ता वां तादृशौ युवां नेदिष्ठ-

मतिशयेन सामीप्यं यथा भवति तथा ईमहे । याचामहे कालविलम्बमन्तरेण धनं दातव्यमित्यर्थः । सप्तदशसु याच्ञाकर्मस्वीमह इति पठितम् ॥ अनुकामम् । कामस्य पश्चादनुकामम् । अथवा कामे कामेऽनुकामम् । अनुरिह पश्चादर्थे । अथवा वीप्सालक्षणे यथार्थे । योग्यता वीप्सा पदार्थानतिवृत्तिः सादृश्यं चेति चत्वारो हि यथार्था गृहीताः । अव्ययं विभक्तीत्यादिना । पा. २-१-६ । अव्ययीभावसमासः । अव्ययीभावश्च । पा. १-१-४१ । इत्यव्ययसंज्ञायामव्ययादाप्सुपः । पा. २-४-८२ । इति प्राप्तस्य लुकोऽपवादो नाव्ययीभावादतोऽम्त्वपञ्चम्याः । पा. २-४-८३ । इति विभक्तेरमादेशः । समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । तर्पयेथाम् । तृपेर्ण्यन्ताल्लोटो णिचश्च । पा. १-३-७४ । इत्यात्मनेपदम् । मध्यमद्विवचनमाथाम् । टेरेत्वे आमेतः । पा. ३-४-९० । इत्यामादेशः । शपि सत्यतो येयः । पा. ७-२-८० । इत्याकारस्येयादेशः । आद्गुणो यलोपश्च । इन्द्रावरुणा । सुपां सुलुगिति द्विवचनस्याकारः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । संहितायामाकारस्य ह्रस्वत्वम् । रायः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । ता । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । पदात्परत्वाद्युष्मदस्मदित्यस्य वामादेशोऽनुदात्तः । नेदिष्ठम् । अतिशयेनान्तिकम् । अतिशायन इष्ठन् । अन्तिकबाढयोर्नेदसाधौ । पा. ५-३-६३ । इति नेदादेशः । यस्येति लोपः । इष्ठनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । ईमहे । ईङ् गतौ । ङित्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । बहुलं छन्दसीति श्यनो लुक् । निघातः ॥

matiśayena sāmīpyaṃ yathā bhavati tathā īmahe | yācāmahe kālavilambamantareṇa dhanaṃ dātavyamityarthaḥ | saptadaśasu yācñākarmasvīmaha iti paṭhitam || anukāmam | kāmasya paścādanukāmam | athavā kāme kāme 'nukāmam | anuriha paścādarthe | athavā vīpsālakṣaṇe yathārthe | yogyatā vīpsā padārthānativṛttiḥ sādṛśyaṃ ceti catvāro hi yathārthā gṛhītāḥ | avyayaṃ vibhaktītyādinā | pā. 2-1-6 | avyayībhāvasamāsaḥ | avyayībhāvaśca | pā. 1-1-41 | ityavyayasaṃjñāyāmavyayādāpsupaḥ | pā. 2-4-82 | iti prāptasya luko 'pavādo nāvyayībhāvādato 'mtvapañcamyāḥ | pā. 2-4-83 | iti vibhakteramādeśaḥ | samāsasyetyantodāttatvam | tarpayethām | tṛperṇyantālloṭo ṇicaśca | pā. 1-3-74 | ityātmanepadam | madhyamadvivacanamāthām | ṭeretve āmetaḥ | pā. 3-4-90 | ityāmādeśaḥ | śapi satyato yeyaḥ | pā. 7-2-80 | ityākārasyeyādeśaḥ | ādguṇo yalopaśca | indrāvaruṇā | supāṃ sulugiti dvivacanasyākāraḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | saṃhitāyāmākārasya hrasvatvam | rāyaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | tā | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ | padātparatvādyuṣmadasmadityasya vāmādeśo 'nudāttaḥ | nediṣṭham | atiśayenāntikam | atiśāyana iṣṭhan | antikabāḍhayornedasādhau | pā. 5-3-63 | iti nedādeśaḥ | yasyeti lopaḥ | iṣṭhano nittvādādyudāttatvam | īmahe | īṅ gatau | ṅittvādātmanepadam | bahulaṃ chandasīti śyano luk | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa, anukāmam, according to our wish, tarpayethām, satisfy us by the gift of rāyaḥ, wealth: make us content on all sides; that is, whenever we desire wealth, then give it. Tā vām, you two, such as you are, īmahe, we beg, so that you are nediṣṭham, nearest: that is, wealth is to be given without delay. Īmahe is read among the seventeen words meaning 'to beg'." (Grammatical tail: anukāmam, "after the wish", or "at each wish", anu here in the sense "after", or in the sense yathā marked by repetition, the four senses of yathā being fitness, repetition, not going beyond the sense of the word, and likeness; an avyayībhāva by Pā. 2-1-6; called avyaya by Pā. 1-1-41, the luk due by Pā. 2-4-82 is overridden by Pā. 2-4-83, which gives am for the ending; final udātta by samāsasya; tarpayethām, ātmanepada after the causative of tṛp by Pā. 1-3-74, 2nd dual āthām, ām for the e by Pā. 3-4-90, iy for the ā by Pā. 7-2-80 since śap follows, guṇa by ād guṇaḥ and the loss of y; indrāvaruṇā, ā for the dual by supāṃ suluk, initial udātta of the vocative, shortened in the Saṃhitā; rāyaḥ, the ending udātta by ūḍidam…; tā, ā for the ending by supāṃ suluk; following a word, vām, unaccented, replaces yuṣmad; nediṣṭham, "very near", iṣṭhan in the sense of excess, neda for antika by Pā. 5-3-63, the loss by yasyeti, initial udātta as iṣṭhan is nit; īmahe, īṅ gatau, ātmanepada as ṅit, luk of śyan by bahulaṃ chandasi, wholly unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | अनुकामम् (anukāmam) — according to our desire, or our desires one by one | रायः (rāyaḥ) — by the gift of wealth | आ तर्पयेथाम् (ā tarpayethām) — satisfy (us) | ता (tā) — such | वाम् (vām) — you two | नेदिष्ठम् (nediṣṭham) — very near (without delay) | ईमहे (īmahe) — we praise.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa, we praise you for riches and the like, that you may be near us. As soon as we pray, give us the wealth we need.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, satisfy us with wealth according to our desires We [sic] therefore pray you to be nearest to us.

Rik 3: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Anukāmam:

कामस्य पश्चादनुकामम् । अथवा कामे कामेऽनुकामम् । अनुरिह पश्चादर्थे अथवा वीप्सालक्षणे यथार्थे ॥ अस्मदीयमभिलाषमनु ॥

kāmasya paścādanukāmam | athavā kāme kāme 'nukāmam | anuriha paścādarthe athavā vīpsālakṣaṇe yathārthe || asmadīyamabhilāṣamanu ||

("After the wish, or at each wish; anu here in the sense 'after', or in the sense yathā marked by repetition: according to our wish.") That is, according to our wish, or every wish that we want.

Nediṣṭham:

अतिशयेन सामीप्यं यथा भवति तथा । अतिशयेनान्तिकम् ।

atiśayena sāmīpyaṃ yathā bhavati tathā | atiśayenāntikam |

("So that nearness is in the highest degree: very near.") The sense is: you should be very near us, so as to give us our desires.

Īmahe: since the word īmahe is read among the seventeen words meaning "to beg", yāmi and the rest (Ni. 3-19), īmahe means "we beg, we pray".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 720–723, noted briefly

अनुकामम् (anukāmam): the analysis is kāmasya paścāt anukāmam; here the preverb anu means "after". Or the analysis is kāme kāme anukāmam; here anu means repetition. This repetition is included in the senses of the word yathā: the word yathā has four senses, fitness, repetition, not going beyond the sense of the word, and likeness. In the first sense the indeclinable anu means "after"; in the second it means yathā. In both views, by "avyayaṃ vibhakti-samīpa-samṛddhi-vyṛddhy-arthābhāvātyayāsaṃprati-śabdaprādurbhāva-paścād-yathānupūrvya-yaugapadya-sādṛśya-saṃpatti-sākalyānta-vacaneṣu" (Pā. sū. 2-1-6) (the sixteen words from vibhakti to anta form a dvandva; the analysis is antaś cāsau vacanāś ca antavacanāḥ, teṣu vibhaktyādi-antavacaneṣu), an indeclinable conveying the sense of a case and the rest is compounded with a subanta that is syntactically fit; it is an avyayībhāva, so the avyayībhāva compound comes. By "avyayībhāvaś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-41) the avyayībhāva compound also is called avyaya; so anukāma is called avyaya. So when the sup suffix comes after anukāma, luk is due by "avyayād āpsupaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-82) (the āp and sup after an avyaya take luk), but by "nāvyayībhāvād ato 'm tv apañcamyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-83) come the bar and the substitute am. In this sūtra nāvyayībhāvād ataḥ is one statement: its sense is that the sup after an a-final avyayībhāva does not take luk. Anukāma is an a-final

original p. 721

Rik 3: grammar

avyayībhāva; so by this statement the sup ending after it does not take luk. Am tv apañcamyāḥ is the second statement: its sense is that a sup other than the ablative after an a-final avyayībhāva takes am. So when the accusative or locative, other than the ablative, is put after anukāma, by the former statement they do not take luk, and by this statement the substitute am comes. Anukāma + am: by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the pūrvarūpa: anukāmam. By "samāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-223) (the last letter of a compound is udātta) anukāma is final udātta. The am is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau. The single substitute is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ". So anukāmam is final udātta.

तर्पयेथाम् (tarpayethām): the root tṛpa prīṇane. By "tatprayojako hetuś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-55) it is called hetu; by "hetumati ca" (Pā. sū. "3-1-26" [?]) ṇic. By "ṇicaś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-3-74) (when the fruit of the action goes to the agent, ātmanepada comes after a root ending in ṇic), in place of the loṭ after the ṇic-final root tṛp + i comes an ātmanepada suffix; when the 2nd dual is meant, āthām comes: tṛp + i + āthām. By "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79) e for the ṭi ām; by "āmetaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-90) (the e belonging to loṭ takes ām) ām: tṛp + i + āthām. With the ṇic as condition, the laghūpadha-guṇa for tṛp by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca, followed by r by uraṇ raparaḥ: tarpi + āthām; śap by kartari śap: tarpi + a + āthām. With the śap as condition, guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84); the substitute ay by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): tarpaya + āthām. Āthām is a sārvadhātuka without p; so by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it is ṅit. So by "āto ṅitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-81) (the ā belonging to a suffix marked with ṅ after a short a takes iy) iy for the ā: tarpaya + iy + thām. By "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) e for a and i: tarpayey + thām. Since the v-class letter [th, a val] follows, by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66) the y drops: tarpayethām. "Ato yeyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-80): here the word division is made in two ways, yā, iyaḥ, or yās, iyaḥ. In the second view, with yās + iya, ru for the s by sasajuṣo ruḥ, y for it by bhobhago…, and after the loss of y by lopaḥ śākalyasya, with yā + iya, the loss of y counts as not done, by pūrvatrāsiddham, when guṇa is to be made; so, though guṇa-sandhi does not come, since this is a ṛṣi's

original p. 722

Rik 3: grammar

usage, it may be said that the sandhi comes as an ārṣa form. In any case, whichever of the two ways is taken, the sense of the sūtra ato yeyaḥ is that yā or yās, part of a sārvadhātuka suffix after a short a, takes iya. In tarpa + ya + āthām there is no yā or yās; so this sūtra does not give iya here. So the account of the iya substitute by this sūtra [in the bhāṣya] may be called an oversight.

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā): the dvandva indraś ca varuṇaś ca indrāvaruṇā. Its explanation is at "indrāvaruṇayor aham" (Ṛ. saṃ. "1-12-1" [as read, ?; the mantra is 1-17-1, Ṛk 17.1 above]). Here after indravaruṇa the vocative dual au; for it ā by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); lengthening of like vowels: indrāvaruṇā. Since it stands at the start of a pāda, it is not wholly unaccented by the eighth-chapter rule; by the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" it is initial udātta, and in the Saṃhitā the ā is shortened.

रायः (rāyaḥ): the word rai means wealth; after it the genitive singular ṅas [as read; the letter may be ಜ, jas, ?]: rai + as; the substitute āy, ru and visarga. By "ūḍidaṃpadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-171) the ending is udātta.

ता (tā): after the word tad the accusative dual auṭ; for it, by supāṃ suluk, the substitute ā. By "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102) a for the d; by ato guṇe the pararūpa; lengthening of like vowels: tā.

वाम् (vām): this stands after a word; so for yuvām, ending in the accusative dual, by "yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-20) the unaccented substitute vām.

नेदिष्ठम् (nediṣṭham): the analysis is atiśayena antikam. By "atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau" (Pā. sū. 5-3-55) the suffix iṣṭhan: antika + iṣṭha. By "antikabāḍhayor nedasādhau" (Pā. sū. 5-3-63), when the suffixes iṣṭhan and īyasun follow, neda is substituted for antika and sādha for bāḍha; so neda: neda + iṣṭha; by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the a drops: nediṣṭha. The suffix iṣṭhan is nit; so nediṣṭha is initial udātta by ñnityādir nityam.

ईमहे (īmahe): the root īṅ gatau, ṅit; so by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12) the ātmanepada comes. Laṭ, 1st plural mahiṅ:

Page 723 (upper) — Rik 3: grammar (end)

ī + mahi; by ṭita ātmanepadānām e for the ṭi; by "divādibhyaḥ śyan" (Pā. sū. 3-1-69) śyan, and by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73) its luk: īmahe. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ it is wholly unaccented.

॥३॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यु॒वाकु॒ हि शची॑नां यु॒वाकु॑ सुमती॒नाम् । भू॒याम॑ वाज॒दाव्ना॑म् ॥४॥

yuvā́ku hí śácīnāṃ yuvā́ku sumatīnā́m | bhūyā́ma vājadā́vnām ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाकु । हि । शचीनाम् । युवाकु । सुऽमतीनाम् ॥ भूयाम । वाजऽदाव्नाम् ॥४॥

yuvāku | hi | śacīnām | yuvāku | su 'matīnām || bhūyāma | vāja 'dāvnām ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number ३-७७ is read with some doubt; the grammar page has "3-362" [?]. वसतीवर्येकधन… is as printed here; the Special Topics print …एकधाना….

हि यस्मात्कारणाच्छचीनामस्मदीयकर्मणां संबन्धि सोमरूपं हविर्युवाकु वसतीवर्येकधनात्मकैरुदकैः पयःसक्त्वादिद्रव्यान्तरैश्च मिश्रितम् । तथा सुमतीनां शोभनबुद्धियुक्तानामृत्विजां स्तोत्ररूपं वचनमपि युवाकु नानाविधैः स्तुत्यगुणैर्मिश्रितम् । तस्मात्कारणात् हे इन्द्रावरुणौ तथाविधं हविः स्वीकुर्वतोर्युवयोः प्रसादाद्वयं वाजदाव्नामन्नप्रदानां पुरुषाणां मध्ये मुख्या भूयाम । भवेम । अपोऽप्न इत्यादिषु षड्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु कर्मनामसु शचीशमीति पठितम् ॥ युवाकु । यु मिश्रणे । कटिकुषिभ्यां काकुः । उ. ३-७७ । इत्यत्र बाहुलकाद्यौतेरपि काकुः प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वेन गुणाभावादुकारस्योवङादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण मध्योदात्तत्वम् । शचीशब्दः केषांचिन्मते शार्ङ्गरवादिः । ङीनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पा. ४-१-७३ । इत्युभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदित्यत्र । का. ६-२-१४० । वृत्तिकृतोक्तम् । सुमतीनाम् । विद्याम सुमतीनाम् । ऋग्वे. १-४-३ । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । भूयाम । प्रार्थनायां लिङ् । उत्तमबहुवचने नित्यं ङित इति सकारलोपः । यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च । पा. ३-४-१०३ । इत्युदात्तो यासुडागमः । लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य । पा. ७-२-७९ । इति सकारलोपः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सतिशिष्टत्वाद्यासुडुदात्त एव शिष्यते । वाजदाव्नाम् । वाजं ददातीति वाजदावानः । आतो मनि-

hi yasmātkāraṇācchacīnāmasmadīyakarmaṇāṃ saṃbandhi somarūpaṃ haviryuvāku vasatīvaryekadhanātmakairudakaiḥ payaḥsaktvādidravyāntaraiśca miśritam | tathā sumatīnāṃ śobhanabuddhiyuktānāmṛtvijāṃ stotrarūpaṃ vacanamapi yuvāku nānāvidhaiḥ stutyaguṇairmiśritam | tasmātkāraṇāt he indrāvaruṇau tathāvidhaṃ haviḥ svīkurvatoryuvayoḥ prasādādvayaṃ vājadāvnāmannapradānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye mukhyā bhūyāma | bhavema | apo 'pna ityādiṣu ṣaḍviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu karmanāmasu śacīśamīti paṭhitam || yuvāku | yu miśraṇe | kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ | u. 3-77 | ityatra bāhulakādyauterapi kākuḥ pratyayaḥ | kittvena guṇābhāvādukārasyovaṅādeśaḥ | pratyayasvareṇa madhyodāttatvam | śacīśabdaḥ keṣāṃcinmate śārṅgaravādiḥ | ṅīnanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | pā. 4-1-73 | ityubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapadityatra | kā. 6-2-140 | vṛttikṛtoktam | sumatīnām | vidyāma sumatīnām | ṛgve. 1-4-3 | ityatroktam | bhūyāma | prārthanāyāṃ liṅ | uttamabahuvacane nityaṃ ṅita iti sakāralopaḥ | yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca | pā. 3-4-103 | ityudātto yāsuḍāgamaḥ | liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya | pā. 7-2-79 | iti sakāralopaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | satiśiṣṭatvādyāsuḍudātta eva śiṣyate | vājadāvnām | vājaṃ dadātīti vājadāvānaḥ | āto mani-

न्नित्यादिना वनिप् । तस्य पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । अल्लोपोऽनः । पा. ६-४-१३४ । इत्यकारलोपः । तस्याचः परस्मिन्निति स्थानिवद्भावाल्लोपो व्योर्वलीति वकारलोपो न भवति ॥

nnityādinā vanip | tasya pittvāddhātusvara eva śiṣyate | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | allopo 'naḥ | pā. 6-4-134 | ityakāralopaḥ | tasyācaḥ parasminniti sthānivadbhāvāllopo vyorvalīti vakāralopo na bhavati ||

Translation: "Because the oblation in the form of soma belonging to śacīnām, our rites, is yuvāku, mixed with waters, the vasatīvarī and ekadhana, and with other substances such as milk and barley meal; and likewise the speech in the form of praise of the priests sumatīnām, with good minds, is yuvāku, mixed with various qualities to be praised; for that reason, O Indra and Varuṇa, by the grace of you two who accept such an oblation, may we bhūyāma, become, chief among vājadāvnām, men who give food. Śacī is read among the twenty-six action words beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ." (Grammatical tail: yuvāku, yu miśraṇe, the suffix kāku of kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ (Uṇ. 3-77 [?]) after yu too by bāhulaka, no guṇa as it is kit, uvaṅ for the u, middle udātta by the suffix accent; śacī, in some views of the śārṅgarava-ādi, ending in ṅīn, initial udātta as nit (Pā. 4-1-73), as the Vṛtti says on ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat (Kā. 6-2-140); sumatīnām, explained at Ṛgveda 1-4-3; bhūyāma, liṅ of prayer, the s lost by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ, the udātta augment yāsuṭ by Pā. 3-4-103, the s lost by Pā. 7-2-79, śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, the udātta of yāsuṭ stays as satiśiṣṭa; vājadāvnām, "they give vāja", vanip by āto maninn…, the root accent as it is pit, which stays in the compound by the accent of the kṛt final member; the a lost by Pā. 6-4-134, and since that loss is sthānivat by acaḥ parasmin, the v is not lost by lopo vyor vali.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हि (hi) — because | शचीनाम् (śacīnām) — of the rites (we perform) (the oblation in the form of soma belonging to them) | युवाकु (yuvāku) — is joined with substances such as milk and barley meal | सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām) — of those with pure minds (the praise of the priests) | युवाकु (yuvāku) — is joined with the various qualities (that hymns should have) (so we) | वाजदाव्नाम् (vājadāvnām) — among those who give food (oblations) (as foremost) | भूयाम (bhūyāma) — may we be (by the grace of you who have accepted the oblation we gave).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

What we offer you as oblation is joined with substances such as milk and barley meal, and the priests praise you as possessed of various excellent qualities. Pleased by both, you should make us chief, or best, among the givers of food.

॥ English Translation ॥

The mingled libations of our pious rites, the different praises of our right-minded priests are prepared; may we be included among the givers of food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Yuvāku:

वसतीवर्येकधानात्मकैरुदकैः पयःसक्त्वादिद्रव्यान्तरैश्च मिश्रितम् ।

vasatīvaryekadhānātmakairudakaiḥ payaḥsaktvādidravyāntaraiśca miśritam |

The commentator here explains this word as the oblation made ready for the homa by mixing water, milk and barley meal (flour). For the word yuvāku in its second occurrence he explains it as a mixture of hymns, or a collection of various hymns. Further, in the ṛk

अश्विना मधुषुत्तमो युवाकुः सोमस्तं पातमा गतं दुरोणे । (ऋ. सं. ३-५८-९)

aśvinā madhuṣuttamo yuvākuḥ somastaṃ pātamā gataṃ duroṇe | (ṛ. saṃ. 3-58-9)

("Aśvins, the soma sweetest-pressed is yuvāku; drink it, come to the house": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 725

Rik 4: Special Topics

for the word yuvākuḥ in it,

युवां कामयमानो वर्तते । यद्वा युवाकुर्वसतीवरीप्रभृतिभिर्मिश्रित इत्यर्थः ॥

yuvāṃ kāmayamāno vartate | yadvā yuvākurvasatīvarīprabhṛtibhirmiśrita ityarthaḥ ||

("It is there desiring you two; or, yuvākuḥ means mixed with the vasatīvarī waters and the rest.") That is, he gives both the sense "desiring you, or wanted by you" and the sense of mixing stated above. Further:

ता विद्वांसा हवामहे वां ता नो विद्वांसा मन्म वोचेतमद्य । प्रार्चद्दयमानो युवाकुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१२०-३)

tā vidvāṃsā havāmahe vāṃ tā no vidvāṃsā manma vocetamadya | prārcaddayamāno yuvākuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-120-3)

("We call on you two, the wise ones; may you two, the wise, speak to us today a thought; the one desiring you, praising, worshipping …": editorial and tentative.)

डुहीयन्मित्रधितये युवाकु राये च नो मिमीतं वाजवत्यै । (ऋ. सं. १-१२०-९)

ḍuhīyanmitradhitaye yuvāku rāye ca no mimītaṃ vājavatyai | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-120-9)

("… desiring you, for the setting of a friend; measure out for us wealth rich in strength": editorial and tentative.)

धामानि मित्रावरुणा युवाकुः सं यो यूथेव जनिमानि चष्टे । (ऋ. सं. ७-६०-३)

dhāmāni mitrāvaruṇā yuvākuḥ saṃ yo yūtheva janimāni caṣṭe | (ṛ. saṃ. 7-60-3)

("Mitra and Varuṇa, the one desiring you, who surveys the abodes, the races, like herds": editorial and tentative.)

अवोर्वां नूनमश्विना युवाकुर्हुवे यद्वां सुते माध्वी वसूयुः । (ऋ. सं. ७-६७-४)

avorvāṃ nūnamaśvinā yuvākurhuve yadvāṃ sute mādhvī vasūyuḥ | (ṛ. saṃ. 7-67-4)

("… Aśvins, the one desiring you, I call, when at your pressing, O sweet ones, seeking goods": editorial and tentative.)

उत त्यं भुज्युमश्विना सखायो मध्ये जहुर्दुरेवासः समुद्रे । निरीं पर्षदरावा यो युवाकुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-६८-७)

uta tyaṃ bhujyumaśvinā sakhāyo madhye jahurdurevāsaḥ samudre | nirīṃ parṣadarāvā yo yuvākuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 7-68-7)

("And that Bhujyu, Aśvins, his ill-going companions left in the middle of the sea; the hostile one who is yours shall bring him across": editorial and tentative.)

In these ṛks the commentator gives for the word yuvākuḥ the sense yuvāṃ kāmayamānaḥ, desiring you, or wanted by you. Yet it seems the word should have some definite sense. डुहीयन् and अवोर्वां are as read; the first letters are not clear [?].

Śacīnām: since the word śacī is read among the fifty-seven words for speech, ślokaḥ, dharā and so on (Ni. "2-23" [as read, ?]), śacī means speech. And since it is read among the twenty-six action-names, apaḥ, apnaḥ and so on (Ni. "3-2" [as read, ?]), it also means action. Since it is read among the eleven names of intelligence, ketaḥ, ketu and so on (Ni. "3-13" [as read, ?]), it also means intelligence. So though the word śacī has three senses, speech, action and intelligence, here the commentator has given first place to the sense action. Yāska too,

त्रयः केशिन ऋतुथा विचक्षते संवत्सरे वपत एक एषाम् । विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्ध्राजिरेकस्य ददृशे न रूपम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-४४)

trayaḥ keśina ṛtuthā vicakṣate saṃvatsare vapata eka eṣām | viśvameko abhi caṣṭe śacībhirdhrājirekasya dadṛśe na rūpam || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-44)

("Three long-haired ones look out in season; one of them shears in the year; one surveys all with his powers; of one the rush is seen, not the form": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 726

Rik 4: Special Topics (end) and grammar

explaining this ṛk, for viśvam eko abhi caṣṭe śacībhiḥ

सर्वमेकोऽभिविपश्यति कर्मभिरादित्यः

sarvameko 'bhivipaśyati karmabhirādityaḥ

("The one, the Sun, looks over all with his actions", Ni. "12-27" [?]), gives the word śacī the sense action. In giving the sense of the present ṛk, any one of the three senses of śacī may be taken.

Sumatīnām:

शोभनबुद्धियुक्तानामृत्विजाम् ।

śobhanabuddhiyuktānāmṛtvijām |

("Of the priests with good minds.") Of the priests who are well endowed with intelligence, or of intelligent people.

Vājadāvnām:

वाजमन्नं ददतीति वाजदावानस्तेषाम् ।

vājamannaṃ dadatīti vājadāvānasteṣām |

("They give vāja, food: of them.") To give the sense "chief among those who give food or oblations (who offer them)", the commentator has supplied the word "chief". On the whole the sense of this ṛk is very tangled; the sense is not clear.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 726–727, noted briefly

युवाकु (yuvāku): the root yu miśraṇe. "Kaṭikuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "3-362" [?]): the sense of this sūtra is that the suffix kāku comes after the roots kaṭe varṣāvaraṇayoḥ and kuṣa niṣkarṣe. Some read this sūtra as kaṭhi kuṣibhyāṃ kākuḥ; in their view the root kaṭha kṛcchrajīvane is to be taken. Here Ujjvaladatta, keeping the reading kaṭikaṣibhyām, says the root kaṣa śiṣa read in the daṇḍaka is meant, and shows the example kaṣākuḥ. Kuṣākuḥ conflicts with the Medinī-kośa "kapivahnyarke" [as printed]. Be that as it may: here, by the word bahula, the suffix kāku comes after the root yu too. The k of the suffix is it, so no guṇa. Yu + āku: by "aci śnudhātu…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) the substitute uvaṅ: yuvāku. By "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3) the ā at the start of the suffix is udātta; so yuvāku is middle udātta.

शचीनाम् (śacīnām): "śacīśabdaḥ keṣāṃcin mate śārṅgaravādiḥ ṅīnantaḥ, nittvād ādyudāttaḥ", says the Vṛttikāra on "ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat" (Pā. sū. 6-2-140). Some say that, since śacī is read among the words of the śārṅgarava-ādi group, the suffix ṅīn comes; the suffix is ñit, so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) the suffix-final śacī is initial udātta: so the Kāśikā Vṛttikāra says in the sūtra ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat. So the word śacī is initial udātta.

सुमतीनाम् (sumatīnām): this is explained at "vidyāma sumatīnām" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-4-3).

original p. 727

Rik 4: grammar (end)

भूयाम (bhūyāma): the root bhū sattāyām. After it, in the sense of prayer, liṅ; 1st plural mas: bhū + mas. By "nityaṃ ṅitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-99) the s drops. By "yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-103) the augment yāsuṭ for the liṅ; being ṭit, it comes as the first part by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46): bhū + yās + ma. By "liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya" (Pā. sū. 7-2-79) (the non-final s belonging to a liṅ called sārvadhātuka drops) the s drops: bhū + yāma. The vikaraṇa śap, come by kartari śap, takes luk by bahulaṃ chandasi. The udātta enjoined for the augment yāsuṭ is satiśiṣṭa; by "satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvaṃ ca" (Pā. Ma. 6-1-158), being the stronger, it alone stays.

वाजदाव्नाम् (vājadāvnām): vājaṃ dadati iti vājadāvānaḥ. With vāja, denoting the object, as upapada, after the root dāñ, by "āto maninkvanibvanipaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-74) (after an ā-final root, in the Veda, the suffixes manin, kvanip and vanip come, whether a subanta or a preverb is the upapada) vanip comes: vāja + am + dā + van. This is a kṛdanta; by kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca it is called prātipadika; by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ luk for the am. Vanip being pit, it is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau; dā is udātta by the root accent. After vāja is compounded with the kṛdanta dāvan by "upapadam atiṅ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-19), by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. "9-2-139" [as printed, for 6-2-139]) the accent of the kṛt final member comes and stays. After it the genitive plural ām: vājadāvan + ām. The part before this suffix is called bha by "yaci bham" (Pā. sū. 1-4-18). By "allopo 'naḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-134) (the short a of an an that is part of the aṅga and stands immediately before a y- or vowel-initial svādi suffix not called sarvanāmasthāna drops) the a of the final an in vājadāvan drops: vājadāv + n + ām. Now, since the val n follows, the loss of v would come by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66). But the a-loss that has come here is sthānivat by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57): the sense of this sūtra is that a substitute that has come in place of a vowel, conditioned by what follows, is treated as the original when an operation is made on what is seen before the original. Here the original is a, what is seen before it is v; when the loss operation is made on it, the loss, which came in place of the vowel a and is conditioned by the following ām, is sthānivat; that is, it is as if the original were there. So, because the a intervenes, the v is not dropped by lopo vyor vali: vājadāvnām.

Sūkta 17, Rik 5 (metre pādanicṛt)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः॑ सहस्र॒दाव्नां॑ वरु॑णः॒ शंस्या॑नाम् । क्रतु॑र्भवत्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥५॥

índraḥ sahasradā́vnāṃ váruṇaḥ śáṃsyānām | krátur bhavaty ukthyaḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः । सहस्रऽदाव्नाम् । वरुणः । शंस्यानाम् ॥ क्रतुः । भवति । उक्थ्यः ॥५॥

indraḥ | sahasra 'dāvnām | varuṇaḥ | śaṃsyānām || kratuḥ | bhavati | ukthyaḥ ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ येयमिति is as printed; the Kannada on p. 731 has जेयम्. छान्दस्यान्न is as printed, probably for छान्दसत्वान्न [?]. ॥३२॥ closes Varga 32.

अयमिन्द्रः सहस्रदाव्नां सहस्रसंख्याकधनप्रदानां मध्ये क्रतुर्धनदानस्य कर्ता भवति । प्रभूतं ददातीत्यर्थः । तथा वरुणः शंस्यानां स्तुत्यानां मध्य उक्थ्यः स्तुत्यो भवति । अतिशयेन स्तुत्य इत्यर्थः ॥ वरुणः उनन्प्रत्ययो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । शंस्यानाम् । शंसु स्तुतौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । तित्स्वरितमिति प्राप्ते ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यत इत्याद्युदात्तः । क्रतुः । कृञः कतुः । उ. १-७८ । इति कतुः । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावे यणादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणाद्युदात्तः । उक्थ्यः । उक्थं शस्त्रम् । तेन स्तुत्यत्वेन तत्र भव उक्थ्यः । भवे छन्दसि । पा. ४-४-११० । इति यत् । यस्येति लोपः । अत्र तित्स्वरितमित्येतद्बाधित्वा तीर्थ्याय कूप्यायेत्यादिवत् द्व्यच्त्वाद्यतोऽनाव इति प्राप्तमाद्युदात्तत्वं सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न क्रियते । ननु यस्येति लोपात्प्रागेव तित्स्वरितत्वमस्तु न हि तदा यतोऽनाव इत्येतदस्ति द्व्यच्त्वाभावात् । अत एव ह्यूर्म्याय च सूर्म्याय चेत्यादौ स्वरितत्वं दृश्यते । न च परत्वान्नित्यत्वाच्च यस्येति लोपेन प्रथमतो भाव्यमिति वाच्यम् । प्रकृतिप्रत्ययाश्रयाद्बहिरङ्गाद्यस्येति लोपात्प्रत्ययमात्राश्रयतयान्तरङ्गत्वेन तित्स्वरितमित्येतस्य प्राबल्यात् । अत ऊर्म्यायेत्यादिवदुक्थ्य इत्यत्रापि लक्षणत एव स्वरितत्वं भविष्यतीति किं छान्दसत्वेन । यत्र हि लोपमन्तरेणैव द्व्यच्त्वं तत्र यतोऽनाव इत्येतद्भवति । यथा चेयं येयमिति । लोपनिबन्धनद्व्यच्त्वप्रदेशेषु तु स्वरितेनैव भवितव्यमिति । एवं तर्हि तीर्थ्याय कूप्यायेत्यादौ यदाद्युदात्तत्वं तदेव छान्दसमस्तु । अथात्र तु वर्णादाङ्गं बलीयः । परि. ५५ । इत्यन्तरङ्गत्वेऽपि स्वरितत्वं बाधित्वा लोप एव भविष्यति । तर्ह्युक्थ्य ऊर्म्याय सूर्म्यायेत्यादौ च छान्दसमस्तु । सर्वथैकत्र छान्दस्यान्न मुच्यते ॥३२॥

ayamindraḥ sahasradāvnāṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākadhanapradānāṃ madhye kraturdhanadānasya kartā bhavati | prabhūtaṃ dadātītyarthaḥ | tathā varuṇaḥ śaṃsyānāṃ stutyānāṃ madhya ukthyaḥ stutyo bhavati | atiśayena stutya ityarthaḥ || varuṇaḥ unanpratyayo nittvādādyudāttaḥ | śaṃsyānām | śaṃsu stutau | ṛhalorṇyat | titsvaritamiti prāpte īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyata ityādyudāttaḥ | kratuḥ | kṛñaḥ katuḥ | u. 1-78 | iti katuḥ | kittvādguṇābhāve yaṇādeśaḥ | pratyayasvareṇādyudāttaḥ | ukthyaḥ | ukthaṃ śastram | tena stutyatvena tatra bhava ukthyaḥ | bhave chandasi | pā. 4-4-110 | iti yat | yasyeti lopaḥ | atra titsvaritamityetadbādhitvā tīrthyāya kūpyāyetyādivat dvyactvādyato 'nāva iti prāptamādyudāttatvaṃ sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti na kriyate | nanu yasyeti lopātprāgeva titsvaritatvamastu na hi tadā yato 'nāva ityetadasti dvyactvābhāvāt | ata eva hyūrmyāya ca sūrmyāya cetyādau svaritatvaṃ dṛśyate | na ca paratvānnityatvācca yasyeti lopena prathamato bhāvyamiti vācyam | prakṛtipratyayāśrayādbahiraṅgādyasyeti lopātpratyayamātrāśrayatayāntaraṅgatvena titsvaritamityetasya prābalyāt | ata ūrmyāyetyādivadukthya ityatrāpi lakṣaṇata eva svaritatvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti kiṃ chāndasatvena | yatra hi lopamantareṇaiva dvyactvaṃ tatra yato 'nāva ityetadbhavati | yathā ceyaṃ yeyamiti | lopanibandhanadvyactvapradeśeṣu tu svaritenaiva bhavitavyamiti | evaṃ tarhi tīrthyāya kūpyāyetyādau yadādyudāttatvaṃ tadeva chāndasamastu | athātra tu varṇādāṅgaṃ balīyaḥ | pari. 55 | ityantaraṅgatve 'pi svaritatvaṃ bādhitvā lopa eva bhaviṣyati | tarhyukthya ūrmyāya sūrmyāyetyādau ca chāndasamastu | sarvathaikatra chāndasyānna mucyate ||32||

Translation: "This Indra, among the sahasradāvan, givers of wealth by thousands, is kratu, the doer of the giving of wealth: that is, he gives abundantly. Likewise Varuṇa, among the śaṃsya, those to be praised, is ukthya, praiseworthy: that is, praiseworthy in the highest degree." (Grammatical tail: varuṇaḥ, in unan, initial udātta as nit; śaṃsyānām, śaṃsu stutau, ṇyat by ṛhalor ṇyat, the svarita due by tit svaritam replaced by initial udātta by īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ; kratuḥ, katu by kṛñaḥ katuḥ (Uṇ. 1-78), no guṇa as it is kit, yaṇ, initial udātta by the suffix accent; ukthyaḥ, "uktha is the śastra; being praised by it, he is bhava, there", yat by bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110), the loss by yasyeti. Here the initial udātta, due as in tīrthyāya, kūpyāya by yato 'nāvaḥ because there are two vowels, overriding tit svaritam, is not made, since all rules are optional in the Veda. The objection follows: let the svarita of tit svaritam come before the loss, when yato 'nāvaḥ has no scope, there not being two vowels; hence the svarita in ūrmyāya ca sūrmyāya ca; nor may one say that the loss comes first as later and nitya, since tit svaritam, depending on the suffix alone, is antaraṅga and stronger than the loss, which depends on base and suffix; so in ukthya too the svarita comes by rule, like ūrmyāya, and why appeal to the Veda? Yato 'nāvaḥ applies where there are two vowels without a loss, as in ceyam, jeyam; where the two vowels depend on the loss, there must be svarita. Then let the initial udātta in tīrthyāya, kūpyāya be the Vedic one. Or, here, by "a rule of the aṅga is stronger than one of letters" (paribhāṣā 55), the loss will override the svarita even though that is antaraṅga; then let ukthya, ūrmyāya, sūrmyāya be Vedic. In every way one does not escape Vedic licence in one place.)

original p. 729

Rik 5: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(अयम् (ayam)) इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra (who accepts the oblations and the rest mentioned above and brings us good) | सहस्रदाव्नाम् (sahasradāvnām) — among those who give (wealth) by thousands | क्रतुः (kratuḥ) — the doer (of the giving of wealth) | भवति (bhavati) — becomes | वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa | शंस्यानाम् (śaṃsyānām) — among those who are praised | उक्थ्यः (ukthyaḥ) — praiseworthy (especially) | भवति (bhavati) — becomes.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Indra, satisfied as described before, gives us as much wealth as we need. In the same way Varuṇa too is especially praised by us.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra is a giver among the givers of thousands; Varuna is to be praised among those who deserve to be praised.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

If the sense given above for this ṛk is changed slightly, the intent fits well: Indra is renowned among those who give wealth and the like by thousands, and Varuṇa among those who are greatly praised; their deeds are worthy of praise.

Kratuḥ: since the word kratu is read among the twenty-six action-names, apaḥ, apnaḥ and so on (Ni. "3-2" [as read, ?]), kratu means action: here, the daring deed that Indra and Varuṇa do, or the deed of giving wealth and the like to people.

Ukthyaḥ:

उक्थं शस्त्रम् । तेन स्तुत्यत्वेन तत्र भव उक्थ्यः ।

ukthaṃ śastram | tena stutyatvena tatra bhava ukthyaḥ |

("Uktha is the śastra; being praised by it, he who is there is ukthya.") Uktha means the śastra mantra; ukthya means fit to be praised by reciting that mantra. Here the intent is that the deed of Indra and Varuṇa in giving wealth and the like is praiseworthy.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 729–732, noted briefly

वरुणः (varuṇaḥ): formed with the suffix unan after the root vṛ by "kṝvṝdāribhya unan" (Uṇ. sū. "3-53" [?]). Initial udātta by the nit accent.

original p. 730

Rik 5: grammar

शंस्यानाम् (śaṃsyānām): the root śaṃsu stutau. By "ṛhalor ṇyat" (Pā. sū. 3-1-124) ṇyat comes. By "tit svaritam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-185) svarita is due; but by its exception "īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-214) śaṃsya, ending in the suffix ṇyat, is initial udātta.

क्रतुः (kratuḥ): by "kṛñaḥ katuḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "1-77" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 1-78) the suffix katu comes after ḍukṛñ karaṇe. So after the root kṛ the suffix katu; by laśakv ataddhite the k at the start of the suffix is called it and dropped; the suffix being kit, guṇa does not come. By "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) the substitute yaṇ, that is, r for ṛ: kratu. This is final udātta by the suffix accent [as printed; the bhāṣya says initial udātta].

उक्थ्यः (ukthyaḥ): uktha means śastra. The yājñikas give the definition of śastra as

अप्रगीतमन्त्रसाध्यगुणिनिष्ठगुणाभिधानं शस्त्रम्

apragītamantrasādhyaguṇiniṣṭhaguṇābhidhānaṃ śastram

("Śastra is the declaration of the qualities residing in the one who has them, accomplished by mantras not sung.") Varuṇa is praised by this śastra. If the analysis ukthe bhavaḥ is made, by "bhave chandasi" (Pā. sū. 4-4-110) (after a locative-final, in the sense bhava, the suffix yat comes) yat comes; luk for the locative singular suffix inside the stem: uktha + ya. By "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) (when ī or a taddhita follows, the i and a belonging to an aṅga called bha drop) the a drops when the taddhita yat follows: ukthya. The suffix yat has t as it; so by "tit svaritam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-185) (the last letter of a suffix with t as it is svarita) the svarita comes. Although here the yat-final ukthya has two vowels (ac), and so, just as initial udātta comes in tīrthya of tīrthyāya and kūpya of kūpyāya by "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-213), the exception to tit svaritam (a two-vowel word ending in a yat enjoined after a word other than nau is initial udātta), initial udātta would be due here too by yato 'nāvaḥ; yet by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (paribhāṣā 35) (in the Veda all rules are optional) yato 'nāvaḥ too is optional, so it does not come here.

But with uktha + ya, let the svarita of tit svaritam come first, before the loss of a by yasyeti ca. Now, since there are three vowels, the exception yato 'nāvaḥ has no scope at all. Yet yasyeti ca is read later than tit svaritam in the Aṣṭādhyāyī; so by "vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam" (Pā. sū. 1-4-2) the later loss by yasyeti must come first. Moreover, yasyeti ca is nitya, that is kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgī: whether the rule tit svaritam

original p. 731

Rik 5: grammar

has applied or not, it comes. Tit svaritam comes if the loss by yasyeti ca has not come; if the loss has come, it is overridden by yato 'nāvaḥ and does not come; so it is not kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgī. (By the paribhāṣā

यस्य च लक्षणान्तरेण निमित्तं विहन्यते तदप्यनित्यम्

yasya ca lakṣaṇāntareṇa nimittaṃ vihanyate tadapyanityam

("That too whose condition is destroyed by another rule is not nitya"), its non-nitya status is established here.) So it is not nitya. Thus, being nitya and being later, yasyeti ca is the stronger; so it may be said that the loss must come first by yasyeti ca, and tit svaritam has no room. Yet tit svaritam depends on the suffix alone, so it needs little, or is not conditioned by what follows, and is antaraṅga; yasyeti ca comes relying on both base and suffix, so it needs much, or is conditioned by what follows, and is bahiraṅga. By "paranityāntaraṅgāpavādānām uttarottaraṃ balīyaḥ" (paribhāṣā 38) the antaraṅga rule is stronger than both the later and the nitya. So by "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" (paribhāṣā 50), when the antaraṅga tit svaritam is made, the bahiraṅga yasyeti ca counts as not done. So tit svaritam comes first, before yasyeti ca. That is why the svarita stands in places such as ūrmyāya ca sūrmyāya ca. In the same way in ukthya the svarita is established by Pāṇini's sūtra itself. That being so, why establish the svarita in ukthya by relying on the paribhāṣā sarve vidhayaś chandasi? If it is said that the sūtra yato 'nāvaḥ has scope where there is a yat-final of two vowels without the loss by yasyeti ca, in places such as ceyam, jeyam, and that in instances where two vowels are got after the loss, svarita alone is right; if the svarita is justified here in this proper way, then in tīrthya and kūpya too, since there are two vowels after the loss, svarita ought to come; so it must be said that initial udātta comes there as a Vedic form. For this there is "vārṇād āṅgaṃ balīyaḥ" (paribhāṣā 55): a rule in the section on the aṅga is stronger than a rule conditioned by letters. Yasyeti ca, being in the aṅga section, is stronger than tit svaritam. So first the loss of a by yasyeti ca, then initial udātta is established by yato 'nāvaḥ, the exception to tit svaritam; it may be said that here no Vedic form need be stated. Then in instances such as ukthyaḥ, ūrmyāya, sūrmyāya, the svarita must be justified by saying that yato 'nāvaḥ does not apply, as a Vedic form. In every way one must accept Vedic licence in some one place. If the svarita in ukthya, sūrmya and the rest is justified as established by the śāstra, the initial udātta in tīrthya and the rest must be justified as Vedic. If the initial udātta in places such as tīrthya is justified as established by the śāstra,

Page 732 (upper) — Rik 5: grammar (end)

the svarita in places such as ukthya, sūrmya must be justified as Vedic. In any case one cannot escape stating Vedic licence in one of the two places.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under यो, व (वयं), स and म (सनेम) and प्र; strokes over व (अवसा), च and रे. The bar under यो and the absence of marks on धीमहि are as printed.

तयो॒रिदव॑सा व॒यं स॒नेम॒ नि च॑ धीमहि । [accent ?] स्यादु॒त प्र॒रे॑चनम् ॥६॥ [accent ?]

tayor íd ávasā vayáṃ sanéma ní ca dhīmahi | [accent ?] syād utá prarécanam ||6|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तयोः । इत् । अवसा । वयम् । सनेम । नि । च । धीमहि ॥ स्यात् । उत । प्रऽरेचनम् ॥६॥

tayoḥ | it | avasā | vayam | sanema | ni | ca | dhīmahi || syāt | uta | pra 'recanam ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

तयोरित्थंविधयोरिन्द्रावरुणयोरेवावसा रक्षणेन वयमनुष्ठातारः सनेम । संभजेम धनमिति शेषः । नि धीमहि च । प्राप्ते धने यावदपेक्षितं तावद्भुक्त्वा ततोऽवशिष्टं धनं क्वचिन्निधिरूपेण स्थापयामश्च । उतापि च प्ररेचनं भुक्तान्निहिताच्च प्रकर्षेणाधिकं धनं स्यात् । संपद्यताम् ॥ अवसा । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वयम् । यूयं हि ष्ठा । ऋग्वे. १-१५-२ । इत्यत्र यदुक्तं तदत्र द्रष्टव्यम् । सनेम । आशिषि लिङ् । तस्य मस् । नित्यं ङित इति सकारलोपः । किदाशिषि । पा. ३-४-१०४ । इति यासुट् । छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकमप्यस्तीति लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्येति सकारलोपः । अतो येय इतीयादेशः । लोपो व्योर्वलीति यलोपः । लिङ्याशिष्यङ् । पा. ३-१-८६ । इत्यङ् । आद्गुणः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । धीमहि । डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः । आशिषि लिङो महिङ् । तस्य छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकसंज्ञे । तत्र सार्वधातुकत्वेन लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्येति सकारलोपः । सार्वधातुकमपिदिति ङित्वं शप् च । बहुलं छन्दसीति जुहोत्यादेरपि शपो लुक् । आर्धधातुकत्वादातो लोप इटि च । पा. ६-४-६४ ।

tayoritthaṃvidhayorindrāvaruṇayorevāvasā rakṣaṇena vayamanuṣṭhātāraḥ sanema | saṃbhajema dhanamiti śeṣaḥ | ni dhīmahi ca | prāpte dhane yāvadapekṣitaṃ tāvadbhuktvā tato 'vaśiṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ kvacinnidhirūpeṇa sthāpayāmaśca | utāpi ca prarecanaṃ bhuktānnihitācca prakarṣeṇādhikaṃ dhanaṃ syāt | saṃpadyatām || avasā | asun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | vayam | yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā | ṛgve. 1-15-2 | ityatra yaduktaṃ tadatra draṣṭavyam | sanema | āśiṣi liṅ | tasya mas | nityaṃ ṅita iti sakāralopaḥ | kidāśiṣi | pā. 3-4-104 | iti yāsuṭ | chandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukamapyastīti liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasyeti sakāralopaḥ | ato yeya itīyādeśaḥ | lopo vyorvalīti yalopaḥ | liṅyāśiṣyaṅ | pā. 3-1-86 | ityaṅ | ādguṇaḥ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | dhīmahi | ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | āśiṣi liṅo mahiṅ | tasya chandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukārdhadhātukasaṃjñe | tatra sārvadhātukatvena liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasyeti sakāralopaḥ | sārvadhātukamapiditi ṅitvaṃ śap ca | bahulaṃ chandasīti juhotyāderapi śapo luk | ārdhadhātukatvādāto lopa iṭi ca | pā. 6-4-64 |
