Rik 6: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

इत्याकारलोपः । निघातः । सनेमेत्यपेक्षया द्वितीयत्वादत्र चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निषेधः । स्यात् । अस्तेः । प्रार्थनायां लिङ् । तिप् । इतश्चेतीकारलोपः । यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्चेति यासुड्ङित्त्वे । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । पादादित्वादनिघातः । उत । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तः । प्ररेचनम् । रिचिर् विरेचने । भावे ल्युट् । योरनादेशः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । प्रादिसमासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

ityākāralopaḥ | nighātaḥ | sanemetyapekṣayā dvitīyatvādatra cavāyoge prathameti na niṣedhaḥ | syāt | asteḥ | prārthanāyāṃ liṅ | tip | itaścetīkāralopaḥ | yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicceti yāsuḍṅittve | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | śnasorallopa ityakāralopaḥ | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | uta | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttaḥ | prarecanam | ricir virecane | bhāve lyuṭ | yoranādeśaḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | prādisamāsaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "By the avas, protection, of those very two, Indra and Varuṇa, such as they are, may we, the performers, sanema, obtain (wealth, is understood); and ni dhīmahi, store it: of the wealth obtained, having enjoyed as much as is wanted, we put the rest away somewhere as a treasure. Uta, and also, may there be prarecanam, wealth exceeding by far what was enjoyed and stored: may it come about." (Grammatical tail: avasā, asun, initial udātta as nit; vayam, as said at yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā (Ṛgveda 1-15-2); sanema, āśīr-liṅ, mas, the s lost by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ, yāsuṭ by kid āśiṣi (Pā. 3-4-104), and, since by chandasy ubhayathā it is also sārvadhātuka, the s lost by liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya, iy by ato yeyaḥ, y lost by lopo vyor vali, aṅ by Pā. 3-1-86, guṇa, not lowered at the start of the pāda; dhīmahi, ḍudhāñ, mahiṅ for āśīr-liṅ, both names by chandasy ubhayathā, the s lost as sārvadhātuka, ṅit by sārvadhātukam apit, and śap, dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi as for the juhoty-ādi, the ā lost as ārdhadhātuka by Pā. 6-4-64, wholly unaccented: being second relative to sanema, the bar cavāyoge prathamā does not apply; syāt, liṅ of prayer after as, tip, the i lost by itaś ca, yāsuṭ udātta and ṅit, śap dropped, the a lost by śnasor allopaḥ, not lowered at the start of the pāda; uta, final udātta by evam-ādīnām antaḥ; prarecanam, ricir virecane, lyuṭ of the action, ana for yu, udātta before the suffix by liti, a prādi compound, the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

तयोः (tayoḥ) — of those Indra and Varuṇa | अवसा इत् (avasā it) — by protection alone | वयम् (vayam) — we (the performers) | सनेम (sanema) — may we gather (wealth) | नि धीमहि च (ni dhīmahi ca) — and may we store it and lay it by | उत (uta) — and | (that wealth) प्ररेचनम् (prarecanam) — more (than what we enjoyed and stored) | स्यात् (syāt) — may it be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ the heading is misprinted ॥ ಪದಪಾಠಃ ॥ [sic]

By the grace of Indra and Varuṇa may we gather boundless wealth, enjoy it as we wish and store what remains; and however much we enjoy, may that wealth keep growing.

॥ English Translation ॥

Through their protection we enjoy riches and heap them up ; still may we have even a surplus.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Ni dhīmahi: let us store it, let us heap it up, "lay by".

Uta: "not only that", or "and": either sense may be taken.

Prarecanam:

भुक्तान्निहिताच्च प्रकर्षेणाधिकं धनम् ।

bhuktānnihitācca prakarṣeṇādhikaṃ dhanam |

("Wealth exceeding by far what was enjoyed and stored.") Wealth more than what we enjoyed as we wished and heaped up: that is, the intent is that the wealth Indra and Varuṇa give should grow greater by their favour.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 733–735, noted briefly

अवसा (avasā): by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]) the suffix asun after the root av; initial udātta by the nit accent; it ends in the instrumental singular.

original p. 734

Rik 6: grammar

वयम् (vayam): the derivation stated for yūyam in the mantra "yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-15-2) is to be stated for vayam too. In yūyam the base is yuṣmad; in vayam the base is asmad: only that is the difference.

सनेम (sanema): the root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ. After it āśīr-liṅ, 1st plural mas: san + mas; by "nityaṃ ṅitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-99) the s of mas drops. By "yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-103) the augment yāsuṭ; being ṭit, it comes as the first part by ādyantau ṭakitau. By "kid āśiṣi" (Pā. sū. 3-4-104) it becomes kit; it was said before that this is not the rule enjoining the augment yāsuṭ. San + yās + ma: by "chandasy ubhayathā" (Pā. sū. 3-4-117) yāsma has both names, sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka. So, putting the sārvadhātuka name first, the s drops; by "liṅy āśiṣy aṅ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-86), when a liṅ of blessing follows, aṅ comes after the root: san + a + yā + ma. By "ato yeyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-80) iy for yā: sana + iy + ma; by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66) the y drops; by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) guṇa: sanema. Since it stands at the start of the pāda, it is not made unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; the single substitute e stays udātta.

धीमहि (dhīmahi): the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ. Liṅ in the sense of blessing; by liṅaḥ sīyuṭ the augment sīyuṭ; 1st plural mahiṅ; by chandasy ubhayathā it has the sārvadhātuka name too. Since it has the sārvadhātuka name, by liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya the s of sīyuṭ drops, and by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it is ṅit. Śap comes by kartari śap; but by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73) the root dhāñ, being of the juhoty-ādi class, takes luk. Or it may be said that, taking the ārdhadhātuka name when śap is to be made, śap does not come. Dhā + īy + mahi: having the ārdhadhātuka name, by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-64) the ā drops; by lopo vyor vali the y drops: dhīmahi. Here, since the suffix is ṅit of itself, the extended ṅit-ness by sārvadhātukam apit has no result; the ṅit-ness is set out with the intent that this too is a result of the sārvadhātuka name. In ni ca dhīmahi the word ca is used; but since the tiṅanta sanema comes first, dhīmahi is the second relative to it. So by "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. sū. 8-1-59) the bar to unaccentedness does not come; by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ it is wholly unaccented.

Page 735 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

स्यात् (syāt): asa bhuvi. By "vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ" (Pā. sū. 3-3-161) liṅ in the sense of prayer; tip. By "itaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-100) the augment yāsuṭ [as printed; itaś ca drops the i, and yāsuṭ comes by Pā. 3-4-103]; by this it is also ṅit. As + yās + t; śap by kartari śap, and its luk by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72). By "śnasor allopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-111) the a of the root drops; by liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya the s of the augment yāsuṭ drops: syāt. Since it stands at the start of the pāda, it is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

उत (uta): final udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ" (Phi. sū. "4-83" [?]).

प्ररेचनम् (prarecanam): the root ricir virecane. By "irit saṃjñā vācyā" (Vārttika "1-3-7" [?]) the ir is called it and dropped. By "lyuṭ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-115) (in the neuter, in the sense of the action, the suffixes kta and lyuṭ come after a root) the suffix lyuṭ; by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1) ana for yu: ric + ana; by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) the laghūpadha-guṇa: recana; by "liti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix ana is udātta. With the word pra, by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18) the prādi compound; by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent of the kṛt final member.

Rik 7: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वम् is as printed; the grammar page (p. 739) says that this sūtra does not apply to the s of vas.

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ वां युवामुभावहं हुवे । आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । चित्राय मणिमुक्तादिरूपेण विविधाय राधसे धनाय । तत आहुतौ युवामस्माननुष्ठातॄन्सु जिग्युषः । शत्रुविषये सुष्ठु जययुक्तान्कृतं कुरुतम् ॥ इन्द्रावरुणा । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना संबोधनस्याकारः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानङ् । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । संहितायां छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वम् । हुवे । ह्वयतेर्लट्युत्तमैकवचनमिट् । शप इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । ह्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वम् । अचि श्नुधात्वित्यादिनोवङ् । पा. ६-४-७७ । न च हुश्नुवोरित्यादिना । पा. ६-४-८७ । यणादेशः । जुहोतेरेव हि प्रतिपदोक्तस्य तत् । न पुनरस्य लाक्षणिकत्वात् । इटः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । राधसे । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अस्मान् । शसि द्वितीयायां च । पा. ७-२-८७ । इत्यात्वम् । शसो नः । पा. ७-१-२९ । इति नत्वम् । जिग्युषः । जि जये । लिटः क्वसुश्चेति क्वसुः । द्विर्भावः । सन्लिटोर्जेः । पा. ७-३-५७ । इति द्वितीयस्य कुत्वम् । क्वसोः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । क्र्यादिनियमात्प्राप्तस्येटो वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमेन निवृत्तिः । द्वितीया बहुवचनं शस् । भसंज्ञायां वसोः संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वम् । एरनेकाच इति यणादेशः । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोकार उदात्तः । कृतम् । डुकृञ् करणे । लोण्मध्यमद्विवचनस्य लङ्वद्भावात्तमादेशः । शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau vāṃ yuvāmubhāvahaṃ huve | āhvayāmi | kimartham | citrāya maṇimuktādirūpeṇa vividhāya rādhase dhanāya | tata āhutau yuvāmasmānanuṣṭhātṝnsu jigyuṣaḥ | śatruviṣaye suṣṭhu jayayuktānkṛtaṃ kurutam || indrāvaruṇā | supāṃ sulugityādinā saṃbodhanasyākāraḥ | devatādvandve ceti pūrvapadasyānaṅ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | saṃhitāyāṃ chāndasaṃ hrasvatvam | huve | hvayaterlaṭyuttamaikavacanamiṭ | śapa ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | hva ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvam | aci śnudhātvityādinovaṅ | pā. 6-4-77 | na ca huśnuvorityādinā | pā. 6-4-87 | yaṇādeśaḥ | juhotereva hi pratipadoktasya tat | na punarasya lākṣaṇikatvāt | iṭaḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | rādhase | asun | nittvādādyudāttatvam | asmān | śasi dvitīyāyāṃ ca | pā. 7-2-87 | ityātvam | śaso naḥ | pā. 7-1-29 | iti natvam | jigyuṣaḥ | ji jaye | liṭaḥ kvasuśceti kvasuḥ | dvirbhāvaḥ | sanliṭorjeḥ | pā. 7-3-57 | iti dvitīyasya kutvam | kvasoḥ kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | kryādiniyamātprāptasyeṭo vasvekājādghasāmiti niyamena nivṛttiḥ | dvitīyā bahuvacanaṃ śas | bhasaṃjñāyāṃ vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇamiti saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatvam | eranekāca iti yaṇādeśaḥ | śāsivasighasīnāṃ ceti ṣatvam | pratyayasvareṇokāra udāttaḥ | kṛtam | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | loṇmadhyamadvivacanasya laṅvadbhāvāttamādeśaḥ | śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Indrāvaruṇā, O Indra and Varuṇa, I call, huve, you both. For what? For rādhas, wealth, citra, of many kinds, in the form of gems, pearls and the like. Then, being called, kṛtam, make us, the performers, su jigyuṣaḥ, well victorious over our enemies." (Grammatical tail: indrāvaruṇā, ā for the vocative by supāṃ suluk…, ānaṅ for the first member by devatādvandve ca, initial udātta of the vocative, shortened in the Saṃhitā as a Vedic form; huve, 1st singular iṭ of laṭ after hve, the śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, saṃprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi with hvaḥ carried on, the pūrvarūpa, uvaṅ by Pā. 6-4-77; not yaṇ by huśnuvoḥ… (Pā. 6-4-87), which is for the pratipadokta juhoti only, not for this, which is lākṣaṇika; iṭ udātta by the suffix accent, not lowered at the start of the pāda; rādhase, asun, initial udātta as nit; asmān, ā by Pā. 7-2-87, n by śaso naḥ (Pā. 7-1-29); jigyuṣaḥ, ji jaye, kvasu for liṭ, doubling, the guttural for the second by Pā. 7-3-57, no guṇa as kvasu is kit, the iṭ due by the kryādi-niyama withdrawn by the restriction vasv ekājādghasām, accusative plural śas, saṃprasāraṇa by vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam in the bha stem, the pūrvarūpa, yaṇ by er anekācaḥ, ṣ by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca, the u udātta by the suffix accent; kṛtam, ḍukṛñ karaṇe, tam for the 2nd dual of loṭ as it is treated as laṅ, śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | वाम् (vām) — you two | अहम् (aham) — I (the performer) | चित्राय (citrāya) — of various forms (diamond, lapis lazuli and the like) | राधसे (rādhase) — for wealth | हुवे (huve) — I call (you, being called thus) | अस्मान् (asmān) — us (the performers) | सु जिग्युषः (su jigyuṣaḥ) — as good victors | कृतम् (kṛtam) — make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa, we praise you with hymns and call you. Give us various kinds of goods such as diamonds and lapis lazuli, and make us conquer our enemies.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, I invoke you for several kinds of wealth ; make us victorious (over our enemies).

original p. 737

Rik 7: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Indrāvaruṇā: though the last syllable of this word is long, in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha it is short to suit the metre. In the same way, in the 3rd ṛk of this sūkta and in the 8th and 9th ṛks too, the last syllable of this word is short in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha.

Citrāya: the commentator says "maṇimuktādirūpeṇa vividhāya", various, in the form of gems, pearls and the like. Rather than saying this, it would be more fitting to say various useful riches such as wealth, cattle and food. It may freely be said that for the ṛṣis of that time the need for cows, food, victory over enemies and the like was greater than for wealth such as gems and pearls.

Jigyuṣaḥ: ji jaye;

शत्रुविषये सुष्ठु जययुक्तान् ॥

śatruviṣaye suṣṭhu jayayuktān ||

("Well endowed with victory over enemies.") The sense is: possessed of the power to conquer enemies.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 737–740, noted briefly

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā): indraś ca varuṇaś ca, a dvandva compound. For the vocative dual suffix au, by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ā. By "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26) the first member takes ānaṅ. Since it stands at the start of a pāda, it is not wholly unaccented by the eighth-chapter āmantritasya ca; by the sixth-chapter āmantritasya ca it is initial udātta. In the Saṃhitā it is shortened as a Vedic form.

हुवे (huve): the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca. Since it is ñit, it is ātmanepadin when the fruit goes to the agent; laṭ, and in its place the 1st singular iṭ: hve + i; śap by kartari śap. In "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73) the word śapaḥ is carried on from adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; so, since in the Veda śap takes luk variously, śap takes luk. In "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34) the sūtra "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) is carried on: in the Veda the root hveñ takes saṃprasāraṇa variously, so saṃprasāraṇa, u for v. By "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108) the pūrvarūpa: hu + i. By "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) the substitute uvaṅ: huve. Here, with hu + i, one may doubt that yaṇ should come, since by "huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke" (Pā. sū. 6-4-87), before a vowel-initial sārvadhātuka suffix, the u, not preceded by a conjunct, of the root hu and of a many-voweled aṅga ending in the suffix śnu

original p. 738

Rik 7: grammar

takes the substitute yaṇ. But in the sūtra huśnuvoḥ only the pratipadokta hu is taken, not the lākṣaṇika hu. Lakṣaṇa means sūtra; lakṣaṇena nirvṛttaṃ lākṣaṇikam: what is produced with the help of a sūtra is called lākṣaṇika. Here hu is produced from the root hve with the help of sūtras such as bahulaṃ chandasi; so it is lākṣaṇika. The root hu dānādanayoḥ is not produced in this way with the help of a sūtra; so it is not lākṣaṇika. In huśnuvoḥ the word hu takes the pratipadokta root hu dānādanayoḥ, by

लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव ग्रहणम्

lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam

("Of the lākṣaṇika and the pratipadokta, only the pratipadokta is taken", paribhāṣā "114" [?].) So yaṇ does not come by huśnuvoḥ for the hu derived from the lākṣaṇika root hveñ. Anekācaḥ, carried on from er anekācaḥ, qualifies the aṅga; since śnu is a suffix, the tadanta is obtained. Huśnuvoḥ, with aṅgasya carried on and changed into aṅgayoḥ, qualifies it; by "yena vidhis tadantasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-72) the tadanta is obtained. Thus the sense of huśnuvoḥ is: the u, not preceded by a conjunct, of an aṅga that ends in the root hu or in the suffix śnu and has more than one vowel takes yaṇ. So with hu + i, since the aṅga does not have more than one vowel, the yaṇ enjoined by huśnuvoḥ has no scope at all. It may be said, rightly, that the Vedabhāṣyakāra barred the yaṇ by the lakṣaṇa-pratipadokta paribhāṣā either by the maxim "upāyasya upāyāntarādūṣakatvam" (one means does not spoil another) or on the view that rejects the mention of anekāc. The iṭ is a suffix, so it is udātta by the suffix accent. Since "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) excludes the start of a pāda, huve, standing at the start of a pāda, is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

राधसे (rādhase): rādha saṃsiddhau. After it the suffix asun by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]); initial udātta by the nit accent, ñnityādir nityam.

अस्मान् (asmān): after the word asmad the accusative plural śas; the ś is called it and dropped: asmad + as. By "dvitīyāyāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-87), when an accusative ending follows, the last letter of yuṣmad and asmad takes ā: ā for d: asma + ā + as; lengthening of like vowels: asmā + as. By "śaso na" (Pā. sū. 7-1-29) n is substituted for the śas after yuṣmad and asmad; that substitute, which would come by alo 'ntyasya, comes for the a of as by its exception "ādeḥ parasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-54). Asmān + s: by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. "0-2-23" [as printed, for 8-2-23]) the s drops: asmān.

original p. 739

Rik 7: grammar

जिग्युषः (jigyuṣaḥ): the root ji jaye; liṭ, and for it the substitute kvasu by "kvasuś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-107). By "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8) doubling: ji + ji + vas. By "sanliṭor jeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-57), what follows the abhyāsa of the root ji, conditioned by san or liṭ, takes a guttural: g for j: ji + gi + vas. The suffix vas is a val-initial ārdhadhātuka; so the augment iṭ is due by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-35); for that the bar comes by "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. sū. 7-2-10). Again, by "kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi" (Pā. sū. 7-2-13), whatever bars to iṭ there are, based on the base and on the suffix, if they come in the liṭ, come only for the roots kṛ, sṛ and the rest. By the kryādi-niyama, that for the liṭ after roots other than the kṛ-ādi the bar to the augment iṭ does not come, the bar does not come for the liṭ vas after the root ji, which is not of the kṛ-ādi. So the augment iṭ is due. For this, by "vasv ekājādghasām" (Pā. sū. 7-2-67), in the view where iṭ comes to vas, only for the vas after a root of one vowel after doubling, a root ending in ā, and the root ghas, does iṭ come; for vas after other roots iṭ does not come: by this restriction it is withdrawn. After jigivas the accusative plural śas: jigivas + as; by "yaci bham" (Pā. sū. 1-4-18) it is called bha. By "vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-4-131) a bha stem ending in the suffix vasu takes saṃprasāraṇa: u for v; the pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca: jigi + us + as; by "er anekācaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-82) yaṇ, y for i; by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for s. For the s of the suffix vas, it was made clear before that ṣ does not come by "śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 8-3-60). Ru and visarga. With jigyuṣaḥ + kṛtam, by "kaḥkarat-karati-kṛdhi-kṛteṣv anaditeḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-50), for a visarga not after the word aditi, when kaḥ and the rest follow, s comes: so s. Though the commentators have explained kṛta as ending in the suffix kta, there is no harm if this too is taken; but there is no sufficient proof that only the kta-final must be taken. Kṛta means a word having the sequence kṛ-ta. Such a sequence exists both when the suffix [kta] has come and when the form is derived as explained below. Here, since nothing is specified, both are taken. In jigyuṣaḥ the u is udātta by the suffix accent.

कृतम् (kṛtam): the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe. Loṭ, 2nd dual thas. By "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) it is treated as laṅ, and by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū.

Page 740 (upper) — Rik 7: grammar (end)

3-4-101) tam for thas: kṛtam. The śap that comes by kartari śap takes luk by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73). Although here the vikaraṇa u is due by "tanādikṛñbhya uḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-79), the exception to kartari śap, it does not come, since it is optional by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (paribhāṣā "75" [as read, ?; elsewhere 35]). To avoid these difficulties it might be said to be kta-final; but in that view the intended total unaccentedness is not obtained. So it cannot be described as kta-final. If it is set out as a tiṅanta in the way stated above, it becomes wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

॥७॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: strokes over द्रा, षा and र्म; bars under ण, वां, धी, अ and भ्यं.

इन्द्रा॑वरुण॒ नू नु वां॒ सिषा॑सन्तीषु धी॒ष्वा । [accent ?] अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ शर्म॑ यच्छतम् ॥८॥ [accent ?]

índrāvaruṇa nū́ nu vāṃ síṣāsantīṣu dhīṣvā́ | [accent ?] asmábhyaṃ śárma yacchatam ||8|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ सिसासन्तीषु, with स, is as printed in the Pada; the Saṃhitā and bhāṣya have सिषासन्तीषु.

इन्द्रावरुणा । नु । नु । वाम् । सिसासन्तीषु । धीषु । आ ॥ अस्मभ्यम् । शर्म । यच्छतम् ॥८॥

indrāvaruṇā | nu | nu | vām | sisāsantīṣu | dhīṣu | ā || asmabhyam | śarma | yacchatam ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ धीष्वस्मदीयबुद्धिषु वां युवां सिषासन्तीषु सनितुं संभक्तुं सम्यक्सेवितुमिच्छन्तीषु तदानीमासमन्तादस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं नू नु अतिशयेन क्षिप्रं यच्छतम् । दत्तम् । षड्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु क्षिप्रनामसु नु मक्ष्विति पठितम् । तस्य द्विरावृत्तिबलादतिशयो लभ्यते ॥ इन्द्रावरुणा । उक्तम् । नू नु । ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् । पा. ६-३-१३३ । इति पूर्वस्य दीर्घत्वम् । सिषासन्तीषु । वन षण संभक्तौ । धात्वादेः षः सः । इच्छायां सन् । द्विर्भावो हलादिशेषः । सन्यत इतीत्वम् । आदेशप्रत्यययोरिति षत्वम् । सनीवन्तेत्यादिना । पा. ७-२-४९ । विकल्पादिडभावः । जनसनखनां सन्झलोः । पा. ६-४-४२ । इति नकारस्याकारः । उपरि लटः शतृ । कर्तरि शप् । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । शप्श्यनोर्नित्यम् । पा. ७-१-८१ । इति नुम् । ङीपः शपश्च पित्त्वाच्छतुश्च लसार्वधातुकत्वेनानुदात्तत्वम् ।

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau dhīṣvasmadīyabuddhiṣu vāṃ yuvāṃ siṣāsantīṣu sanituṃ saṃbhaktuṃ samyaksevitumicchantīṣu tadānīmāsamantādasmabhyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ nū nu atiśayena kṣipraṃ yacchatam | dattam | ṣaḍviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu kṣipranāmasu nu makṣviti paṭhitam | tasya dvirāvṛttibalādatiśayo labhyate || indrāvaruṇā | uktam | nū nu | ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām | pā. 6-3-133 | iti pūrvasya dīrghatvam | siṣāsantīṣu | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | icchāyāṃ san | dvirbhāvo halādiśeṣaḥ | sanyata itītvam | ādeśapratyayayoriti ṣatvam | sanīvantetyādinā | pā. 7-2-49 | vikalpādiḍabhāvaḥ | janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ | pā. 6-4-42 | iti nakārasyākāraḥ | upari laṭaḥ śatṛ | kartari śap | ugitaśceti ṅīp | śapśyanornityam | pā. 7-1-81 | iti num | ṅīpaḥ śapaśca pittvācchatuśca lasārvadhātukatvenānudāttatvam |

original p. 741

Rik 8: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

सनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तदेव शिष्यते । धीषु । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अस्मभ्यम् । अस्मभ्यमप्रतिष्कुतः । ऋग्वे. १-७-६ । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । यच्छतम् । दाण् दाने । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना यच्छादेशः ॥

sano nittvādādyudāttatvam | tadeva śiṣyate | dhīṣu | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | asmabhyam | asmabhyamapratiṣkutaḥ | ṛgve. 1-7-6 | ityatroktam | yacchatam | dāṇ dāne | śapi pāghretyādinā yacchādeśaḥ ||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa, while dhīṣu, our minds, are siṣāsantīṣu, wishing to serve you two, to attend on you well, at that time give, yacchatam, to us from all sides śarma, happiness, nū nu, very quickly. Nu is read among the twenty-six names for 'quick' as nu, makṣu; from its repetition the intensity is obtained." (Grammatical tail: indrāvaruṇā, explained; nū nu, the first lengthened by Pā. 6-3-133; siṣāsantīṣu, vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau, s for ṣ, san of desire, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, i by sanyataḥ, ṣ by ādeśapratyayayoḥ, no iṭ as it is optional by Pā. 7-2-49, ā for the n by Pā. 6-4-42, then śatṛ for laṭ, śap, ṅīp by ugitaś ca, num by Pā. 7-1-81; ṅīp and śap unaccented as pit, śatṛ as an lasārvadhātuka; initial udātta as san is nit, and that stays; dhīṣu, the ending udātta by sāv ekācaḥ; asmabhyam, as said at Ṛgveda 1-7-6; yacchatam, dāṇ dāne, yaccha by pāghrā… before śap.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | धीषु (dhīṣu) — (our) minds | वाम् (vām) — you two | सिषासन्तीषु (siṣāsantīṣu) — while wishing to serve | अस्मभ्यम् (asmabhyam) — to us | आ (ā) — in every respect | शर्म (śarma) — happiness | नू नु (nū nu) — very quickly | यच्छतम् (yacchatam) — give.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa, our minds are always absorbed in serving you; that is, we are serving you constantly. So, being pleased, give us happiness in every way.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Varuna, quickly bestow happiness upon us, for our minds are devoted to you both.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Nū nu: since the word nu is read among the twenty-six words meaning "quick", nu, makṣu and so on, nu means quickly, swiftly. Here, since nu is read twice, it means very quickly, without the least delay. To suit the metre the first nu is long. Besides this, Yāska gives some more senses for the word nu:

नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा । इदं नु करिष्यतीति हेत्वपदेशे । अथाप्युपमार्थे भवति ॥ (नि. १-४)

nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā | idaṃ nu kariṣyatīti hetvapadeśe | athāpyupamārthe bhavati || (ni. 1-4)

("Nu has many uses: in 'he will now do this' it states a cause; it also has the sense of comparison": editorial and tentative.) The word nu denotes many actions and a cause, and is used in the sense of comparison too. For example,

वृक्षस्य नु ते (ऋ. सं. ६-२४-३)

vṛkṣasya nu te (ṛ. saṃ. 6-24-3)

means

वृक्षस्येव ते

vṛkṣasyeva te

("Like a tree's, your …": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 742

Rik 8: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Siṣāsantīṣu dhīṣu: our minds, or hearts, longing to serve you, expecting it. Here the locative is used in the sense of the nominative. Such usage is especially common in modern Sanskrit too.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 742–743, noted briefly

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā): explained in the previous mantra.

नू नु (nū nu): by "ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. sū. 6-3-133) the first nu is lengthened.

सिषासन्तीषु (siṣāsantīṣu): the root vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau; by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ s for the ṣ of the root ṣaṇa, and the ṇ is withdrawn. By "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-7), when sanitum icchati is meant, the suffix san after the root san: san + sa. By "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9) doubling: san san + sa; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60) the n of the first san, of the abhyāsa, is withdrawn; by "sanyataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-79) i for the a of the abhyāsa: sisan + sa. The suffix san is ārdhadhātuka, so the augment iṭ is due by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. "3-2-34" [as printed, for 7-2-35]). But by "sanīvantardhabhrasjadambhuśrisvṛyūrṇubharajñapisanām" (Pā. sū. 7-2-49), for the san after the roots ending in iv, and ṛdh, bhrasj, dambh, śri, svṛ, yu, ūrṇu, bhara, jñapi and san, the augment iṭ comes optionally; so for the san after the root san, iṭ is enjoined optionally, and in one alternative it does not come. By "janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-42), before a jhal-initial san, and before a jhal-initial suffix that is kit or ṅit, the last letter of the three roots jan, san, khan takes ā: ā for n; lengthening of like vowels: sisā + sa. By "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for the second s: siṣāsa; it is called dhātu by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-32). After it laṭ; by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) the suffix śatṛ; śap by kartari śap: siṣāsa + a + at; by ato guṇe the pararūpa twice: siṣāsat. By "ugitaś ca" (Pā. sū. 4-1-6) ṅīp: siṣāsat + ī. By "śapśyanor nityam" (Pā. sū. 7-1-81), for an aṅga ending in the śatṛ part that follows the a belonging to śap or śyan, when śī or a letter called nadī follows, the augment num comes always;

Page 743 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

so the augment num. By "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-47) it comes after the last vowel: siṣāsantī. Ṅīp and śap are both pit, so unaccented by anudāttau suppitau. The suffix śatṛ stands after the śap, an adupadeśa; so it is unaccented by "tāsyanudātteṅ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186). The suffix san is nit; so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) siṣāsa is initial udātta, and that accent stays. In the locative plural it becomes siṣāsantīṣu.

धीषु (dhīṣu): dhyai cintāyām. By "dhyāyateḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca" (Pā. sū. "3-2-178" [as printed; a vārttika there]) the root dhyai takes saṃprasāraṇa and after it the suffix kvip; so kvip, which drops; saṃprasāraṇa, i for y; by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. "6-1-100" [as printed, for 6-1-108]) the pūrvarūpa: dhi. By "halaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-2) lengthening: dhī. After it the locative plural sup: dhī + su; ṣ by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; by "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-168) the ending is udātta.

अस्मभ्यम् (asmabhyam): explained at "asmabhyam apratiṣkutaḥ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-7-6).

यच्छतम् (yacchatam): dāṇ dāne; loṭ, 2nd dual thas; treated as laṅ by loṭo laṅvat, tam by tasthasthamipām, śap by kartari śap; by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78) yacch for dāṇ: yacchatam.

॥८॥

Page 743 (lower) — Sūkta 17, Rik 9 (last ṛk of the sūkta)

प्र वा॑मश्नोतु सुष्टुतिरिन्द्रा॑वरुण॒ यां हु॒वे । [accent ?] यामृ॒धा॑थे स॒धस्तु॑तिम् ॥९॥ [accent ?]

prá vām aśnotu suṣṭutír índrāvaruṇa yā́ṃ huvé | [accent ?] yā́m ṛdhā́the sadhástutim ||9|| [accent ?]

प्र । वाम् । अश्नोतु । सुऽस्तुतिः । इन्द्रावरुणा । याम् । हुवे ॥ याम् । ऋधाथे इति । सधऽस्तुतिम् ॥९॥

pra | vām | aśnotu | su 'stutiḥ | indrāvaruṇā | yām | huve || yām | ṛdhāthe iti | sadha 'stutim ||9||

Rik 9: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥३३॥ closes Varga 33; ॥४॥ closes the fourth Anuvāka.

इन्द्रावरुणा हे इन्द्रावरुणौ यामस्मत्कर्तृकां शोभनस्तुतिं प्रति हुवे युवामुभावाह्वयामि । किंच सधस्तुतिं युवयोरुभयोः साहित्येन क्रियमाणायाः स्तवक्रियाया यां सुष्टुतिं प्रतिलभ्य ऋधाथे युवां वर्धेथे । तादृशी सुष्टुतिः शोभनस्तुतिहेतुभूत ऋक्समूहो वामश्नोतु । युवां व्याप्नोतु ॥ अश्नोतु । अशू व्याप्तौ । लोटो व्यत्ययेन तिप् । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । सुष्टुतिः । न विन्धे अस्य सुष्टुतिम् । ऋग्वे. १-७-७ । इत्यत्रोक्तम् । इन्द्रावरुणा । हुवे । उक्ते । अत्र तु यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः । ऋधाथे । ऋधु वृद्धौ । लट् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । मध्यमद्विवचने श्नोर्बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणाकार उदात्तः । यच्छब्दयोगान्न निघातः । सधस्तुतिम् । सह स्तुतिर्यस्यां सुष्टुतौ सा सधस्तुतिः । अत्र सुष्टुतिरित्यन्यपदार्थे स्तुतिशब्दस्य स्तूयतेऽनयेति करणसाधनत्वेन ऋक्परत्वेऽयं स्तुतिशब्दो भावसाधनतया स्तवनक्रियापरः । तस्मिन्भावसाधनत्वेन क्रियापरेऽयं करणसाधनतया ऋक्पर इति समस्यमानपदार्थादन्यः । सहेत्यत्र हकारस्य व्यत्ययेन धकारः । सहशब्द एवमादित्वादन्तोदात्तः । बहुव्रीहित्वेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥३३॥ ॥४॥

indrāvaruṇā he indrāvaruṇau yāmasmatkartṛkāṃ śobhanastutiṃ prati huve yuvāmubhāvāhvayāmi | kiṃca sadhastutiṃ yuvayorubhayoḥ sāhityena kriyamāṇāyāḥ stavakriyāyā yāṃ suṣṭutiṃ pratilabhya ṛdhāthe yuvāṃ vardhethe | tādṛśī suṣṭutiḥ śobhanastutihetubhūta ṛksamūho vāmaśnotu | yuvāṃ vyāpnotu || aśnotu | aśū vyāptau | loṭo vyatyayena tip | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | suṣṭutiḥ | na vindhe asya suṣṭutim | ṛgve. 1-7-7 | ityatroktam | indrāvaruṇā | huve | ukte | atra tu yadvṛttayogānna nighātaḥ | ṛdhāthe | ṛdhu vṛddhau | laṭ | vyatyayenātmanepadam | madhyamadvivacane śnorbahulaṃ chandasīti luk | pratyayasvareṇākāra udāttaḥ | yacchabdayogānna nighātaḥ | sadhastutim | saha stutiryasyāṃ suṣṭutau sā sadhastutiḥ | atra suṣṭutirityanyapadārthe stutiśabdasya stūyate 'nayeti karaṇasādhanatvena ṛkparatve 'yaṃ stutiśabdo bhāvasādhanatayā stavanakriyāparaḥ | tasminbhāvasādhanatvena kriyāpare 'yaṃ karaṇasādhanatayā ṛkpara iti samasyamānapadārthādanyaḥ | sahetyatra hakārasya vyatyayena dhakāraḥ | sahaśabda evamāditvādantodāttaḥ | bahuvrīhitvena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||33|| ||4||

Translation: "O Indra and Varuṇa, I call you both towards the excellent praise that we make. Further, the suṣṭuti, excellent praise, which is sadhastuti, an act of praise made of you both together, by obtaining which you ṛdhāthe, grow: may such suṣṭuti, the collection of ṛks that is the cause of excellent praise, aśnotu, reach you." (Grammatical tail: aśnotu, aśū vyāptau, tip for loṭ by exchange, śnu by svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ; suṣṭutiḥ, as said at Ṛgveda 1-7-7; indrāvaruṇā, huve, explained; here, though, not lowered because joined with yad; ṛdhāthe, ṛdhu vṛddhau, laṭ, ātmanepada by exchange, in the 2nd dual the śnu dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, the ā udātta by the suffix accent, not lowered because joined with yad; sadhastutim, "the suṣṭuti in which there is praise together"; here the word stuti in suṣṭuti, the other thing meant, being an instrument noun, "that by which one praises", denotes the ṛk, while this stuti [in the compound], an action noun, denotes the act of praising; where that one is an action noun denoting the act, this one, an instrument noun, denotes the ṛk; so it differs from the sense of the compounded words. In saha, dh for h by exchange; saha is final udātta as one of the evam-ādi; as a bahuvrīhi, the accent of the first member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रावरुणा (indrāvaruṇā) — O Indra and Varuṇa | याम् (yām) — which (praise of ours, towards it) | हुवे (huve) — I call (you both) | (and) याम् सधस्तुतिम् (yām sadhastutim) — by which hymn made of you both together | ऋधाथे (ṛdhāthe) — you grow (you are pleased) | सुष्टुतिः (suṣṭutiḥ) — (such a) collection of ṛks in the form of a hymn | वाम् अश्नोतु (vām aśnotu) — may it reach you.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Varuṇa, we call each of you separately with praise. At times we also praise you both together. Be pleased with such hymns.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the earnest praise which I offer to Indra and Varuna reach you both ; and may you fulfil that prayer addressed to you both.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Aśnotu: vyāpnotu, may it reach: the sense is, may the hymn we make reach you and be dear to you.

original p. 745

Rik 9: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Ṛdhāthe:

ऋधु वृद्धौ । वर्धेथाम् ॥

ṛdhu vṛddhau | vardhethām ||

("Ṛdhu, to grow: may you grow.") The senses "you liked the praise we made, or praised it, and so were well satisfied" and the like may be given.

Sadhastutim:

सह स्तुतिर्यस्यां सुष्टुतौ सा सधस्तुतिः ॥

saha stutiryasyāṃ suṣṭutau sā sadhastutiḥ ||

("The suṣṭuti in which there is praise together is the sadhastuti.") A hymn that praises two together is called sadhastuti. Here the two deities Indra and Varuṇa are praised together.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 745–746, noted briefly

अश्नोतु (aśnotu): aśū vyāptau. Loṭ; the root is anudāttet, so ātmanepada ought to come by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam". But by "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85) the parasmaipada suffix ti comes by exchange. By "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-73) the vikaraṇa śnu: aś + nu + ti; guṇa; by eruḥ u for the i.

सुष्टुतिः (suṣṭutiḥ): explained at "na vindhe asya suṣṭutim" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-7-7).

इन्द्रावरुणा, हुवे (indrāvaruṇā, huve): see the 7th mantra of this sūkta. There it was said that, standing at the start of a pāda, it is not wholly unaccented; here too, by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) (a tiṅanta after a word containing yad does not become unaccented), it is not wholly unaccented.

ऋधाथे (ṛdhāthe): ṛdhu vṛddhau. Laṭ; by exchange, ātmanepada, 1st-person [as printed; āthām is 2nd person] dual āthām. By "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79) e for the ṭi (ām). By svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ the suffix śnu; for it luk by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73): ṛdhāthe. By the suffix accent, that is, by "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3), the ā at the start of the suffix āthe is udātta. Yām ṛdhāthe: it follows a word formed with yad; so, since the bar comes by yadvṛttān nityam, it is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

सधस्तुतिम् (sadhastutim): saha stutir yasyāṃ suṣṭutau sā sadhastutiḥ: by "anekam anyapadārthe" (Pā. sū. 2-2-24) a bahuvrīhi. The sense of the sūtra is: several subantas are compounded in the sense of another word, and these are called bahuvrīhi. Anyapadārtha means that which stands in the sense of a word other than the words that are compounded. Here the words saha and stuti are compounded. So there is no room for the doubt how stuti can be the anyapadārtha. The sense of the word stuti included in the compound is

Page 746 (upper) — Rik 9: grammar (end)

one thing; the sense set forth by the word suṣṭuti, meant as the anyapadārtha, is another. For in suṣṭuti, the anyapadārtha, if the word stuti means stūyate anayā iti stutiḥ, with ktin in the sense of instrument, the ṛk which is the instrument of praise, then the word stuti in the compound, stavanaṃ stutiḥ, with ktin in the sense of the action, means the act of praising. If in the anyapadārtha the word stuti is meant to state the praising, as ending in ktin in the sense of the action, then the word stuti in the compound, ending in ktin in the sense of instrument, sets forth the sense ṛk. Thus the sense put forward by the word suṣṭuti differs from the sense set forth by the compounded words, so it is the anyapadārtha. In saha the h becomes dh by exchange. By "evādīnām antaḥ" (Phi. sū. "4-83" [?]) the word saha is final udātta. After the bahuvrīhi compound has come too, by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member comes.

॥९॥ Sūkta 17 ends here, mid-page; p. 746 continues with the title of the Eighteenth Sūkta. No colophon is printed. Printed p. 746, lower half: the title ಹದಿನೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Eighteenth Sūkta") and an ornament.

॥ ಹದಿನೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 18 — "somānaṃ svaraṇaṃ kṛṇuhi" ("The Eighteenth Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

Page 746 (lower) — Sūkta 18: introduction

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note) सादसस्पत्या, in the Anukramaṇī quotation, is as printed.

पञ्चमेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र सोमानमित्यादिकं नवर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवताविशेषस्त्वेवमनुक्रम्यते । सोमानमिति पञ्च ब्राह्मणस्पत्याश्चतुर्थ्यामिन्द्रश्च सोमश्च पञ्चम्यां दक्षिणा चान्याः सादसस्पत्या नाराशंसी वान्त्येति । सूक्तगता आद्याः पञ्चर्चो ब्रह्मणस्पतिदेवताकाः । तासां मध्ये स घा वीर इत्येतस्याश्चतुर्थ्या ऋचो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरिन्द्रश्च सोमश्चेति तिस्रो देवताः । त्वं तमित्येतस्याः पञ्चम्या दक्षिणया सह पूर्वोक्तास्तिस्रो देवताः । षष्ठीमारभ्य तिसृणां सदसस्पतिर्देवता । नराशंसमित्येतस्या नवम्याः सदसस्पतिर्नराशंसो वा विकल्प्यते ॥ विनियोगस्तु पूर्ववत् ॥

pañcame 'nuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatra somānamityādikaṃ navarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktam | ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | devatāviśeṣastvevamanukramyate | somānamiti pañca brāhmaṇaspatyāścaturthyāmindraśca somaśca pañcamyāṃ dakṣiṇā cānyāḥ sādasaspatyā nārāśaṃsī vāntyeti | sūktagatā ādyāḥ pañcarco brahmaṇaspatidevatākāḥ | tāsāṃ madhye sa ghā vīra ityetasyāścaturthyā ṛco brahmaṇaspatirindraśca somaśceti tisro devatāḥ | tvaṃ tamityetasyāḥ pañcamyā dakṣiṇayā saha pūrvoktāstisro devatāḥ | ṣaṣṭhīmārabhya tisṛṇāṃ sadasaspatirdevatā | narāśaṃsamityetasyā navamyāḥ sadasaspatirnarāśaṃso vā vikalpyate || viniyogastu pūrvavat ||

Translation: "In the fifth anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of them the sūkta beginning somānam, of nine ṛks, is the first. The ṛṣi and metre are as before. The particular deities are stated in the Anukramaṇī thus: 'somānam: five to Brahmaṇaspati; in the fourth Indra and Soma too; in the fifth Dakṣiṇā too; the others to Sadasaspati; the last optionally to Narāśaṃsa.' The first five ṛks of the sūkta have Brahmaṇaspati as deity. Among them, the fourth ṛk, sa ghā vīraḥ, has three deities: Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma. The fifth, tvaṃ tam, has the three named before together with Dakṣiṇā. From the sixth on, three have Sadasaspati as deity. For the ninth, narāśaṃsam, Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa is the option. The application is as before."

original p. 747

Sūkta 18: introduction (end), heading, Rik 1 Saṃhitā and Pada

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): With this sūkta the fifth anuvāka begins. In this anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of them the nine-ṛk sūkta somānam is the first. The ṛṣi and metres are as in the previous sūkta. The particular deities are stated in the Anukramaṇikā thus: "somānam iti pañca brāhmaṇaspatyaś caturthyām indraś ca somaś ca pañcamyāṃ dakṣiṇā cānyāḥ sādasaspatyā nārāśaṃsī vāntyeti"; that is, in the sūkta somānam of the fifth anuvāka, the deities are Brahmaṇaspati for the first three ṛks; Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma for the fourth; Brahmaṇaspati and Dakṣiṇā for the fifth; Sadasaspati for the ṛks from the sixth to the eighth; and Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa for the ninth. The first five ṛks of the sūkta have Brahmaṇaspati as deity. Among them the fourth ṛk, sa ghā vīraḥ, has three deities, Brahmaṇaspati, Indra and Soma. The fifth ṛk, tvaṃ tam, has the three deities of the previous ṛk together with the deity Dakṣiṇā. The three ṛks from the sixth to the eighth have Sadasaspati as deity. The ninth ṛk, narāśaṃsam, has Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa as deity, optionally. The application is as before.

Brahmaṇaspatir Indraś ca Somaś ca । 5. Brahmaṇaspatir Dakṣiṇā ca । 6–8. Sadasaspatiḥ । 9. Sadasaspatir Narāśaṃso vā ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 18, Rik 1

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सो॒मानं॒ स्वर॑णं कृणु॒हि ब्र॑ह्मणस्पते । क॒क्षीव॑न्तं॒ य औ॑शि॒जः ॥१॥

somā́naṃ sváraṇaṃ kṛṇuhí brahmaṇaspate | kakṣī́vantaṃ yá auśijáḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सोमानम् । स्वरणम् । कृणुहि । ब्रह्मणः । पते ॥ कक्षीवन्तम् । यः । औशिजः ॥१॥

somānam | svaraṇam | kṛṇuhi | brahmaṇaḥ | pate || kakṣīvantam | yaḥ | auśijaḥ ||1||

original p. 748

Rik 1: bhāṣya

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ पर आट्णारः is as printed (also in the Kannada on p. 750).

हे ब्रह्मणस्पते एतन्नामकदेव सोमानमभिषवस्य कर्तारं मामनुष्ठातारं स्वरणं देवेषु प्रकाशनवन्तं कृणुहि । कुरु । अत्र दृष्टान्तः । कक्षीवन्तमेतन्नामकमृषिम् । इवशब्दोऽत्राध्याहर्तव्यः । कक्षीवान्यथा देवेषु प्रसिद्धस्तद्वदित्यर्थः । यः कक्षीवानृषिरौशिज उशिजः पुत्रः । तमिवेति पूर्वत्र योजना । कक्षीवतोऽनुष्ठातृषु मुनिषु प्रसिद्धिस्तैत्तिरीयैराम्नायते । एवं वै पर आट्णारः कक्षीवाँ औशिजो वीतहव्यः श्रायसस्त्रसदस्युः पौरुकुत्स्यः प्रजाकामा अचिन्वत । तै. सं. ५-६-५-३ । इति । ऋगन्तरेऽप्यृषित्वकथनेनानुष्ठातृत्वप्रसिद्धिः सूच्यते । अहं कक्षीवाँ ऋषिरस्मि विप्रः । ऋग्वे. ४-२६-१ । इति । तस्मादस्यानुष्ठातारं प्रति दृष्टान्तत्वं युक्तम् । सोऽयं मन्त्रो यास्केनैवं व्याख्यातः । सोमानं सोतारं प्रकाशनवन्तं कुरु ब्रह्मणस्पते कक्षीवन्तमिव य औशिजः । कक्षीवान्कक्ष्यावानौशिज उशिजः पुत्र उशिग्वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मणोऽपि त्वयं मनुष्यकक्ष एवाभिप्रेतः स्यात्तं सोमानं सोतारं मा प्रकाशनवन्तं कुरु ब्रह्मणस्पते । नि. ६-१० । इति । अस्मिन्मन्त्रे सोमानमिति पादेन कृणुहि ब्रह्मण इति पादेन सूचितं तात्पर्यं तैत्तिरीया आमनन्ति । सोमानं स्वरणमित्याह सोमपीथमेवाव रुन्द्धे । कृणुहि ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्याह ब्रह्मवर्चसमेवाव रुन्द्धे । तै. सं. १-५-८-४ । इति ॥ सोमानम् । सुनोतीति । षुञ् अभिषवे । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । दृशिग्रहणस्य विध्यन्तरोपसंग्रहणार्थत्वान्नित्त्वेऽपि नाद्युदात्तत्वं किंतु प्रत्ययस्वर एव । उञ्छादिषु वा सोमञ्शब्दो द्रष्टव्यः । पा. ६-१-१६० । बहुलग्रहणादौणादिको वा मनिर्द्रष्टव्यः । स्वरणम् । प्रख्यातम् । स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलम् । पा. ३-३-११३ । इति कर्मणि ल्युट् । लितीत्यकार उदात्तः । कृणुहि । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । लोटः सिपो हिः । शपि प्राप्ते धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । तत्सन्नियोगेन वकारस्याकारः । तस्यातो लोप इति लोपः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावान्न पूर्वस्य लघूपधगुणः । हेर्ङित्त्वादुकारस्य न गुणः । उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छन्दो वा वचनम् । पा. ६-४-१०६-१ । इति हेर्लुङ्न । सतिशिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्य इति वचनाद्धेरेव प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । ब्रह्मणः । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेत्यादिना । पा. ८-३-५३ । संहितायां विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः । सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवद्भावात्पदद्वयस्यामन्त्रितनिघातः । कक्षीवन्तम् । कक्षे भवा कक्ष्या अश्वोदरसंबन्धिनी रज्जुः । भवे छन्दसि । पा. ४-४-११० । इति यत्प्रत्ययः । सास्यास्तीत्यर्थ आसन्दीवदष्ठीवच्चक्रीवत्कक्षीवत् । पा. ८-२-१२ । इत्यृषिविशेषनाम कक्षीवच्छब्दो निपातितः । छन्दसीर इति वत्वम् । यप्रत्ययस्वरेण तदादेशो निपातित ईकार उदात्तः । मतुप्सुपौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । औशिजः । वश कान्तौ । इजीत्यनुवृत्तौ वशेः किच्च । उ. २-७१ । इतीजिप्रत्ययः । तस्य कित्त्वाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वे गुणाभावः । तस्यापत्यम् । पा. ४-१-९२ । इति प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् । पा. ४-१-८३ । आदिवृद्धिः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

āsandīvadaṣṭhīvaccakrīvatkakṣīvat | pā. 8-2-12 | ityṛṣiviśeṣanāma kakṣīvacchabdo nipātitaḥ | chandasīra iti vatvam | yapratyayasvareṇa tadādeśo nipātita īkāra udāttaḥ | matupsupau pittvādanudāttau | auśijaḥ | vaśa kāntau | ijītyanuvṛttau vaśeḥ kicca | u. 2-71 | itījipratyayaḥ | tasya kittvādgrahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatve guṇābhāvaḥ | tasyāpatyam | pā. 4-1-92 | iti prāgdīvyato 'ṇ | pā. 4-1-83 | ādivṛddhiḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam ||

Translation: "O Brahmaṇaspati, god of that name, kṛṇuhi, make somānam, me the performer, the presser of soma, svaraṇam, renowned among the gods. Here is an example: kakṣīvantam, the ṛṣi of that name; the word 'like' is to be supplied: as Kakṣīvān is renowned among the gods, so; that ṛṣi Kakṣīvān who is auśija, the son of Uśij; the construction is 'like him' with what precedes. Kakṣīvān's renown among the sages who perform rites is recorded by the Taittirīyas: '… Kakṣīvān Auśija, Vītahavya Śrāyasa, Trasadasyu Paurukutsya, desiring offspring, piled [the fire]' (Tai. saṃ. 5-6-5-3). In another ṛk too, by the statement that he is a ṛṣi, his renown as a performer is indicated: 'I am Kakṣīvān, the ṛṣi, the inspired one' (Ṛgveda 4-26-1). So it is fitting that he is the example for the performer. Yāska explains this mantra thus: 'Make the somānam, the presser, renowned, O Brahmaṇaspati, like Kakṣīvān, who is Auśija; Kakṣīvān is one having a girth [kakṣyā]; Auśija is the son of Uśij; uśik is from vaś, an action of desire; but here a man's girth may be meant; make me, the presser, renowned, O Brahmaṇaspati' (Ni. 6-10). The purport suggested in this mantra by the pāda somānam and by the pāda kṛṇuhi brahmaṇaḥ the Taittirīyas declare: 'He says somānaṃ svaraṇam: he secures the drinking of soma. He says kṛṇuhi brahmaṇaspate: he secures brahmavarcas' (Tai. saṃ. 1-5-8-4)." (Grammatical tail: somānam, "he presses", ṣuñ abhiṣave, manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; since the mention of dṛśi takes in other operations, though nit it is not initial udātta but has the suffix accent; or the word soman is to be seen in the uñcha-ādi (Pā. 6-1-160); or, by the mention of bahula, the manin is an Uṇādi one; svaraṇam, "renowned", svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ, lyuṭ in the object sense by Pā. 3-3-113, the a udātta by liti; kṛṇuhi, kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, num by idito num dhātoḥ, hi for sip of loṭ, in place of śap the suffix u by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca, with it a for the v, dropped by ato lopaḥ, and since that is sthānivat no laghūpadha-guṇa of what precedes, no guṇa of the u as hi is ṅit, the hi not dropped by Pā. 6-4-106-1, and by the statement on satiśiṣṭa accent "except for vikaraṇas" the hi alone is udātta by the suffix accent, not lowered at the start of the pāda; brahmaṇaḥ, s for the visarga in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 8-3-53, both words unaccented as a vocative by parāṅgavadbhāva; kakṣīvantam, kakṣyā, "being at the girth", the girth-rope of a horse's belly, yat by Pā. 4-4-110; "it has that": the ṛṣi's name kakṣīvat is given ready-made by Pā. 8-2-12, v by chandasīraḥ, the ī given as its substitute udātta by the accent of the suffix ya, matup and sup unaccented as pit; auśijaḥ, vaśa kāntau, iji by vaśeḥ kic ca (Uṇ. 2-71), saṃprasāraṇa by grahijyā… as it is kit, no guṇa; aṇ by Pā. 4-1-92 and 4-1-83, initial vṛddhi, final udātta by the suffix accent.)

original p. 749

Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे ब्रह्मणस्पते (he brahmaṇaspate) — O Brahmaṇaspati | यः (yaḥ) — who | औशिजः (auśijaḥ) — the son of Uśik, the ṛṣi called Kakṣīvān, was | कक्षीवन्तम् (kakṣīvantam) — like that ṛṣi Kakṣīvān | सोमानम् (somānam) — the one who prepares soma juice (me, the sacrificer) | स्वरणम् (svaraṇam) — renowned among the gods, or full of brahmavarcas | कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi) — make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Kakṣīvān, son of Uśik, is renowned among the gods as one who performed the soma sacrifice. O Brahmaṇaspati, make me too, the performer of the sacrifice, renowned as a performer of soma sacrifice, like that Kakṣīvān.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Brahmanaspati, make (me) who offer Soma juice illustrious among the gods like Kakshivan, the son of Usij.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The deity of this sūkta is Brahmaṇaspati. Who is this Brahmaṇaspati? What are his place and rank among the gods? We explain this briefly. In the Nirukta (Ni. 10-14) Yāska says this about Brahmaṇaspati:

ब्रह्मणस्पतिः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणः पाता वा पालयिता वा ॥

brahmaṇaspatiḥ | brahmaṇaspatirbrahmaṇaḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā ||

("Brahmaṇaspati: the protector or guardian of brahman.") Here the word brahman means food, wealth and hymn (Ni. 3-9). So brahmaṇaḥ pātā means annasya pātā, the lord or master of food. As an example of how Brahmaṇaspati is lord of food, Yāska gives the ṛk

अश्मास्यमवतं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभि यमोजसातृणत् । तमेव विश्वे पपिरे स्वर्दृशो बहु साकं सिसिचुरुत्समुद्रिणम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-२४-४)

aśmāsyamavataṃ brahmaṇaspatirmadhudhāramabhi yamojasātṛṇat | tameva viśve papire svardṛśo bahu sākaṃ sisicurutsamudriṇam || (ṛ. saṃ. 2-24-4)

("The stone-mouthed, honey-streaming one which Brahmaṇaspati pierced with might: from it all the sun-seers drank; together they poured out much the watery spring": editorial and tentative.) and for it gives the Nirukta

अशनवन्तमास्यन्तनवन्तमवातितं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मधुधारमभियमोजसा बलेनाभ्यतृणत्तमेव सर्वे पिबन्ति रश्मयः सूर्यदृशो बह्वेनं सह सिञ्चन्त्युत्समुद्रिणमुदकवन्तम् ॥ (नि. १०-१२)

aśanavantamāsyantanavantamavātitaṃ brahmaṇaspatirmadhudhāramabhiyamojasā balenābhyatṛṇattameva sarve pibanti raśmayaḥ sūryadṛśo bahvenaṃ saha siñcantyutsamudriṇamudakavantam || (ni. 10-12)

आस्यन्तनवन्तम् is as printed. ("Having food, having an outflow, unbroken, the honey-streaming one which Brahmaṇaspati pierced with force, with strength: from it all the rays, the sun-seers, drink; together they pour it out abundantly, the spring that has water": editorial and tentative.)

original p. 750

Rik 1: Special Topics

The chief intent is this: since this Brahmaṇaspati, with the help of the sun's rays, makes the clouds drink the water of the ocean and makes that water fall especially on the earth as rain, herbs and trees come from the rain, and from the herbs and trees food and the like are obtained; so Brahmaṇaspati is the protector of food. When the word brahman is taken as hymn or wealth, Brahmaṇaspati is the lord of mantra, and must be called the lord of wealth. The commentator states this very sense when explaining the ṛk cited above.

Mantras about Brahmaṇaspati are especially numerous in the Ṛgveda. In those mantras Brahmaṇaspati is said to give wealth and food. Many doubt whether this Brahmaṇaspati is a separate deity or another form of Agni. Since other deities such as Agni also give wealth and food, some argue that Brahmaṇaspati is a special form of Agni. Yāska is silent on this matter; that is, he has said nothing clearly. In the ṛks about Brahmaṇaspati too there is not enough basis to say this deity is a form of Agni. So it may freely be said that Brahmaṇaspati is a separate deity, like Indra and Agni.

Somānam:

अभिषवस्य कर्तारम्

abhiṣavasya kartāram

("The doer of the pressing.") The intent is: (me) who have prepared the soma juice.

Svaraṇam:

देवेषु प्रकाशनवन्तम् । प्रख्यातमित्यर्थः ॥

deveṣu prakāśanavantam | prakhyātamityarthaḥ ||

("Renowned among the gods; that is, famous.") The intent is: renowned and famous among the gods.

Kakṣīvantam, auśijaḥ: the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān is the son born to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas from a woman named Uśik. It is told in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that this Uśik was a maid of the queen of the king of Kaliṅga; that the king of Kaliṅga, wishing for a son, sent his wife to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas; and that the king's wife, unwilling, secretly sent her maid Uśik, and this son Kakṣīvān was born to her from the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas. Though this ṛṣi Kakṣīvān was born of a kṣatriya woman [as printed], by contact with brāhmaṇas he is known as a brāhmaṇa. This ṛṣi is the seer of many ṛks of the Ṛgveda. That this ṛṣi Kakṣīvān is renowned among those who perform sacrifices is stated in Taittirīya-saṃhitā 5-6-5-3:

एवं वै पर आट्णारः कक्षीवाँ औशिजो वीतहव्यः श्रायसस्त्रसदस्युः पौरुकुत्स्यः प्रजाकामा अचिन्वत ॥

evaṃ vai para āṭṇāraḥ kakṣīvā~ auśijo vītahavyaḥ śrāyasastrasadasyuḥ paurukutsyaḥ prajākāmā acinvata ||

So this ṛṣi is very renowned both in composing mantras and in performing sacrifices. Medhātithi, the ṛṣi of this sūkta, has prayed to the deity Brahmaṇaspati to make him renowned like Kakṣīvān.

original p. 751

Rik 1: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 751–754, noted briefly

सोमानम् (somānam): sunotīti somā; the root ṣuñ abhiṣave; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ. The suffix manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante. Here the mention of dṛśi serves to enjoin other operations; so, though the suffix is nit, initial udātta by ñnityādiḥ does not come; the suffix accent alone comes. Or it is widely accepted that the uñcha-ādi is an ākṛtigaṇa; so, putting the word soman in the uñcha-ādi, final udātta may be stated by "uñchādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-160). Or, since "uṇādayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-3-1) contains the word bahula, the Uṇādi suffix manin comes after the root su; so it is final udātta by the suffix accent. In any case the word soman is final udātta, and in the accusative singular becomes somānam.

स्वरणम् (svaraṇam): meaning "renowned". The root svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ. By "kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-3-113) the suffix lyuṭ in the object sense; by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1) ana for yu; guṇa followed by r; by liti the a of sva before the suffix is udātta; by raṣābhyām ṇ for n. Accusative singular am; the pūrvarūpa by ami pūrvaḥ: svaraṇam.

कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi): the root kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca. The augment num by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-58): kṛnv; after it loṭ, 2nd singular sip. By "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87) hi for sip; śap is due by kartari śap, but by its exception "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-80) the vikaraṇa u, and with it a for the v: kṛna + u + hi. By "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48) the a drops: kṛn + u + hi. Now, with the suffix u as condition, the laghūpadha-guṇa would be due by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86); but by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57) the loss of a is sthānivat, so the laghūpadha-guṇa does not come. With hi as condition, guṇa would be due for the u in kṛnu by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84); but by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) hi is ṅit, so by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) guṇa is barred. By "utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt" (Pā. sū. 6-4-106) luk of hi would be due; but by the statement "utaś ca pratyayāc chando vā vacanam" (Pā. sū. 6-4-106-1), that in the Veda utaś ca pratyayāt applies optionally, in one alternative the loss does not come. In "satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ", sati

original p. 752

Rik 1: grammar

means "having come about", śiṣṭa means "enjoined". When udātta is due for several letters, the udātta enjoined last, after udātta has come for some, is the stronger. But since it is said that this part does not hold for vikaraṇas, the accent that would come to the vikaraṇa u, though satiśiṣṭa, is not the stronger. So the udātta comes to hi by the suffix accent. Since it stands at the start of a pāda, the bar apādādau comes, so it is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

ब्रह्मणस्पते (brahmaṇaspate): with brahmaṇaḥ pate, by "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputrapṛṣṭhapārapadapayasposheṣu" (Pā. sū. 8-3-53), when pati and the other words follow, the visarga belonging to the genitive takes s; so in the Saṃhitā the visarga becomes s. Pate is a vocative. By "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. 2-1-2) brahmaṇaḥ is treated as part of what follows; so by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) both words are unaccented.

कक्षीवन्तम् (kakṣīvantam): kakṣa means the side; with the analysis kakṣe bhavā, by "bhave chandasi" (Pā. sū. 4-4-110) yat; since the feminine is meant, the suffix ṭāp: kakṣyā. The analysis kakṣyā asya asti. By "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup: kakṣyā + mat. "Āsandīvad-aṣṭhīvac-cakrīvat-kakṣīvad-rumaṇvac-carmaṇvatī" (Pā. sū. 8-2-12): the sense of the sūtra is that these six words are given ready-made when a name is meant. Nipātana means pronouncing a form containing an operation not got from another rule. In kakṣyā no saṃprasāraṇa comes from another rule; since this sūtra pronounces the operation of saṃprasāraṇa within it, saṃprasāraṇa comes: i for y; the pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca; lengthening by "halaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-2): kakṣīmat. Now by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-15) the m of a matup after a word ending in an i-vowel or in r takes v: kakṣīvat. After it the suffix su. By "atvasantasya cādhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-14), when a sarvanāmasthāna suffix other than the vocative follows, the penultimate of an aṅga ending in atu and of a non-root aṅga ending in as is lengthened: the penultimate lengthening. By "ugid acām" (Pā. sū. 7-1-70) the augment num. Though the augment num is later and nitya, by force of the statement it must be taken that first comes the lengthening, then the augment num. By "halṅyābbhyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68) the loss of su; by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-23) the loss of t. When the loss of n is to be made by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya, the loss of the conjunct final counts as not done by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1); so the n is not dropped: kakṣīvān. Kakṣīvān is the ṛṣi's name. In the sūtra "na saṃprasāraṇe

original p. 753

Rik 1: grammar

saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. "9-1-37" [as printed, for 6-1-37]), Patañjali in the Mahābhāṣya has begun the statement "kakṣyāyāḥ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 6-1-37-2), that when a name is meant saṃprasāraṇa is to be stated for the word kakṣyā before the suffix matup. By this very statement the form kakṣīvān is established. So some think the reading kakṣīvat in the sūtra āsandīvat… is an interpolation. By "saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 8-2-11), when a name is meant, v for the m of the suffix matup; so the v for m is also established. So it cannot be said that the word kakṣīvat must be placed in the sūtra to give the v ready-made. The sense of chandasīraḥ is that the m of a matup enjoined after a word ending in an i-vowel or in r takes v. So in revān the v for m is established with no trouble; there is no need to strive as seen in the next mantra. Here matup is enjoined after the word kakṣyā, not after an i-final word. So here the justification of v by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-15) is not quite right; it is proper to justify the v for m by saṃjñāyām. After kakṣīvat the accusative singular am; the augment num by ugid acām: kakṣīvantam. The suffix yat is udātta by the suffix accent; the ī that comes as its substitute is udātta by sthānivadbhāva; the suffix matup, being pit, and am, being a sup, are unaccented by anudāttau suppitau.

औशिजः (auśijaḥ): the root vaśa kāntau. With iji carried on from "paṇer ij ādeś ca vaḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 2-70), by "vaśeḥ kic ca" (Uṇ. sū. 2-71) the suffix iji comes after the root vaśa kāntau, and it is kit; so after the root vaś the suffix iji. Vaś + iji: the suffix is kit; so by "grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭi…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-16) the root takes saṃprasāraṇa, u for v; the pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca. Since the suffix is kit, the bar kṅiti ca comes, so the laghūpadha-guṇa by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca does not come for uś: uśij. The analysis is uśijaḥ apatyaṃ pumān. "Tasyāpatyam" (Pā. sū. 4-1-92). "Prāg dīvyato 'ṇ" (Pā. sū. "5-1-83" [as read, ?; for 4-1-83]): up to the sūtra tena dīvyati the heading aṇ runs, so the word aṇ is carried on. The sense of the sūtra [tasyāpatyam] is: after a syntactically fit word ending in the genitive, which is one of the ṅyanta, āpanta or prātipadikas understood from the word first pronounced in the rule enjoining the taddhita suffix, aṇ comes optionally in the sense of offspring; it comes after; it is called a suffix;

Page 754 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

it is initial udātta; and it is a taddhita: so the Kannada sense. When the suffix aṇ comes by this sūtra, uśij + a; by "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-117) the initial vṛddhi, au for u: auśija. After it the nominative singular su, ru and visarga: auśijaḥ. Auśija is final udātta by the suffix accent [as printed].

॥१॥

Page 754 (lower) — Sūkta 18, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: strokes over म (अमीव), व, पु and र्ध; bars under रे, व (अमीवहा), सु and ष्टि; in line 2 a stroke over नः and a bar under स्तु; the bar under क्तु is not certain.

यो रे॒वान्यो अ॑मीव॒हा व॑सु॒वित्पु॑ष्टि॒वर्ध॑नः । [accent ?] स नः॑ सिषक्तु॒ यस्तु॒रः ॥२॥ [accent ?]

yo revā́n yó amīvahā́ vasuvít puṣṭivárdhanaḥ | [accent ?] sá naḥ siṣaktu yás turáḥ ||2|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥ सिसक्तु, with स, is as printed in the Pada.

यः । रेवान् । यः । अमीवऽहा । वसुऽवित् । पुष्टिऽवर्धनः ॥ सः । नः । सिसक्तु । यः । तुरः ॥२॥

yaḥ | revān | yaḥ | amīva 'hā | vasu 'vit | puṣṭi 'vardhanaḥ || saḥ | naḥ | sisaktu | yaḥ | turaḥ ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यो ब्रह्मणस्पती रेवान्धनवान्यश्चामीवहा रोगाणां हन्ता वसुविद्धनलब्धा पुष्टिवर्धनः पुष्टेर्वर्धयिता यश्च तुरस्त्वरोपेतः शीघ्रफलदः स ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्नोऽस्मान् सिषक्तु । सेवताम् । परिगृह्यानुगृह्णात्वित्यर्थः । अत्र सिषक्तुशब्दस्य सेवार्थत्वं यास्क आह । सिषक्तु सचत इति सेवमानस्य । नि. ३-२१ । इति प्रत्याय्यकौ शब्दाविति शेषः ॥ रेवान् । रयिरस्यास्तीति मतुप् । रयेर्मतौ बहुलम् । पा. ६-१-३७-६ । इति यकारस्य संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वम् । छन्दसीर इति वत्वम् । आद्गुणः । ननु वत्वस्यासिद्धत्वाद्बहिरङ्गत्वाच्च प्रागेव गुणे कृते इवर्णाभावान्न वत्वम् । न चान्तादिवच्च । पा. ६-१-८५ । इत्यादिवद्भावेनेवर्णसंपादनं वर्णाश्रयविधौ तत्प्रतिषेधात् । अन्यथा खट्वाभिरित्यत्र सवर्णदीर्घस्यान्तवद्भावेनाकारत्वादतो भिस ऐस् । पा. ७-१-९ । इत्यैसादेशः स्यात् । न च निरवकाशत्वेन वत्वस्यानवकाशत्वम् । अग्निवान्वैदर्भस्तम्बः । उप ब्रह्माणि हरिवः । ऋग्वे. १०-१०४-६ । इत्यादावनवकाशलाभात्

सत्यम् । अत्र गुणप्रवृत्तेः प्रागिकारात्परो मतुप् । कदाचिदिवर्णात्परस्य मतुपः पश्चादेकारादेशेनेवर्णाभावेऽपि भवति वत्वमिति छन्दसीर इति सूत्रकृता विवक्षितम् । अमुमेवाभिप्रायेण हरिव इत्यादिकमुदाहृत्याप्यन्ते वृत्तिकृता आरेवानित्युदाहृतम् । का. ८-२-१५ । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामित्यत्रारेशब्दान्मतुप उदात्तत्वं वक्तव्यम् । पा. ६-१-१७६-१ । इत्यत्रारेशब्दो रेशब्दस्याप्युपलक्षणम् । अत एव हि रेवाँ इन्द्रेत्यादौ मतुप उदात्तत्वं दृष्टम् । अथवा ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामित्यत्रापि कदाचिद्ध्रस्वात्परस्य मतुप उदात्तत्वमित्येव व्याख्येयम् । एवं च संप्रसारणपरपूर्वत्वयोः कृतयोर्गुणात्प्राग्ध्रस्वात्परो मतुबिति रेवानारेवानित्यादौ सर्वत्रोदात्तत्वं सिध्यति । अयमेव सूत्रकृतोऽभिप्रायो वार्तिककृता व्याख्यात इति ॥ अमीवहा । अम रोग इत्येतस्माद्वन्प्रत्ययेनामीवशब्दो निपातितः । तं हन्तीति बहुलं छन्दसीति क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वसुवित् । वसु विन्दतीति वसुवित् । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । उत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पुष्टिवर्धनः । वर्धयतेर्नन्द्यादित्वाल्ल्युः । पा. ३-१-१३४ । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । पुष्टेर्वर्धन इति कर्मणि षष्ठ्याः समासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सिषक्तु । षच समवाये । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । श्लाविति द्वित्वे हलादिशेषे बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्याकारस्येकारः । पा. ७-४-७८ । तुरः । तुर त्वरणे । इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः । कः प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

satyam | atra guṇapravṛtteḥ prāgikārātparo matup | kadācidivarṇātparasya matupaḥ paścādekārādeśenevarṇābhāve 'pi bhavati vatvamiti chandasīra iti sūtrakṛtā vivakṣitam | amumevābhiprāyeṇa hariva ityādikamudāhṛtyāpyante vṛttikṛtā ārevānityudāhṛtam | kā. 8-2-15 | hrasvanuḍbhyāmityatrāreśabdānmatupa udāttatvaṃ vaktavyam | pā. 6-1-176-1 | ityatrāreśabdo reśabdasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | ata eva hi revā~ indretyādau matupa udāttatvaṃ dṛṣṭam | athavā hrasvanuḍbhyāmityatrāpi kadāciddhrasvātparasya matupa udāttatvamityeva vyākhyeyam | evaṃ ca saṃprasāraṇaparapūrvatvayoḥ kṛtayorguṇātprāgdhrasvātparo matubiti revānārevānityādau sarvatrodāttatvaṃ sidhyati | ayameva sūtrakṛto 'bhiprāyo vārtikakṛtā vyākhyāta iti || amīvahā | ama roga ityetasmādvanpratyayenāmīvaśabdo nipātitaḥ | taṃ hantīti bahulaṃ chandasīti kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vasuvit | vasu vindatīti vasuvit | kvipceti kvip | uttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | puṣṭivardhanaḥ | vardhayaternandyāditvāllyuḥ | pā. 3-1-134 | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | puṣṭervardhana iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyāḥ samāsaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | siṣaktu | ṣaca samavāye | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | ślāviti dvitve halādiśeṣe bahulaṃ chandasītyabhyāsasyākārasyekāraḥ | pā. 7-4-78 | turaḥ | tura tvaraṇe | igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ | kaḥ pratyayasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "The Brahmaṇaspati who is revān, wealthy, and who is amīvahā, slayer of diseases, vasuvit, finder of wealth, puṣṭivardhana, increaser of nourishment, and who is tura, swift, giving fruit quickly: may that Brahmaṇaspati siṣaktu, serve us: that is, take us up and favour us. Yāska states that siṣaktu means serving: 'siṣaktu, sacate: of one who serves' (Ni. 3-21); 'two words to be understood' is to be supplied." (Grammatical tail: revān, matup in "he has rayi", saṃprasāraṇa of the y by Pā. 6-1-37-6, the pūrvarūpa, v by chandasīraḥ, guṇa by ād guṇaḥ. An objection: since the v is asiddha and bahiraṅga, guṇa comes first and there is no i, so no v; nor can the i be supplied by treating it as the beginning by antādivac ca (Pā. 6-1-85), since that is barred in a rule depending on letters; otherwise in khaṭvābhiḥ the lengthened vowel, treated as the end, would be a and take ais by Pā. 7-1-9; nor is the v rule left without scope, since it has scope in agnivān vaidarbhaḥ stambaḥ, upa brahmāṇi harivaḥ (Ṛgveda 10-104-6). Answer: true; here, before guṇa applies, the matup follows the i; the author of the sūtra meant chandasīraḥ to give v even when, after a matup once following an i, the e substitute has removed the i. With this intent the Vṛttikāra, after giving harivaḥ and the rest, gives ārevān at the end (Kā. 8-2-15). In the statement on hrasvanuḍbhyām, "the udātta of matup after the word āre" (Pā. 6-1-176-1), āre stands also for re; hence the udātta of matup seen in revām̐ indra and the like. Or in hrasvanuḍbhyām too the sense is "the udātta of a matup once following a short vowel"; thus, saṃprasāraṇa and the pūrvarūpa done, before guṇa the matup follows a short vowel, and the udātta is established everywhere, in revān, ārevān and the rest. This intent of the sūtra's author is what the Vārttikakāra explained. Amīvahā, amīva given ready-made with the suffix van after ama roge; "he kills it", kvip by bahulaṃ chandasi, the accent of the kṛt final member; vasuvit, "he finds wealth", kvip by kvip ca, the accent of the final member; puṣṭivardhanaḥ, lyu after the causative of vṛdh as one of the nandy-ādi (Pā. 3-1-134), udātta before the suffix by liti, compounded with the genitive of the object, puṣṭer vardhanaḥ, the accent of the kṛt final member; siṣaktu, ṣaca samavāye, ślu for śap in the loṭ by bahulaṃ chandasi, doubling by ślau, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, i for the a of the abhyāsa by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. 7-4-78); turaḥ, tura tvaraṇe, ka by igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ, the suffix accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यः (yaḥ) — which Brahmaṇaspati | रेवान् (revān) — is possessed of wealth | यः (yaḥ) — which Brahmaṇaspati | अमीवहा (amīvahā) — removes diseases | वसुवित् (vasuvit) — provides wealth | पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — increases nourishment | यः (yaḥ) — who | तुरः (turaḥ) — gives fruit quickly | सः (saḥ) — that Brahmaṇaspati | नः (naḥ) — us | सिषक्तु (siṣaktu) — may he serve (favour).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Brahmaṇaspati is very rich, a giver of wealth to others, one who brings about nourishment, a quick giver of fruit. May such a Brahmaṇaspati favour us.

॥ English Translation ॥

May he (Brahmanaspati) who is wealthy, the healer of disease; the acquirer of riches, incraaser [sic] of nourishments, the prompt bestower of rewards be favourable to us.

original p. 756

Rik 2: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Revān:

रयिरस्यास्तीति रेवान् ॥

rayirasyāstīti revān ||

("He has rayi: revān.") One who has wealth.

Amīvahā:

अम रोगः । तं हन्तीति अमीवहा ॥

ama rogaḥ | taṃ hantīti amīvahā ||

("Ama is disease; he kills it: amīvahā.") One who destroys disease.

Turaḥ:

त्वरोपेतः शीघ्रफलदः ॥

tvaropetaḥ śīghraphaladaḥ ||

("Possessed of speed, giving fruit quickly.") One who gives fruits quickly. Though the word tura means "possessed of speed, quick", that is, one who works quickly or fast, here the commentator has taken the sense "one who gives fruit to rites quickly".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 756–759, noted briefly

रेवान् (revān): the analysis rayiḥ asya asti. By "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup; the su that is part of the stem takes luk by supo dhātu…: rayi + mat. By "rayer matau bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-37-6), when the suffix matup follows, the word rayi takes saṃprasāraṇa variously: saṃprasāraṇa, i for y; the pūrvarūpa by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108): ra + i + mat. By "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-15) v for the m; by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) e for a + i: re + vat. With ra + i + mat, does the v of chandasīraḥ come first, or the guṇa of ād guṇaḥ? Chandasīraḥ is in the second pāda of the eighth chapter; the sūtra ād guṇaḥ is in the first pāda of the sixth chapter. So by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1), when the guṇa of the earlier rule is made, the v of the later rule, of the tripādī, is asiddha. So it is proper that guṇa comes first. Further, ghaṭakanimittakam antaraṅgam is the definition of antaraṅga. Here, since guṇa is conditioned only by a pair of letters included in the group of conditions of the bahiraṅga rule, the v rule, guṇa is antaraṅga; since the v is conditioned by what contains such a pair of letters, the v is bahiraṅga. So by "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" (paribhāṣā 50), when the antaraṅga guṇa is made, the bahiraṅga v rule is asiddha. For these two reasons it is right that guṇa comes first. If guṇa comes first in this way,

original p. 757

Rik 2: grammar

it becomes re + mat. Now there is no matup after an i-final word. So how does the v come, by "chandasīraḥ" (8-2-15), v for the m of a matup after an i-final or r-final word? Since "antādivac ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-85) says a single substitute is like the end of what precedes and like the beginning of what follows, here we resort to its being like the beginning of what follows, as the intended form requires. Since there is the bar "ubhayata āśrayaṇe nāntādivat", being like the end of the former and like the beginning of the latter cannot both be stated at once. So for the single substitute in the form of guṇa, what follows is the i; it is like its beginning, so it becomes like the i

original p. 758

Rik 2: grammar

itself. So if it is said that following an i is possible, that cannot be said, because i-ness is a property residing in a letter alone. So, since na vā atādrūpyātideśāt [is said], there is no need to make the statement that, in a rule depending on letters, being like the end or the beginning does not come; for in na vā atādrūpyātideśāt, tādrūpya means a property residing in a letter, and the extension does not come from this sūtra at all; since it is said that the statement mentioned before need not be begun, the extension by antādivac ca does not come for the letter-property i-ness. If the extension antādivac ca were admitted in a rule depending on letters, the substitute ais would have to come in khaṭvābhiḥ: for after the word khaṭvā, ṭāp, lengthening of like vowels: khaṭvā. Though this does not end in short a, the letter before the single substitute is short; so by being like the end of the former, the a-ness of the former letter comes to the single substitute. So, since bhis follows a short-a-final, the substitute ais would have to come by "ato bhisa ais" (Pā. sū. 7-1-9). So when an operation depending on letters is made, being like the beginning does not come. In are + mat there is no following an i-final; how then does the v come? For this we say that the v, being an exception, comes earlier than the antaraṅga. For niravakāśo vidhir apavādaḥ: scope means some application in an instance; if that is not found, the rule is an exception. Here, if guṇa comes before the v, it may happen so in the other places too. Since no other instance is found for it, we would call it an exception. Being an exception, we would say the v comes earlier than guṇa; but that cannot be said, because it could be said only on the view in which the v rule is wholly useless. But the v rule has scope in agnivān and harivaḥ in the mantras "agnivān vaidarbhaḥ stambaḥ" (Tai. Brā. "2-2-1-5" [?]) and "upa brahmāṇi harivaḥ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 10-104-6). So this is not an exception. For that reason too it cannot be said that the v comes first as an exception. So how revān is established: though what was said before is true, here, before guṇa comes, with ra + i + mat, the matup stands after the i; so, even if the e substitute comes later to the matup that once followed an i and there is no following an i-final, the v comes; that is why the author, giving harivaḥ and other examples for chandasīraḥ, also cited ārevān at the end. In hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup (Pā. sū. 6-1-176), there is the statement "āreśabdāt matupaḥ" (Pā. sū. Vā. 6-1-176-1), that a matup after the word āre is udātta. Here the word āre also stands for the word re; the sense is that a matup after the word re should be taken as udātta too. That is why in places such as revām̐ indra the matup is udātta. Or, in hrasvamaḍbhyāṃ matup [as printed]

Page 759 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar (end)

too the meaning to be stated is that a matup that once followed a short-final is udātta. So, whether when the word rayi precedes, or when, after the saṃprasāraṇa and pūrvarūpa of y, it stands as ra + i + mat before guṇa comes, the matup follows a short-final; so in all instances, revān, ārevān and the rest, the udātta accent of the matup is established. This is what the sūtrakāra intended; the vārttikakāra explained just this. So in revān both the v and the accent are established. If chandasīraḥ is explained as in the previous mantra, that the m of a matup enjoined after an i-final or r-final word takes v, then even though there is no i after guṇa, the matup is enjoined after the word rayi; since it is enjoined after an i-final, there is no obstacle at all to the v. In hrasvanuḍbhyām the Bhāṣya has the vārttika "reśabdāc ca". So there is no room at all for explaining āre as standing for something.

अमीवहा (amīvahā): the root ama roge. By "śevayahva…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-153" [?]) the suffix van after the root am and the augment īṭ for it are given ready-made. Amīvaṃ hanti: being meant, though another upapada is connected, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 3-2-88) kvip comes variously after the root han: amīvahan; han is final udātta by the root accent; after compounding, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent of the kṛt final member comes and that accent stays.

वसुवित् (vasuvit): vasu vindati iti vasuvit: by kvip ca, after vidḷ lābhe, kvip; the accent of the kṛt final member as before.

पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ): puṣṭiṃ vardhayati iti puṣṭivardhanaḥ; the root vṛdhu vṛddhau. After it ṇic. In

नन्दिवाशिमदिदूषिसाधिवर्धिशोभिरोचिभ्यो ण्यन्तेभ्यः संज्ञायाम्

nandivāśimadidūṣisādhivardhiśobhirocibhyo ṇyantebhyaḥ saṃjñāyām

the ṇic-final root vṛdh is read among the nandy-ādi. So after it the suffix lyu by "nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-134); the loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi; ana for yu by yuvor anākau; the laghūpadha-guṇa, followed by r: vardhana. By "liti" (Pā. sū. "2-1-1" [as printed, for 6-1-193]) what precedes the suffix ana is udātta. Puṣṭer vardhanaḥ: compounded with the genitive of the object; the accent of the kṛt final member.

सिषक्तु (siṣaktu): ṣaca samavāye; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; loṭ, tip; by eruḥ u for the i of ti. Śap by kartari śap; for it, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-76), in the Veda ślu (loss) comes variously for śap: so ślu; doubling by "ślau" (Pā. sū. 6-1-10): sac sac + tu; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60) the c of the abhyāsa drops; by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Ṛ. saṃ. [as printed, for Pā. sū.] "2-4-78" [as printed, for 7-4-78]) the a of the abhyāsa takes i variously in the Veda: i for the a of the first s: sisac + tu; by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-30) k for c; by ādeśapratyayayoḥ ṣ for the second s: siṣaktu.

तुरः (turaḥ): the root tura tvaraṇe, with i/u as penultimate. After it, by "igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-135), the suffix ka; the k is called it and dropped; the suffix is kit, so the laghūpadha-guṇa does not come. By ādyudāttaś ca the suffix accent comes; turaḥ is final udātta.

अररुषो मर्त्यस्योपद्रवं कर्तुमस्मत्समीपं प्राप्तस्य शत्रुरूपस्य मनुष्यस्य धूर्तिर्हिंसकः शंसः शंसनम् । अधिक्षेप इत्यर्थः । तादृशो वाग्विशेषो नोऽस्मान्मा प्रणक् । मा संपृणक्तु । शत्रुणा प्रयुक्तोऽधिक्षेपः कदाचिदस्मान्मा प्राप्नोत्वित्यर्थः । तदर्थं हे ब्रह्मणस्पते नोऽस्मान्रक्ष । पालय ॥ मा । निपातः । शंसनं शंसः । भावे घञ् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अररुषः । अर्तेररुः । उ. ४-७९ । इत्यन्तर्भावितण्यर्थादृ गतावित्यस्मादरुस् । गुणो रपरत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरे प्राप्ते वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । धूर्तिः । धुर्वी हिंसार्थः । क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामिति क्तिच् । तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु चेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । उपधायाश्च । पा. ७-१-१०१ । इत्युपधादीर्घत्वम् । वलि लोपं बाधित्वोठि प्राप्ते । पा. ६-४-१९ । राल्लोपः । पा.
