६-४-२१ । इति वकारलोपः । प्रणक् । पृची संपर्के । लङस्तिप् । इतश्चेतीकारलोपः । हल्ङ्यादिलोपः । कुत्वम् । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । तस्य व्यत्ययो बहुलम् । पा. ३-१-८५ । इत्याडागमः । यणादेशः । अकारस्यागमानुदात्तत्वं बाधित्वा व्यत्ययेनोदात्तत्वम् । चादिलोपे विभाषेति निघाताभावः । मर्त्यस्य । मृङ् प्राणत्यागे । असिहसिमृ इत्यादिना । उ. ३-८६ । औणादिकस्तन्प्रत्ययः । मर्तेषु भव इत्यर्थे भवे छन्दसीति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । रक्ष । रक्ष पालने । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । रक्षा णः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । उपसर्गाद्बहुलम् । पा. ८-४-२८ । इति बहुलग्रहणादनुपसर्गादपि नसो णत्वम् । ब्रह्मणस्पते । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति संहितायां विसर्गस्य सकारः । सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवद्भावात्पदद्वयस्यामन्त्रितनिघातः ॥

6-4-21 | iti vakāralopaḥ | praṇak | pṛcī saṃparke | laṅastip | itaścetīkāralopaḥ | halṅyādilopaḥ | kutvam | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | tasya vyatyayo bahulam | pā. 3-1-85 | ityāḍāgamaḥ | yaṇādeśaḥ | akārasyāgamānudāttatvaṃ bādhitvā vyatyayenodāttatvam | cādilope vibhāṣeti nighātābhāvaḥ | martyasya | mṛṅ prāṇatyāge | asihasimṛ ityādinā | u. 3-86 | auṇādikastanpratyayaḥ | marteṣu bhava ityarthe bhave chandasīti yat | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | rakṣa | rakṣa pālane | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | rakṣā ṇaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | upasargādbahulam | pā. 8-4-28 | iti bahulagrahaṇādanupasargādapi naso ṇatvam | brahmaṇaspate | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti saṃhitāyāṃ visargasya sakāraḥ | subāmantrite parāṅgavadbhāvātpadadvayasyāmantritanighātaḥ ||

Translation: "May the dhūrti, harmful, śaṃsa, speech, that is, reviling, of the araruṣ mortal, the man in the form of an enemy who has come near us to do harm: may such a particular speech mā praṇak, not touch us: that is, may the reviling set going by the enemy never reach us. For that, O Brahmaṇaspati, rakṣa, protect us." (Grammatical tail: mā, a particle; śaṃsaḥ, "speaking", ghañ of the action, initial udātta as ñit; araruṣaḥ, arus by arter aruḥ (Uṇ. 4-79 [?]) after ṛ gatau with the causative sense included, guṇa with r, initial udātta, though the suffix accent was due, as one of the vṛṣa-ādi; dhūrtiḥ, dhurvī in the sense of harm, ktic by kticktau ca saṃjñāyām, no iṭ by titutra…, the penultimate lengthened by Pā. 7-1-101; overriding the loss before val, ūṭh being due (Pā. 6-4-19), the v lost by rāl lopaḥ (Pā. 6-4-21); praṇak, pṛcī saṃparke, tip for laṅ, the i lost by itaś ca, halṅyādi loss, the guttural, śnam by rudhādibhyaḥ, for it the augment āṭ by Pā. 3-1-85, yaṇ, the a made udātta by exchange, overriding the unaccentedness of augments, not lowered by cādilope vibhāṣā; martyasya, mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, the Uṇādi tan by asihasimṛ… (Uṇ. 3-86 [?]), yat by bhave chandasi in "being among mortals", initial udātta by yato 'nāvaḥ; rakṣa, rakṣa pālane, śap unaccented as pit, the root accent stays, not lowered at the start of the pāda; rakṣā ṇaḥ, lengthened by dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ, ṇ for the n of nas though not after a preverb, by the bahula of Pā. 8-4-28; brahmaṇaspate, s for the visarga in the Saṃhitā by ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…, both words unaccented as a vocative by parāṅgavadbhāva.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अररुषः (araruṣaḥ) — come with the intent to harm (in the form of an enemy) | मर्त्यस्य (martyasya) — of a man | धूर्तिः (dhūrtiḥ) — causing harm | शंसः (śaṃsaḥ) — speech in the form of reviling | नः (naḥ) — us | मा प्रणक् (mā praṇak) — may it not touch (for that) | हे ब्रह्मणस्पते (he brahmaṇaspate) — O Brahmaṇaspati | नः (naḥ) — us | रक्ष (rakṣa) — protect.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Brahmaṇaspati, protect us so that no trouble comes to us from the reviling words our enemies speak.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the harmful imprecation of the wicked mortal not reach us ; protect us, O Brahmanaspati.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Śaṃsaḥ: śaṃsanam. Though this word means speech, saying, here the commentator has supported the sense, for the words dhūrtiḥ śaṃsaḥ, of reviling words, bad words, abuse, words joined with the wish that harm come.

original p. 761

Rik 3: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Araruṣaḥ martyasya: of a man with the intent to do harm or trouble.

Mā praṇak:

मा संपृणक्तु ॥

mā saṃpṛṇaktu ||

("May it not touch.") May it not touch: "not reach us". The word mā expresses prohibition.

Rakṣa: the last syllable of this word is long in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha to suit the metre.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 761–764, noted briefly

मा (mā): this is a particle; so it is initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Pā. sū. "80" [as printed; a Phiṭ-sūtra]).

शंसः (śaṃsaḥ): the root śaṃsu stutau. By "bhāve" (Pā. sū. 3-3-18) ghañ in the sense of the action; being ñit, it is initial udātta by ñnityādir nityam. The analysis is śaṃsanaṃ śaṃsaḥ.

अररुषः (araruṣaḥ): by "arter aruḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "4-5[?]" [?]) the suffix arus comes after the root ṛ gatau, with the causative sense included: ṛ + arus; guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), followed by r by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51): ar + arus, ararus. By ādyudāttaś ca the a of the suffix arus would be udātta; but since the vṛṣa-ādi is an ākṛtigaṇa, this word is to be included there; so initial udātta comes by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203). Genitive singular ṅas: ararus + as; by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for the s after the u; ru for the final s by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66), visarga by "kharavasānayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-15): araruṣaḥ. Some derive araruṣaḥ another way: the root rā ādāne; after it liṭ; the substitute kvasu by "kvasuś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-107); doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8): rā rā + vas; by "vasv ekājādghasām" (Pā. sū. 7-2-67) the augment iṭ for the vas after the ā-final root rā; by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-64) the ā of the second rā drops; by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59) the first rā is shortened: rarivas. In the nominative singular it becomes rarivān, like sedivān. When the genitive singular ṅas [as printed: jas] comes, saṃprasāraṇa by "vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-4-131).

original p. 762

Rik 3: grammar

With rarāvas [as printed], if the genitive singular is added, the saṃprasāraṇa comes and the vas becomes us; so it is not val-initial. So, though the augment iṭ enjoined by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ is antaraṅga, there is a possibility that its condition, being val-initial, is destroyed by the bahiraṅga rule of saṃprasāraṇa. For that reason, by "akṛtavyūhāḥ pāṇinīyāḥ" (paribhāṣā 42) (if the destruction of the condition of an antaraṅga rule by a bahiraṅga rule is possible, the antaraṅga rule does not come first), some state the exclusion of the augment iṭ, that it does not come where saṃprasāraṇa comes. Others again, on the view of the padāvadhika explanation, that words are derived as having case-endings, if the word is analysed it is rarāvas + as. Now both the augment iṭ and the saṃprasāraṇa are due. Though the augment iṭ is antaraṅga, the saṃprasāraṇa is a rule enjoined by naming a particular word, so, being pratipadokta, it alone comes first. Then, since there is no val-initial ārdhadhātuka, the augment iṭ does not come: in this way they state the exclusion of the augment iṭ. Now, even without the augment iṭ, by "asaṃyogāl liṭ kit" (Pā. sū. "1-2-5" [?]) a non-pit liṭ not after a conjunct is kit; since the ārdhadhātuka us, which is kit, follows, the loss of ā comes by āto lopa iṭi ca. The ṣ and the rest as before. When raruṣaḥ is established in this way, if nañ is compounded with na raruṣaḥ, the form araruṣaḥ results. Now by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the first member, an indeclinable, comes. The first member, nañ, is a particle, so it is initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Pā. sū. "80" [as printed]). After compounding too this comes by the accent of the first member. So it need not be included in the vṛṣa-ādi group. The Vedabhāṣyakāra too has explained it in this same way at "gurudveṣo araruṣe dadhanti" (Tai. Brā. [no number printed]). Besides, in "yo no agne ararivān" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-147-4) there is agreement of another mantra with this kind of explanation. So the derivation in this way is right for araruṣa. The suffix enjoined in arter aruḥ ends in u, not in s. That is why the word araru ends in u in the mantras "kaṃ cid yāvīr araruṃ śūra martyam" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-129-3) and "apāraruṃ adevayuṃ jano jahi" [no number printed]. If arter aruḥ enjoined an s-final suffix, the accent of araruṣaḥ would be

original p. 763

Rik 3: grammar

hard to account for, and besides, the words araru in the mantras just cited could not be formed. So the suffix enjoined by arter aruḥ ends in u only. It is more fitting to describe araruṣaḥ as formed from the root rā.

धूर्तिः (dhūrtiḥ): the root dhurvī hiṃsārthaḥ. The suffix ktic by "kticktau ca saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 3-3-174). The augment iṭ is due for it by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-35); but by "ti-tu-tra-ta-tha-si-su-sara-ka-seṣu ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-9) these ten suffixes do not take the augment iṭ; so ti takes no iṭ. With dhurv + ti, by "upadhāyāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-78), when a consonant follows the r or v standing in the penultimate place of a root, the i, u, ṛ, ḷ before that r or v is lengthened: so the u is lengthened: dhūrv + ti. In "upadhāyāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-101) the preceding sūtra "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-100) is carried on; so its sense is that the ṝ in the penultimate of a root takes i. So the lengthening must be stated by upadhāyāṃ ca [the bhāṣya's citation of 7-1-101 being taken as for upadhāyāṃ ca]. There the sūtras "rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-76) and "hali ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-77) are carried on, and from "sipi dhātor rur vā" (Pā. sū. 8-2-74) the word dhātoḥ too. So upadhāyāṃ ca enjoins lengthening. With dhūrv + ti, the loss of v would come by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66). But overriding that, by "cchvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-19), when an initial-nasal suffix follows, or kvip, or a jhal-initial suffix that is kit or ṅit, ś for ch with the augment tuk, and the substitute ūṭh for v; since the kit ktic, jhal-initial, follows, the substitute ūṭh for v is due. Yet overriding this substitute ūṭh too, by "rāl lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-21), when kvip, a jhal-initial suffix, or an initial-nasal suffix follows, the ch with the augment tuk and the v after an r drop; so the v after the r drops: dhūr + ti = dhūrti.

प्रणक् (praṇak): the root pṛcī saṃparke, of the rudh-ādi class. After it laṅ, 3rd singular tip. By "itaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-100) the i drops. The vikaraṇa śnam enjoined by "rudhādibhyaḥ śnam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-78), being mit, comes after the ṛ by "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-47): pṛnac + t. By "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85) the augment āṭ for the vikaraṇa śnam: pṛ + an + c + t. By "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) yaṇ, r for ṛ: pranac + t. By "halṅyābbhyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68) the t drops; by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-30) k for c; by "aṭkupvāṅ…" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for n: praṇak. The a that came as an augment to the śnam would be unaccented by āgamā anudāttāḥ; by exchange it is udātta. By "cādilope vibhāṣā" (Pā. sū. 8-1-63), when ca, vā, ha, aha, eva are dropped, the first tiṅanta is optionally not unaccented; because of this bar praṇak is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

original p. 764

Rik 3: grammar (end)

मर्त्यस्य (martyasya): the root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge. "Hasimṛgriṇvāmidamilūpūdhurvibhyas tan" (Uṇ. sū. "3-366" [?]): the sense of the sūtra is that the suffix tan comes after the roots hase hasane, mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, gṝ nigaraṇe, iṇ gatau, vā gatigandhanayoḥ, ama gatyādiṣu, damu upaśame, lūñ chedane, pūñ pavane, dhurvī hiṃsāyām. Here the Vedabhāṣyakāra has read at the beginning one more root, asi; it is not seen in the sūtras as they now stand. With tan after the root mṛ, mṛ + ta; guṇa by sārvadhātuka…, followed by r: marta. The analysis marteṣu bhavaḥ: the suffix yat by "bhave chandasi" (Pā. sū. 4-4-110); the a drops by yasyeti ca. The svarita due by tit svaritam is overridden by "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-213), and initial udātta comes.

रक्ष (rakṣa): the root rakṣa pālane. Loṭ, 2nd singular sip; śap by kartari śap; hi by ser hy apic ca; luk of hi by ato heḥ. Śap is pit, so unaccented by anudāttau suppitau; the root accent alone remains. Since it stands at the start of a pāda, the bar "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) comes; so it is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ. Rakṣā ṇaḥ: by "dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-135) it is lengthened in the Saṃhitā. "Upasargād bahulam" (Pā. sū. 8-4-28): the sense of this is that the n of nas after the r or ṣ in a preverb takes ṇ. By nas both the nas that stands for the word nāsikā and the nas enjoined as bahuvacanasya vasnasau are taken; here it is the second nas. But it stands after the word rakṣā, which is not a preverb. Yet by force of the mention of bahula, ṇ comes even for the n of a nas after an r or ṣ not marked as a preverb. In fact, there is no need to labour to establish the ṇ by the mention of bahula here. "Naś ca dhātusthoruṣubhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-27): the sense of the sūtra is that the n of the nas standing for asmad after the r or ṣ in a root, after the word uru, and after ṣu (the ṣ coming for ṣuñ abhiṣave), takes ṇ. Here rakṣa is a root, and it contains ṣ. So the n of the nas after the ṣ, one of the r or ṣ contained in the root, takes ṇ by this sūtra.

ब्रह्मणस्पते (brahmaṇaspate): for the visarga belonging to the genitive in brahmaṇaḥ, in the Saṃhitā the substitute s by "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…" (Pā. sū. 8-3-53). Pate is a vocative. So the word before it takes parāṅgavadbhāva by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. 2-1-2). So the name vocative rests on the whole brahmaṇaspate. So by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) both words are wholly unaccented.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: strokes over घा, रि, ह्म, तिः, सो and र्त्य; bars under वी, ति (रिष्यति), द्रो, ण, हि and ति (हिनोति). A mark over मि of यमिन्द्रो is not clear.

स घा॑ वी॒रो न रि॑ष्यति॒ यमिन्द्रो॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ । [accent ?] सो॑मो हि॒नोति॒ मर्त्य॑म् ॥४॥ [accent ?]

sá ghā vīró ná riṣyati yám indro bráhmaṇaspátiḥ | [accent ?] somo hinóti mártyam ||4|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । घ । वीरः । न । रिष्यति । यम् । इन्द्रः । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ सोमः । हिनोति । मर्त्यम् ॥४॥

saḥ | gha | vīraḥ | na | riṣyati | yam | indraḥ | brahmaṇaḥ | patiḥ || somaḥ | hinoti | martyam ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इन्द्रो देवो यं मर्त्यं यक्ष्यमाणं हिनोति प्राप्नोति वर्धयति वा । तथा ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्देवो हिनोति । तथा सोमो हिनोति । स घ स एव यजमानो वीरो वीर्ययुक्तः सन्न रिष्यति । न विनश्यति ॥ घ । चादिरनुदात्तः । संहितायामृचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् । पा. ६-३-१३३ । इति दीर्घः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिः । उक्तम् । हिनोति । हि गतौ वृद्धौ च । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । तिपः पित्त्वाच्छ्नुप्रत्ययस्वर एव शिष्यते ॥

indro devo yaṃ martyaṃ yakṣyamāṇaṃ hinoti prāpnoti vardhayati vā | tathā brahmaṇaspatirdevo hinoti | tathā somo hinoti | sa gha sa eva yajamāno vīro vīryayuktaḥ sanna riṣyati | na vinaśyati || gha | cādiranudāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāmṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām | pā. 6-3-133 | iti dīrghaḥ | brahmaṇaspatiḥ | uktam | hinoti | hi gatau vṛddhau ca | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | tipaḥ pittvācchnupratyayasvara eva śiṣyate ||

Translation: "The mortal, about to sacrifice, whom the god Indra hinoti, reaches or makes to grow; likewise whom the god Brahmaṇaspati furthers; likewise whom Soma furthers: sa gha, that very sacrificer, being vīra, possessed of valour, na riṣyati, does not perish." (Grammatical tail: gha, unaccented as one of the ca-ādi; lengthened in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 6-3-133; brahmaṇaspatiḥ, explained; hinoti, hi gatau vṛddhau ca, śnu by svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ; since tip is pit, the accent of the suffix śnu alone stays.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | यम् (yam) — which | मर्त्यम् (martyam) — sacrificer (performing the sacrifice) | हिनोति (hinoti) — reaches, or protects | ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (brahmaṇaspatiḥ) — Brahmaṇaspati too | हिनोति (hinoti) — protects | सोमः (somaḥ) — (likewise) the deity Soma | हिनोति (hinoti) — protects | सः घ (saḥ gha) — that very man | वीरः (vīraḥ) — being possessed of valour | न रिष्यति (na riṣyati) — does not perish.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

For the sacrificer devoted to the sacrifice, the three deities Indra, Brahmaṇaspati and Soma bring increase; that is, they become his protectors. A man who has become worthy of their grace never comes to ruin.

original p. 766

Rik 4: English, Special Topics and grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

That valiant man whom Indra, Brahmanaspati and Soma protect never perishes.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This ṛk is addressed to the three deities Indra, Brahmaṇaspati and Soma. The intent is: the man whom these deities take to themselves, that is, favour, lives as a hero, and never meets with ruin.

Ghā: this syllable is long in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha to suit the metre.

Yaṃ martyam: which man; that is, the man who worships Indra, Brahmaṇaspati and Soma.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 766–767, noted briefly

घ (gha): since the ca-ādi group is an ākṛtigaṇa, this is included in it. So it is unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 4-84). In the Saṃhitā, by "ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. sū. 6-3-133), the word gha takes in the sequence gha (gh followed by a). Since the lengthening of gha is seen in the Veda, it is to be taken this way. "Kṛtrimākṛtrimayoḥ kṛtrimasyaiva grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā):

कृत्रिमाकृत्रिमयोः कृत्रिमस्यैव ग्रहणम्

kṛtrimākṛtrimayoḥ kṛtrimasyaiva grahaṇam

kṛtrima means "fixed by the convention of grammar"; akṛtrima means "known in the world"; the sense of the paribhāṣā is that when both could be taken, the kṛtrima is taken. By "taraptamapau ghaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-22) the suffixes tarap and tamap have this conventional name in grammar. Yet here it is not taken in the way just stated; for in the Veda lengthening is not seen for tarap and tamap, while lengthening is seen for gha. Since the sūtra says ṛci, it must apply in the Ṛgveda alone. So, if tarap and the rest were taken, the sūtra would have no purpose. So the word gha itself is taken. For tha [as printed], the 2nd plural of taṅ [as printed], when the substitute ta comes by tasthasthamipām, it becomes ṅit by sārvadhātukam apit; the ta substituted for tha, having this ṅit-ness, is taken. When lengthening comes to gha by this sūtra, it becomes ghā.

ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (brahmaṇaspatiḥ): by "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ pati…" (Pā. sū. 8-3-53) s for the visarga belonging to the genitive.

Page 767 (upper) — Rik 4: grammar (end)

हिनोति (hinoti): the root hi gatau vṛddhau ca. Laṭ, tip. By "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-73) the vikaraṇa śnu: hi + nu + ti. With ti as condition, guṇa for śnu by "sārvadhātukārdha…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84): o. By "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) hi [as printed; nu is meant] is ṅit. Since the bar kṅiti ca comes, the ik-guṇa for hi, with nu as condition, does not come. Tip is pit, so unaccented by anudāttau…; the accent of the suffix śnu alone remains.

he brahmaṇaspate tvaṃ taṃ martyamanuṣṭhātāraṃ manuṣyamaṃhasaḥ pāpātpāhīti śeṣaḥ | tathā somaḥ pātu | indraśca pātu dakṣiṇākhyā devatā ca pātu || dakṣiṇā | dakṣa vṛddhau | drudakṣibhyāminan | u. 2-50 | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | aṃhasaḥ | nabviṣayasyetyādinādyudāttaḥ ||34||

Translation: "O Brahmaṇaspati, you (protect, is to be supplied) that mortal, the performer, from aṃhas, sin. Likewise may Soma protect; may Indra protect; and may the deity called Dakṣiṇā protect." (Grammatical tail: dakṣiṇā, dakṣa vṛddhau, inan by drudakṣibhyām inan (Uṇ. 2-50), initial udātta as nit; aṃhasaḥ, initial udātta by nabviṣayasya….)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) ब्रह्मणस्पते ((he) brahmaṇaspate) — O Brahmaṇaspati | त्वम् (tvam) — you | तं मर्त्यम् (taṃ martyam) — that man (the performer) | अंहसः (aṃhasaḥ) — from sin (protect) | सोमः (somaḥ) — the deity Soma | पातु (pātu) — may he protect | इन्द्रः च (indraḥ ca) — and Indra | पातु (pātu) — may he protect | दक्षिणा (dakṣiṇā) — the deity called Dakṣiṇā too | पातु (pātu) — may she protect.

original p. 768

Rik 5: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Brahmaṇaspati, protect the sacrificer so that he does no sinful deed: you, Indra, Soma and Dakṣiṇā, all of you.

॥ English Translation ॥

Do you Brahmanaspati, and do you Soma, Indra. and Dakshina protect that man from sin.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this ṛk the deities Brahmaṇaspati, Soma, Indra and Dakṣiṇā are set forth.

Dakṣiṇā: in this ṛk the word dakṣiṇā indicates the deity presiding over the dakṣiṇā. For the word dakṣiṇā Yāska gives this derivation of sense (Ni. "1-7" [?]):

दक्षिणा दक्षतेः समर्धयतिकर्मणो व्यृद्धं समर्धयतीति । अपि वा प्रदक्षिणागमनात् । दिशमभिप्रेत्य दिग्घस्तप्रकृतिः दक्षिणो हस्तो दक्षतेरुत्साहकर्मणः । दाशतेर्वा स्याद्दानकर्मणः ॥

dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayatikarmaṇo vyṛddhaṃ samardhayatīti | api vā pradakṣiṇāgamanāt | diśamabhipretya digghastaprakṛtiḥ dakṣiṇo hasto dakṣaterutsāhakarmaṇaḥ | dāśatervā syāddānakarmaṇaḥ ||

("Dakṣiṇā, from dakṣ, meaning 'to make prosper': it makes prosperous what has failed; or from going round to the right; with reference to the quarter, it has the right hand as its source; the right hand, from dakṣ, meaning energy; or it may be from dāś, meaning giving": editorial and tentative.) He gives four kinds of sense:

  1. Dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayatikarmaṇo vyṛddhaṃ samardhayatīti: the word dakṣiṇā comes from the root dakṣ; for this root the sense is "make (wealth) grow". Since the little wealth spent in the sacrifice, that is, given as dakṣiṇā, is made to grow greatly (as fruit), the word is named dakṣiṇā.

  2. Api vā pradakṣiṇāgamanāt: since on the sacrificial altar one goes round the places called gārhapatya, sadas and āgnīdhrīya clockwise and stands in the inner altar, the going round clockwise done in this way is named dakṣiṇā.

  3. Diśam abhipretya dighastaprakṛtiḥ dakṣiṇo hasto dakṣater utsāhakarmaṇaḥ: since among the hands of Prajāpati, who faces east, the right hand faces south (is on the side of the southern quarter), and since the right hand does with energy whatever work is to be done, it has become usage to call the right hand dakṣiṇo hastaḥ with the word dakṣiṇa.

  4. Dāśater vā syād dānakarmaṇaḥ: the root dāś means giving. Since in giving one usually uses the right hand, the act of giving is named dakṣiṇā.

Page 769 (upper) — Rik 5: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Of these four kinds of sense, the last, the act of giving, is what is meant in this ṛk as the deity presiding over the dakṣiṇā.

Pātu, aṃhasaḥ: aṃhaḥ means sin. "May he protect from sin" means: may he protect by giving good understanding so that one does no sinful deeds.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar on p. 769, noted briefly

ब्रह्मणस्पते (brahmaṇaspate): explained in an earlier mantra.

दक्षिणा (dakṣiṇā): the root dakṣa vṛddhau. By "drudakṣibhyām inan" (Uṇ. sū. "2-208" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-50), after the roots dru gatau and dakṣa vṛddhau the suffix inan; so after dakṣ the suffix inan; the n of the suffix is called it: dakṣi + na; by "aṭkupvāṅnum…" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for n. What is to be given in rites enjoined by the śāstra, such as sacrifice, is named dakṣiṇā; in this sense it is feminine. The Medinī-kośa has

द्रविणं न द्वयोर्वित्ते काञ्चने च पराक्रमे । दक्षिणा दक्षिणोद्भूतसरलच्छन्दवृत्तिषु । अवामे त्रिषु यज्ञादिविधिदाने दिशि स्त्रियाम् ॥

draviṇaṃ na dvayorvitte kāñcane ca parākrame | dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇodbhūtasaralacchandavṛttiṣu | avāme triṣu yajñādividhidāne diśi striyām ||

("Draviṇa, not of two genders, is wealth, gold and valour; dakṣiṇā … in the senses of south-born, straight, will and conduct; in the three genders for 'not left'; feminine for the gift at a sacrifice and the like, and for the quarter": editorial and tentative; the lines are as printed.) So, with ṭāp by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-4) and lengthening of like vowels, it becomes dakṣiṇā. Since dakṣiṇa ends in a suffix with n as it, it is initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197).

अंहसः (aṃhasaḥ): initial udātta by "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" [no number printed].

Rik 6: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अनुप्रवचनीयचरोर्होमे सदसस्पतिमित्येषा विनियुक्ता । तथा च गृह्ये मेखलामाबध्येति खण्डे पठ्यते । आचार्यः समन्वारब्धे जुहुयात्सदसस्पतिमद्भुतम् । आ. गृ. १-२२-११ । इति ॥ मेधां लब्धुं सदसस्पतिमेतन्नामकं देवमयासिषम् । प्राप्तवानस्मि । कीदृशम् । अद्भुतमाश्चर्यकरम् । इन्द्रस्य प्रियं सोमपाने सहचारित्वात् । काम्यं कमनीयम् । सनिं धनस्य दातारम् ॥ सदसः । षद्लृ विशरणादौ । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पतिम् । पातेर्डतिः । उ. ४-५७ । टिलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । प्रियम् । इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः । इयङादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । काम्यम् । कामयतेरचो यत् । णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सनिम् । षणु दाने । धात्वादेः षः सः । अच इरित्यनुवृत्तौ खनिकष्यञ्ज्यसिवसिवनिसनिध्वनिग्रन्थिचरिभ्यश्च । उ. ४-१४० । इति इप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अयासिषम् । या प्रापणे । लुङ् । मिपोऽमादेशः । यमरमनमातां सक् च । पा. ७-२-७३ । इति सिच इडागमः । धातोः सगागमः । निघातः ॥

anupravacanīyacarorhome sadasaspatimityeṣā viniyuktā | tathā ca gṛhye mekhalāmābadhyeti khaṇḍe paṭhyate | ācāryaḥ samanvārabdhe juhuyātsadasaspatimadbhutam | ā. gṛ. 1-22-11 | iti || medhāṃ labdhuṃ sadasaspatimetannāmakaṃ devamayāsiṣam | prāptavānasmi | kīdṛśam | adbhutamāścaryakaram | indrasya priyaṃ somapāne sahacāritvāt | kāmyaṃ kamanīyam | saniṃ dhanasya dātāram || sadasaḥ | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇādau | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | patim | pāterḍatiḥ | u. 4-57 | ṭilopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | priyam | igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ | iyaṅādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | kāmyam | kāmayateraco yat | ṇeraniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | sanim | ṣaṇu dāne | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | aca irityanuvṛttau khanikaṣyañjyasivasivanisanidhvanigranthicaribhyaśca | u. 4-140 | iti ipratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | ayāsiṣam | yā prāpaṇe | luṅ | mipo 'mādeśaḥ | yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca | pā. 7-2-73 | iti sica iḍāgamaḥ | dhātoḥ sagāgamaḥ | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "This ṛk sadasaspatim is applied in the oblation of the anupravacanīya rice-pot. So it is read in the Gṛhya, in the section beginning mekhalām ābadhya: 'While the teacher is held on to, he should offer with sadasaspatim adbhutam' (Āśv. Gṛ. 1-22-11). To obtain medhā, intelligence, I have ayāsiṣam, approached, the god named Sadasaspati. Of what kind? Adbhuta, causing wonder; priya, dear, to Indra, as his companion in soma-drinking; kāmya, lovely; sani, a giver of wealth." (Grammatical tail: sadasaḥ, ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau, asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun, initial udātta as nit; patim, ḍati by pāter ḍatiḥ (Uṇ. 4-57), the loss of the ṭi, the suffix accent; priyam, ka by igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ, the substitute iyaṅ, the suffix accent; kāmyam, yat by aco yat after the causative of kam, the loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi, initial udātta by yato 'nāvaḥ; sanim, ṣaṇu dāne, s for ṣ, the suffix i by Uṇ. 4-140 with aca iḥ carried on, the suffix accent; ayāsiṣam, yā prāpaṇe, luṅ, am for mip, the augment iṭ for sic by Pā. 7-2-73, the augment sak for the root, wholly unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मेधाम् (medhām) — the power of intelligence | लब्धुम् (labdhum) — to obtain | अद्भुतम् (adbhutam) — wonder-working | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — to Indra | प्रियम् (priyam) — dear | काम्यम् (kāmyam) — lovely | सनिम् (sanim) — giving wealth | सदसस्पतिम् (sadasaspatim) — the deity called Sadasaspati | अयासिषम् (ayāsiṣam) — I have approached (taken refuge with, or pray to).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

I take refuge with (pray to) the deity called Sadasaspati, who is wonder-working, that is, does wondrous daring deeds, who is dear to Indra, of lovely form, and a giver of wealth, to obtain the power of intelligence.

॥ English Translation ॥

I pray, for wisdom, Sadasaspati, the wonderful, the beloved of Indra, the dcsirable [sic], and the giver of riches.

original p. 771

Rik 6: Special Topics

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Sadasaspati is the deity of this ṛk. In domestic rites such as marriage, this ṛk sadasaspati is recited when the oblation called the anupravacanīya rice-pot is made. In the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra, in the section mekhalām ābadhya, the order of application of this ṛk is given as ācāryaḥ samanvārabdhe juhuyāt sadasaspatim adbhutam (Āś. Gṛ. 1-22-11).

Sadasaspatim: the deity named Sadasaspati. To give the sense of the parts, sadasaḥ patim means the lord of the sadas or of the assembly. What Skandasvāmin says on this matter is acceptable:

चतस्रः सादसस्पत्याः । सदः प्रसिद्धं यज्ञगृहं तस्याधिपतिः सदसस्पतिः । कोऽसौ । अग्निः । कुत एतत् । अग्नेः सर्वयज्ञाधिपतित्वात् । अपि च यज्ञसाधनहविष्कृतिसमर्थनाद्यग्निकर्मदर्शनात्तद्देवत्याश्चतस्रश्चर्चः । सदसस्पतिमग्निम् ॥

catasraḥ sādasaspatyāḥ | sadaḥ prasiddhaṃ yajñagṛhaṃ tasyādhipatiḥ sadasaspatiḥ | ko 'sau | agniḥ | kuta etat | agneḥ sarvayajñādhipatitvāt | api ca yajñasādhanahaviṣkṛtisamarthanādyagnikarmadarśanāttaddevatyāścatasraścarcaḥ | sadasaspatimagnim ||

("Four ṛks are to Sadasaspati. Sadas is the well-known sacrificial hall; its lord is Sadasaspati. Who is he? Agni. Why so? Because Agni is lord of all sacrifices; and also, since Agni's acts, such as preparing the oblations, the means of sacrifice, are seen, the four ṛks have him as deity: Sadasaspati is Agni": editorial and tentative.) This ṛk and the three ṛks that follow, four ṛks in all, have Sadasaspati as deity. Sadas means the well-known sacrificial hall; since he is its lord, he is named Sadasaspati. Who is the lord of this hall? Agni. For Agni is well known as the lord of all sacrifices. Moreover, since these four ṛks set forth acts connected with Agni, such as preparing the oblation, the means of sacrifice, and the acts of Agni, it is beyond dispute that Sadasaspati is Agni. The name Sadasaspati is not found elsewhere in the Ṛgveda apart from these ṛks. Yāska too has said nothing about this Sadasaspati. So it must be accepted that what Skandasvāmin says is fitting.

Adbhutam: the commentator says āścaryakaram, wonder-working; Skandasvāmin explains the word as mahāntam, great, excellent.

Kāmyam: kamanīyam, wished for, lovely. Skandasvāmin's sense is kāmyaṃ prārthayitavyaṃ stotṛṇām, worthy to be prayed to by the praisers.

Sanim: this word, formed from the root ṣaṇu dāne, may be taken as dhanasya dātāram, Sadasaspati who gives wealth, or as dhanadānam, Sadasaspati for the gift of wealth.

Ayāsiṣam: this word, formed from the root yā prāpaṇe, means "I have reached" or "I have taken refuge with": I have taken refuge with Sadasaspati for intelligence and gain of wealth.

original p. 772

Rik 6: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Since Skandasvāmin says in the Nirukta that words such as īmahe and yāmi are used in the sense of begging, he explains ayāsiṣam, a variant form of the root yā, as yāce, I beg or pray.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 772–773, noted briefly

सदसः (sadasaḥ): the root ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; after sad the suffix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun. The suffix is nit, so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197), whereby what ends in a suffix with ñ or n as it is initial udātta, sadas is initial udātta. When the genitive singular ṅas [as printed: jas] comes, sadas + as, ru and visarga: sadasaḥ. After it stands the word pati; so by "ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…" (Pā. sū. 8-3-53) s for the visarga.

पतिम् (patim): the root pā rakṣaṇe. By "pāter ḍatiḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "4-57" [?]) the suffix ḍati comes after the root pā rakṣaṇe; the ḍ at the start of the suffix is called it by "cuṭū" (Pā. sū. 1-3-7) and dropped by "tasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-9): pā + ati. By force of the suffix being made ḍit, though the former has no bha name, by "ṭeḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-143) the ā of pā, called ṭi, drops: pati. It is initial udātta [as printed] by the suffix accent.

प्रियम् (priyam): the root prīñ tarpaṇe. Since the suffix ka comes after roots with i, u, ṛ, ḷ in the penultimate and after jñā avabodhane, prīñ tarpaṇe and kṝ vikṣepe, the suffix ka after prī. By "laśakv ataddhite" (Pā. sū. 1-3-8) the k is called it and dropped: prī + a. By "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) the substitute iyaṅ for the ī: priya. This is final udātta by the suffix accent; accusative singular am; the pūrvarūpa by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107).

काम्यम् (kāmyam): the root kamu kāntau; kānti means wish. By "kamer ṇiṅ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-30) ṇiṅ in the sense of the root itself: kam + i. By "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi of the penultimate: kāmi. This is vowel-final, so by "aco yat" (Pā. sū. 3-1-97), whereby yat comes after a vowel-final root, the suffix yat: kām + i + ya. By "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-51), when an ārdhadhātuka without iṭ follows, ṇi is dropped: kāmya. By "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-213), the exception to tit svaritam, it is initial udātta. It ends in the accusative singular.

Page 773 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

सनिम् (sanim): ṣaṇu dāne; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ. In "khani-kaṣy-añjy-asi-vasi-vani-sani-dhvani-granthi-calibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "4-139" [?]) the iḥ of "aca iḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "4-138" [?]) is carried on. The suffix i comes after the roots khanu avadāraṇe, kaṣa hiṃsāyām, aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ, asu kṣepaṇe, vasa ācchādane, vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau, vanu yācane, ṣaṇu dāne, dhvana śabde, grantha bandhane (both of the cur-ādi) and cala kampane; so the suffix i: san + i. Final udātta by the suffix accent; am, the pūrvarūpa: sanim.

अयासिषम् (ayāsiṣam): yā prāpaṇe; luṅ, 1st singular mip: yā + mi. By "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) am for mi: yā + am. By "cli luṅi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-43) cli; for it the substitute sic by "cleḥ sic" (Pā. sū. 3-1-44); by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-71) the augment aṭ for the root: ayā + s + am. By "yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-73), for the roots yam, ram, nam and the ā-final roots, the augment sak, and for the sic after them the augment iṭ, when a parasmaipada suffix follows; so the augment sak for the ā-final yā, and iṭ for the sic: ayās + is + am. By "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for the s of sic: ayāsiṣam. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

॥६॥

यस्मा॑दृ॒ते न सि॒ध्य॑ति य॒ज्ञो वि॒प॒श्चित॑श्च॒न । [accent ?] स धी॒नां योग॑मिन्वति ॥७॥ [accent ?]

yásmād ṛté na sidhyati yajñó vipaścítaś caná | [accent ?] sa dhīnā́ṃ yógam invati ||7|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

यस्मात् । ऋते । न । सिध्यति । यज्ञः । विपःऽचितः । चन ॥ सः । धीनाम् । योगम् । इन्वति ॥७॥

yasmāt | ṛte | na | sidhyati | yajñaḥ | vipaḥ 'citaḥ | cana || saḥ | dhīnām | yogam | invati ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यज्ञोऽयमनुष्ठातव्यो विपश्चितश्चन विदुषोऽपि यजमानस्य यस्मात्सदसस्पतिदेवादृते न सिध्यति सोऽयं सदसस्पतिर्देवो धीनां मनोऽनुष्ठानविषयाणामस्मद्बुद्धीनामनुष्ठेयकर्मणां वा योगं संबन्धमिन्वति । व्याप्नोति । यजमानमनुगृह्य तदीयं यज्ञं निष्पादयतीत्यर्थः ॥ यस्मात् । अन्यारादित्यादिना । पा. २-३-२९ । ऋतेयोगात्पञ्चमी । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । सिध्यति । षिधु संराद्धौ । श्यनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । धीनाम् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । योगम् । युजिर् योगे । घञो ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । इन्वति । इवि व्याप्तौ । शप् । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । निघातः ॥

yajño 'yamanuṣṭhātavyo vipaścitaścana viduṣo 'pi yajamānasya yasmātsadasaspatidevādṛte na sidhyati so 'yaṃ sadasaspatirdevo dhīnāṃ mano 'nuṣṭhānaviṣayāṇāmasmadbuddhīnāmanuṣṭheyakarmaṇāṃ vā yogaṃ saṃbandhaminvati | vyāpnoti | yajamānamanugṛhya tadīyaṃ yajñaṃ niṣpādayatītyarthaḥ || yasmāt | anyārādityādinā | pā. 2-3-29 | ṛteyogātpañcamī | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatve prāpte na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | sidhyati | ṣidhu saṃrāddhau | śyano nittvādādyudāttatvam | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | dhīnām | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | yogam | yujir yoge | ghaño ñittvādādyudāttatvam | invati | ivi vyāptau | śap | idito num dhātoriti num | nighātaḥ ||

Rik 7: (bhāṣya ends at the top of this page, from …णामस्मद्बुद्धीनाम्…) word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

Translation: "Without which god Sadasaspati this sacrifice to be performed by a sacrificer, vipaścitaś cana, even a learned one, na sidhyati, does not succeed, that god Sadasaspati invati, pervades, the yoga, connection, of dhī, our minds, whose object is the performance, or of the rites to be performed: that is, favouring the sacrificer he accomplishes his sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: yasmāt, the ablative because of the connection with ṛte by anyārāt… (Pā. 2-3-29); the ending udātta due by sāv ekācaḥ is barred by na gośvan…; sidhyati, ṣidhu saṃrāddhau, initial udātta as śyan is nit, the lowering barred by yadvṛttān nityam; dhīnām, the ending udātta by sāv ekācaḥ; yogam, yujir yoge, initial udātta as ghañ is ñit; invati, ivi vyāptau, śap, num by idito num dhātoḥ, wholly unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

यज्ञः (yajñaḥ) — the sacrifice (we have to perform) | विपश्चितः चन (vipaścitaḥ cana) — even for a learned sacrificer | यस्मात् ऋते (yasmāt ṛte) — without the help of which Sadasaspati | न सिध्यति (na sidhyati) — is not accomplished | सः (saḥ) — that Sadasaspati | धीनाम् (dhīnām) — to the mind set on performing the sacrifice, or to the rites to be performed | योगम् (yogam) — connection | इन्वति (invati) — pervades (brings about).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Even a learned sacrificer cannot accomplish the rite without the help of Sadasaspati. For this Sadasaspati brings about the connection between the matters that come into our mind and the rites we have to do; that is, he makes our minds intent on the rites to be performed.

॥ English Translation ॥

Without whose aid the sacrifice even of the wise does not prosper, he prompts the pious feelings in our thonghts [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Cana: api; this word means "even".

Dhīnām: the word dhī has two senses, intelligence and action (Ni. "3-13" and Ni. "3-2" [as read, ?]). So dhīnāṃ yogam invati means he brings about connection with the rites such as sacrifice that we do; or he brings about connection to our understanding so that we do the rites. "Brings about connection" means: he urges our understanding to engage in the performance of rites.

original p. 775

Rik 7: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar on p. 775, noted briefly

यस्मात् (yasmāt): here the word yad is connected with the word ṛte. So by "anyārāditarartedikśabdāñcūttarapadājāhiyukte" (Pā. sū. 2-3-29), when connected with anya, ārāt, itara, ṛte, words seen to denote the quarters such as pūrva, words with añc as final member, and āc and āhi, the ablative comes after the stem denoting the sense construed with them; so the ablative comes after the word yad, construed with the sense of the word ṛte: yad + ṅasi. By "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102) a for the d; by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97) the pararūpa. By "ṅasiṅyoḥ smātsminau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-15), for ṅasi and ṅi after a pronoun ending in short a, the substitutes smāt and smin respectively; so smāt for ṅasi: yasmāt. By "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-168), su here meaning the locative plural suffix, the sense of the sūtra is that after a word that has a single vowel when that suffix follows, the case-endings from the instrumental on are udātta. In the locative plural the form is yeṣu; the ye before the locative plural su is the word yad with one vowel. So udātta would come to the ablative ending after yad, which is among the endings from the instrumental on. But in the nominative singular yaḥ, before su, the word ends in a. So the bar comes to it by "na gośvansāvavarṇa…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-182). So smāt is unaccented by the sup accent.

सिध्यति (sidhyati): ṣidhu saṃrāddhau, of the div-ādi; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; laṭ, tip. By "divādibhyaḥ śyan" (Pā. sū. 3-1-69) śyan: sidhyati. Śyan is nit, so it is initial udātta by the nit accent. Since it follows a word containing yad, yasmāt, the bar "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) comes, so it is not wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.

धीनाम् (dhīnām): the ending is udātta by sāv ekācaḥ.

योगम् (yogam): the root yujir yoge. By bhāve the suffix ghañ. By "cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-52), when a suffix with gh as it or the suffix ṇyat follows, c and j take the corresponding guttural; so for j, the third of the c-class, g, the third of the k-class; the laghūpadha-guṇa. The suffix is ñit, so yoga is initial udātta.

इन्वति (invati): the root ivi vyāptau. By "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-58) the augment num; laṭ, tip, śap: invati. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ it is wholly unaccented.

॥७॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: strokes over दृ, ष्कृ, चं, त्रा and वे; bars under ह, तिं, ध्व and दे. Positions not all certain.

आदृ॑ध्नोति ह॒विष्कृ॑तिं॒ प्राञ्चं॑ कृणोत्यध्व॒रम् । [accent ?] होत्रा॑ दे॒वेषु॑ गच्छति ॥८॥ [accent ?]

ā́d ṛdhnoti havíṣkṛtiṃ prā́ñcaṃ kṛṇoty adhvarám | [accent ?] hótrā devéṣu gacchati ||8|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आत् । ऋध्नोति । हविःऽकृतिम् । प्राञ्चम् । कृणोति । अध्वरम् ॥ होत्रा । देवेषु । गच्छति ॥८॥

āt | ṛdhnoti | haviḥ 'kṛtim | prāñcam | kṛṇoti | adhvaram || hotrā | deveṣu | gacchati ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number ४-१६७ is read with some doubt [?]; the grammar page has "4-602" [?].

आदनन्तरमेव हविष्कृतिं हविःसंपादनयुक्तं यजमानमृध्नोति । सदसस्पतिर्देवो वर्धयति । हविर्दानानन्तरमेव फलं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः । तथाविधफलसिद्धयेऽध्वरं यजमानेनानुष्ठीयमानं यज्ञं प्राञ्चं प्रकर्षेण गच्छन्तमविघ्नेन परिसमाप्तियुक्तं कृणोति । करोति । होत्रा हूयमाना देवता तुष्टा सती यजमानं प्रख्यापयितुं देवेषु गच्छति । यद्वा । होत्रास्मदीयस्तुतिरूपा वाक् देवान्परितोषयितुं देवेषु गच्छति । श्लोको धारेत्यादिषु सप्तपञ्चाशत्सु वाङ्नामसु होत्रा गीरिति पठितम् ॥ हविष्कृतिम् । हविषः कृतिः संपादनं यस्य यजमानस्य सोऽयं हविष्कृतिः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्येति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । प्राञ्चम् । अनिगन्तोऽञ्चतौ वप्रत्यये । पा. ६-२-५२ । इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पश्चादेकादेशस्वरः । अध्वरम् । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । हूयतेऽस्यामिति होत्रा देवता । हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन् । उ. ४-१६७ । इति त्रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

ādanantarameva haviṣkṛtiṃ haviḥsaṃpādanayuktaṃ yajamānamṛdhnoti | sadasaspatirdevo vardhayati | havirdānānantarameva phalaṃ prayacchatītyarthaḥ | tathāvidhaphalasiddhaye 'dhvaraṃ yajamānenānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ yajñaṃ prāñcaṃ prakarṣeṇa gacchantamavighnena parisamāptiyuktaṃ kṛṇoti | karoti | hotrā hūyamānā devatā tuṣṭā satī yajamānaṃ prakhyāpayituṃ deveṣu gacchati | yadvā | hotrāsmadīyastutirūpā vāk devānparitoṣayituṃ deveṣu gacchati | śloko dhāretyādiṣu saptapañcāśatsu vāṅnāmasu hotrā gīriti paṭhitam || haviṣkṛtim | haviṣaḥ kṛtiḥ saṃpādanaṃ yasya yajamānasya so 'yaṃ haviṣkṛtiḥ | bahuvrīhau prakṛtyeti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | prāñcam | aniganto 'ñcatau vapratyaye | pā. 6-2-52 | iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | paścādekādeśasvaraḥ | adhvaram | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | hūyate 'syāmiti hotrā devatā | huyāmāśrubhasibhyastran | u. 4-167 | iti tran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "Āt, right after, (the god Sadasaspati) ṛdhnoti, makes grow, the sacrificer who is haviṣkṛti, engaged in preparing the oblation: that is, right after the giving of the oblation he gives the fruit. For obtaining such fruit, he kṛṇoti, makes, the adhvara, the sacrifice being performed by the sacrificer, prāñcam, going forward well, brought to completion without obstacle. Hotrā, the deity being called, being pleased, goes among the gods to proclaim the sacrificer. Or hotrā, our speech in the form of praise, goes among the gods to please them. Hotrā and gīḥ are read among the fifty-seven names for speech beginning ślokaḥ, dhārā." (Grammatical tail: haviṣkṛtim, "the sacrificer whose kṛti, preparing, is of the oblation", the first member's accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā; prāñcam, the preverb keeps its accent by Pā. 6-2-52, then the accent of the single substitute; adhvaram, "in which there is no dhvara, harm", final udātta of the final member by nañsubhyām; hotrā, "she is called on", the deity, tran by huyāmāśrubhasibhyas tran (Uṇ. 4-167 [?]), initial udātta as nit.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

आत् (āt) — then | हविष्कृतिम् (haviṣkṛtim) — the sacrificer who has prepared the oblation | ऋध्नोति (ṛdhnoti) — (Sadasaspati) makes prosper | अध्वरम् (adhvaram) — (the sacrificer's undertaken) sacrifice | प्राञ्चम् (prāñcam) — so that it goes on well, or ends without obstacle | कृणोति (kṛṇoti) — makes | होत्रा (hotrā) — by the invoking (the deity called, being pleased,

original p. 777

Rik 8: word-meanings (end), overall sense, English, Special Topics

to make the sacrificer renowned) | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among the gods (to where the gods are) | गच्छति (gacchati) — goes [or: होत्रा (hotrā) — (our) speech in the form of praise (to please the gods) | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among the gods | गच्छति (gacchati) — goes and reaches.]

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

As soon as we have given the share of oblation in the sacrifice, Sadasaspati brings good to the sacrificer; he brings the sacrifice begun to completion without obstacle. And the deity we invoked, pleased by the sacrifice, goes to the gods to praise the sacrificer; or the speech in the form of praise that we make goes to the gods to praise the sacrificer, that is, makes the gods hear it.

॥ English Translation ॥

And then he rewards the presenter of oblations ; brings the sacrifiee [sic] to its conclusion ; our prayer then reaches the gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Āt: atha, meaning "then". For the word āt in the ṛk

यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै (ऋ. सं. १-११५-४)

yadedayukta haritaḥ sadhasthādādrātrī vāsastanute simasmai (ṛ. saṃ. 1-115-4)

("When he has yoked the bay horses from their seat, then night spreads her garment for all": editorial and tentative.) Yāska in the Nirukta gives the sense atha, then (Ni. "4-11" [?]).

Haviṣkṛtim: haviṣaḥ kṛtiḥ saṃpādanaṃ yasya yajamānasya so 'yaṃ haviṣkṛtiḥ: the sense is the sacrificer who gives the oblation. Or, as Skandasvāmin says,

हविष्कृतिं हविष्क्रियां हवींषि सारतो वृद्धानि करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

haviṣkṛtiṃ haviṣkriyāṃ havīṃṣi sārato vṛddhāni karotītyarthaḥ ||

("Haviṣkṛtim means the making of the oblation: he makes the oblations grown in substance.") Haviṣkṛti means the act of giving oblation; the intent is that he makes it substantial.

Prāñcam:

प्रकर्षेण गच्छन्तमविघ्नेन परिसमाप्तियुक्तं करोतीत्यर्थः ॥

prakarṣeṇa gacchantamavighnena parisamāptiyuktaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||

("Going forward well, he makes it reach completion without obstacle.") The sense is: he makes the sacrifice reach its end without obstacle.

Hotrā:

हूयमाना देवता अथवा अस्मदीयस्तुतिरूपा वाक्

hūyamānā devatā athavā asmadīyastutirūpā vāk

("The deity being called, or our speech in the form of praise.") Two senses are given: the deity called in the sacrifice, or the speech in the form of praise that we make. Of these two the second, speech, seems fitting here. Since the word hotrā is read among the fifty-seven names for speech beginning ślokaḥ, dhārā (Ni. [?]), hotrā means speech.

original p. 778

Rik 8: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Deveṣu gacchati: going to the gods. If it refers to the deity, the intent is that the deity pleased in the sacrifice goes to the gods to tell that the sacrificer has satisfied him well; if it refers to speech, the intent is: may our words of praise reach the gods, or become known to them, or be heard by them, and may they be pleased.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 778–779, noted briefly

हविष्कृतिम् (haviṣkṛtim): haviṣaḥ kṛtiḥ saṃpādanaṃ yasya yajamānasya saḥ haviṣkṛtiḥ: the sacrificer who has the preparation of the oblation is called haviṣkṛti. By "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member.

प्राञ्चम् (prāñcam): the analysis pra añcati. In this sense, with the subanta pra as upapada, by "ṛtvigdadhṛk…" (Pā. sū. 3-2-59) the suffix kvin; k, n, i are called it and dropped; v remains. By "anidhitāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-24), before a kit or ṅit suffix, the n in the penultimate of a consonant-final aṅga not having short i as it is dropped: pra + ac + v; lengthening of like vowels: prāc + v. By "anigantoñcatau vapratyaye" (Pā. sū. 6-2-52), when the root añc ending in a suffix that is v follows, a gati not ending in ik keeps its own accent; so the first member keeps its accent; the first member pra is initial udātta by upasargāś cābhivarjam, and after compounding the same accent stays by the sūtra just stated. With pra + ac + v the single substitute from lengthening of like vowels is udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ. By "ver apṛktasya" the v is dropped. Accusative singular am: prāc + am. By "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-70) the augment num: prānc + am; by "naś cāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. sū. 8-3-24) anusvāra for the n; for it, by "anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-58), the homorganic ñ: prāñcam.

अध्वरम् (adhvaram): na vidyate 'dhvaraḥ [as printed] hiṃsā yasmin sa adhvaraḥ. Overriding the first-member accent due by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172), the final member after nañ and su is final udātta; so the final member is final udātta.

होत्रा (hotrā): hūyate asmin iti hotrā, the deity. By "huyāmāśrubhasibhyas tran" (Uṇ. sū. "4-602" [?]), after the roots hu dānādanayoḥ, yā prāpaṇe, mā māne, śru śravaṇe and bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ,

Page 779 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

the suffix tran comes; so after the root hu, tran; guṇa: hotra. Naming a deity, it is feminine; so ṭāp: hotrā. The suffix is nit; so hotrā is initial udātta by the nit accent.

॥८॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Deity: Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa.

नरा॒शंसं॑ सु॒धृष्ट॑म॒मप॑श्यं स॒प्रथ॑स्तमम् । [accent ?] दि॒वो न सद्म॑मखसम् ॥९॥ [accent ?]

नराशंसम् । सुऽधृष्टमम् । अपश्यम् । सप्रथःऽतमम् ॥ दिवः । न । सद्मऽमखसम् ॥९॥

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥३५॥ closes Varga 35.

नराशंसमेतन्नामकं देवविशेषम् । यद्वा । अवयवार्थव्युत्पत्त्या सदसस्पतिदेवतापरोऽयं शब्दः । व्युत्पत्तिं च यास्को दर्शयति । नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यो नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसन्त्यग्निरिति शाकपूणिर्नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति । नि. ८-६ । इति । अत्राग्निवत्सदसस्पतेरपि नरैः शस्यमानत्वान्नराशंसत्वम् । एवमेवाभिप्रायं हृदि निधाय ब्राह्मणमेवमाम्नायते । प्रजा वै नरो वाक् शंसः । ऐ. ब्रा. ६-२७ । इति । अतो मनुष्यैः शस्यमानो यः सदसस्पतिर्यो वा नराशंसनामको देवस्तमपश्यं शास्त्रदृष्ट्या दृष्टवानस्मि । कीदृशम् । सुधृष्टममत्याधिक्येन धार्ष्ट्ययुक्तं सप्रथस्तममतिशयेन प्रख्यातं सद्ममखसं प्राप्ततेजस्कम् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । दिवो न द्युलोकानिव । आदित्यचन्द्रादिभिरधिष्ठिता द्युलोकविशेषा यथा तेजस्विनस्तद्वदयं नराशंसस्तेजस्वीत्यर्थः ॥ सुधृष्टमम् । शोभनं धृष्णोतीति सुधृक् । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । अतिशायनिकस्तमप् । षकारस्य जश्त्वाभावश्छान्दसः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन ऋकार उदात्तः । अपश्यम् । पाघ्राध्मेत्यादिना पश्यादेशः । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । पा. ६-४-७१ । इत्यट उदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । सप्रथस्तमम् । प्रथ प्रख्याने ।

Rik 9: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

प्रथनं प्रथः । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सह प्रथसा वर्तत इति तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे । पा. २-२-२८ । इति बहुव्रीहिसमासः । वोपसर्जनस्य । पा. ६-३-८२ । इति सादेशः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सद्ममखसम् । सीदन्तीति सद्म । षद्लृ विशरणादौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सद्म महो यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ हकारस्य व्यत्ययेन खकारः ॥३५॥

prathanaṃ prathaḥ | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | nittvādādyudāttatvam | saha prathasā vartata iti tena saheti tulyayoge | pā. 2-2-28 | iti bahuvrīhisamāsaḥ | vopasarjanasya | pā. 6-3-82 | iti sādeśaḥ | pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | divaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | sadmamakhasam | sīdantīti sadma | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇādau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | sadma maho yasyeti bahuvrīhau hakārasya vyatyayena khakāraḥ ||35||

Translation: "Narāśaṃsa, the particular god of that name. Or, by derivation from the sense of its parts, this word refers to the deity Sadasaspati. Yāska shows the derivation: 'Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice, says Kātthakya: men, seated in it, praise; Agni, says Śākapūṇi: he is to be praised by men' (Ni. 8-6). Here, like Agni, Sadasaspati too is narāśaṃsa because he is praised by men. With just this intent in mind the Brāhmaṇa declares: 'The creatures are men; speech is śaṃsa' (Ai. Brā. 6-27). So I apaśyam, have seen with the eye of the śāstra, the Sadasaspati praised by men, or the god named Narāśaṃsa. Of what kind? Sudhṛṣṭama, endowed with boldness in the highest degree; saprathastama, most renowned; sadmamakhas, who has attained radiance. Here is the example: divo na, like the heavenly worlds: as the particular heavenly regions presided over by the sun, the moon and the rest are radiant, so this Narāśaṃsa is radiant." (Grammatical tail: sudhṛṣṭamam, "he dares well", sudhṛk, kvip by kvip ca, tamap of excess, the absence of jaś for the ṣ Vedic, the ṛ udātta by the accent of the kṛt final member; apaśyam, paśya by pāghrādhmā…, the aṭ udātta by Pā. 6-4-71, not lowered at the start of the pāda; saprathastamam, pratha prakhyāne, "prathanaṃ prathaḥ", asun, initial udātta as nit; "it is with prathas", a bahuvrīhi by tena saheti tulyayoge (Pā. 2-2-28), sa substituted by Pā. 6-3-82; the first member's accent being due, initial udātta of the final member by parādiś chandasi bahulam; divaḥ, the ending udātta by ūḍidam…; sadmamakhasam, "they sit": sadma, ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau, manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, initial udātta as nit; in the bahuvrīhi "whose mahas is a seat", kh for h by exchange.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

  1. सुधृष्टमम् (sudhṛṣṭamam) — very bold | सप्रथस्तमम् (saprathastamam) — exceedingly renowned | दिवः न (divaḥ na) — like the heavenly world | सद्ममखसम् (sadmamakhasam) — shining with abundant radiance | नराशंसम् (narāśaṃsam) — Sadasaspati, praised by men, or the deity called Narāśaṃsa (Agni) | अपश्यम् (apaśyam) — I have seen.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

This Sadasaspati (or Narāśaṃsa) has great valour, is very renowned, and shines with exceeding radiance like the heavenly world (where the sun, moon and the rest are). Such a Sadasaspati (or Narāśaṃsa) I have seen.

॥ English Translation ॥

I have seen Narasamsa the most valiant, the most renowned and radiant as the heavens.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The deity of this ṛk is Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa. Though the name Sadasaspati is not indicated in the ṛk, because the three previous ṛks refer to Sadasaspati, and because it is said that the deity of this ṛk is either Sadasaspati or Narāśaṃsa, one should take the word narāśaṃsa in the sense of its parts, "praised by men", and treat it as a qualifier of the word sadasaspatim (that word is to be supplied here). Or, on the view that names the deity Narāśaṃsa for this ṛk, there is no difficulty, since the very word narāśaṃsam is in the ṛk. Yāska explains the sense of the parts of the word narāśaṃsa thus:

original p. 781

Rik 9: Special Topics (end) and grammar

नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यो नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसन्त्यग्निरिति शाकपूणिर्नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति ॥ (नि. ८-६)

narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyo narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsantyagniriti śākapūṇirnaraiḥ praśasyo bhavati || (ni. 8-6)

("Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice, says Kātthakya: men, seated in it, praise; Agni, says Śākapūṇi: he is to be praised by men": editorial and tentative.) Kātthakya's view is that narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice; Śākapūṇi's view is that narāśaṃsa is the one praised (Agni), since narāḥ, men, praise him. On this the commentator cites a statement of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

प्रजा वै नरो वाक् शंसः (ऐ. ब्रा. ६-२७)

prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ (ai. brā. 6-27)

Nara means creatures or men; śaṃsa means speech. So the intent is that narāśaṃsa means one praised by creatures or men. The word narāśaṃsa can be construed with reference to three deities, Sadasaspati, Narāśaṃsa or Agni. We have discussed this point earlier (see page [the number is left blank in the print]).

Sudhṛṣṭamam:

शोभनं धृष्णोतीति

śobhanaṃ dhṛṣṇotīti

("He dares well.") One who has excellent valour (or steadfastness).

Saprathastamam:

प्रथ प्रख्याने । सह प्रथसा वर्तते इति । तेन सह

pratha prakhyāne | saha prathasā vartate iti | tena saha

("Pratha, to be renowned; it is with prathas; together with it.") Since the root pratha means make known, praise, the word saprathastamam means accompanied by special renown.

Divo na: like heaven. This comparison does not fit very well. The ṛṣi may have spoken this comparison with in mind the sun, moon and the rest shining brightly in heaven (in the sky).

Sadmamakhasam: here, in the word makhasam, kh has been used by exchange in place of h; so makhasam means mahasam.

सद्म महो यस्य सः सद्ममहाः अथवा सद्ममखाः तम्

sadma maho yasya saḥ sadmamahāḥ athavā sadmamakhāḥ tam

("He whose mahas is a seat, sadmamahāḥ or sadmamakhāḥ: him.") Such is the analysis. One who is like a house for radiance: the intent is one who shines with exceeding radiance or splendour.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 781–782, noted briefly

सुधृष्टमम् (sudhṛṣṭamam): the root ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye, of the sv-ādi. When su = śobhanam, dhṛṣṇoti is meant, kvip by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); all of kvip drops. By "atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau" (Pā. sū. 5-3-55) tamap in the sense of excess: sudhṛṣ + tama. That jaś does not come for the ṣ by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-53) is Vedic. By "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-41) ṭ for the t. Accusative singular am; by ami pūrvaḥ the pūrvarūpa: sudhṛṣṭamam. The ṛ of dhṛṣ is udātta by the root accent.

original p. 782

Rik 9: grammar (end)

After compounding with the word su, the accent of the kṛt final member comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), and that accent stays.

अपश्यम् (apaśyam): the root dṛśir prekṣaṇe. Laṅ, 1st singular mip; for it the substitute am by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101); the vikaraṇa śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68). By "pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyarti…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78) the substitute paśya for dṛś: paśya + a + am. By "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the pūrvarūpa: apaśyam. By luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ the udātta augment aṭ. Since it stands at the start of a pāda, it is not wholly unaccented.

सप्रथस्तमम् (saprathastamam): the root pratha prakhyāne; prathanaṃ prathaḥ: by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun the suffix asun in the sense of the action; prathas is initial udātta by the nit accent. Saha prathasā vartate: a bahuvrīhi compound, by "tena saheti tulyayoge" (Pā. sū. 2-2-28): the word saha, conveying an action at the same time, is compounded with a fit word ending in the instrumental, and that is called bahuvrīhi. "Vopasarjanasya" (Pā. sū. 6-3-82): a compound all of whose members are upasarjana is a bahuvrīhi; the word saha, standing immediately before the final member in a compound forming a bahuvrīhi, takes the substitute sa; so sa for saha: saprathas. Since this is a bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent is due; but by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-199) the final member prathas is final udātta [as printed]. When excess is meant, the suffix tamap: saprathastama; accusative singular, saprathastamam.

दिवः (divaḥ): by "ūḍidaṃpadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-171) the ending is udātta.

सद्ममखसम् (sadmamakhasam): ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ. By "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. sū. 3-2-75) the suffix manin: sadman. By the nit accent it is initial udātta. Sadma mahaḥ yasya saḥ sadmamahāḥ: a bahuvrīhi compound. By "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85) kh for h: sadmamakhas; accusative singular am: sadmamakhasam.

॥९॥ An ornament closes Sūkta 18 at the foot of p. 782; no colophon is printed. Printed p. 783 opens with the title ಹತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Nineteenth Sūkta").

॥ ಹತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 19 — "prati tyaṃ cārum adhvaram" ("The Nineteenth Sūkta"; second sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka; last sūkta of this volume)

original p. 783

Sūkta 19: introduction, heading, Rik 1 Saṃhitā

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note)

प्रति त्यमिति नवर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवता त्वनुक्रम्यते । प्रति त्यमाग्निमारुतमिति ॥ कारीरीष्ट्यां प्रति त्यमित्येषा धाय्या । तथा च सूत्रितम् । वर्षकामेष्टिः कारीरी तस्यां प्रति त्यं चारुमध्वरमीळे अग्निं स्ववसं नमोभिरिति धाय्ये । आ. २-१३ । इति ॥

prati tyamiti navarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | devatā tvanukramyate | prati tyamāgnimārutamiti || kārīrīṣṭyāṃ prati tyamityeṣā dhāyyā | tathā ca sūtritam | varṣakāmeṣṭiḥ kārīrī tasyāṃ prati tyaṃ cārumadhvaramīḷe agniṃ svavasaṃ namobhiriti dhāyye | ā. 2-13 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta beginning prati tyam, of nine ṛks, is the second. The ṛṣi and metre are as before. The deity is stated in the Anukramaṇī: 'prati tyam: to Agni and the Maruts.' In the kārīrī rite this ṛk prati tyam is the dhāyyā. So it is laid down in the sūtra: 'The kārīrī is the rite of one who desires rain; in it prati tyaṃ cārum adhvaram and īḷe agniṃ svavasaṃ namobhiḥ are the two dhāyyās' (Āśv. 2-13)."

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): Pratityam is the second sūkta in this fifth anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. On the deity of this sūkta the Anukramaṇikā says, pratityam āgnimārutam: the deities of the sūkta pratityam are Agni and the Maruts. In the rite called kārīrīṣṭi the sūkta prati tyam is to be recited: varṣakāmeṣṭiḥ kārīrī tasyāṃ prati tyaṃ cārum adhvaram īḷe agniṃ svavasaṃ namobhir iti dhāyye (Āśv. 2-13); that is, kārīrī is the rite of one who desires rain, a particular rite done for the coming of rain. In it the two ṛks prati tyaṃ cārum adhvaram (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-19-1) and īḷe agniṃ svavasaṃ namobhiḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 5-60-1) are to be recited as the yājyā and puronuvākyā ṛks, says the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Āś. 2-13).

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 19 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 19 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 36, 37 ॥ ॥ Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 1–9 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣiḥ — Medhātithiḥ Kāṇvaḥ ॥ ॥ Devatā — Agnir Marutaś ca ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥ Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Sūkta 19, Rik 1

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: strokes over रु (चारु), गो, हू, द्भि and ग (गहि); bars under ति, ध्व, पी, य (थाय) and म.

प्रति॒ त्यं चारु॑मध्व॒रं गो॑पी॒थाय॒ प्र हू॑यसे । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न आ ग॑हि ॥१॥ [accent ?]

prati tyáṃ cā́rum adhvaráṃ gopīthā́ya prá hūyase | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||1|| [accent ?]

original p. 784

Rik 1: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रति । त्यम् । चारुम् । अध्वरम् । गोऽपीथाय । प्र । हूयसे ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥१॥

prati | tyam | cārum | adhvaram | go 'pīthāya | pra | hūyase || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

त्यच्छब्दः सर्वनाम तच्छब्दपर्यायः । हे अग्ने यो यज्ञश्चारुरङ्गवैकल्यरहितस्त्यं तथाविधं चारुमध्वरं प्रतिलभ्य गोपीथाय सोमपानाय प्र हूयसे । प्रकर्षेण त्वं हूयसे । तस्मादस्मिन्नध्वरे त्वं मरुद्भिर्देवविशेषैः सहा गहि । आगच्छ । सेयमृग्यास्केनैवं व्याख्याता । तं प्रति चारुमध्वरं सोमपानाय प्रहूयसे सोऽग्ने मरुद्भिः सहागच्छ । नि. १०-३६ । इति ॥ प्रति । निपात आद्युदात्तः । त्यम् । त्यदादीनामः । पा. ७-२-१०२ । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । चारुम् । दृसनिजनिचरीत्यादिना । उ. १-३ । ञुण् । अत उपधाया इति वृद्धिः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । गोपीथाय । निशीथगोपीथावगथाः । उ. २-९ । इति थक्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । प्र । निपातस्वरः ॥

tyacchabdaḥ sarvanāma tacchabdaparyāyaḥ | he agne yo yajñaścāruraṅgavaikalyarahitastyaṃ tathāvidhaṃ cārumadhvaraṃ pratilabhya gopīthāya somapānāya pra hūyase | prakarṣeṇa tvaṃ hūyase | tasmādasminnadhvare tvaṃ marudbhirdevaviśeṣaiḥ sahā gahi | āgaccha | seyamṛgyāskenaivaṃ vyākhyātā | taṃ prati cārumadhvaraṃ somapānāya prahūyase so 'gne marudbhiḥ sahāgaccha | ni. 10-36 | iti || prati | nipāta ādyudāttaḥ | tyam | tyadādīnāmaḥ | pā. 7-2-102 | prātipadikasvaraḥ | cārum | dṛsanijanicarītyādinā | u. 1-3 | ñuṇ | ata upadhāyā iti vṛddhiḥ | ñittvādādyudāttaḥ | gopīthāya | niśīthagopīthāvagathāḥ | u. 2-9 | iti thakpratyayānto nipātitaḥ | pra | nipātasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "The word tya is a pronoun, a synonym of the word tad. O Agni, the sacrifice which is cāru, free from any defect in its parts: having obtained tyam, such a cārum adhvaram, you are pra hūyase, called with eminence, gopīthāya, for the drinking of soma. Therefore come to this sacrifice with the Maruts, the particular gods. This ṛk Yāska explains thus: 'To that lovely sacrifice you are called for the drinking of soma; O Agni, come with the Maruts' (Ni. 10-36)." (Grammatical tail: prati, a particle, initial udātta; tyam, a by tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. 7-2-102), the stem accent; cārum, ñuṇ by dṛsanijanicari… (Uṇ. 1-3), vṛddhi by ata upadhāyāḥ, initial udātta as ñit; gopīthāya, given ready-made as a thak-final by niśīthagopīthāvagathāḥ (Uṇ. 2-9); pra, the particle accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | चारुम् (cārum) — free from the faults of deficiency and excess, lovely, or complete (whatever sacrifice there is) | त्यम् (tyam) — that | अध्वरं प्रति (adhvaraṃ prati) — to that sacrifice | गोपीथाय (gopīthāya) — for drinking soma | प्र हूयसे (pra hūyase) — you are invited | (therefore you) | मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — together with the deities called Maruts | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, you are invited for the drinking of soma in every excellent sacrifice performed without the faults of deficiency, excess or omission. So come here now together with the Marut deities.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Agni, to every perfect and handsome sacrifice you are invoked to drink Soma ; come hither, Agni, with the Maruths [sic].

original p. 785

Rik 1: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Yāska has explained the sense of this ṛk in the Nirukta. That explanation is just as the commentator gives it; there is no difference.

Tyam = tam: this is a pronoun. By exchange tyam stands in place of tam. We give a few ṛks in which the word tyam has the sense tam, as examples:

त्यं चिदत्रिमृतजुरमर्थमश्वं न यातवे । (ऋ. सं. १०-१४३-१)

tyaṃ cidatrimṛtajuramarthamaśvaṃ na yātave | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-143-1)

("That Atri, worn out by age, like a horse, to go to his goal …": editorial and tentative.)

त्यं सुमेषं महया स्वर्विदं शतं यस्य सुभ्वः साकमीरते । (ऋ. सं. १-५२-१)

tyaṃ sumeṣaṃ mahayā svarvidaṃ śataṃ yasya subhvaḥ sākamīrate | (ṛ. saṃ. 1-52-1)

("Magnify that ram, the finder of light, whose hundred good helpers go forth together": editorial and tentative.)

त्यमूषु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानाम् । (ऋ. सं. १०-१७८-१)

tyamūṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānām | (ṛ. saṃ. 10-178-1)

("That prize-winner, sped by the gods, mighty, the victor of chariots": editorial and tentative.)

उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५०-१)

udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-50-1)

("The rays carry up that god Jātavedas": editorial and tentative.)

and so on. In these ṛks the word tyam means tam.

Gopīthāya: though the word go has many senses, cow, water, ray, hymn, soma, speech and so on, here the commentator has taken it as soma. The author of the Vedārthayatna and some others take the word go as milk or ghee. This is not very fitting; the sense soma given by the commentator is right.

The last pāda of every ṛk of this sūkta, marudbhir agna ā gahi, is read again and again like a refrain.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 785–786, noted briefly

प्रति (prati): a particle; initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ", particles are initial udātta.

त्यम् (tyam): tyad is in the tyad-ādi, within the sarva-ādi group. By "phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ" (Phi. sū. 1-1) it is final udātta. After it the accusative singular am: tyad + am. By "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102), when a case-ending follows, the last letter of the words read in the tyad-ādi group takes a: a for the d: tya + a + am. By "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97), after a short a not at the end of a word, when a, e, o, called guṇa, follow, the single pararūpa comes in place of both; so the pararūpa. This

Page 786 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

is udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ. Tya + am: by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the pūrvarūpa; the a from this pūrvarūpa too is udātta by ekādeśa….

चारुम् (cārum): "dṛsanijanicaraticaṭibhyo ñuṇ" (Uṇ. sū. 1-3): after dṛ vidāraṇe, ṣaṇu dāne, jana janane, cara gatau and caṭe bhedane the suffix ñuṇ comes; so after the root car the suffix ñuṇ; ñ and ṇ are called it and dropped; u remains: car + u. By "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116), when a ñit or ṇit suffix follows, the short a in the penultimate takes vṛddhi: cāru. The suffix is ñit, so it is initial udātta by ñnityādir nityam; in the accusative singular, cārum.

गोपीथाय (gopīthāya): "niśīthagopīthāvagathāḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "2-166" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-9): the three words niśītha, gopītha and avagatha are given ready-made as ending in the suffix thak; so it is given ready-made as a thak-final. The Vṛttikāra explains gopītha as tīrtha; the Vedabhāṣyakāra explains it as soma-drinking.

प्र (pra): the particle accent.

नहि । देवः । न । मर्त्यः । महः । तव । क्रतुम् । परः ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥२॥

nahi | devaḥ | na | martyaḥ | mahaḥ | tava | kratum | paraḥ || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number १-७८ is read with some doubt; लुङ् न is as printed, for लुङ् न / लुग्न.

हे अग्ने महो महतस्तव संबन्धिनं क्रतुं कर्मविशेषमुल्लङ्घ्य परो नहि उत्कृष्टो देवो न भवति खलु । तथा मर्त्यो मनुष्यश्च परो न भवति । ये मनुष्यास्त्वदीयं क्रतुमनुतिष्ठन्ति ये च देवास्त्वदीये क्रताविज्यन्ते त एवोत्कृष्टा इत्यर्थः । मरुद्भिरित्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥ नहि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तो-

he agne maho mahatastava saṃbandhinaṃ kratuṃ karmaviśeṣamullaṅghya paro nahi utkṛṣṭo devo na bhavati khalu | tathā martyo manuṣyaśca paro na bhavati | ye manuṣyāstvadīyaṃ kratumanutiṣṭhanti ye ca devāstvadīye kratāvijyante ta evotkṛṣṭā ityarthaḥ | marudbhirityādi pūrvavat || nahi | evamādīnāmanta ityanto-

दात्तः । देवः । पचाद्यजन्तश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । महः । महतस्तलोपश्छान्दसः । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् । पा. ६-१-१७३-१ । इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । तव । युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसीत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । क्रतुम् । कृञः कतुः । उ. १-७८ । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । गहि । गमॢ सृप्ॢ गतौ । लोटः सेर्हिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति लुङ् न भवति । निघातः ॥

dāttaḥ | devaḥ | pacādyajantaścittvādantodāttaḥ | mahaḥ | mahatastalopaśchāndasaḥ | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam | pā. 6-1-173-1 | iti vibhakterudāttatvam | tava | yuṣmadasmadorṅasītyādyudāttatvam | kratum | kṛñaḥ katuḥ | u. 1-78 | pratyayādyudāttatvam | gahi | gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau | loṭaḥ serhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | anudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhādityasiddhatvādato heriti luṅ na bhavati | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O Agni, no god is para, superior, so as to go beyond the kratu, the particular rite, belonging to you who are mahas, great; likewise no martya, man, is superior. That is, the men who perform your rite and the gods who are worshipped in your rite: they alone are superior. Marudbhiḥ and the rest, as before." (Grammatical tail: nahi, final udātta by evam-ādīnām antaḥ; devaḥ, an ac-final of the pac-ādi, final udātta as cit; mahaḥ, the loss of t of mahataḥ Vedic, the ending udātta by bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. 6-1-173-1); tava, initial udātta by yuṣmadasmador ṅasi; kratum, katu by kṛñaḥ katuḥ (Uṇ. 1-78 [?]), initial udātta of the suffix; gahi, gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau, hi for si of loṭ, śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, the nasal dropped by anudāttopadeśa…, and since that counts as not done by asiddhavad atrābhāt, hi is not dropped by ato heḥ; wholly unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(O Agni) | महः (mahaḥ) — excellent | तव (tava) — your | क्रतुम् (kratum) — the rite (sacrifice), going beyond | परः (paraḥ) — another | देवः (devaḥ) — god | नहि (nahi) — there is not | (likewise) | मर्त्यः (martyaḥ) — a man too | न (na) — there is not | (therefore) हे अग्ने (he agne) — O Agni | (you) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — together with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, the rite or sacrifice connected with you is very great. There is no god or man able to transgress it. Therefore, O Agni, come here together with the Marut deities.

॥ English Translation ॥

Neither god nor man has power over a rite (dedicated) to you who are great : come hitter [sic], Agni, with the Maruths [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Mahaḥ: mahataḥ: excellent, or very strong, possessed of great power. Here the t has been dropped.

Kratum: though this word has two senses, action (Ni. "3-2" [?]) and intelligence (Ni. "3-13" [?]), the commentator gives only the sense action.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 787–788, noted briefly

नहि (nahi): final udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ".

देवः (devaḥ): the root divu krīḍādau, of the pac-ādi; so by "nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-134) the suffix ac; by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) the laghūpadha-guṇa; the suffix being cit, final udātta by citaḥ.

Page 788 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar (end)

महः (mahaḥ): for the t of the word mahataḥ, a Vedic loss. The genitive ending after the word mahat is udātta by "bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173, Vā. 1): after the words bṛhat and mahat, the letters called nadī and the vowel-initial case-endings from śas on are udātta. Although, since it is treated like śatṛ by "vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca" (Uṇ. sū. "2-241" [?]), the udātta is established by "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173) itself, so that the vārttika might appear purposeless, it was shown earlier that the vārttika is purposeful as a restriction.

तव (tava): by "yuṣmadasmador ṅasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-211), when ṅas follows, the first syllable of the words yuṣmad and asmad is udātta; so it is initial udātta.

क्रतुम् (kratum): (Uṇ. sū. "1-77" [?]) since the suffix katu comes after the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe, after the root kṛ the suffix katu; the k is called it and dropped: kṛ + atu. The suffix being kit, guṇa is barred by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5), so guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) does not come. By the substitute yaṇ, r for the ṛ; by "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3), the suffix accent, kratu is initial udātta.

गहि (gahi): the root gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau; loṭ, 2nd singular sip; by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87) hi for si: gam + hi; the vikaraṇa śap by kartari śap; for it luk by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73). In the Mahābhāṣya on the sūtra "[ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt]" (Pā. sū. 7-2-10) [the sūtra name is garbled in the print], the kārikā that counts the anudāttopadeśa roots (lip, lup, vap, svap, sṛp, yabh, rabh, labh, gam, nam …) contains gam. So it is anudātta; so by "anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-37), before a jhal-initial suffix marked with k or ṅ, the last letter of the nasal-final anudāttopadeśa roots, of the nasal-final tanoty-ādi roots and of the root van drops; so the nasal m drops: ga + hi. By "asiddhavad atrābhāt" (Pā. sū. 6-4-22), when the luk of hi is made by the ābhīya rule "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105), the ābhīya loss of m is asiddha. So there is no being a-final; so the luk of hi does not come. In gahi, by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28), it is wholly unaccented.
