Rik 3: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । महः । रजसः । विदुः । विश्वे । देवासः । अद्रुहः ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥३॥

ye | mahaḥ | rajasaḥ | viduḥ | viśve | devāsaḥ | adruhaḥ || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने ये मरुतो महो रजसो महत उदकस्य वर्षणप्रकारं विदुस्तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः । कीदृशा मरुतः । विश्वे सर्वे सप्तविधगणोपेताः । सप्तगणा वै मरुतः । तै. सं. २-२-११-१ । इति श्रुतेः । देवासो द्योतमाना अद्रुहो द्रोहरहिता वर्षणेन सर्वभूतोपकारित्वात् । तथा चोपरिष्टादाम्नायते । उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतो यूयं वृष्टिं वर्षयथा पुरीषिणः । ऋग्वे. ५-५५-५ । इति । शाखान्तरेऽपि मन्त्रान्तरस्य ब्राह्मणमेवमाम्नायते । मरुतां पृषतयः स्थेत्याह मरुतो वै वृष्ट्या ईशते इति । रजःशब्दो यास्केन बहुधा व्याख्यातः । रजो रजतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यत उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यन्तेऽसृगहनी रजसी उच्येते । नि. ४-१९ । इति ॥ रजसः । नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः । विदुः । विद ज्ञाने । विदो लटो वा । पा. ३-४-८३ । इति झेरुसादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । विश्वे । विशेः क्वन्नन्तस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । देवासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । देवशब्दः पचाद्यजन्तः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । अद्रुहः । संपदादित्वाद्भावे क्विपि बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । कर्तरि वा क्विप् तत्पुरुषे ह्यव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं स्यात् । न च कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं यतो नञ् न गतिर्न च कारक इति । पा. ६-२-१३९ ॥

he agne ye maruto maho rajaso mahata udakasya varṣaṇaprakāraṃ vidustairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ | kīdṛśā marutaḥ | viśve sarve saptavidhagaṇopetāḥ | saptagaṇā vai marutaḥ | tai. saṃ. 2-2-11-1 | iti śruteḥ | devāso dyotamānā adruho droharahitā varṣaṇena sarvabhūtopakāritvāt | tathā copariṣṭādāmnāyate | udīrayathā marutaḥ samudrato yūyaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ varṣayathā purīṣiṇaḥ | ṛgve. 5-55-5 | iti | śākhāntare 'pi mantrāntarasya brāhmaṇamevamāmnāyate | marutāṃ pṛṣatayaḥ sthetyāha maruto vai vṛṣṭyā īśate iti | rajaḥśabdo yāskena bahudhā vyākhyātaḥ | rajo rajaterjyotī raja ucyata udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyante 'sṛgahanī rajasī ucyete | ni. 4-19 | iti || rajasaḥ | nabviṣayasyānisantasyetyādyudāttaḥ | viduḥ | vida jñāne | vido laṭo vā | pā. 3-4-83 | iti jherusādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | viśve | viśeḥ kvannantasya nittvādādyudāttatvam | devāsaḥ | ājjaserasuk | devaśabdaḥ pacādyajantaḥ | cittvādantodāttaḥ | adruhaḥ | saṃpadāditvādbhāve kvipi bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityantodāttatvam | kartari vā kvip tatpuruṣe hyavyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ syāt | na ca kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ yato nañ na gatirna ca kāraka iti | pā. 6-2-139 ||

Translation: "O Agni, the Maruts who viduḥ, know, the manner of raining of the mahas rajas, the great water: with those Maruts (come): that is the construction. Of what kind are the Maruts? Viśve, all, endowed with seven kinds of troops, from the Śruti 'The Maruts are of seven troops' (Tai. saṃ. 2-2-11-1); devāsaḥ, shining; adruhaḥ, free from malice, since by raining they benefit all beings. So it is declared later: 'O Maruts, you raise it from the ocean; you, rich in moisture, make the rain fall' (Ṛgveda 5-55-5). In another śākhā too the Brāhmaṇa of another mantra declares: 'He says, you are the dappled mares of the Maruts: the Maruts rule over rain.' The word rajas is explained by Yāska in many ways: 'Rajas is from rañj; light is called rajas; water is called rajas; the worlds are called rajāṃsi; blood and day are called the two rajasī' (Ni. 4-19)." (Grammatical tail: rajasaḥ, initial udātta by nabviṣayasyānisantasya; viduḥ, vida jñāne, us for jhi by vido laṭo vā (Pā. 3-4-83), the suffix accent, not lowered because joined with yad; viśve, initial udātta as viśva, ending in kvan, is nit; devāsaḥ, asuk by āj jaser asuk, the word deva an ac-final of the pac-ādi, final udātta as cit; adruhaḥ, kvip in the sense of the action as one of the sampad-ādi, and in the bahuvrīhi final udātta by nañsubhyām; or, with kvip in the agent sense, in a tatpuruṣa the first member, an indeclinable, would keep its accent; nor would the accent of the kṛt final member come, since nañ is neither a gati nor a kāraka (Pā. 6-2-139).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अद्रुहः (adruhaḥ) — without malice, that is, of a nature to do good | विश्वे (viśve) — all, that is, endowed with seven kinds of troops | ये देवासः (ye devāsaḥ) — which shining Marut deities | महः (mahaḥ) — much | रजसः (rajasaḥ) — of water (the manner of raining, that is, of pouring rain) | विदुः (viduḥ) — know | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — together with the Marut deities | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Marut deities are shining, joined in seven kinds of troops (the seven Maruts); they do no harm to anyone and do only good. They know how to pour rain abundantly. O Agni, come here together with such Marut deities.

original p. 790

Rik 3: English, Special Topics and grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

Come, Agni, with the Maruths [sic], who are ali [sic] divine, and devoid of malignity and who know how to cause the descent of great waters.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Maho rajasaḥ: mahata udakasya, of much water (the rain). For the word rajaḥ Yāska says

रजः । रजो रजतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यते । उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यन्ते ।

rajaḥ | rajo rajaterjyotī raja ucyate | udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyante |

(Ni. 4-19), that is, rajaḥ has the senses light (radiance), water and world; here the commentator has taken the sense water. The author of the Vedārthayatna gives the sense light. On his view the sense is: the Maruts who move in the sky full of great light. This sense too fits well here.

Devāsaḥ: an ancient usage of the word devāḥ; it means gods.

Viśve: all, that is, accompanied by seven troops. There is the Śruti statement

सप्तगणा वै मरुतः

saptagaṇā vai marutaḥ

(Tai. saṃ. 2-2-11-1).

Adruhaḥ: droharahitāḥ, those who do no malice, that is, those who do only good to people by pouring rain. On this the commentator has cited the following ṛk:

उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतो यूयं वृष्टिं वर्षयथा पुरीषिणः ॥ (ऋ. सं. ५-५५-५)

udīrayathā marutaḥ samudrato yūyaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ varṣayathā purīṣiṇaḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 5-55-5)

("O Maruts, you raise it from the ocean; you, rich in moisture, make the rain fall": editorial and tentative.) He has also cited the Brāhmaṇa statement

मरुतां पृषतयः स्थेत्याह मरुतो वै वृष्ट्या ईशते । (तै. ब्रा.)

marutāṃ pṛṣatayaḥ sthetyāha maruto vai vṛṣṭyā īśate | (tai. brā.)

("He says, you are the dappled mares of the Maruts; the Maruts rule over rain": editorial and tentative.) These mantras make clear the sense that the Marut deities bring about rain.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 790–792, noted briefly

रजसः (rajasaḥ): the word rajas is always neuter. So by "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū. "2-26" [?]), the first syllable of a word always neuter, not ending in is, is udātta; so rajas is initial udātta; it ends in the genitive singular.

विदुः (viduḥ): the root vida jñāne; after it laṭ, the 3rd plural substitute jhi: vid + jhi; śap by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68), luk of śap by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72). "Vido laṭo vā" (Pā. sū. 3-4-83): after the root vida jñāne, in place of the nine parasmaipada suffixes tip and the rest that came in place of laṭ,

original p. 791

Rik 3: grammar

the substitutes ṇal, atus, us | thal, athus, a | ṇal, va, ma come respectively; so us for jhi: vid + us, ru and visarga: viduḥ. Since, as ye maho rajaso viduḥ, there is connection with yad, the bar to total unaccentedness comes by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66). So the us has the suffix accent.

विश्वे (viśve): by "aśūpruṣi……viśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. sū. 1-149), the suffix kvan after viśa praveśane; by the nit accent it is initial udātta. After the word viśva the nominative plural jas; by "jasaḥ śī" (Pā. sū. 7-1-17) the substitute śī; the ś is called it and dropped: viśva + ī; guṇa by ād guṇaḥ.

देवासः (devāsaḥ): by "nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-134) the suffix ac after the root div. The suffix is cit, so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) it is final udātta. With the suffix ac as condition, the laghūpadha-guṇa for the i of the root. After the word deva, jas: deva + as; by "āj jaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) the augment asuk for jas. Being kit, by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46) it comes as the first part of jas: deva + asas; lengthening of like vowels: devāsas; ru and visarga.

अद्रुहः (adruhaḥ): the root druha jighāṃsāyām. After it, in the sense of the action, by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip, kvip; na druhaḥ yeṣāṃ te: a bahuvrīhi; the sense is the Maruts who have no doing of malice. Though the first member's accent is due by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, overriding it by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172), in a bahuvrīhi the final member after nañ and su is final udātta; so final udātta. Or, by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76), kvip comes after all roots, with or without upapadas, in the Veda and in the world too; so kvip in the agent sense; na + druhaḥ yeṣāṃ te: here too a bahuvrīhi. Druhaḥ are drohakartāraḥ: the Maruts who have no doers of malice. One must not make the tatpuruṣa na druhaḥ, adruhaḥ, not doers of malice. For if the tatpuruṣa is made, by "tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2), in a tatpuruṣa compound, words of equal sense, instrumental-final words, locative-final words, words denoting the standard of comparison, indeclinables, accusative-final words and kṛtya-final words, standing as the first member, keep their own accent. The word avyaya does not take indeclinables in general; there is the enumeration avyaye nañkunipātānām; so by this the first member's accent must come. Here the first member nañ is initial udātta by nipātā ādyudāttāḥ. So, the first member's

Page 792 (upper) — Rik 3: grammar (end)

accent coming, adruhaḥ would have to be initial udātta. But even if the tatpuruṣa is made, though the first member's accent is due by tatpuruṣe…, by its overriding rule "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), in a tatpuruṣa compound a kṛdanta after a gati, a kāraka or an upapada keeps its own accent; so the accent of the kṛt final member comes. The final member druh is final udātta by the root accent. So if the final member's accent comes, final udātta alone results. Although here druh follows neither a gati nor a kāraka, since nañ is neither a gati nor a kāraka, nañ is still an upapada. So, since the kṛdanta druh stands after an upapada, there is no obstacle at all to the accent of the kṛt final member. Thus the tatpuruṣa compound may be stated. Here the Vedabhāṣya says "yato nañ na gatiḥ na ca kārakam": since nañ has neither the name gati nor kāraka, the accent of the kṛt final member does not come, so the tatpuruṣa must not be stated and only the bahuvrīhi compound must be stated. It does not say here that nañ is not an upapada; so this may be known as deficient.

य उ॒ग्रा अ॒र्कमा॑नृ॒चुरना॑धृष्टास॒ ओज॑सा । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥४॥ [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । उग्राः । अर्कम् । आनृचुः । अनाधृष्टासः । ओजसा ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥४॥

ye | ugrāḥ | arkam | ānṛcuḥ | anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ | ojasā || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे मरुत उग्रास्तीव्राः सन्तोऽर्कमुदकमानृचुः अर्चितवन्तः । वर्षणेन संपादितवन्त इत्यर्थः । तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः । कीदृशा मरुतः । ओजसा बलेनानाधृष्टासोऽतिरस्कृताः । सर्वेभ्योऽपि प्रबला इत्यर्थः । अर्कशब्दस्योदकवाचित्वं वाजसनेयिन आमनन्ति । आपो वा अर्कः । शत. ब्रा. १०-६-५-२ । इति । तन्निर्वचनं च त-

he maruta ugrāstīvrāḥ santo 'rkamudakamānṛcuḥ arcitavantaḥ | varṣaṇena saṃpāditavanta ityarthaḥ | tairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ | kīdṛśā marutaḥ | ojasā balenānādhṛṣṭāso 'tiraskṛtāḥ | sarvebhyo 'pi prabalā ityarthaḥ | arkaśabdasyodakavācitvaṃ vājasaneyina āmananti | āpo vā arkaḥ | śata. brā. 10-6-5-2 | iti | tannirvacanaṃ ca ta-

एवामनन्ति । सोऽर्चन्नचरत्तस्यार्चत आपोऽजायन्तार्चते वै मे कमभूदिति तदेवार्कस्यार्कत्वम् । शत. ब्रा. १०-६-५-१ । इति । जगत्स्रष्टा हिरण्यगर्भ उदकं स्रष्टुमुद्युक्तोऽर्चन् उदकसत्यसंकल्पमहिमप्रख्यापनेन स्वात्मानं पूजयन्नचरत् । तथा पूजयतो हिरण्यगर्भस्य सकाशादुदकमुत्पन्नं तदानीमर्चतो मत्तः कमभूदित्यवोचत् । तेनोदकस्यार्कनाम निष्पन्नमित्यर्थः ॥ आनृचुः । अर्चतेः । अपस्पृधेथामित्यादिना । पा. ६-१-३६ । निपातितः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः । अनाधृष्टासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । ओजसा । उब्जेर्बले बलोपश्च । उ. ४-१९१ । इत्यसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

evāmananti | so 'rcannacarattasyārcata āpo 'jāyantārcate vai me kamabhūditi tadevārkasyārkatvam | śata. brā. 10-6-5-1 | iti | jagatsraṣṭā hiraṇyagarbha udakaṃ sraṣṭumudyukto 'rcan udakasatyasaṃkalpamahimaprakhyāpanena svātmānaṃ pūjayannacarat | tathā pūjayato hiraṇyagarbhasya sakāśādudakamutpannaṃ tadānīmarcato mattaḥ kamabhūdityavocat | tenodakasyārkanāma niṣpannamityarthaḥ || ānṛcuḥ | arcateḥ | apaspṛdhethāmityādinā | pā. 6-1-36 | nipātitaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogānna nighātaḥ | anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | ojasā | ubjerbale balopaśca | u. 4-191 | ityasun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "O Maruts: the Maruts who, being ugra, fierce, ānṛcuḥ, worshipped, the arka, water: that is, brought it about by raining; with those Maruts: that is the construction. Of what kind are the Maruts? Anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ, not overcome, ojasā, by strength: that is, mightier than all. That the word arka denotes water the Vājasaneyins declare: 'The waters are arka' (Śat. Brā. 10-6-5-2). Its derivation they declare too: 'He went about worshipping; from him, worshipping, the waters were born; "to me, worshipping, kam has come to be," he said: that is the arka-ness of arka' (Śat. Brā. 10-6-5-1). Hiraṇyagarbha, the creator of the world, intent on creating water, arcan, went about worshipping himself by making known the greatness of his true resolve concerning water. From Hiraṇyagarbha so worshipping water arose; then he said, 'From me, worshipping, kam has come to be.' So water got the name arka." (Grammatical tail: ānṛcuḥ, from arc, given ready-made by apaspṛdhethām… (Pā. 6-1-36), the suffix accent, not lowered because joined with yad; anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ, the accent of the indeclinable first member; ojasā, asun by ubjer bale balopaś ca (Uṇ. 4-191), initial udātta as nit.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

उग्राः (ugrāḥ) — moving swiftly | ओजसा (ojasā) — by strength | अनाधृष्टासः (anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ) — unchecked | ये (ye) — which Marut deities | अर्कम् (arkam) — water | आनृचुः (ānṛcuḥ) — rained | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — together with the Marut deities | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, come here together with the Marut deities, who have power and might that no one can check and who, blowing swiftly, rain water (pour down rain).

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, come hither with the Maruts, who are fierce (or blow fiercely) and send down rain and are unsurpassed in strength.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Ugrāḥ: tīvrāḥ; blowing swiftly.

Arkam: water. We explained earlier (page "384" [?]) the four kinds of sense Yāska gives for the word arka. Here the commentator gives another sense, water, for the word arka, and to support it he cites a statement of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa of the White Yajurveda:

सोऽर्चन्नचरत्तस्यार्चत आपोऽजायन्तार्चते वै मे कमभूदिति तदेवार्कस्यार्कत्वम् ॥ (श. ब्रा. १०-६-५-१)

so 'rcannacarattasyārcata āpo 'jāyantārcate vai me kamabhūditi tadevārkasyārkatvam || (śa. brā. 10-6-5-1)

The commentator explains it thus:

original p. 794

Rik 4: Special Topics (end) and grammar

जगत्स्रष्टा हिरण्यगर्भ उदकं स्रष्टुमुद्युक्तोऽर्चन् उदकसत्यसंकल्पमहिमप्रख्यापनेन स्वात्मानं पूजयन्नचरत् । तथा पूजयतो हिरण्यगर्भस्य सकाशादुदकमुत्पन्नम् । तदानीमर्चतो मत्तः कमभूदित्यवोचत् । तेनोदकस्यार्कनाम निष्पन्नमित्यर्थः ॥

jagatsraṣṭā hiraṇyagarbha udakaṃ sraṣṭumudyukto 'rcan udakasatyasaṃkalpamahimaprakhyāpanena svātmānaṃ pūjayannacarat | tathā pūjayato hiraṇyagarbhasya sakāśādudakamutpannam | tadānīmarcato mattaḥ kamabhūdityavocat | tenodakasyārkanāma niṣpannamityarthaḥ ||

That is: Hiraṇyagarbha (Prajāpati), having created the world, then intent on creating water, being true-willed, began to worship himself. While he was worshipping thus, water arose from that Prajāpati. Then Prajāpati said, "What is this that has arisen from me? (kam)"; for that reason, since kam (water) arose from worship, water got the name arka: that is the intent.

Ānṛcuḥ:

अर्चितवन्तः । वर्षणेन संपादितवन्तः

arcitavantaḥ | varṣaṇena saṃpāditavantaḥ

("They worshipped; they brought it about by raining.") They worshipped, they adored; that is, they rained the water produced by the act of worship.

Anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ:

अतिरस्कृताः । सर्वेभ्योऽपि प्रबलाः

atiraskṛtāḥ | sarvebhyo 'pi prabalāḥ

("Not overcome; mightier than all.") Those whom none can put down, that is, mightier than all, of greater power.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 794–795, noted briefly

आनृचुः (ānṛcuḥ):

अपस्पृधेथामानृचुरानृहुश्चिच्युषेतित्याजश्राताःश्रितमाशीराशीर्ताः

apaspṛdhethāmānṛcurānṛhuścicyuṣetityājaśrātāḥśritamāśīrāśīrtāḥ

(Pā. sū. 6-1-36). The root spardha saṃgharṣe; laṅ, 3rd-person [as printed; āthām is 2nd person] dual āthām: spardh + āthām. Here the root is doubled: spardh spardh + āthām. The r of the latter part takes saṃprasāraṇa, ṛ, and the a before the r drops: these are given ready-made. Spardh spṛdh + āthām: by "śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-61), in the abhyāsa the khay letters after ś, ṣ, s remain and the other letters drop; so in the first spardh the p remains and the other letters drop: paspṛdh, āthām, the augment aṭ, śap. By "āto ṅitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-81) iy for the ā; by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66) the y drops; by ād guṇaḥ: apaspṛdhethām. Or, with apa a separate preverb, the root spardh, laṅ, āthām, śap, āto ṅitaḥ, loss of y before val; the absence of the augment aṭ is Vedic: spardhethām. Ānṛcuḥ: arca pūjāyām; liṭ, jhi; by "parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatususthalathusaṇalvamāḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-82) us: arc + us; by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8) doubling: arc arc + us; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60), on the view taking the class or on the view of splitting the rule, the consonants of the abhyāsa drop: a + arc + us; by "ata ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-70) the short a at the start of the abhyāsa is lengthened: ā + arc + us; by "tasmān nuḍ dvihalaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-71) the augment nuṭ for a root with two consonants after the lengthened ā: ā + n + arc + us; ānarcuḥ is the usage in the world.

Page 795 (upper) — Rik 4: grammar (end)

In the Veda, by this sūtra, saṃprasāraṇa of the r, ṛ, and the loss of the a before the r: ānṛcuḥ. In ānṛhuḥ the same process for the root arh. Cyuṅ gatau: laṭ, thās, thāsas se; doubling: cyu + cyu + se; i for the u from the saṃprasāraṇa of the abhyāsa is given ready-made, and so is the absence of iṭ for se; pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca: cicyuṣe; in the world cucyuviṣe. Tyaja vayohānau: liṭ, tip, ṇal, doubling: tyaj + tyaj + a; saṃprasāraṇa of the abhyāsa given, the pūrvarūpa, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ: ti + tyaj + a, the penultimate vṛddhi: tityāja. Śrīñ pāke: the suffix kta; śrā substituted for śrī is given; in the plural, śrātāḥ; in śritam the shortening for that root is given. For śrīñ preceded by ā, before kvip, the substitute śir. In āśīrtāḥ, for śrīñ preceded by ā, before the kta suffix, the substitute śir, and the absence of the n due for the kta by radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ, are given. So by this sūtra ānṛcuḥ is given ready-made. The us has the suffix accent. Since the bar "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) comes, it is not wholly unaccented.

अनाधृष्टासः (anādhṛṣṭāsaḥ): the analysis is na ādhṛṣṭāḥ. Āj jaser asuk. By "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the indeclinable first member.

ओजसा (ojasā): ubja ārjave. By "ubjer bale balopaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "4-631" [?]), after ubja ārjave, in the sense of strength, asun comes, and the b drops: uj + as; the laghūpadha-guṇa: ojas. Initial udātta by the nit accent. With the instrumental singular ṭā: ojasā.

॥४॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under शु, घो, क्ष, रि, म and ग्न; strokes over व, सो, द, द्भि and ग.

ये शु॒भ्रा घो॒रव॑र्पसः सुक्ष॒त्रासो॑ रि॒शाद॑सः । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥५॥ [accent ?]

ye śubhrā́ ghorávarpasaḥ sukṣatrā́so riśā́dasaḥ | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||5|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । शुभ्राः । घोरऽवर्पसः । सुऽक्षत्रासः । रिशादसः ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥५॥

ye | śubhrāḥ | ghora 'varpasaḥ | su 'kṣatrāsaḥ | riśādasaḥ || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||5||

original p. 796

Rik 5: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥३६॥ closes Varga 36.

ये मरुतः शुभ्रत्वादिगुणोपेतास्तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः । शुभ्राः शोभना घोरवर्पस उग्ररूपधराः सुक्षत्रासः शोभनधनोपेता रिशादसो हिंसकानां भक्षकाः । मघमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु क्षत्रं भग इति पठितम् ॥ शुभ्राः । स्फायितञ्चीत्यादिना शुभेरौणादिको रक्प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । घोरवर्पसः । घोरं वर्पो येषाम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुक्षत्रासः । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसि । पा. ६-२-११९ । इत्येतत्तु न भवति । क्षत्रशब्दस्यान्तोदात्तत्वात् । रिशन्ति हिंसन्तीति रिशाः । तानदन्तीति रिशादसः । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन्प्रत्ययः । नित्स्वरेणोत्तरपदमाद्युदात्तम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते ॥३६॥

ye marutaḥ śubhratvādiguṇopetāstairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ | śubhrāḥ śobhanā ghoravarpasa ugrarūpadharāḥ sukṣatrāsaḥ śobhanadhanopetā riśādaso hiṃsakānāṃ bhakṣakāḥ | maghamityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu dhananāmasu kṣatraṃ bhaga iti paṭhitam || śubhrāḥ | sphāyitañcītyādinā śubherauṇādiko rakpratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | ghoravarpasaḥ | ghoraṃ varpo yeṣām | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | sukṣatrāsaḥ | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchandasi | pā. 6-2-119 | ityetattu na bhavati | kṣatraśabdasyāntodāttatvāt | riśanti hiṃsantīti riśāḥ | tānadantīti riśādasaḥ | sarvadhātubhyo 'sunpratyayaḥ | nitsvareṇottarapadamādyudāttam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva śiṣyate ||36||

Translation: "The Maruts who are endowed with qualities such as brightness: with those Maruts: that is the construction. Śubhrāḥ, beautiful; ghoravarpasaḥ, bearing fierce forms; sukṣatrāsaḥ, possessed of fine wealth; riśādasaḥ, devourers of those who do harm. Kṣatram and bhagaḥ are read among the twenty-eight names for wealth beginning magham." (Grammatical tail: śubhrāḥ, the Uṇādi suffix rak after śubh by sphāyitañci…, the suffix accent; ghoravarpasaḥ, "whose form is fierce", the first member's accent in the bahuvrīhi; sukṣatrāsaḥ, final udātta of the final member in the bahuvrīhi by nañsubhyām; ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (Pā. 6-2-119) does not apply, since kṣatra is final udātta; riśādasaḥ, "riśāḥ, those who harm; they eat them", the suffix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun, the final member initial udātta by the nit accent, and that alone stays by the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | ये (ye) — which Marut deities | शुभ्राः (śubhrāḥ) — endowed with qualities such as brightness | घोरवर्पसः (ghoravarpasaḥ) — bearing fierce forms | सुक्षत्रासः (sukṣatrāsaḥ) — accompanied by excellent wealth | रिशादसः (riśādasaḥ) — devouring (destroying) the enemies who do harm | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — together with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, the Marut deities are always bright; they have fierce forms (by their nature of blowing swiftly); they have excellent wealth; they kill enemies. Come here together with such Marut deities.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, come with the Maruths [sic] who are brilliant, have frightful forms who are possessors of great wealth and destroyers of the enemies.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Śubhrāḥ: shining, clear: "Brilliant, resplendent, (transparent ?)" [as printed] and so on.

Ghoravarpasaḥ:

घोररूपाः द्वयोश्चानयोः परस्परविरोधित्वात्कालभेदेन योजना । शोभनाः क्रीडाकाले । घोररूपाः संग्रामकाले ।

ghorarūpāḥ dvayoścānayoḥ parasparavirodhitvātkālabhedena yojanā | śobhanāḥ krīḍākāle | ghorarūpāḥ saṃgrāmakāle |

("Of fierce forms; since these two contradict each other, they are to be joined by difference of time: beautiful at the time of play, of fierce form at the time of battle.") Having cruel or fearful forms, "of terrible or frightful forms" [as printed]. The words used in this ṛk,

original p. 797

Rik 5: Special Topics (end) and grammar

śubhrāḥ, shining or endowed with gentle qualities, and ghoravarpasaḥ, having fearful forms, are they not words of mutually contradictory sense? So the sense is: gentle in nature at the time of play, and taking fierce form at the time of war.

Sukṣatrāsaḥ: since the word kṣatram is read among the twenty-eight names for wealth beginning magha (Ni. "2-10" [as read, ?]), sukṣatrāsaḥ means those who have good wealth.

Riśādasaḥ:

रिशन्ति हिंसन्तीति रिशाः शत्रवः । तानदन्तीति रिशादसः ।

riśanti hiṃsantīti riśāḥ śatravaḥ | tānadantīti riśādasaḥ |

("Riśāḥ, the enemies who harm; they eat them: riśādasaḥ.") The sense is: devouring, that is destroying, the enemies who do harm.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar on p. 797, noted briefly

शुभ्राः (śubhrāḥ): by "sphāyitañcivañciśakikṣipikṣudisṛpitṛpidṛpivandyundiśvitivṛtyajinīpadimadimudikhidichidibhidimandicandidahidasidambhivasivāśiśīṅhasisidhiśubhibhyo rak" (Uṇ. sū. "2-170" [?]), the Uṇādi suffix rak after the root śubh; the suffix accent comes.

घोरवर्पसः (ghoravarpasaḥ): by "vṛñśīṅbhyāṃ rūpasvāṅgayoḥ puṭ ca" (Uṇ. sū. "4-640" [?]), after the roots vṛñ saṃbhaktau and śīṅ svapne, when the senses form and body-part respectively are to be expressed, the suffix asun comes, and the augment puṭ for it; so after the root vṛ the suffix asun with the augment puṭ. Varpaḥ means form. Ghoraṃ varpaḥ yeṣāṃ te ghoravarpasaḥ; being a bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent; the word ghora is final udātta.

सुक्षत्रासः (sukṣatrāsaḥ): sukṣatraṃ dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te. Āj jaser asuk. The first member's accent being due, by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172), overriding it, final udātta comes. Here the word kṣatra stands after the word su. Yet the initial udātta for kṣatra by "ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-2-119), the exception to nañsubhyām, does not come, because the word kṣatra is final udātta. "Ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-2-119) means that in a bahuvrīhi compound a two-vowel word after the word su, if initial udātta, remains initial udātta. Dvyac means a word with two vowels. Since the word kṣatra is final udātta, ādyudāttaṃ dvyac… does not apply.

रिशादसः (riśādasaḥ): the root riśa hiṃsāyām; riśanti hiṃsanti iti riśāḥ; riśān adanti bhakṣayanti iti riśādas. After the root ad, with the word riśa as upapada, the suffix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; the final member is initial udātta by the nit accent; after compounding, the accent of the kṛt final member by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139). So the initial udātta of the final member alone stays.

॥५॥

original p. 798

Sūkta 19, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under क (नाक), च, दि, दे, स (देवास), म and ग्न; strokes over धि, स (आसते), द्भि and ग.

ये नाक॒स्याधि॑ रोच॒ने दि॒वि दे॒वास॒ आस॑ते । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥६॥ [accent ?]

ye nākasyā́dhi rocané diví devā́sa ā́sate | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||6|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । नाकस्य । अधि । रोचने । दिवि । देवासः । आसते ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥६॥

ye | nākasya | adhi | rocane | divi | devāsaḥ | āsate || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये मरुतो नाकस्याधि दुःखरहितस्य सूर्यस्योपरि दिवि द्युलोके रोचने दीप्यमाने ये देवासः स्वयमपि दीप्यमाना आसते । तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः ॥ नाकस्य । कं सुखम् । तद्यस्मिन्नास्त्यसावकः इति बहुव्रीहिं कृत्वा पश्चान्नञ् । न अकोऽनाक इति नञ्तत्पुरुषः । नलोपो नञः । पा. ६-३-७३ । इति लोपो न भवति । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना । पा. ६-३-७५ । प्रकृतिभावात् । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थेत्यादिना । पा. ६-२-२ । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेनोदात्तत्वम् । प्रथमतस्तत्पुरुषं कृत्वा पश्चाद्बहुव्रीहावुत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं स्यात् । अधिशब्द उपर्यर्थे । उपसर्गप्रतिरूपको निपातः । रोचने । रुच दीप्तौ । अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेरिति युच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । दिवि । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । देवासः । आज्जसेरसुगित्यसुक् । आसते । आस उपवेशने । अनुदात्तेत्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । झस्यादादेशः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तेत्त्वाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वम् । यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः ॥

ye maruto nākasyādhi duḥkharahitasya sūryasyopari divi dyuloke rocane dīpyamāne ye devāsaḥ svayamapi dīpyamānā āsate | tairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ || nākasya | kaṃ sukham | tadyasminnāstyasāvakaḥ iti bahuvrīhiṃ kṛtvā paścānnañ | na ako 'nāka iti nañtatpuruṣaḥ | nalopo nañaḥ | pā. 6-3-73 | iti lopo na bhavati | nabhrāṇnapādityādinā | pā. 6-3-75 | prakṛtibhāvāt | tatpuruṣe tulyārthetyādinā | pā. 6-2-2 | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvenodāttatvam | prathamatastatpuruṣaṃ kṛtvā paścādbahuvrīhāvuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ syāt | adhiśabda uparyarthe | upasargapratirūpako nipātaḥ | rocane | ruca dīptau | anudāttetaśca halāderiti yuc | cita ityantodāttatvam | divi | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | devāsaḥ | ājjaserasugityasuk | āsate | āsa upaveśane | anudāttettvādātmanepadam | jhasyādādeśaḥ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | anudāttettvāllasārvadhātukānudāttatvam | yadvṛttayogānna nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "The Maruts who, devāsaḥ, themselves shining too, āsate, sit nākasyādhi, above the sun, which is free from sorrow, divi, in the heavenly world, rocane, shining: with those Maruts: that is the construction." (Grammatical tail: nākasya, "kam is happiness; he in whom it is not is aka": having made the bahuvrīhi, then nañ: "not aka, nāka", a nañ-tatpuruṣa; the loss by nalopo nañaḥ (Pā. 6-3-73) does not come because of the prakṛtibhāva by nabhrāṇ napāt… (Pā. 6-3-75); udātta by the accent of the indeclinable first member by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (Pā. 6-2-2); if the tatpuruṣa were made first and then the bahuvrīhi, there would be final udātta of the final member; adhi in the sense "above", a particle resembling a preverb; rocane, ruca dīptau, yuc by anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ, final udātta by citaḥ; divi, the ending udātta by ūḍidam…; devāsaḥ, asuk by āj jaser asuk; āsate, āsa upaveśane, ātmanepada as anudāttet, at for jha, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ, the lasārvadhātuka unaccented as the root is anudāttet, not lowered because joined with yad.)

original p. 799

Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | ये देवासः (ye devāsaḥ) — which Marut deities | नाकस्य (nākasya) — of the sun's orb, free from sorrow | अधि (adhi) — above | रोचने (rocane) — shining | दिवि (divi) — in the heavenly world | आसते (āsate) — (sitting) are | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — joined with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, come here with the Marut deities who are in the shining heaven in the region above the sun's orb, which is free from sorrow.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, come hither with those divine Maruths [sic] who sit in resplendent heaven above the sky.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Nākasya: though nāka means heaven, since this ṛk has another word for heaven, divi, the commentator has derived the word nāka from the sense of its parts:

कं सुखम् । तद्यस्मिन्नास्तीत्यसावकः न अकः नाकः

kaṃ sukham | tadyasminnāstītyasāvakaḥ na akaḥ nākaḥ

Kam means happiness. Since it is not there, sorrow is called akaḥ. Again, since there is no akaḥ (sorrow), the place of happiness is named nākaḥ, heaven: that is the intent. Here, saying that nākaḥ is the sun's orb, he takes the word adhi as "above it".

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 799–800, noted briefly

नाकस्य (nākasya): kam means happiness. Na vidyate kam, sukhaṃ yasmin saḥ: a bahuvrīhi. By "nalopo nañaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-73), when a final member follows, the n of nañ drops; so the n drops: aka. The word final member is current in the sense of the last member of a compound. Now na + akaḥ: a tatpuruṣa. By "nabhrāṇnapānnavedānāsatyānamucinakulanakhanapuṃsakanakṣatranakranākeṣu prakṛtyā" (Pā. sū. 6-3-75) the nañ in all these words keeps its form; since the prakṛtibhāva comes, the n of nañ does not drop by nalopo nañaḥ. Nañ, being a particle, is initial udātta by nipātā ādyudāttāḥ; after the tatpuruṣa compound na-akaḥ, nākaḥ, by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the indeclinable first member comes. Here one must not first make the tatpuruṣa, na kam, akam, and then the bahuvrīhi, na vidyate akaṃ sukhābhāvaḥ yasmin saḥ. If so made, by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172) the final member aka would have to be final udātta.

अधि (adhi): this is in the sense "above". Being a particle resembling a preverb, it is initial udātta; in nākasya, the a of sya is unaccented by the sup accent. The ā from the single substitute of lengthening of like vowels

original p. 800

Rik 6: grammar (end)

is udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ. Since this udātta follows, the unaccented ka before it takes the anudātta tone by "udāttasvaritaparasya [sannataraḥ]".

रोचने (rocane): the root ruca dīptau, anudāttet. By "anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-149), after a consonant-initial intransitive root that is anudāttet, the suffix yuc comes; so the suffix yuc. By "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1) ana for yu; the laghūpadha-guṇa: rocana. The suffix is cit; so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) final udātta; locative singular rocane.

दिवि (divi): by "ūḍidaṃpadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-171) the case-ending after div is udātta.

देवासः (devāsaḥ): by āj jaser asuk the augment asuk for jas.

आसते (āsate): āsa upaveśane, anudāttet; so by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12) the ātmanepada; laṭ, 3rd plural jha. Śap as vikaraṇa by kartari śap; luk of śap by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72); by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5), for the jh of an ātmanepada suffix after what does not end in a, the substitute at: ās + ata. By "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79) e for the a that is the ṭi: āsate. Since it follows the word ye, containing yad, by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) (vartate asminn iti vṛttam, the sense being the substrate: yadaḥ vṛttam, the word that is the substrate of the presence of the word yad, that is, after whatever word contains yad, a tiṅanta is not unaccented). Since yadvṛttāt is a fifth-case statement, the sense is "a tiṅanta immediately after a word containing yad is not unaccented"; this would arise from the paribhāṣā "tasmād ity uttarasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-67). Yet since the word pūjita is taken again in "pūjanāt pūjitam…" (Pā. sū. 8-1-37 [as printed "8-1-1-37"]), it is made known that "atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam iṣyate", that in this section, even with a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required. So tasmād ity uttarasya does not apply here. Though there is an intervening word, the bar comes by yadvṛttān nityam. So it is not wholly unaccented. The root ās being anudāttet, by "tāsyanudātteṅ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186) and the rest, the ate, a lasārvadhātuka, is unaccented.

॥६॥ An ornament follows at the foot of p. 800. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The print has ई॒ङ्खय॑न्ति; the Kannada grammar writes ईङ्खयन्ति / ईन्ख्.

original p. 801

Sūkta 19, Rik 7

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under ई, न्ति, ति (तिरः), मु, ण, म (मरु) and ग्न; strokes over य (ईङ्खय), व (पर्व), स (समु), म (मर्ण), द्भि and ग.

य ई॒ङ्खय॑न्ति॒ पर्व॑तान्ति॒रः स॑मु॒द्रम॑र्ण॒वम् । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥७॥ [accent ?]

ya īṅkháyanti párvatān tiráḥ samudrám arṇavám | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||7|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । ईङ्खयन्ति । पर्वतान् । तिरः । समुद्रम् । अर्णवम् ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥७॥

ye | īṅkhayanti | parvatān | tiraḥ | samudram | arṇavam || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये मरुतः पर्वतान्मेघानीङ्खयन्ति चालयन्ति तथार्णवमुदकयुक्तं समुद्रं तिरः कुर्वन्तीति शेषः । निश्चलस्य जलस्य तरङ्गाद्युत्पत्तये चालनं तिरस्कारः । तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः ॥ ईङ्खयन्ति । उख उखीत्यादावीखिर्गत्यर्थः । हेतुमति चेति णिच् । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । णिजन्तधातोश्चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । पर्वतान् । पूर्व पर्व मर्व पूरणे । औणादिकोऽतन् । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

ye marutaḥ parvatānmeghānīṅkhayanti cālayanti tathārṇavamudakayuktaṃ samudraṃ tiraḥ kurvantīti śeṣaḥ | niścalasya jalasya taraṅgādyutpattaye cālanaṃ tiraskāraḥ | tairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ || īṅkhayanti | ukha ukhītyādāvīkhirgatyarthaḥ | hetumati ceti ṇic | idito num dhātoriti num | ṇijantadhātościta ityantodāttatvam | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | parvatān | pūrva parva marva pūraṇe | auṇādiko 'tan | pratyayasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "The Maruts who īṅkhayanti, set moving, the parvatas, clouds, and likewise tiraḥ, make overturned (is to be supplied), the samudra, arṇava, which has water: setting the still water in motion to raise waves and the like is the tiraskāra. With those Maruts: that is the construction." (Grammatical tail: īṅkhayanti, īkhi in the sense of going, as in ukha ukhi…, ṇic by hetumati ca, num by idito num dhātoḥ, final udātta of the ṇic-final root as cit, śap unaccented as pit, and with the lasārvadhātuka accent of the tiṅ the root accent alone remains; parvatān, pūrva parva marva pūraṇe, the Uṇādi atan, the suffix accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | ये (ye) — which Marut deities | पर्वतान् (parvatān) — the clouds | ईङ्खयन्ति (īṅkhayanti) — set moving | अर्णवम् (arṇavam) — joined with water | समुद्रम् (samudram) — the ocean | तिरः (tiraḥ) — stir up into waves | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, the Marut deities have the power to shake the clouds; they stir up the great ocean, full of fathomless water. Come here together with such Marut deities.

original p. 802

Rik 7: English, Special Topics and grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, come hither with Maruths [sic] who scatter the clouds and agitate the sea (with waves).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Parvatān: meghān. Since the word parvata is read among the thirty names for cloud beginning adriḥ (Ni. "1-10" [as read, ?]), here parvata means cloud. Skandasvāmin gives two senses for parvata, mountain and cloud. Since it is impossible for the wind, however hard it blows, to shake a mountain, it is right to give the sense cloud here.

Tiraḥ: tiraskurvanti: here the word kurvanti is to be supplied. "Overturning" means: blowing hard so that waves rise in the ocean, and stirring up the ocean.

Arṇavam: arṇaḥ means water (Ni. "1-12" [as read, ?]). Arṇavam means that which has water, that is, the ocean.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 802–803, noted briefly

ईङ्खयन्ति (īṅkhayanti): the root īkhi is in the daṇḍaka "ukha ukhi …… gatyarthāḥ". It is idit; so by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-58) the augment num: īnkh. By "naś cāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. sū. 8-3-24) anusvāra for the n; by "anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-58) the homorganic: īṅkh. Parvatāḥ īṅkhanti: the clouds move. Īṅkhataḥ parvatān prerayanti marutaḥ: the Maruts drive the moving clouds. So the Maruts are causing agents; they also have the name hetu. "Tatprayojako hetuś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-55): tasya prayojakaḥ hetusaṃjñaḥ kartṛsaṃjñaś ca syāt: that which impels the agent gets the names hetu and agent. So the Maruts, impellers of the clouds, which are the agents of the root īṅkh, have both the names agent and hetu. The activity residing in the causer is called hetumat: hetuḥ asmin asti iti hetumān, the activity that is the substrate of the located-ness defined by the locus residing in the hetu: that is the sense of hetumat. When this activity is meant, by "hetumati ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-26), in the sense of impelling and the like, the activity of the causer, the suffix ṇic comes after the root; so the suffix ṇic after the root: īṅkh + i.

Page 803 (upper) — Rik 7: grammar (end)

The suffix ṇic is cit; so īṅkhi is final udātta by citaḥ. After it laṭ, the suffix jhi; by "jho 'ntaḥ" ant for the jh; by kartari śap: īṅkhi + a + anti; guṇa, the substitute ay, the pararūpa: īṅkhayanti. Śap being pit, it is unaccented; jhi, standing after the śap, an adupadeśa, is unaccented by "tāsyanudātteṅ…". The root accent alone remains.

पर्वतान् (parvatān): after (pūrva) parva marva pūraṇe the Uṇādi suffix atan comes. The suffix being nit, the word parvata is initial udātta by ñnityādir nityam.

॥७॥

original p. 803

Sūkta 19, Rik 8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under त (तन्व), र (रश्मि), ति (तिरः), मु, म (मरु) and ग्न; strokes over न्ति, भि, स (समु), ज, द्भि and ग.

आ ये त॒न्वन्ति॑ र॒श्मिभि॑स्ति॒रः स॑मु॒द्रमोज॑सा । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥८॥ [accent ?]

ā ye tanvánti raśmíbhis tiráḥ samudrám ójasā | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||8|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । ये । तन्वन्ति । रश्मिऽभिः । तिरः । समुद्रम् । ओजसा ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥८॥

ā | ye | tanvanti | raśmi 'bhiḥ | tiraḥ | samudram | ojasā || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये मरुतो रश्मिभिः सूर्यकिरणैः सहा तन्वन्ति आप्नुवन्ति । आकाशमिति शेषः । किंच ओजसा स्वकीयबलेन समुद्रं तिरस्कुर्वन्ति । तैर्मरुद्भिरित्यन्वयः ॥ तन्वन्ति । तनु विस्तारे । लटो झोऽन्तः । तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः । पा. ३-१-७९ । सतिशिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्य इति तिङ एवाद्युदात्तत्वम् । समुद्रम् । उन्दी क्लेदने । स्फायितञ्चीति रक् । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

ye maruto raśmibhiḥ sūryakiraṇaiḥ sahā tanvanti āpnuvanti | ākāśamiti śeṣaḥ | kiṃca ojasā svakīyabalena samudraṃ tiraskurvanti | tairmarudbhirityanvayaḥ || tanvanti | tanu vistāre | laṭo jho 'ntaḥ | tanādikṛñbhya uḥ | pā. 3-1-79 | satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvamanyatra vikaraṇebhya iti tiṅa evādyudāttatvam | samudram | undī kledane | sphāyitañcīti rak | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "The Maruts who, raśmibhiḥ, with the sun's rays, ā tanvanti, pervade (the sky, is to be supplied); and further, ojasā, by their own strength, overturn the ocean: with those Maruts: that is the construction." (Grammatical tail: tanvanti, tanu vistāre, ant for jha of laṭ, u by tanādikṛñbhya uḥ (Pā. 3-1-79); by the statement on satiśiṣṭa accent "except for vikaraṇas", the tiṅ alone is initial udātta; samudram, undī kledane, rak by sphāyitañci…, in the compound the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | ये (ye) — which Marut deities | रश्मिभिः (raśmibhiḥ) — together with the sun's rays | (the sky) आ तन्वन्ति (ā tanvanti) — pervade everywhere | (and) ओजसा (ojasā) — by their own power | समुद्रम् (samudram) — the ocean | तिरः (tiraḥ) — stir up into waves | (such) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

original p. 804

Rik 8: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, come here with the Marut deities who, together with the sun's rays, pervade all the sky and by their strength stir up the ocean.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, come hither with the Maruths [sic] who spread all over the sky with the rays of the Sun and with their strength agitate the ocean.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Raśmibhiḥ ā tanvanti: pervading the sky together with the sun's rays: that is, as the sun's rays pervade the whole sky in an instant, so the wind too pervades the sky or the air.

Ojasā: the intent is that, because the wind blows hard, huge waves rise in the ocean.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 804–805, noted briefly

तन्वन्ति (tanvanti): the root tanu vistāre; after it, by "vartamāne laṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-123), laṭ, 3rd plural jhi. By "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3) ant for the jh: tan + anti. By "tanādikṛñbhya uḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-79), after the roots of the tan-ādi group and after the root kṛñ, when a sārvadhātuka in the agent sense follows, the suffix u comes; so after tan the suffix u: tan + u + anti. By "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) guṇa o is due for the u; but by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) the sārvadhātuka jhi is ṅit, so by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) guṇa is barred; so no guṇa. By "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) v for the u by the yaṇ substitute: tanvanti. The suffix accent of u comes by a rule enjoining it after the accents of the others have arisen; so, though it is satiśiṣṭa, by "satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ", while the satiśiṣṭa accent is strong in places other than vikaraṇas, the satiśiṣṭa accent of u, being a vikaraṇa, is not strong. So the anti belonging to the tiṅ suffix is initial udātta by the suffix accent.

Page 805 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

समुद्रम् (samudram): after the root undī kledane preceded by the preverb sam, by "sphāyitañcivañciśakikṣipikṣudisṛpitṛpidṛpivandyundi…" (Uṇ. sū. "2-170" [?]) the suffix rak comes. By "anidhitāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-24) the penultimate n drops: samudra. The word udra is final udātta by the suffix accent; after compounding with sam too, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), the accent of the kṛt final member comes, and that accent stays.

॥८॥

Page 805 (lower) — Sūkta 19, Rik 9 (last ṛk of the sūkta and of the volume)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥ Read as printed: bars under अ, त्वा, सृ, सो, म (मरु) and ग्न; strokes over व (पूर्व), मि, धु, द्भि and ग.

अ॒भि त्वा॒ पूर्व॑पीतये सृ॒जामि॑ सो॒म्यं मधु॑ । [accent ?] म॒रुद्भि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥९॥ [accent ?]

abhí tvā pū́rvapītaye sṛjā́mi somyáṃ mádhu | [accent ?] marúdbhir agna ā́ gahi ||9|| [accent ?]

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि । त्वा । पूर्वऽपीतये । सृजामि । सोम्यम् । मधु ॥ मरुत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥९॥

abhi | tvā | pūrva 'pītaye | sṛjāmi | somyam | madhu || marut 'bhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥३७॥ closes Varga 37.

हे अग्ने पूर्वपीतये पूर्वकाले प्रवृत्ताय पानाय त्वां प्रति सोम्यं मधु सोमसंबन्धिनं मधुररसमभि सृजामि । सर्वतः संपादयामि । अतस्त्वं मरुद्भिः सहात्रागच्छ ॥ अभि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । त्वा । त्वामौ द्वितीयाया इति त्वादेशः सर्वानुदात्तः । पूर्वपीतये । पूर्वा चासौ पीतिश्च । पुंवत्कर्मधारयेत्यादिना । पा. ६-३-४२ । पुंवद्भावः । सृजामि । सृज विसर्गे । मिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । विकरणस्वरः । सोम्यम् । सोममर्हति यः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । मधु । फलिपाटिनमीत्यादिना । उ. १-१९ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वम् । अन्यद्गतम् ॥३७॥

he agne pūrvapītaye pūrvakāle pravṛttāya pānāya tvāṃ prati somyaṃ madhu somasaṃbandhinaṃ madhurarasamabhi sṛjāmi | sarvataḥ saṃpādayāmi | atastvaṃ marudbhiḥ sahātrāgaccha || abhi | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttatvam | tvā | tvāmau dvitīyāyā iti tvādeśaḥ sarvānudāttaḥ | pūrvapītaye | pūrvā cāsau pītiśca | puṃvatkarmadhārayetyādinā | pā. 6-3-42 | puṃvadbhāvaḥ | sṛjāmi | sṛja visarge | mipaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | vikaraṇasvaraḥ | somyam | somamarhati yaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | madhu | phalipāṭinamītyādinā | u. 1-19 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtterādyudāttatvam | anyadgatam ||37||

Translation: "O Agni, pūrvapītaye, for the drinking that takes place first, abhi sṛjāmi, I prepare on all sides, towards you, the somya madhu, the sweet juice belonging to soma. So come here with the Maruts." (Grammatical tail: abhi, final udātta by evam-ādīnām antaḥ; tvā, the substitute tvā by tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ, wholly unaccented; pūrvapītaye, "it is first and it is a drinking", puṃvadbhāva by puṃvat karmadhāraya… (Pā. 6-3-42); sṛjāmi, sṛja visarge, mip unaccented as pit, the vikaraṇa accent; somyam, "that which deserves soma", final udātta by the suffix accent; madhu, the suffix u by phalipāṭinami… (Uṇ. 1-19), initial udātta as nit is carried on; the rest has been explained.)

original p. 806

Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | त्वा (tvā) — for you, or with you in view | पूर्वपीतये (pūrvapītaye) — for drinking first (before all) | सोम्यम् (somyam) — belonging to soma | मधु (madhu) — the sweet juice | अभि सृजामि (abhi sṛjāmi) — I pour (into the vessel) and make ready | (you) मरुद्भिः (marudbhiḥ) — with the Marut deities | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, I pour the tasty soma juice into the vessel and make it ready for you to drink first of all. So come here together with the Marut deities.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, I pour out the sweet drink of Soma to you that you may drink first ; come hither with the Maruths [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Pūrvapītaye: for drinking first of all. For this word the scholar Wilson has given the wrong sense "as of old" [as printed], formerly. The sense given by the commentator, "first of all", is the fitting one.

Abhi sṛjāmi:

सर्वतः संपादयामि

sarvataḥ saṃpādayāmi

("I prepare on all sides.") I pour into the vessel and make ready.

Somyam:

सोममर्हति यः

somamarhati yaḥ

("That which deserves soma.") Worthy of soma, belonging to soma. Madhu: sweet, tasty; somyaṃ madhu means the tasty soma juice.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 806–808, noted briefly

अभि (abhi): final udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ".

त्वा (tvā): for tvām, the accusative-final of the base yuṣmad, by "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-23), the accusative-singular forms of yuṣmad and asmad, standing after a word and not at the start of a pāda, take the substitutes tvā and mā respectively, and these are wholly unaccented; so the wholly unaccented substitute tvā comes.

original p. 807

Rik 9: grammar

पूर्वपीतये (pūrvapītaye): pūrvā cāsau pītiś ca, pūrvapītiḥ. In "puṃvat karmadhārayajātīyadeśīyeṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-3-42) the words striyāḥ, puṃvat, bhāṣitapuṃskād anūṅ and striyām are carried on from the sūtra "striyāḥ puṃvad bhāṣitapuṃskād anūṅ samānādhikaraṇe striyām apūraṇīpriyādiṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-3-34). By "aluk uttarapade" (Pā. sū. 6-3-1) uttarapade is the heading. Bhāṣitaḥ pumān yasmin pravṛttinimitte tat bhāṣitapuṃskam; bhāṣitapuṃskam asyāsti iti bhāṣitapuṃskam, ending in ac in the sense of arśa-ādi: a word that has a ground of use in which masculinity has been stated is meant as bhāṣitapuṃska. Ūṅaḥ abhāvaḥ, or na ūṅ, anūṅ; bhāṣitapuṃskāt anūṅ ūṅabhāvaḥ yasyāḥ sā: a bahuvrīhi; by force of the ready-made form, the ablative of the compound member bhāṣitapuṃskāt is not dropped, and the genitive after the compound is dropped. The vyadhikaraṇa compound too is by the ready-made form; by force of the explanation, apūraṇīpriyādiṣu is not carried on here. Extension is said to be of seven kinds: "kārya-rūpa-nimittārtha-śāstra-tādātmya-śabditāḥ | vyapadeśaś ca saptaite 'tideśān pracakṣate". In subāmantrite there is extension of identity; here, extension of form: whatever form there is in the masculine, that same form comes. So the sense of the sūtra puṃvat is: the feminine word that stands immediately before the final member of a karmadhāraya, or immediately before the suffixes jātīyar and deśīyar, having a ground of use in which masculinity has been stated and not having the suffix ūṅ, takes the masculine form. With pūrvā + pīti, by this sūtra pūrvā takes the masculine form: pūrvapīti; in the dative singular pūrvapītaye.

सृजामि (sṛjāmi): sṛja visarge, a root of the tud-ādi. Laṭ, 1st singular mip: sṛj + mi; the vikaraṇa śap [as printed; the tud-ādi take śa]: sṛj + a + mi; by "ato dīrgho yañi" (Pā. sū. 7-3-101) lengthening: sṛjāmi. Mip being pit, it is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau. The vikaraṇa has the suffix accent.

सोम्यम् (somyam): by "somam arhati yaḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-4-137), after the accusative-final word soma, in the sense "deserves", the suffix ya comes; so ya after somam: soma + am + ya. The am, part of the stem, takes luk by supo dhātu…; by yasyeti ca the a before the suffix drops: somya. This is final udātta by the suffix accent.

मधु (madhu): by "phalipāṭinami…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-18" [?; the second digit is blotted]) the suffix u. Since in the sūtra phalipāṭi… "nit" is carried on, by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197)

Page 808 (upper) — Rik 9: grammar (end)

the word madhu is initial udātta. The derivation of the word madhu is set out at "madhumantaṃ" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-13-2). For the other words the derivation was set out earlier.

॥ Closing verse and colophon (Sanskrit, in Kannada script) ॥

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थाँश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthām̐ś caturo deyād vidyā-tīrtha-maheśvaraḥ ||

Translation: "May Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the light of the meaning of the Veda, grant the four human aims." The verse is the standard benediction found at the close of each section of the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa; It is given as printed, and the English is editorial.

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये प्रथमाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ ॐ तत्सत् ॥

iti śrīmad-rājādhirāja-parameśvara-vaidika-mārga-pravartaka-śrī-vīrabukka-bhūpāla-sāmrājya-dhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārtha-prakāśe ṛk-saṃhitā-bhāṣye prathamāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || oṃ tat sat ||

Translation: "Thus ends the First Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛk-saṃhitā-bhāṣya — the Mādhavīya Vedārthaprakāśa — composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the bearer of the burden of the empire of the glorious King Vīra-Bukka, the King of Kings, Supreme Lord, the establisher of the Vedic path. Oṃ, That is the Real."

॥ Kannada colophon ॥ "Here the First Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and a Kannada rendering, comes to its end."

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥

yad akṣara-pada-bhraṣṭaṃ mātrā-hīnaṃ tu yad bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ||

Translation: "Whatever may be faulty in letter or word, or deficient in measure — may all that be forgiven, O God, Lord of Speech; salutations to you." The English is editorial.

॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥ ॥ मंगळं ॥

|| śubhaṃ bhūyāt || || maṅgaḷaṃ ||

"May there be auspiciousness. Blessing."

¶ Continuing "vocēyuḥ":) …लिङ्याशिषि… (liṅ āśiṣy aṅ, पा. ३-१-८६ [as printed; the usual number is different, and the print is recorded]) puts "aṅ" in the āśīrliṅ; झेर्जुस् (पा. ३-४-१०८) puts "jus" for "jhi"; the "j" of "jus" is an "it" by चुटू (पा. १-३-७) and the "s" ... elided by तस्य लोपः (पा. १-३-९); "vac + a + us" — वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति (पा. ६-१-१५) and वचेरुम् (पा. ७-४-२०) — before "aṅ" the augment "um" comes to "vac"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) gives guṇa; यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च (पा. ३-४-१०३) — the augment "yāsuṭ" in the parasmaipada, acute and "ṅit"; किदाशिषि (पा. ३-४-१०४) — "yāsuṭ" in the āśīrliṅ is "kit" (so no guṇa); the Mādhava school adds that by this very sūtra "yāsuṭ" comes. Hence "vac + yās + us." By छन्दस्युभयथा (पा. ३-४-११७) in the Veda the affix is both "sārvadhātuka" and "ārdhadhātuka"; hence "yās + us" takes the "sārvadhātuka" label, and लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) elides the "s" of "yās" ("s" not at the end); अतो येयः (पा. ७-२-८०) turns the "yā" (after an "a"-final stem) into "iy" → "voc-iy-us"; आद्गुणः (पा. ६-१-८७) → "vocēyuḥ." The "sārvadhātuka" accent is lost by तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित् (पा. ६-१-१८६) and the affix "aṅ" keeps its own acute; the single substitute "ē" of "i + a" … is acute by एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. ८-२-५). - "Dasma" — "dasu upakṣaye" with the Uṇādi ईषियुधीन्धिदसिश्याधूसूभ्योऽमुक् [as printed] (उ. सू. १-१४४) the affix "ma" with the augment "muk"; as a vocative standing after another word it loses its accent (आमन्त्रितस्य च, as printed). - "Kṛṣṭayaḥ" — क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (पा. ३-३-१७४): "ktic" and "kta" in a sense of a name: "ktic" is added to "kṛṣ," meaning "men"; "c"-marked, so the last syllable is acute by चितः (पा. ६-१-१६३). - "Syāma" — "as bhuvi" (to be) in the optative (vidhi-liṅ), first-person plural; "yāsuṭ"; by लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) the "s" is elided; the affix "mas" loses its final "s" (नित्यं ङितः, पा. ३-४-९९); श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. ६-४-१११) the "a" of "as" is elided before an affix that is "k" or "ṅ"-marked; hence "s-yā-ma" → "syāma." (The page ends mid-derivation of "syāma"; it continues on p. 116.

Points of substance: हर्योः (haryoḥ) — "harata iti harī," from hṛ with the suffix in, "n"-marked, so initial-udātta. सचा (sacā) — glossed "with" (Nirukta 5-5, "sacā saheti"). सम्मिश्लः (sammiślaḥ) — "mixing" from miśra + ghañ (Pā. 3-3-18) with a Vedic l for r, so "one who mixes thoroughly"; accent of the first member retained in the bahuvrīhi. वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — "yoked with a word"; the dual case-ending replaced by ā; the second member yuj has the final accent. वज्री (vajrī) — "having a vajra", suffix ini (Pā. 5-2-115). हिरण्ययः (hiraṇyayaḥ) — by ऋत्व्यवास्त्व्यवास्त्वमाध्वीहिरण्ययानि छन्दसि (Pāṇini 6-4-175), the m of hiraṇmaya is dropped irregularly in the Veda, so hiraṇyaya is the form; it is udātta on the ā by the suffix-accent.

¶ Rik 5 grammar, continued; Kannada; numbers as printed.) "Havāmahe" — स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले (पा. सू. १-३-७२) the ātmanepada; "mahiṅ" by तिप्तस्झि… (पा. सू. ३-४-७८); टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे (पा. सू. ३-४-७९) "mahe"; कर्तरि शप् (पा. सू. ३-१-६८); बहुलं छन्दसि (पा. सू. ६-१-३४), with ह्वः संप्रसारणम् (पा. सू. ६-१-३२) carried on: "hu + a + a + mahe"; संप्रसारणाच्च (पा. सू. ६-१-१०८) the prior form; guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (पा. सू. ७-३-८४); एचोऽयवायावः (पा. सू. ६-१-७८) "av"; अतो दीर्घो यञि (पा. सू. ७-३-१०१) the long "ā": "havāmahe"; unaccented by तिङ्ङतिङः (पा. सू. ८-१-२८). "Yujam" — "yuja samādhau" + "kvip": its "p" is "it" by हलन्त्यम् (पा. सू. १-३-३), the "i" by उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् (पा. सू. १-३-२), the "k" by लशक्वतद्धिते (पा. सू. १-३-८), all dropped by तस्य लोपः (पा. सू. १-३-९); the apṛkta "v" by वेरपृक्तस्य (पा. सू. ६-१-६७): the whole affix is lost. In the accusative "yuj + am," युजेरसमासे (पा. सू. ७-१-७१) would give "num" before a sarvanāmasthāna; but the sūtra names "yuji" (with "i"), i.e. "yujir yoge," not "yuja samādhau," so no "num"; and even if "yujir yoge" is taken, by अनित्यमागमशासनम् (परिभा. ९३-२) the augment rule is anitya, so "num" is to be withheld. "Vṛtreṣu" — "vṛtu vartane": "pratikūlatayā vartanta iti" (those standing in opposition), "vṛtrāṇi," hosts of enemies; स्फायितञ्चिवञ्चिशकिक्षिपिक्षुदिसृपितृपिदृपिवन्द्युन्दिश्वितिवृत्य… (continues on p. 279

20. Grammar: tatra — formed with tral after the word tad in the seventh case (Pā. 5-3-10), the syllable before the suffix being udātta since tral is l-marked; indra — the vocative, initially udātta, but as the first word of a pāda not lowered; rāye — the case-ending udātta by "ūḍidam…"; rabhasvataḥ — root rabha rābhasye, 'the beginning of an act'; the suffix asun, initial-udātta since nit; matup is pit and so unaccented; by Pā. 1-4-17 and 1-4-19 the word is not a pada before matup, but has the technical bha status, which blocks the pada status; tuvidyumna — 'he whose wealth (dyumna) is much (tuvi)', a bahuvrīhi, the vocative initially udātta; yaśasvataḥ — 'who has fame' with matup, not barred by vini (Pā. 5-2-121) since the two are combined everywhere; the word yaśas initial-udātta as a neuter not ending in -isan.

21. grammar pages 363–365, noted briefly

22. Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.

¶ The accompanying grammar, noted briefly: gomat and vājavat take their stem accent because matup is unaccented; vāja is a vṛṣādi word, initial-udātta; asme is formed by the substitute śe for the plural dative ending after asmad, replacing the whole as it is śit, final-udātta by the stem accent; by śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. 7-2-90) — on the view that the ṭi is dropped, the case-ending is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta; on the view that the final is dropped, the pararūpa by ato guṇe is a single substitute udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ; pṛthu — root prtha prakhyāne with the suffix ku and saṃprasāraṇa of r to ṛ (Uṇ. 1-29); śravaḥ — 'that which is heard' = wealth, with asun, initial-udātta; viśvāyuḥ — a bahuvrīhi 'in which wealth the whole life [is]'; the first-member accent of a bahuvrīhi being displaced by parādiś chandasi bahulam to the end of the first member, and the single substitute udātta, so initial-udātta; akṣitam — from kṣi kṣaye with the causative sense inside, the past-participle suffix in the passive; no lengthening by Pā. 6-4-60 and hence no n-substitution by kṣiyo dīrghāt (Pā. 8-2-46); the nañ compound has the accent of its indeclinable first member. One word, printed syadarthatvāt, is kept as printed [?].

23. grammar pages 367–368, noted briefly

24. Grammar noted briefly: asme as in Rik 7; dhehi — the root dhā with hi, with the substitution of e for ā and loss of the reduplicate (Pā. 6-4-119); śravaḥ with asun; sahasrasā — 'one who gives a thousand': root ṣaṇu dāne with viṭ (Pā. 3-2-67), ā for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41), final-udātta by the root, then the second-member rule; rathinyaḥ — 'those who have chariots,' feminine in ṅīp (Pā. 4-1-5), unaccented because pit; iṣaḥ takes the root accent if taken in its component sense and the stem accent if taken as a settled word.

¶ Grammar, noted briefly: suvivṛtam — root vṛñ varaṇe with kta, compounded with vi and then su; the i of vi is udātta by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199), setting aside Pā. 6-2-49; a long discussion with paribhāṣās 23 and 28 shows that, since "kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi" is not applied to "gatir anantaraḥ", the ṛ is udātta; sunirajam — root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ with khal (Pā. 3-3-126) after su and nis; tvādātam — root daip śodhane with kta, not dad- since it is not ghu (Pā. 1-1-20, 7-4-46; paribhāṣās 6, 105, 106), compounded with tvā (Pā. 7-2-97, 2-1-32, 6-3-14), first-member accent (Pā. 6-2-48); yaśaḥ — Uṇ. 4-190; gavām — stem accent; vṛdhi — dhi for hi (Pā. 6-4-102); kṛṇuṣva — root kṛvi with u (Pā. 3-1-80), ātmanepada by Vedic exchange; adrivaḥ — matup with v (Pā. 8-2-15), num (Pā. 7-1-70), ru (Pā. 8-3-1), unaccented as a vocative.

Continuing "Tvādātam":) … dāp śodhane: "daip śodhane takes the form dāp by the rule ādeca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. 6-1-45), and he explains it accordingly" — "purified by you, made clear," as the Bhāṣyakāra explains. According to Skandasvāmī's explanation, tvādātam is tvayā dattam, "given by you." The sense in the end is one, though the derivation of the word differs. The word tvādātam occurs not only in this rik but in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-40-6, 5-6-10 and 5-39-1; the word tvādattaḥ at Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-92-18, and tvādatrebhiḥ at Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-33-2.
